articles.title: A Mixed-Method Feasibility Study of an Online Group Program for Pregnant Women With ADHD.
articles.journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
articles.authors: Marcussen K, Kristensen RK, Jensen AT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnant women with ADHD may experience specific challenges related to executive functioning, emotional regulation, and preparation for motherhood. ADHD Mother's Online Resources (AMOR) is a 10-week online group program developed to provide ADHD-adapted psychoeducation, practical coping strategies, and peer support during pregnancy. This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of AMOR among pregnant women with ADHD in Denmark.
METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods feasibility study using pre- and post-intervention questionnaires and post-program individual and focus group interviews. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, adherence, satisfaction, perceived credibility, and negative effects. Secondary outcomes included self-reported ADHD symptoms, perceived stress, depressive and anxiety symptoms, emotion regulation difficulties, and ADHD-related quality of life. Qualitative interviews with 12 participants were analysed using the Framework Method, informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability.
RESULTS: Fifty-seven women self-referred within 3 months, and all three groups reached capacity within 24 h. Thirty-two women were enroled; 27 completed the program (program retention 84.4%) and 25 completed follow-up questionnaires (follow-up retention 92.6%), and mean session attendance was 80%. Satisfaction was high with a total mean Client Satisfaction Questionnaire score of 25.76; 88% would recommend the program and 88% intended to continue using the techniques. Reported negative effects were infrequent and mild. Qualitative findings indicated high acceptability, with participants describing the program as relevant, supportive, and meaningful. Perceived benefits included practical strategies, normalization, peer support, increased self-acceptance, improved partner communication, and greater confidence in communicating with healthcare professionals. Quantitative changes in symptom-based measures were small, with improvements observed particularly for anxiety symptoms and ADHD-related quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Findings suggest substantial unmet need for ADHD-adapted perinatal support. AMOR appeared feasible, acceptable, and well tolerated among pregnant women with ADHD. Future controlled studies should evaluate its effectiveness and impact on maternal psychosocial outcomes and postpartum well-being.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: S-20240074, 11/05/2024.

articles.title: Tumo​r-associated macrophages in ovarian, prostate, thyroid and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: molecular crosstalk and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.authors: Patel D, Ravindran S, Sojan MM et al.
articles.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment and play dual roles in endocrine cancer progression by exhibiting remarkable functional plasticity beyond the conventional M1/M2 paradigm. Their interactions with tumor cells influence immune evasion, angiogenesis, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance through complex signaling networks and extracellular vesicle-mediated communication. This review summarizes the current understanding of TAM biology across some key endocrine and hormone-dependent cancers, including ovarian, prostate, thyroid, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, highlighting their prognostic significance and molecular mechanisms. We further discuss emerging TAM-targeted therapeutic strategies, including macrophage depletion, immune checkpoint modulation, macrophage reprogramming, and nanoparticle-based approaches. Finally, we outline the challenges associated with clinical translation and emphasize the potential of single-cell and multi-omics technologies to enable precision macrophage-targeted therapies for endocrine cancers, including a summary of recent developments in the field of precision mapping of TAMs.

articles.title: Sex differences in gastrointestinal permeability during acute uncompensable heat stress: Role of menstrual phase hormones.
articles.authors: Leach S, Allsop EJ, Martin IA et al.
articles.abstract: Hyperthermia can increase gastrointestinal permeability, allowing microbes to leak from the intestinal lumen to the hepatic portal and systemic circulation. However, the extent to which sex and menstrual cycle hormones impact the risk of increased gastrointestinal permeability during heat stress is unclear. Twenty-four healthy young adults [12 male, 24 ± 3 years old; 12 female (5 oral contraceptive users), 23 ± 2 years old] participated in the study. Initially, participants completed a control trial (no heat or exercise) to determine baseline gastrointestinal permeability. Then, participants took part in a hyperthermia trial, in which deep body temperature was increased by +1.5°C from baseline via a water-perfused suit combined with semi-recumbent cycling at 40 W. Oestradiol was measured at baseline during the hyperthermia trial. In both trials, permeability was assessed by measuring the urinary excretion of orally ingested sucrose (10 g) and the lactulose/rhamnose ratio (L/R, 1 g each) to assess gastroduodenal and small intestinal permeability, respectively. Data are presented as the change in excretion from control to hyperthermia. Pooled analysis of all participants identified that hyperthermia increased small intestinal permeability [ΔL/R = 0.012 ± 0.029 (95% confidence interval 0.000 to 0.025), P = 0.050, d z   = 0.43]. Although there were no sex differences at the group level, we identified a strong positive correlation between ΔL/R and baseline oestradiol concentration within females (r = 0.709, P = 0.040). Gastroduodenal permeability did not increase with hyperthermia (P = 0.136), nor were there any differences between the sexes (P = 0.411). Future studies should confirm whether oestradiol plays an independent role in modulating heat-induced gastrointestinal permeability in humans.

articles.title: Underfunded, Overperforming: Endometrial cancer leads basic and translational science publications per NCI dollar.
articles.authors: Richardson MT, Gallivan A, Zello L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare relative research funding and basic and translational science publications for gynecologic cancers vs. other common cancers, normalized to incidence and mortality rates.
METHODS: SEER data were used to investigate incidence and deaths in the US from 2004 to 2024. Research funding was derived from National Cancer Institute (NCI) data. Google Scholar was utilized to identify oncology and medicine related journals with the highest H-indices. All abstracts on PubMed were reviewed and number of basic and translational science articles manually calculated.
RESULTS: In 2024, new diagnoses of breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancers totaled 313,510, 299,010, 234,580, and 152,810, respectively. Endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers accounted for 67,880, 19,680, and 13,820, respectively.NCI funding in 2023 was approximately $542.0 million for breast, $258.6 million for prostate, $435.0 million for lung, and $238.6 million for colorectal cancers, compared to $20.0 million, $132.0 million, and $20.7 million for endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers, respectively.Across the highest impact journals from 2004 to 2024, 24,169 basic/translational science publications were found: 8859 (breast), 4161 (prostate), 3537 (lung), 4321 (colorectal), 412 (endometrial), 2231 (ovarian), and 648 (cervical). When adjusted for incidence, ovarian cancer had the highest number of publications, at 220.9 publications per 100,000 cases. When adjusted for funding, endometrial cancer had the highest number of publications, at 23.1 publications per $1 million average annual NCI funding.
CONCLUSION: Funding relative to disease burden varies considerably among gynecologic cancers. Endometrial cancer receives the lowest NCI funding of any cancer studied when adjusted by incidence and mortality. Despite this, endometrial cancer produced the most basic and translational science publications per dollar.

articles.title: Updates in osteoporosis medications: maximizing benefits and minimizing risks.
articles.authors: Okazaki KM, Wang JY, Yu EW
articles.abstract: Osteoporosis is a major public health concern affecting approximately 1 in 3 women and 1 in 5 men over the age of 50 globally. Hip fractures are a significant complication of osteoporosis and are associated with approximately 20%-24% mortality in the year after fracture. While medications can substantially reduce fracture risk, these therapies remain significantly underutilized. This treatment gap is partly driven by confusion among healthcare professionals and patients regarding potential treatment complications. This narrative review provides a practical overview of strategies to maximize benefits and minimize risks of pharmacologic osteoporosis therapies, including calcium/vitamin D, bisphosphonates, denosumab, parathyroid hormone (PTH) analogs, romosozumab, raloxifene, and menopausal hormone therapy (MHT). In addition to reviewing the latest data about therapeutic efficacy and safety, we provide a summary of best practices to mitigate potential side effects. Relevant updates include new data on the efficacy of bisphosphonates in lower risk patients, recommendations for using osteoanabolic agents as first-line for very high fracture risk patients, important considerations regarding multiple vertebral fractures when discontinuing denosumab, as well as cardiovascular safety data and the option of a shortened course for romosozumab. FDA updates are highlighted: removal of the osteosarcoma black-boxed warning for PTH analogs, nuances in the warnings regarding MHT, and addition of a black-boxed warning for severe hypocalcemia with denosumab in chronic kidney disease. The benefits of osteoporosis medications in preventing high-morbidity fragility fractures significantly outweigh the small risks of serious complications. It is essential for clinicians to understand the myths and realities of these treatments and to implement mitigation strategies to ensure patient safety. By effectively addressing these issues, healthcare professionals can play a vital role in closing the osteoporosis treatment gap.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the Indonesian-Adapted Chapron Questionnaire as a Non-Invasive Screening Tool for Endometriosis: A Cross-Sectional Diagnostic Test Accuracy Study.
articles.authors: Hendrana ARA, Tjahyadi D, Bayuaji H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a long-term systemic inflammatory disease that affects approximately 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. The diagnosis of endometriosis often leads to delays of up to 11 years due to several obstacles, such as difficulty in diagnosing the condition, inaccurate beliefs, and self-management of symptoms. This delay results in an impaired quality of life, infertility, pain, sexual function, and diminished work productivity. Therefore, early screening of endometriosis is essential.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of the Indonesian-adapted Chapron symptom-based screening questionnaire by evaluating its sensitivity and specificity in relation to postoperative histopathological results.
METHODS: This cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at a gynecology outpatient clinic at a tertiary referral facility in Indonesia. Women who had undergone gynecologic surgery were enrolled, excluding those with suspected malignancy and pregnancy. Subjects has filled out a questionnaire after obtaining informed consent before. Histopathological analysis was performed as a reference standard. The sensitivity and specificity of both scores were calculated. The Youden index was used to determine the optimal cut-off using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.
RESULTS: A total of 316 women participated in this study. Score 1 (optimal cut-off >16) had a sensitivity of 76.2% and a specificity of 59.2% (AUC 0.715). For score 2 (optimal cut-off >14), the sensitivity of 74.3% and a specificity of 66.4% (AUC 0.739). At a cutoff value of >16, score 1 showed a PPV of 48.2% and an NPV of 83.3%. Score 2, using a cutoff value of >14, demonstrated slightly better predictive performance, with a PPV of 52.3% and an NPV of 83.8%.
CONCLUSION: The Indonesian adaptation of Chapron's screening questionnaire exhibits commendable diagnostic efficacy and may function as an effective non-invasive screening tool for identifying high-risk women with endometriosis in settings with limited resources to minimize diagnostic delays.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Pudendal Nerve Block in Elderly Pelvic Organ Prolapse Surgery: Impact on Anesthetic Consumption and Postoperative Recovery-A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Yang C, Lu Z, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nerve block is often used for multimodal analgesia. Surgeries for pelvic organ prolapse (POP) in elderly patients are focused on the perineal area, where pudendal nerve block (PNB) can provide analgesia or anaesthesia. There are limited studies on PNB in POP surgery, mainly addressing postoperative pain relief. This prospective randomized controlled trial examined the impact of ultrasound-guided PNB on intraoperative medication and postoperative recovery in elderly POP surgery patients.
METHODS: Patients aged 60-70 undergoing total vaginal hysterectomy (with or without sacral fixation/colporrhaphy) under general anesthesia were randomized into two groups: PNB (pudendal nerve block) and NPNB (no pudendal nerve block). Anesthesia was induced with target-controlled infusions of remifentanil (3 ng/mL) and propofol (3 µg/mL). The study compared intraoperative anesthetic doses, hemodynamic changes, cardiovascular drug needs, wakefulness time, and post-op recovery quality between the groups.
RESULTS: 58 patients completed the study. The PNB group required significantly less remifentanil (386.6 ± 239.1 µg vs 563.1 ± 235.7 µg, p = 0.005) and propofol (645.5 ± 315.2 mg vs 804.2 ± 297.2 mg, p = 0.028) compared to the NPNB group. Intraoperative hemodynamics were more stable in the PNB group, with a reduced need for vasopressors. The PNB group also exhibited faster emergence, lower postoperative pain, and less oversedation,with a non-significant trend toward higher QoR-40 scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided PNB in elderly POP surgery patients reduced opioid and anesthetic doses, shortened awakening time, and produced clinically favourable improvements in postoperative recovery. Larger studies are needed to confirm these benefits for postoperative rehabilitation.

articles.title: Prevalence of Thrombocytopenia Among Pregnant Women at Rabia Balkhi Hospital in Afghanistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Ahmadzai M, Ahmadzai AS
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Thrombocytopenia is common during pregnancy, but published evidence from Afghanistan is limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of documented thrombocytopenia among pregnant women admitted to selected wards at Rabia Balkhi Hospital, Kabul, and, among affected women, to describe severity, trimester distribution, maternal age, platelet count, and recorded diagnostic categories.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of inpatient registers and medical records from the general internal medicine and obstetric emergency wards between August 23, 2025, and March 20, 2026. The registers contained 1,760 unique pregnant women. Medical records of 138 women identified as having thrombocytopenia were reviewed, and all 138 women had platelet counts below 150 × 10⁹/L. Severity was classified as mild (100-149 × 10⁹/L), moderate (50-99 × 10⁹/L), or severe (<50 × 10⁹/L). Data were summarized descriptively using SPSS Statistics version 32.0 (IBM Corp. Released 2026. IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 32.0. Armonk, NY).
RESULTS: The documented prevalence of thrombocytopenia was 7.84% (138/1,760; 95% confidence interval: 6.67-9.19%). Mild, moderate, and severe thrombocytopenia occurred in 46 (33.3%), 64 (46.4%), and 28 (20.3%) women, respectively. Most affected women were in the third trimester (114; 82.6%). Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy constituted the largest recorded diagnostic category (79; 57.2%), including hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count (HELLP) syndrome (35 cases), preeclampsia (28 cases), and eclampsia (16 cases). Gestational thrombocytopenia accounted for 24 cases (17.4%), immune thrombocytopenia for nine (6.5%), and other or associated conditions for 26 (18.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: Documented thrombocytopenia affected 7.84% of pregnant women registered in the selected wards. Moderate thrombocytopenia was the most frequent severity category, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy constituted the largest recorded diagnostic category. The findings apply to this selected tertiary hospital population and should not be generalized to routine antenatal populations.

articles.title: Maternal cardiovascular and pregnancy outcomes among pregnant patients with mechanical and bioprosthetic valves.
articles.authors: Essa A, Kovell LC, Wilkie GL
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with mechanical heart valves in pregnancy are at a substantially higher risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Management of patients with mechanical heart valves poses a unique challenge, and strategies for anticoagulation in these patients remain controversial. The goal of this project was to determine rates of adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes in patients with mechanical valves compared to those with bioprosthetic valves, and assess outcomes in patients with mechanical valves using low molecular weight heparin and warfarin.
METHODS: A retrospective query was performed using Epic Cosmos to evaluate pregnancies affected by mechanical and bioprosthetic heart valves between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. Patient demographics and rates of adverse cardiac outcomes in the perinatal period, including heart failure, arrhythmia, and stroke, were assessed. The rate of anticoagulation with low molecular weight heparin and warfarin in patients with mechanical heart valves was evaluated, and cardiac and perinatal outcomes were determined and compared between groups. Rare outcomes were reported as <10 to protect patient privacy.
RESULTS: Baseline demographics between patients with mechanical and bioprosthetic heart valves were similar. Rates of heart failure (22.9%) and stroke (11.7%) were significantly higher in patients with mechanical compared to bioprosthetic heart valves, though the rates of maternal arrhythmia were similar between groups. Valve thrombosis was a rare outcome for patients with mechanical valves, with fewer than 10 events in the study sample. Perinatal outcomes including preterm and cesarean delivery were similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, mechanical heart valves are associated with high rates of heart failure and stroke in pregnancy. Rates of adverse events may be similar for patients using low molecular weight heparin compared to warfarin for anticoagulation in pregnancy.

articles.title: Feminizing and masculinizing gender-affirming hormone therapy have distinct effects on fibrinogen γ'.
articles.journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
articles.authors: Bøgehave M, Glintborg D, Christensen LL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibrinogen γ' is an alternatively spliced fibrinogen isoform. Higher fibrinogen γ' levels are associated with arterial thrombosis and lower levels with venous thrombosis. Feminizing gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) increases venous thrombosis risk, whereas masculinizing GAHT increases arterial thrombosis risk. How GAHT affects fibrinogen γ' is unknown.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate changes in fibrinogen γ' levels after 12 months of feminizing or masculinizing GAHT.
METHODS: Fibrinogen γ' and total fibrinogen were measured at baseline and after 12 months of GAHT in 245 transgender women and 318 transgender men (cohort study). Feminizing GAHT included oral or transdermal estradiol combined with cyproterone acetate (CPA) (3 groups). Masculinizing GAHT included intramuscular or transdermal testosterone with or without progestin (7 groups). Fibrinogen γ' was measured by ELISA and total fibrinogen by nephelometry. Relative fibrinogen γ' levels were calculated as the fibrinogen γ'/total fibrinogen ratio.
RESULTS: Fibrinogen γ' increased during feminizing GAHT (588 vs 628 μg/mL, P < .001), while relative fibrinogen γ' levels decreased (0.23 vs 0.22, P < .01). The increase in fibrinogen γ' was most pronounced with oral estradiol plus CPA (P < .02), while the decrease in relative fibrinogen γ' levels was comparable between treatment groups of feminizing GAHT. Fibrinogen γ' decreased during masculinizing GAHT (698 vs 660 μg/mL, P < .001), while relative fibrinogen γ' levels remained unchanged. No between-group differences were observed for masculinizing GAHT.
CONCLUSION: Feminizing and masculinizing GAHT for 12 months had opposite effects on fibrinogen γ' levels. Only the reduction in relative fibrinogen γ' levels during feminizing GAHT may contribute to increased venous thrombosis risk.

articles.title: Focal Adenomyosis and Uterine Junctional Zone Abnormalities Are Associated With Live Birth Rates in Women With Infertility and Adenomyosis Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Peng Y, Tang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Previous studies have shown that adenomyosis increases the incidence of failure and recurrent miscarriage in patients undergoing in vitro fertilization embryo transfer. This study aimed to evaluate the association between magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of women with infertility and adenomyosis and their assisted reproductive technologies (ART) outcomes, as indicated by ongoing pregnancy and live birth rates.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 1679 women diagnosed with adenomyosis via 3D ultrasound who underwent ART between October 2021 and December 2023. Pelvic MRI was performed by two qualified radiologists, and assessments were conducted according to standard diagnostic criteria. Baseline demographics, MRI manifestations, as well as parameters and outcomes of the first embryo transfer cycle were collected. Clinical and imaging factors of live birth in patients were identified. A predictive model for live birth in women with infertility and adenomyosis was developed using multivariable logistic regression and visualized as a nomogram.
RESULTS: In total, 1400 women underwent MRI and completed ART. The mean age of the participants was 31.84 ± 3.56 years. Ongoing pregnancy rate was 58.21% (815/1400), whereas live birth rate was 56.21% (787/1400). Multivariable logistic regression of MRI characteristics identified focal adenomyosis and junctional zone abnormalities as factors associated with live birth rates. A predictive model incorporating six clinical and imaging factors had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.640 (95% confidence interval: 0.607-0.673).
CONCLUSION: This study represents the first large-scale prospective observational cohort study to explore the relationship between MRI features of adenomyosis and clinical outcomes of ART. Focal adenomyosis and JZ abnormalities were associated with live birth rates in women with adenomyosis undergoing ART; further research is needed to confirm these associations and to explore their clinical utility.

articles.title: Generation of mixed ovarian cancer and fibroblast spheroids by bioprinting.
articles.authors: Atwal A, Richardson A
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional tumour-stroma models are urgently needed to improve the predictive power of preclinical drug screening in ovarian cancer, a disease with high mortality and limited therapeutic success. Here, we present a droplet-bioprinted ovarian cancer model incorporating OVCAR-4 cells expressing nano-luciferase and primary cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) embedded within a collagen (Telecol)-based hydrogel. Using the CELLINK BIO X system, we generated reproducible mini-spheroids with controlled architecture, enabling systematic evaluation of cancer and CAF cell density and chemotherapeutic response. Bioprinted spheroids showed good reproducibility across plates when bioink volume and printing conditions were stable. Increasing cancer cell density produced a non-linear rise in luminescence, and this could be at least partially corrected by normalisation to initial cell number. CAFs consistently and robustly enhanced cancer cell growth in a ratio-dependent manner, and confocal imaging revealed that CAFs frequently organised into encapsulating structures around cancer clusters, forming stromal niches associated with matrix contraction and increased cancer-CAF interface. However, CAFs did not protect cancer cells against carboplatin, as drug sensitivity remained comparable in monoculture and CAF co-cultures. This suggests that CAF-driven growth support and CAF-driven chemoresistance are mechanistically separable in this model. Together, this work establishes a mechanically tunable, spatially defined bioprinted ovarian cancer-CAF model that captures key stromal interactions which are not reproduced in studies using CAF conditioned media alone, while remaining compatible with automated, higher-throughput workflows.

articles.title: Fragment-end sequence architecture of cell-free DNA and its association with tumour DNA in non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.authors: Das D, Gupta P, Tambade R et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentation patterns provide a promising source of molecular information for liquid biopsy applications. However, the sequence features underlying fragmentation and their relationship to tumour-derived DNA remain incompletely understood. Here, we characterized fragment-end sequence signatures of extracellular cfDNA across cell lines, extracellular compartments, stress conditions and plasma from patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: cfDNA derived from cell lines was characterized using Oxford Nanopore sequencing, followed by fragment-end analysis. Publicly available Nanopore cfDNA datasets from healthy individuals and NSCLC patients were analyzed to examine dinucleotide patterns and derive a motif ratio index. These signatures were further assessed for their association with estimated ctDNA abundance in an independent cohort of 50 EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients.
RESULTS: Nanopore sequencing of A549, H460 and WI38 cell-line cfDNA revealed reproducible end-motif patterns, with enrichment of AT-, GT- and CT-containing termini. Analysis of plasma cfDNA from healthy individuals showed distinct end-motif profiles from cell-line-derived cfDNA, with separation maintained after reducing 4-mer motifs to 5'-terminal dinucleotide features. An exploratory motif ratio based on these patterns showed a modest increase in lung cancer patients compared with healthy individuals. In an independent Illumina cohort of 50 NSCLC patients with activating EGFR mutations, 5'-terminal dinucleotide frequencies were associated with estimated circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) abundance using cross-validated LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression (Spearman ρ = .73, p = 3.35 × 10‒9). The predefined motif ratio showed a strong correlation with estimated ctDNA concentration (Spearman ρ = .76, p = 1.89 × 10‒10).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that simple, interpretable cfDNA end-motif signatures capture sequence features associated with ctDNA abundance and warrant further validation for non-invasive cancer monitoring.

articles.title: Preoperative prediction of lymphovascular space invasion in early-stage cervical cancer using a deep learning-based 3D super-resolution MRI radiomics model.
articles.authors: Guo Y, Ye Y, Mu Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) is a critical prognostic factor guiding adjuvant therapy in early-stage cervical cancer, yet its preoperative assessment is often limited by the spatial resolution of standard MRI. This study aimed to investigate the value of a deep learning-based 3D super-resolution (SR) MRI radiomics model in predicting LVSI and to evaluate how SR reconstruction impacts image quality and radiomic feature robustness.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 117 patients with early-stage cervical cancer (training cohort: n = 81; validation cohort: n = 36). A 3D Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) reconstructed T2-SPAIR and DWI sequences into super-resolution images (SRI) with a 4× upsampling factor. Radiomic features were extracted, and an SRI-based multimodal fusion model was developed and systematically compared with original image (OI)-based and clinical models using the Area Under the Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: SR reconstruction significantly improved the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for both DWI (P = 0.012) and T2-SPAIR (P = 0.030). For DWI, SRI preserved intratumoral texture heterogeneity, leading to improved diagnostic performance (Validation AUC: SRI-DWI 0.864 vs. OI-DWI 0.727, P = 0.041). The final SRI-Fusion model achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (Validation AUC: 0.934), significantly outperforming the OI-Fusion model (AUC: 0.828, P = 0.044) and the clinical model (AUC: 0.626, P = 0.012).
CONCLUSIONS: SRGAN-based reconstruction effectively improves MRI quality and feature robustness, particularly in DWI. The SRI-based multimodal radiomics model demonstrates superior predictive performance for LVSI in early-stage cervical cancer compared to conventional imaging and clinical models.

articles.title: Levator hiatus width as a complementary measurement tool in assessing pelvic floor dysfunction.
articles.authors: Gayathri AP, Subbaiah P, Neshatian L et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Levator hiatus width (LHW) is a measurement along with H- and M-lines in MR defecography to evaluate pelvic floor dysfunction. Our study aimed to correlate the resting LHW with the resting and defecation-phase H-line and M-line, the presence of pelvic organ prolapse (POP), and to evaluate the reliability of measurement between readers.
METHODS: This Institutional Review Board (IRB) approved case-control study retrospectively reviewed MR defecography exams of 70 patients with symptomatic pelvic floor dysfunction and 19 age-matched controls. LHW, H-line, and M-line in resting (RPH, RPM) and dynamic defecation phases (DPH, DPM) were measured, and the anterior, middle, and posterior compartment pelvic floor descent was graded. Three readers analyzed each exam, and their interobserver variability was compared.
RESULTS: LHW was abnormal (>4.5 cm) in 29 patients (41.4%). Mean (± SD) LHW was 4.4 ± 1.1 cm in patients and 3.7±1.0 cm in controls. Abnormal LHW was significantly associated with RPH (P<0.001), RPM (P<0.001), and several compartment-specific prolapse findings on logistic regression, including bladder descent, vaginal descent, enterocele, and sigmoidocele. Intraclass correlation coefficients showed greater agreement between the two readers with dedicated training to read MR defecography.
CONCLUSION: Resting LHW was associated with several MRI markers of POP and may provide complementary information during MR defecography. Its added diagnostic value beyond H-line and M-line was not formally assessed in this exploratory analysis and requires validation. Dedicated training in reporting MR defecography can reduce interobserver variability in interpretations.

articles.title: When It All Falls On the Physicians: A Qualitative Study of Physician Workforce Changes Post-Dobbs in Four States With Abortion Bans.
articles.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health
articles.authors: Stratis CR, Fortman EC, Shiman LJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to explore how abortion bans in four highly restrictive states affected physician workforce dynamics among physicians of diverse specialties after the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision.
METHODS: The Medical Integrity Initiative conducted in-depth interviews with physicians in Alabama, Idaho, Oklahoma, and Tennessee, states with strict abortion bans and severe legal penalties for physicians. Participants included specialists in emergency medicine, maternal-fetal medicine, medical genetics, obstetrics, oncology, and reproductive endocrinology and infertility. We used stratified and snowball sampling and conducted interviews via Zoom from July to October 2024. Grounded theory methodology informed the inductive approach to data analysis. We began with open (descriptive) coding and followed it with axial (interpretive) analysis.
RESULTS: Thirty-two physicians across all specialties reported new challenges following the Dobbs decision. We identified the following overarching themes: 1) heightened liability concerns, 2) shifting burden of care onto academic hospitals, 3) added advocacy responsibilities, 4) emotional strain and ethical dilemma of leaving the state, and 5) increased challenges regarding workforce size and workload. Challenges that participants described included colleagues' exodus, difficulty recruiting providers and trainees, and labor and delivery unit closures. Many reported that they considered leaving their state. Participants expressed a desire for their institutions to support evidence-based clinical practice.
CONCLUSION: Physicians experienced changes in workforce composition and responsibilities following the Dobbs decision. Collective action and robust occupational, legal, and mental health support from their institutions and medical societies might enable physicians to safely stay and sustainably advocate in states with abortion bans.

articles.title: Prenatal cannabis exposure and adverse neonatal outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression on tobacco co-use.
articles.authors: Sainz K, Gonzalez Herrera D, Robinson M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal cannabis use has risen; tobacco co-use clouds its contribution to neonatal outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To quantify these associations and how far between-arm tobacco imbalance explains them.
METHODS: Observational studies, eight databases to 20 September 2026. Random-effects models pooled tobacco-unadjusted risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences. Meta-regression used the between-arm tobacco difference, with and without study size; tobacco-balanced studies pooled separately; within-study adjusted/unadjusted pairs compared.
RESULTS: 79 studies covered about 18.2 million pregnancies. Exposure was associated with small for gestational age (SGA; RR 1.90, 1.66 to 2.17), low birth weight (LBW; 1.72, 1.47 to 2.03), perinatal mortality (1.76, 1.34 to 2.30), preterm birth (1.41, 1.25 to 1.60) and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission (1.41, 1.18 to 1.67), and 166 g lower birth weight (122 to 211). Trim-and-fill raised preterm, NICU and mortality to 1.52, 1.50, 1.85; none for LBW or SGA. Associations rose with the between-arm tobacco difference for SGA, LBW, preterm and NICU (p≤0.001), independently of size. Where tobacco was balanced, they were smaller (SGA 1.35, LBW 1.38), imprecise for preterm and NICU. Multivariable adjustment including tobacco gave a within-study ratio of risk ratios of 0.78 (median 55% log-scale reduction, 31 pairs). With biologically verified exposure, LBW (1.66, 1.41 to 1.95) and SGA (1.79, 1.54 to 2.07) persisted.
CONCLUSIONS: Across more studies than any previous review, cannabis exposure was associated with small for gestational age, low birth weight, preterm birth, NICU admission and perinatal mortality. When controlling for tobacco smoking, preterm birth and NICU admission were no longer significantly increased; small for gestational age and low birth weight remained raised. Perinatal mortality showed no tobacco gradient, so is not attributable to tobacco, though balanced studies were too few. Counselling should address both substances. Evidence is observational and source-study adjustment erratic; certainty is very low and further evidence is needed.

articles.title: Sample size calculations for developing clinical prediction models for binary outcomes: applied methodological study with real examples.
articles.authors: Yimer NB, Belsti Y, Teede H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare existing sample size calculations for developing prediction models in rare and common outcome scenarios, and to explore how the choice of method influences required sample sizes and their implications for clinical use.
DESIGN: Applied methodological study with real examples.
SETTING: Monash Health public maternity hospitals (two secondary and one tertiary), Australia, 1 January 2016 to 31 December 2024.
PARTICIPANTS: 78 170 singleton pregnancies recorded from 2016 to 2024.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Required sample size, and model calibration, discrimination, prediction errors, and clinical use (net benefit).
RESULTS: Three sample size calculation methods were applied: method 1, target of minimising overfitting and estimating average risk precisely based on a closed form solution; method 2, target of minimising overfitting and overall prediction error based on a simulation based approach; and method 3, targeting individual level prediction stability. A simulation based general framework that encompassed and extended methods 1-3 was also applied. These approaches were illustrated with rare (pre-eclampsia) and common (gestational diabetes) outcomes to determine how sample sizes influenced the main outcome measures. Sample sizes required for developing a clinical prediction model varied by sample size method, choice of predicted outcome, development method, and performance targets. Compared with the gestational diabetes model, the pre-eclampsia model required consistently larger sample sizes (eg, method 1 required 3097 and 519 patients for pre-eclampsia and gestational diabetes, respectively). For both outcomes, method 2 required moderate minimum sample sizes (pre-eclampsia 3935 and gestational diabetes 954 patients), whereas method 3 needed larger sample sizes (pre-eclampsia 150 318 and gestational diabetes 52 269 patients to target prespecified uncertainty interval widths). The general simulation based approach showed that penalised logistic regression models had the most stable calibration, even at smaller sample sizes, whereas unpenalised regression models improved with increasing data. The random forest model gave consistent discrimination but showed persistent miscalibration (slope 1.7) across all sample sizes.
CONCLUSIONS: Required sample sizes varied across methods because different model performance targets were optimised: population level accuracy was achieved with modest samples, whereas individual level accuracy and prediction…

articles.title: Tex11 mutant mouse models of human azoospermia.
articles.authors: Atkins GR, Hvasta-Gloria R, Ausavarungnirun C et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Do different patient TEX11 mutations lead to non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) when modeled in mice?
SUMMARY ANSWER: A frameshift mutation in Tex11 leads to azoospermia in mice (Tex11D); a missense mutation had no impact on fertility (Tex11A); and a splice site mutation caused reduced testis weights and sperm counts with variable sub-fertility (Tex11L).
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Half of all NOA cases are unexplained but may arise from unidentified genetic mutations. Several variants in TEX11 have been identified in men with NOA; and Tex11 knockout in mice causes NOA.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: For fertility analysis of the different mutations, the sample sizes were as follows: n = 3 wild-type controls; n = 5 Tex11D; n = 3 Tex11A; and n = 3 Tex11L. Wild-type males and hemizygous mutant male mice in each Tex11 line were bred with two to four different wild-type females for fertility analysis. At 12 weeks, testes and epidiymides were then collected for histological analysis and sperm counts. Additional Tex11L mice (n = 3) and wild-type controls (n = 3) were bred for 52 weeks with 2 new wild-type females every 2-3 weeks, then testes and epididymides were collected for further analysis. Testes and epididymides from Tex11L mice (n = 3 for wild type and mutants) were also collected at 24 and 36 weeks of age for histological analyses.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: TEX11 variants identified in male patients with NOA were introduced into the orthologous region of the mouse genome using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. Lines were expanded onto a DBA/2 background by breeding female heterozygous carriers to wild-type DBA/2 males. Hemizygous males from the third generation and beyond were used for fertility studies, gross tissue morphology, sperm counts, and histological analysis.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Compared to wild-type mice (145.0 ± 17.56 mg testis weight; 1.72 ± 0.50 million sperm/cauda epididymis; 6.42 ± 0.73 pups/breeding), Tex11D mice had reduced testis weight (28.33 ± 0.68 mg), no sperm in the epididymis, and were infertile with a maturation arrest testicular phenotype. We did not observe any spermatogenesis or fertility defects in Tex11A mice (145.0 mg ± 0 mg; 1.52 ± 0.11 million sperm/cauda; 5.83 ± 0.81 pups/breeding) compared to wild type. Tex11L mice had reduced testis weight (78.33 ± 16.41 mg) and reduced epididymal sperm counts (0.33 ± 0.13 million/cauda epididymis) but a variable fertility phenotype (5.42 ± 1.13…

articles.title: A hypothesis framework linking the menopausal transition, sleep and brain waste clearance: Insights from experimental models.
articles.authors: Zamani A, Jenkins L, Rodger J et al.
articles.abstract: The menopausal transition is increasingly recognized as a neuroendocrine transition with implications for brain health, sleep, cognition and vulnerability to neurodegenerative disease. Fluctuating and declining ovarian hormones coincide with sleep disruption, vasomotor symptoms, cognitive complaints, neuroinflammation and altered blood-brain barrier integrity. Current preclinical models each capture selected components of the menopause transition and provide essential mechanistic insights into the effect of ovarian hormone loss on the brain. Across these models, endocrine change is associated with impairments in hippocampal and prefrontal-dependent cognition, altered sleep-wake regulation, vascular dysfunction, glial activation, disrupted synaptic and mitochondrial homeostasis and exacerbation of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease-like pathology. An emerging but understudied mechanism linking menopause, sleep and neurodegeneration is the glymphatic system, a sleep-dependent brain waste clearance pathway. This review synthesises current evidence to highlight how menopause-related sleep disruption, vascular dysfunction, neuroinflammation and potential alterations in brain-waste clearance may converge to shape cognitive ageing and neurodegenerative disease risk.

articles.title: 1H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women.
articles.authors: Mekle R, Fleck L, Bauer M et al.
articles.abstract: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.

articles.title: Dexamethasone rescues fertility in unexplained recurrent endometrial cavity fluid patients via the NR3C1/PER1/SCNN1A-autophagy axis.
articles.authors: Zeng Z, Mo D, Xiao T et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Unexplained recurrent endometrial cavity fluid (ECF) is a poorly understood condition that severely impairs embryo implantation and IVF outcomes, yet no targeted therapy exists.
OBJECTIVES: To bridge this gap, our study shifts the clinical paradigm from symptomatic observation to mechanism-based intervention.
METHODS: We used a novel patient-derived organoid model that recapitulates the key phenotypic features of unexplained recurrent ECF in vitro.
RESULTS: We found that unexplained recurrent ECF primarily results from reduced fluid absorption (due to a reduction in SCNN1A), rather than increased fluid secretion. Beyond its role in fluid homeostasis, SCNN1A deficiency was shown to overactivate autophagy in patient-derived endometrial organoids, leading to a loss of ciliated cells and disruption of adherens junction integrity. This cascade creates a vicious cycle that further aggravates unexplained recurrent ECF. Notably, model-based drug screening showed phenotypic rescue of patient-derived organoids by dexamethasone (DXMS) via the NR3C1/PER1/SCNN1A-autophagy pathway.
CONCLUSION: These results revealed the pathological mechanism underlying unexplained recurrent ECF patients and provided a proposed pathway and tangible evidence to support personalized treatment strategies for this challenging condition.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided suction with balloon tamponade for cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy: a combined treatment strategy.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Lucidi A, Liberati M, Di Tizio L et al.
articles.abstract: Cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy (CSEP) is a severe iatrogenic complication of cesarean delivery (CD). However, there is no consensus yet on how to treat CSEP. This report describes a minimally invasive approach combining ultrasound-guided suction evacuation of the ectopic sac followed by immediate balloon tamponade insertion at the site of the prior CD. Continuous visualisation of the uterine-bladder interface helps prevent accidental uterine or bladder injuries, while mechanical balloon may help in providing adequate haemostasis. In our experience, this method may be a reasonable and potentially effective minimally invasive approach to treating CSEP, though it requires confirmation in adequately powered randomised controlled trials.

articles.title: Robotic Myomectomy for High Fibroid Burden: A Multimodal Blood-Sparing Strategy for the Removal of 40 Leiomyomas.
articles.authors: Augusto KL, Bilhar APM, Karbage SAL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate robotic myomectomy for a high leiomyoma burden using a multimodal blood-sparing strategy.
SETTING: Tertiary referral center for advanced minimally invasive gynecologic surgery.
PARTICIPANTS: A 25-year-old nulligravid woman. MRI showed a 1152-cm³ uterus with multiple leiomyomas, including an 8.6-cm dominant lesion.

articles.title: Digital health interventions and maternal outcomes among pregnant women in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Avenorgbo SK, Acheampong K, Morgan AK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The burden of maternal mortality and morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remains high, driven by under-resourced health systems and challenges with accessibility and affordability. However, Digital Health Interventions (DHIs) are optimising maternal health, particularly antenatal care (ANC) outcomes in these settings.
OBJECTIVES: This paper presents a comprehensive synthesis of the effects of DHIs on maternal outcomes during pregnancy in LMICs.
METHODS: The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and searched six databases, Cochrane, Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, between 1st and 30th June 2023. Reference list screening, which involved manually checking the bibliographies of included full-text studies to identify additional relevant studies, complemented the electronic search. The review included empirical quantitative studies published in English between 2018 and 2023 that reported on DHIs in ANC in any LMIC. We critically appraised, extracted data from, and narratively synthesised all included studies.
RESULTS: The included papers comprised randomised controlled trials (RCTs) (n = 3), cross-sectional studies (n = 3), and mixed-methods studies (n = 2) from five LMICs. Most DHIs used smartphone technologies primarily for education, advice, and ANC reminders. DHIs improved maternal health behaviours, but evidence on clinical outcomes was inconclusive because data were limited.
CONCLUSION: The paper reports that DHIs improve maternal behaviours and could foster the attainment of maternal and neonatal goals in LMICs. Future research should establish the clinical outcomes associated with DHIs to inform inclusive policy responses, since equity, sustainability, and clinical outcomes remain uncertain.

articles.title: Global hemostatic assessment in infertile women with endometriosis seeking fertility consultation: A prospective case-control study.
articles.authors: Casalechi M, Reschini M, Padovan L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic gynecological disease characterized by ectopic endometrium-like tissue, inflammation, pelvic pain and infertility. Alterations in coagulation and platelet-related parameters have been reported, particularly in advanced disease, but whether these findings reflect a systemic functional prothrombotic phenotype remains unclear. This study aimed to assess whether infertile women with advanced endometriosis seeking fertility consultation exhibit systemic hypercoagulability using complementary global and functional assays of hemostasis.
METHODS: This prospective case-control study included 145 women seeking fertility consultation: 74 with advanced endometriosis and 71 controls without clinical or imaging evidence of the disease. Conventional coagulation parameters, thrombin generation assay with and without thrombomodulin, and thromboelastometry were assessed in the whole cohort. Flow-based thrombus formation was evaluated using the Total Thrombus-formation Analysis System in 31 participants.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were largely comparable. Thrombin generation parameters, including endogenous thrombin potential and the endogenous thrombin potential/thrombomodulin ratio, did not differ between groups. Conventional coagulation parameters, including fibrinogen, D-dimer, von Willebrand factor antigen, ADAMTS13 activity, and the von Willebrand factor antigen/ADAMTS13 activity ratio, were comparable. In thromboelastometry, EXTEM clotting time was longer in women with endometriosis and remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons, but this finding was not consistent with a prothrombotic profile. In the flow-based subgroup, atheroma-chip parameters were comparable, whereas platelet-chip parameters showed nominal differences that did not remain significant after correction.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of infertile women with advanced endometriosis, global functional hemostatic assays did not identify a consistent systemic prothrombotic phenotype compared with controls. These findings should not be interpreted as excluding hypercoagulability in all endometriosis populations. Further studies should clarify whether subtle platelet-dependent alterations occur in specific endometriosis subgroups or within the lesion microenvironment.

articles.title: Electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarization in early and late-onset preeclampsia: implications for maternal cardiovascular involvement.
articles.authors: Işık E, Özgü Erdinç AS, Gürbüz HS et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate electrocardiographic (ECG) parameters in pregnant women with early-onset and late-onset preeclampsia (PE) compared with healthy controls, and to explore their association with maternal cardiovascular involvement.
METHODS: This prospective case-control study included 91 pregnant women with PE and 130 healthy controls. ECG parameters, including PR interval, QRS duration, QT and corrected QT (QTc), were measured between 28 and 37 weeks of gestation. Subgroup analyses were performed to compare early- and late-onset PE. ROC curve analysis was used to evaluate the discriminative performance of ECG parameters.
RESULTS: PR interval, QRS duration, QT and QTc were significantly prolonged in the PE group compared with controls (p < 0.001). These alterations were more pronounced in early onset PE. In ROC analysis, QTc demonstrated the highest discriminatory performance for identifying early-onset PE (AUC = 0.78), followed by PR interval and QRS duration.
CONCLUSIONS: PE particularly early-onset PE, was associated with significant alterations in electrocardiographic parameters, including QTc interval prolongation. These findings suggest that preeclampsia may be accompanied by changes in maternal cardiac electrical activity. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and determine the potential clinical relevance of these electrocardiographic alterations.

articles.title: First-cycle β-hCG dynamics predict single-agent chemoresistance in low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Kong Y, Che Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to introduce a first-cycle β-hCG response marker for predicting first-line single-agent chemoresistance in low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 299 patients. Patients were randomly assigned to a development cohort (n = 198) and internal validation cohort (n = 101). The primary exposure was the C2/C1 β-hCG ratio, defined as the serum β-hCG level before cycle 2 divided by the level before cycle 1. Restricted cubic spline and receiver operating characteristic analyses were used to derive the optimal threshold. Three models were evaluated: a FIGO-only model, a baseline clinical model, and a first-cycle dynamic model incorporating the C2/C1 ratio.
RESULTS: First-line single-agent chemoresistance occurred in 45 patients in the development cohort and 23 in the internal validation cohort. The optimal C2/C1 β-hCG threshold was 0.38. Patients with a poor first-cycle response had higher chemoresistance rates than favorable responders in both the development cohort (43.8% vs. 8.5%) and internal validation cohort (44.7% vs. 9.5%). The dynamic model showed superior discrimination compared with the baseline clinical model, with AUCs of 0.867 in the development cohort and 0.844 in the internal validation cohort. Addition of the C2/C1 ratio improved calibration, reduced Brier scores, and yielded significant reclassification improvement. Poor responders required more cycles to β-hCG normalization, more total chemotherapy cycles, and more frequent second-line or multi-agent therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: The first-cycle C2/C1 β-hCG ratio showed potential for predicting first-line single-agent chemoresistance in low-risk GTN. A threshold of 0.38 may help identify patients requiring closer monitoring, but requires prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Oocyte quality modulates paternal age effects on ICSI outcomes: an AI-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Braga DPAF, Setti AS, Del Collado M et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Does oocyte quality, assessed by an artificial intelligence (AI) tool, modify the association between paternal age and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) outcomes?
DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study including 12,337 mature oocytes from 1989 ICSI cycles in 1479 participants (January 2020 to December 2024). Oocytes were scored with MAGENTA (a continuous AI quality score, range 0-10). Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the independent effect of paternal age, MAGENTA score, maternal age, body mass index, and prespecified paternal age × MAGENTA score and paternal age × maternal age interactions on laboratory and clinical outcomes. Cluster bootstrapping (B = 300) verified the principal interactions.
RESULTS: A higher MAGENTA score was the strongest predictor of laboratory outcomes (per +1 SD: fertilization, odds ratio [OR] 1.76; blastulation, OR 1.69; both P < 0.001). The paternal age × MAGENTA score interaction for cumulative clinical pregnancy was confirmed by cluster bootstrapping (P = 0.040): cumulative pregnancy was 54.7% in cycles combining paternal age ≤39 years and high MAGENTA score versus 40-45% otherwise. A paternal age × maternal age interaction was observed for embryo euploidy (OR 0.86 per 1 SD product term; P = 0.007). In unambiguous cycles (n = 258, 415 embryos), implantation was predicted by maternal age (OR 0.68; P = 0.021) and MAGENTA score (OR 1.45; P = 0.020) but not by paternal age; implantation findings should be interpreted with caution given the reduced subset available for this analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-derived oocyte quality modulates the impact of paternal age on ICSI laboratory outcomes and cumulative clinical pregnancy, supporting the use of AI-based oocyte metrics to refine prognostic assessment and patient counselling in ICSI cycles.

articles.title: Prevalence of chaotic PGT-A results and limited euploid or mosaic reclassification after selective warming and rebiopsy.
articles.authors: Lin PY, Lee CI, Cheng EH et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the prevalence of chaotic results in next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), and how are selected chaotic embryos classified after repeat trophectoderm biopsy?
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study analysing 30,083 blastocysts from 8822 cycles undergoing NGS-based PGT-A at a single high-volume IVF centre between August 2016 and December 2024. Embryos initially classified as chaotic (five or more whole-chromosome aneuploidies) were selected for warming-rebiopsy based on morphology (≥4BB) or physician discretion. The main outcome was post-rebiopsy reclassification (euploid/mosaic versus aneuploid/chaotic). Subsequent transfer and live birth outcomes were reported descriptively.
RESULTS: Among 30,083 blastocysts, 151 (0.50%) were chaotic, with 95 out of 151 (62.9%) originating from women aged 39 years or older. Of 46 embryos selected for thaw‒rebiopsy, 43 out of 46 (93.5%, 95% CI 84.8 to 100%) survived warming and provided interpretable results. Re-analysis classified 23 out of 43 embryos (53.5%, 95% CI 39.5 to 67.4%) as persistently chaotic and 11 out of 43 (25.6%, 95% CI 14.0 to 39.5%) as other aneuploid. In contrast, nine out of 43 embryos (20.9%; 95% CI 9.3-32.6%) were reclassified as euploid (two out of 43) (4.7%, 95% CI 0.0 to 11.6%) or mosaic (seven out of 43) (16.3%, 95% CI 7.0 to 27.9%).
CONCLUSIONS: Chaotic PGT-A results were uncommon in this single-centre cohort. Among selected embryos undergoing warming-rebiopsy, most remained chaotic or aneuploid, whereas a minority were reclassified as euploid or mosaic. Because rebiopsy was conducted in a selected subgroup and subsequent transfer experience was limited, these findings are preliminary and do not establish the clinical benefit of rebiopsy.

articles.title: Allele-frequency optimization of SNP panels for non-invasive prenatal paternity testing (NIPAT): a theoretical analysis.
articles.authors: Trombetta B, Pistacchia L, Diverio S et al.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive prenatal paternity testing (NIPAT) exploits cell-free fetal DNA circulating in maternal plasma to assess paternity before birth and is increasingly based on large panels of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). In SNP-based NIPAT, marker panels are traditionally designed by selecting polymorphisms with a minor allele frequency (MAF) near 0.5, in order to maximize expected heterozygosity. However, this criterion does not necessarily maximize the evidential value contributed to the Combined Paternity Index (CPI). Here we develop an analytical model that, starting from the informative mother-fetus genotype configurations observed in maternal plasma cell-free DNA, formally derives the expected contribution of a single biallelic SNP to the CPI as a function of allele frequency. We show that the expected proportion of informative loci, corresponding to one-half of the expected heterozygosity, is maximized at MAF = 0.5, but that this frequency corresponds to a local minimum of the expected evidential contribution, which instead peaks at MAF = 0.147. At this optimum, the reduced probability that a locus is informative is more than offset by the higher Paternity Index generated when the detectable paternal allele is rare. We further show that the expected Probability of Exclusion (PE) reaches its own maximum at MAF = 0.211. Overall, these results demonstrate that no single allele frequency simultaneously maximizes all three relevant forensic performance metrics (proportion of informative markers, PI, and PE), and that SNP selection for NIPAT should explicitly consider which of these quantities is to be optimized, rather than relying implicitly on the maximum-heterozygosity criterion alone.

articles.title: Zona pellucida-based immunocontraception for canine fertility control: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Awawdeh L, Alani N, Callcott ET et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map the extent, characteristics and gaps in published evidence on zona pellucida (ZP)-related immunocontraceptive development relevant to female dogs, distinguishing canine reproductive observations from immunogenicity, surrogate-model and mechanistic evidence.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological guidance and reported using the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The eligibility period was expanded to include studies published from 1979 through December 2025, ensuring inclusion of early foundational research on canine zona pellucida (ZP)-based immunocontraception. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and databases accessed through EBSCO were searched. Supplementary searches of Google Scholar and citation searching were undertaken to identify additional relevant records. Eligible evidence was charted descriptively according to publication, animal model, intervention, study design, and reported outcomes. Consistent with the descriptive scoping review approach, no meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken.
RESULTS: The current map contains 19 primary reports, including seven with female-dog reproductive or ovarian observations and two additional canine immunogenicity reports. These are report counts, not independent-cohort counts. Canine pregnancy, pup-production, cycle, endocrine and ovarian outcomes were measured in varying combinations. Related endocrine and histopathology reports explicitly reused animals. Small groups, inconsistent outcome denominators, incompletely described assessment procedures and incomplete source availability limit interpretation. A structured post-treatment breeding assessment establishing reproductive recovery was not identified in the available canine texts.
CONCLUSIONS: The literature maps a heterogeneous development pathway from antigen characterisation to small canine reproductive experiments. The main gaps concern cohort independence, reproductive denominators, standardised ovarian assessment, post-treatment fertility recovery and longitudinal welfare outcomes. This map identifies questions for research; it does not estimate comparative effectiveness, grade safety, or recommend clinical use.

articles.title: Let-7b-5p differentially regulates human first trimester trophoblast migration and sFlt-1 through TLR7 and TLR8.
articles.authors: Siegel EG, Salmeron LC, Abrahams VM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preeclampsia is characterized by a pro-inflammatory, anti-migratory and anti-angiogenic placental phenotype. Impaired spiral artery remodeling stemming from trophoblast dysfunction is a key pathogenic mechanism. Little is known about the processes that govern trophoblast function normally and in preeclampsia. In preeclampsia, placental Let-7b-5p is reduced. The objectives of this study were to determine the normal function of Let-7b-5p in human trophoblast cells, to examine whether the ssRNA sensors, Toll-like receptor (TLR) 7 and/or TLR8 are mediators of trophoblast Let-7b-5p function, and whether disruption of this pathway promotes a preeclampsia-like phenotype in the trophoblast.
METHODS: The human first trimester trophoblast cell line, Sw.71, was transfected with a Let-7b-5p mimic, a Let-7b-5p inhibitor, or scramble control. Cells were treated with or without the TLR7 inhibitor IRS661 or the TLR8 inhibitor CUCPT9a. Trophoblast migration was measured using a two-chamber assay and interactions with human endometrial endothelial cells (HEECs) was measured using a 3D matrigel model. Trophoblast anti-angiogenic sFlt-1 release was measured by ELISA and sFLT1 mRNA measured by RT-qPCR.
RESULTS: Transfection of trophoblast cells with a Let-7b-5p mimic elevated migration through activation of TLR7 and TLR8, while in a TLR7-dependent manner, the Let-7b-5p mimic negatively regulated sFlt-1 production. Furthermore, inhibition of trophoblast Let-7b-5p reduced migration, elevated FLT1 mRNA expression and sFlt-1 release, and reduced trophoblast-endometrial endothelial cell interactions.
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights a role for TLR7/TLR8-activating Let-7b-5p in promoting normal trophoblast function and endothelial interactions and that disruption in this miR-driven signaling pathway may be relevant to processes driving a pre-eclamptic placental phenotype.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicle-based regenerative strategies for male infertility and erectile dysfunction: Molecular mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges.
articles.authors: Aslanian-Kalkhoran L, Ebrahimi-Warkiani M, Hasanzadeh A et al.
articles.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane contained vesicles of nano size that transport cargo such proteins, lipids, and microRNAs (miRNAs) for interaction between cells. Naturally released EVs and their cargos have been implicated in the control of male reproductive physiology that includes spermatogenesis, testicular homeostasis, and erectile function. In addition to their physiological activities, compounds related to EVs have been proposed as possible biomarkers for male reproductive disorders. Administered EV preparations, especially those produced from stem cells, have been explored as prospective cell-free restorative therapies for male infertility and erectile dysfunction (ED). Recent research has shown that stem cell-derived EVs can promote tissue healing via anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, pro-angiogenic, and immunomodulatory processes. Preclinical and experimental investigations indicate that these EV formulations might help improve spermatogenic and testicular results while facilitating neurovascular restoration and erectile recuperation; however, therapeutic effectiveness has primarily been shown in animal studies. Furthermore, the advances in EV engineering and biomaterial-based delivery strategies may increase their therapeutic potential through elevated targeting efficiency, cargo loading and regulated release. This review highlights current evidence on EV biology, potential as biomarkers, regenerative mechanisms, and therapeutic uses in male infertility and ED. A literature search was first undertaken in February 2025 on PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science and updated until September 16, 2026, focusing on papers dealing with EVs, male infertility, spermatogenesis, ED, biomarkers, and regenerative applications. The review also points to the main challenges that are limiting clinical translation, such as EV heterogeneity, large-scale production, standardization, characterization, delivery approaches, and long-term safety. Although EV-based interventions represent a promising cell-free regenerative strategy, clinical translation will require standardized nomenclature, manufacturing, characterization, potency testing, dosing, delivery, and long-term safety evaluation.

articles.title: Ultrasonography assessment of adnexal masses: how to predict malignancy.
articles.journal: Best practice & research. Clinical obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Best Pract Res Clin Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Ferrero S, Barra F, Cagnacci A et al.
articles.abstract: Adnexal masses are frequently encountered in gynecological practice, and the primary clinical challenge is to estimate the likelihood of malignancy in order to guide appropriate patient management. Transvaginal ultrasonography is the first-line imaging modality and, in expert hands, a highly accurate technique for characterizing adnexal lesions, with magnetic resonance imaging serving as a complementary second-line test for sonographically indeterminate masses. This review provides a practical overview of contemporary ultrasound assessment of adnexal masses, focusing on the sonographic features associated with benign and malignant tumors, standardized terminology, and validated risk prediction models. We summarize the International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) terminology and discuss the principal ultrasound-based approaches for risk stratification, including the IOTA Simple Rules, the Simple Rules Risk score, the Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa (ADNEX) model, and the benign-descriptors two-step strategy, together with their integration into the Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS). The review also examines the ultrasound characteristics that may help distinguish primary ovarian malignancies from metastatic lesions, emphasizing features that support differential diagnosis and appropriate referral. Current evidence indicates that standardized ultrasound assessment, combined with validated prediction models, provides an accurate and reproducible estimation of malignancy risk while complementing expert subjective evaluation. The ADNEX model offers the additional advantage of estimating the probability of different malignant subtypes, including metastatic disease, whereas O-RADS provides a structured reporting and management framework. A systematic, evidence-based ultrasound approach improves preoperative risk stratification, facilitates communication among clinicians, optimizes referral to gynecological oncology centers, and helps reduce both unnecessary surgery for benign disease and delayed diagnosis of ovarian cancer.

articles.title: FABP4 is associated with ROS-dependent ferroptosis inhibition and platinum resistance in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Xing S, Tan Y, Lu X et al.
articles.abstract: Platinum resistance remains the major obstacle in ovarian cancer treatment, yet the role of lipid metabolism regulators in chemo-resistance mechanisms is not well understood. To address this, this study combined computational and experimental approaches to identify FABP4 as a candidate factor associated with platinum resistance through ferroptosis suppression. Transcriptomic data from GSE51373 were analyzed using limma for differential expression, and machine learning algorithms (XGBoost/Lasso/Random Forest) were employed to prioritize resistance-associated genes. Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer cell lines (Resistance Index,RI=3.8) were established by pulse exposure to increasing cisplatin concentrations (0.5-10 μM) over 6 months for functional validation. In vitro assays, including CCK-8 proliferation,Annexin V/PI apoptosis detection, ROS detection, ferroptosis markers (GPX4 activity/MDA/Western blot), and shRNA-mediated FABP4 knockdown, were performed, and the therapeutic potential was evaluated in BALB/c nude mouse xenografts. The results showed that multi-algorithm screening identified FABP4 as a top platinum resistance biomarker (AUC=0.861,95% CI: 0.782-0.940). TCGA survival analysis further revealed that high FABP4 expression was significantly associated with worse prognosis in ovarian cancer. Experimentally, FABP4 was upregulated in resistant cells (p < 0.01), and its knockdown suppressed proliferation (p < 0.01) and tumor growth (p < 0.001). Mechanistically, FABP4 was associated with reduced intracellular ROS and alterations in ferroptosis markers, as demonstrated by increased GPX4 activity and SLC7A11 expression and decreased lipid peroxidation (MDA reduced 35%, p < 0.01) in resistant cells. Notably, FABP4 knockdown increased cisplatin-induced apoptosis and elevated ROS levels. In conclusion, FABP4 is associated with platinum resistance and correlates with ROS-dependent ferroptosis marker alterations, and may restore chemosensitivity, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for refractory ovarian cancer.

articles.title: HIF-1α-SLC2A1 signaling contributes to neutrophil extracellular trap-induced senescence-associated changes in retinal pigment epithelial cells.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Li J, Xue H et al.
articles.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been implicated in sterile inflammatory injury, but their contribution to dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is not well defined. We examined NET formation in patients with dry AMD and assessed its effects on retinal injury and retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells. Neutrophils isolated from patients with dry AMD exhibited greater PMA-induced NET formation than those from healthy controls, accompanied by higher serum levels of MPO-DNA complexes and cell-free DNA. In sodium iodate (NaIO₃)-treated mice, H3Cit signals accumulated predominantly in the outer retina adjacent to the RPE. Suppression of NET formation with GSK484, as well as neutrophil depletion with anti-Ly6G, reduced retinal damage, preserved RPE morphology, and improved retinal function. NET exposure also induced senescence-related changes in ARPE-19 cells, whereas DNase I markedly weakened these effects. Proteomic profiling pointed to Toll-like receptor and HIF-1 signaling as candidate pathways involved in NET-mediated injury. NET treatment increased TLR2 and MyD88 expression and promoted HIF-1α accumulation in the nucleus without an obvious change in total HIF-1α abundance. Further analysis identified SLC2A1 as a downstream target of HIF-1α. Reporter assays showed that HIF-1α enhanced SLC2A1 promoter activity through a hypoxia-response element, while HIF1A knockdown reduced NET-induced RPE senescence. Re-expression of SLC2A1 partially restored the senescent phenotype. These findings support a contribution of NETs to experimental retinal injury and implicate HIF-1α-SLC2A1 signaling in NET-induced senescence-associated changes in RPE cells.

articles.title: Data-driven cardiometabolic profiling in untreated women with Rotterdam-defined polycystic ovary syndrome: Unsupervised clustering and machine-learning profile assignment.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Kurt A, Yıldız AG, Ulusoy CO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic risk in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is heterogeneous and may not be fully captured by Rotterdam phenotypes. We aimed to identify data-driven cardiometabolic profiles at initial diagnosis and to evaluate supervised models for profile assignment.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, clinic-based study included 485 newly diagnosed, untreated women aged 18-45 years with Rotterdam-defined PCOS. Ten routinely available cardiometabolic variables were median-imputed, standardized, reduced by principal component analysis (PCA), and clustered using k-means. Profiles were characterized using variables withheld from clustering and evaluated in missing-data, anthropometry-excluded, age/body mass index-adjusted laboratory-only, and internal assignment-stability analyses. Patient-level cross-validated logistic-regression and random-forest models were used for profile assignment.
RESULTS: K-means identified a metabolically favorable profile in 342 patients (70.5%) and a metabolically unfavorable profile in 143 (29.5%). The unfavorable profile showed higher adiposity, central obesity, fasting glucose, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol, transaminases, white blood cell count, insulin resistance, post-load glucose responses, C-reactive protein (CRP), platelet count, lipid-derived indices, and androgen bioavailability, together with lower sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG). Rotterdam phenotype distribution did not differ between profiles (P = 0.650). The profile structure was broadly robust to k-nearest-neighbor-imputed and complete-case clustering (adjusted Rand index [ARI] = 0.783 and 0.909, respectively), whereas age/BMI-adjusted laboratory-only clustering showed lower agreement with the primary partition (ARI = 0.307). Training-fold refitting with held-out centroid assignment showed high internal assignment stability (ARI = 0.909). The independent clinical-endocrine model showed moderate discrimination (receiver operating characteristic area under the curve [ROC-AUC], 0.718), whereas secondary cluster-recovery models showed higher discrimination (ROC-AUC, 0.889-0.942; random forest, 0.935).
CONCLUSIONS: Routine baseline clinical and laboratory data identified a metabolically unfavorable PCOS profile that was not fully reflected by Rotterdam phenotype distribution in this clinic-based cohort. These exploratory findings require external validation and outcome-based evaluation before their…

articles.title: Association between vulvovaginal symptoms and intimate hygiene habits, sociodemographic and clinical data in Spanish women: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Domínguez-Romero MV, Alburquerque-Sendín F, Punzano-Martínez N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between self-reported vulvovaginal symptoms, intimate hygiene practices, and sociodemographic and clinical characteristics in adult Spanish women.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between February 2025 and January 2026 among 154 adult women (median age 27 years, interquartile range [IQR] 20). Self-reported vulvovaginal symptoms were assessed with the Spanish version of the Vulvovaginal Symptoms Questionnaire (VSQ), and intimate hygiene practices with a questionnaire adapted from a previously published instrument.
