Variables with p < 0.20 in non-parametric bivariate analyses were entered into a forward stepwise multiple linear regression model.
RESULTS: Overall, 57.8 % of women reported at least one physical vulvovaginal symptom, most frequently discharge (34.4 %), odor (22.7 %) and dryness (20.1 %); emotional, daily-life and sexual-life impact was reported by 66.2 %, 33.1 % and 38.3 %, respectively. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were not associated with VSQ scores, except for sexual activity. In the multivariable model (adjusted R2 = 0.334), higher VSQ scores were associated with external (β = 0.416) and intravaginal (β = 0.328) use of anti-itch creams, use of sanitary pads or pantyliners outside menstruation (β = 0.242) and sexual activity (β = 0.208) (all p ≤ 0.002). Washing the genital area after defecation was associated with lower VSQ scores (β = - 0.157, p = 0.021).
CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported vulvovaginal symptoms were common and more closely associated with product use and behavioral factors than with sociodemographic or clinical characteristics. Given the cross-sectional design, the associations with anti-itch creams and pantyliners could reflect product use in response to pre-existing symptoms and should not be interpreted as causal.

articles.title: What Patients are Reading About Prenatal Cell-Free DNA: An Analysis of Leading Publicly Available AI-Chatbots.
articles.authors: Finkelstein MS, Rose SL, Jenkins L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the quality, consistency, and framing of information about prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening generated by publicly available chatbots, including variation across simulated user age profiles.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative content analysis of outputs from three publicly available chatbots. To reduce carryover effects and personalization, prompts were entered using a VPN, private browsing, and cleared browser cookies. Outputs were generated using distinct simulated user age profiles. Analysis examined informational completeness, framing of benefits and limitations, terminology, source transparency, and age-related differences in responses.
RESULTS: Chatbot outputs varied substantially across platforms and user profiles, with misinformation, omissions, and incomplete information identified. Common themes included inconsistent explanations of the purpose and scope of cfDNA screening, frequent omission of test limitations and downstream implications, and variable readability scores (at a 9th-14th grade level) and terminology that sometimes conflate screening with diagnostic testing. Citations to high-quality sources were limited or absent. Age-based profile variation was associated with differences in tone, complexity, and emphasis, suggesting implicit tailoring of information presentation.
CONCLUSION: Publicly available chatbots may provide inaccurate or inconsistent information about cfDNA screening. As these tools are increasingly used outside clinical settings, improving accuracy, transparency, discussion of limitations, and source citation is essential to support reliable patient-facing health information.

articles.title: Endometrial ultrasound features associated with methotrexate success in tubal ectopic pregnancy: a prospective case series.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Shirazinezhad S, Khademi F, Elhaie M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopic pregnancy is an important cause of maternal morbidity in early pregnancy. Single-dose methotrexate is commonly used for haemodynamically stable women with unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy, but treatment success varies. The association between pre-treatment endometrial ultrasonographic features and treatment outcome remains uncertain.
METHODS: This prospective case series included 177 women with confirmed tubal ectopic pregnancy who received a single intramuscular dose of methotrexate (50 mg/m2) at two tertiary hospitals in Isfahan, Iran, between January and December 2024. Transvaginal ultrasonography was used to measure endometrial thickness and classify the endometrial echo pattern as homogeneous or triple-layer. Treatment success was defined as a ≥ 15% decline in serum β-hCG from day 4 to day 7 after treatment, followed by weekly monitoring until the concentration became undetectable. Associations with treatment success were assessed using univariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Treatment success occurred in 94 of 177 women (53.1%). Responders had lower median baseline β-hCG concentrations (500 versus 1400 mIU/mL; P < 0.001), thinner endometrium (7 versus 9 mm; P = 0.009), and a higher proportion of homogeneous endometrial appearance (65.9 versus 49.4%; P = 0.026). In univariable logistic regression, baseline β-hCG (P = 0.003), ectopic pregnancy size (P = 0.013), and homogeneous endometrial appearance (P = 0.027) were significantly associated with treatment success; endometrial thickness showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.0498).
CONCLUSION: Baseline β-hCG, ectopic pregnancy size, and endometrial appearance were associated with single-dose methotrexate success in univariable analyses, while endometrial thickness showed a borderline association. Because no multivariable model was fitted, these findings should not be interpreted as independent predictors. Endometrial ultrasonographic features may provide supportive information alongside established clinical factors such as baseline β-hCG.

articles.title: Protocol to assess self-renewal capacity and post-treatment line derivation using an organoid drug resistance assay.
articles.authors: Reichenbach J, Hierlmayer S, Geweniger S et al.
articles.abstract: Platinum resistance drives unfavorable outcomes in ovarian cancer, but its mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we present a detailed protocol for measuring sustained carboplatin effects on post-treatment regenerative capacity in patient-derived ovarian cancer organoids using an organoid drug resistance assay. The assay mimics clinical chemotherapy cycles, recovery, and long-term growth in vitro. We describe the steps for carboplatin treatment and for quantifying organoid number and size. We then detail procedures to establish platinum-treated patient-derived organoids (PDOs) for rechallenge against matched parental PDOs to assess acquired platinum resistance. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Reichenbach et al.1.

articles.title: Impact of HPV Status on Inter- and Intraobserver Agreement in ThinPrep Cervical Cytology: A Swedish Multicenter Study.
articles.authors: Basic V, Edvardsson H, Roumelis N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is the necessary cause of cervical cancer. As cervical screening programs increasingly adopt primary HPV testing with reflex cytology triage, the diagnostic performance and reproducibility of cytological interpretation have become increasingly important. Knowledge of HPV status may influence cytological assessment, particularly in cases with equivocal and low-grade lesions, potentially affecting diagnostic consistency, clinical management, and healthcare resource utilization. This study aimed to assess interobserver and intraobserver agreement among Swedish cytotechnologists and to evaluate the impact of HPV genotype and oncogenic-risk information on cervical cytology interpretation.
METHODS: In this multicenter, multi-rater reproducibility study, 20 Swedish cytotechnologists independently evaluated 107 ThinPrep cervical cytology cases representing the full diagnostic spectrum defined by the Bethesda System and Swedish national reporting guidelines. Each case was assessed twice: blinded to HPV results in Round 1 and informed of HPV genotype and oncogenic-risk information in Round 2. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement were evaluated using multiple agreement measures, and the influence of HPV information and observer characteristics on diagnostic interpretation was assessed using mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Interobserver agreement remained stable following disclosure of HPV genotype and oncogenic-risk information. Across all observers, agreement measures showed only small numerical changes between rounds. In paired analyses restricted to the 18 observers who completed both assessments, none of the differences in Cronbach's α, Kendall's W, ICC (2,1), Fleiss' κ, mean pairwise Spearman's ρ, or Krippendorff's α reached statistical significance (all p > 0.05). Similar findings were observed after stratification by cytological diagnosis, HPV status, and HPV risk classification. Intraobserver agreement remained substantial, with exact agreement ranging from 52.3% to 80.4% and agreement within one diagnostic category from 79.4% to 97.2%. Observer characteristics were not significantly associated with intraobserver agreement.
CONCLUSION: Disclosure of HPV genotype and oncogenic-risk information had only a limited impact on cervical cytology reproducibility. Diagnostic agreement remained largely unchanged, indicating that interpretation was driven primarily by cytomorphological features. HPV…

articles.title: Ethnic Features of Oxidative Modification of Lipids and DNA in the Peripheral Blood and Ejaculate of Reproductive-Age Men with Idiopathic Pathospermia.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.authors: Kurashova NA, Dashiev BG, Kolesnikov SI et al.
articles.abstract: We studied the characteristics of lipid and DNA oxidative modification in the peripheral blood and ejaculate of reproductive-age men with idiopathic oligoasthenoteratozoospermia from two ethnic groups: Caucasians (represented by Russians, n = 222) and Mongoloids (represented by Buryats, n = 131). Significant ethnic differences were revealed: in the peripheral blood, Mongoloids exhibited elevated levels of lipid oxidative modification, as well as higher activities of both the non-enzymatic and enzymatic antioxidant defense systems. Conversely, in the ejaculate, higher glutathione S-transferase activity and a significantly lower oxidative stress index were recorded in Mongoloids compared to the Caucasian cohort. These results indicate potentially more effective compensatory and adaptive mechanisms at both the systemic (peripheral blood) and local (ejaculate) levels in Mongoloids than in Caucasians.

articles.title: Longitudinal associations between perceived social support and maternal depression and anxiety across the perinatal period.
articles.authors: Choudhary M, Donkin L, Kercher A
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Despite robust international evidence that social support protects maternal mental health, the role of social support across the perinatal period remains poorly understood in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to examine how perceived social support relates to maternal depression and anxiety during the perinatal period, comparing partner, family, and friend support, and testing whether stress and sleep moderate these associations.
METHODS: Participants were 121 pregnant women who completed monthly surveys over 12 months, including the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale, and Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, along with measures of stress and sleep. Linear mixed models tested longitudinal associations and moderation effects.
RESULTS: Higher perceived social support was consistently associated with lower depression and anxiety. Family support was the most reliable protective source. Stress predicted higher distress and moderated the effect of support on anxiety, with support being more protective under high stress. Sleep problems predicted greater distress but did not moderate support effects.
CONCLUSION: Findings suggest that perceived social support, particularly from family, is an important protective factor for maternal mental health. Screening for social support and stress in perinatal care may strengthen early identification and guide family-centred interventions.

articles.title: Computed tomography derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in high-risk breast cancer using fully automated deep learning algorithms.
articles.authors: Tsou TC, Yang Z, Wang T et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer.
METHODS: We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins.
RESULTS: Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis.
CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.

articles.title: Post-ICSI oocyte degeneration inflates the conventional blastocyst utilization rate: degeneration-penalized and MII-anchored denominator corrections.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Onder E, Olcay IO, Duzcu T et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Conventional IVF laboratory key performance indicators (KPIs) are reported as single ("sole") ratios, with the denominator excluding mature oocytes lost during the procedure. We tested whether the blastocyst utilization rate overstates measured performance by excluding post-ICSI oocyte degeneration from its denominator, and we developed two complementary corrections that return degeneration to the denominator.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of a single pooled ICSI cohort of 7,216 cycles and 56,349 MII oocytes. Against the conventional blastocyst utilization rate (BUR = Frozen/2PN), we defined: a degeneration-penalized BUR (DP-BUR) that adds degenerated oocytes to the denominator-additive, Frozen/(2PN + ATR), and multiplicative, (Frozen/2PN) × (1 - ATR/MII)-and a true BUR (TBUR = Frozen/MII) anchored to all mature oocytes. ATR denotes post-ICSI degenerated oocytes. We directly measured degeneration in 1,552 cycles (21.5%) and modeled it within the documented 1-5% institutional range in the remainder; a sensitivity analysis was restricted to the directly measured cycles. We stratified degeneration as < 5% versus ≥ 5%. Each metric was compared against the 40% competence benchmark defined for conventional BUR-applied to the corrected metrics to quantify recalibration, not as a validated threshold-and we counted how many operators (anonymized analysis units) changed benchmark status across metrics; these metrics are not proposed as tools to attribute error to individual operators.
RESULTS: Conventional BUR was 41.9; DP-BUR was 40.2 (additive) and 40.5 (multiplicative); TBUR was 32.8-bracketing the correction, with DP-BUR attributing the gap to degeneration alone (+ 4% over the degeneration-penalized value) and TBUR to all mature-oocyte attrition (+ 28%). In the sensitivity analysis restricted to cycles with directly measured degeneration (1,552 cycles; 14,433 MII; degeneration 6.5%), the gap persisted and widened: conventional BUR 53.6 versus DP-BUR 49.6 (additive) and TBUR 43.0 (+ 8.2% and + 24.8%, respectively). The corrections were degeneration-dependent and, for DP-BUR, degeneration-specific: from < 5% to ≥ 5% degeneration, DP-BUR fell from 54.4% to 42.7% while conventional BUR barely moved (54.6% → 52.0%), so DP-BUR is essentially flat where degeneration is low and drops only where it is high; TBUR fell from 46.1% to 38.4%. Against the 40% benchmark, conventional BUR passed 24 of 38 operators, DP-BUR passed 17 (7 flipped from pass to fail), and…

articles.title: Interleukin-11 Contributes to TGF-β-induced Fibrotic Responses in Endometriosis.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Ono Y, Zhang D, Tanaka K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory gynecological disorder characterized by progressive fibrosis, yet the mechanisms driving fibrosis remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the role of interleukin-11 (IL-11) in endometriosis-associated fibrosis.
METHODS: With informed consent, ovarian endometriotic tissues, cyst fluids, and primary human endometriotic stromal cells (ESCs) were obtained from patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery. Publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to identify the cellular source of IL11 expression. IL-11 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry and ELISA, and its functional role in ESCs was investigated using quantitative PCR, IL-11 neutralization, and collagen gel contraction assays.
RESULTS: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified an IL11-high stromal cell population enriched for extracellular matrix remodeling genes. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated strong IL-11 expression predominantly localized within fibrotic areas of ovarian endometriotic lesions. In addition, IL-11 concentrations in ovarian endometrioma cyst fluid were significantly higher than those in non-endometriotic ovarian cyst fluid (median: 90.81 vs. 28.91 pg/mL, p < 0.001). In ESCs, TGF-β stimulation significantly increased IL11 mRNA expression (19.2-fold, p < 0.05) and IL-11 secretion (3.7-fold, p < 0.001). IL-11 stimulation also increased the mRNA expression of CTGF (1.4-fold, p = 0.02), PAI-1 (1.3-fold, p = 0.027), and IL-6 (1.4-fold, p = 0.020) in ESCs. Furthermore, IL-11 significantly enhanced collagen gel contraction (relative gel area: 1.00 vs. 0.81, p < 0.05), whereas IL-11 neutralization partially attenuated TGF-β-induced gel contraction (0.46 vs. 0.77, p = 0.063).
CONCLUSION: IL-11 acts as a downstream mediator of TGF-β signaling and promotes profibrotic remodeling in endometriotic stromal cells. These findings identify IL-11 as a potential therapeutic target for endometriosis-associated fibrosis.

articles.title: Effects of Cooking With Liquefied Petroleum Gas or Biomass on Lung Function Among Pre-School Aged Children in Peru: A Prospective Follow-Up of a Randomized Trial.
articles.authors: Nicolaou L, Checkley W, Rha J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Billions worldwide are exposed to household air pollution (HAP) from solid fuel use, increasing risk of lung function impairment and chronic respiratory disease. Understanding HAP effects on early life lung function may identify critical windows for intervention.
METHODS: We performed respiratory oscillometry in 3-5-year-olds whose mothers participated in a randomized trial of LPG versus usual solid fuel use during pregnancy and infancy. We assessed resistance (R7) and reactance (X7) at 7 Hertz, frequency dependence of resistance (R7-19), resonance frequency (fres) and area above the reactance curve from 7 Hertz (AX7). We computed z-scores for R7, X7, fres, and AX7 from pediatric reference equations. Rigorous quality control was applied. Exposure-response analyses examined the association between R7 or AX7 z-scores and prenatal or postnatal PM2.5 or CO exposures.
RESULTS: We tested 101 children (mean [±SD] age 4.4 ± 0.6 years, 51.5% male, 50.5% intervention). Mean R7, X7, fres and AX7 z-scores were similar between intervention and control groups: -0.1 ± 1.0 vs -0.2 ± 1.2, -0.8 ± 1.0 vs -1.0 ± 1.1, 0.9 ± 1.1 vs 0.4 ± 1.1, and 1.2 ± 1.0 vs 1.3 ± 1.3, respectively. Intention-to-treat analysis showed no differences between arms in pre-bronchodilator lung function or bronchodilator response, except for a larger post-bronchodilator decrease in mean fres z-score in the intervention arm (-0.36, 95% CI -0.71 to -0.02). Postnatal CO exposure was associated with higher AX7 z-scores, indicating worse reactance (0.041 per 1 ppm CO increase, 95% CI 0.003 to 0.078). No associations were found for PM2.5 exposure.
CONCLUSION: Early-life LPG use did not improve oscillometric lung function compared with those exposed to biomass smoke. An exploratory association between postnatal CO exposure and impaired lung reactance warrants confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Rising Prevalence and Lateralization Differences of Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformations: A 12-Year Study in Urban China, 2013-2024.
articles.authors: Cheng X, Nie L, Meng C et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Congenital pulmonary airway malformations (CPAMs) are rare developmental anomalies of the lung, with limited population-based data on their epidemiological characteristics and temporal trends, particularly in China.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the demographic and clinical characteristics of CPAM cases in urban China, analyze associated maternal and fetal risk factors, and evaluate temporal trends in overall prevalence and by lung laterality.
METHODS: A total of 135 CPAM cases and 3208 controls were included in a retrospective population-based study using data from a major maternal and child health registry in Beijing. Descriptive statistics, multivariable logistic regression, and Joinpoint regression were used to analyze trends and identify risk factors.
RESULTS: The overall prevalence of CPAMs increased significantly from 2013 to 2024 (APC = 6.69%, p < 0.05). Right-lung CPAM cases exhibited an increase (APC = 16.48%, p < 0.05), while left-lung cases remained stable (APC = -0.61%, p > 0.05). Multivariable analysis identified gravidity (aOR = 41.91, 95% CI: 25.65-71.09) and twin pregnancy (aOR = 4.66, 95% CI: 1.38-13.32) as significant risk factors. Maternal age, education, residence, and gestational age were also associated with CPAM occurrence.
CONCLUSION: This study provides epidemiological evidence on CPAMs in a Chinese urban population, highlighting a considerable increase in prevalence over the past decade, particularly in right-lung cases. Identified risk factors suggest a role of obstetric history and plurality in CPAM etiology. These findings underscore the need for enhanced prenatal surveillance and further investigation into the mechanisms underlying laterality-specific trends.

articles.title: Mitochondrial mass and cell ratio: predictors of maternal-specific imprinted methylation levels in ART-produced embryos.
articles.authors: Panko AJ, White CR, Zhang J et al.
articles.abstract: Infertile couples worldwide seek assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs) to help conceive biological children. Even when treatment is successful, there is increased risk for perinatal complications, including preterm birth, intrauterine growth restriction, low and high birth weight, and genomic imprinting disorders. Consequently, there is a need to investigate effects of ARTs on oocytes and preimplantation embryos, simultaneously, for metabolism (mitochondria), development and genomic imprinting. We hypothesized that ARTs disrupt mitochondrial dynamics and function, altering embryo developmental rates and maintenance of imprinted methylation during preimplantation development. To address this, we used a mouse model to determine relationships between these processes across multiple preimplantation stages. We observed that superovulation disrupted mitochondria in mouse oocytes, including decreased mean total and active mitochondrial mass, and altered mitochondrial distribution in superovulated MII oocytes. In preimplantation embryos, mean active mitochondrial mass was decreased in morula and blastocyst-stage embryos, with outer cells possessing asymmetric distribution of active mitochondria mass and increased superoxide levels. Further comparison of No ART controls to ART-produced blastocysts revealed lower inner:outer cell ratios, higher cavity:blastocyst volume ratios, lower mean total mitochondrial mass/cell, and lower mean active mitochondrial mass/cell. Regression analyses demonstrated that mitochondrial mass and inner:outer cell ratio independently predicted maternal Snrpn and Kcnq1ot1 methylation loss in ART-produced blastocysts, respectively. This contrasted with paternal H19 methylation. ART treatment acted as the primary driver of paternal methylation loss, with altered blastocyst variables acting downstream of ART treatment. Overall, this work provides novel linkages between metabolism, embryo developmental rates and genomic imprint regulation in preimplantation embryos.

articles.title: One number, no agreed definition: why uterine age is not yet a measurable quantity.
articles.authors: Wang Q, Zhang J
articles.abstract: Reproductive age is measured on two axes, ovarian reserve and embryo ploidy, and both scales move with age. The uterus has one number, endometrial thickness, and it does not move. Three recent studies removed the oocyte or the embryo from the causal chain, using donor oocytes, donor oocytes with gestational carriers, or euploid blastocysts only. All three reported lower pregnancy rates with increasing age. In the two that measured endometrial thickness, it was unchanged. The variables that do change with age are not the ones national registries record. We propose three requirements for measurement and reporting that can each be tested with existing data, and argue that until they are met no causal claim about uterine aging can be settled.

articles.title: Prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening of chromosome abnormalities: A technical standard of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and the College of American Pathologists (CAP).
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
articles.authors: Hilton BA, Bhatt S, Cacheris P et al.
articles.abstract: The American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the College of American Pathologists work group developed this technical standard to address challenges associated with laboratory validation and implementation of prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening. Given that cfDNA screening is the most sensitive and specific screening test available for common fetal aneuploidies, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine recommend that prenatal cfDNA screening be offered to all pregnant persons as a first-tier screening option, regardless of their risk status. Fetal cfDNA in maternal circulation originates from placenta-derived trophoblasts, allowing for the identification of fetuses at increased risk for trisomies 13, 18, and 21 and aneuploidy of sex chromosomes, in addition to recurrent segmental aneuploidies associated with syndromes. Multiple cfDNA analysis techniques exist, and because of the complex nature of this screening, this technical standard aims to promote uniform laboratory practices. This document deals with the technical standards applicable to prenatal cfDNA screening of chromosome abnormalities in maternal plasma. This document serves as a resource to assist clinical laboratories with the validation methods, ongoing monitoring of test quality and performance, and the interpretation and reporting of these results.

articles.title: Spatial genotype-by-environment interaction for growth traits in Italian Podolica beef cattle: a Bayesian random regression study.
articles.authors: Landi V, Lasagna E, Sbarra F et al.
articles.abstract: Genotype-by-environment (G×E) interaction is a key driver of selection efficiency in beef cattle reared across heterogeneous environments, but it has not been quantitatively documented for autochthonous Italian breeds. We investigated spatial G×E for three sequential growth phenotypes, average daily gain before testing (ADGpre), during a 30-day acclimation (ADGacclim) and during the 120-day performance test (ADGtest), in 787 Italian Podolica young bulls from 126 herds in Southern Italy (2001-2022), recorded by the National Association of Italian Beef Cattle Breeders (ANABIC). We derived long-term climatologies of seven biometeorological variables from NASA POWER data across five time windows [late gestation (LG), peri-natal (PERI), neonatal (NEO), mid-suckling (MID), and late-suckling (LATE)] and summarized by window-specific principal components, oriented so that positive values identified hot/dry environments. G×E was tested by likelihood-ratio tests and differences in Akaike's information criterion between nested single-step genomic random-regression animal models (4,382 pedigreed and 1,070 genotyped animals, 21,034 SNPs), analyses were conducted using reaction-norm sire models. The same animal models were fitted in a Bayesian framework to estimate heritability as a function of the environment, h²(ENV). Posterior heritabilities without an environmental covariate were 0.11, 0.26, and 0.31 for ADGpre, ADGacclim and ADGtest. For ADGtest, G×E was not detected in LG and was significant in all four post-natal windows (FDR-corrected p ≤ 0.006), supporting maternal-fetal buffering during gestation. In these windows, heritability of ADGtest was higher in cool/humid (0.43-0.50) than in hot/dry environments (0.24-0.27), with differences whose 95% highest posterior density intervals excluded zero, and additive genetic correlations between environments of 0.48-0.58, suggesting moderate re-ranking of bulls. ADGacclim showed the same direction with less reliable estimates, whereas ADGpre showed the opposite direction, supported only in LG and consistent with confounding by maternal and management effects at the home farm. These results suggest that the genetic determination of Podolica growth varies along the spatial climate gradient of the breed range, with higher expected genetic gain for ADGtest in cool environments, and could lay the foundation for a potential environment-aware genomic evaluation.

articles.title: Global barriers among healthcare professionals in the adoption of imaging for endometriosis diagnosis: Impact on clinical practice.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Fragkoudi A, Sirohi D, Avery JC et al.
articles.abstract: This study aims to explore healthcare professionals' perceptions of barriers and clinical impact influencing the adoption of non-invasive imaging modalities for endometriosis diagnosis. A global cross-sectional survey was distributed through formal and informal FIGO committee networks. Content analysis was used to analyze the qualitative responses from the survey. Of the 360 respondents, 83.3% were gynecologists. In total, seven main topics were identified as barriers, including the lack of training and expertise (n = 173, 48.2%), cost and accessibility (n = 98, 27.3%), professional and institutional challenges (n = 28, 7.8%), diagnostic limitations (n = 15, 4.2%), equipment quality (n = 11, 3.1%), patient barriers (n = 9, 2.5%), and cultural and clinical resistance (n = 4, 1.1%). Respondents felt that adopting non-invasive imaging techniques for endometriosis diagnosis could lead to general impact on clinical practice (n = 118, 32.8%), changes in surgical and medical management (n = 84, 23.3%), shift in diagnostic approach (n = 77, 21.4%), challenges and considerations (n = 32, 9.7%), and improved patient-centered care (n = 25, 6.9%). This study highlights barriers and potential clinical impact of integrating non-invasive imaging into endometriosis diagnosis. Although clinicians recognize its potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce reliance on surgery, widespread adoption is hindered by training gaps, resource limitations, and systemic variability.

articles.title: Providing Donor Insemination in Midwifery Care.
articles.authors: Kali L
articles.abstract: Guidelines for providing donor insemination from American Society for Reproductive Medicine indicate that, for ovulatory individuals with no indications of infertility, components of care can be as simple as providing prepregnancy care, offering education and informed decision-making, performing the intrauterine insemination procedure, and referring as needed. Prepregnancy care is a core competency of midwifery; however donor insemination is typically not included in midwifery education programs. Therefore, it is common to refer individuals, most of whom are same-sex couples or single, to fertility clinics. The fertility clinic model of care is designed for heterosexual couples with clinical infertility. For those without infertility, the routine model of care may increase risk and cost without improving outcomes, it is often not covered by health insurance, and it can be impacted by geographical as well as social barriers. Therefore, a patient-centered, low-tech model of care for donor insemination, broadly available across reproductive care contexts, is needed. This article provides basic considerations for providing donor insemination in midwifery practice. Clinical implications include increased access to evidence-based, culturally appropriate, widely accessible care for families who need donor sperm to conceive.

articles.title: Association of second-trimester maternal serum AFP with umbilical venous blood flow and placental morphometry: a prospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Tavukcuoglu Z, Cicek S, Kapudere B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and umbilical venous Doppler measurements may reflect different aspects of fetoplacental function, but their relationship during the second trimester remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate associations between maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein multiples of the median (AFP MoM) and umbilical venous Doppler parameters, foetal weight percentile, and placental morphometry.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 104 singleton pregnancies examined at 16-22 weeks. Maternal blood sampling and ultrasound/Doppler assessment were performed on the same day. Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlations and partial Spearman correlations adjusted for gestational age. Exploratory comparisons between pregnancies with AFP <2.0 MoM and AFP ≥2.0 MoM were also adjusted for gestational age. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate.
RESULTS: AFP MoM was available for 103 pregnancies and was not associated with foetal weight percentile or umbilical venous Doppler parameters. A weak inverse association with placental length was observed after gestational-age adjustment (partial r = -0.229; nominal p = 0.021), but it did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction (p = 0.193). In the exploratory analysis, the AFP ≥2.0 MoM group had a lower adjusted placental length (difference, -11.63 mm; 95% confidence interval, -21.10 to -2.17; nominal p = 0.017), but this difference was not significant after correction (p = 0.149).
CONCLUSION: Maternal serum AFP MoM was not associated with contemporaneous umbilical venous Doppler parameters or foetal weight percentile. Findings involving placental length were weak and should be considered exploratory.

articles.title: Fertility preservation and reproductive counseling in women with hereditary gynecological cancer predisposition: A scoping review of BRCA1/2 and Lynch syndrome care pathways.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Mondal R, Nandi M
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study maps the evidence on fertility preservation, reproductive counseling, contraception, hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and care pathway integration for women with hereditary gynecological cancer predisposition, principally breast cancer genes 1 and 2 (BRCA1 and BRCA2) and Lynch syndrome, and derives a clinical decision-making framework.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The core search covered seven databases, Google Scholar and 11 gray literature sources from January 2000 to June 2025; a targeted supplementary search of MEDLINE and Embase for contraception and HRT was run to 7 October 2026 in response to peer review. Records from both searches were combined for selection. Two reviewers screened records and charted data, and findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Of 5113 records identified, 4273 were screened after de-duplication, 280 were assessed in full, and 99 sources were included. Evidence came mainly from high-income countries and concerned BRCA1/2 carriers; 12 sources focused on Lynch syndrome. Oocyte and embryo cryopreservation were feasible, but live-birth outcomes were rarely reported. Oral contraception was associated with lower ovarian cancer risk and, in BRCA1 carriers, a modest increase in breast cancer risk with longer use. HRT after premenopausal risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy was not associated with increased breast cancer risk in women without breast cancer yet remained underused. Counseling content and timing were inconsistent, and evidence for Lynch syndrome, low- and middle-income countries, and minority ethnic populations was sparse.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive counseling covering fertility preservation, preimplantation genetic testing, contraception, and HRT should begin at genetic diagnosis and precede irreversible surgery. The proposed 10-step framework requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Mode-specific fetal heart rate signal dropout as a marker of perinatal asphyxia: A multicenter observational study using causal machine learning methods.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Karmakar D, Mendis L, Keenan E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiotocography (CTG) is the standard method for intrapartum fetal monitoring. Modern systems acquire fetal heart rate (FHR) using external Doppler ultrasound (US) or internal fetal scalp electrocardiography (ECG). We evaluated whether mode-specific FHR signal dropout was associated with perinatal asphyxia and whether it should be retained as an informative, mode-aware feature for downstream predictive models.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study using routinely collected clinical and CTG data from Mercy Hospital for Women, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010-2021; Werribee Mercy Hospital, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010-2021; and the Czech CTU-UHB database from University Hospital Brno, for 2010-2012. A total of 46 662 labor episodes at ≥36 weeks' gestation with ≥15 min of interpretable CTG data in the final 60 min before birth were analyzed (32 242 in the model-development cohort, 548 in the Czech validation cohort, and 13 872 in the Australian community validation cohort). The exposure was mode-specific FHR dropout, classified as US low dropout, US high dropout (>30%), ECG low dropout, or ECG high dropout (>30%). The primary outcome was sustained perinatal asphyxia, defined using a Delphi-consensus composite of clinical, biochemical, and neurologic criteria.
RESULTS: In the model-development cohort, 860 cases of perinatal asphyxia occurred (2.67%, 95% CI 2.49%-2.85%). Compared with US low dropout, ECG high dropout was associated with higher risk of asphyxia (inverse probability weighting IPW-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.14, 95% CI 2.20-4.48; targeted maximum likelihood estimation-adjusted OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.21-3.58), corresponding to an absolute risk increase of 2.27% (one additional case per 44 births). Survival analysis supported elevated hazards (HR 4.76, 95% CI 2.98-7.62). External validation supported the direction of association, although estimates varied across cohorts.
CONCLUSION: In retrospective multicenter analyses, high FHR dropout during ECG monitoring was associated with increased perinatal asphyxia risk. These findings support evaluating mode-specific dropout as an informative signal-quality feature in future predictive models. Prospective validation of such models is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (Breus' mole): A nationwide retrospective study in Japan.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Nagao T, Ito Y, Suemitsu T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence, diagnostic features, and perinatal outcomes of massive subchorionic thrombohematoma (MST) in Japan.
METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective study (2018-2023) analyzed confirmed cases of MST, defined as a laminated hematoma with a maximum thickness ≥1 cm. Maternal characteristics, sonographic patterns, and perinatal complications were evaluated.
RESULTS: Of 346 741 deliveries across 87 tertiary perinatal centers, 69 pathologically confirmed MST cases were identified at 27 centers, yielding an incidence of 0.019% (69/346 741). Median maternal age was 33 years and body mass index (BMI) was 21.1. Chronic hypertension was present in 8.7% (6/69). Diagnoses occurred antenatally in 81.2% (56/69) and postpartum in 18.8% (13/69). Ultrasound findings included placentomegaly or a placental mass with variable echogenicity. During follow-up, echogenicity changed in 28% of cases and lesion size in 57%. Perinatal outcomes included induced abortion in 13.0% (9/69), miscarriage before 22 weeks in 5.8% (4/69), stillbirth in 7.2% (5/69), preterm birth in 52.2% (36/69), and term delivery in 21.7% (15/69). Among preterm births, one neonatal death and two infant deaths occurred. After excluding induced abortion and miscarriage before 22 weeks, small-for-gestational-age status was present in 53.6% (30/56) of infants, pre-eclampsia occurred in 16.1% (9/56), and preterm premature rupture of membranes occurred in 23.2% (13/56). Neonatal intensive care unit admission was required for 82.4% (42/51) of live births.
CONCLUSION: MST is a rare but high-risk placental disorder associated with miscarriage, stillbirth, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth, and pre-eclampsia. When MST is suspected antenatally, close maternal and fetal surveillance is warranted.

articles.title: Assessment of fetal head descent and risk of complicated forceps delivery: Role of the suprapubic descent angle.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Hashiramoto S, Takita H, Suzuki Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the suprapubic descent angle (SDA) with conventional measures for discriminating complicated forceps delivery and to explore whether discrepancies between SDA-derived station and conventional fetal station assessments identify higher-risk cases among women undergoing forceps delivery.
METHODS: This prospective cohort included consecutive women with term, singleton, cephalic fetuses in occiput anterior position undergoing forceps delivery at a single tertiary center in Japan during 2025. Before forceps application, SDA, transperineal ultrasound station, angle of progression, head direction, and digital station were assessed. Complicated forceps delivery comprised ≥3 traction attempts, failed forceps requiring cesarean delivery, obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI), blood loss >1500 g, or significant neonatal trauma. Receiver operating characteristic curves assessed discrimination. Internal validation used 2000 participant-level bootstrap samples, repeating regression fitting and Youden cutoff selection. Sensitivity analysis excluding OASI from the composite outcome was also conducted.
RESULTS: Among 118 women, 23 (19.5%) experienced the composite outcome. SDA showed the highest area under the curve (AUC) among individual measures (0.765; 95% confidence interval, 0.641-0.890). The discrepancy between digital station and SDA-derived station had an apparent AUC of 0.838 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.836. Apparent sensitivity and specificity at the data-derived cutoff were 69.6% and 91.6%; corresponding optimism-corrected estimates were 64.8% and 90.5%. Excluding OASI left 12 events; the apparent and optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.880 and 0.879.
CONCLUSIONS: The SDA and the discrepancy between digital station and SDA-derived station showed promising discrimination of complicated forceps delivery. External validation is required before clinical application or recommendation of a cutoff.

articles.title: Women's and healthcare professionals' perspectives on postpartum health research priorities: A qualitative multi-methods analysis.
articles.authors: Thompson C, Moffat M, Möller-Christensen C et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe postpartum period is a critical time for infant and maternal well-being, as well as for public health interventions and research. However, we have limited insight into postpartum research and health priorities from the perspectives of those who deliver and receive postpartum care.ObjectivesThis study set out to capture insights from women who have recently given birth, regarding their perspectives on public health research priorities during the postpartum period, as well as ideas, based on their own experiences, for improving postpartum women's engagement in research. It also explores healthcare professionals' opinions on these topics.DesignThe study uses a qualitative, multi-method analysis of survey data from recently postpartum women and focus group data from healthcare professionals who deliver postpartum care.MethodsA content analysis of survey data was conducted to identify topics commonly cited as research priorities and methods for improving engagement. From those topics, responses from both the survey and focus groups were coded deductively and inductively using codebook thematic analysis to identify themes identified across each topic.ResultsFrom 1391 free-text survey responses, the following three key research priorities were identified: general postpartum aftercare (17.5%, n=244), postpartum mental health (15.5%, n=216), and infant feeding (10.6%, n=147). Seven focus groups (ranging from two to seven participants) and four interviews involving a total of 33 healthcare professionals provided suggestions that aligned with these three priority areas. Thematic analysis identified barriers to research engagement from the perspectives of postpartum women and healthcare providers, e.g., difficulties with face-to-face and online research and a lack of public awareness of research opportunities.ConclusionFor many postpartum women and healthcare professionals, postpartum care and research are neglected areas of the maternity pathway. Ways in which postpartum research engagement can be facilitated, supporting further representation of postpartum women in research, are suggested.

articles.title: Effect of the menstrual cycle on common cold susceptibility and severity: insights from the Pittsburgh cold study 3 dataset.
articles.authors: Hanstock HG, Harrison SE
articles.abstract: Changes in circulating immune parameters over the menstrual cycle have been previously described, but there is limited evidence linking these changes to alterations in common cold susceptibility. Using data from the Pittsburgh Cold Study 3 we investigated whether menstrual cycle phase affects susceptibility to and severity of experimental rhinovirus infection. This secondary analysis included 27 naturally menstruating (NM) women and 17 hormonal contraception (HC) users <40 years. Cycle day and phase were estimated from self-reported data, whereby the first five days of the cycle were labelled as the early follicular (EF) phase, the final 10 days as the luteal (L) phase and remaining days as the transition period (TP). Dominant phase during the 5-day post-inoculation quarantine was taken as the mode for EF (n = 9) and L phases (n = 5) only. Objective cold development did not differ between NM (44%) and HC (35%; p = 0.549), nor between phase on quarantine day 1 within NM (χ2 = 0.89, p = 0.64). However, rhinovirus severity was lower during in L versus EF, represented by peak viral nasal titre (p = 0.003, d = 1.71), total symptom scores (p = 0.01, d = 1.37) and total adjusted mucus weight (p = 0.03, d = 0.86). These observations were supported by linear mixed models for viral load and symptoms during quarantine, which showed blunted viral load and symptom trajectories in L vs. EF. These exploratory, hypothesis generating findings suggest that menstrual cycle phase may influence common cold severity in healthy premenopausal women.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and predictive factors of microsurgical varicocelectomy in men with idiopathic non-obstructive azoospermia or cryptozoospermia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Huang H, Tang S, Zhou H
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate clinical outcomes and non-invasive predictors of ejaculated sperm recovery after microsurgical varicocelectomy in men with idiopathic non-obstructive azoospermia (iNOA) or cryptozoospermia.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of patients with iNOA or cryptozoospermia and varicocele at the First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University from January 2017 to January 2024. All patients were concurrently diagnosed with clinical varicocele via combined Doppler ultrasound and physical examination, and all underwent subinguinal microscopic varicocelectomy. A total of 30 patients were included in the study and followed-up for at least 1 year. Patients were divided into two groups according to their postoperative outcomes. The differences in various parameters between the two groups were compared. Univariate logistic regression was used to calculate the odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (95% CI) for each predictor. The logistic regression model was used to evaluate the association between sperm recovery and clinical factors. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to evaluate the accuracy of predictive factors.
RESULTS: Among the 30 patients who received microsurgical varicocelectomy, motile sperm was detected in postoperative ejaculates in nine patients (30.0%). Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) levels differed significantly between the two groups (P < 0.05). Binary logistic regression analysis of age, mean testicular volume, FSH, LH and testosterone (T) levels showed that only FSH was associated with sperm recovery after surgery, while FSH was negatively associated with sperm recovery (OR = 0.587, 95% CI [0.345-0.998], P = 0.049). There was no statistically significant correlation between the other parameters. ROC analysis showed that preoperative serum FSH level could effectively predict sperm recovery after surgery (area under curve (AUC) = 0.931, 95% CI [0.805-1.000]). The sensitivity of FSH was 95.2%, the specificity was 88.9%, and the cutoff value was 10.86.
CONCLUSIONS: Microscopic varicocelectomy for the treatment of iNOA or cryptozoospermia may benefit a subset of patients, with motile sperm appearing in the non-centrifuged semen postoperatively. Preoperative serum FSH level serves as an independent predictive biomarker for postoperative sperm recovery among men with iNOA. Lower baseline FSH values correlate with a greater probability of…

articles.title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome is Associated with Lower Pregnancy Outcomes Even After Transfer of Morphologically High-Quality Embryos: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Shan H, Wang Y, Zhou P et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether PCOS is independently associated with pregnancy outcomes in ART cycles in which only morphologically high-quality embryos were transferred.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 11,558 patients (3,203 with PCOS, 8,355 controls) who underwent their first IVF/ICSI cycle with fresh embryo transfer (January 2018-December 2021) and subsequent frozen-thawed embryo transfers (January 2018-December 2022) at Peking University Third Hospital. Only cycles with morphologically high-quality embryos were included. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance baseline characteristics between groups. Odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using multivariate logistic regression to assess the association between PCOS and pregnancy outcomes.
RESULTS: In fresh embryo transfer cycles, PCOS patients exhibited lower rates of viable pregnancy (41.4% vs 45.9%) and live birth (34.2% vs 39.1%). After adjustment, the aOR for viable pregnancy was 0.84 (95% CI 0.72-0.98, P=0.024) and for live birth was 0.84 (95% CI 0.72-0.99, P=0.034).
CONCLUSIONS: In fresh embryo transfer cycles, PCOS was associated with lower viable pregnancy and live birth rates, even when only high-quality embryos were used, corresponding to a modest but clinically meaningful reduction in success (adjusted OR 0.84). These findings suggest that factors beyond embryo quality-particularly endometrial function-may contribute to the poorer pregnancy outcomes observed in PCOS patients. Given the retrospective design and the possibility of residual confounding, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further investigation is warranted.

articles.title: Development of a Self-Management Program for Pelvic Organ Prolapse Patients Based on the LEARNS Model: A Delphi Study.
articles.authors: Zhang L, He F, Qiao X et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop a practical, scientifically valid self-management care plan for patients with Pelvic Organ Prolapse (POP) based on the LEARNS model, thereby providing evidence-based guidance for clinical practice and improving patient outcomes.
METHODS: Following comprehensive preliminary work-including an extensive literature review-we initially drafted a self-management plan for POP patients grounded in the LEARNS framework. Subsequently, we conducted two rounds of written expert consultation using the Delphi method, followed by rigorous statistical analysis to validate the proposed indicators.
RESULTS: All 15 questionnaires distributed in each of the two Delphi rounds were returned, yielding a 100% response rate that demonstrated high expert engagement. In the first and second rounds, coefficients of variation ranged from 0.11 to 0.24 and 0 to 0.24, respectively, while expert authority coefficients reached 0.876 and 0.906. Kendall's coefficients of concordance for primary and secondary indicators ranged from 0.158 to 0.215 in the first round and 0.184 to 0.327 in the second round, with all P-values < 0.05 indicating significant consensus. Ultimately, the program comprised six primary indicators and sixty secondary indicators, structured systematically according to the LEARNS model.
CONCLUSION: The self-management program for POP patients, developed based on the LEARNS model, provides a structured framework through six key stages- "Listen, Establish, Adopt, Reinforce, Name, and Strengthen"-to help patients progressively master self-management measures and enhance their self-management capabilities during the hospital stay.

articles.title: Inflammatory biomarkers and immune dysregulation in gestational diabetes mellitus: emerging mechanisms and therapeutic prospects.
articles.authors: Zhang Q, Shu Y, Gao Y
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common pregnancy-related metabolic disorder that increases the risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes and predisposes both mothers and offspring to long-term metabolic disease. Beyond pregnancy-induced insulin resistance, accumulating evidence indicates that GDM is shaped by chronic low-grade inflammation and immune dysregulation at systemic, adipose, and placental levels. Pro-inflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1β, disrupt insulin receptor signaling through NF-κB, JAK/STAT-SOCS3, mTOR, and inflammasome-related pathways, thereby amplifying insulin resistance and β-cell stress. Acute-phase proteins such as high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, pentraxin 3, serum amyloid A, and procalcitonin reflect distinct layers of inflammatory activation and may provide complementary value for early risk stratification, although their diagnostic performance is influenced by gestational timing, maternal adiposity, and population heterogeneity. Alterations in leukocyte profiles, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte/macrophage activation, Treg dysfunction, Th1/Th17 skewing, oxidative stress, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation further reveal the immune imbalance underlying GDM progression. This review synthesizes current evidence on inflammatory biomarkers and immune mechanisms in GDM, emphasizing their predictive potential, mechanistic relevance, and translational implications for biomarker-guided diagnosis, individualized risk assessment, and future anti-inflammatory interventions.

articles.title: Influence of reproductive experience on the antidepressant-like effect of estradiol and prolame in middle-aged rats.
articles.authors: Hernández-Hernández OT, Herrera-Pérez JJ, González-Longoria SM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Reproductive experience may affect the antidepressant action of estrogen replacement therapy (ERT). In the most used animal model of menopause, ovariectomized young adult rats, prolame produces estrogenic and antidepressant-like effects, making it a potential alternative to conventional ERT. A previous study indicated that aging cancels out the antidepressant-like effect of estradiol and reduces the window of antidepressant action of prolame, limiting it to only 3 weeks after ovariectomy. However, the aged females (middle-aged) used in that study were retired breeders, a factor that could explain their antidepressant response to both estrogens. Thus, the present study aimed to determine how reproductive experience influences the antidepressant-like effects of estradiol (30 μg/kg) and prolame (60 μg/kg) in middle-aged Wistar rats.
METHODS: The antidepressant-like effect of both estrogens was evaluated 3 weeks after ovariectomy in nulliparous and multiparous middle-aged rats using the forced swim test. We also assessed the effect of estrogens on uterine weight.
RESULTS: Our results suggest that reproductive experience confers stress resilience. Prolame, but not estradiol, produced an antidepressant-like effect in middle-aged female rats, both multiparous and nulliparous. Treatment with estradiol and prolame increased uterine weight similarly; however, the uterus of nulliparous rats showed greater sensitivity to estrogens.
CONCLUSION: Taken together, the results suggest that prolame might be a viable therapeutic alternative for perimenopausal or postmenopausal women to alleviate depressive symptoms, and a candidate for ERT.

articles.title: HPV E6/E7, O-GlcNAcylation and mitochondrial remodeling in cervical cancer: mechanistic links and translational opportunities.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Tao Y, He H et al.
articles.abstract: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection initiates cervical carcinogenesis, while progression and treatment resistance also involve metabolic adaptation. O-GlcNAcylation is a reversible post-translational modification (PTM) controlled by O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) and O-GlcNAcase (OGA), with UDP-GlcNAc generated by the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP) serving as the donor substrate. This review evaluates evidence linking HPV E6/E7-associated metabolic demand, HBP flux, O-GlcNAcylation, and mitochondrial function. We distinguish observations made under untreated conditions from acute treatment responses, identify whether validated resistant models were used, and examine HPV genotype as a source of heterogeneity. Cervical cancer studies support links between O-GlcNAcylation and pathways involved in growth and survival, but no mitochondrial O-GlcNAcylation site has been causally validated in HPV-positive cervical cancer. We therefore grade evidence by model, temporal context, and causal depth and place the proposed relationships within a broader PTM network. This synthesis separates findings obtained in cervical cancer from mechanisms inferred from other systems and identifies the main gaps limiting biomarker and therapeutic development.

articles.title: Preeclampsia prevention by risk-stratified timed birth: a post-hoc Bayesian analysis of the PREVENT-PE randomised trial.
articles.authors: Wright D, Singh L, Syngelaki A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PREVENT-PE showed that screening for preeclampsia risk at 35-36 weeks followed by risk-stratified timed birth reduced birth with preeclampsia overall. We aimed to assess possible benefit and harm within each risk stratum.
METHODS: This post hoc Bayesian analysis included 4734 participants recruited at King's College Hospital, London, UK, in PREVENT-PE. The parent trial included women aged 16 years or older with a live singleton pregnancy, no major fetal abnormality or preeclampsia, and no conflicting trial participation. We included all 2871 intervention participants and 1863 control participants with stored serum and haemodynamic measurements that allowed retrospective calculation of 35-36-week preeclampsia risk. We estimated incidence proportions, ratios, and differences using independent Beta(1, 1) priors and binomial likelihoods. PREVENT-PE is registered with ISRCTN, ISRCTN41632964.
FINDINGS: PREVENT-PE recruited between May 9, 2023, and June 7, 2024. Birth with preeclampsia occurred in 117/2871 (4.1%; 95% credible interval [CrI] 3.4-4.9) intervention participants and 106/1863 (5.7%; 4.7-6.8) controls; the posterior median incidence ratio was 0.72 (95% CrI 0.56-0.93), with probability of benefit 0.995. Estimates at 39 and 40 weeks favoured intervention and were more precise; estimates at 37 and 38 weeks were much less precise. Heterogeneity of treatment effect was not established. Overall incidence ratios were 1.03 (0.92-1.15) for emergency caesarean and 0.97 (0.76-1.25) for neonatal unit admission for at least 48 h.
INTERPRETATION: The overall PREVENT-PE strategy is supported by randomised evidence, but these post hoc data do not establish different treatment effects across risk strata. The balance of benefit and harm of routine planned birth at 37-38 weeks remains uncertain and needs further evaluation.
FUNDING: Fetal Medicine Foundation.

articles.title: Pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A beyond the first trimester: Predictive value for adverse pregnancy outcomes (Review).
articles.authors: Kavvalou M, Tzanaki I, Velegrakis A et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) is a placentally-derived metalloproteinase that serves a key role in trophoblast invasion and fetal growth through the regulation of insulin-like growth factor bioavailability. Since its introduction into first-trimester aneuploidy screening, low maternal serum PAPP-A concentrations have been consistently associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preeclampsia, preterm birth, fetal growth restriction, low birth weight and stillbirth. Although the clinical importance of reduced first-trimester PAPP-A concentrations is well established, the predictive value of PAPP-A measurements beyond the first trimester, particularly during the second trimester, remains less clearly defined. The present review summarizes the current research regarding the association between maternal serum PAPP-A concentrations throughout pregnancy and adverse obstetric outcomes, with a particular emphasis on second-trimester findings. Available evidence suggests that persistently low maternal serum PAPP-A concentrations from the first into the second trimester are associated with placental dysfunction-related complications. However, despite statistically significant associations, the predictive performance of PAPP-A as a standalone biomarker remains limited. Future prospective studies are required to determine whether incorporating second-trimester PAPP-A into multimarker prediction models can improve risk stratification, clinical decision-making and pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Plasma cell-free DNA-based next-generation sequencing for molecular profiling of diffuse gliomas.
articles.authors: Singh S, Singh J, Bhardwaj S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the utility of plasma-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) using targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) for molecular profiling of diffuse gliomas (DG) by assessing concordance with matched tumor tissue DNA, mutation profiles, variant allele frequencies, therapeutically actionable alterations, and survival associations.
METHODS: A total of 30 DG cases were included, and 10 healthy controls were included. Paired plasma cfDNA and formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor tissue DNA were analyzed using targeted NGS.
RESULTS: Plasma cfDNA concentrations were higher in patients with DG (n = 30) than in healthy controls (P = .0002), though this comparison was limited by the small, unmatched control cohort (n = 10). Targeted sequencing predominantly identified single nucleotide variants (81%). Gene-level concordance between plasma cfDNA and tumor tissue DNA was 90.0%, whereas ≥1 matched variant was identified in 76.7% of cases. Plasma cfDNA detectability and concordance varied across DG subtypes, and multiple therapeutically actionable alterations involving receptor tyrosine kinase, MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and mismatch repair pathways were identified. Higher plasma cfDNA concentrations were associated with shorter survival, whereas cases with matched plasma and tissue variants demonstrated longer survival; however, these associations were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Plasma cfDNA-based liquid biopsy may serve as a minimally invasive approach for molecular profiling of DG, demonstrating high gene-level concordance with tumor tissue DNA and detection of clinically relevant, potentially actionable genomic alterations. Although variant-level concordance and detectability varied across glioma subtypes, these findings support a complementary role for plasma cfDNA analysis in DG. Further prospective studies, including serial sampling and matched leukocyte controls, are needed to improve analytical sensitivity and define its clinical utility.

articles.title: Oocyte lipid damage from maternal ageing marks neurodevelopment in mouse offspring.
articles.authors: Gulzar H, Musson R, Depciuch J et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Is advanced maternal age (AMA) associated with lipid dysregulation in oocytes that correlates with the intergenerational persistence of altered lipid homeostasis and neurodevelopmental pathway signatures in downstream offspring?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Lipid profile alterations characterized in AMA oocytes are associated with distinct lipidomic and spectral variations in the foetal brain and yolk sac, displaying intergenerational persistence that extends up to the fourth generation (F4), independently of the gestational uterine environment.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: AMA is a recognized prenatal risk factor for neurodevelopmental conditions in offspring. However, whether early-life oocyte lipid variations correlate with altered lipid profiles and molecular signatures in the developing brains of subsequent generations remain uncharacterized.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: This controlled animal model study compared oocytes, blastocysts, and foetuses from AMA mice (8-16 months old) to those from young maternal age (YMA, 3-4 months old) controls and featured an embryo transfer (ET) of AMA blastocysts into young surrogates and longitudinal, lineage-specific tracking up to the F4.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Complementary approaches, including liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) proteomics and lipidomics, Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization-Tandem Time-of-Flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF/TOF MS), RNA sequencing, atomic force microscopy, Coherent Anti-Stokes Raman Scattering (CARS) chemical imaging microscopy, Raman and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopies, and histology were conducted on single oocytes, blastocysts, and foetal structures (brain and yolk sac) from AMA and YMA mice. ET was utilized to decouple the oocyte-derived phenotype from the effects of an ageing maternal uterine environment.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: AMA oocytes and preimplantation blastocysts exhibited significant lipid droplet and lipid membrane alterations, a higher relative absorbance of intracellular lipid bands, and altered expression of lipid-regulatory transcripts, corresponding to early embryonic pathway shifts. Following the ET of AMA blastocysts to young surrogates (ET AMA group), distinct lipidomic variations and structural alterations were observed in the F1 yolk sac and foetal brains. Furthermore, these lipid-associated spectral and molecular signatures displayed intergenerational persistence, tracking through the…

articles.title: Performance evaluation of a novel size-based microfluidic platform for rare cell detection in blood and malignant effusions.
articles.authors: Saini VM, Oner E, Cahill C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating tumour cells (CTCs) are promising minimally invasive biomarkers of tumour dissemination and disease biology, but low abundance and phenotypic heterogeneity make them challenging to isolate, particularly in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Physical cell-selection approaches based on size and deformability may facilitate recovery of heterogeneous tumour populations. This study evaluated the performance of the Bio-Rad™ Genesis Cell Isolation System, a microfluidic platform based on these properties, across different tumour phenotypes and liquid biopsy sample types.
METHODS: Recovery capabilities of the Genesis enrichment and enumeration workflows were evaluated using the EpCAM-high H1975 and EpCAM-low H1299 NSCLC cell lines, and a standardised spike-in protocol. Following optimisation, peripheral (Pe) and pulmonary vein (PV) blood from patients with resectable NSCLC, ascites from patients with advanced gynaecological cancers, and matched Pe blood and pleural fluid (PF) from patients with advanced NSCLC were assessed using the enumeration workflow. Tumour cells were identified by immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: High and consistent recovery was observed for both H1975 and H1299 cells, independent of EpCAM expression, with mean recovery of 68.81 ± 10.53% and 65.17 ± 9.53% using enrichment, and 70.05 ± 10.06% and 80.51 ± 5.72% using enumeration, respectively. CTCs were detected in 2/11 Pe blood and 3/4 PV samples from patients with resectable NSCLC. Ascites contained 69-1113 ascites epithelial cells (AECs)/mL, with 89.31-98.21% occurring within clusters. Pleural epithelial cells (PECs) were identified in 3/3 PF samples from advanced NSCLC patients (16.3-132 cells/mL), predominantly as clusters, but were absent from matched Pe blood. Notably, PECs were detected in PF despite negative cytology in one patient.
CONCLUSIONS: The Genesis demonstrated consistent, EpCAM-independent recovery, across NSCLC models and enabled tumour cell and cluster detection across diverse clinical liquid biopsy specimens. Its ability to analyse tumour-rich fluids, including a cytology-negative PF sample, supports further investigation as a versatile and complementary platform for rare cell detection and characterisation.

articles.title: PADI2 facilitates progression and cisplatin resistance of epithelial ovarian cancer via m6A methylation.
articles.authors: Yin X, Zhou J, Zhao S et al.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy resistance is a challenge in the management of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). The regulation of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification has emerged as a potential strategy to overcome this resistance. Peptidyl Arginine Deiminase 2 (PADI2) was found to be upregulated and highly methylated in EOC samples, correlating with a poor prognosis. Downregulation of PADI2 inhibited colony formation, cell proliferation, and cisplatin (cDDP) resistance in EOC cells. METTL3 was identified as the m6A writer of PADI2 mRNA, while YTHDF2 recognized and bound the m6A-methylated PADI2 mRNA, enhancing its translation. This activation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway facilitated cDDP resistance in EOC cells both in vitro and in vivo. Knockdown of METTL3 or YTHDF2 decreased PADI2 mRNA expression and suppressed tumor growth and cDDP resistance. In conclusion, a mechanism was identified whereby m6A-modified PADI2 induces cDDP resistance and EOC progression, providing a potential target for the development of therapeutic strategies for EOC treatment.

articles.title: Household wealth, marriage, and male fertility in sub-Saharan Africa: a cross-sectional comparative study from three countries.
articles.authors: Michael TO
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male fertility remains underexplored in demographic and health research across sub-Saharan Africa, where analytical focus is disproportionately placed on women. Yet men's socioeconomic positions, particularly as reflected by household wealth, and marital union trajectories play critical roles in shaping fertility outcomes and population dynamics.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined how household wealth and marital union status intersect to influence fertility outcomes among men in Nigeria, South Africa, and Uganda.
DESIGN: A cross-sectional, comparative analysis was conducted using harmonized data from multiple rounds of the Integrated Public Use Microdata Series-Demographic and Health Surveys (IPUMS-DHS).
METHODS: The study analysed a pooled weighted sample of 20,587 men aged 15-59 years. Descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and general linear models (GLMs) were used to assess associations between fertility (number of children fathered), household wealth quintiles, marital union status, and their interaction effects.
RESULTS: Mean number of children fathered was highest in Uganda (2.60), followed by Nigeria (2.29), and lowest in South Africa (1.48). Men in multiple marital unions reported substantially higher fertility (mean = 6.10) compared with men in one union (3.44) and never-married men (0.16). Fertility declined across wealth gradients, from 2.57 among the poorest to 1.87 among the richest quintile and increased sharply with age and early union entry. Marital union status was a strong predictor of fertility (Partial η² = 0.082), and the interaction between union status and wealth was statistically significant (p < 0.001). Men in one union within the poorest quintile had 1.47 fewer children (B = -1.465, p < 0.001) compared with men in multiple unions.
CONCLUSION: Male fertility in sub-Saharan Africa is strongly shaped by the intersection of household wealth and marital union status. Without male-inclusive and socioeconomically responsive reproductive health policies, fertility inequalities and demographic pressures are likely to persist across the region.

articles.title: Pelvic organ prolapse: emerging concepts in molecular mechanisms and tissue repair.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: He Z, Tong H, Liu J et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common and progressive pelvic floor disorder associated with pregnancy and vaginal delivery, ageing, obesity, menopause and other conditions that increase or prolong mechanical burden on pelvic supportive tissues. Previous studies have linked POP to extracellular matrix remodeling, oxidative stress, hormonal changes, genetic susceptibility and fibroblast dysfunction. However, these findings are still often presented as separate pathogenic theories or molecular observations, which makes it difficult to explain how mechanical challenge, cellular dysfunction and structural failure are biologically connected during disease progression. In this Review, we propose that POP can be more coherently understood along a mechanics-cell-matrix axis. Within this framework, chronic mechanical loading and impaired adaptive repair are regarded as the disease-setting in which prolapse develops. Mechanotransduction-related pathways are then considered the upstream bridge linking altered tissue mechanics to fibroblast state change. Oxidative stress, autophagy-related disturbance, apoptosis and senescence are further discussed as bridge-amplifier processes that deepen repair failure, whereas extracellular matrix imbalance is viewed as the structural endpoint of declining tissue support. Hormonal status, genetic susceptibility and immune remodeling further influence the course of POP. Fibrosis-associated fibroblast activation may coexist with collagen disorganization, matrix degradation and impaired elastic recoil. This review connects these tissue findings with the distinctive mechanical demands of pelvic support and considers their implications for repair (Tian et al., BJOG, 2024, 131, 1029-1041; Guler and Roovers, Biomolecules, 2022, 12, 94; Wu et al., Front. Med., 2024, 11, 1303044; Ruiz-Zapata et al., Sci. Rep., 2016, 6, 22971).

articles.title: Identification of novel ferroptosis-associated prognostic genes in cervical cancer using bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Chu H, Tang G et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is a common malignant tumor among women worldwide. However, the relationship between CC and ferroptosis remains to be elucidated. The present study screened differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in CC from The Cancer Genome Atlas database and identified DEGs associated with ferroptosis using the FerrDb database. A total of 2,563 DEGs were upregulated and 2,120 DEGs were downregulated which were more notably enriched in the early region 2 binding factor targets and G2M checkpoint. By crossing ferroptosis-driver, ferroptosis-marker and ferroptosis-suppressor genes and DEGs, 80 ferroptosis-associated prognostic genes were identified. In total, 24 potential targeted drugs targeting key genes were predicted, providing a possible basis to predict the prognosis and treatment of CC. The expression levels of stearoyl-CoA desaturase, transferrin receptor (TFRC) and carbonic anhydrase 9 were experimentally validated by PCR, which was consistent with the present bioinformatics analysis. Furthermore, knocking down TFRC inhibited cell proliferation and migration in CC cells in vitro. In conclusion, the present study identified key genes associated with ferroptosis in CC and further research is warranted to explore their underlying mechanisms and potentially become effective clinical prognostic biomarkers in the future.

articles.title: Impact of EXO1(K589E) Genetic Variant on Breast Cancer Risk: Evidence From Bangladesh.
articles.journal: Breast cancer : basic and clinical research
articles.authors: Kabir MM, Rahman MA, Bellah SF et al.
articles.abstract:
