BACKGROUND: Exonuclease 1 (EXO1) is a key nuclease in the DNA mismatch repair (MMR) pathway and is involved in correcting replication errors while maintaining genomic stability. The K589E (rs1047840) single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) of EXO1 has been associated with cancer susceptibility in different populations.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the association between the EXO1 K589E polymorphism and breast cancer risk, as well as its relationship with selected clinicopathological characteristics in Bangladeshi women.
DESIGN: Hospital-based case-control study.
METHODS: The present case-control study included 184 patients with histologically confirmed breast cancer and 200 age-matched cancer-free controls. Genotyping of the EXO1 K589E variant was carried out using polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP) analysis and subsequently confirmed by direct sequencing. The associations between the polymorphism and breast cancer risk were assessed using logistic regression, with odds ratios (ORs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) calculated.
RESULTS: The frequencies of G/G, G/A, and A/A genotypes were 49.5, 41.8, and 8.7% among cases, compared with 69, 27.5, and 3.5% among controls, respectively. Both the heterozygous (G/A) and homozygous variant (A/A) genotypes were significantly associated with elevated breast cancer risk (OR= 2.12, 95% CI= 1.37-3.28, p= 0.0007; OR= 3.46, 95 % CI= 1.37-8.76, p= 0.0086, respectively). The combined variant genotypes (G/A + A/A) conferred a 2.27-fold higher risk (p= 0.0001), and the A allele was also strongly associated with breast cancer predisposition (OR= 2.01, 95% CI= 1.43-2.84, p = 0.0001). The association remained significant under codominant, dominant, recessive, overdominant, and log-additive genetic models. Significant correlations were observed between the variant genotype and menopausal status, body mass index (BMI), and tumor stage.
CONCLUSION: The results indicate that the EXO1 K589E polymorphism is significantly associated with an increased risk of breast cancer in Bangladeshi women and may also be related to key clinicopathological features of the disease.

articles.title: Temporal patterns and adverse pregnancy outcomes of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and gestational diabetes mellitus in Hebei Province, China, 2017-2023: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Liu L, Liu S, Du L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are common complications with overlapping metabolic, vascular, and inflammatory pathways. GDM is associated with fetal overgrowth but may also coexist with fetal growth restriction, particularly when placental vascular dysfunction is present. Regional evidence on recorded temporal patterns and joint maternal-neonatal outcomes remains limited in northern China.
METHODS: We analyzed 264,278 eligible singleton deliveries at ≥28 gestational weeks recorded in the Hebei Obstetric Critical Illness Monitoring System across 31 hospitals from 2017 to 2023. Pregnancies were classified as HDP alone, GDM alone, coexisting HDP and GDM, or unaffected. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, marital status, education, hospital level, gravidity, parity, prenatal examination frequency, and previous cesarean section. Sensitivity analyses examined center composition and hospital-specific random intercepts. Associations were interpreted as non-causal because important metabolic and behavioral covariates were unavailable.
RESULTS: Of eligible deliveries, 11,708 (4.43%) had HDP alone, 18,600 (7.04%) had GDM alone, 2,138 (0.81%) had coexisting HDP-GDM, and 231,832 (87.72%) were unaffected. The recorded prevalence of HDP alone rose from 3.42% in 2017 to 7.60% in 2023. GDM alone and coexisting HDP-GDM peaked in 2021 (13.21 and 1.39%) and then fell abruptly in 2022-2023. HDP alone showed the strongest associations with placental abruption, preterm delivery, small-for-gestational-age birth, and neonatal asphyxia; GDM alone was associated with macrosomia and premature rupture of membranes; the combined group had a mixed risk profile. Estimates for stillbirth and puerperal infection in the combined group were imprecise because only one and two events, respectively, occurred.
CONCLUSION: HDP, GDM, and their coexistence were associated with distinct but overlapping outcome profiles. The abrupt post-2021 decline in recorded GDM persisted in center-composition sensitivity analyses but cannot be interpreted as a confirmed population-level decline because screening and ascertainment differences remain unresolved. The results support cautious, guideline-concordant integrated surveillance rather than study-derived monitoring thresholds.

articles.title: Differentiation of PD, MSA and PSP using clinical data from the prospective AIDP cohort.
articles.authors: Xie T, Vaillancourt DE, Barmpoutis A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiation of clinical features among Parkinson's disease (PD), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy parkinsonism (MSAp) is challenging, with a paucity of comparative studies on comprehensive and overlapped clinical features across three of them.
OBJECTIVE: Comprehensive data from the Automated Imaging Differentiation for Parkinsonism (AIDP) study could offer valuable insights into their diagnostic differentiation among PD, PSP and MSAp.
METHODS: Demographics, comprehensive motor and non-motor features, daily living function and quality of life (QoL) data were prospectively collected from individuals with PD, probable PSP, and probable MSAp at their second AIDP study visit. Clinical diagnoses were confirmed independently by three movement disorder neurologists. Cross-sectional group comparisons were conducted using Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise tests. Median and logistic regression models were applied to assess differences, adjusting for age, sex, disease duration and levodopa equivalent dosage.
RESULTS: Among 168 individuals (90 PD, 56 probable PSP, 22 probable MSAp), overall motor, non-motor, daily living functions and QoL measures were found to be more impaired in MSAp and PSP than PD. Individuals with PSP experienced more oculomotor and cognitive impairment than PD and MSAp. Systolic and diastolic orthostatic blood pressure (BP) drop, orthostatic lightheadedness, and urinary incontinence were associated with MSAp. The presence of systolic orthostatic BP drop was also against the diagnosis of PSP. There were no differences in anxiety, depression, fatigue and constipation across three parkinsonism subtypes.
CONCLUSION: Distinct impairments across PD, PSP, and MSAp in this well-characterized, prospectively collected, comprehensive motor and non-motor dataset provide valuable information for clinical differentiation.

articles.title: Controlled Pt Doping of Silica-Supported Ni Nanoparticles through Surface Organometallic Chemistry on Metals: Applications as Catalysts for Selective Hydrogenation Reactions.
articles.authors: Zuluaga A, Smitkriti S, Vanoye L et al.
articles.abstract: Silica-supported Ni/Pt nanoparticles were synthesized through the selective Pt doping of silica-supported Ni nanoparticles using an original approach that can be considered as a Surface OrganoMetallic Chemistry on Metals (SOMC@M). The targeted bimetallic nanoparticles were obtained via the selective grafting of Pt-(COD)-Me2 onto the surface of the nickel nanoparticles. The resulting solids were fully characterized using several techniques, including infrared spectroscopy, HAADF-STEM, and HRTEM with EDX, confirming the successful incorporation and uniform distribution of Pt centers onto the Ni nanoparticles without side deposition of Pt onto the silica support. These experimental observations were also supported by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations. Further H2 treatments at 500 °C were applied to the Pt-grafted Ni NPs to enable the removal of surface Pt ligands and the diffusion of Pt atoms into the Ni nanoparticles. This SOMC@M methodology was able to secure the precise control over Pt loading and Pt distribution within the Ni NPs, key parameters for enhancing catalytic performance. The resulting materials were found to exhibit remarkable selectivity in both the hydrogenation of 4-nitrostyrene and the semihydrogenation of hex-3-yn-1-ol, demonstrating the potential of SOMC@M as a versatile approach for the design of tunable and efficient bimetallic catalysts.

articles.title: Is polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome a legacy of excessive gestational weight gain? A review of developmental and transgenerational programming.
articles.authors: Ge Z, Wang J, Zhang C
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), is increasingly recognized as a systemic endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, insulin resistance, adipose tissue dysfunction, and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis alterations. Evidence suggests susceptibility may originate before reproductive maturity, potentially during fetal development. This review examines whether excessive gestational weight gain (EGWG) elevates offspring PMOS risk through developmental (intergenerational and, potentially, transgenerational) endocrine programming. EGWG, defined as weight gain above the recommended range for prepregnancy body mass index, may reflect heterogeneous changes in maternal and fetal tissues rather than excess maternal fat accumulation alone. In some pregnancies, EGWG co-occurs with insulin resistance, altered lipid metabolism, inflammation, or adipokine dysregulation. These changes could modify placental nutrient transfer and endocrine signaling, thereby influencing offspring metabolic and reproductive development. However, the pathways linking EGWG specifically to PMOS remain uncertain. Human studies associate maternal metabolic conditions and PMOS with selected offspring outcomes, but provide limited evidence that EGWG independently predicts PMOS in daughters. Experimental models show that prenatal androgen exposure and maternal dietary perturbations can produce PCOS-like reproductive and metabolic traits, supporting the biological plausibility of developmental programming. This review evaluates whether EGWG may act as a marker or modifier of intrauterine conditions relevant to later PMOS susceptibility, while considering prepregnancy adiposity, maternal PMOS, genetic predisposition, and postnatal exposures as alternative or interacting explanations. Prospective mother-daughter cohorts with repeated pregnancy measures, placental profiling, and follow-up through puberty and adulthood are needed to test this hypothesis.

articles.title: Short-term low-dose aspirin attenuates metabolic and endothelial dysfunction, as well as prothrombotic and inflammatory responses, orchestrated by combined oral contraceptive exposure in female rats.
articles.authors: Fabunmi OA, Fabunmi FC, Olaiya AO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherothrombosis is a chronic, multifactorial, and progressive disease responsible for a significant number of deaths globally. It involves interactions between endothelial dysfunction, coagulation activation, platelet activity, and fibrin turnover. Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) may influence these pathways, potentially altering thrombotic risk. The aim was to assess the impact of COC administration on metabolic status and the risk of atherothrombotic disorders in young female rats, beyond evaluating the therapeutic effects of short-term low-dose aspirin (LDA) treatment.
METHODS: Thirty (n = 30) five-week-old female Sprague Dawley rats were given low-dose COC (LCOC) or a high-dose COC (HCOC) for six weeks before treatment with LDA for another four weeks. These rats were compared with those given only LCOC or HCOC without LDA treatment. Whereas rats that received distilled water (as a vehicle) and LDA only served as controls. Body weight and metabolic status were measured weekly. Parameters related to glucose regulation, lipid profiles, inflammatory cytokines, haematological indices, coagulation, and endothelial dysfunction were evaluated at the end of the experiment.
RESULTS: Rats exposed to HCOC exhibited abnormal metabolic and lipid profiles, including impaired glucose tolerance, accompanied by significantly higher insulin (p < 0.001), triglycerides and very low-density lipoprotein levels (p = 0.004) when compared with control groups. The HCOC treatment was also associated with elevated platelet count (p = 0.02) and markers of inflammation and endothelial dysfunction, including IL-6 (p < 0.05), TNF-alpha (p < 0.05), MCP-1 (p < 0.001), TF (p < 0.001), D-dimer (p < 0.001), von Willebrand factor (p < 0.05), and low nitric oxide (p < 0.001) when compared with control groups. Notably, SBP and MAP (p = 0.02) were also significantly higher in these animals, suggesting an increased atherothrombotic risk in response to HCOC when compared to control groups. Interestingly, short-term LDA attenuate atherothrombotic risk by improving metabolic status, alleviating inflammation, and lowering the markers of coagulation and endothelial dysfunction in rats exposed to HCOC.
CONCLUSION: Short-term LDA reduces the risk of atherothrombotic disorders by attenuating biomarker level associated with metabolic dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, proinflammation, and hypercoagulation in female rats exposed to high-dose COC. However, additional experimental…

articles.title: "Hearing the Ovarian Cancer Whisper": A Pipeline Program Introducing Medical Students to Gynecologic Oncology, Focusing on the Diagnosis and Management of Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Slaybe A, Barengo NC, Runowicz CD
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pipeline programs help medical students explore and define future career pathways. The "Hearing the Ovarian Cancer Whisper" (HOW) Dr. Robert C. Knapp Award was created to expose medical students to gynecologic oncology, with emphasis on recognizing, treating, and improving outcomes for patients with ovarian cancer. This study describes and analyzes the characteristics of HOW participants and their eventual residency choices.
METHOD: We conducted a non-concurrent cohort study evaluation using the HOW database of medical students who received the Dr. Robert C. Knapp Medical Student Award and completed the four-week gynecologic oncology elective between 2011 and 2025. Baseline information included medical school, sex, and scholarship year. Follow-up information was obtained through phone, email, or text communication and included residency, fellowship, specialty, and practice location. Of 149 award recipients, 24 were excluded because of missing information, nonresponse, dropout, or pending follow-up, resulting in 125 participants in the primary analytic cohort.
RESULTS: Among the 125 participants included in the primary analysis, 53.6% entered an OBGYN residency and 46.4% another specialty. Three participants subsequently pursued gynecologic oncology fellowship training during the observation period. Most participants were female (84.0%). Florida International University Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine accounted for the largest proportion of participants (44.0%). The distribution of OBGYN residency entry varied by scholarship year, although the overall association did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.080).
CONCLUSION: These findings describe the longitudinal career trajectories of participants in a gynecologic oncology educational program but do not establish that program participation caused or independently influenced specialty choice.

articles.title: Study on copy number variant detection results of 472 fetuses with non-structural ultrasound abnormalities in non-advanced age pregnant women and the correlation with adverse obstetric history.
articles.authors: Lin L, Wu H, Zheng Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate copy number variant (CNV) results in 472 fetuses with non-structural ultrasound abnormalities among pregnant women under 35 years, and analyze the association between adverse obstetric history and pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) CNVs and variants of uncertain significance (VUS).
METHODS: A total of 472 pregnant women aged <35 years with fetal non-structural ultrasound abnormalities were retrospectively enrolled. All participants were divided into groups with or without adverse obstetric history. We summarized the distribution of non-structural ultrasound abnormalities, calculated the overall and stratified detection rates of P/LP CNVs and VUS, and compared differences between groups.
RESULTS: The mean maternal age was 28.73 ± 3.59 years; 22.0% had a positive history. Abnormal ultrasound soft markers accounted for 82.6% of cases, followed by fetal growth restriction (12.3%) and abnormal amniotic fluid volume (4.0%). The overall detection rates were 5.7% for P/LP CNVs and 9.1% for VUS. The highest detection rate of P/LP CNVs was observed in fetuses with abnormal amniotic fluid volume (10.5%), while the highest detection rate of VUS was seen in abnormal ultrasound soft markers (9.2%). The combined detection rate of P/LP and VUS differed among different types of isolated abnormal ultrasound soft markers, with tricuspid regurgitation, persistent right umbilical vein and persistent left superior vena cava showing higher detection rates. No significant differences in overall P/LP CNV and VUS rates were found between women with and without adverse pregnancy history (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Non-advanced age pregnant women with fetal non-structural ultrasound abnormalities carry a non-negligible risk of P/LP CNVs and VUS. Different ultrasound soft markers present distinct CNV detection rates. Adverse obstetric history does not alter the P/LP CNVs and VUS detection rate.

articles.title: Association between Diet Quality Index-International and the odds of polycystic ovary syndrome: a case-control study.
articles.authors: Ramaiah P, Nomani I, Asfour HI et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the most common endocrine-metabolic disorder in women of reproductive age, associated with reproductive, metabolic, and psychological complications. Given the role of lifestyle factors in the pathophysiology of PCOS, dietary patterns have gained attention as modifiable determinants. However, previous studies have mostly focused on specific dietary indices, and the association between a comprehensive diet quality index and PCOS risk remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between a comprehensive diet quality index and the odds of PCOS using a case-control design.
METHOD: This case-control study enrolled 300 women (150 PCOS cases and 150 healthy controls) aged 20-35 years from Umm Al-Qura University Hospital. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated FFQ, and diet quality was measured by the Diet Quality Index-International (DQI-I) (score 0-100). Anthropometrics and physical activity were recorded. Logistic regression, adjusted for age, body mass index, smoking status, dietary fiber intake, physical activity, and total energy intake, was used to evaluate the association between DQI-I tertiles and PCOS risk, with p < 0.05 considered significant.
RESULTS: PCOS cases had higher BMI (29.1 vs. 27.0 kg/m2, p = 0.044) and lower DQI-I scores (68.0 vs. 70.0, p < 0.001) than controls, with lower intakes of fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy (p < 0.05) but higher MUFA and PUFA (p < 0.05). In adjusted logistic regression, the highest DQI-I tertile was associated with 70% lower odds of PCOS versus the lowest tertile (OR = 0.30, 95% CI: 0.16-0.56, P for trend <0.001), while the middle tertile was non-significant (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.47-1.28).
DISCUSSION: Our findings demonstrated that overall diet quality, as measured by the DQI-I, was significantly lower among women with PCOS compared to healthy controls. This reduced diet quality remained independently and inversely associated with the odds of PCOS after adjustment for age, BMI, smoking, fiber, physical activity, and energy intake. Notably, women in the highest DQI-I tertile had approximately 70% lower odds of PCOS compared with those in the lowest tertile, an association that is both statistically robust and clinically meaningful.

articles.title: AGE is just a Number: MARC-Modified Microflare GnRH Agonist Protocol Shows Equal Effectiveness Across POSEIDON Groups 3 and 4.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology of India
articles.authors: Adiga P, Mundkur A, Poojari VG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor ovarian reserve is a challenge in IVF cycles. How to get the optimum response for a given stimulation protocol is always a question that needs to be answered.
PURPOSE OF THE STUDY: This study investigates the efficacy of the MARC-modified microflare-up Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone (GnRH) agonist protocol in POSEIDON group 3 and group 4, focusing on its impact on various indices of ovarian response and pregnancy outcomes. Despite the challenges presented by poor ovarian reserve (POR), our research evaluates whether this protocol can deliver consistent results irrespective of age, antral follicle count (AFC), or anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels, Using metrics such as the Follicular Output Rate (FORT), Follicle-to-Oocyte Index (FOI), and Oocyte Sensitivity Index (OSI), we compared outcomes between the two groups.
METHODS: Women with an Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) ≤ 1.5 ng/mL or an Antral Follicle Count (AFC) ≤ 5 were recruited for the MARC-modified microflare protocol. Modification of the standard micro flare protocol was by avoiding the pre-treatment COC. Eight patients were excluded from the analysis due to cycle cancellation (11.7%) resulting from nonresponse to stimulation. The remaining 60 patients were included for evaluation and grouped into four according to POSEIDON criteria.
RESULTS: Eight of the 68 women enrolled were excluded due to cycle cancellation, resulting in a final analysis of 60 women, with 28 in Group A (POSEIDON 3) and 32 in Group B (POSEIDON 4).FORT, FOI, and OSI in both groups were comparable, suggesting the effectiveness of the stimulation protocol. Importantly, the study highlights that age is not a limiting factor in the effectiveness of the MARC-modified microflare protocol. The protocol consistently facilitated a favorable ovarian response regardless of age, AFC, or AMH levels. Key measures, including biochemical and clinical pregnancy rates, showed no significant differences, demonstrating the protocol's uniform effectiveness.
CONCLUSION: MARC-modified microflare-up GnRH agonist protocol proves to be an effective and versatile option for ovarian stimulation in POR patients. Delivering consistent outcomes across varied patient profiles offers a robust solution for managing POR, reinforcing the notion that age is merely a number in the context of ovarian stimulation efficacy in POSEIDON groups 3 and 4.

articles.title: Appraisal of clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements on aspirin in pregnancy: a systematic review using the AGREE II instrument.
articles.authors: Hu Y, Chen D, Ni J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recommendations regarding the use of aspirin in obstetrics vary across clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements of differing quality. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the quality of these documents, with particular focus on the recommended daily dosage, timing of initiation, and cessation of aspirin in the obstetric setting. This study employed a systematic review and quality appraisal approach using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation (AGREE) II methodology.
METHODS: The study included the most recent versions of all international and national/regional clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements on aspirin use in pregnancy, published in English or Chinese. Data were retrieved from PubMed (11 April 2025), three Chinese academic databases (the Chinese Medical Association Database, Wanfang Data and China National Knowledge Infrastructure) and four guideline databases (11 April 2025). Two reviewers independently screened the searched items and extracted data. Four reviewers independently scored documents using AGREE II. Recommendations from all documents were tabulated and visualized using a color-coded grid.
RESULTS: A total of 32 documents were include, encompassing six obstetric conditions: Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS), Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR), advanced maternal age, pregnancy loss, stillbirth and hypertension/pre-eclampsia. The included documents demonstrated strong performance in the domains of scope and purpose (median score: 89.67%, inter-quartile range [IQR] 61.11%-98.61%) and clarity of presentation (median 87.93%, IQR 50%-100%). The editorial independence domain also received relatively high score (median 73.59%, IQR 0%-100%). However, performance was lower in the domain of applicability (median 45.08%, IQR 0%-89.58%). Although aspirin 75-100 mg daily represents the most commonly recommended dosage, a broad range of dosing recommendations exists across most clinical scenarios. However, considerable controversy existed regarding the optimal timing of discontinuation, particularly in cases of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy/pre-eclampsia.
CONCLUSION: Guidelines and consensus statements, which were generally of relatively high quality, demonstrated that most documents support the use of aspirin for specific obstetric complications. Given these substantial variations in dosage ranges, treatment timing, and combination therapy recommendations, developing standardized,…

articles.title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of Treatment with Botulinum Toxin A Compared to Drug Therapy in Patients with Urge Incontinence: A Clinical Trial Study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology of India
articles.authors: Ghanbari Z, Eftekhar T, Deldar M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urge incontinence is one of the disorders that affect many individuals. Treatment of patients is based on drug strategies; however, complete recovery has not been established. The use of botulinum toxin A is an important therapeutic approach that is used alongside other treatments today; however, few studies have been conducted.
METHODS: Sixty patients participated in this study. Patients are divided into three groups of 20 people. One group was treated with Botox (200 IU), the second with Botox (300 IU), and the third with antimuscarinic drugs. Patients were followed up for 6 months. At the end of 6 months of treatment, the results were evaluated by visiting the patient or calling them and asking the questions of the ICIQ-OAB questionnaire.
RESULTS: The percentage of changes in the number of urinations at night in the second group was higher compared to the other two groups; it was statistically significant (p = 0.018). Based on the results, it was shown that no complications were observed in the patients of the both groups. On the contrary, it was shown that in the second group, complications were observed in 4 patients (20%) (p = 0.03).
CONCLUSION: In general, it can be said that treatment with Botox (200 IU) can have a better effect on improving the frequency of urination compared to the other two types of treatment.

articles.title: An Observational Study to Determine the Maternal and Fetal Outcomes in Multifetal Pregnancies at an Urban Tertiary Care Centre.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology of India
articles.authors: Kampoowale S, Changede P, Chavan N et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Multifetal pregnancy is a high-risk pregnancy and a challenge for obstetricians globally. This observational study aims to determine the demographic data of mothers with multifetal pregnancies, the outcomes during the antenatal period, labor and postnatal period, the fetal complications in multifetal pregnancies, and the mode of delivery in these cases.
METHODOLOGY: A prospective observational, monocentric study was done at Lokmanya Tilak Municipal Medical College and General Hospital, Mumbai.104 patients with multifetal pregnancy who had either aborted or delivered in our tertiary care centre during the study period of 18 months (all patients with multifetal pregnancy-registered/ unregistered/ referred and irrespective of the pregnancy outcome [abortus, livebirth or stillbirth] were included). Demographic factors, Obstetric history and treatment history were recorded; gestational age at delivery, and high-risk factors were noted. Mode of delivery and indication of LSCS were noted from the labor case records. Details of the maternal and neonatal complications in the antenatal period or during the hospital stay were obtained from the indoor papers.
RESULTS: Among the 104 cases, 97 (93.26%) were spontaneous conception, 2 cases (1.94%) were through IVF, 4 cases (3.8%) with ovulation induction and 1 case (1%) was through ovulation induction and intrauterine insemination (OV + IUI). The study included 103 twins and 1 (0.96%) triplet pregnancy. Out of the twin gestations, 94 cases (90.39%) were dichorionic diamniotic, 7 cases (6.73%) were monochorionic diamniotic twins, 2 cases (1.92%) were monochorionic monoamniotic, and no case of conjoined twins was found. Preterm delivery was observed in 82 patients (78.8%) while 22 cases (21.2%) were term at delivery. Maximum cases(78 cases) delivered between 28 and 37 weeks (75%) of gestation. 11 cases (10.6%) delivered < 28 weeks of gestation while only 15 cases (14.4%) delivered > 37 weeks gestation at the time of delivery. Mode of delivery was emergency LSCS in 58 cases (55.85%), vaginal delivery for both babies in 35 cases (33.65%), elective LSCS in 4 cases (3.8%), and instrumental delivery in 2 cases (1.9%). Emergency LSCS for the second twin was done in 5 cases (4.80%). Most common indication of Cesarean section in our study was fetal distress. The most common presentation in our study was cephalic- cephalic 63 (60.6%) followed by cephalic breech 19 (18.3%). This study also included the maternal…

articles.title: A leakage-aware and interpretable machine learning framework for ovarian cancer prediction using the PLCO screening dataset.
articles.authors: M SLJ, P S
articles.abstract: Early diagnosis of ovarian cancer is a significant clinical problem, and this is mainly because there are no strongly sensitive early-detection biomarkers, and the standard screening parameters like CA-125 blood tests and transvaginal ultrasounds are very insensitive in making a diagnosis. This paper presents a machine learning architecture, which is organized and interpretable based on the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening data to enhance the risk stratification of ovarian cancer. The original analytical cohort comprised 78,209 participants, including 518 ovarian cancer cases. To select 20 informative pre-diagnostic predictors in a high dimensional feature space, a comprehensive feature selection pipeline with ANOVA (f classifier), Chi-square, Random Forest importance, and XGBoost importance were used. Several classification algorithms were tested and the boosting based methods proved to have a good predictive value. A stacking ensemble of K-Nearest Neighbors and AdaBoost was the highest performing overall (accuracy: 0.7644), and a test-set AUROC of 0.8399, with additional evaluation using sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, balanced accuracy, MCC, and PR-AUC. SHAP analysis and permutation importance were used to provide model interpretability and consistently regarded questionnaire-based screening variables, age, and CA-125 attributes as the strongest ones. The suggested framework offers a methodologically rigorous and transparent method of assessment of population level ovarian cancer risk, providing a foundation for future research toward a clinically useful ovarian cancer screening decision-support system, pending external validation.

articles.title: Information rather than architecture: cross-learner attribution and clinician-model complementarity in CIN2+ risk prediction for women referred for colposcopy.
articles.authors: Wu Y, Wang A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep tabular models, including self-supervised and pretrained foundation models, are increasingly proposed for clinical risk prediction, but their value over conventional learners is rarely tested against matched controls, and their role relative to clinician judgement is seldom examined.
METHODS: In a retrospective single-centre cohort of 879 women referred for colposcopy (242 CIN2+, 27.5%), 15 routinely recorded variables, including a clinician image-based assessment documented before histopathology, were modelled with ten model families under one fixed protocol (single fold assignment and seed, no tuning). Discrimination was compared by paired DeLong tests and bootstrap. Two analyses were pre-specified: exact Shapley attribution of discrimination to five clinical groups of variables in every model family, and a complementarity analysis asking whether routine data identify CIN2+ among women judged negative by the clinician. Frozen models were evaluated in a 103-case two-centre external cohort.
RESULTS: Out-of-fold AUROC ranged from 0.726 to 0.761. No model outperformed logistic regression (AUROC 0.757; CatBoost -0.002, p = 0.860; TabPFN +0.004, p = 0.554), and three matched ablations of a self-supervised tabular Transformer were null (all p ≥ 0.096). Removing the clinician assessment lowered AUROC in all ten families (by 0.041 to 0.072; all p ≤ 0.008). Shapley attribution ranked five variable groups identically in every family (Kendall's W = 1.00; permutation p < 0.001): the clinician assessment (39% to 50% of discrimination above chance), then cytology, HPV testing, colposcopic findings and demographic history. The clinician assessment alone had sensitivity 0.504 and specificity 0.882; 49.6% of CIN2+ occurred in clinician-negative women. Re-reviewing the 20% of clinician-negative women with the highest model risk identified 34.2% (95% CI 25.7-42.7%) of the missed CIN2+, against 20% expected at random, raising pathway sensitivity to 0.674 at specificity 0.733. External AUROC of logistic regression was 0.710.
CONCLUSIONS: On routine structured data from a colposcopy-referral population, and under a common protocol, model architecture did not determine performance; predictor information did. Retrospectively, routine data complemented the clinician modestly in clinician-negative women, rather than replacing clinical judgement. Claims that complex architectures improve clinical tabular prediction should be tested against logistic regression with…

articles.title: Association of pre-treatment sleep characteristics with reproductive outcomes among women undergoing assisted reproductive technology: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Li Y, Chen S, Xu P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations between pre-treatment sleep characteristics and reproductive outcomes in infertile women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART) and to explore whether embryo development may represent a potential pathway linking sleep characteristics with cumulative live birth.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, pre-treatment sleep characteristics before ovarian stimulation were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The primary outcome was cumulative live birth, while secondary outcomes included embryo developmental parameters. Associations with ovarian reserve indicators were also evaluated. Multivariable regression, restricted cubic spline, exploratory mediation, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: In an analysis of 11,090 included oocyte retrieval cycles, women with very poor sleep quality had a lower 1-year cumulative live birth rate (CLBR) (RR = 0.927, 95% CI: 0.881-0.977, P = 0.004). Sleep duration of 5 to less than 6 hours significantly reduced both 1-year (RR = 0.788, 95% CI: 0.737-0.843, P < 0.001) and 2-year CLBR (RR = 0.798, 95% CI: 0.748-0.852, P < 0.001). Furthermore, severe impairment in sleep efficiency, severe sleep disturbances, and severe daytime dysfunction were associated with lower CLBRs (P < 0.05). Secondary outcomes showed that poor sleep quality, short sleep duration of less than 5 hours, and use of sleeping medication 1-2 times per week correlated with lower available embryo rates (P < 0.05). Very bad subjective sleep quality was associated with an increased slow-cleaving embryo rate and high fragmentation rate (P < 0.05). Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations between sleep characteristics and ovarian reserve indicators. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that embryo development may partially explain the associations of very bad subjective sleep quality and mild impairment in sleep latency with CLBRs.
CONCLUSION: Poor sleep quality was associated with lower cumulative live birth outcomes and poorer cleavage-stage embryo development among women undergoing ART. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that embryo development may partially explain the observed associations between sleep characteristics and CLBRs. As a potentially modifiable factor, sleep characteristics may represent an important consideration in optimizing reproductive care, although further prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Hierarchical detection of neonatal brain pathologies using a two-stage deep learning framework from magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.authors: Ampiah CA, Malalanirainy T, Crimi A
articles.abstract: Automated neonatal brain pathology detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) faces a dual challenge: preterm birth produces a characteristic but confounding pattern of delayed myelination that can obscure concurrent structural abnormalities, while conditions such as hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) and hydrocephalus demand timely identification in their own right. Existing frameworks typically address these clinical questions in isolation or collapse them into a single flat classifier, discarding the natural clinical decision hierarchy. This study presents a hierarchical two-stage deep learning pipeline that emulates clinical reasoning from paired T1-weighted and T2-weighted neonatal brain MRI. An initial Stage-1 deploys a brain-age gap classifier, built on a 3-D ResNet-18 regressor followed by a gap-thresholded binary decision intended to screen for myelination delay. Then the same subjects advance to a Stage-2, where a second 3-D ResNet-18, trained for structural pathology, performs three-class classification: normal, HIE, and hydrocephalus. Experiments demonstrate that a regression from MRI scan to age with an R 2 of 0.941 at Stage-1, the proposed hierarchical pipeline achieves a Stage-2 area under the curve (AUC) of 0.919 ± 0.024.

articles.title: Preparedness of undergraduate health students to provide women-specific epilepsy care: knowledge gaps and stigmatizing attitudes in Saudi Arabia.
articles.authors: Alzahrani F, Alharbi Y, Almuzaini Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with epilepsy have distinct reproductive, clinical, and psychosocial healthcare needs that require women-specific care. This study assessed the preparedness of undergraduate health students by examining their knowledge, attitudes, and stigmatizing beliefs.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 339 undergraduate health students at Taibah University, Saudi Arabia, using a structured self-administered questionnaire. Multiple linear regression examined the factors associated with total knowledge score, while the ≥60% knowledge benchmark was retained for descriptive and exploratory sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 7.37 ± 2.96 out of 16 (46.1%), and 23.6% met the ≥60% benchmark. Knowledge gaps were most evident in reproductive health, hormonal influences, fertility, antiseizure medication safety, and contraceptive counseling topics. Attitudes were generally supportive, although stigma persisted regarding marriage, parenting, and close relationships. Male gender and earlier academic year were associated with lower adjusted knowledge scores, whereas field of study, epilepsy history, formal education, and recent training were not significantly associated with knowledge.
CONCLUSION: Undergraduate health students demonstrated substantial knowledge gaps in women-specific epilepsy care, despite generally supportive attitudes. Reviewing curricular coverage and addressing identified gaps in reproductive health, medication safety, contraception, pregnancy-related care, and stigma may enhance preparedness for evidence-based, patient-centered care. The threshold-based logistic sensitivity analysis should be considered exploratory because of the low events-per-parameter ratio.

articles.title: Analysis of Sepsis-Related Maternal Near-Miss Morbidity in a Tertiary Care Hospital: a Prospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology of India
articles.authors: Arora A, Thakur G, Jain V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal sepsis is the third most frequent cause of direct maternal deaths. Failure to recognize sepsis early is a significant cause of preventable morbidity and mortality.
AIM: Our study aimed to assess the prevalence, clinical spectrum and residual morbidity amongst women experiencing near-miss morbidity due to sepsis.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted from December 2018 to November 2020 at PGIMER, Chandigarh, a tertiary care hospital in north India after ethical approval.Critically ill pregnant, labouring, post-partum/post-abortal women within 42 days, admitted to index institution premises with suspected or diagnosed sepsis fulfilling near-miss criteria according to GOI and/or WHO, were included. Data were collected by medical doctors who were hired for the research study. The clinical presentation, initial management, hospital course and residual morbidity at the time of discharge were noted.
RESULTS: Sepsis was the primary cause of near-miss morbidity in 54 women out of the total 426 near-miss cases, accounting to 12.7%. Out of these, 46 (85.2%) cases were referred from peripheral health facilities. There were 13 (24.1%) antenatal, 31 (57.4%) post-partum and 10 (18.5%) in post-abortion period. Direct obstetric sepsis was identified in 33 (61.1%), indirect in 8 (14.8%), while focus remained unidentified in 13 (24.1%). Peritonitis was the most common diagnosis at admission in 27 (50%). Immediate surgical intervention was required in 30 (55%) of the cases. Around 69% of cases had residual morbidity at discharge.
CONCLUSION: Index study shows that direct obstetrical sepsis is more common amongst post-partum women and medical comorbidities are importantly associated with sepsis.

articles.title: From evidence to impact: purposeful use of implementation science theories, models, and frameworks in genomics and precision health.
articles.authors: Fariman S, Best S, Taylor N et al.
articles.abstract: A growing number of genomics precision health applications are supported by robust evidence, yet their integration into routine clinical and population health practice remains slow, uneven, and inequitable. This article demonstrates how implementation science (IS) theories, models, and frameworks (TMFs) can support the translation of evidence-based genomics applications by presenting three cases from pediatric precision oncology, reproductive genetic carrier screening, and population genomic screening for hereditary conditions. Across the three cases, IS TMFs were purposefully selected, adapted, combined, or supplemented to fit the implementation context, core complexities, and the conceptual work required, and were revisited as implementation evolved. We argue that this purposeful approach can provide an operational backbone for integrating precision health innovations into real-world systems of care and help transform individual implementation efforts into transferable knowledge.

articles.title: Age-specific HPV genotype distribution and associations with cervical lesions and vaginal microecological status in Northeast China: a retrospective study of 73,828 individuals.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: He Y, Pan Y, Sheng Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is a major etiological factor in cervical carcinogenesis. HPV prevalence and genotype distribution show substantial geographic heterogeneity across China, highlighting the need for region-specific epidemiological data. This study characterized age-specific HPV infection and genotype patterns in Northeast China and further examined their associations with cervical pathology and vaginal microecological status.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed HPV genotyping data from 73,828 individuals tested between 2020 and 2024. Histopathological data were available for 8,755 women, and vaginal microecological assessments were available for 2,428 women. Age-related differences, HPV genotype distributions, infection patterns, and their associations with cervical pathology and vaginal microecological categories were evaluated using nonparametric and χ² tests.
RESULTS: Overall HPV positivity was 20.83% (15,376/73,828) and showed a bimodal age distribution, with the highest prevalence among participants aged < 25 years (34.44%) and a second peak at 60-65 years (25.90%). HPV16, HPV52, and HPV58 were the three most frequently detected genotypes. Single HR-HPV infection differed significantly across cervical histopathological categories and was most frequent in cervical cancer (57.81%, P < 0.001). HPV positivity also differed across vaginal microecological categories (P < 0.001), with the highest rate observed in the bacterial vaginosis group (32.66%); however, no individual HPV genotype remained significantly associated with microecological category after FDR correction.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide regional epidemiological evidence for HPV surveillance and cervical cancer prevention planning and support further prospective investigation of the relationship between vaginal microecological alterations and HPV infection.

articles.title: The impact of post-thaw culture time on clinical outcomes of embryos at different developmental stages.
articles.authors: Jiang M, Zou Y, Liu Z
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aims to investigate the effect of post-thaw embryo culture time on the clinical outcomes of embryos at different developmental stages.
METHODS: This study adopted a retrospective analysis design, in which frozen embryo transfer cycles were divided into four subgroups: single cleavage-stage embryo transfer cycles, double cleavage-stage embryo transfer cycles, single blastocyst transfer cycles, and double blastocyst transfer cycles. Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to evaluate the effect of post-thaw culture time on live birth rate, gestational age at birth, birth weight, and body length at birth within each subgroup. The live birth rate was defined as the primary outcome.
RESULTS: In double cleavage-stage embryo transfer cycles (n=936), the <4h post-thaw embryo culture group had a significantly lower live birth rate (45.1%) than the ≥4h group (57.2%), with P = 0.001. After adjusting for confounding factors in the multivariable regression model, post-thaw culture time remained significantly associated with live birth rate (P = 0.008), and the adjusted OR (95% CI) was 1.524 (1.117-2.081). In single blastocyst transfer cycles (n=688), the <4h post-thaw embryo culture group had a significantly higher live birth rate (47.2%) compared with the ≥4h group (34.3%), with P = 0.017. After adjusting for confounding factors, post-thaw culture time still maintained a significant association with live birth rate (P = 0.003), and the adjusted OR (95% CI) was 0.493 (0.308-0.788). A statistically significant interaction was detected (adjusted interaction OR = 0.424, 95%CI 0.272-0.663, P<0.001), confirming that the effect of post-thaw culture time on live birth rate differs between cleavage-stage and blastocyst-stage embryos.
CONCLUSION: Post-thaw culture time significantly impacts live birth rates in both double cleavage-stage embryo transfer cycles and single blastocyst transfer cycles, and the effect varies according to the embryonic developmental stage.

articles.title: A transparent 13-gene transcriptomic candidate signature for cervical neoplastic spectrum across GEO cohorts.
articles.authors: Zhao P, Lu H
articles.abstract: Transcriptomic classifiers can prioritize molecular signals associated with cervical neoplastic lesions, but high-dimensional feature selection is vulnerable to overfitting, information leakage, and cohort-selection bias. We performed a retrospective computational reanalysis of six Gene Expression Omnibus microarray cohorts retained from the original project, with cervical tissue or epithelial expression profiles, extractable binary labels, and harmonizable gene annotation. GSE63514, GSE67522, and GSE9750 formed the development cohort (n = 200; 127 case samples and 73 control samples), whereas GSE64217, GSE6791, and GSE7803 were reserved for external evaluation. A glmBoost-derived 13-gene panel was coupled to a gradient boosting machine (GBM). The supervised stages of internal evaluation used 10 repeats of stratified five-fold nested cross-validation; scaling, feature selection, and GBM tuning were repeated within every outer-training split. The inherited expression matrix had undergone cohort-wide ComBat adjustment before this reconstruction, so the analysis does not establish fully end-to-end foldwise preprocessing validation. The aggregated out-of-fold AUC for the reconstructed selection pipeline was 0.9161 (95% CI 0.8731-0.9591). External discrimination was high but cohort dependent; the nominal AUC of 1.0000 in the six-sample GSE64217 cohort was too imprecise to support a claim of perfect performance. Five genes were selected in all 50 outer models. In a post hoc fixed-panel sensitivity analysis, the 13-gene and five-gene panels had similar repeated-CV out-of-fold AUCs (0.924 and 0.931; paired DeLong P = 0.390). The signature is therefore a candidate computational model for a heterogeneous cervical neoplastic spectrum. It does not establish biological validation, comparative clinical utility, or a deployable single-patient assay.

articles.title: The crosstalk between ferroptosis and cellular senescence in gestational diabetes mellitus: from iron dyshomeostasis to trophoblast dysfunction.
articles.authors: Li M, Zhao W, Jiang L et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) comprises heterogeneous placental phenotypes that include fetal overgrowth, large-for-gestational-age birth, and fetal growth restriction (FGR). We propose a testable endotype model in which maternal hyperglycemia, advanced glycation end products, diabetic dyslipidemia, altered polyunsaturated fatty-acid delivery, gestational iron exposure, and the physiologic fall in hepcidin converge on a redox-stressed trophoblast microenvironment. In proliferative cytotrophoblasts and extravillous trophoblasts, the relative reserve of GPX4 and FSP1/CoQ10, ACSL4-dependent PUFA-phospholipid loading, proliferative status, and insult intensity and duration are predicted to determine whether cells undergo ferroptosis, enter senescence, or occupy an intermediate state. We further propose an asymmetric crosstalk model: senescent trophoblasts are relatively ferroptosis-resistant, retain iron, and act in trans through SASP factors, reactive oxygen species, and oxidized lipids on ferroptosis-susceptible neighboring cells. The model predicts a gestational-age-dependent window in which physiologic senescence accumulates and its paracrine effects become injurious. Ferrostatin-1 or liproxstatin-1 should rescue lipid-peroxidation-driven death in susceptible cells without reversing senescence in iron-retaining cells. The model is GDM-specific in its initiating inputs and gestational context, but the reciprocal links remain hypotheses rather than established facts. It predicts that an injury-dominant placental endotype will show spatially adjacent iron-retaining senescence-like cells and lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, impaired nutrient transport, and FGR, whereas compensatory transport and villous expansion may produce large-for-gestational-age phenotypes in other GDM placentas. We outline experiments that could support or falsify this model and define pregnancy-specific safety constraints for therapeutic testing.

articles.title: Culture-Confirmed Significant Bacteriuria and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Patterns Among Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Care at a District Hospital in Ghana.
articles.authors: Ofosu M, Domar VE, Sam Barko P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary tract infections are common during pregnancy and may be associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Antimicrobial resistance can complicate treatment and varies across healthcare settings. This study assessed the prevalence of culture-confirmed significant bacteriuria and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Father Thomas Rooney Catholic Hospital, Ghana.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 200 pregnant women. Clean-catch midstream urine samples were cultured using standard microbiological procedures, with significant bacteriuria defined as ≥ 105 CFU/mL of a single organism. Isolates were identified using conventional biochemical methods, and susceptibility was determined by Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion according to CLSI 2024 guidelines. Associations with culture positivity were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, followed by binary logistic regression restricted to two predictors. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported.
RESULTS: Culture-confirmed significant bacteriuria was identified in 23/200 participants (11.5%). Six species were isolated, with Escherichia coli predominant (8/23, 34.8%), followed by Staphylococcus aureus (5/23, 21.7%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (4/23, 17.4%), Proteus mirabilis (3/23, 13.0%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (2/23, 8.7%), and Proteus vulgaris (1/23, 4.3%). Two P. aeruginosa isolates were excluded from susceptibility analysis, leaving 21 isolates. Among 16 gram-negative isolates, susceptibility to amikacin and gentamicin was 81.3% each, ampicillin susceptibility was 31.3% with resistance in 43.8%, and ceftriaxone resistance was 62.5%. Tight underwear use (AOR = 6.56; 95% CI: 2.36-18.22; p < 0.001) and douching or deodorant use (AOR = 8.50; 95% CI: 2.83-25.54; p < 0.001) were associated with culture positivity.
CONCLUSION: Significant bacteriuria was common in this antenatal population, with retained aminoglycoside activity but low ampicillin susceptibility and substantial ceftriaxone resistance. These findings support considering urine culture at the first antenatal visit where laboratory capacity permits, establishing facility-level antibiograms, and including genital hygiene counseling in antenatal education. Larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Biologic and immunologic characteristics of ovarian cancers that are associated with p53 autoantibodies.
articles.authors: Qiu C, Høgdall C, Yang H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoantibodies (AAbs) against p53 develop in a fraction of patients with ovarian cancer, but the mechanisms underlying their development remain unknown. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC) is the most prevalent and lethal histotype, and nearly all HGSCs exhibit TP53 mutations, although only 20%-30% evoke anti-p53 AAbs.
METHODS: Serum and tissue samples were analyzed from 174 patients with ovarian cancer who were included in the Danish Pelvic Mass/Gynecologic Ovarian Vulva Endometrial and Cervix Cancer study.
RESULTS: Elevated levels of immunoglobulin G anti-p53 AAbs were detected in 30 patients, all with HGSC. Among the patients who had HGSC, elevated levels of anti-p53 AAbs were identified in 17% of those with early stage (I-II) disease and in 23% of those with late stage (III + IV) disease. Ninety-seven percent of samples with elevated anti-p53 AAbs had TP53 mutations, 93% had mutations restricted to the DNA-binding domain, and 89% had overexpression of p53 protein in tissue sections. Neither anti-p53 AAb levels nor p53 protein expression was associated with survival. Infiltration of CD20-positive/CD23-positive B cells and CD8-positive T cells correlated with anti-p53 AAbs, consistent with heightened immune activation. Increased immunoglobulin production appeared to be specific for p53 in that no correlation was observed between anti-p53 AAbs and human epididymis protein 4 antigen-AAb complexes. Absorption experiments have suggested that anti-p53 AAbs associated with HGSC are directed against epitopes on wild-type p53 protein. TP53 mutation and overexpression of p53 appear to be necessary, but not sufficient, for the induction of anti-p53 AAbs.
CONCLUSIONS: Anti-p53 AAbs identify a distinct subset of TP53-mutant HGSC with an active tumor immune microenvironment and warrant further development as a biomarker for early detection.

articles.title: Altered Sensory and Affective Inflammatory Pain Responding in the VPA Model of Autism Is Associated With Reduced IL1β-NLRP3 Expression in the ACC in Males but Not Females.
articles.authors: Humphrey RM, Costello J, Thornton AM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal valproic acid (VPA) exposure, a well-validated preclinical model of autism, is associated with altered sensory responding to noxious heat and mechanical stimuli. However, whether sensory and affective responding to inflammatory noxious stimuli are altered, and whether effects are sex-specific is unknown. Neuroimmune crosstalk in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) modulates sensory and affective dimensions of pain and may contribute to altered pain in autism.
METHODS: This study examined acute and chronic inflammatory pain responding following intraplantar formalin or complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) in male and female VPA-exposed rats, and associated gene changes in the ACC.
RESULTS: VPA-exposed male and female rats exhibited heat and mechanical hyposensitivity, with no change in responses to innocuous cold. Nociceptive responding in the formalin test was unaltered; however, following CFA administration, VPA-exposed rats displayed higher mechanical, but not cold, withdrawal thresholds compared with saline counterparts. VPA-exposed rats showed higher paw withdrawal latencies in the Hargreaves' test following CFA, with effects influenced by sex and time. VPA-exposed males exhibited reduced anxiety-like behavior in the open field test following CFA and reduced affective/aversive pain behavior in the PEAP test prior to and following CFA administration, effects not observed in females. In male VPA-exposed rats, CFA-induced mechanical hypersensitivity and aversive-like behavior were associated with reduced Il1b and Nlrp3 expression in the ACC.
CONCLUSION: These data demonstrate that prenatal VPA exposure alters nociceptive and chronic inflammatory pain responding and suggest that sex-specific neuroimmune alterations in the ACC may play a central role in these effects.
SIGNIFICANCE: Pain in autism is poorly understood and challenging to manage. This study shows sex-dependent changes in chronic inflammatory pain responding and associated alterations in neuroimmune gene expression in the ACC in an autism-relevant preclinical model. These findings highlight neuroimmune signalling as a potential contributor to atypical pain processing in autism and an important avenue for future translational pain research.

articles.title: The Psychological and Relational Impact of Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser Syndrome: Perspectives of Patients, Mothers and Partners.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Li K, Wakefield CE, McGill BC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome (MRKHS) is a rare reproductive disorder with long-term psychosocial impacts. However, understanding of family and partner relationships that integrates the perspectives of patients, parents, and partners remains limited.
AIMS: To evaluate the psychosocial impact of MRKHS with a focus on psychological and relational functioning, from patient, parent, and partner perspectives in an Australian cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with MRKHS aged ≥ 18 years (n = 23), their parents (n = 8), and partners (n = 3) were recruited from a tertiary centre in Sydney, Australia. Three tailored questionnaires used validated self-report measures to assess physical and psychological health, family functioning, relationship satisfaction, fertility-related quality of life (QoL), sexual function, and personal identity. Comparison data were drawn from published validation studies.
RESULTS: Patients with MRKHS reported comparable self-perceived health and relationship satisfaction to reference groups, but higher anxiety (p = 0.002), more significant dyspareunia (p = 0.006), and poorer perceived family functioning (p < 0.001). They reported better overall fertility-related QoL than couples undergoing fertility treatment (p = 0.03) but had lower scores on the relationship subscale (p = 0.002). MRKHS had a central impact shaping self-identity (p = 0.002). Mothers and partners reported positive wellbeing and family or relationship functioning, although the findings are preliminary due to the limited sample size.
CONCLUSION: MRKHS affects multiple facets of patients' lives, particularly psychological well-being, pain-related sexual function, family dynamics, and personal identity. Optimal care should incorporate tailored psychological support and facilitate open communication between patients and their support network. Larger studies are warranted to examine the psychological impact of MRKHS on parents and partners.

articles.title: Is Ultrasound in Pregnancy an Opportunity for Prevention of Pelvic Floor Dysfunction: A Randomised Controlled Feasibility Study.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Ma S, Hay-Smith J, Davie G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy and childbirth are major risk factors for urinary incontinence. Antenatal pelvic floor muscle exercises (PFME) may prevent urinary incontinence. Transabdominal ultrasound scan (TAUS) in pregnancy offers a teachable moment for voluntary pelvic floor muscle contraction (VPFMC).
AIMS: To assess trial methods and feasibility of TAUS in pregnancy to confirm correct VPFMC.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A parallel randomised controlled pilot trial (registered 22/4/2022, Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, ACTRN12622000608763, https://www.anzctr.org.au/Trial/Registration/TrialReview.aspx?id=383043). Between 30/5/2022 and 29/2/2024, 50 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies were randomised to routine fetal anatomy scan (FAS) or FAS with TAUS assessment of VPFMC. Participants completed questionnaires in pregnancy and postpartum. Sonographers recorded TAUS information. Study findings were analysed descriptively.
RESULTS: From 50 participants (27 control, 23 intervention), 44 (24 control, 20 intervention) and 40 (21 control, 19 intervention) completed the 36 weeks and 3 months postpartum questionnaires, respectively. VPFMC assessment added 3 min (interquartile range 2-5) to FAS. Twenty (91%) intervention participants demonstrated correct VPFMC; sonographers considered VPFMC identification 'easy' for 19/22 (86%). Sixteen of twenty participants (80%) agreed the intervention was worthwhile. Mean PFME self-efficacy increased from baseline in both groups. The proportion of women reporting practicing PFME at least a few times a week increased in both groups during pregnancy, but this was only maintained postpartum in the intervention group.
CONCLUSION: Using TAUS to confirm correct VPFMC at FAS is feasible and acceptable to women and sonographers, and may improve PFME engagement postpartum. A definitive trial is warranted.

articles.title: Operationalizing a Framework for Appraising Seriousness to Guide Decision-Making in Prenatal Care.
articles.authors: Kleiderman E, Laberge AM, Newson AJ et al.
articles.abstract: The seriousness of a genetic condition plays an important role in shaping expectant parents' understanding of results and options following prenatal testing. Yet it is well recognized that the decisions that follow such testing can be fraught. One key concern is that prenatal care professionals can emphasize biomedical or clinical interpretations of seriousness at the expense of more contextual elements as they relate to the circumstances and values of expectant parents. In this article, we draw on three exemplar clinical case studies to demonstrate how a framework for considering seriousness can be employed to expand the breadth and depth of conversations between prenatal care professionals and expectant parents, encourage shared meaning-making around seriousness, and support expectant parents to navigate prenatal decision-making in a way that aligns with their preferences, values, and circumstances. Our framework provides an underpinning structure to the conversations and conceptual spaces in which parental perceptions of seriousness are contextualized and animated. This, in turn, can lead to more effective counseling and improved decision-making based on relevant and contextualized information.

articles.title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy and Female Infertility: A Systematic Review of Human Clinical Evidence.
articles.authors: Moccia E, Longobardi P, Lionetti V et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Female infertility represents a major global health issue, and effective treatment remains challenging in several infertility-related conditions. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) has been proposed as a potential adjunctive intervention in reproductive medicine, although human clinical evidence remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the available human evidence regarding the association between HBOT and reproductive outcomes in women with infertility or infertility-related conditions. Potential biological mechanisms, including the hypothetical involvement of sirtuin-related signaling in adaptive responses to intermittent hyperoxia, were also considered. Methods: A systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, LILACS and the Cochrane Library was updated through 10 May 2026. The search was restricted to studies published from 1 January 2016 to 10 May 2026, reflecting the review's prespecified focus on approximately the preceding decade of human clinical evidence. Original human studies investigating HBOT in women with infertility or infertility-related conditions and reporting reproductive outcomes were eligible. Study selection was conducted according to predefined eligibility criteria and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and the certainty of evidence for the main outcomes was evaluated using the GRADE approach. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity and the absence of sufficiently comparable outcomes across studies, a pooled meta-analysis was not performed. Results: Seventy-six records were identified through electronic database searches, and 11 reports underwent full-text eligibility assessment. Two original human studies involving women with resistant thin endometrium or poor ovarian response met the eligibility criteria. In women with resistant thin endometrium undergoing frozen embryo transfer, endometrial thickness increased after HBOT (6.57 ± 1.23 vs. 5.76 ± 1.66 mm before HBOT; p = 0.002). Compared with propensity-score-matched concurrent controls, women receiving HBOT had a higher implantation rate (RR, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.26-7.14) and a higher intrauterine pregnancy rate after blastocyst transfer (RR, 2.96; 95% CI, 1.14-7.70). articles.title: Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Endometrial Cancer in the Molecular Era: Current Evidence, Clinical Controversies, and Unresolved Questions.
articles.authors: Tinelli R, Sorrentino F, Surico D et al.
articles.abstract: Sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping is an established approach to nodal staging in presumed uterine-confined endometrial cancer, but its integration with molecular risk assessment raises unresolved clinical questions. This narrative review examines tracer and injection-site selection, persistent mapping failure, high-risk histologies, para-aortic assessment, low-volume nodal disease, and interpretation across POLEmut, MMRd, NSMP and p53abn tumors. A focused literature update and bibliographic verification were performed in October 2026. Cervical indocyanine green injection with near-infrared imaging supports reproducible pelvic mapping; comparative tracer studies favor it over blue dye. Prospective high-risk cohorts demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy when a complete algorithm is applied, but do not establish survival non-inferiority within every histologic or molecular subgroup. An unmapped hemipelvis requires technical reassessment and management according to baseline staging indication and operative feasibility. Negative pelvic SLNs do not exclude all para-aortic disease; additional assessment should address a defined treatment-planning question. Micrometastases constitute nodal metastasis, whereas isolated tumor cells are reported as pN0(i+). Molecularly annotated cohorts refine prognostic interpretation, but do not validate subgroup-specific treatment rules for low-volume disease. Future trials should evaluate treatment changes, morbidity and oncologic outcomes, rather than detection alone. The review distinguishes current staging practice from prognostic observations and hypotheses requiring prospective validation.

articles.title: Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Daily Clinical Practice, from Voice Dictation to Operating Room Organization: A Targeted Narrative Review with Hysteroscopy as a Clinical Exemplar.
articles.authors: Haimovich S, Fazel A
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering routine care through documentation tools, decision support, and hospital operations. The central question is whether these systems improve clinical work and patient care once embedded in routine workflows, not only whether they perform well on test data. This targeted narrative review follows AI from voice dictation and ambient documentation to operating room (OR) organization, using hysteroscopy as a clinical exemplar of the transition from technical performance to clinical utility. Evidence identified through targeted searches completed on 6 September 2026 was appraised with a framework that distinguishes image-level from patient-level results, internal from independent validation, and discrimination from clinical utility. Randomized trials and multisite observational data show modest, product-dependent benefits of clinician-reviewed ambient documentation; inaccuracies persist. Evidence for patient-message drafting derives from ratings of responses to public-forum questions and supports only bounded, supervised feasibility testing. In hysteroscopy, selected models discriminate well in narrowly defined tasks, but most studies are retrospective, image-level, or internally validated, and patient-level errors in high-risk categories are seldom reported. Reported gains in OR scheduling come largely from simulation. Safe implementation requires a defined clinical need, baseline measurement, subgroup-aware local validation, accountable review, and predefined criteria for expansion or withdrawal.

articles.title: Ovarian Preservation Before Puberty: Surgical Management of Adnexal Torsion in Prepubertal and Prepubertal-Predominant Paediatric Cohorts-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Bakhsh H
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adnexal torsion is a gynaecological emergency in which ovarian preservation or removal is decided intraoperatively. Prepubertal girls have the longest reproductive and endocrine horizon, yet they are commonly pooled with postmenarchal adolescents. This review estimated how often torsion episodes in prepubertal and prepubertal-predominant paediatric cohorts are managed by oophorectomy, together with imaging findings after ovarian-sparing surgery, recurrence and diagnosed malignancy. Methods: A PRISMA 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420261496245) searched Europe PMC (including MEDLINE), OpenAlex, preprint servers, ClinicalTrials.gov and citation networks to 2 September 2026, with an update search to 12 October 2026; Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL and CENTRAL were not searched. Eligible cohorts documented premenarchal status (direct evidence) or had a central age of 12.0 years or younger (indirect evidence). Proportions were pooled with a binomial-normal generalised linear mixed model; JBI appraisal and GRADE were applied. Results: Thirty studies were included. Across 14 cohorts (1011 episodes), 42.8% (95% CI 28.1-58.9) were managed by oophorectomy, with extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 94.0%; 95% prediction interval 6.0-89.9%); the estimate was 33.4% (8.5-69.8) in the 4 cohorts with documented premenarchal status and 24.8% (14.4-37.3) in the 7 cohorts meeting all appraisal items. Follicular activity or normal morphology was seen on follow-up imaging in 89.9% (81.9-95.9) of 234 imaged adnexa after ovarian-sparing surgery. Recurrence was 12.9% (6.6-21.0; 11 cohorts) and diagnosed malignancy 2.7% (1.0-4.6; 7 cohorts). Certainty was very low for ovarian loss and imaging findings and low for recurrence and malignancy. Conclusions: Reported oophorectomy rates in prepubertal-predominant cohorts vary widely and often exceed the low prevalence of diagnosed malignancy, but these data cannot establish how many removals were avoidable. The findings support alignment with existing ovarian-conservation guidance and better reporting of menarchal status, indications for removal and functional follow-up.

articles.title: From Established Care to Precision Menopause Medicine: A Clinical-Actionability Framework for Contemporary Menopause Management.
articles.authors: Iuhas CI, Marinescu MM, Danciu C et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause care now spans established hormone therapy, mechanism-based non-hormonal drugs, behavioural interventions, and emerging microbiome- and biomarker-guided approaches. This state-of-the-art narrative review evaluated which dimensions of personalisation are clinically actionable and which remain hypotheses of precision medicine. A structured PubMed/MEDLINE search (January 2020-July 2026), updated to August 2026 and supplemented by landmark studies, current guidelines, and regulatory sources, was synthesized using a four-tier clinical-actionability framework (A, established; B, evidence-supported off-label; C, emerging; D, experimental). Menopausal hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and prevents bone loss during use; the 2025-2026 FDA labelling revisions altered risk communication rather than the underlying evidence, and professional responses diverged. Fezolinetant and elinzanetant provide mechanism-based non-hormonal options, while SSRIs/SNRIs, gabapentin, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), CBT for insomnia, and clinical hypnosis remain evidence-supported. Exercise, yoga, acupuncture, soy, and equol are not guideline-recommended for reducing vasomotor symptom frequency despite benefits in other domains. Gut and genitourinary microbiome findings should not be conflated: pooled evidence identifies no consistent postmenopausal gut signature, whereas vaginal Lactobacillus depletion is more reproducible but does not reliably predict symptom resolution. Evidence-based personalisation therefore remains principally clinical; microbiome sequencing, equol testing, and multi-omic treatment selection require prospective test-guided validation.

articles.title: Predictors of Blood Transfusion Following Cesarean Delivery in Resource-Constrained Settings: The Impact of Out-of-Hours Surgery.
articles.authors: Muresan C, Biriș M, Roșca R et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Perioperative red blood cell (RBC) transfusion after cesarean delivery reflects both obstetric hemorrhagic risk and the capacity of the care environment. We evaluated whether out-of-hours cesarean delivery was independently associated with transfusion in a Romanian tertiary maternity unit operating under constrained resources. Methods: We conducted a retrospective unmatched case-control study of cesarean deliveries performed from 2023 to 2025. All eligible transfused women were included as cases; two non-transfused controls per case were randomly selected within each calendar year. Eligibility required preoperative hemoglobin ≥ 10 g/dL and normal coagulation. The primary exposure was out-of-hours surgery, and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal, obstetric, placental, and hematological factors. Results: The source population contained 6773 cesarean deliveries, with 608 transfusions (9.0%). The analytical sample comprised 401 cases and 802 controls. Out-of-hours procedures occurred in 64.1% of cases and 52.5% of controls (crude OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.26-2.07). After adjustment, out-of-hours delivery remained associated with transfusion (aOR 2.03, 95% CI 1.45-2.84). Placenta previa, suspected placenta accreta spectrum, and lower preoperative hemoglobin were the strongest clinical predictors. When postoperative/pre-transfusion hemoglobin was added, the out-of-hours association attenuated to an aOR of 1.02 (95% CI 0.63-1.65); sensitivity analyses remained consistent with the primary model. Conclusions: Out-of-hours cesarean delivery was associated with approximately two-fold higher transfusion odds after adjustment for the measured clinical factors. Because cesarean indication, urgency, and labor characteristics were not available, this association may partly reflect the different case mix and acuity of out-of-hours surgery rather than the working period itself. Attenuation after adjustment for post-exposure hemoglobin is compatible with, but does not establish greater perioperative blood loss. In high-cesarean, resource-constrained settings, standardized hemorrhage-risk identification and equivalent preparedness across duty periods warrant prospective evaluation in studies that also record indication and urgency.

articles.title: Early Changes in Myocardial Mechanics and Diastolic Function in Women During the Menopausal Transition.
articles.authors: Koikov V, Derbissalina G, Balmukhamedova Z et al.
articles.abstract: Background: The menopausal transition is associated with cardiovascular remodeling, but it remains unclear whether regional alterations in left ventricular (LV) myocardial mechanics are present despite preserved global systolic function. This study investigated myocardial deformation and diastolic function in women during the menopausal transition, with particular attention to the effects of chronological age and cardiometabolic factors.
