Methods: This cross-sectional study included 153 women aged 45-55 years, comprising 93 perimenopausal and 60 menopausal women. Menopausal status was determined using menstrual history and hormonal assessment. Conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography were performed to assess LV structure, diastolic function, global longitudinal strain (GLS), and regional longitudinal strain. Multivariable regression models were adjusted for age, body mass index, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Results: GLS was similar in menopausal and perimenopausal women (-19.62 ± 2.08% vs. -19.50 ± 1.96%; p = 0.723), whereas mean basal longitudinal strain was less negative in menopausal women (-18.14 ± 2.19% vs. -19.11 ± 2.22%; p = 0.009). This association persisted after multivariable adjustment (β = 1.07, 95% CI 0.27-1.88; p = 0.009). The largest segmental difference occurred in the basal inferior segment, which was considered an exploratory finding. Basal inferior strain was associated with LV diastolic dysfunction (OR 1.13 per 1 percentage-point shift toward less negative strain, 95% CI 1.01-1.26; p = 0.038). Its addition to the clinical model increased the apparent AUC from 0.619 to 0.667 (likelihood-ratio p = 0.035), although the difference between AUCs was not statistically significant by the paired DeLong test (p = 0.167). This finding should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Conclusions: Menopause was associated with a selective shift toward less negative basal LV longitudinal deformation and less favorable diastolic function despite preserved LVEF and GLS. In an exploratory analysis, basal inferior longitudinal strain was associated with LV diastolic dysfunction, although its apparent incremental discriminative value was modest. Regional longitudinal strain may provide complementary information on subclinical cardiac functional alterations associated with menopausal status, but its clinical utility requires validation in independent cohorts.

articles.title: Venous Thromboembolism and Pregnancy: Prevention and Treatment.
articles.authors: Nwachukwu N, Gaddh M
articles.abstract: Pregnancy-related venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Physiologic changes in pregnancy, along with patient-specific and pregnancy-specific risk factors, increase this VTE risk. The prevention and treatment of pregnancy-related VTE is often complex and requires the careful consideration of variation in clinical guidelines, VTE risk profile, bleeding assessment, careful delivery planning and patient preference. The mainstay of treatment for an acute VTE in pregnancy is the use of low-molecular-weight heparin. In this review, we highlight three clinical cases to review clinical approaches to the prevention and treatment of VTE in pregnancy in these scenarios. Importantly, this review goes over the current understanding of the pathophysiology and clinical practice experience for pregnant patients with VTE. We also explored the variation in professional clinical guidelines on VTE prophylaxis and treatment strategies in pregnancy, and how these guidelines may be interpreted in the context of patient care for optimal outcomes.

articles.title: Diagnostic Yield of Endometrial Sampling by Age in Premenopausal Women with Abnormal Uterine Bleeding: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Erdelean I, Erdelean D, Roșca R et al.
articles.abstract: Background: An age of 45 years is often used to guide endometrial assessment in abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), but age is only one component of clinical risk. We described the relationship between age and histopathological yield among premenopausal women who had undergone endometrial sampling. Methods: This single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study analysed the index sampling episodes of 824 women with AUB documented as premenopausal or perimenopausal (January 2022-May 2026). The clinically more consequential endpoint was endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (EIN)/atypical hyperplasia or carcinoma; the primary statistical outcome was a broader composite that also included hyperplasia without atypia. Modified Poisson regression estimated the adjusted association between age ≥45 years and the primary outcome. Discrimination of age alone and of an exploratory model using variables available before biopsy was compared in 776 complete cases with bootstrap internal validation. Results: EIN/carcinoma occurred in 4/361 (1.1%) women aged <45 years and 25/463 (5.4%) aged ≥45 years (crude RR 4.87, 95% CI 1.71-13.88). The broad outcome occurred in 24/361 (6.6%) and 57/463 (12.3%), respectively (absolute difference 5.7 percentage points, 95% CI 1.6-9.6; adjusted RR 1.62, 95% CI 1.01-2.61; p = 0.047). Results were similar across sensitivity analyses (adjusted RRs 1.52-1.68). With age coded as ≥45 years in both models, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.686 for the exploratory pre-biopsy model and 0.575 for age alone (difference 0.111, 95% CI 0.060-0.196). Conclusions: Among premenopausal women selected for endometrial sampling, histopathological yield increased with age, and most EIN/carcinoma cases occurred at age ≥45 years, but the adjusted association for the broad outcome was imprecise, and age alone had limited discrimination. Model performance was assessed only internally and only in sampled women; this study cannot establish a biopsy rule for all women with AUB because women not sampled were not observed.

articles.title: Testicular Elastography in Male Infertility: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Semen Parameters and Azoospermia.
articles.authors: Falsetti F, Cafarelli A, Maurizi V et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Quantitative testicular elastography has been proposed as a non-invasive marker of spermatogenic impairment, but published results differ across semen phenotypes, azoospermia categories, and ultrasound platforms. Methods: We performed a PRISMA-conformant systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies in which quantitative testicular elastography contributed extractable data to at least one meta-analysis. Correlation coefficients were pooled after Fisher-z transformation and back-transformed to r; group contrasts were synthesized as standardized or raw mean differences using random-effects models. SWE/SWV formed the main evidence base, with strain-ratio studies analyzed separately as an ancillary synthesis. Risk of bias was assessed uniformly with the revised JBI tool for analytical cross-sectional studies. Results: Eleven studies contributed to the final quantitative synthesis. Mean stiffness was inversely associated with sperm concentration (r = -0.37, 95% CI -0.41 to -0.32, p < 0.001; I2 = 0%) and motility (r = -0.43, 95% CI -0.58 to -0.24, p < 0.001; I2 = 8%), whereas morphology was not significantly associated (r = -0.12, 95% CI -0.31 to 0.08, p = 0.25). Azoospermic men had greater standardized stiffness than normozoospermic men (SMD 1.695, 95% CI 1.491-1.899; I2 = 0%). No evidence of a stiffness difference between NOA and OA was found (SMD 0.47, 95% CI -0.43 to 1.38; I2 = 97%). The ancillary strain-ratio retrieval estimate was highly imprecise (SMD 4.10, 95% CI -2.44 to 10.64; I2 = 99%). Neither comparison establishes equivalence or excludes a clinically important difference. The stiffness-volume correlation was also highly heterogeneous (I2 = 95%). Conclusions: Available evidence suggests inverse associations of testicular stiffness with sperm concentration and motility and higher stiffness in azoospermia. Few studies per outcome, a dominant cohort, and technical and statistical heterogeneity limit confidence in the pooled estimates. The NOA-OA, retrieval, and stiffness-volume syntheses are exploratory and cannot support clinical recommendations. Diagnostic thresholds and the value of elastography for individual clinical decisions remain unestablished.

articles.title: Experiences of Diagnostic Delay and Fertility Anxiety Among Women with Endometriosis: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Aktaş Demir S, Ölmez Yalazı R
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endometriosis often follows a prolonged diagnostic pathway and raises uncertainty about fertility. This study explored how women experienced diagnostic delay, fertility anxiety, healthcare encounters, and coping. Methods: In a qualitative descriptive study, 18 women were recruited from the gynecology outpatient clinic of a private hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye. All reported a previous physician diagnosis of endometriosis and an interval of at least two years between symptom onset and diagnosis. Individual semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed with a collaboratively developed thematic codebook. Results: Participants' mean age was 30.3 ± 4.8 years, and their mean self-reported diagnostic interval was 7.9 ± 3.6 years. Five themes addressed experiences of diagnostic delay; the meaning and consequences of diagnosis; fertility anxiety and reproductive decisions; healthcare experiences and expectations; and social support and coping. Women described the normalization of severe pain, dismissive or fragmented care, and the need to persist in seeking answers. Diagnosis validated symptoms but also brought the perceived costs of lost time into focus. Some participants described concerns about future fertility before attempting conception, while others discussed anxiety during pregnancy attempts; these concerns shaped treatment choices, relationships, and future plans. Participants described anxiety about ovarian reserve, unsuccessful fertility treatment, and pressure around marriage or motherhood; they sought clearer explanations and continuity of care. Conclusions: In this sample, diagnostic delay and fertility anxiety were intertwined with social expectations and healthcare experiences. Timely recognition of disabling symptoms, individualized fertility information, validating communication, and coordinated care may address needs across the endometriosis pathway.

articles.title: Construction and Temporal Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Clinically Significant (Grade ≥2) Acute Radiation Enteritis After Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Hu W, Song X, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Purpose: To develop and temporally validate prediction models for clinically significant acute radiation enteritis, defined as Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade ≥2 ARE and hereafter abbreviated SARE to remain consistent with the published literature on this endpoint, in patients with cervical cancer undergoing pelvic radiotherapy. Methods: A total of 363 patients diagnosed with cervical cancer were retrospectively included and received concurrent chemoradiation at the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University. The training set (n = 203, 70%) and the internal test set (n = 87, 30%) were recruited from January 2020 to January 2024; an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 73; 72 with complete outcome and prediction data) was recruited from January 2024 to December 2025. Feature selection (Boruta plus random-forest recursive feature elimination) and hyperparameter tuning were performed exclusively within the training set. Six models were constructed-logistic regression (LR), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), XGBoost and LightGBM-and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the final model. Results: Twelve optimal predictors were selected. The LR model demonstrated the most balanced performance, achieving AUCs of 0.855 (95% CI 0.792-0.910) in the training set, 0.830 (95% CI 0.721-0.918) in the internal test set, and 0.753 (95% CI 0.621-0.864) in the temporal external validation cohort. RF and LightGBM fitted the training data perfectly (AUC 1.000) but fell to 0.762 and 0.757 in validation, and XGBoost, the SVM and the MLP were lower (0.661, 0.599 and 0.616). In temporal validation LR had the lowest Brier score (0.176) but a sensitivity of only 0.40 (95% CI 0.176-0.619) at the 0.5 threshold. Decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit for LR across threshold probabilities of 0.05-0.80. SHAP ranked Rectal_Dmean, Bowel_V30 and SII as the leading contributors. Conclusions: Dosimetric parameters combined with composite inflammatory-nutritional indices show promising discrimination for grade ≥2 ARE. The LR model provides a simple, interpretable tool for pre-radiotherapy risk stratification, but prospective, multicenter validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Fixed Versus Flexible GnRH Antagonist Initiation in Women with Suboptimal Ovarian Response Undergoing IVF/ICSI: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Medić N, Roje D, Šprem Goldštajn M
articles.abstract: Background: Suboptimal ovarian responders are a clinically important subgroup of patients treated with in vitro fertilization (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). Although their ovarian reserve is usually normal, fewer oocytes than expected are retrieved after controlled ovarian stimulation. Whether the timing of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist initiation affects their reproductive outcomes is unknown. Objective: The objective of this study was to compare reproductive outcomes between fixed and flexible GnRH antagonist protocols in women with suboptimal ovarian response undergoing IVF/ICSI treatment. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 419 women treated with GnRH antagonist protocol between January 2019 and February 2020. After applying the exclusion criteria, 322 women undergoing IVF/ICSI with a GnRH antagonist protocol were eligible for analysis. Of these, 98 women with normal ovarian reserve and a suboptimal ovarian response (4-9 oocytes retrieved) were included, of whom 89 had a fresh embryo transfer (fixed protocol, n = 41; flexible protocol, n = 48). The primary outcome was live birth rate. Secondary outcomes included ovarian stimulation characteristics, embryo transfer strategy and pregnancy outcomes. Outcomes were analysed per embryo transfer and per oocyte retrieval, and factors associated with live birth were explored with Firth's penalised logistic regression. Results: Baseline characteristics, including age, AMH, duration of infertility and number of previous IVF attempts, were comparable between groups. Antagonist initiation was later in the flexible group (median day 8 vs. 7), and more embryos were transferred in the fixed group (median 2 vs. 1). The numbers of retrieved and metaphase II oocytes did not differ. Live birth rate per transfer was higher with the fixed protocol (13/41, 31.7% vs. 6/48, 12.5%; p = 0.038), whereas positive β-hCG (43.9% vs. 27.1%; p = 0.12) and clinical pregnancy (41.5% vs. 22.9%; p = 0.071) did not differ significantly; results per oocyte retrieval were similar (live birth 29.5% vs. 11.1%; p = 0.038). In Firth regression, the crude OR for live birth with flexible vs. fixed initiation was 0.32 (95% CI 0.11-0.89); estimates were similar after adjustment for age and previous IVF attempts, whereas the confidence interval crossed 1 once the number of transferred embryos was added to the model (OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.11-1.04). Conclusions: In this small retrospective…

articles.title: The Effect of Vitamins During Pregnancy on Pregnancy and Assisted Reproduction Outcomes: An Umbrella Review.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Liu H, Qin L et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Vitamin deficiency is associated with multiple adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Objective: To summarize systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and to evaluate the impact of vitamin deficiency and vitamin supplementation during pregnancy on maternal and fetal outcomes, including outcomes of assisted reproductive technology (ART). Methods: Prior to conducting this umbrella review, we registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251026875). We searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library for all systematic reviews and meta-analyses concerning vitamin status assessment and supplementation during pregnancy up to April 2025, and extracted all relevant pregnancy outcomes associated with prenatal vitamins. Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment (AMSTAR 2) were completed by two independent reviewers. Data were quantitatively synthesized, and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were mainly reported. Results: A total of 33 eligible systematic reviews and meta-analyses covering 679 primary studies were included, which explored 29 maternal-fetal outcomes related to six vitamins from the perspectives of vitamin insufficiency/deficiency and supplementation. Vitamin B12, folate, vitamin C and D deficiencies were linked to higher risks of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), pre-eclampsia, low birth weight, recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA), preterm birth and other adverse outcomes. Low vitamin D also correlated with poorer assisted reproductive outcomes including reduced clinical pregnancy and live birth rates. Appropriate supplementation of folate, vitamin C and D may lower the risks of megaloblastic anemia, premature rupture of membranes, GDM and stillbirth, and improved neonatal growth. Vitamin A exerted no notable influence on pregnancy outcomes. Conclusions: Insufficiency or deficiency in vitamin B12, folic acid, vitamin C, and vitamin D is more likely to result in adverse pregnancy outcomes. Supplementation with folic acid, vitamin C and vitamin D during pregnancy can improve the incidence of maternal and fetal outcomes to some extent.

articles.title: Clinical and Functional Outcomes of Contemporary Salvage Robotic-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy for Failed Primary Therapy: A Single Institution Review.
articles.authors: Ye E, Bissette RG, Vassallo M et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Salvage radical prostatectomy (SRP) is a potentially curative option for recurrent localized prostate cancer after primary radiation or focal therapy, historically limited by technical complexity and poor functional outcomes. This study characterizes contemporary perioperative, oncologic, and functional outcomes of salvage robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (sRARP) at a single institution over two decades. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed patients undergoing SRP from 01/01/2004 to 06/30/2026, identified via institutional database queries and natural language processing keyword searches with chart confirmation; analysis was restricted to the robotic-assisted subset. Complications within 90 days were graded by the Clavien-Dindo classification. Biochemical recurrence-free survival (bRFS) required freedom from PSA persistence and recurrence (PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL, with biochemical recurrence documented in the medical record) and is reported as a proportion. Results: Of 4002 records identified, 30 patients met inclusion criteria; 24 (80%) underwent sRARP. Extraprostatic disease was present in 54% (13/24) and positive margins in 43% (10/23). Within 90 days, 43% (10/23) had a complication (13% grade ≥ III); 30% (7/23) had a later complication, and 4% (1/24) required later urinary diversion. At a median follow-up of 32.1 months, bRFS was 39% (9/23), and 33% (8/24) had PSA persistence. Incontinence rose from 18% (3/17) at diagnosis to 87% (20/23) post-SRP; at longer-term follow-up (27.3 months), 79% (11/14) used ≥1 pad/day. Erectile dysfunction was present in 82% (14/17) at 22.0 months. Additional cancer-directed therapy was given in 50% (12/24). Conclusions: In this small, descriptive series, sRARP was feasible, but only 39% of patients were free of biochemical recurrence and functional burden was substantial. sRARP may represent a treatment option for carefully selected patients with recurrent localized prostate cancer; however, individualized counseling and further multicenter evaluation are essential.

articles.title: Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Endometrial Cancer: Experience from a Tertiary Referral Center in Türkiye.
articles.authors: Turmuş EG, Oktar O, Koca Yildirim HE et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping has become an established alternative to systematic lymphadenectomy for surgical staging in endometrial cancer. This study evaluated SLN mapping rates, anatomical distribution, factors associated with mapping failure, and perioperative outcomes in patients with early-stage endometrial cancer. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included patients with early-stage endometrial cancer who underwent SLN mapping during minimally invasive surgical staging between September 2022 and January 2025. Overall and bilateral SLN detection rates were calculated. Anatomical distribution of SLNs, factors associated with mapping failure (including a hemipelvis-level generalized estimating equation [GEE] analysis), and perioperative outcomes according to surgical approach were analyzed. Results: A total of 165 patients were included. The overall SLN detection rate was 96.4%, and bilateral mapping was achieved in 125 patients (75.8%). A total of 584 SLNs were removed, most commonly from the iliac basin. In the hemipelvis-level GEE analysis (330 hemipelves, 46 failures), ICG use (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.50, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-18.83) and, in a sensitivity model, conventional laparoscopy compared with robotic surgery (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.14-4.69) were associated with higher odds of mapping failure, whereas age and BMI were not. Operative time and intraoperative complication rates were comparable among laparoscopic, robotic-assisted, and vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) procedures. Postoperative complication rates and length of hospital stay differed significantly across surgical approaches (both p = 0.002); post hoc pairwise comparison of complication rates showed that the difference was driven mainly by conventional laparoscopy compared with robotic-assisted surgery, whereas the small vNOTES group (n = 8) did not differ significantly from either approach and does not permit conclusions on its comparative safety. Conclusions: SLN mapping demonstrated high overall detection rates and acceptable bilateral mapping success in early-stage endometrial cancer. These findings support the feasibility of SLN mapping as a minimally invasive staging strategy in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Age-Dependent Association of Hepatic Steatosis with Vertebral Trabecular Attenuation in Asymptomatic Adults.
articles.authors: Koike Y, Endo T, Fujita R et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Preserving skeletal health before osteoporosis develops has become an important challenge in preventive medicine. In addition to aging, metabolic dysfunction has emerged as a potential contributor to skeletal deterioration. Hepatic steatosis, a manifestation of systemic metabolic dysfunction, has been associated with impaired bone health; however, whether this relationship differs according to age remains unclear, particularly among asymptomatic adults. This study investigated the age-specific association between hepatic steatosis and CT-derived vertebral trabecular attenuation in adults undergoing voluntary health screening. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 553 asymptomatic Japanese adults (median age, 51 years; range, 20-88 years) who underwent non-contrast trunk CT during voluntary health checkups. Hepatic steatosis was assessed using the liver-to-spleen Hounsfield unit (HU) ratio (L/S ratio), with lower values indicating greater hepatic fat accumulation. Vertebral trabecular attenuation was assessed using the mean L1-L3 HU value. Participants were categorized as younger (≤49 years), middle-aged (50-64 years), or older (≥65 years). Multivariable regression analyses adjusted for demographic, clinical, and lifestyle factors were performed overall and by age group. An additional model assessed whether the association between the L/S ratio and vertebral HU values varied with age. Results: In the overall cohort, a lower L/S ratio was independently associated with lower vertebral HU values (β = 0.088, p = 0.018). In age-stratified analyses, this association was most evident in the younger group (β = 0.169, p = 0.010), but was attenuated in the middle-aged (β = 0.073, p = 0.260) and older groups (β = -0.113, p = 0.355). This age-related attenuation was statistically significant (β = -0.112, p = 0.004). Conclusions: Hepatic steatosis was independently associated with lower CT-derived vertebral trabecular attenuation, with the strongest association observed in adults aged ≤ 49 years. Although unmeasured factors, including menopausal status, may partly explain the observed age-dependent pattern, these findings suggest that hepatic steatosis may be relevant to skeletal health in younger adults and could help identify individuals who may benefit from early assessment and preventive care.

articles.title: Adjunctive Autonomic Regulation Practices in Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Ersoy Ö, Akçay M, Pekmez YT et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pelvic floor physiotherapy (PFPT) and biofeedback are established conservative treatments for pelvic floor dysfunctions, but clinical response is heterogeneous. We explored whether exposure to a structured multicomponent set of non-device home practices, described here as adjunctive autonomic regulation practices, was associated with patient-reported improvement when used alongside standard PFPT/biofeedback. The study was exploratory and was not designed to establish an autonomic mechanism or causal treatment effect. Methods: This retrospective, observational, nonconcurrent comparative cohort study included adults treated in the same tertiary pelvic floor rehabilitation unit during two distinct periods. The adjunct-exposed cohort (Group A; September 2022-March 2023) received PFPT/biofeedback plus a structured multicomponent home program; the historical comparator (Group B; January-June 2019) received PFPT/biofeedback without the adjunct. Both programs included diaphragmatic breathing; in the standard program, no fixed breathing rate or duration was prescribed, whereas the adjunct included slow-paced breathing at approximately 6 breaths/min for 5 min three times daily. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients classified as responders according to improvement in the MYMOP2 Profile Score from baseline to approximately 2 months. The historical dataset operationalized clinically meaningful response as >1.0-point improvement. Between-group analyses were unadjusted. Results: A total of 111 patients were analyzed (Group A, n = 35; Group B, n = 76). MYMOP2 response occurred in 31/35 patients (88.6%) in Group A and 42/76 patients (55.3%) in Group B (Pearson chi-square: chi2(1) = 11.81, p < 0.001). The unadjusted risk ratio (RR) was 1.60 (95% CI 1.27-2.03), and the unadjusted absolute difference was 33.3 percentage points (95% CI 17.9-48.7). Using recently proposed physiotherapy-specific RR reference thresholds at a baseline risk near 0.5, the numerical RR lies in the upper medium range and close to the proposed large-effect threshold; this describes magnitude only and does not imply a causal treatment effect. Conclusions: Patients exposed to the adjunctive multicomponent program had a higher unadjusted MYMOP2 responder rate than patients in a nonconcurrent historical standard-rehabilitation cohort. Because the cohorts were separated in time, baseline characterization was incomplete, follow-up availability may have introduced…

articles.title: Beyond Traditional Risk Scores: Precision Medicine for Comprehensive Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Women and Men.
articles.authors: Gámez JM, Vivas D, Goya M et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Conventional 10-year cardiovascular risk estimation algorithms are insufficient because they fail to integrate non-traditional clinical, biological, reproductive, and psychosocial modifiers that exhibit marked sex differences. The objective of this position framework is to address this gap by developing structured, sex-stratified clinical checklists for routine clinical practice. Methods: An expert narrative review and literature screening were conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, and 14 international clinical practice guidelines (2020-2026 window) to identify robust sex-stratified risk modifiers. The multidisciplinary working group (comprising cardiology, gynecology, and primary care) conducted iterative internal review rounds to synthesize evidence and structure two comprehensive clinical checklists across six operational domains. Results: Epidemiological evidence mandates a life-course prevention model starting prior to conception. In women, obstetric history (preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth), gynecological milestones (PMOS, endometriosis), early menopause, and oncological therapies markedly elevate vascular risk. In men, persistent erectile dysfunction, functional hypogonadism, androgen deprivation therapy, and premature androgenetic alopecia serve as early indicators of vascular and metabolic risk. Advanced biomarkers (Lp(a) ≥ 50 mg/dL, ApoB > 100 mg/dL, persistent hs-CRP ≥ 2 mg/L) and social determinants of health further refine risk stratification. Conclusions: Incorporating these structured checklists into daily consultations complements validated population risk scores (SCORE2, PREVENT, QRISK3), mitigates systematic underdiagnosis-especially in women-and provides an actionable framework for personalized cardiovascular prevention.

articles.title: Effects of Vibration Training on Bone Mineral Density and Balance in Postmenopausal Women with Osteopenia: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Hernandez-Martínez J, Cid-Calfucura I, Vásquez-Carrasco E et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Osteopenia is highly prevalent after menopause and increases the risk of osteoporosis, falls, and fragility fractures. Whole-body vibration has been proposed as a low-impact exercise strategy, but its clinical effectiveness remains uncertain. This systematic review with meta-analysis aims to analyze the effects of whole-body vibration on bone mineral density and balance in postmenopausal women with osteopenia. Methods: Five electronic databases were searched following PRISMA guidelines. Randomized controlled trials including postmenopausal women diagnosed with osteopenia by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry were included. Methodological quality, risk of bias, and certainty of evidence were assessed using TESTEX, RoB 2, and GRADE, respectively. Effect sizes were calculated using Hedges' g with 95% confidence intervals. Results: Five randomized controlled trials involving 248 women were included. Interventions lasted from 8 weeks to 12 months. Whole-body vibration did not produce significant improvements in bone mineral density at the tibia, radius, or lumbar spine, nor did it significantly improve balance compared with control conditions. The certainty of evidence was low for bone mineral density and very low for balance, mainly due to risk of bias, small sample sizes, and imprecision. Conclusions: Current evidence does not provide sufficient support for clinically meaningful improvements in BMD or balance following WBV in postmenopausal women with osteopenia. Nevertheless, conclusions remain uncertain because they are based on only five randomized controlled trials and very few studies per pooled outcome. Therefore, WBV cannot currently be recommended as a stand-alone intervention for improving BMD or balance, but neither can a potentially beneficial effect be definitively excluded. Larger, adequately powered, and methodologically rigorous trials are required before firm clinical recommendations can be established.

articles.title: The Effects of Time-Restricted Eating on Glycemic Control, Lipid Profiles, Androgen Levels, and Blood Pressure in PMOS: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Yang Y, Liu Z, Zhang J
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a common endocrine-metabolic disorder. Time-restricted eating (TRE) has emerged as a potential dietary intervention, but its efficacy in PMOS remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of TRE on metabolic, hormonal, and anthropometric parameters in women with PMOS. Methods: A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science databases, Embase, Cochrane Library, and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform for studies published from inception to 1 July 2026. Eight studies involving 363 women with PMOS were included in the systematic review. Among these, five controlled studies (four randomised controlled trials and one randomised crossover trial), involving 264 participants, were eligible for quantitative synthesis. Results: Quantitative synthesis was conducted using five controlled studies involving 264 participants. Meta-analysis showed that TRE significantly reduced fasting plasma glucose (MD = -0.17 mmol/L, 95% CI: -0.31 to -0.03), fasting insulin (MD = -28.86 pmol/L, 95% CI: -51.98 to -5.74), and HOMA-IR (MD = -0.66, 95% CI: -0.86 to -0.45). TRE also significantly improved QUICKI (SMD = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.05 to 0.92) and reduced HbA1c levels (MD = -1.70%, 95% CI: -3.18 to -0.22). No statistically significant differences were observed for body weight, BMI, waist circumference, lipid profiles (LDL-C, HDL-C, TC, and TG), total testosterone, SHBG, free androgen index, or blood pressure outcomes (SBP P = 0.05; DBP P = 0.11). Subgroup analyses based on comparator type revealed no significant subgroup differences for the key outcomes. Conclusions: TRE may improve insulin sensitivity-related outcomes-including fasting plasma glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and QUICKI-as well as HbA1c in women with PCOS. However, current evidence does not demonstrate significant effects on anthropometric measures, lipid metabolism, androgen-related outcomes, or blood pressure. Long-term, larger trials are warranted to confirm these benefits.

articles.title: A Cross-Sectional Study Investigating Urinary Levels of Nerve Growth Factor and Its Precursor in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.authors: Nociti V, Bientinesi R, Cicia A et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: As multiple sclerosis (MS) progresses, most patients develop lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) indicative of an overactive bladder (OAB), primarily due to neurogenic detrusor overactivity, which is the most common abnormality identified during urodynamic testing. Therefore, biomarkers for OAB would be valuable additions to diagnostic tools. This study aimed to compare urinary levels of nerve growth factor (NGF) and its precursor, pro-NGF, in MS patients with and without OAB. Methods: We enrolled patients with relapsing MS (RMS), some exhibiting LUTS suggestive of OAB, along with healthy controls (HCs). Urine samples were collected, and NGF and pro-NGF levels were measured using ELISA kits. Results: Neither an ELISA kit specific for NGF nor a kit recognizing both NGF and pro-NGF detected measurable levels of these proteins. However, an ELISA kit selective for pro-NGF detected similarly low concentrations of this protein in a few samples from each group. Conclusions: Our ELISA results, measuring urinary NGF and pro-NGF levels in MS patients and HCs, are consistent with other studies that failed to detect these proteins in the urine of patients with OAB of various etiologies or in HCs. It is possible that urinary levels of NGF and pro-NGF are so low that the detection limits of ELISA kits and other available immunoassays are insufficient for their reliable measurement.

articles.title: Advances in Intrauterine Contraception and Therapeutic Intrauterine Devices, 2016-2026: A Targeted Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Biriș M, Buciu VB, Cîtu IM et al.
articles.abstract: Intrauterine contraception has changed over the past decade through longer validated duration, lower-dose hormonal devices, redesigned copper devices, new indications, and better safety surveillance. This targeted scoping review (OSF registration 10.17605/OSF.IO/3GUQF) mapped English-language primary human studies published from 1 January 2016 to 5 September 2026 in journals indexed in the Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE). A reproducible search targeted to the major device programs, randomized trials, and large surveillance cohorts identified 766 PubMed/MEDLINE records, with no additional unique records from Scopus or Web of Science; of the 624 unique records screened, 123 reports were assessed, and 114, from 66 distinct trials, cohorts, or data sources, were included and appraised with design-specific Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools. Two single-arm programs and a 7-year randomized trial supported the efficacy of 52 mg levonorgestrel intrauterine devices (LNG-IUDs) through 8 years. Lower-dose LNG-IUDs eased placement but were associated with higher ectopic pregnancy rates in four Scandinavian analyses and with less antidepressant use than the 52 mg device. Smaller or size-matched copper devices improved continuation and reduced expulsion in randomized comparisons, whereas a low-copper nitinol device had a higher 5-year pregnancy rate than expected with TCu380A. Perforation was uncommon but more frequent after postpartum insertion and during breastfeeding; immediate postpartum insertion carried the highest expulsion risk. One randomized trial and its secondary analyses supported the 52 mg LNG-IUD for emergency contraception. Therapeutic evidence was strongest for heavy menstrual bleeding and endometrial hyperplasia, whereas intrauterine ball and precious metal designs showed no consistent benefit. Progress refined rather than replaced the T-shaped IUD.

articles.title: Associations Between Masseter Muscles Tension, Postural Pattern, Pelvic Type and Postural Stability in Women with Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
articles.authors: Wójcik M, Góral K, Małysz J et al.
articles.abstract: Background: This study aimed to examine the associations of pelvic type and body posture pattern with masseter muscle measurements and postural stability parameters in women with POP, and to assess the relationship between masseter muscle measurements and postural stability under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Methods: This observational study included 61 women: 31 with advanced POP (grade 3-4 according to the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification system [POP-Q]) and 30 healthy controls. Masseter muscle measurements, postural stability parameters (center-of-pressure sway and surface area), body posture pattern, and pelvic type were assessed. Postural stability was measured with eyes open and closed. Two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Tukey's post-hoc test, and Pearson's correlation coefficient were used for statistical analysis. Results: Pelvic type was not significantly associated with any of the analyzed parameters. Body posture pattern was associated with significant differences in most postural stability parameters (p < 0.05) under both visual conditions, with the highest values observed in women with a posterior posture pattern. Conclusions: In women with advanced POP, body posture pattern was associated with differences in postural stability parameters, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed for pelvic type. No statistically significant correlations were detected between masseter muscle measurements and postural stability. These findings should be interpreted cautiously, given the observational study design, and do not establish causal relationships.

articles.title: Documented Obstetric Haemorrhage in a General Intensive Care Unit in Ghana: Outcomes and the Unadjusted Association Between Recorded GCS and Mortality.
articles.authors: Djokoto RMK, Bandoh I, Sam-Awortwi WKJ et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Obstetric haemorrhage remains an important cause of maternal death and severe morbidity. Outcomes depend on timely recognition, resuscitation, referral, access to blood and essential treatment, and critical care. This study described the clinical characteristics, documented haemorrhage diagnoses, and ICU outcomes of women admitted with obstetric haemorrhage to the main intensive care unit (ICU) of Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), Kumasi, Ghana. Methods: This retrospective cohort analysis included 79 women with an obstetric haemorrhage-related diagnosis documented in ICU records, drawn from 344 obstetric ICU admissions between 17 July 2022 and 16 July 2023. Demographic and clinical characteristics, ICU treatments, and outcomes were summarized. Survivors and non-survivors were compared using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test and the chi-square or Fisher exact test, as appropriate. Only unadjusted comparisons are reported because the patient-level dataset required for a prespecified admission-only model was not available for analysis. Results: Among 344 obstetric admissions to KATH's main ICU, 79 women (23.0%) had documented obstetric haemorrhage and were included. Postpartum haemorrhage was the most common diagnosis (32/79, 40.5%), followed by abruptio placentae (18/79, 22.8%) and uterine rupture (12/79, 15.2%). Forty-four women died in the ICU (55.7%). The GCS variable, labelled "admission GCS" in the source dataset, was lower among non-survivors than survivors (median 8 vs. 15; p < 0.001), as was diastolic blood pressure (71.5 vs. 86 mmHg; p = 0.010). Mechanical ventilation was more frequent among non-survivors (70.5% vs. 40.0%; p = 0.013), while hospital stay was shorter (4 vs. 9 days; p < 0.001). GCS measurement timing could not be verified; treatment and length-of-stay differences describe post-admission care and course. Conclusions: Among women admitted to a general mixed ICU with documented obstetric haemorrhage, ICU mortality was high and postpartum haemorrhage was the most common diagnosis. Lower recorded GCS among non-survivors was an unadjusted descriptive finding; the source dataset's GCS timing could not be confirmed, and no adjusted prognostic effect can be inferred. Prospective studies with verified admission measures, explicit case criteria, and treatment timing are needed.

articles.title: From Early Diet to Immune Phenotype: Childhood Nutrition and Immunometabolic Programming Across the Life Course-A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Cristun LI, Mărginean O, Jugănaru I et al.
articles.abstract: Childhood diet may shape immune and inflammatory trajectories through interacting metabolic, microbial, and developmental pathways, but the long-term human evidence remains heterogeneous. This scoping review mapped longitudinal studies examining dietary exposures from birth to 18 years in relation to subsequent immune, inflammatory, allergic, autoimmune, gastrointestinal, immunometabolic, hepatic, neurocognitive, and endocrine-immunometabolic outcomes. The review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported according to PRISMA-ScR principles. A total of 403 studies were included. Evidence was concentrated in infancy and early childhood and predominantly addressed allergic and atopic outcomes; evidence on other immunological outcomes and on middle childhood and adolescence was more limited. Thirty studies provided relatively direct immunometabolic evidence, 149 contributed mechanistically indirect evidence, and 224 primarily reported longitudinal clinical diet-outcome associations. The principal mechanistic axes involved allergic sensitization and immune tolerance, lipid and fatty-acid metabolism, micronutrient and antioxidant pathways, cytokine signaling, gut microbiome and metabolite pathways, and human-milk-derived bioactive signals. Dietary diversity and overall diet quality intersected with several of these pathways. Associations were frequently context-dependent, varying according to developmental timing, host susceptibility, genetic background, immune state, and feeding context. Mechanistic interpretation rests on convergence across complementary studies rather than on complete pathways demonstrated within individual cohorts. Overall, the evidence is compatible with a proposed life-course nutritional immunology framework in which childhood diet acts as a dynamic developmental exposure interacting with microbial, metabolic, and immune processes; however, this framework derives mainly from early-life exposures and allergic and atopic outcomes, and the persistence of effects beyond early childhood remains insufficiently demonstrated. Limitations include restriction to English-language publications, marked methodological heterogeneity, residual confounding, and the absence of a formal risk-of-bias assessment.

articles.title: Weekly Calcifediol 100 µg in Women with Vitamin D Deficiency: A Post Hoc Analysis of a Randomised Placebo-Controlled Phase II/III Trial.
articles.authors: Pérez Castrillón JL, Jódar-Gimeno E, García-Bea A et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objective: Given the high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency, particularly among older women, this post hoc analysis was conducted to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of weekly calcifediol 100 µg in women with vitamin D deficiency participating in a randomised, double-blind, phase II/III trial. Methods: A total of 261 women were included (calcifediol, n = 192; placebo, n = 69). The primary objective was to compare the proportions of women achieving serum 25(OH)D concentrations ≥20 ng/mL or ≥30 ng/mL over the 12-month treatment period. Exploratory analyses of body mass index (BMI) and menopausal status were performed. Results: Weekly calcifediol 100 µg demonstrated superior efficacy versus placebo from week 4 in women achieving ≥20 ng/mL (68.2% vs. 5.8%; p < 0.001) or ≥30 ng/mL (21.4% vs. 0%; p < 0.001), and consistently higher proportions were maintained through week 52. Mean 25(OH)D concentrations increased from 12.21 ng/mL at baseline to 39.47 ng/mL at week 16, and remained stable (41-43 ng/mL) thereafter. No significant differences were observed across BMI or menopausal status subgroups. The safety profile of weekly calcifediol 100 µg was similar to placebo, with no evidence of toxicity. Conclusions: Weekly calcifediol 100 µg is a safe and effective option for achieving and maintaining adequate vitamin D levels in vitamin D-deficient women over a period of 12 months, and is associated with consistent effects across BMI and menopausal status.

articles.title: Chrononutrition and Prenatal Mental Health: The Relationship Between Food Intake Indicators and Prenatal Depressive Symptomatology.
articles.authors: Personette CM, Phan D, Duan D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We examined cross-sectional associations between mid-pregnancy food intake indicators and prenatal depressive symptomatology.
METHODS: This secondary analysis of the Comparison of Two Screening Strategies for Gestational Diabetes (GDM2) trial (N = 716) examined five domains of mid-pregnancy food intake (direct timing, energy timing, meal/snack structure, meal energy distribution, and diet quality) derived from 24 h dietary recalls. Depressive symptoms were measured with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Generalized linear models examined associations between food intake indicators and both total and high (EPDS ≥ 13) depressive symptoms.
RESULTS: The mean (SD) EPDS score was 6.3 (4.9); a total of 12.4% (n = 89) of subjects had high depressive symptoms. Eating frequency (exp(B) = 1.084 [1.021, 1.151], p = 0.008), snack frequency (exp(B) = 1.063 [1.004, 1.126], p = 0.037), nighttime snacking frequency (exp(B) = 1.060 [1.003, 0.121], p = 0.040), and total daily energy intake (exp(B) = 1.058 [1.002, 1.118], p = 0.044) were positively associated with total depressive symptoms. Energy intake from breakfast (PR = 1.178 [1.029, 1.349], p = 0.017) was associated with higher prevalence of high depressive symptoms. Energy intake from dinner (PR = 0.809 [0.695, 0.943], p = 0.007), a later timing of the first eating episode (PR = 0.830 [0.699, 0.986], p = 0.034) and the first energy quartile (PR = 0.837 [0.702, 0.998], p = 0.048) were associated with lower prevalence of high depressive symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings extend the prior chrononutrition-depression literature to the prenatal period, implicating eating frequency, energy intake, and meal energy timing and distribution in depressive symptomatology during pregnancy, and warrant further longitudinal investigation.

articles.title: Effects of Heat-Killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum L-137 on Menopause-Related Outcomes and Gut Barrier-Related Biomarkers in Japanese Women: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Nakajima T, Ohara T, Hirose Y et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Menopause-related issues-such as mood disturbance, hot flashes, and sleep disturbance-are thought to be influenced not only by hormonal changes but also by everyday stress and gut barrier-related host responses. Heat-killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum L-137 (HK L-137) has shown immunomodulatory and gut barrier-related effects, but clinical evidence for its effects in menopausal women is limited. We investigated whether HK L-137 intake affects menopause-related outcomes and gut barrier-related biomarkers in women reporting daily stress. Methods: We conducted a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in healthy Japanese women aged 45-69 years who self-reported daily stress (UMIN000055687). Participants were randomly assigned to receive one tablet containing 10 mg HK L-137 or placebo daily. Mood state, menopausal symptoms, and sleep quality-as menopause-related outcomes-and gut barrier-related biomarkers were assessed at baseline and week 12. Results: A total of 121 participants were included, and 119 completed the study. No significant between-group differences were observed in the questionnaire scores of mood state, menopausal symptoms, or sleep quality. Changes in serum soluble CD14 (sCD14) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) differed significantly between groups, favoring the HK L-137 group (p = 0.020 and p = 0.010, respectively). In the prespecified subgroup with higher baseline levels of negative mood, HK L-137 significantly improved hot flashes item and sleep maintenance score, and was associated with favorable changes in sCD14, LDH, and body mass index versus placebo. No intervention-related safety concerns were identified. Conclusions: HK L-137 favorably affected sCD14 and LDH in the overall analysis and improved selected menopause-related outcomes in women with higher baseline levels of negative mood. These findings suggest a possible role of gut barrier-related host responses associated with microbial translocation.

articles.title: Anti-Inflammatory Dietary Supplements in Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Apan A, Pop C, Iaru I et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence on the safety and efficacy of anti-inflammatory dietary supplements used during pregnancy, assessing maternal and fetal outcomes.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2016-June 2026), following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The protocol was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework (10.17605/osf.io/4kmv9). Eligible studies included human clinical trials and observational studies evaluating anti-inflammatory dietary supplements in pregnant women.
RESULTS: Eighty unique studies (96 publications) from 28 countries were included, of which 63 (78.8%) were randomized clinical trials. Thirteen supplement categories were identified. Vitamin D (n = 23) and omega-3 fatty acids (n = 17) accounted for nearly half of all studies; probiotics (n = 11) formed the third-largest category. For these three supplements, most studies reported changes in inflammatory and glycemic markers, primarily in gestational diabetes mellitus and high-risk populations, but adverse events were collected in a minority of studies, so tolerability is documented rather than established. Evidence for zinc, magnesium, and alpha-lipoic acid was limited. Curcumin, chlorella, vitamin E, epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), resveratrol, and ginger were each supported by only one or two studies. Supplementation was initiated in the first trimester in 19 studies (23.8%), and neonatal safety outcomes were reported infrequently.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on anti-inflammatory dietary supplements in pregnancy is concentrated in a few compounds, in a small number of countries, and in biochemical outcomes measured in selected populations. Tolerability was evaluated in only a small number of studies, which limits its use as an indicator of safety. The map highlights the scarcity of controlled studies with prespecified harm outcomes, of first-trimester initiation, and of infant follow-up beyond the first months of life.

articles.title: Association Between Salt Intake Habits and Vasomotor Symptoms According to Adiposity Among Middle-Aged Korean Women: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Jang Y, Kim SM, Shin S et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Whether habitual salt consumption is related to vasomotor symptoms (VMS) during the menopausal transition has received little attention. We investigated the relationship of salt-related eating behaviors with bothersome VMS over time and explored whether body composition modified this relationship. Methods: We analyzed repeated observations from 3664 Korean women who entered the cohort between 2014 and 2018 and were followed until July 2024. A three-item questionnaire was used to generate a salt intake habit score, which was divided into tertiles. Bothersome VMS across repeated visits were analyzed using logistic mixed-effects models with inverse probability weighting, and effect modification by adiposity was explored. Results: At enrollment, mean age was 45.6 years; among women with repeated assessments, the median observation period was 5.6 years. Relative to the lowest salt intake tertile, adjusted odds ratios (95% CI) for bothersome VMS were 1.48 (1.22-1.80) in the middle tertile and 1.51 (1.20-1.89) in the highest tertile. The association appeared stronger among women with percentage body fat ≥35% (p for interaction = 0.032), although the interaction did not reach the Bonferroni-corrected threshold (p < 0.0167). Conclusions: Saltier eating habits were related to a greater likelihood of bothersome VMS during follow-up. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating, and whether reducing salt consumption also decreases VMS warrants testing in intervention studies.

articles.title: Integrative Proteomics Reveals That Ejiao Alleviates Premature Ovarian Insufficiency and Restores Bone Metabolism in Mice.
articles.authors: Wang C, Fu X, Feng Q et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is an intractable reproductive endocrine disease characterized by accelerated ovarian aging, accelerated follicle depletion and hormonal disorders, leading to secondary bone metabolic dysfunction and impaired long-term female health. Conventional hormone replacement therapy is the guideline-recommended first-line therapy for young women with POI, yet its long-term safety must be individualized; natural nutritional interventions are best viewed as complementary strategies. Donkey-hide gelatin (Ejiao), a natural food rich in bioactive collagen and amino acids, is commonly used for female reproductive care. Nevertheless, its systematic efficacy and molecular mechanisms against POI and related bone complications remain poorly defined. Methods: This study established a tripterygium glycosides (TG)-induced POI mouse model. Mice received low-dose (1.5 g/kg) and high-dose (3.0 g/kg) Ejiao treatment for 30 consecutive days. Reproductive organ morphology, estrous cycle, serum hormone levels, ovarian histopathology, bone microarchitecture and ovarian proteomic profiles were assessed. Results: Ejiao remarkably restored ovarian index and tended to improve uterine index (non-significant), corrected estrous cycle disturbance, and partially corrected the endocrine profile (E2, AMH, GnRH). It upregulated the ovarian reserve markers E2 and AMH and downregulated GnRH. Histological examination verified improved follicular development and reduced atresia. Furthermore, Ejiao alleviated POI-induced bone loss, optimized trabecular microstructure and rescued abnormal RANKL/OPG ratio to stabilize bone metabolism. Proteomic analysis revealed 313 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) between Ejiao-treated and model groups, with enrichment in calcium signaling, cAMP, cGMP-PKG, and TGF-β/Smad pathways. Conclusions: As a natural bioactive food, Ejiao exerts dual protective effects against POI and concurrent bone metabolic dysfunction associated with modulation of multiple core signaling pathways and functional proteins (suggesting involvement of these pathways in its effects).

articles.title: The Early Nutrition Paradox in Preterm and Intrauterine Growth Restricted (IUGR) Infants: A Critical Review of the Developmental Programming Hypothesis and the Limits of Its Evidence.
articles.authors: Riskin A, Iofe A, Safadi RZ et al.
articles.abstract: Nutrition during early life may be an important determinant of long-term health. Preterm birth, affecting approximately 10% of deliveries worldwide, and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) are major perinatal conditions. The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) hypothesis proposes that early nutritional and environmental exposures shape adult disease risk. This narrative review synthesizes epidemiological, cohort, animal, and interventional evidence on early nutrition and long-term outcomes in these infants. Rapid weight gain has been associated with later obesity and cardio-metabolic risk; however, this does not show that the tempo of gain, rather than attained size, carries the risk, and catch-up growth after preterm birth or growth restriction supports neurodevelopment. Preterm birth has been associated with a 53% higher risk of ischemic heart disease, whereas IUGR confers overlapping but distinct risks. Hypothesized mechanisms include epigenetic modification, structural organ deficits, hormonal reprogramming, gut-microbiome dysbiosis, and oxidative stress. Because the human evidence is almost entirely observational and vulnerable to confounding and to over-adjustment for attained body size, these associations should be read as hypotheses rather than established causal effects. Individualized, guideline-based and responsive feeding strategies, with support for mothers to provide their own milk, are needed to optimize immediate outcomes while limiting lifelong disease susceptibility.

articles.title: Association of Circulating Irisin with Adiposity, Sarcopenia-Related Indices, and Phenotypes in Premenopausal and Postmenopausal Women.
articles.authors: Aljawini N, Habib SS, Al-Regaiey K
articles.abstract: Background: Irisin is an exercise-induced myokine also produced by adipose tissue and thus considered an adipo-myokine. Its relationship with adiposity and sarcopenia-related indices remains unclear. We examined these associations and compared circulating irisin concentrations across operationally defined phenotypes in premenopausal and postmenopausal women. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 79 women underwent body-composition assessment by BIA and HGS measurement by dynamometry, of whom 78 underwent serum irisin measurement by ELISA. Participants were classified into four operational phenotypes (Control, Obesity, Sarcopenia, and Sarcopenic Obesity) using BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 for obesity and HGS < 16 kg for low muscle strength. Irisin was compared across phenotypes and correlated with adiposity and sarcopenia-related indices. Results: Circulating irisin was significantly lower in women with BMI-defined obesity than in those without obesity (173.70 [89.03-357.20] vs. 347.30 [188.90-716.00] pg/mL; p = 0.0024) but did not differ when obesity was defined by %BF (≥35%; p = 0.1034). Overall, irisin did not differ by menopausal status. Among postmenopausal women, irisin concentrations were lower in those with obesity than in those without obesity (179.70 [85.30-321.90] vs. 403.60 [219.20-801.70] pg/mL; p = 0.0043), whereas no significant difference was observed among premenopausal women (p = 0.2666). Across the operational phenotypes, irisin was lowest in the sarcopenic obesity group (128.90 [68.57-321.90] pg/mL) and significantly lower than in controls (322.40 [164.10-498.40] pg/mL; p = 0.0076). Irisin was not significantly associated with HGS, ASM, or MQI, whereas ASMI showed an inverse association (r = -0.2773, p = 0.0153). Significant inverse associations were observed with FMI (r = -0.3835, p = 0.0006), BMI (r = -0.3609, p = 0.0013), and %BF (r = -0.3396, p = 0.0025). In exploratory univariable regression analyses, BMI, FMI, and %BF accounted for 15.9%, 15.2%, and 8.4% of the variance in circulating irisin, respectively. Conclusions: Circulating irisin showed consistent inverse associations with adiposity indices but a less consistent pattern across muscle-related indices, suggesting that adiposity may be particularly relevant to circulating irisin in women.

articles.title: Effects of Intravenous Versus Oral Iron Replacement on Inflammatory Markers and Serum Uric Acid in Premenopausal Women with Iron Deficiency: A Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Demircan V, Yazar K, Eminoğlu H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Iron deficiency may be associated with alterations in systemic inflammatory activity and metabolic parameters. However, whether oral and intravenous (IV) iron replacement have different effects on inflammatory markers and serum uric acid remains unclear. We compared inflammatory and metabolic responses to oral and IV iron in premenopausal women with iron deficiency.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 72 oral iron recipients, 77 IV iron recipients, and 76 healthy controls. Patients were reassessed at Day 30. The primary outcome was change in C-reactive protein (CRP); changes in erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and uric acid were secondary outcomes. Additional regressions used robust standard errors, adjusting for age, baseline hemoglobin, and baseline outcome values; the uric acid model additionally included baseline creatinine.
RESULTS: Baseline CRP and ESR were significantly higher in both iron-deficient groups than in controls (all Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001). The IV iron group had more severe baseline anemia than the oral iron group (median hemoglobin: 8.60 vs. 10.70 g/dL; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001). Increases in hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation over 30 days were greater with IV iron (all p < 0.001). Median CRP changes were -0.22 mg/L with IV iron and 0.07 mg/L with oral iron (unadjusted p = 0.041). However, multivariable regression with robust standard errors showed no statistically significant difference in Day 30 CRP after adjustment for age, baseline hemoglobin, and baseline CRP (IV minus oral: -1.585 mg/L; 95% CI, -3.261 to 0.091; p = 0.064; n = 149). The corresponding adjusted analysis showed lower Day 30 ESR with IV iron (-2.118 mm/h; 95% CI, -3.817 to -0.418; p = 0.015; n = 91). The adjusted serum uric acid difference, additionally accounting for baseline creatinine, was not statistically significant (0.389 mg/dL; 95% CI, -0.009 to 0.787; p = 0.055; n = 149).
CONCLUSIONS: IV iron was associated with greater hematologic and iron-store repletion over 30 days. Adjusted comparisons showed no statistically significant differences in CRP or serum uric acid, whereas ESR was modestly lower with IV iron, with uncertain clinical significance. Nonrandomized treatment allocation and premedication restricted to the IV group preclude attributing these findings solely to iron administration.

articles.title: Salvira™ Does Not Modulate Estrogen Receptor: Reassessing Salvia officinalis Proposed Phytoestrogenic Properties.
articles.authors: Iannitti R, Ceccarelli G, Melfi V et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Salvia officinalis L. is widely used in food supplements, particularly those intended to support women's health and alleviate menopausal vasomotor symptoms. However, the extent to which estrogen receptor signaling contributes to its reported clinical benefits remains unclear. Therefore, evaluating its potential endocrine activity is a key aspect of its toxicological characterization and overall safety assessment. The present study aimed to investigate the potential estrogenic effects of a standardized Italian Salvia officinalis L. extract (Salvira™), as well as its biological effects on estrogen-responsive breast cancer cells (MCF-7). Methods: In vitro enzymatic assays and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) agonist- and antagonist-mode experiments were performed to assess its ability to modulate ERα signaling. Moreover, cell viability, proliferation, and clonogenic capacity were assessed in MCF-7 cells following exposure to increasing concentrations of the extract. Results: The extract did not exhibit estrogenic activity in all experimental dose-response assays. In MCF-7 cells, treatment with the sage extract did not produce an overall effect on cell viability or proliferative capacity. Moreover, no impairment of long-term clonogenic potential was observed at the tested concentrations. Conclusions: Under the experimental conditions investigated, the present findings suggest that the standardized Salvia officinalis L. extract showed no evidence of estrogenic activity and did not induce relevant ERα-mediated biological effects in estrogen-responsive MCF-7 cells. These findings contribute to the characterization of the endocrine safety profile of the extract, supporting its safe use as an ingredient in food supplements.

articles.title: Clinical Applications of Flavonoids in Pregnancy: Potential Therapeutic Strategies for Gestational Disorders-An Update.
articles.authors: Kozłowska A
articles.abstract: Gestational disorders, including pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, and fetal growth restriction, represent major maternal-fetal health challenges, with limited pharmacological options that can be used safely throughout pregnancy. Flavonoids, a diverse group of plant-derived polyphenols, exert antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and vasoprotective effects in preclinical models. Translational evidence from these mechanistic studies has increased interest in their potential role in maternal-fetal health. This narrative review evaluates the clinical evidence regarding maternal flavonoid exposure across preconception care, pregnancy complications, postpartum recovery, and offspring health. A comprehensive literature search identified thirteen studies published within the past five years, comprising randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, and evidence from major prospective birth cohorts. Available clinical evidence suggests that higher dietary intake of flavonoid-rich fruits, berries, and vegetables is associated with a lower risk of gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and small-for-gestational-age births. Clinical studies of targeted supplementation with specific compounds, including quercetin, epigallocatechin gallate, and botanical extracts, have reported potential benefits in selected clinical settings, including endocrine and reproductive outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome, blood pressure management in pre-eclampsia, and postpartum or post-cesarean pain. Furthermore, maternal flavonoid exposure has been associated with differences in offspring immune development and a potentially lower incidence of food allergies in early childhood. Overall, current clinical evidence supports further investigation of dietary flavonoid intake and selected flavonoid-based interventions in maternal-fetal medicine. Overall, while current evidence strongly supports habitual consumption of a varied, plant-rich diet naturally high in flavonoids during pregnancy, clinical data remain insufficient to recommend routine high-dose isolated flavonoid supplementation in standard obstetric practice.

articles.title: Carrier Screening and Potential-Difference Response of a Piezomagnetic-Piezoelectric Semiconductor PN-Junction Sandwich Fiber Under a Local Magnetic Field.
articles.authors: Liu C, Zhou W, Ma Y et al.
articles.abstract: Carrier screening and observation geometry determine how a local magnetoelectric response contributes to a potential-difference readout. This study develops a finite-length one-dimensional analytical model for a weak PN-junction piezoelectric-semiconductor fiber between magnetostrictive layers subjected to a localized magnetic-field increment about a prescribed bias. Cross-sectional force balance, two-carrier drift-diffusion, blocking end conditions, and interface continuity yield a four-region solution that separates the junction reference from the magnetic increment. In the representative weak-junction case, the end-to-end difference is about 1% of the peak local magnetically induced potential, whereas observation pairs at the field-region edges and near the junction give differences about 200 and 50 times larger than the end-to-end value. For equal screening and a step field, the response of a fixed interior pair peaks when the field-region edges reach the observation points. Uniformly doped and symmetric weak-junction controls have identical magnetic increments under equal screening despite their different reference fields. Layer thickness modifies both magnetic conversion and carrier screening. The resulting continuum-model relations identify how excitation width, screening length, and observation position jointly govern internal magnetic-field readout.

articles.title: New Chromone Analogues as Potential Bioactive Compounds: Cyclodextrin Complexation and Molecular Docking.
articles.authors: Czapnik P, Małecka M, Hikisz P et al.
articles.abstract: Chromone is an important structural motif in numerous biologically active natural and synthetic compounds. The aim of the present study is to synthesize and characterize a series of novel chromone derivatives bearing imidazole and pyrazole moieties. The synthesis involved a two-step procedure in which methyl 3-chromonecarboxylate derivatives were prepared and then condensed with imidazole and pyrazole analogues. The structures of the compounds were characterized using spectroscopy, single-crystal X-ray diffraction and Hirshfeld surface analysis. Compounds 1 and 1A were subjected to ITC titration in DMSO. Anticancer potential of synthetized substances was evaluated against three breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7, MDA-MB-231 and HCC38), and two endometrial cancer cell lines (Ishikawa and Hec-1-A). Compounds 1B and 1C, bearing 3-(1H-imidazol-1-yl)propan-1-amine and3-(3,5-dimethyl-4H-pyrazol-4-yl)propan-1-amine moieties, respectively, exhibited the most pronounced, albeit modest, cytotoxic activity against MCF-7 cells, with IC50 values of approximately 80 μM. In HMEC-1 human microvascular endothelial cells (used as a non-cancerous reference model), the same compounds lowered the signal of the dihydroethidium (DHE) probe, suggesting a modest antioxidant effect; these redox results are reported separately from the anticancer assays. The compounds were subjected to further complex analysis using 2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate (H2DCFDA) and molecular docking studies. This complex approach provided a qualitative insight into the structure-activity relationships of the studied derivatives. Given the modest cytotoxicity and limited selectivity of Compounds 1B and 1C, together with their redox-modulating effect observed in HMEC-1 cells, these compounds should be regarded as a starting point for further investigation rather than as promising anticancer candidates.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal Stability and Microbiota-Mediated Deglycosylation of Triterpene Glycosides from Cimicifuga racemosa Extract Ze 450.
articles.authors: Senn R, Pugin B, Merk VM et al.
articles.abstract: Triterpene glycosides (TTGs) are characteristic constituents of Cimicifuga racemosa extract Ze 450 and may contribute to its pharmacological effects in the treatment of menopausal symptoms. This exploratory study investigated their gastrointestinal stability, transformation during incubation with human fecal microbiota, and potential effects on microbial community composition and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production. The stability of 23-epi-26-deoxyactein was assessed during simulated oral and gastric digestion using the INFOGEST protocol. Microbiota-associated biotransformation of actein, 23-epi-26-deoxyactein, cimigenol-3-β-D-xyloside, and cimigenol-3-α-L-arabinoside was subsequently examined during 48 h anaerobic ex vivo cultivation with fecal microbiota from eight female donors. 23-Epi-26-deoxyactein remained largely stable during simulated oral and gastric digestion. During fecal incubation, all investigated TTGs were depleted and the corresponding aglycones were detected. Quantification of the 23-epi-26-deoxyactein aglycone revealed marked donor-dependent differences, indicating substantial interindividual variability in TTG biotransformation. Individual TTGs had little effect on microbial community composition or SCFA profiles, whereas Ze 450 induced a small but significant shift in overall community structure without substantially affecting SCFA production. These findings demonstrate extensive microbiota-mediated TTG deglycosylation and highlight marked interindividual variability in TTG metabolism, providing a rationale for further investigation of microbiome-dependent differences in the pharmacological fate of Ze 450.

articles.title: Obesity and Diabetes in Pregnancy and Maternal and Child Health: The Gerar Cohort Profile, Brazil.
articles.authors: Oliveira MP, Stork SS, Piovezan AP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-pregnancy obesity and GDM increase maternal-fetal oxidative stress, but their consequences for women's health and child development are still unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This paper describes the methodological design, recruitment strategy, data collection methods, and baseline characteristics of the Gerar Cohort, a prospective longitudinal study designed to investigate the relationship between pre-pregnancy obesity and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) with oxidative stress biomarkers and their effects on maternal and child health outcomes through 12 months postpartum.
METHODS: Women were recruited early in their prenatal care in a city in Southern Brazil. Sociodemographic and clinical data, as well as blood samples, were collected each trimester. At childbirth, umbilical cord blood and placental tissue were collected. Children were followed up until 12 months of age, with blood collection at 4 and 12 months. The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee.
RESULTS: A total of 189 women were recruited in the first trimester; 136 were followed up until the third trimester; 23 pregnancy losses were recorded. Pre-gestational obesity was observed in 24.3% (95% CI 18.4-31.1), and 27% (95% CI 20.8-33.9) of women were diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus. Fifty-nine umbilical cord blood samples and 61 placental fragments were collected. In the children's follow-up, 71 children were taken for ophthalmological examination at 1 month of age; 60 attended the pediatric consultation at 4 months; 56 children attended the neurological evaluation at 6 months and 50 at 12 months.
CONCLUSIONS: The Gerar Cohort successfully implemented its recruitment and biospecimen collection procedures within public healthcare services.

articles.title: Sexual Function, Medication-Related Motivation and Knowledge, and Perceived Spousal Support in Women with Eczema: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Atila D, Yeşiltepe A, Bulbuloglu S et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Eczema may affect not only dermatological health but also sexual well-being, treatment-related behaviors, and interpersonal relationships. Examining sexual function alongside medication-related factors and perceived spousal support may provide a broader understanding of women's experiences of eczema. Methods: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate sexual dysfunction, medication adherence, and perceived spousal support and to examine the relationships among these factors in women with eczema. The study included 218 women diagnosed with eczema who were regularly followed in the dermatology unit of a private hospital in İzmir, Turkey. Data were collected using a personal information form, the Modified Morisky Adherence Scale (MMAS), the Spousal Support Scale (SS), and the Arizona Sexual Experiences Scale (ASEX). Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, Spearman sensitivity analyses, and three-step hierarchical multiple linear regression were performed. Results: All participants were using antihistamines, and 71.6% reported using them twice daily. According to the ASEX cutoff score, 59.2% of participants screened positive for potential sexual dysfunction, while 56.9% reported not receiving spousal support. The mean ASEX score was 16.19 ± 8.94, and the mean MMAS score was 2.53 ± 2.21. ASEX scores were moderately and positively correlated with MMAS scores (r = 0.528, p < 0.001), whereas the SS total score was not significantly correlated with ASEX (r = -0.026, p = 0.704). ASEX scores were found to be positively correlated with scores on both the motivation (r = 0.568; p < 0.001) and knowledge (r = 0.426; p < 0.001) subdimensions. In hierarchical regression, MMAS scores remained positively associated with ASEX scores after adjustment for age, menopausal status, chronic disease, and antihistamine use duration, although the association was considerably weaker (B = 0.700, p = 0.038); this model explained 51.4% of the variance. Adding sexual intercourse frequency increased the explained variance to 70.5%, and the MMAS association was no longer statistically significant (B = 0.316, p = 0.237). Conclusions: Sexual dysfunction was common in this sample of women with eczema. In bivariate analyses, higher scores for medication-related motivation and knowledge were associated with greater sexual dysfunction. The association between total MMAS and ASEX scores remained significant after adjustment for clinical factors; however, this association…

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Gynecology and Obstetrics: Medico-Legal, Ethical, and Governance Challenges-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Santangelo G, De Angelis G, Muzii L et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering gynecologic and obstetric imaging, risk prediction, decision support, robotic surgery, remote monitoring, and patient communication. An estimated 260,000 maternal deaths occurred worldwide in 2023, and in England obstetric claims account for 11% of clinical negligence claims but 55% of their value. AI errors, bias, or opacity in this specialty therefore carry major clinical and legal consequences. Objective: To synthesize the principal medico-legal and bioethical challenges associated with AI in gynecology and obstetrics and to propose a lifecycle governance framework for responsible clinical adoption. Methods: A narrative review with thematic synthesis was conducted.
