PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for records published from January 2020 to August 2026, supplemented by citation chaining and official legal databases. Two reviewers screened 131 records against predefined eligibility criteria; 41 sources (36 publications and 5 legal instruments) were included and analyzed thematically. Selection is reported in a PRISMA-style flow diagram. Results: Six connected risk domains were derived from five prespecified themes, namely validation and generalizability; professional competence and automation bias; distributed liability and evidentiary opacity; informed consent and patient autonomy; privacy and cybersecurity of reproductive data; and discrimination, access, and reproductive justice. Generative AI adds risks of hallucination, non-reproducibility, persuasive framing, and undocumented use. Existing law does not eliminate clinician responsibility: accountability is shared across developers, institutions, and professionals, but clinical judgment and documented oversight remain central. In the European Union, Medical Device Regulation and GDPR obligations already apply, whereas AI Act requirements for AI-enabled medical devices apply from August 2028 and the revised Product Liability Directive covers products placed on the market after 9 December 2026; causation and professional fault remain governed by national law. Conclusions: Safe adoption requires more than technical accuracy. We translate the findings into seven actionable institutional requirements, namely accountable ownership, minimum local validation, role-specific training, auditable documentation, equity monitoring, post-deployment surveillance, and incident reporting. AI should augment-not displace-clinically accountable and…

articles.title: A Protocol for Evaluating the Effectiveness of an Integrated Group Postpartum and Well-Child Care Model on Maternal and Child Health Outcomes.
articles.authors: Gresh A, Kapito E, Mambulasa J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The building and then testing of high-quality maternal and infant health care service delivery models are urgently needed to address the persistent maternal and infant health disparities globally. A range of health system and social drivers contribute to maternal and infant morbidities and mortality, including limited access to care and preventive services and variation in care quality. These poor outcomes have led to calls for a broader redesign of maternal and infant health services and delivery systems. One promising model is group care, which has shown potential for maternal and child health care redesign, but has been studied mainly during the antenatal period. This paper describes the study protocol our team will use to evaluate the effectiveness of group postpartum and well-child care.
METHODS: We will conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial with mixed methods across 16 clinics in Zomba District, Malawi to test the model's impact on select maternal and infant health outcomes. We hypothesize that compared to usual care, women in the intervention group will have decreased postpartum depression symptoms, anemia, and hypertension and infants will have increased vaccination rates and more optimal secondary outcomes for the dyad, such as uptake of family planning, exclusive breastfeeding, childhood development (gross and fine motor skills, social-adaptive development, and nutrition). We will also qualitatively explore clinic- and patient-level implementation facilitators and barriers for group care and the health and social needs that arise in the 12 months after birth for both women and their infants in both arms.
DISCUSSION: This study will be the first to conduct an adequately powered trial of a group postpartum and well-child care model in a low-resource setting. Findings from the study will contribute important evidence on how postpartum and well-child care may be improved during the first year after birth.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov registration number: NCT07414901.

articles.title: Congenital Syphilis in South Africa: A Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Health System Drivers, Prevention, and the Path to Elimination.
articles.authors: Phiri S, Skepu A, Nxumalo Z et al.
articles.abstract: Congenital syphilis (CS), caused by vertical transmission of Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum, remains a major but preventable cause of foetal and neonatal morbidity and mortality globally. Despite established antenatal screening programmes and the availability of effective treatment with benzathine penicillin G (BPG), South Africa continues to experience a substantial burden of maternal and congenital syphilis, with a 2023 national case rate approximately four times the World Health Organization (WHO) elimination target. This narrative review synthesises evidence from peer-reviewed publications, national surveillance reports, and policy documents identified through systematic searches conducted up to September 2026 [searched through August 2026] on congenital syphilis in South Africa. It addresses the microbiology and pathogenesis, epidemiology, clinical burden, diagnostic approaches, health system determinants, and strategies for elimination. Persistent transmission is associated with documented gaps in antenatal booking, repeat screening, treatment completion and partner management, and with recurrent benzathine penicillin shortages; HIV co-infection, poverty and other social and structural factors are likely contributors, but direct evidence for them is more limited. Congenital syphilis remains associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including miscarriage, stillbirth, prematurity, neonatal mortality, and long-term disability. The elimination of congenital syphilis in South Africa requires strengthening antenatal care coverage, universal and repeat syphilis screening, prompt and complete maternal treatment, partner services, enhanced surveillance systems, and closer integration with HIV programmes. Progress towards the country's 2028 elimination target will depend on a coordinated health systems approach aligned with WHO triple-elimination validation criteria.

articles.title: Clinical, Endocrine, and Reproductive Profiles of Patients with Primary Ovarian Insufficiency at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.authors: AlHefdhi HA, Aldeery M, Mahmood SE
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a condition causing hypergonadotropic hypogonadism before age 40, leading to menstrual irregularities, infertility, and estrogen deficiency. This study aimed to describe the clinical, endocrine, and reproductive characteristics of patients diagnosed with primary ovarian insufficiency (POI). and describe the distribution of these clinical and biochemical characteristics.
METHODS: This hospital-based retrospective study was conducted at King Faisal Specialized Hospital and Research Center (KFSHRC) in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Medical records of patients diagnosed with POI between 2008 and 2018 were reviewed and analyzed.
RESULTS: The onset of POI occurred before 20 years of age in 64.1% of patients. The most common presenting symptoms included infertility (50%), menstrual disturbances (42.2%), delayed puberty (25%), and estrogen deficiency (25%). More than half of the patients were overweight or obese (29.7% each). A family history of POI was reported in 12.5% of cases. Autoimmune diseases were present in 60.9% of patients, while dyslipidemia (25%), and psychiatric disorders (14.1%) were also common. A history of abdominal/pelvic surgery (25%), chemotherapy (28.1%), and radiotherapy (7.8%) was noted. Pelvic ultrasonography revealed that 18.5% of patients had normal findings, while 23/54 (42.6%) had gonadal dysgenesis/agenesis, and 16/54 (29.6%) had uterine abnormalities. Vitamin D deficiency was present in 25/35 (71.4%) of patients, while 3/35 (17.1%) had vitamin D insufficiency, and 3/35 (8.6%) had hypervitaminosis D. Diabetes mellitus was observed in 6/60 (10%) of patients. Autoimmune markers were positive in a subset of patients: anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies (15/64, 23.4%), anti-thyroglobulin antibodies (12/64, 18.8%), rheumatoid factor (6/64, 9.4%), and other autoimmune markers 3/64 (4.7%). Bone mineral density was low in 23/44 (52.3%) of patients, and 2/44 (4.5%) had delayed bone age. Karyotype analysis identified Turner syndrome in 6/44 (13.6%) of patients, while 38/44 (86.4%) had a normal 46 XX karyotype. Molecular genetic testing for Fragile X syndrome identified one patient with a single gene mutation (1.6%) and one premutation carrier (1.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, POI was commonly diagnosed before age 20 and was associated with delayed puberty, estrogen deficiency, infertility, and menstrual disturbances. Autoimmune diseases, vitamin D deficiency, and low bone mineral density were also…

articles.title: The Effect of Virtual Reality on Pain and Anxiety During Pap Smear Testing: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Güney BN, Abiç A
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pap smear testing is an important cervical cancer screening procedure; however, the pain, discomfort, and anxiety experienced during the procedure may negatively affect women's screening experiences and adherence to future screening. Virtual reality (VR) is a nonpharmacological intervention that may help manage procedure-related pain and anxiety through immersive distraction. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of VR on pain and anxiety during Pap smear testing.
METHODS: This randomized controlled experimental study included 60 women undergoing Pap smear testing. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 30) or a control group (n = 30). Data were collected using the Personal Information Form, the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-State (STAI-S), and the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). During the Pap smear test procedure, the intervention group watched a relaxing nature video using a VR glasses, whereas the control group received routine nursing care. STAI-S was administered before and after the procedure, and pain intensity was assessed using the VAS after the procedure.
RESULTS: No significant difference was found between the groups in pretest STAI-S scores (39.83 ± 11.00 vs. 41.46 ± 10.10, p = 0.534). However, posttest STAI-S scores were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (24.80 ± 6.70 vs. 40.13 ± 9.58, p < 0.001). Postprocedure VAS pain scores were also significantly lower in the intervention group compared with the control group (1.43 ± 1.25 vs. 2.86 ± 2.43, p = 0.028).
CONCLUSIONS: Virtual reality was effective in reducing pain and anxiety during Pap smear testing. VR may be used as a simple, nonpharmacological nursing intervention to support pain and anxiety management and improve women's comfort during gynecological procedures.

articles.title: Correlates of Health Satisfaction in a Web-Based Sample Enriched for Self-Reported Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Bacușcă ED, Bacușcă AE, Bacușcă AI et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), named polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome by a 2026 global consensus, combines metabolic, dermatological and psychological features. We examined which clinical, anthropometric and symptom-related characteristics were associated with health satisfaction in a web-based sample enriched for self-reported PCOS.
METHODS: Cross-sectional web-based survey using a Romanian-language questionnaire (October-November 2023). Of 212 submissions retained after integrity screening, 159 (75.0%) reported a previous diagnosis of PCOS. Health satisfaction (study-specific five-point item) was analysed with proportional-odds ordinal regression including seven covariates, irrespective of diagnostic status (n = 194). Sensitivity analyses restricted the model to respondents reporting a diagnosis, adjusted for diagnostic status or sociodemographic characteristics and retained all submissions.
RESULTS: Lower health satisfaction was associated with higher body mass index (OR 0.92 per kg/m2; 95% CI 0.87-0.97), self-reported hirsutism (OR 0.43; 95% CI 0.24-0.76) and reported anxiety (OR 0.49; 95% CI 0.28-0.87; reference group mostly "do not know/no answer"). Estimates changed little after these adjustments or with all submissions; among respondents reporting a diagnosis (n = 145), the estimates for self-reported hirsutism and reported anxiety were attenuated and imprecise. Age, menstrual irregularity, infertility diagnosis and dysmenorrhea severity showed no statistically detectable association.
CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory, mutually adjusted associations involve higher body mass index, self-reported hirsutism and endorsement of the questionnaire's anxiety option; the last reflects a response contrast, not clinically assessed anxiety. They warrant confirmation in clinically characterised cohorts using validated instruments.

articles.title: Pregnancy-Recognized Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Maternal-Fetal Outcomes: A Narrative Review of Gestational Rhinitis, Upper-Airway Mechanisms, and Treatment Evidence.
articles.authors: Alas-Pineda C, Ferrer G, Pavón-Varela DJ et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pregnancy-recognized obstructive sleep apnea (POSA) is an operational construct, not a validated biological phenotype, and remains underrecognized in prenatal care. This review synthesizes evidence on POSA-related outcomes, evaluates gestational rhinitis as a candidate contributor to upper-airway vulnerability, and distinguishes pregnancy safety from demonstrated efficacy for OSA-related endpoints. Methods: This structured narrative review, informed by SANRA criteria, used a structured PubMed search (7 March 2026) with targeted supplementary searches through 9 October 2026, across six predefined domains. Results: Pregnancy-recognized OSA is associated in observational studies with hypertensive disorders, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth (in small pregnancy-specific studies), and severe maternal morbidity; residual confounding by obesity precludes causal inference. In a 2024 meta-analysis of randomized and observational studies (n = 809), continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was associated with lower risks of gestational hypertension (RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.47-0.89) and preeclampsia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.50-0.98). Although secondary endpoints in individual trials suggested benefit, the pooled preeclampsia effect was fragile in sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Gestational rhinitis affects approximately one in five pregnant women and is a plausible but untested contributor to pregnancy-recognized OSA. Saline irrigation, budesonide (mainly inhaled-exposure data), and chlorpheniramine have gestational safety data, but the only randomized trial of an intranasal corticosteroid in gestational rhinitis was null, and we identified no study of OSA endpoints. Conclusions: Given the largely observational evidence, objective testing and individualized treatment may be considered in high-risk patients, pending adequately powered trials. CPAP is the standard treatment for objectively confirmed OSA.

articles.title: Association Between Self-Reported Climacteric Symptoms and Pain Intensity: A Cross-Sectional Study of 6000 Japanese Men and Women.
articles.authors: Shiro Y, Inoue S, Arai YC et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The prevalence of pain increases with age, particularly in middle-aged women, when sex hormone levels fluctuate drastically. While climacteric symptoms and their relationship with pain have been extensively studied in women, it remains unclear whether these symptoms and their association with pain are limited to women. This study aimed to investigate the association between climacteric symptoms and pain in both women and men. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey using a non-probability quota panel conducted in March 2024 assessed the presence, location, and intensity of pain during the past 28 days (numerical rating scale ≥ 1, irrespective of pain duration) among 6000 Japanese adults aged 30-59 years (3000 women, 3000 men). Climacteric symptoms were assessed using the Simplified Menopausal Index for women and the Aging Males' Symptoms scale for men. Quality of life was assessed using the EQ-5D-5L. Pain intensity was analyzed only in participants with pain (433 women, 488 men). Results: As symptom scores increased, both men and women showed higher pain prevalence and intensity and lower quality of life. Symptom scores were positively correlated with pain intensity in both sexes (Spearman's ρ = 0.35 in women, 0.39 in men), with no evidence of a sex difference (interaction p = 0.991). Somatic scores showed the strongest associations (standardized β = 0.21 in women, 0.22 in men), followed by vasomotor symptoms in women (β = 0.16) and psychological symptoms in men (β = 0.20). The associations remained after excluding pain-related items. Conclusions: Climacteric symptoms were associated with pain intensity in both men and women, without clear evidence of a sex difference. Causality cannot be inferred from this cross-sectional design; prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Cross-Phenotype Genomics Reveals Heterogeneous Genetic Susceptibility Architecture Relevant to Menopause.
articles.authors: Torres De Souza G, Vila-Vecilla L, Russo V et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Menopause is accompanied by substantial interindividual variation in hormonal, metabolic, cardiovascular, skeletal, and thrombotic phenotypes. Although the genetics of reproductive ageing and individual menopause-associated traits are increasingly characterised, the cross-phenotype architecture of individual menopause-relevant germline variants remains less well defined. Methods: We performed a variant-centred genomic analysis of 31 prespecified menopause-relevant germline variants. Cross-trait evidence comprised 766 variant-trait records across 52 phenotypes and was integrated with a targeted Pan-UK Biobank phenome-wide association study (PheWAS; 1462 tests across 57 endpoints), clinically relevant outcome analyses, linkage disequilibrium assessment, FinnGen R12 venous thromboembolism (VTE) associations, regional fine-mapping, and molecular annotation. Association strength, between-study heterogeneity, phenotypic breadth and sharing, and locus resolution were evaluated as distinct evidence dimensions. Results: In total, 25 of 31 variants showed at least one cross-trait association at p < 1 × 10-5 and 21 reached genome-wide significance. Phenotypic breadth varied markedly, from restricted profiles to 16 associated phenotypes, and strong associations frequently coexisted with substantial between-study heterogeneity. In Pan-UK Biobank, 222 associations involving 25 variants met false-discovery-rate correction, spanning hormonal, reproductive, cardiometabolic, skeletal, nutritional, hepatic, and neurological phenotypes. Cross-phenotype reconstruction identified recurrent connectivity through sex hormone-binding globulin, testosterone, adiposity, lipid, and skeletal traits, while linkage disequilibrium analyses distinguished phenotypic sharing from genetic redundancy. Clinically, F5 rs6025 and F2 rs1799963 showed strong VTE associations in FinnGen (OR 2.387 and 1.921, respectively), but markedly different locus resolution: rs6025 had posterior inclusion probability (PIP) 0.979 and constituted a single-variant 95% credible set, whereas rs1799963 had PIP 0.596 within a four-variant credible set. Conclusions: Menopause-relevant germline variation exhibits heterogeneous cross-phenotype architectures in which association strength, phenotypic breadth, between-study consistency, genetic independence, and locus resolution are not interchangeable. This variant-centred framework provides a basis for evaluating inherited susceptibility relevant to menopause…

articles.title: Correlation Between Clinicopathological Findings, Cervical Smear, and HPV Results: A Retrospective Study of Women Referred for Colposcopy.
articles.authors: Kökbudak N, Solmaz M, Kılınç F et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the association of cervical cytology, human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes, and colposcopic findings with histopathological outcomes in women referred for colposcopy. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 756 women who underwent colposcopy with cervical biopsy at a tertiary center between January 2022 and June 2025 and had HPV genotyping and conventional cytology results. The primary endpoint was cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) on biopsy; the highest grade across biopsy and conization specimens and CIN3+ were secondary endpoints. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, and diagnostic accuracy was reported according to STARD 2015. Results: CIN2+ was found in 85 women (11.2%). HPV-16 positivity (OR: 2.87; 95% CI: 1.72-4.77), epithelial cell abnormality on cytology (OR: 4.28; 95% CI: 2.05-8.92), and positive colposcopy (OR: 3.39; 95% CI: 2.00-5.73) were independently associated with higher odds of CIN2+. Adding colposcopy to a pre-colposcopy model increased the AUC from 0.730 to 0.770 (p = 0.034; optimism-corrected 0.753). Colposcopy had a sensitivity of 71.8% (95% CI: 61.4-80.2%) and an NPV of 94.6% (95% CI: 92.1-96.3%), but 24 of 85 CIN2+ cases (28.2%) had a negative colposcopic impression; results were similar for the highest-grade endpoint (92 CIN2+ cases). Conclusions: In this referral population, HPV-16, cytological abnormality, and colposcopic impression provided complementary information on the odds of CIN2+. Because more than one-quarter of CIN2+ cases were not colposcopically apparent, a negative colposcopy should not be considered sufficient to exclude high-grade disease, particularly in women with HPV-16 positivity or abnormal cytology. Prospective validation is required before these associations are used for triage.

articles.title: Legionella Pneumonia in the Molecular Diagnostics Era: From Intracellular Pathogenesis to Precision Management.
articles.authors: Liu L, Zhang B, Sang K et al.
articles.abstract: Legionella pneumophila is a major cause of severe community-acquired pneumonia and one of the most lethal respiratory pathogens. Nevertheless, it remains substantially underdiagnosed because conventional diagnostic assays are slow, insensitive, or limited to specific serogroups. In this narrative review, we integrate fragmented literature regarding Legionella pneumonia, covering its intracellular pathogenesis, clinical spectrum and patient management. Evidence was identified through a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC (23 September 2026) and prioritized by design, with primary clinical and mechanistic studies and systematic reviews taking precedence over narrative summaries and with society guidelines used to anchor management recommendations. We argue that this field is undergoing a diagnostic paradigm shift fueled by culture-independent molecular assays. We first review the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system and intracellular lifecycle that allow Legionella to replicate within macrophages while evading host innate immunity. We then summarize the full clinical spectrum, ranging from self-limited Pontiac fever to fatal Legionnaires' disease complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome, as well as epidemiological characteristics including waterborne transmission and outbreak risks. The core of this review examines how metagenomic next-generation sequencing, targeted NGS, plasma microbial cell-free DNA and syndromic multiplex PCR are reshaping diagnostic workflows, and compares the strengths and limitations of these novel tools with urinary antigen testing and bacterial culture. Pooled estimates place the sensitivity of urinary antigen testing at 0.79 overall and 0.86 for serogroup 1, and that of respiratory PCR at 97.4%, with specificities of 1.00 and 0.99, respectively. We further evaluate contemporary therapeutic evidence, including fluoroquinolone versus macrolide monotherapy, combination regimens, and adjunctive corticosteroid therapy. Throughout this review, we highlight that Legionella is a pathogen whose clinical presentation, diagnostic yield and prognosis are highly dependent on host immune status, exposure setting and appropriate diagnostic stewardship. We conclude by identifying critical knowledge gaps and outlining a framework for diagnosis-driven precision antimicrobial management of this underrecognized pathogen. That framework is an evidence-informed synthesis rather than a validated pathway: no prospective study has yet…

articles.title: Retinal Vasculature as a Non-Invasive Window for Preeclampsia Prediction and Assessment: From Fundoscopy to Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Retinal Imaging.
articles.authors: Baroutis D, Fanaki M, Koukoumpanis K et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, and effective prevention depends on the early identification of women at risk. Because the disorder is fundamentally a state of systemic endothelial dysfunction and microvascular maladaptation, the retina has long attracted interest as a candidate in vivo biomarker. It is the only vascular bed that can be visualised directly, repeatedly and non-invasively. This review appraises retinal assessment across four modality classes, classifying each study by the timing of imaging relative to diagnosis to distinguish early prediction from diagnostic discrimination, severity assessment and long-term follow-up. Qualitative fundoscopy reliably grades hypertensive retinopathy but is subjective and insensitive in mild disease. Quantitative retinal vessel analysis links narrower retinal vessels with the hypertensive disorders of pregnancy; in one longitudinal cohort, pressure-corrected arteriolar and venular calibre was reduced from 13 weeks in women who later developed preeclampsia, although effects were modest. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography studies, almost all performed after diagnosis, report choroidal and microvascular changes of inconsistent direction and, therefore, inform diagnosis and severity assessment rather than prediction. Ophthalmic artery Doppler may offer adjunctive discrimination. Two single-centre deep learning models applied to early-pregnancy fundus photographs reported areas under the curve of 0.87-0.88 for preeclampsia, but without external validation, calibration or head-to-head comparison with established first-trimester screening. Retinal imaging is, therefore, a mechanistically grounded but unproven avenue for preeclampsia prediction. Prospective pre-diagnostic cohorts, standardised acquisition, adjustment for blood pressure and other confounders, and externally validated, calibrated models tested for incremental value over established screening are required. Only then can retinal biomarkers, particularly artificial intelligence-assisted analysis with portable fundus cameras, be adopted as a scalable screening adjunct, including in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Eosinophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Potential Inflammatory Marker Associated with Endometrial Cancer: An Analysis of NHANES 2017-2023 and an Independent Institutional Cohort.
articles.authors: Moon H, Kim BY, Kim S
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluates the Eosinophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (ELR) as a systemic inflammatory marker associated with endometrial cancer using a two-stage approach combining a national population-based discovery analysis of self-reported uterine cancer (NHANES) and an independent institutional cohort of histologically confirmed endometrial cancer. Methods: In the discovery cohort, survey-weighted logistic regression was conducted among 6859 women from NHANES 2017-2023, comparing 6757 non-cancer controls with 102 women with self-reported gynecological cancers (45 cervical, 38 uterine, and 19 ovarian); the uterine cancer model was adjusted for age and BMI. In the independent institutional cohort, 901 patients with histologically confirmed primary endometrial cancer and 200 benign surgical controls were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test, unadjusted logistic regression, and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Adjusted analyses were not performed in this cohort. Results: In NHANES, mean ELR was higher in the uterine cancer group than in controls (0.1204 vs. 0.0868, p = 0.0193). After adjustment for age and BMI, ELR was associated with higher odds of self-reported uterine cancer (OR = 10.288 per 1.0-unit increase, 95% CI: 1.722-61.472, p = 0.0130; equivalent to OR = 1.26 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI: 1.06-1.51). In the institutional cohort, median ELR was significantly higher in endometrial cancer patients than in benign controls (0.1180 [IQR: 0.1380] vs. 0.0487 [IQR: 0.0574], p < 0.001). Unadjusted logistic regression showed that higher ELR was associated with endometrial cancer (OR = 2.725 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI: 2.154-3.515, p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed moderate discriminative capability (AUC = 0.7147, 95% CI: 0.6780-0.7514), with an exploratory (non-validated) cut-off of 0.0810 (sensitivity: 65.5%; specificity: 74.8%). Conclusions: Higher ELR was associated with self-reported uterine cancer in NHANES after adjustment for age and BMI, and with histologically confirmed endometrial cancer in an unadjusted institutional analysis, with moderate discriminative performance. These hypothesis-generating findings do not establish an independent association; ELR may be a candidate complementary, non-invasive marker, but its clinical utility requires confirmation in adjusted, prospective studies.

articles.title: Decreased Circulating Glutamine and Myo-Inositol in Cervical Cancer: Exploratory NMR Metabolomics and Internal Discrimination Using Their Additive Feature (MQ).
articles.authors: Kumar P, Nigam N, Gupta A et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but circulating NMR metabolite signatures require rigorous statistical assessment before clinical interpretation. Methods: Serum metabolite concentrations were analyzed in 33 cervical cancer (CC) cases and 31 normal controls (NC). Group differences across 35 primary metabolites were assessed using Welch's t-test with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) control; Mann-Whitney tests were used as distribution-robust sensitivity analyses. Age-adjusted linear models with HC3 robust standard errors were fitted for each primary metabolite (primary analysis: raw concentrations; sensitivity analysis: log2-transformed concentrations), with FDR correction across the 35 models. MQ was defined as [glutamine] + [myo-inositol]. ROC discrimination was summarized using stratified-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and paired DeLong testing compared MQ with glutamine. Results: Glutamine (CC 229.7 ± 102.2 μM; NC 434.8 ± 123.8 μM) and myo-inositol (CC 18.3 ± 8.8 μM; NC 35.8 ± 11.0 μM) were lower in CC, and both remained significant after age adjustment and FDR correction. Within CC, serum glutamine was strongly inversely correlated with tumor length (Spearman ρ = -0.94, n = 31; exploratory, requires independent replication). Apparent ROC AUCs were 0.906 for glutamine, 0.889 for myo-inositol, and 0.919 for MQ. The paired DeLong comparison of MQ versus glutamine was not statistically significant (AUC difference 0.0132; approximate 95% CI -0.0031 to 0.0295; p = 0.113). Repeated cross-validation is reported as within-cohort resampling performance and not independent validation. Conclusions: The findings support lower circulating glutamine and myo-inositol in this cohort. MQ is an exploratory additive feature without demonstrated superiority over glutamine alone; external validation and adjustment for additional clinical confounders are required.

articles.title: First-Trimester Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index, APRI and FIB-4 Scores in Women Who Later Develop Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy: Association with the Disease and with Perinatal Outcomes in a Retrospective Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Ceylan M, Balcı MF, Öktem A et al.
articles.abstract: Objective: To examine whether the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), AST-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score, derived from routine first-trimester tests, are associated with subsequent intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) and, within ICP, with adverse perinatal outcomes. Materials and Methods: This retrospective case-control study included 115 women with ICP and 64 controls with normal liver tests. Indices were derived from 11- to 14-week values. The two primary hypotheses concerned APRI and SII (Bonferroni α = 0.025); all other analyses were exploratory, with false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment. Within ICP, the co-primary outcomes were a composite of preterm birth, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, fetal distress, neonatal intensive care admission or 1-min Apgar score < 7, and the same composite excluding preterm birth, because delivery timing was protocol-driven by bile acids. Results: APRI (AUC 0.786; 95% CI 0.718-0.852; p < 0.001) and SII (AUC 0.615; 0.530-0.697; p = 0.011) were higher in women who later developed ICP; FIB-4 was not. ALT alone discriminated better (AUC 0.895; DeLong p = 0.003), APRI and SII added no discrimination beyond ALT (AUC 0.904; p = 0.465), and when cases were restricted to the transaminase range of controls (ALT ≤ 31 U/L), the AUC of APRI fell to 0.644. Within ICP, no index demonstrated an association with either composite outcome (all FDR-adjusted q > 0.15), although power was only ~45% for an AUC of 0.60. Bile acids were associated with the composite excluding preterm birth (AUC 0.681; adjusted OR 1.43 per 10 µmol/L; 1.16-1.76); the stronger association with the full composite (AUC 0.754) is partly definitional. Conclusions: First-trimester APRI and SII carry a group-level signal in women who later develop ICP, but this signal largely reflects transaminases and is inflated by control selection. The indices did not demonstrate an association with perinatal outcomes, although small effects cannot be excluded; surveillance and delivery timing should continue to rely on bile acids.

articles.title: DBS Direct Elution and Multiplex Digital PCR for SMN1 and SMN2 Copy-Number and CFTR Variant Detection: Development and Validation of a Molecular Screening Workflow.
articles.authors: Dikoglou-Tzanetatou E, Skopa I, Poulou M et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Scalable molecular workflows may facilitate carrier screening for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and cystic fibrosis (CF). This study aimed to develop and validate a dried blood spot (DBS)-based multiplex digital PCR (dPCR) workflow for SMN1 and SMN2 copy-number analysis and targeted detection of CFTR p.Phe508del. Methods: The workflow combined direct DNA elution with multiplex dPCR. Analytical validation used 50 previously characterized samples, with multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) and Sanger sequencing as reference methods. The workflow was subsequently applied to 1670 women from Crete and Ikaria, Greece, followed by targeted testing of 10 partners. Results: All 50 directly eluted samples amplified successfully. dPCR showed complete agreement with reference methods. Repeatability coefficients of variation were below 5%. Copy-number classification performance estimates are apparent, as thresholds were derived and evaluated in the same small validation cohort. Among 1670 women screened, 34 (2.04%) were identified as SMN1 carriers and 20 (1.20%) as CFTR p.Phe508del carriers. Partner testing identified two carrier couples. Conclusions: The DBS-based multiplex dPCR workflow demonstrated complete analytical concordance with reference methods in this preliminary validation and was implemented in a population screening cohort. Its targeted scope leaves residual carrier risk, requiring appropriate counseling. Larger independent validation and formal throughput and cost assessments are needed before routine implementation.

articles.title: Persistent High-Risk HPV Positivity Without Confirmed CIN2+: Diagnostic Uncertainty, Risk Stratification, and Management-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Gavril ST, Matasariu DR, Scripcariu IS et al.
articles.abstract: Primary high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing detects cervical precancer earlier than cytology and, by design, generates a large population of virus-positive women in whom high-grade disease is not confirmed. Where the infection persists, the clinician must judge whether a negative or non-diagnostic assessment reflects absence of disease or failure of detection. This review asks what that state represents, which tools reclassify absolute CIN3+ risk, and how surveillance and intervention should be balanced. This narrative review synthesises relevant evidence from published studies and international guidance on persistent hrHPV infection, diagnostic assessment, risk stratification and management, with reporting guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). Persistent hrHPV positivity without confirmed CIN2+ is a heterogeneous risk state, not a diagnosis, and covers three clinical situations that should not be conflated. Absolute CIN3+ risk is set principally by genotype and by the duration of type-specific persistence; genotype alone spans an approximately twenty-fold range of immediate risk in hrHPV-positive screening populations. Pooled colposcopic sensitivity for CIN2+ was approximately 75% in heterogeneous referral populations, while one selected retrospective series of cytology-negative hrHPV-positive women reported sensitivity near 50%. Selected referral cohorts have reported CIN2+/HSIL detection yields of approximately 8% to 14% among persistently hrHPV-positive women with normal cytology; these composite, selection-dependent estimates should not be read as the prevalence of occult CIN3+. Extended genotyping and p16/Ki-67 dual-stain cytology carry guideline-adopted management rules, although validation specifically after documented persistence remains limited. Controlled evidence for treating persistent hrHPV without confirmed CIN2+ is sparse and conflicting. Recent randomised trials of vaginal interventions report discordant short-term virological results, and none establishes durable clearance or a reduction in CIN3+ risk. Short-term loss of HPV detectability is not equivalent to prevention of precancer, and management should remain risk-based.

articles.title: CD138-Positive Plasma Cells in the Endometrium of Women with a Caesarean Scar Defect.
articles.authors: Rathberger K, Kappelmeyer M, Jungbauer-Oberheinrich J et al.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study seeks to assess the prevalence of CD138-positive plasma cells in endometrial biopsies from women undergoing surgery for symptomatic caesarean scar defect (CSD) and examine associations with niche morphology, defect size, symptoms, and surgical approach. Study design: In this prospective single-centre study, women undergoing surgery for symptomatic CSD between January 2024 and June 2026 were included if an endometrial biopsy had been assessed for CD138. Plasma-cell counts were categorised as negative (0 cells/HPF), borderline (1-4 cells/HPF), or elevated (≥5 cells/HPF). Preoperative niche morphology was assessed by transvaginal ultrasound. Associations with CD138 status were tested using Mann-Whitney U and Fisher's exact tests and multivariable logistic regression. Results: Of 235 surgically treated women, 196 had an assessable CD138 result. CD138 positivity was present in 26 (13.3%); 19 (9.7%) had 1-4 cells and seven (3.6%) > 4 cells. CD138 status was not associated with defect size, uterine position, inclusion cysts, concomitant peritoneal endometriosis, surgical approach, or any recorded symptom. The absence of associations persisted after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions: Endometrial CD138-positive plasma cells were present in a minority of women with symptomatic CSD and did not reflect defect morphology, severity, or symptom burden. Routine CD138 testing cannot be justified on the basis of niche subtype or defect size.

articles.title: Incidence, Prognosis, and Management of Occult Endometrial Carcinoma After Hysterectomy for Benign Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Chen YH, Ding DC
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Occult endometrial carcinoma, incidentally diagnosed after hysterectomy for presumed benign disease, raises concerns regarding its incidence, the prognostic effects of minimally invasive surgery and morcellation, and subsequent management. This systematic review synthesized the available evidence and performed meta-analysis where appropriate. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register were searched using a sensitivity-tested strategy. After de-duplication and screening, 76 studies met the eligibility criteria. Incidence was pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis of proportions with the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation. Subgroup analyses examined surgical contexts, including hysterectomy for benign disease, morcellation-specific cohorts, and pelvic organ prolapse surgery. Survival and management outcomes were synthesized narratively. Results: Among 68 studies with extractable denominators, the pooled incidence (proportion of hysterectomies with carcinoma on final pathology) of occult endometrial carcinoma following hysterectomy for benign disease was 0.33% (95% prediction interval, 0.04-0.87%). Incidence was lowest in selected morcellation cohorts (0.22%) and higher in unselected benign hysterectomy cohorts (0.33%) and prolapse populations (0.43%; test for subgroup differences, p = 0.03), with substantially higher rates among older patients. The pooled incidence of occult uterine malignancies, including sarcoma, was 0.54%. For endometrial carcinoma specifically, the limited observational evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between power morcellation or laparoscopic surgery and poorer survival, although confidence intervals were wide. However, morcellation was associated with increased mortality among patients with uterine sarcoma. Occult endometrial carcinomas were predominantly early-stage and low-grade, with 81.8% classified as International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics IA, and approximately 91% achieving 5-year overall survival. In a small series of selected high-risk patients, completion staging resulted in upstaging in 25% and informed adjuvant treatment decisions. Limited observational data did not demonstrate a statistically significant survival benefit of complementary lymphadenectomy, although estimates were imprecise. Conclusions: Occult endometrial carcinoma occurs in approximately 0.2-0.4% of hysterectomies performed for benign disease, with a…

articles.title: Integrating Assisted Reproductive Technologies, Biobanking, and Genomic Rescue for Endangered Wildlife: A Vertebrate-Focused Review.
articles.authors: Khan I, Khalil AAK, Rungsiwiwut R et al.
articles.abstract: Assisted reproductive technologies (ART) provide opportunities for conservation of endangered wildlife, but their use is still limited by species-specific reproductive physiology, variable gamete competence, cryoinjury, and lack of validation of new approaches. This narrative review covers ART, biobanking, somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT), induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), in vitro gametogenesis (IVG) and conservation genomics in vertebrates. Key molecular barriers include oxidative and mitochondrial damage, aberrant embryonic genome activation, incomplete epigenetic reprogramming, nuclear-mitochondrial incompatibility and defective germ-cell differentiation. Technological readiness is used to evaluate the evidence and separate demonstrated reproductive outcomes from experimental proof of concept, and indirect findings from domestic or laboratory models. Semen cryopreservation and artificial insemination are established in selected species, while embryo-based interventions remain species-dependent and stem-cell-derived reproductive approaches require functional validation. We propose an integrated decision framework linking reproductive diagnosis, biobanking, genomic donor selection, technological readiness, animal welfare, and resource allocation with reproductive and population-level outcomes. Importantly, laboratory milestones alone cannot demonstrate conservation success without sustained genetic contribution across multiple subsequent generations. Successful translation depends on species-specific protocols, standardized endpoints, and evidence of genetically valuable offspring survival, reproduction, and contribution to long-term population viability.

articles.title: Multicenter Evaluation of Decentralized Homologous Recombination Deficiency Testing for Enhanced Molecular Diagnosis of Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Vargas-Parra G, Sesé M, Hernández-Illán E et al.
articles.abstract: Assessment of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and tumor BRCA1/2 mutation status in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) is clinically relevant for treatment decisions and for identifying tumors that may benefit from poly(adenosine diphosphate-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. The Myriad MyChoice® CDx HRD (M-HRD) assay is an established clinically validated HRD testing platform that is performed as a send-out test. We conducted a multicenter pilot study to assess the analytical feasibility and interlaboratory agreement of decentralized testing using the SOPHiA DDM™ Dx HRD Solution (SG-HRD). Three hospitals each contributed eight clinical HGSOC samples previously tested with M-HRD or with SG-HRD in a send-out platform. All centers independently prepared SG-HRD libraries and sequenced the complete set of 24 samples. Agreement with M-HRD was evaluated separately from comparisons with previous SG-HRD send-out results. Among specimens with interpretable M-HRD, overall percent agreement with local SG-HRD results was 95.0% (19/20), 90.0% (18/20), and 88.9% (16/18) at the three hospitals. BRCA1/2 variant calls were concordant with previous testing. Overall, the comparison with previous analyses by Myriad genetics or with previous SOPHiA GENETICS send-out results showed a high level of agreement, with discordances mainly observed in samples with values close to the classification threshold. The small, selected cohort, limited clinical replication, and absence of treatment-outcome assessment restrict precision estimates, generalizability, and conclusions regarding clinical validity. These findings support the analytical feasibility of decentralized SG-HRD testing, but larger studies are needed to characterize performance across a broader range of specimens and testing conditions.

articles.title: Bile Acid Stress Disrupts Homeostasis and Placental Functional Programs in Human First-Trimester Trophoblast Organoids.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Li L, Zheng S et al.
articles.abstract: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is characterized by elevated maternal bile acids (BAs), yet their effects on human trophoblast organization and transcriptional responses remain incompletely understood. Here, we used human first-trimester trophoblast organoids (TOs) to characterize cellular and transcriptional responses to a defined six-component BA mixture (50-150 μM). BA exposure disrupted organoid architecture and intercellular organization, with attenuated proliferation-associated features and more prominent SDC1 staining. These changes were accompanied by increased DNA fragmentation and cleaved caspase-3 staining and by reduced ATP-dependent viability, supporting an apoptotic component of BA-associated trophoblast injury. Bulk RNA sequencing after exposure to 150 μM BA for 96 h identified 413 differentially expressed genes, of which 364 were downregulated and 49 were upregulated. Downregulated transcripts were primarily associated with placental endocrine and secretory processes, epithelial organization, cell adhesion, and transport, whereas a smaller subset of lipid-handling genes was upregulated. RT-qPCR confirmed concordant upregulation of PLIN2 and ABCG1 in two independent donor-derived TO lines. Collectively, these findings show that BA mixture exposure is associated with structural injury and altered transcriptional profiles in human TOs, thereby providing insight into trophoblast responses to BA stress.

articles.title: Extracellular Vesicles in Pregnancy: From Maternal-Fetal Communication to Environmental Perturbation.
articles.authors: Affranchi F, Aloi N, Cosentini I et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy is a uniquely sensitive moment during which environmental exposures may have profound and long-lasting consequences for maternal health, placental function, and fetal development. A successful pregnancy depends on continuous molecular communication among maternal, placental, and fetal compartments. The disruption of these processes by environmental stressors may increase the risk of pregnancy complications, impaired neurodevelopment, and susceptibility to non-communicable diseases later in life. Pregnant women are exposed to dynamic mixtures of chemical, physical, occupational, behavioral, and social stressors from the air, diet, drinking water, consumer products, and residential or workplace environments. The pregnancy exposome framework integrates these external exposures with internal biological responses, including oxidative stress, inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, epigenetic alterations, and changes in circulating biomolecules. However, the mechanisms through which exposure-related signals are transmitted across the maternal-placental-fetal unit remain incompletely understood. Extracellular vesicles may be a key component of this communication network as they transfer protected molecular cargoes, including proteins, lipids, metabolites, and regulatory nucleic acids. Understanding how environmental exposures modify extracellular vesicle biogenesis, composition, and function may reveal mechanisms linking the pregnancy exposome to placental dysfunction, adverse pregnancy outcomes, fetal programming, and early biomarkers of biological effects. This review examines the role of extracellular vesicles in physiological maternal-fetal communication and critically summarizes current human and experimental evidence on how environmental exposures may affect EV characteristics and function during pregnancy, with particular attention to their potential involvement in placental dysfunction and adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal FNDC5 and ADIPOQ Genetic Variants as Potential Modulators of Susceptibility to Spontaneous Preterm Birth.
articles.authors: Kadivnik M, Zlatunić P, Drinić M et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) is a complex and heterogeneous pregnancy outcome in which maternal metabolic and endocrine pathways may contribute to susceptibility to preterm delivery. This study investigated whether two maternal genetic variants involved in metabolic signaling, ADIPOQ rs266729 and FNDC5 rs1746661, are associated with preterm birth (PTB) in a Croatian population. This case-control study included 401 women: 200 with PTB and 201 with term delivery. Maternal genomic DNA was isolated from peripheral blood, and both variants were genotyped using TaqMan-based real-time PCR. Genotype and allele distributions, inheritance models, allelic combinations, logistic regression, and gene-gene interaction were analyzed. Neither variant was significantly associated with overall PTB, and no significant gene-gene interaction was observed (p = 0.18). In early PTB, only a borderline, non-significant tendency toward a higher ADIPOQ rs266729 G allele frequency was found (39% vs. 27%; OR 1.74, 95% CI 0.99-3.04; p = 0.05), which was not supported by genotype, inheritance-model, or regression analyses. The G-T allelic combination was more frequent in early PTB (13.6% vs. 4.6%; p = 0.03) but not after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (adjusted p = 0.09). No significant association between the investigated variants and PTB was demonstrated. The borderline findings in early PTB are hypothesis-generating and require replication in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Angiotensin II-Induced Cardiac Fibrosis: Genomic and Molecular Drivers, Emerging Biomarkers and Therapeutic Perspectives.
articles.authors: Martínez-Rodríguez NL, Campos-González JA, López-Camarillo C et al.
articles.abstract: Chronically elevated angiotensin II (Ang II) drives adverse cardiac remodelling, converting a reparative response into progressive interstitial and perivascular fibrosis that stiffens the ventricle and precedes overt heart failure. Acting through the angiotensin II type 1 receptor, Ang II generates reactive oxygen species, recruits and polarises immune cells and activates resident fibroblasts, converging on transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-dependent and mechanotransductive programmes that drive myofibroblast differentiation and excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. The magnitude of this response varies between patients: germline variation in renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) genes, loci for heart failure and imaging-defined fibrosis, epigenomic reprogramming of the fibroblast, non-coding RNA networks and metabolic rewiring of collagen-producing cells all modulate the transition from compensated hypertrophy to fibrotic failure. This review integrates these genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic layers with the signalling architecture of Ang II-induced fibrosis, and reviews the circulating biomarkers-collagen turnover peptides, matricellular and immune mediators, non-coding RNAs and cell-free DNA methylation signatures-that could detect fibrotic activity before remodelling becomes irreversible. We then consider why fibrosis regression under RAAS blockade appears heterogeneous, which emerging targets are mechanistically credible, and how genotype-biomarker-imaging phenotyping could enrich antifibrotic trials. Priorities for ancestrally diverse cohorts and standardised biomarker methodology are identified.

articles.title: Hypoxia-Associated Glycolytic-Lipogenic Reprogramming and Impaired Antigen Presentation in SPP1+ Tumor-Associated Macrophages in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Zuo X, Huang S, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer has an immunosuppressive microenvironment in which SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are linked to poor prognosis and immune evasion, yet their molecular features and metabolic mechanisms remain unclear. We therefore set out to determine whether SPP1 marks a discrete TAM subpopulation or a functional state in treatment-naïve high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), to define the transcriptional and metabolic program that accompanies it, and to test whether local hypoxia is associated with it. Tumor-derived, treatment-naïve samples from three single-cell datasets (one lesion per patient; 47 patients) yielded 385,504 cells; Seurat v5 and Harmony were used for clustering, annotation, and batch correction. SPP1+/SPP1- macrophages were compared by differential expression, GO/KEGG/GSEA, metabolic scoring, and transcription factor inference, and the definition was retested with within-sample SPP1-high versus SPP1-low comparisons and with MSigDB Hallmark gene sets scored by two independent algorithms. Validation used Visium spatial transcriptomics (GSE263920), TCGA-OV (n = 429), CD8+ T cell exhaustion analysis, CellChat and a syngeneic ID8 model. Of 64,067 macrophages (16.62%), 82.0% were SPP1+; upregulated genes were enriched in glycolysis, monocyte migration and tissue remodeling, whereas MHC class II and neutrophil-related genes were downregulated. At the sample level, glycolysis, fatty acid synthesis and glutaminolysis scores were elevated and the cholesterol synthesis score was reduced, with no evidence of suppressed fatty acid oxidation or oxidative phosphorylation; HIF1A ranked 4th and NR1H3 3rd among 271 transcription factors. All 8 spatial sections showed positive hypoxia-SPP1 correlations, and hotspots showed elevated glycolysis, EMT, immunosuppression and macrophage scores. No robust association was found between SPP1+ TAM infiltration and CD8+ T cell exhaustion (p = 0.315). MDK-LRP1/SDC1 was the major macrophage-directed input. Immunofluorescence showed SPP1 immunoreactivity in a subset of CD68+ macrophages within HIF1α-rich areas of ID8 tumors, without CD8+PD-1+ T cell aggregation. SPP1+ TAMs therefore correspond to a hypoxic functional state with HIF1A activation, a glycolytic-lipogenic transcriptional program, reduced cholesterol synthesis gene expression and a reduced MHC class II program; protein-level and functional validation, and direct tests of HIF1A dependency, remain necessary.

articles.title: Pregnancy as a Stress Test for β-Cell Autoimmunity: The Autoimmune Phenotype of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.authors: Yanachkova V, Shivarov V, Kostadinov N et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous metabolic disorder comprising pathophysiological phenotypes that differ in their underlying mechanisms, clinical presentation and long-term outcomes. While pregnancy-induced insulin resistance remains the predominant pathogenic mechanism, a subset of women develops hyperglycemia largely because of reduced pancreatic β-cell reserve accompanied by islet autoimmunity. This autoimmune phenotype links gestational diabetes with autoimmune diabetes, but its boundaries and clinical significance remain incompletely defined. We aimed to review current knowledge of the autoimmune phenotype of GDM, with focus on immune pathophysiological mechanisms, biomarkers, clinical characteristics and implications for precision medicine, and to distinguish findings demonstrated directly in GDM from mechanisms extrapolated from type 1 diabetes (T1D). This narrative review was based on a structured PubMed/MEDLINE search from database inception through the end of October 2026, supplemented by targeted searches, manual screening of reference lists, and relevant clinical guidelines and consensus documents. Evidence obtained directly in women with GDM was considered alongside selected mechanistic literature from T1D and adult autoimmune diabetes. In some women with GDM, islet autoantibodies are associated with impaired β-cell function and an increased risk of autoimmune diabetes after delivery. The cellular mechanisms underlying these associations remain insufficiently studied in GDM. Pregnancy may act as a physiological metabolic stress test that exposes previously compensated β-cell dysfunction associated with islet autoimmunity, although its influence on the underlying autoimmune process remains uncertain. Islet autoantibodies are enriched among women with GDM, but their frequency varies widely between populations and assays and is lower after delivery than during pregnancy. The number and persistence of antibodies, particularly when combined with reduced endogenous insulin secretion, carry considerably more prognostic weight than a single positive result. Cellular immune mechanisms are well characterized in T1D but remain largely unvalidated in GDM. Recognition of the autoimmune phenotype extends the concept of GDM beyond a purely glucose-based classification. It is best viewed as a spectrum ranging from isolated seropositivity to pregnancy-unmasked autoimmune diabetes rather than as a uniform…

articles.title: Comparison of Sonidegib and Vismodegib Efficiency in Drug-Sensitive and Resistant Ovarian Cancer Cell Lines-2D and 3D Model Study.
articles.authors: Stasiak P, Sopel J, Płóciennik A et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a leading cause of mortality among gynecological malignancies. Despite the initial effectiveness of chemotherapy, multidrug resistance (MDR), driven by ABC transporters such as P-glycoprotein, limits treatment success by reducing intracellular paclitaxel (PAC) accumulation. Abnormalities in the Cancer Stem Cells signaling pathway Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) play a role in drug resistance development and ovarian cancer progression. We evaluated two Shh pathway inhibitors, Sonidegib (LDE225) and Vismodegib (VIS), in the W1 drug-sensitive ovarian cancer cell line and PAC-resistant sublines, using the 2D monolayer model, as well as the 3D spheroid model, to better simulate conditions of the tumor microenvironment. qPCR analysis showed similar levels of Shh pathway gene expression in 2D and 3D cell culture conditions. PAC-resistant cell lines were 3- to 6-fold more sensitive to both LDE225 and VIS than the PAC-sensitive cell line. LDE225 showed a 6- to 10-fold lower IC50 than Vismodegib, indicating higher potency. Both agents inhibited proliferation and colony formation in a concentration-dependent manner. Differences in IC50 between 2D and 3D dense spheroids formed by the W1 cell line were small, suggesting that high spheroid density does not reduce the activity of LDE225 and VIS against cancer cells. In conclusion, both inhibitors present pleotropic effects against ovarian cancer cells, especially drug-resistant ones, and can be considered as a new treatment opportunity in this cancer. Nevertheless, further investigation of Hedgehog pathway inhibition in more advanced models is required to assess the potential of clinical application for these compounds.

articles.title: Quercetin Suppresses LCN2 and Restores Autophagy via the MAPK/ERK-mTOR Pathway in Bovine Endometrial Epithelial Cells and Attenuates Fibrotic Remodeling in LPS-Induced Mouse Endometritis.
articles.authors: Zhao L, Chen X, Zhou Y et al.
articles.abstract: Bovine endometritis frequently progresses to endometrial fibrosis, a leading cause of implantation failure and infertility in dairy cows, yet the upstream events that disrupt endometrial autophagy during uterine inflammation remain poorly defined, and the anti-fibrotic target of quercetin (Que) in the bovine endometrium is unknown. We therefore combined data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics of healthy and fibrotic bovine endometria (n = 4 per group) with network pharmacology, molecular docking and a cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), gain- and loss-of-function studies in TGF-β1-stimulated primary bovine endometrial epithelial cells (BEECs), and a 48 h LPS-induced mouse endometritis model in female C57BL/6 mice. LCN2 was markedly upregulated in fibrotic endometria and was prioritized among five candidate targets; docking predicted binding within the LCN2 pocket, and CETSA showed increased thermal stability of LCN2, consistent with target engagement. In BEECs, LCN2 overexpression activated MAPK/ERK-mTOR signaling, suppressed autophagic flux and promoted epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), whereas LCN2 silencing reversed these phenotypes. Quercetin dose-dependently reduced LCN2 abundance and MAPK/ERK-mTOR phosphorylation, restored autophagic flux and reversed TGF-β1-induced EMT, and ERK inhibition abolished the LCN2-driven phenotype. In LPS-challenged mice, oral quercetin lowered uterine LCN2, recovered autophagy markers and reduced collagen deposition and endometrial damage. These preclinical findings associate LCN2 with impaired endometrial autophagy and EMT and suggest that quercetin may attenuate this cascade; binding affinity, LCN2 dependency and efficacy in cattle were not established and require validation in larger cohorts, purified-protein binding assays and chronic bovine models.

articles.title: The Role of Fatty Acid-Binding Protein 4 in Pregnancy Complications and Fetal Health.
articles.authors: Mierzyński R, Poniedziałek-Czajkowska E, Świda K et al.
articles.abstract: Fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) is an adipokine involved in regulating lipid metabolism, glucose homeostasis, and inflammatory processes. Altered circulating FABP4 concentrations have been associated with insulin resistance, adipose tissue dysfunction, and endothelial abnormalities. Growing evidence suggests that FABP4 dysregulation may contribute to impaired maternal metabolic and vascular adaptation during pregnancy, although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. FABP4 has been implicated in the pathophysiology of several pregnancy-related conditions, including maternal obesity, gestational diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, preeclampsia, and recurrent pregnancy loss. Circulating FABP4 has also emerged as a potential biomarker for the early identification of women at increased risk of pregnancy-related metabolic and vascular complications, potentially improving risk assessment and providing earlier preventive or therapeutic interventions. This review summarizes current evidence on the role of FABP4 during pregnancy and its potential involvement in the pathophysiology of pregnancy-related complications, with particular emphasis on its biological functions, diagnostic and prognostic potential, and emerging therapeutic implications. Further mechanistic and prospective clinical studies are needed to determine whether FABP4 is a clinically useful biomarker and to clarify its potential as a therapeutic target in the management of pregnancy-related complications.

articles.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis of Rat Urethral Tissue Following Simulated Childbirth Injury and Microenergy Acoustic Pulse Therapy.
articles.authors: Lin G, Zhao L, Xing E et al.
articles.abstract: Microenergy acoustic pulse (MAP) therapy has been associated with functional and structural improvement after childbirth-related urethral injury, but its multicellular effects remain incompletely defined. We explored treatment- and injury-associated differences in the urethral microenvironment using single-cell RNA sequencing. Eight female Sprague-Dawley rats were assigned to sham, vaginal balloon dilation plus ovariectomy (VBDO), VBDO plus beta-aminopropionitrile (BAPN), or VBDO plus BAPN and MAP (MAP) groups, with one 24-week-old and one 48-week-old rat per group. Urethral tissues were analyzed for cell composition, differential gene expression, Gene Ontology enrichment, stem/progenitor features, senescence-associated secretory phenotype activity, and CellChat-inferred intercellular communication. A balanced single-cell dataset comprising 23,128 cells was used for downstream comparative analyses and resolved 19 annotated cell-type/state categories. Across the injury- and age-associated experimental conditions, epithelial, vascular, stromal, immune, and muscle compartments showed distinct transcriptional patterns, whereas MAP-treated samples showed a distinct cellular distribution; a separate histological cohort showed higher urethral muscle content. MAP-treated samples also showed differences in CellChat-inferred signaling activity in selected extracellular-matrix, adhesion, vascular, developmental, and neural/neuromuscular pathways, including fibronectin 1 (FN1), collagen (COLLAGEN), angiopoietin (ANGPT), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), Wingless/Integrated (WNT), Notch (NOTCH), reelin (RELN), Slit guidance ligand (SLIT), neural cell adhesion molecule (NCAM), and neurexin (NRXN). Exploratory enrichment analysis identified treatment-associated differences in translation, oxidative metabolism, stress adaptation, synaptic-organization processes, progenitor-associated transcriptional states, and senescence-related programs. The treatment-split marker manifold approximation and projection (UMAPs) are descriptive and do not provide evidence of increased muscle-cell number; the reported difference in muscle-associated staining content derives from a separate animal-level histological analysis. Overall, the findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require validation in independently replicated cohorts.

articles.title: Maternal Angiogenic Profiles in Preeclampsia-Associated Versus Isolated Fetal Growth Restriction or Small-for-Gestational-Age Pregnancies: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Kim MA, Lee E, Lee HS et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal angiogenic imbalance is a hallmark of preeclampsia (PE), but whether it differs between PE-associated and isolated fetal growth restriction (FGR)/small-for-gestational-age (SGA) pregnancies is unclear, particularly before clinical recognition. We searched PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL for observational studies comparing maternal soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1), placental growth factor (PlGF), or their ratio between these phenotypes. Analyses were stratified by sampling context and pooled as Hedges' g using random-effects models. Twenty-three studies (630 PE-associated, 1476 isolated FGR/SGA pregnancies) were included. After clinical recognition, PE-associated FGR/SGA showed a higher sFlt-1/PlGF ratio (g = 1.04, 95% CI 0.51 to 1.57), higher sFlt-1 (1.05, 0.73 to 1.38), and lower PlGF (-0.60, -0.82 to -0.38) than isolated FGR/SGA; differences in the same directions were present before clinical recognition (ratio 0.86, 0.38 to 1.33; sFlt-1 0.38, 0.12 to 0.64; PlGF -0.46, -0.77 to -0.16). The sFlt-1 difference was larger after clinical recognition in the test for subgroup differences (p = 0.002) but not in meta-regression (p = 0.064), and this between-context contrast is therefore reported as exploratory; the PlGF difference was similar in both contexts. These group-level differences do not establish individual-level prediction, discrimination or threshold performance. PE-associated and isolated FGR/SGA should therefore be distinguished in biomarker research, and angiogenic thresholds derived in suspected PE require validation before application to normotensive FGR/SGA.

articles.title: Identifying a Shared Metabolomic Signature in Mother-Newborn Dyads With and Without Gestational Diabetes: Implications for Early Metabolic Programming.
articles.authors: Omaña-Guzmán I, López-Alvarenga JC, Palacios-González B et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy is a critical window for metabolic programming, during which adverse intrauterine exposures may influence long-term health. GDM alters the intrauterine environment, but its role in early metabolic programming remains poorly understood. Thus, the objective of this study was to identify the shared metabolomic signature in mother-newborn dyads and to assess whether GDM modifies this signature. For this purpose, we conducted a cross-sectional study including mother-newborn dyads recruited at the General Hospital of Mexico. Blood samples were collected from dyads. Amino acids and acylcarnitines were quantified by tandem mass spectrometry. Sparse partial least squares (sPLS) analysis was used to identify shared metabolomic signatures within mother-newborn dyads. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated the modifying effect of GDM on shared metabolites. A total of 112 mother-newborn dyads (68 without GDM and 44 with GDM) were included. Two shared metabolomic signatures were identified. The first, characterized by arginine, methionine, acetylcarnitine, and free carnitine, showed a strong maternal-newborn correlation. Although this core signature was preserved in both groups, valine and alanine contributed exclusively to the GDM-exposed dyads. In conclusion, a shared metabolomic signature related to fetal development and energy metabolism was conserved regardless of GDM status, although GDM partially modified this signature. These findings provide insights into metabolic processes potentially involved in early metabolic programming.

articles.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid and Saxagliptin Attenuate Ferroptosis-Related Ovarian Injury and Modulate FGF21/NOX4-NRF2/HO-1 Signaling in Letrozole-Induced Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.authors: Yousef EH, Zohny MH, Abdel-Lah ES et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by ovarian dysfunction, hormonal imbalance, and emerging ferroptosis-related abnormalities. This study investigated the effects of alpha-lipoic acid (ALA), saxagliptin (Saxa), and their combination in a letrozole-induced PCOS model, with focus on the ovarian FGF21/NOX4-NRF2/HO-1 and ferroptosis-related pathways. PCOS was induced in female rats by oral letrozole administration for 21 days. Rats were allocated into control, PCOS, ALA, Saxa, and ALA/Saxa groups, followed by 14 days of treatment. Body weight, ovarian index, ovarian histopathology, reproductive hormones, oxidative stress markers, ovarian FGF21 and NOX4 expression, NRF2/HO-1 signaling, and ferroptosis-related markers, including Fe2+, GPX4, and SLC7A11, were assessed. Letrozole induced weight gain, ovarian hypertrophy, follicular disruption, endocrine imbalance, and ferroptosis-related alterations, marked by increased ROS, MDA, Fe2+, and NOX4, alongside reduced FGF21, NRF2/HO-1, GPX4, and SLC7A11. ALA or Saxa attenuated these alterations, whereas ALA/Saxa produced greater improvements in ovarian morphology, hormonal status, redox homeostasis, and ferroptosis-related markers. These effects were associated with FGF21 upregulation, NOX4 suppression, enhanced NRF2/HO-1 signaling, and preservation of GPX4 and SLC7A11. In conclusion, ALA/Saxa therapy markedly ameliorated letrozole-induced PCOS in rats, accompanied by restoration of ovarian FGF21/NOX4 homeostasis, associated with enhancement of NRF2/HO-1 antioxidant responses, and attenuation of ferroptosis-related alterations.

articles.title: Adenomyosis and Its Impact on Reproduction, Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Newborn.
articles.authors: Signorile PG
articles.abstract: This narrative review covers the diagnosis of adenomyosis; its impact on fertility, assisted reproduction, pregnancy, childbirth, and the newborn; and its uterus-sparing management. Diagnosis is delayed by about 11 years, and no classification is universally accepted. After in vitro fertilization, adenomyosis lowers clinical pregnancy and live birth rates and doubles miscarriage risk. Because oocyte number and morphology are preserved and miscarriage remains increased with donor oocytes and euploid embryos, the deficit appears mainly uterine; however, age and coexistent endometriosis contribute. In pregnancy, it is associated with preeclampsia, preterm birth, placental malposition and placenta accreta spectrum, cesarean delivery, and postpartum hemorrhage, and newborns are more often small for gestational age, of low birth weight, and extremely preterm. The evidence is observational and of low to very low certainty, and defective remodeling of the junctional zone spiral arteries remains a hypothetical unifying mechanism. In selected observational cohorts, pregnancy was reported in approximately half of infertile women after uterus-sparing surgery, which has not been compared with medical treatment or assisted reproduction in randomized trials and carries a risk of uterine rupture. Management rests on individualized counseling; proposed preventive measures, including low-dose aspirin and correction of vitamin D or folate deficiency, remain untested in adenomyosis.

articles.title: Comparative Acetylation and Ubiquitination Profiling in Cervical Cancer-Cell Models Supports a Proposed Lysine-Fate Code.
articles.authors: Bastida RA, Reyes MA, Marko-Varga G et al.
articles.abstract: Post-translational modifications are rarely studied as an integrated system. Most studies have focused on acetylation or ubiquitination in isolation, despite both frequently targeting the same lysine residues on the same proteins. This study investigated whether the interplay between these modifications, rather than their individual effects, constitutes a meaningful regulatory layer in cervical cancer cells. Quantitative stoichiometric proteomics was applied to HPV-positive and HPV-negative cell models, with a non-cancerous keratinocyte cell line serving as the control. The results demonstrate that acetylation and ubiquitination form coordinated, context-dependent patterns rather than acting independently. In HPV-positive cells acetylation predominated and was enriched in transcriptional regulators. Conversely, the HPV-negative C33A line exhibited a substantially larger ubiquitinome, indicative of increased proteostatic surveillance. Site-specific stoichiometry analysis revealed that the relative occupancy of each modification at shared lysine residues determines regulatory outcomes, rather than their mere presence. This competition is proposed to constitute a "lysine-fate code" that integrates transcriptional regulation, metabolic adaptation, and immune signaling into a unified proteostatic logic. Beyond their implications for cervical cancer biology, these findings suggest that the acetylation-ubiquitination balance may represent a key regulatory principle. Targeting enzymes that modulate this balance could provide novel therapeutic strategies that surpass single-pathway inhibition.

articles.title: The Seminal Microenvironment as a Potentially Tractable Interface Between Metabolic Disease and Sperm Damage.
articles.authors: Yao Y, Zhang X, Li L et al.
articles.abstract: Male reproductive disorders are increasingly linked to metabolic diseases, but mechanistic research remains predominantly focused on the testis. The seminal microenvironment, shaped by epididymal and accessory-gland secretions, contains metabolites, lipids, ions, cytokines, extracellular vesicles, and microbial products, and may act as a metabolically responsive post-testicular interface that continues to influence sperm after spermatogenesis. Obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and chronic inflammation can remodel this environment by disrupting secretory activity, redox homeostasis, immune signaling, and microbial ecology. These changes may converge on oxidative and inflammatory pathways, promoting membrane lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired motility and capacitation, oxidative DNA base lesions, DNA fragmentation, and potentially epigenetic alterations. Mouse studies separately report obesity-associated epididymal vesicle remodeling and RNA-dependent changes in embryonic gene expression. In this Review, we examine the regulation and metabolic remodeling of the seminal microenvironment, how these changes may translate systemic metabolic stress into sperm injury, and emerging interventions including metabolic correction, antioxidant strategies, and microbiome-targeted approaches. Overall, current evidence remains largely observational and cross-sectional, with additional technical limitations in low-biomass seminal microbiome studies. Longitudinal and mechanistic studies are therefore needed to determine whether the seminal microenvironment is a causal mediator of metabolic infertility and a clinically tractable target for mechanism-guided preconception care.

articles.title: Folate Receptor Alpha (FRα/FOLR1) in Cancer: Diagnostic, Prognostic or Predictive Biomarker? A Critical Review of Its Clinical Utility.
articles.authors: Kapczuk P, Marcinowska Z, Kołodziejczak M et al.
articles.abstract: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) plays a key role in folate homeostasis. Folate is involved, among other processes, in nucleotide biosynthesis, and the marked difference between FRα expression in certain cancers and under physiological conditions gives this receptor potential as a cancer biomarker.
