However, the current state of knowledge points to a specific role for this marker and defines its potential place in cancer diagnosis and treatment. This review aims to critically evaluate the available evidence regarding the clinical utility of FRα. Analysis of the literature indicates that despite differences in expression, the sensitivity and specificity of FRα are insufficient for its use as a standalone diagnostic marker. In contrast, its potential as a prognostic marker is strongly dependent on cancer type. The strongest evidence of clinical utility concerns membranous FRα protein expression assessed by a validated immunohistochemical companion diagnostic assay for selecting patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer for mirvetuximab soravtansine treatment. In contrast, the predictive relevance of FRα for other targeted therapeutic strategies remains under investigation. Overall, FRα should be regarded as a clinically actionable biomarker in a defined therapeutic setting and as a promising, but not universally validated, diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive candidate in other oncological applications.

articles.title: Low MATR3 Expression Is Associated with Poor Prognosis in Endometrial Carcinoma: An Integrated Immunohistochemical and Transcriptomic Analysis.
articles.authors: Podemski J, Grzanka D, Podemska E et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is the most common malignancy of the female genital tract, yet reliable prognostic biomarkers remain limited. Matrin-3 (MATR3), a nuclear matrix protein involved in genome stability and RNA processing, has been implicated in various cancers, but its role in EC has not been described. Here, we performed an integrated analysis combining immunohistochemical evaluation of MATR3 protein expression in a retrospective institutional cohort of 112 patients with EC and in silico analysis of MATR3 mRNA expression in 172 TCGA cases. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed nuclear MATR3 expression in both EC and normal endometrial tissues, with significantly lower protein levels in EC compared to control tissues (p < 0.0001). MATR3 mRNA was significantly reduced in EC tumour tissues compared to adjacent normal tissues (p < 0.0001). Low MATR3 protein expression was associated with shorter OS after adjustment for age, histological grade, pT, pN and pM in an LVSI-stratified Cox model (HR = 2.296; 95% CI: 1.284-4.104; p = 0.0050). Low MATR3 mRNA expression was associated with improved overall survival in TCGA (median OS = 110.1 months; HR = 2.174; 95% CI: 1.066-4.43; p = 0.0303). Co-expression analysis identified BCLAF1 and TOP2B as key positive correlates, while TRAPPC5 and FASTK showed the strongest negative correlations. Genes positively correlated with MATR3 mRNA expression were enriched for nuclear transcription and RNA-processing annotations, whereas negatively correlated genes were enriched for mitochondrial processes. These associations do not establish a mechanistic link between MATR3 and pathway activity. Our findings support further investigation of MATR3 as a candidate prognostic marker in EC, with independent validation and functional studies required.

articles.title: Immunotargeting of Cervical Cancer Cells with the Adaptor CAR T-Cell Platform RevCAR.
articles.authors: Jones-Cifuentes N, Arndt C, Loureiro LR et al.
articles.abstract: The Prostate Stem Cell Antigen (PSCA) is not only overexpressed in prostate cancer (PC) but also in many other tumors, including cervical cancer (CC). The adaptor chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) platform RevCAR can be used for immunotargeting of PSCA-expressing tumor cells. We found that the CC cell line SiHa natively expresses PSCA. The expression was sufficient for redirection of RevCAR T-cells using recently described RevCAR target modules (RevTMs) directed against PSCA. Like almost all PC cell lines, however, SiHa cells also downregulate their PSCA expression in cell culture. To overcome this limitation, we established artificially PSCA-overexpressing SiHa cells. Retargeting of RevCAR T-cells strictly depends on PSCA-directed RevTMs and PSCA-expressing target cells. It leads to (i) upregulation of CD69, Perforin and Granzyme B, (ii) lysis of target cells with EC50 values in the picomolar range, and (iii) cytokine secretion of IFN-γ, TNF-α, GM-CSF and IL-2. Phenotypic analysis shows a prominent increase in memory RevCAR T-cells but only a slight increase in exhausted cells, indicating a low level of tonic signaling of RevCAR T-cells. Together, our data supports an efficient and safe immunotargeting of PSCA-expressing CC cells with the RevCAR technology.

articles.title: Ovariectomy Exacerbates Chronic Constriction Injury-Induced Neuropathic Pain Through Dysregulation of Spinal Estrogen Receptor Balance in Rats.
articles.authors: Chan YC, Lin SC, Huang CT et al.
articles.abstract: Estrogen depletion after menopause has been associated with altered pain sensitivity; however, the spinal mechanisms linking estrogen deficiency to neuropathic pain remain incompletely understood. This study investigated whether ovariectomy (OVX)-induced estrogen depletion exacerbates chronic constriction injury (CCI)-induced neuropathic pain and whether this effect is associated with changes in spinal estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) and estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) expression. Female Sprague Dawley rats underwent OVX or sham surgery, followed 5 weeks later by median nerve CCI or sham CCI. Mechanical withdrawal thresholds and thermal withdrawal latencies were evaluated using von Frey filaments and the plantar test, respectively. ERα and ERβ expression in the spinal dorsal horn was assessed via immunofluorescence staining and Western blotting. Selective ERα and ERβ agonists were administered intrathecally to examine their effects on OVX/CCI-induced pain behaviors. Plasma estradiol levels were significantly reduced after OVX, and OVX rats developed mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity. Rats in the OVX/CCI group exhibited more pronounced pain behaviors than those in the Sham/CCI group, indicating that OVX exacerbated CCI-induced neuropathic pain. In the spinal dorsal horn, ERα expression was increased in the OVX/Sham, Sham/CCI, and OVX/CCI groups, with the greatest increase observed in the OVX/CCI group. In contrast, ERβ expression was decreased in the Sham/CCI and OVX/CCI groups, with no significant difference between these groups. Intrathecal administration of an ERα agonist further aggravated mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia in OVX/CCI rats, whereas an ERβ agonist attenuated these pain behaviors. These findings suggest that OVX-induced estrogen depletion exacerbates CCI-induced neuropathic pain, potentially through a shift toward ERα-dominant signaling relative to ERβ in the spinal dorsal horn. Selective modulation of ERα and ERβ may therefore represent a potential therapeutic approach for chronic pain exacerbated by estrogen depletion.

articles.title: Preliminary Evaluation of the Anticancer Activity of a PGK1 Small Molecule Inhibitor in Ishikawa Endometrial Cancer.
articles.authors: Cao H, Xue S, Xue M et al.
articles.abstract: To investigate the roles of a phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (PGK1) small-molecule inhibitor in Ishikawa endometrial cancer. The role of a PGK1 small molecule inhibitor in endometrial cancer was identified by cell viability, transwell, cell cycle, and apoptosis analyses. The expression levels of PGK1 in cancer cells treated with various concentrations of the PGK1 small molecule inhibitor at 48 h and 72 h were determined via Western blotting. Xenograft mouse models were established through subcutaneous tumor transplantation, and immunofluorescence analysis of PGK1 and apoptosis in tumor tissue was performed. The results of the cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay revealed that NG52 inhibited the activity of human endometrial carcinoma Ishikawa, HEC-1-A, and HEC-1-B cells in a concentration-dependent manner. Moreover, NG52 significantly reduced the migration ability of the Ishikawa cell line in a dose-dependent manner. Flow cytometry (FCM) demonstrated that NG52 affected the survival of endometrial carcinoma cells by arresting the cell cycle at the G1 phase and inducing apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. Western blot analysis also revealed that the apoptosis-inducing effects of NG52 were accompanied by a reduction in PGK1 expression after 48 h and 72 h of NG52 treatment. Moreover, NG52 partially suppressed tumor growth in a human Ishikawa xenograft model, and transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) showed an increasing trend of NG52-treated tumor tissue apoptosis, with a decreasing trend in PGK1 expression in the treatment group. NG52, a PGK1 small molecule inhibitor, can serve as a structural basis for developing potential anti-endometrial carcinoma agents. The findings are limited to the preliminary preclinical activity of NG52, and further mechanistic, pharmacologic, efficacy, and safety studies are warranted before improved PGK1 inhibitors can proceed to clinical translation.

articles.title: Serial Tumor-Agnostic Plasma Profiling with a Compact NGS Panel During First-Line Therapy for Newly Diagnosed Metastatic Colorectal Cancer.
articles.authors: Zakharova G, Zauzolkov O, Khristichenko A et al.
articles.abstract: Plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling may complement tissue hotspot testing and reveal molecular changes during treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). We prospectively studied 39 patients with newly diagnosed unresectable mCRC receiving first-line therapy. Cell-free DNA was collected before treatment and after two and four cycles and analyzed using a 10 kb, 10-gene hybrid-capture sequencing panel with molecular barcodes and error correction. Baseline oncogenic variants were detected in 32 of 35 evaluable patients (91.4%). Compared with routine tissue PCR for shared RAS/BRAF targets, plasma testing showed 84.2% sensitivity (16/19) and 100% specificity (19/19) in the intention-to-test cohort, compared with 88.2% sensitivity (15/17) and 100% specificity (17/17) among technically evaluable samples. Three activating KRAS variants (L19F, A59T, and A146T) lay outside the tissue assays' target regions; patients carrying these alterations received anti-EGFR therapy. Patients with metastases in two or more organs had more detectable oncogenic alterations than those with one metastatic site (median, three versus two; adjusted q = 0.00184; rank-biserial correlation = 0.687). Serial sampling revealed divergent trajectories of individual variants in nine patients. Early reductions in plasma variant allele frequencies tended to be greater among partial responders, although associations with radiological response were not significant after multiple testing correction. Compact tumor-agnostic plasma sequencing provides complementary molecular information, but its clinical utility requires further validation.

articles.title: Exploratory Association of 12S-HETE with Postprandial Hyperinsulinemia Rather than HOMA-IR in Women with PCOS/PMOS.
articles.authors: Szczuko M, Skórka-Majewicz M, Żwierełło W et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) is one of the most commonly diagnosed endocrine disorders among women of reproductive age. The proposed term more accurately reflects the pathophysiology of the condition, emphasizing its multisystem nature rather than restricting it to ovarian dysfunction. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is estimated to affect approximately 6-20% of women of reproductive age. The condition is characterized by considerable clinical heterogeneity, including menstrual irregularities, hyperandrogenism, difficulties conceiving, and abdominal obesity. In addition to hormonal disturbances, an important and often underestimated aspect of PMOS is its association with insulin resistance and chronic low-grade inflammation. Current evidence indicates that insulin resistance represents an important component of the pathogenesis of PMOS. In this context, the identification of biomarkers reflecting metabolic and inflammatory disturbances in affected women is of particular interest. Pro-inflammatory lipid mediators, such as hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids (HETEs) and hydroxyoctadecadienoic acids (HODEs), are products of fatty acid oxidation and act as active modulators of the inflammatory response. Increased concentrations of these metabolites have been reported in individuals with type 2 diabetes, excessive body weight, cardiovascular diseases, and in women with PMOS. The study included 45 women diagnosed with PMOS, who were divided into groups according to the presence of insulin resistance assessed using the HOMA-IR index. Venous blood plasma was used as the biological material, and the concentrations of selected HETE and HODE metabolites were determined using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). The obtained data were subjected to statistical analysis to assess the associations between lipid mediator concentrations, parameters of carbohydrate metabolism, and selected metabolic indices. Statistical analysis revealed no significant differences in the concentrations of the analyzed oxylipins (HETE and HODE) between patient groups stratified according to HOMA-IR. No significant direct correlations were observed between most of the analyzed metabolites and body mass index (BMI) or fasting blood glucose levels. However, a nominally significant association was identified for 12S-HETE (p = 0.0258), which did not remain significant after Bonferroni correction (adjusted p = 0.1806). Its concentration was nearly twofold higher in…

articles.title: Diabetes Mellitus: Review of the Common, Rare, and Uncommon (Conceptual and Metaphorical) Types.
articles.authors: Pliszka M, Szablewski L
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) comprises a complex heterogeneous group of chronic metabolic disorders that affect various organ systems, resulting in a number of complications, including kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, immune dysfunction, retinopathy, neuropathy, and cancer. Uncontrolled DM may also lead to a coma and confusion, and if untreated, death due to ketoacidosis or nonketotic hyperosmolar syndrome. In 2019, DM was directly responsible for 1.5 million deaths, with an additional 460,000 due to kidney disease, as well as about 20% of cardiovascular-associated deaths. In addition to the well-known types-viz. type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)-several other rare conceptual/metaphoric forms have been described, although they are not regarded as formal diagnoses. The aim of this review is to present the various types of DM and summarize their characteristics, clinical features, diagnosis, pathophysiology, risk factors, management, and therapy.

articles.title: Effect of the rs12249854 Polymorphism in the HECTD2 Gene and Selected Clinical Variables on the Response to Intradetrusor Injection of Botulinum Neurotoxin Type a in Female Patients with Overactive Bladder: A Single-Center Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Ciećwież SM, Lewandowska K, Boroń A et al.
articles.abstract: The HECTD2:rs12249854 polymorphism may be associated with a weaker response to an intradetrusor injection of botulinum neurotoxin type A (BoNT/A) in patients with overactive bladder (OAB). This prospective study analyzed the link between the HECTD2:rs12249854 polymorphism and the response to BoNT/A treatment in 156 OAB patients, based on changes in urodynamic parameters and ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-LUTS-QoL scores six months after the injection. BoNT/A treatment contributed to improvements in all parameters except the average flow rate. Wild-type homozygotes (TT, n = 137) differed from TA heterozygotes (n = 19) solely in terms of pretreatment ICIQ-OAB Part A and ICIQ-LUTS-QoL Part A scores, both of which were higher in the heterozygotes. Thus, the HECTD2:rs12249854 polymorphism does not appear to be associated with the response to BoNT/A treatment. Patients with neurogenic OAB (n = 60) had a higher pretreatment detrusor pressure at maximum flow than those with idiopathic OAB (n = 96), but this difference was no longer observed after BoNT/A treatment. Good responders to the BoNT/A injection (defined as at least 50% decrease in the ICIQ-LUTS-QoL Part A score, n = 50) had a higher body mass index and parity and a lower pretreatment maximum flow rate than poor responders (n = 106). Before formulating any definitive conclusions, the results of this exploratory study should be verified in an adequately powered multicenter cohort.

articles.title: Validation of Multi-Residue GC-MS/MS and LC-MS/MS Methods for the Analysis of Pesticide Residues in Botanicals.
articles.authors: Butovskaya E, Castrezzati G, Migliorato G et al.
articles.abstract: Botanical food supplements are increasingly consumed worldwide. As finished products, they may be contaminated with pesticide residues, which can potentially become concentrated relative to the raw botanical materials during processing steps. In this study, analytical methods were developed for the quantification of 252 pesticide residues in botanical food supplements using LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS, with both techniques employing a common sample preparation procedure. Sample extraction and clean-up were performed using a QuEChERS-based approach combined with dispersive solid-phase clean-up step using graphitized carbon black (GCB) and primary-secondary amine (PSA) sorbents followed by Oasis® WAX cartridge purification. Method validation was performed in accordance with the EU guidance document SANTE/11312/2021. The validated methods were subsequently applied to ten plant extract samples to assess their applicability to different botanical food supplement matrices. Multiple pesticide residues were detected in three samples, with concentrations ranging from 0.01 to 0.19 mg/kg. The application of the methods to real samples confirmed suitability for the analysis of diverse botanical matrices and underscored the need for robust analytical approaches to support the routine monitoring of pesticide residues in botanical food supplements and ensure consumer safety.

articles.title: Comparative Label-Free Proteomics of a High-Glucose Syncytialised Trophoblast Model Identifies Mitochondrial Fission Factor (MFF) as a Candidate Serum Biomarker Associated with Hyperglycaemic Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Sharma AK, Yalavarthi C, Savithri P et al.
articles.abstract: Placental protein markers of maternal hyperglycaemia in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) remain scarce. We aimed to find trophoblast proteins that change under high glucose and to test whether a lead candidate is also raised in maternal serum. In our established insulin-resistant model, we used label-free liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to compare BeWo cells syncytialised with forskolin/8-Br-cAMP in high-glucose (25 mM) medium, with or without vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), with undifferentiated control cells in normoglycaemic (5 mM) medium (n = 3 per group); glucose and differentiation therefore varied together. Of 3528 protein groups, 388 were differentially abundant (24 at Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.05). Mitochondrial fission factor (MFF), the outer-membrane receptor for dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1), increased 4.5-fold (q = 0.040), whereas DRP1 was unchanged; mitochondrial calcium-uniporter components, pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 3 and glycogen synthase 1 also increased. VEGF did not alter this signature (MFF: 0.91-fold, p = 0.71). Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) confirmed higher MFF in high-glucose cell lysates (+48%) and, independently of in vitro differentiation, in gestational-day-7 serum of streptozotocin-treated hyperglycaemic pregnant rats (+41%; both p < 0.001; n = 3 per group), consistent with reported increases of MFF in GDM placentae. As serum was sampled after hyperglycaemia developed, these data show association, not prediction. MFF is a candidate serum biomarker of hyperglycaemic pregnancy; studies separating glucose from differentiation and validation in women are needed.

articles.title: Immune Resistance and Anti-Tumor Immunity in the Ovarian Tumor Microenvironment.
articles.authors: Stiff PJ, Czerlanis CM, Potkul RK et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a lethal gynecologic malignancy with limited effective treatment options. It is expected that in 2026 there will be about 21,010 new cases of ovarian cancer diagnosed and about 12,450 deaths within the United States. Unfortunately, conventional therapies such as chemotherapy and radiation have limited efficacy for high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) and also produce significant toxicity. HGSOC is characterized by an ovarian tumor microenvironment (TME) consisting of immune inhibitory T regulatory cells and inhibitory tumor-associated macrophages, including myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) and M2 cells, which confer immune suppression. Immunocompetent T cells, tumor-suppressing M1 cells, natural killer cells, and other cellular subsets are also present. The TME is further shaped by soluble molecules, extracellular matrix, and other structural components, as well as the presence of blood vessels and ascitic fluid in the peritoneal cavity, which aid in the distribution of cancer cells to the omentum where more lesions soon develop. This review outlines the heterogenous immune cell subsets in the ovarian TME and other structural targets that promote or reduce cancer burden. Most single-agent immune strategies have shown limited efficacy in unselected HGSOC populations due to the complex immune-suppressive nature of the TME. Here, we also discuss novel combination treatments in clinical trials or in clinical practice for HGSOC. Advances in understanding the ovarian TME will reveal new immunotherapy and drug targets for translational medicine and aid in determining effective drug and immunotherapy combinations, which may ultimately lead to improved overall survival in HGSOC.

articles.title: BORIS in Hormone-Driven Cancers: Epigenetic Reprogramming, Transcriptional Plasticity, and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.authors: Saleem S, Gaughan L, Robson CN
articles.abstract: Hormone-driven cancers, including prostate, breast, endometrial and ovarian cancers, are a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Endocrine therapies targeting androgen receptor and oestrogen receptor/progesterone receptor signalling have improved outcomes, but acquired resistance arising through genetic and epigenetic mechanisms that bypass receptor dependence remains a major challenge. BORIS (Brother of the Regulator of Imprinted Sites), a CTCF paralogue, is a germline-restricted regulator that becomes aberrantly reactivated in cancer through promoter hypomethylation, p53 loss, and loss of CTCF-mediated repression. Once expressed, BORIS occupies CTCF sites, displacing or co-occupying them with CTCF, and reprograms clustered sites into alternative transcriptional start sites through SRCAP-mediated H2A.Z deposition, activating germline genes that sustain proliferation, and therapeutic resistance. BORIS expression correlates with poor prognosis in ovarian and endometrial cancers, associates with ER/PR levels in breast cancer, and correlates with Gleason score in prostate cancer. BORIS represses AR signalling in ovarian cancer and inversely correlates with receptor expression in endometrial cancer. Its cancer-testis antigen properties position BORIS as an immunotherapy target, with preclinical vaccine efficacy demonstrated in breast cancer models. This review synthesises the disease-specific evidence positioning BORIS as a driver of transcriptional reprogramming and endocrine resistance, identifies current knowledge gaps, and discusses translational implications of targeting this pathway.

articles.title: Exploratory Multi-Compartment Profiling of Steroid and Bile Acid Metabolites in Relation to Maternal Perceived Stress at Term.
articles.authors: Gomez Junco Lobo R, Uttarkar A, Lager J et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal stressors during pregnancy are linked to adverse birth outcomes, but the biochemical pathways involved remain poorly defined. We previously reported that the human placenta buffers the fetus from several effects of maternal perceived stress in a cohort of term pregnancies. Here, using the same cohort and no additional participants, we analyze a broader steroid panel and, for the first time, a targeted bile acid metabolomic panel across four maternal-fetal compartments: maternal plasma, placental tissue, cord plasma, and maternal hair. Nulliparous women were recruited during the third trimester at UCSF Mission Bay Hospital; perceived stress was measured using the 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) and retained as a continuous variable for the primary analysis from 17 women. Of 212 analyte compartment pairs evaluated, 38 metabolites met a predefined detectability criterion and were tested for association with PSS and sociodemographic scores using Kendall's tau b, with permutation p-values, bootstrap confidence intervals, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. No association survived multiple testing corrections. In exploratory, uncorrected comparisons (p < 0.05), three metabolites were nominally lower in a cohort-derived, higher-PSS group: placental estrone (E1), cord plasma glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA), and maternal plasma ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA). Nearly 47.1% of women had gestational diabetes; 20-hydroxyprogesterone (20-OH-PROG) in maternal plasma, dihydroprogesterone (DHP), and pregnenolone (PELN) in placental tissues were nominally decreased in women who developed gestational diabetes compared to women who did not develop gestational diabetes. Maternal hair was not a good compartment for detection of bile acid metabolites. Despite a wide range of perceived stress/sociodemographic scores and a substantial burden of maternal clinical comorbidities in this cohort, all pregnancies resulted in favorable neonatal outcomes at delivery. These findings support the hypothesis that the placenta functions as a buffering organ that protects the developing fetus against broad insults while remaining susceptible to more selective disruptions.

articles.title: Landscape of m6A Modification in Testicular Tissues of Normal and Cryptorchid Tianhua Mutton Sheep.
articles.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
articles.authors: Liu J, Liang W, Li W et al.
articles.abstract: Cryptorchidism is a common male reproductive disorder generally characterized by spermatogenic failure. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying infertility induced by cryptorchidism in sexually mature rams remain insufficiently characterized. N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most prevalent internal RNA modification, plays a dynamic role in testicular development and spermatogenesis. In the present study, testicular tissues collected from normal and cryptorchid Tianhua mutton sheep were used to construct a transcriptome-wide m6A methylation atlas of the testis. Histological observation showed significantly reduced numbers of Sertoli and Leydig cells and diminished seminiferous tubule diameters in cryptorchid testes. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) results demonstrated the dysregulated tissue-level mRNA expression of m6A regulators in cryptorchid testes. Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) revealed 2080 differentially methylated m6A peaks, with 1449 hypermethylated and 631 hypomethylated m6A peaks in cryptorchid testes. The majority of these peaks were concentrated in the CDS region, followed by the stop codons and 3' UTR. The integrative analysis of MeRIP-seq and RNA-seq data revealed that differentially expressed and m6A methylated genes were enriched in the apoptosis, AMPK, FoxO, TNF, and MAPK signaling pathways. Seven candidate genes, including RRM2, GTSE1, ATM, GORAB, INSR, HSPA1L, and MAPK9 were screened. In conclusion, this study identified differences in the mRNA abundance of m6A regulators and regional m6A enrichment between normal and cryptorchid sheep testes. These tissue-level differences may partly reflect changes in cellular composition. The findings provide a basis for further investigation of the potential involvement of m6A regulation in cryptorchidism-associated spermatogenic impairment.

articles.title: Influence of Donor Cells on the Efficiency of Cloned Ỉ Pig Production.
articles.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
articles.authors: Hoang AT, Huong VTT, Quan HX et al.
articles.abstract: In this study, we investigated the effects of donor cell on the efficiency of producing cloned Ỉ pigs, an endangered Vietnamese breed. Cloned Ỉ pig embryos were generated using somatic cell nuclear transfer technology (SCNT). The results demonstrated that pregnancy, farrowing, and piglet production rates of Ỉ pig fibroblasts (ID:6004) at the 5th and 6th passages were significantly higher compared with those observed at the 4th and 7th passages. Under the conditions of this study, no significant effect of donor cell sex or cell lines on the efficiency of cloned Ỉ pig embryo transfer was observed. The pregnancy, farrowing, and piglet production rates did not differ significantly between donor cell groups of male and female origin (p > 0.05). Similarly, no significant differences were observed in pregnancy rates, farrowing outcomes, or one-week survival of live cloned piglets among the three donor cell lines (IDs: 6004, 9154, and 9157) (p > 0.05). These findings contribute to improving the efficiency of the somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) technique in efforts to conserve the critically endangered Vietnamese Ỉ pig.

articles.title: The Molecular Landscape of Placental Dysfunction in Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR): From Integrated Signaling Networks to Epigenetic Control.
articles.authors: Varra FN, Varras M, Varra VK et al.
articles.abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major pregnancy complication linked to placental insufficiency, resulting from defective trophoblast differentiation, impaired maternal-fetal vascular adaptation, and altered nutrient sensing. This review synthesizes current evidence on the interconnected molecular networks driving placental dysfunction. We map the reciprocal crosstalk between the pro-inflammatory shift, highlighted by NLRP3 inflammasome-driven trophoblast pyroptosis, and dysregulated extracellular matrix remodeling mediated by the MMP-9/TIMP system. This hostile microenvironment feeds directly into the angiogenic imbalance defined by the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, accelerating cellular senescence via p53 and disrupting survival hubs like the PTEN/PI3K/AKT axis. Consequently, downstream metabolic sensors, notably the mTOR pathway, are blunted, causing trafficking failure of essential amino acid (SNAT2, LAT1) and glucose (GLUT) transporters. Crucially, we introduce an original framework integrating emerging spatial transcriptomics and single-cell epigenomics, demonstrating that these pathomechanisms are anatomically regionalized rather than uniform. Finally, we provide a critical evaluation of translation-ready therapeutic targets, emphasizing that strict safety constraints against fetal teratogenesis render ligand-functionalized nanoparticles a non-negotiable prerequisite for placenta-selective drug delivery. Integrating molecular stratification with longitudinal biomarker profiling represents the next milestone for mechanism-based, targeted management of FGR.

articles.title: LncRNA-Mediated Regulation of Hepatic Metabolic Homeostasis: Cholesterol, Triglyceride, Glucose and Pathological Implications.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Liu T, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract: The liver coordinately maintains cholesterol, triglyceride, and glucose homeostasis by integrating the synthesis, storage, utilization, and inter-conversion of these metabolic programs, and their dysregulation contributes to metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are not translated into proteins, regulate gene expression through interactions with DNA, RNA, and proteins at transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and epigenetic levels, and have emerged as central determinants of hepatic metabolic balance. This review systematically summarizes how lncRNAs govern cholesterol biosynthesis and efflux, triglyceride synthesis and lipolysis, glycogen turnover, gluconeogenesis, and glycolysis in hepatocytes. Unlike pathway-by-pathway descriptions, we highlight that these programs are coupled through shared signaling networks, including PI3K/AKT/mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), 5'-AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), SREBP, PPAR, and FoxO1, and that pleiotropic lncRNAs coordinate lipid and glucose outputs rather than controlling a single isolated process. We further examine how lncRNA dysregulation drives MASLD, HCC, T2DM, and GDM, and evaluate their potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Finally, we outline current limitations, including incomplete molecular characterization, low cross-species conservation, heterogeneous experimental validation, and unresolved delivery challenges, which must be addressed before lncRNA-based strategies reach clinical application.

articles.title: Prominent Hepatic Injury in 56-Week-Old Female Mice with Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Adenosine Monophosphate Synthase (cGAS) Deficient.
articles.authors: Suksamai C, Bhunyakarnjanarat T, Dityen K et al.
articles.abstract: Current preclinical studies evaluating cGAS inhibition as a novel anti-inflammatory strategy rely predominantly on young murine models, leaving the impact of aging largely unexplored. At baseline, aged (56-week-old) female mice, in both WT and cGAS-/- mice, demonstrated more pronounced oxidative stress (malondialdehyde) and diminished antioxidant capacity (glutathione) relative to young (8-week-old) controls. Upon the induction of liver ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), the most severe hepatic damage was provoked exclusively in aged cGAS-/- mice. This exacerbated injury was confirmed by elevated liver enzymes, higher histological scores, widespread apoptosis (activated caspase-3), enhanced macrophage accumulation (F4/80+ cells), and increased serum cell-free DNA as a tissue damage marker. Additionally, aged cGAS-/- mice exhibited a significant surge in serum IL-6 and gut barrier dysfunction (FITC-dextran assay) at 6 h post-injury. Mechanistically, while cGAS-/- macrophages showed blunted inflammatory signaling upon lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation, co-incubation with D-galactose, which induces intracellular peroxide accumulation, restored their pro-inflammatory responses to WT levels. Concurrently, starvation protocols revealed that cGAS-/- hepatocytes were more vulnerable to mitochondrial oxidative stress (MitoSOX) than WT cells. Ultimately, aging critically modifies the cGAS-deficient phenotype, warranting the careful re-evaluation of cGAS therapeutic models in aged populations.

articles.title: Intron-mRNA Matching Patterns in Differentially Expressed Genes in Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Sun P, Feng Y, Yan Z et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is characterized by widespread transcriptomic dysregulation, yet sequence matching patterns between mRNAs and their corresponding introns remain insufficiently characterized in differentially expressed genes (DEGs). This study aimed to describe computationally predicted intron-mRNA matching features in the reference sequences of CC DEGs. DEGs were identified using Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) datasets, and the corresponding mRNA and intron sequences were retrieved from the Ensembl human reference genome. Reverse complementation combined with Smith-Waterman local alignment was used to analyze the positional distributions of predicted matching fragments across full-length mRNAs and within translation initiation and termination regions. Descriptive analyses were further stratified by the GC content of the matching fragments. On normalized full-length mRNA coordinates, high-GC fragments exhibited higher matching frequencies in certain segments near the 5' end, whereas matching frequencies of low-GC fragments increased toward the 3' end. Within the translation initiation region, predicted matching frequencies were generally higher upstream than downstream of the AUG codon, and the low-GC group exhibited a local peak near the initiation codon. Within the translation termination region, the low-GC group exhibited a pronounced peak downstream of the stop codon, whereas the high-GC group showed no similarly pronounced downstream peak and displayed greater positional fluctuations in matching frequency. Overall, the predicted matching distributions differed across the analyzed regions and GC groups. This study provides a sequence-level description of intron-mRNA matching patterns within this reference sequence collection of CC DEGs; their biological significance requires further validation.

articles.title: Dry-Sand Layer Regulates Soil Moisture Stratification and Plant Community Assembly in the Desert-Oasis Ecotone.
articles.authors: Lu Y, Wang J, Ma J et al.
articles.abstract: The desert-oasis ecotone is ecologically fragile, yet the profile-scale role of the Dry-Sand Layer (DSL) in regulating soil moisture stratification and plant community assembly remains poorly understood. We systematically investigated six representative sites across the middle Heihe River Basin (with soil types transitioning from silt loam to aeolian sandy soils), combining multi-depth soil hydro-physical profiling (0-120 cm) with comprehensive vegetation sampling (across 90 nested quadrats recording 37 vascular plant species). A distinct DSL commonly formed at 60-80 cm depth across sandy sites, characterized by a bulk density of 1.39 g. cm-3 and a distinct moisture trough (typically < 2.0%), decoupling shallow root zones from subsoil moisture pools (1.10% to 5.09%). This edaphic boundary filtered out deep-rooted species, restricting vegetation to shallow-rooted xerophytic shrubs and grasses (e.g., Reaumuria soongarica (Pall.) Maxim., Aristida adscensionis L.) exhibiting high interspecific niche overlap (>0.86) and clustered spatial patterns (C > 1). Structural equation modeling indicated that subsoil moisture regulated by the DSL directly drives plant community diversity (path coefficient β = +0.54) and coverage (β = +0.61). Overall, the DSL serves as an essential eco-hydrological buffer balancing shallow soil moisture retention and subsoil conservation, indicating that ecological restoration in hyper-arid ecotones should prioritize DSL preservation and native shallow-rooted vegetation.

articles.title: Extracellular Vesicle-Associated Epithelial-Mesenchymal Plasticity (EMP) as a Driver of Metastatic Evolution and Therapeutic Resistance in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Hibbard JN, Ullah A, Alam F
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a lethal gynecologic malignancy, with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) accounting for a large proportion of advanced-stage disease. HGSOC commonly disseminates across the peritoneal cavity, where malignant ascites contain tumour cells, stromal and immune cells, soluble mediators, and extracellular vesicles (EVs). Although epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) has often been used to explain invasive behaviour, tumour cells may occupy reversible hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal states rather than completing a uniform transition. This review synthesizes evidence linking EV-associated communication with epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity (EMP), peritoneal dissemination, and treatment resistance, with particular attention to the strength and context of the evidence. We distinguish endosome-derived exosomes from small EV (sEV) preparations whose biogenesis has not been established, and separate observational associations from functional experiments, animal-model findings, and clinical evidence. Our central contribution is an evidence-calibrated framework connecting EV biology, ascites-associated selection pressures, and dynamic cell states while identifying where causal mechanisms and clinical utility remain unproven. EV-associated cargo and EV-targeting approaches are promising research directions, but neither biomarker performance nor therapeutic benefit should be considered clinically established without independent validation.

articles.title: Early-Onset Breast, Cervical, Colorectal and Stomach Cancer Across the States of India, 1990-2023: Divergent Trends and a Mismatch Between Burden Rate and Caseload.
articles.authors: Kamath R, Kini SB, Prabhu V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Cancer diagnosed before the age of 50 is rising across many countries, and the rise is not accounted for by population growth alone. India carries one of the world's largest cancer burdens, and it varies greatly between its states, variation camouflaged by the national average. We characterised early-onset breast, cervical, colorectal and stomach cancer across the states of India.
METHODS: Secondary ecological analysis of Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates, ages 15-49 years, 1990-2023; rates per 100,000 population of both sexes. Trends were summarised as the estimated annual percentage change, with autocorrelation-robust confidence intervals, and by segmented regression. Gradients across 30 states were assessed against the 2023 Socio-Demographic Index (SDI). Case growth was decomposed into population growth, within-band ageing and rate change.
RESULTS: In 2023, breast cancer had the highest early-onset incidence, 9.63 per 100,000 (19.63 per 100,000 women), and cervical cancer 8.18 (16.87). Breast incidence rose 2.72% per year and colorectal 1.11%; stomach fell 0.52%. Cervical incidence fell until 2011 and rose unevenly thereafter, with a near-zero net trend (-0.09% per year). Within-band standardisation shifted it downward (-0.39%; 95% confidence interval -0.87 to 0.09), and separating within-band ageing turned its rate-change share negative (-8.1%). Breast cases rose from 15,550 to 76,806: 59.0% of the rise was rate change, 51.8% after separating ageing. Point estimates suggested a stronger inverse SDI gradient for cervical disability-adjusted life years (ρ = -0.43) than incidence (ρ = -0.31). Neither survived multiple-testing correction, and the two were not distinguishable. No association was detected between burden rate and caseload across the states (ρ = +0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: The early-onset cancer burden in India is not uniform. Breast cancer cases are growing faster than the population, with a rising recorded rate. The cervical gradient is exploratory. The states with the highest rates and the states with the most cases differ, and each answers a different planning question.

articles.title: Comparison of Survival Outcomes with First-Line PARP Inhibitor Maintenance According to BRCA Mutation and Homologous Recombination Deficiency Status in Advanced Ovarian Cancer: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Choi YJ, Lee JY, Nam EJ et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: First-line poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) maintenance is standard in advanced ovarian cancer, but direct comparisons between active regimens within biomarker-defined groups are limited. We compared survival outcomes after first-line PARPi maintenance according to BRCA mutation and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 218 patients who initiated olaparib, olaparib plus bevacizumab, or niraparib after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were measured from maintenance initiation. We compared olaparib with niraparib in BRCA-mutated disease and olaparib plus bevacizumab with niraparib in HRD-positive, BRCA-wild-type disease. Results: Overall, 82 patients received olaparib, 33 olaparib plus bevacizumab, and 103 niraparib. Median follow-up was 23.9 months. In BRCA-mutated disease, 2-year PFS was 68.2% with olaparib (n = 81) and 69.0% with niraparib (n = 44; niraparib vs. olaparib: hazard ratio [HR] 1.14, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.60-2.17; log-rank p = 0.695). In HRD-positive, BRCA-wild-type disease, 2-year PFS was 81.0% with olaparib plus bevacizumab (n = 22) and 62.6% with niraparib (n = 51; niraparib vs. combination: HR 1.58, 95% CI 0.61-4.09; log-rank p = 0.338). A bevacizumab-containing induction regimen was more frequent in the combination group (13/22 vs. 2/51), and only seven deaths occurred in this comparison. Conclusions: Neither comparison showed a statistically significant PFS difference, and the study was not powered to evaluate OS or to establish superiority or equivalence. The small HRD-positive comparison and differences in prior treatment preclude a definitive conclusion about the relative efficacy of olaparib plus bevacizumab and niraparib.

articles.title: Role of Serum HE4, Selected Clinical Features and Diagnostic Prediction Models in Differentiating Benign and Malignant Endometrial Lesions in Polish Women: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Krejczy K, Rzepka J, Wiśniewska O et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The differentiation of endometrial cancer from non-malignant endometrial findings remains clinically important. We evaluated serum human epididymis protein 4 (HE4), clinical and ultrasound features, and two published diagnostic models, the Risk of Endometrial Malignancy (REM) score and Model A.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort, 110 women with abnormal uterine bleeding and/or ultrasound abnormalities underwent HE4 testing, transvaginal ultrasonography, and hysteroscopy with histopathological assessment. Original univariable analyses were supplemented by reanalysis of the individual study records, including ROC metrics, paired comparisons of AUCs, and an exploratory logistic model adjusting for age and endometrial thickness.
RESULTS: Endometrial cancer was diagnosed in 18 women; 92 had non-malignant findings. Median HE4 was higher in the cancer group (118.35 versus 52.3 pmol/L; p < 0.001, as originally reported). The AUC (95% bootstrap CI) was 0.834 (0.686-0.951) for HE4, 0.905 (0.794-0.981) for REM, and 0.840 (0.702-0.948) for Model A. AUC differences were not statistically significant (paired DeLong tests, all p > 0.10). In an exploratory adjusted analysis, each doubling of HE4 was associated with higher odds of malignancy (adjusted OR 5.41; 95% CI 1.81-16.21; p = 0.0025).
CONCLUSIONS: HE4 and both published models discriminated between malignant and non-malignant findings in this selected cohort. The findings are exploratory and require independent validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Platelet-Derived Extracellular Vesicles for the Diagnosis of Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Karlsson E, Gabrysch K, Stålberg K et al.
articles.abstract: Objective: Differentiating ovarian cancer from benign and borderline adnexal lesions remains challenging. We previously identified nine platelet protein markers associated with ovarian cancer. This study aimed to validate these markers on platelet-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) and assess their ability to distinguish ovarian cancer from benign and borderline adnexal lesions. Methods: Patients were recruited between 2021 and 2025 at Uppsala University Hospital and Gävle Hospital, Sweden, and grouped according to postoperative histopathological diagnosis. Platelet-free plasma samples were analyzed by flow cytometry. Platelet-derived EVs (CD41+) and nine platelet protein markers (ACTN4, CRKL, ERP29, GELS, MAP1A, MYCT1, PHB, RELN, and SRC) were quantified in CD41+CD62P+ and CD41+CD62P- EV populations. Group differences were assessed using non-parametric tests, binary and proportional-odds logistic regression, and Boruta feature selection. Results: The total CD41+ EVs and CD41+CD62P+ EVs did not differ between groups. The levels of CD62P+anti-GELS, CD62P+anti-SRC, and CD62P-anti-MYCT1 were highest in ovarian cancer. CD62P+anti-GELS was independently associated with ovarian cancer in both crude analysis (OR: 1.47, 95% CI: 1.16-1.85; C-statistic 0.63) and analysis adjusted for age and CA125 (OR: 1.59, 95% CI: 1.21-2.08; C-statistic 0.82). The Boruta algorithm identified ultrasound assessment and CA125, followed by CD62P+anti-GELS, CD62P-anti-SRC, CD62P-anti-ERP29, CD62P-anti-MAP1A, and CD62P+anti-ACTN4, as the variables associated with ovarian cancer. CD62P+anti-ERP29 was specifically associated with advanced-stage ovarian cancer compared with other abdominal malignancies (OR: 2.43, 95% CI: 1.53-4.38; C-statistic 0.85). Conclusion: CD62P+anti-GELS on platelet EVs was independently associated with ovarian cancer after adjustment for age and CA125. Together with CD62P+/CD62P- anti-SRC, CD62P+anti-ACTN4, CD62P-anti-ERP29 and CD62P-anti-MAP1A, it may complement ultrasound evaluation and CA125 in distinguishing ovarian cancer from benign and borderline adnexal lesions. The findings require further validation.

articles.title: DAMPs and NETs in Thyroid Diseases: Biological, Diagnostic, and Translational Perspectives.
articles.authors: Waczyński K, Choromańska B, Maciejczyk M et al.
articles.abstract: Thyroid diseases encompass a broad spectrum of autoimmune, inflammatory, and neoplastic disorders, yet current diagnostic approaches provide limited insight into innate immune activation and tumor-associated inflammatory remodeling. Damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as interconnected mediators of sterile inflammation with potential relevance to thyroid carcinogenesis, disease progression, and biomarker development. This narrative review synthesized literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus to evaluate the biological, diagnostic, and translational significance of DAMP- and NET-associated pathways in thyroid diseases, with particular emphasis on thyroid cancer. DAMPs such as high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), S100A8/A9, serum amyloid A, heat shock proteins, and extracellular nucleic acids may sustain inflammatory signaling through pattern-recognition receptors and contribute to tumor proliferation, angiogenesis, immune modulation, and therapeutic resistance. In parallel, circulating analytes associated with NET biology-including nonspecific cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and nucleosomes, pathway-associated citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), and composite myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA) complexes-have shown associations with thyroid malignancy, dedifferentiated disease, metastatic presentation, and greater disease severity. Experimental data further suggest that aggressive thyroid cancer cells, particularly anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, can induce extracellular trap formation and exploit neutrophil-derived signals to support tumor growth. However, limited disease specificity, assay heterogeneity, and the predominance of small or exploratory cohorts currently restrict clinical implementation. Future strategies should prioritize standardized, prospective validation of multimarker panels integrating DAMP- and NET-related analytes with imaging, cytology, molecular diagnostics, and clinicopathological risk stratification to determine whether they provide incremental value for diagnosis, prognostication, and longitudinal monitoring in thyroid cancer.

articles.title: Immune and Circulating Biomarkers in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Prognostic and Predictive Relevance for Immunotherapy.
articles.authors: Sidhom F, Karabiber E, ElBeblawy R et al.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based combinations have become the standard first-line systemic therapy, yet objective response rates remain modest (20-36%), and no HCC-specific immune biomarker has been validated to guide selection among standard ICI-based regimens. This review examines the prognostic and exploratory treatment-response associations of potential immune biomarkers in HCC, including markers within the tumor microenvironment (TME) and peripheral blood. A narrative review was conducted evaluating PD-L1 and soluble PD-L1, tumor mutational burden (TMB), tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), including machine learning-based assessment, gene expression profiles and tumor-intrinsic pathway alterations, long non-coding RNAs, inflammatory markers (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, alpha-fetoprotein), gut microbiota, and liquid biopsy analytes (circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, cell-free DNA). PD-L1 expression shows prognostic associations and inconsistent associations with ICI outcomes; inter-assay heterogeneity further limits its use, and routine PD-L1 testing is not recommended by current guidelines. TMB is generally low in HCC, with inconsistent associations with ICI response. High CD8+ TIL density is associated with improved survival after resection and favorable outcomes in exploratory ICI-treated cohorts, without validated treatment-selective utility. Inflammatory gene signatures and WNT/β-catenin pathway activation are associated with ICI outcomes. Gut microbiome features have shown exploratory associations with anti-PD-1 outcomes, with limited consistency across small datasets. Liquid biopsy markers, particularly ctDNA, show promise for recurrence prediction and treatment monitoring but lack assay standardization. Multiple immune biomarkers demonstrate prognostic value in HCC, and pre-existing immunity characterized by high CD8+ T-cell infiltration and inflammatory gene signatures is associated with improved ICI-based therapy outcomes in exploratory studies. However, these exploratory markers have not been validated for routine selection among HCC regimens. Future directions include prospective validation of composite biomarker panels, standardization of assessment methodologies, and integration of artificial intelligence for TME characterization.

articles.title: Risk Factor Profiles May Differ Between Younger-Onset and Late-Onset Colorectal Cancer: An Exploratory Analysis of Individual and Cumulative Risk Factors Among the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cohort.
articles.authors: Wigston L, Ahmed M, Abebe Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of young-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) are on the rise globally. Despite this growing burden, the drivers of young-onset adult CRC remain largely unknown.
AIMS: This study aimed to compare risk factor profiles between younger-onset and late-onset CRC to evaluate differences in their risk factor profiles.
METHODS: The Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial dataset, comprising ∼155,000 US participants including 1219 CRC cases, was analysed. Participants were stratified by age (≤59 vs. ≥60 years). Associations of demographic, clinical and behavioural risk factors with CRC were computed using multivariable Cox regression with the multiplicative interaction of exposures. Reduced rank regression was used to derive dietary patterns (DPs).
RESULTS: Among the ≤59-year cohort, no individual risk factor (excluding age) was independently associated with the risk of CRC. However, the multiplicative effect of hypertension and smoking had a nominal association with younger-onset CRC (p = 0.047). In contrast, in the ≥60-year cohort, individual (sex, body mass index, diabetes and alcohol) as well as combinations of risk factors were associated with CRC. Significant DPs appeared exclusively to impact the risk of CRC in the ≥60-year cohort. However, no interactions remained significant following correction for multiple testing; findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the drivers of CRC in younger individuals may be different from their older counterparts. These exploratory findings offer novel insight into CRC risk in the young and highlight the need to reconsider interactions between CRC risk factors.

articles.title: Pre-clinical medical students' perception of surgical professions and balance with personal life - a single-centre exploratory analysis.
articles.authors: Becker H, Gött H, Tellermann J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical professions deal with serious challenges to inspire students to pursue a surgical career and counteract demographic change. Students' interest in sub-specialization is influenced by socio-economic factors including work-life balance, flexible working hours and appreciation. However, robust data about the current perception of surgical professions in the early stage of medical education is lacking so far.
METHODS: We performed a voluntary online survey among students who participated in an elective neurosurgical course during their preclinical stage of medical studies. The investigator-developed survey addressed perception of unspecified surgical professions, including personal requirements, profession impact on health and lifestyle and the topic of gender disparities and family planning and was conducted before the students entered their elective course. We also assessed viewpoints on support programs facilitating compatibility of surgical training and family life.
RESULTS: A total of 109 students participated in the voluntary survey (66.1% female, 33.0% male, 0.9% not specified). Overall, 56.0% of respondents reported prior experience with surgical professions and 33.9% planned to pursue a surgical career. Most respondents (68.8%) rated surgical professions as more physically demanding than other specialties, and about half (49.5%) considered them more harmful to physicians' health. In contrast, only 26.6% rated the mental burden as higher in surgical than in other specialties. In the exploratory gender comparison, female participants more often agreed that male residents have better career chances in surgery, whereas male participants more often responded neutrally to this statement. Overall, 89.0% of participants expressed interest in unspecified support programs to improve the compatibility of professional and personal life, and 65.1% would be willing to accept a one-year extension of their surgical residency.
CONCLUSIONS: In summary, pre-clinical medical students of a preselected cohort tend to rate surgical disciplines as demanding, competitive and difficult to balance with private life. Most participants expressed interest in support programs for combining surgical training and family life which needs further evaluation in future studies.

articles.title: Serum concentrations of legacy, alternative, and precursor per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances: a descriptive analysis of premenopausal participants in the Canadian CARTaGENE cohort.
articles.journal: Environmental health : a global access science source
articles.authors: Borghese MM, Lelievre R, Packull-McCormick S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human biomonitoring studies of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have typically focused on legacy PFAS. Data for alternative and precursor PFAS are emerging, but are still scarce. These data are critical for assessing exposure and human health risk.
METHODS: We measured serum concentrations of 40 PFAS among 2,775 premenopausal participants from the CARTaGENE cohort (Phase A: 2009-2010; Phase B: 2013-2014). We examined differences in geometric mean serum concentrations of PFAS with > 60% detection, as well as the sum of 7 PFAS (Σ7PFAS), across categories of sociodemographic, lifestyle, and reproductive history characteristics.
RESULTS: Eight PFAS were detected in > 60% of participants. Geometric mean serum concentrations ranged from 0.03 µg/L (PFHpS and MeFOSAA) to 4.25 µg/L for PFOS and 8.00 µg/L for Σ7PFAS. The largest differences in serum PFAS concentrations were observed across reproductive history characteristics. Concentrations of PFOS, PFNA, PFOA, PFHxS, and the Σ7PFAS were monotonically lower with each additional child birthed, higher with increasing time since last pregnancy, and lower among those with a history of breastfeeding. The PFAS reducing effect of parity appeared to outweigh the bioaccumulative effect of age for most legacy PFAS. Concentrations of PFOS, PFNA, PFOA, PFHxS, PFDA, PFUnA and the Σ7PFAS were lower among participants with a reported household income below the Canadian low-income cut-off. Several alternative and precursor PFAS were detected in this population, including sulfonamidoacetic acids, sulfonamides, fluorotelomers, and fluoroethers, but serum concentrations were relatively low, with 95th percentiles < 0.5 µg/L.
CONCLUSIONS: This work contributes to expanding human biomonitoring data beyond legacy PFAS, and our findings suggest that exposure to low levels of some alternative and precursor PFAS may be widespread in Canada. These results also reinforce the role of pregnancy and breastfeeding as excretion pathways for legacy PFAS and support previous investigations demonstrating that exposure to some PFAS may be lower amongst financially disadvantaged populations.

articles.title: Breast arterial calcification in women with permanent postoperative hypoparathyroidism: a case-control study.
articles.authors: Önder ÇE, Öztekin PS, Fırat SN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoparathyroidism (HypoPT) has been reported to cause calcifications in multiple organs over the long term. This study evaluated breast arterial calcification (BAC) in female patients who developed permanent hypoparathyroidism (persisting for more than 12 months) after thyroidectomy.
METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study, 40 women with permanent postoperative hypoparathyroidism (Po-HypoPT) were compared with 40 post-thyroidectomy women without hypoparathyroidism (control group). All mammograms were reviewed for the presence of parenchymal, ductal, and breast arterial calcification, and the BAC score was calculated in women with mammographically detected BAC.
RESULTS: The two groups were comparable in terms of age, body mass index, and menopausal status (p = 0.784, p = 0.142, and p = 0.653, respectively). The median interval after thyroidectomy was 9.50 (6.00-15.00) years in the permanent Po-HypoPT group and 10.00 (8.00-15.75) years in the control group (p = 0.354). The frequencies of parenchymal and ductal calcification did not differ between the permanent Po-HypoPT and control groups (p = 1.000 and p = 0.241, respectively). In terms of BAC, the permanent Po-HypoPT group had more patients with BAC than the control group (12 [30.0%] and 3 [7.5%], respectively, p = 0.010; OR = 5.28, 95% CI: 1.36-20.53). The mean total BAC scores were 1.75 ± 2.99 in the permanent Po-HypoPT group and 0.32 ± 1.18 in the control group (p = 0.008). In multivariable linear regression analysis, permanent Po-HypoPT emerged as a significant independent predictor of the total BAC score (β = 0.331, p = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: Permanent Po-HypoPT was independently associated with an increased BAC burden, after adjustment for age, menopausal status, and metabolic risk factors. BAC assessment on routine mammography may represent a potential imaging marker of cardiovascular risk in this population. Given the modest sample size and the wide confidence interval of the effect estimate, these findings should be regarded as exploratory and require confirmation in larger, prospective studies.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Clinical, virological and immunological characteristics of people living with HTLV at a Swedish tertiary referral center.
articles.authors: Svensson AK, Vesterbacka J, Gredmark-Russ S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of HTLV in Sweden is presumed to be low, however comprehensive data are lacking. This study describes clinical and laboratory characteristics of patients with HTLV infection followed at the outpatient clinic of Karolinska University Hospital in Stockholm, Sweden.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of all HTLV positive patients followed at our clinic between January 2013 and May 2024. Demographics, mode of transmission, HTLV type, proviral load (PVL), co-infections, diagnosis of HTLV-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP) or adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL), and immunological markers were extracted from medical records.
RESULTS: We included 102 patients (82% HTLV-1, 18% HTLV-2). The median age was 56 years (IQR 42-62; range 23-81) and 54% were women. Twenty-nine percent of the patients were born in Sweden, while the rest had other countries of origin (33% Middel East; 16% South America; 11% Africa, and 5% the Caribbean). HTLV infection was identified by contact tracing (35%), blood donor or IVF screening (31%), and symptom-based testing (7%). Mother-to-child transmission was considered a possible route of infection in four Swedish born individuals. Ten individuals (12% of people living with HTLV-1) had HAM/TSP, and two were diagnosed with ATLL. Patients with HAM/TSP had higher median PVL than asymptomatic carriers. The proportion of regulatory T cells were higher in symptomatic individuals and was positively correlated with PVL.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first comprehensive characterization of a cohort of people living with HTLV in Sweden. Despite the low national prevalence, we observed a notable proportion of symptomatic cases, including HAM/TSP and ATLL. We also observed four cases of MTCT in individuals born in Sweden.

articles.title: A scoping review of micro-ultrasound in male infertility: mapping the evidence from testicular microarchitecture to the distal seminal tract.
articles.authors: Dell'Atti L
articles.abstract: Micro-ultrasound (micro-US), a 29-MHz modality with a resolution of about 70 µm established in prostate cancer diagnosis, and related very-high-resolution ultrasound techniques could refine the evaluation of male infertility, but their use in this field has not been mapped. This scoping review, reported according to PRISMA-ScR, charted the evidence on micro-US, very-high-frequency (≥ 20 MHz) ultrasound and ultrasound localisation microscopy (ULM) for the diagnosis and prognosis of male infertility, from testicular microarchitecture to the distal seminal tract. On 1 October 2026, 38 web-based queries and citation tracking covered sources indexing PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar. Of the 91 records screened, nine sources were included: four ULM studies, three reports of 36-46-MHz quantitative ultrasound (two preprints, one conference abstract), one high-frequency study with histological correlation and one registered 29-MHz micro-US trial without results. Human cohorts ranged from 7 to 94 men. ULM vessel diameter and density were lower in non-obstructive than in obstructive azoospermia (area under the curve, AUC, 0.81-0.95), and ULM detected the response to gonadotrophin therapy earlier than testicular volume in seven men. Quantitative features discriminated sperm presence (AUC 0.77-0.93). No study examined the vas deferens, epididymis, seminal vesicles, ejaculatory ducts or varicocele; none was externally validated, and none reported retrieval, pregnancy or live birth outcomes. The evidence is early, small and testis centred, and these methods remain investigational. Prospective validation against histology and surgical sperm retrieval, with clinical outcomes, and exploration of the distal seminal tract are priorities.

articles.title: Metabolomics and lipidomics in the differentiation of CIN 2 and CIN 3: an exploratory pilot study.
articles.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
articles.authors: de Souza Leão LQ, Marques GM, de Souza Carolino A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: High-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 2-3) is a precursor lesion to cervical cancer and, although it presents different probabilities of regression and progression, it is usually grouped together in screening and managed similarly. However, the mechanisms that determine its evolution are still poorly understood, and standard treatment by conization can lead to reproductive complications such as subfertility and premature birth.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify metabolic and lipid signatures that can distinguish between CIN 2 and CIN 3 lesions using liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS).
METHODS: Tissue samples from the lesion and adjacent margin of 24 women with CIN 2-3 were subjected to metabolomic and lipidomic analysis by LC-HRMS. Multivariate statistical analyses, pathway analysis, and correlation were performed to understand these neoplasms' development and progression and identify potential metabolites and lipids to distinguish such lesions.
RESULTS: Metabolomic and lipidomic analysis by LC-HRMS in cervical tissue identified molecular signatures with differential abundance between CIN 2 and CIN 3, highlighting patterns associated with the degree of lesion. Multivariate analyses highlighted metabolites (serine, glutamic acid, guanidine-6-monophosphate, succinic acid, mannose 6-phosphate, and taurine) and lipids (TG 49:1, TG 50:1, and TG 52:2) as the main contributors to the discrimination between the groups, suggesting relevant biological alterations in high-grade cervical lesions.
CONCLUSION: Combination metabolomic and lipidomic approach enabled the identification of metabolites and lipids potentially involved in the pathogenesis of intraepithelial neoplasia (CINs). In addition, these identified metabolite and lipid panels are promising as complementary tools for future screening strategies for these lesions.

articles.title: "Aguantarse, Sacar Adelante": A Hermeneutic Phenomenological Account of Paternal Postpartum Distress among Mexican Fathers.
articles.authors: Sable S
articles.abstract: Paternal perinatal distress is increasingly recognized as a clinical and family-systems concern, yet remains underexamined in Mexico and across Latin America. Situated within Mexican ethnopsychology and the study of cultural idioms of distress, this hermeneutic phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of three first-time Mexican fathers navigating emotional difficulty during the first 24 months following childbirth. Interviews were conducted in Spanish and analyzed through the hermeneutic circle, with attention to the cultural-moral frameworks within which fathers' narratives became sayable. Three themes were identified: the cultural shape of paternal distress in fathers' own vocabulary; the script of endurance and silence organized around aguantarse (to endure silently) and sacar adelante (to push forward for the family); and the invisibility of paternal distress within clinical, familial, and structural support systems. Findings indicate that paternal postpartum distress in Mexican contexts is produced and obscured by a culturally specific masculine script that constitutes a meaningful and addressable target for clinical and policy intervention.

articles.title: Epigenetic alterations in the placenta associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy.
articles.authors: Ganster F, Kallenberg F, Titova A et al.
articles.abstract: Histone modifications play a key role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulatory potential. Previously, reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 and acetylated H3K9ac were observed in placentas from women with preeclampsia. Building on these findings, this study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy or at delivery is associated with changes in placental histone modifications. Immunohistochemical staining, exploratory western blot analysis, and qualitative immunofluorescence were performed on placental sections from 60 patients stratified into four groups: women with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery, women with prior infection during gestation, vaccinated controls, and unvaccinated controls. H3K4me3 levels in the syncytiotrophoblast were significantly reduced in both SARS-CoV-2-exposed groups compared to unvaccinated controls, with the most pronounced reduction observed in women with prior infection during gestation. H3K9ac levels did not differ significantly between groups in any compartment after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant associations were found between SCT H3K4me3 levels and maternal age, gestational age, or birthweight, and a sensitivity analysis excluding cases with additional placental pathologies confirmed the robustness of the findings. As no gene expression profiling was performed, functional or transcriptional consequences of the observed H3K4me3 changes cannot be inferred. These descriptive findings warrant further investigation integrating epigenetic and transcriptomic approaches to clarify their functional relevance for placental biology and pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Antenatal inflammation drives postpartum cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
articles.authors: Bert S, Christensen AP, Bulletti M et al.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), including preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, are strongly associated with maternal cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy. We hypothesized that maternal inflammation drives persistent postpartum cardiac maladaptation after HDPs. We conducted a prospective longitudinal study assessing cardiac function and circulating inflammatory profiles during pregnancy and 3-6 months postpartum, complemented by a preclinical mechanistic mouse model recapitulating key antenatal and postpartum immune and cardiac features of HDPs. Here we show that distinct antenatal inflammatory signatures, including elevated chemokines, correlated with adverse left ventricular structure and function 3-6 months postpartum, despite resolution of systemic inflammation. Mechanistically, our preclinical HDP mouse model demonstrates that reduced antenatal progesterone, also observed in patients with HDPs, drives inflammation and postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Antenatal (embryonic day 14.5), but not postpartum (postpartum day 28), progesterone treatment prevented postpartum cardiac dysfunction, identifying both a potential mechanistic and therapeutic strategy to reduce long-term maternal cardiovascular morbidity.

articles.title: Future considerations in the surgical technique for vasectomy.
articles.authors: Mutter M, Garrett J, Williams J et al.
articles.abstract: There have been minimal changes in the vasectomy surgery technique in the last 50 years. Since the introduction of the "No Scalpel" technique in the 1970's, which itself is a minor change in how to open the scrotal skin, the traditional vasectomy has changed little with time. Nevertheless, there are now exciting new modalities being developed for the obstruction of the vas deferens that could change the technique for the better in the future. One of them is injection of a vasal-occlusive polymer (plug) that aims to be a less invasive and reversible form of male contraception. This product appears to be in the development pipeline of several companies worldwide. Another technique involves using a bipolar laparoscopic vessel sealing technology for a sealed vasectomy procedure that may be done transdermal in the future. In the everchanging area of reproductive health, there will be more male contraceptive techniques developed that improve accessibility, efficiency, and likely reversibility of male sterility.

articles.title: Neuropathic Pain in Women With Chronic Pelvic Pain: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses
articles.authors: Nogueira Neto J, Camapum LFC, Camapum DMSR et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate the prevalence of neuropathic pain among women with chronic pelvic pain and explore associated clinical characteristics.
DESIGN: Prospective observational study.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a pelvic pain and endometriosis outpatient clinic between August 2022 and July 2025. Women underwent anamnesis, physical and complementary examinations, and questionnaire assessment. Neuropathic pain was classified using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 questionnaire. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment was applied to comparisons as a single family.
RESULTS: The prevalence of neuropathic pain was 34.3%. A higher Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire total score was the only association retained after adjustment (p < .001; q = 0.004). Parity (p = .010), miscarriage history (p = .049), fibromyalgia (p = .016), infertility (p = .019), irritable bowel syndrome (p = .046), urinary symptoms (p = .005), myofascial pain (p = .004), and anxiety (p = .024) showed nominal associations only.
CONCLUSION: Neuropathic pain was common in this specialized clinic population, and greater sensory and affective pain severity was the only association retained after multiplicity adjustment. The other eight nominal findings are exploratory and require confirmation; multidimensional assessment remains relevant to individualized care.
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Neuropathic pain screening may complement comprehensive nursing assessment of women with chronic pelvic pain. Integrating pain characteristics, associated symptoms, and patient priorities may support individualized multidisciplinary evaluation and care.

articles.title: Illuminating the in vivo placenta: Use of optical spectroscopy techniques for assessing placental oxygenation.
articles.authors: Arenas GA, Ko T, Schwartz N
articles.abstract: Placental oxygenation reflects a dynamic interplay between maternal perfusion, villous architecture, and fetal consumption. Disturbances in this system often precede adverse pregnancy outcomes. Optical spectroscopy, the use of light to analyze the properties of matter, has been applied to non-invasively interrogate these physiologic processes. By illuminating tissue at select wavelengths in the near-infrared range, near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) can detect relative changes in oxyhemoglobin and deoxyhemoglobin, which exhibit distinct absorption properties at these wavelengths. Moreover, diffuse optical spectroscopy, commonly used to refer to advanced NIRS techniques that independently quantify scattering and absorption in deep tissues, provide absolute quantification of oxyhemoglobin and deoxyhemoglobin tissue concentrations, thereby linking tissue composition to functional oxygen delivery and enabling the study of these dynamics during maternal or fetal stress. Photoacoustic imaging, another related technique, further enhances physiologic assessment by combining optical contrast with ultrasound resolution to map vascular structure and estimate oxygen saturation within specific placental regions, enabling serial assessments of vascular remodeling and metabolic alterations. In this review, we will provide an overview of these methods and how they have been applied to the study of placental function and pregnancy outcomes. For example, some of these techniques have been used to demonstrate that pregnancies complicated by hypertensive disorders of pregnancy or fetal growth restriction show reduced placental oxygenation and altered hemodynamic responsiveness. We illustrate how optical spectroscopy has the potential to evaluate physiologic vulnerabilities that are otherwise undetectable with conventional imaging.

articles.title: Gynecologic hybrid and interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy.
