articles.authors: Patel AK, Dare A, Horne ZD et al.
articles.abstract: Advances in high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy techniques have improved local control and reduced morbidities associated with brachytherapy. Interstitial brachytherapy (ISBT) has traditionally been used for locally advanced gynecologic cancers not amenable to less invasive intracavitary brachytherapy (ICBT) techniques. The recent advent of hybrid brachytherapy (HBT) involves using modern brachytherapy applicators that combine intracavitary and interstitial components to optimize tumor target coverage and reduce normal tissue exposure. Given the importance of brachytherapy in the non-operative management of locally advanced gynecologic cancers, knowledge of and procedural competency with ISBT and HBT is crucial. However, gynecologic brachytherapy training during radiation oncology residency is variable, with significant gaps in experience and case numbers reported by resident trainees. The advent of HBT and ISBT may further exacerbate these gaps, as not all centers are equipped to provide training in high-quality HBT and ISBT. To this end, this article aims to summarize important concepts in ISBT and HBT, with a focus on cervical cancer, and to describe brachytherapy applicators, aspects of procedural competency, target delineation, treatment planning, and toxicity management.

articles.title: Prevalence and patterns of parental disability in UK families: findings from a nationally representative birth cohort study.
articles.authors: Zeng L, Auyeung B, Marryat L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Parental disability not only affects parents’ own health but may also impact the health and development of the children they care for. However, little is known about families in which a parent is disabled, particularly in the UK context. This study addresses this gap to examine the prevalence, longitudinal patterns and family characteristics of parental disability using UK birth cohort data spanning 14 years.
DESIGN: This population-based birth cohort study uses a longitudinal design.
SETTING: The UK.
PARTICIPANTS: Data came from the UK Millennium Cohort Study, a nationally representative dataset of 11 153 children and their families (including 11 138 mothers and 8534 fathers) followed from birth to age 14 years.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Parental disability was measured using parents’ self-report of limiting longstanding illness at the 9-month, 5-year, 7-year, 11-year and 14-year sweeps. Longitudinal patterns of parental disability were identified using latent class analysis. We examined associations between patterns of parental disability and demographic, health, socioeconomic and geographical characteristics across time using regression models.
RESULTS: Of the cohort children, 42.5% (95% CI 41.1 to 43.8) had a parent who reported disability at least once by the time children were 14 years old. Four longitudinal patterns of parental disability were identified: low-probability (77.1% (76.0 to 78.1)), early-childhood-peak (11.7% (10.9 to 12.5)), late-childhood-onset (7.0% (6.4 to 7.6)) and chronic (4.2% (3.7 to 4.7)) parental disability. Compared with the low-parental disability pattern, chronic parental disability had the strongest associations with parental general ill-health and mental distress, poverty, area-level deprivation and child disability; early-childhood-peak parental disability was associated with a higher prevalence of child preterm birth, and late-childhood-onset parental disability was characterised by lower household education, younger parents and single-parenthood.
CONCLUSIONS: A substantial population of British children grows up in families in which a parent experiences disability, with distinct longitudinal patterns of parental disability differing in associations with family health, socioeconomic and area disparities. Our findings underline the importance of taking a whole-family perspective when designing services and policies that affect disabled people.

articles.title: Genome sequencing in prenatal precision medicine of congenital malformations: Clinical experience from a single center.
articles.authors: Westenius E, Conner P, Sahlin E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As a part of implementing genome sequencing in prenatal precision medicine at the department of Clinical Genetics and Genomics, Karolinska University Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden, we evaluated the utility of genome sequencing for prenatally detected malformations, including diagnostic yield, turnaround time and impact on current and future pregnancies.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study comprised 218 fetuses with different malformations. One hundred and two prospectively collected samples were analyzed using clinical trio genome sequencing, and if non-diagnostic, they underwent research analysis. In addition, 116 samples were collected retrospectively and included all fetuses referred for clinical trio genome sequencing during the study period. As part of the clinical routine at the time of the study, quantitative fluorescent-polymerase chain reaction and chromosomal microarray had been performed before genome sequencing in 84.9% (185/218) of cases.
RESULTS: Clinical genome sequencing identified a molecular diagnosis in 22.5% (49/218) of the cases. Research analysis revealed two additional causative variants increasing the diagnostic yield to 23.4% (51/218). The phenotypes of the cases were divided into different groups with following diagnostic yields: 36.2% (21/58) in multisystem malformations, 30.8% (8/26) in skeletal malformations, 25.0% (14/56) in malformations in the central nervous system, 15.6% (5/32) in thoracic malformations, 11.5% (3/26) in abdominal malformations, and 0% (0/20) in other isolated anomalies. Additionally, four variants were considered potentially clinically relevant. A total of 39.2% (20/51) of the causative variants were related to a risk of recurrence. The turnaround time for clinical genome sequencing in ongoing pregnancies, when requested before gestational week 21 + 6 and prior to a parental decision on pregnancy continuation, was 12.5 ± 5 days (mean ± standard deviation, n = 40). Pregnancies with diagnostic results from genome sequencing were more likely to be terminated than those with normal results (p = 0.012, Fisher's exact test).
CONCLUSIONS: Genome sequencing has an important role in prenatal precision medicine, since it can detect the underlying cause of prenatally detected malformations in a reasonable time. As causative chromosome aberrations were excluded in most of the cases, an even higher diagnostic yield can be expected if genome sequencing is offered as a first-line test or after a normal rapid…

articles.title: Chronic Endometritis: Does the Current Evidence Justify Routine Diagnosis and Treatment?
articles.authors: Pirtea P, Hurni Y, Polyzos NP et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic endometritis (CE) has become a widely investigated and increasingly treated condition in reproductive medicine, despite persistent uncertainty regarding its biological and clinical validity. In this review, we critically examine whether CE, as currently defined by endometrial CD138-positive plasma cells, constitutes a clinically meaningful pathology that justifies routine screening and management. Current diagnostic criteria are heterogeneous and unvalidated; CD138-positive plasma cells vary across the menstrual cycle and are also found in fertile women, while evidence for a consistent infectious or inflammatory phenotype remains lacking. Although an association between CE and reproductive failure has been reported in several observational studies vulnerable to confounding, large euploid embryo transfer studies challenge the existence of a prevalent endometrial factor that substantially impairs implantation. Most importantly, while antibiotics reduce CD138 positivity, controlled studies have not shown any impact of treatment on reproductive outcomes, and apparent benefits largely arise from methodologically weaker comparisons. Until biological validity and clinical benefit are established, routine screening and treatment for CE in reproductive medicine cannot be justified.

articles.title: VIEWS AND REVIEWS DIFFUSE ADENOMYOSIS PRIOR TO FROZEN EMBRYO TRANSFER: CLINICAL RELEVANCE, DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT.
articles.authors: Luna M, Hernández-Martínez C, Alkon T
articles.abstract: Adenomyosis has evolved from a rare histopathological curiosity, first described in hysterectomy specimens in the nineteenth century, into a condition now commonly recognized in reproductive-aged women undergoing assisted reproductive technology. This transition largely reflects the widespread adoption of high-resolution transvaginal ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging, which have made it possible to identify the disease well before the stage of overt symptoms or surgical specimens. As a result, diffuse adenomyosis, once regarded as a symptomatic disease of older, parous women, is now frequently found as a clinically silent condition in young, nulliparous patients presenting for fertility care. This growing recognition has clinical importance because adenomyosis is consistently associated with poorer reproductive outcomes after in vitro fertilization, including lower pregnancy and live birth rates and a higher risk of miscarriage, with the strength of this association tied to disease severity and phenotype rather than to its mere presence. These observations provide the biological rationale for optimizing the uterine environment before frozen embryo transfer (FET), an approach made feasible by the ability to separate embryo availability from the timing of transfer. A range of hormonal, medical, and surgical strategies have been proposed for this purpose, though current evidence does not yet support a single, universal pretreatment approach. This manuscript reviews the historical background, contemporary epidemiology, and clinical impact of diffuse adenomyosis in assisted reproduction outcome and introduces a planned series of subsequent manuscripts addressing its pathophysiology, diagnosis, and medical and surgical management prior to FET in greater depth.

articles.title: Uterine management during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy: outcomes from a standardized surgical technique.
articles.authors: Duca LL, Armengaud C, Bader G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The optimal uterine management during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy remains debated. Although supracervical hysterectomy is generally preferred because of concerns regarding mesh exposure, total hysterectomy may be indicated in selected clinical situations. We compared perioperative and anatomical outcomes according to uterine management during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 178 patients undergoing primary laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy for stage ≥2 pelvic organ prolapse (POP-Q) between January 2010 and May 2025. Patients underwent uterine preservation (n=115), supracervical hysterectomy (n=31), or total hysterectomy (n=32). Primary outcomes were severe postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo grades III-IV) and prolapse recurrence according to the composite Barber definition. Secondary outcomes included mesh exposure and postoperative anatomical results.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 18.5 months, severe complications were uncommon with no statistically significant differences between groups (0.9%, 3.2%, and 3.1%; P=0.30). Mesh exposure (2.6%, 0%, and 6.2%; P=0.40) and prolapse recurrence (12%, 19%, and 6.3%; P=0.30) did not differ according to uterine management. Post operative point C differed across groups (P<0.01), as did point Ba (P=0.03). Point Bp did not differ significantly (P=0.20;).
CONCLUSIONS: Severe postoperative complications and prolapse recurrence were uncommon in this cohort, with no statistically significant differences between uterine management groups. Given the small number of events and the limited size of the hysterectomy groups, these findings do not establish comparable safety or effectiveness. The clinical relevance of the observed differences in postoperative POP-Q measurements remains uncertain.

articles.title: Two Decades of Single Ventricle Palliation: Survival Improvement and the Persistent Burden of Fontan Morbidity.
articles.authors: Lim JH, Kim MJ, You J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population-level data on long-term outcomes after single ventricle staged palliation in East Asian cohorts are lacking. We examined era-specific trends in survival, Fontan completion, and morbidity in a Korean nationwide cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data (2002-2023). Patients undergoing Stage I palliation were stratified into four calendar-period eras and followed through December 2023. Survival and morbidity were assessed by Cox regression; Fontan completion was analyzed by Fine-Gray competing risk methods and at fixed post-palliation horizons.
RESULTS: Among 1,732 patients (median follow-up 20.0-199.9 months), adjusted mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.54 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.69) and 0.35 (95% CI, 0.26-0.48) in eras 3 and 4 versus era 1 (both P<.001), with the largest gains in hypoplastic left heart syndrome. Fontan completion did not differ across eras; at 36 months, cumulative incidence was 17.3%-19.4% (P=.80). Heart failure (HR, 2.12), thromboembolism (HR, 2.37), and reintervention hazards rose in era 4, whereas arrhythmia declined (HR, 0.26). Female sex, preterm birth, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome independently predicted mortality, as did socioeconomic position below the highest stratum in a categorical specification.
CONCLUSIONS: Over two decades, survival after single ventricle palliation improved substantially in Korea, most strikingly in hypoplastic left heart syndrome, whereas Fontan attainment did not improve at a common horizon. The rise in heart failure and thromboembolism, together with higher mortality below the highest socioeconomic stratum, identifies a growing population requiring lifelong surveillance and targeted support.

articles.title: Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT) alleviates inflammation-driven perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 cascade.
articles.authors: Du J, Cheng Y, Liu B et al.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction is closely correlated with chronic ovarian inflammation and decreased ovarian reserve, with the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory pathway serving as the core pathogenic regulator. Targeted inhibition of this inflammatory signaling cascade and subsequent ovarian cell apoptosis is a key therapeutic approach for improving perimenopausal ovarian lesions. Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT), a classic TCM formula, clears internal heat and nourishes yin and blood, and is traditionally used for perimenopausal night sweats due to yin deficiency with internal heat. Consistent with the pathology of perimenopausal ovarian inflammatory injury, these traditional properties provide an ethnopharmacological basis for alleviating chronic ovarian inflammation and protecting granulosa cells, supporting its potential in treating perimenopausal ovarian dysfunction.
AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms of Danggui Liuhuang Tang (DGLHT) and its heat-clearing herb group (QRJD) on ovarian dysfunction in a natural perimenopause (PM) rat model.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: UHPLC-MS/MS characterized the chemical and blood-absorbed components of DGLHT and QRJD. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations identified core targets and bioactive constituents. Naturally aged rats (12-14 months old) were randomized into Control, PM, DGLH-L/M/H, QRJD, and celecoxib (CEL) groups. Parameters assessed included body weight, ovarian index, estrous cyclicity, serum sex hormones, follicular atresia, granulosa cell apoptosis, inflammatory factors in serum and ovarian tissue, and the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway activity. Validation was performed in TLR4-overexpressing KGN cells treated with DGLHT-containing serum.
RESULTS: Baicalein and Wogonin were identified as key blood-absorbed components targeting TLR4, Caspase-3, IL-1β, and TNF-α. Both DGLHT and QRJD restored estrous cycles, improved ovarian coefficients, expanded the pool of healthy follicles, and reduced follicular atresia rates. Additionally, both formulations reduced granulosa cell apoptosis, corrected hormonal imbalances (increased E2 and P4, decreased FSH and LH), and downregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-18, TNF-α) and key proteins (TLR4, NF-κB p65, NLRP3, Caspase-3). Their anti-inflammatory efficacy was comparable to that of CEL, with medium- and high-dose DGLHT demonstrating superior endocrine protection. In vitro,…

articles.title: Distinct Plasma and Fecal Lipidomic Responses to Stearic, Palmitic and Oleic Acids-Enriched Diets in Postmenopausal Women.
articles.authors: Zhang W, Matuszek G, Dolnikowski GG et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary saturated fat intake is associated with an unfavorable plasma lipidomic profile and increased CVD risk. Stearic acid (18:0), a saturated fatty acid (SFA) has been shown to lower plasma LDL-cholesterol concentrations compared to other shorter-chain SFAs, but its broader lipidomic effects remain unclear. We aimed to address this by analyzing fasting and non-fasting plasma and fecal lipidomes using samples from a randomized crossover study in postmenopausal women (N=20, 64±7 years, BMI 26.4±3.4kg/m2) who consumed isocaloric diets enriched in 16:0, 18:0, and 18:1 for 5 weeks each, with 2-week washouts. Lipidomic profiles (cholesteryl esters [CE], diglycerides and triglycerides [DG, TG], phosphatidylcholines [PC], ceramides (Cer), sphingomyelins [SM], and free fatty acids [FFA]) were measured by QTOF mass spectrometry. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis, and spearman correlation analyses assessed diet separation (Variable Importance of Projection score >1.0) and associations between lipidomic and circulating lipid profiles, respectively. The 16:0 diet resulted in higher fasting plasma concentrations of lipid species across multiple classes relative to the 18:0 and 18:1 diet. The nonfasting lipidome showed higher long-chain glycerolipids, PC species, and CE 16:1 concentrations after the 18:0 compared to the 16:0 diet, and higher FFAs and several sphingolipid species in the fecal lipidome relative to the 18:1 diet. Several SM, DG, TG, and PC species were positively associated with LDL cholesterol and TG concentrations (r= 0.68 to 0.75, FDR<0.1) in fasting plasma following the 18:0 diet. These findings demonstrate that individual SFAs exert differential effects across metabolic compartments, influencing circulating lipid concentrations.

articles.title: Mechanistic and Clinical Implications of Apolipoprotein Abnormalities in Preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Wang H, Liu W, Wan S et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-specific disorder characterized by hypertension and organ dysfunction. Lipid disturbances are associated with PE, but conventional lipid concentrations do not fully describe the accompanying changes in lipoprotein function. This narrative review examines apolipoprotein physiology during pregnancy, reported abnormalities in PE, and their possible mechanistic and clinical implications. Human observational and proteomic studies report changes in apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), apolipoprotein C-III (ApoC-III), and apolipoprotein E (ApoE), although their direction and magnitude vary with gestational timing, population, and disease phenotype. Experimental studies support selected pathways involving cholesterol handling and vascular protection; emerging research on apolipoprotein D (ApoD) also implicates placental ferroptosis in model systems. Direct causal evidence for an apolipoprotein M (ApoM)-sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) pathway in PE remains limited, although gestation-dependent alterations in ApoM and S1P have been reported in late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE). The available evidence supports a bidirectional conceptual framework in which placental hypoxia may influence maternal lipid and vascular dysfunction, while maternal metabolic disturbances may also aggravate placental injury. Apolipoprotein alterations could therefore be contributors, consequences, or both. Their potential use as complementary biomarkers requires prospective validation and demonstration of added value beyond established clinical and angiogenic assessment. Pregnancy-specific efficacy and safety data are also needed before apolipoprotein-directed therapies can be considered for PE.

articles.title: Functional contribution of TERT to mitigation of endometrial stromal cell senescence by metformin through modulation of the AKT/mTOR axis.
articles.authors: Lee W, Song G, Bae H
articles.abstract: Uterine aging contributes significantly to infertility and adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly in women of advanced reproductive age. While telomere dysfunction and cellular senescence are established hallmarks of aging, therapeutic strategies targeting these processes in the uterus remain limited. This study investigated the effects of metformin on senescence-associated phenotypes in hTERT-immortalized human endometrial stromal cells (THESCs) and examined the potential contribution of TERT and AKT/mTOR signaling. Through an integrative network pharmacology approach, we identified 37 overlapping targets related to metformin, senescence, and uterine function, with TERT, AKT, and mTOR emerging as key targets. Metformin significantly restored cell proliferation, reduced senescence markers (P16, P21), and alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress in late-passage and D-galactose-treated THESCs. Notably, Metformin also increased relative telomere length and TERT expression. TERT knockdown attenuated selected metformin-associated effects, including changes in cellular phenotypes and AKT/mTOR signaling, supporting a functional contribution of TERT. Exploratory molecular docking identified predicted binding poses of metformin with TERT, AKT, and mTOR. Moreover, metformin treatment in aged mice was associated with improved uterine histological features and changes in TERT, AKT, mTOR, and P16 immunoreactivity, and an increased number of pups. Collectively, these findings support a functional contribution of TERT to selected metformin-associated responses in THESCs, accompanied by changes in mitochondrial and redox phenotypes and AKT/mTOR phosphorylation. Further studies are required to define the causal relationships among these pathways and determine their relevance to physiological reproductive aging.

articles.title: Association of over-the-counter contraceptive pill use and knowledge of side effects in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.authors: Rodriguez MI, Burns H, Modlin EW et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Misconceptions about oral contraceptive side effects are common among users and may contribute to dissatisfaction and discontinuation independent of actual side effect experience.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether users of oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) hold accurate expectations about common side effects, including both labeled effects and commonly held misconceptions, and whether these expectations differ by how the pill is obtained, by prescription or over the counter (OTC).
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of baseline survey data that included information on contraceptive counseling (e.g., source, timing, and content) in a prospective cohort study of OCP users. Our primary outcome was the difference in knowledge of expected side effects between individuals obtaining their pills by prescription versus OTC. We assessed four side effects in two categories: effects listed in FDA-approved labeling for both progestin-only (POP) and combined (COC) pills (irregular bleeding/spotting; lighter or absent periods) and commonly held beliefs not supported by placebo-controlled evidence (weight change; decreased libido).
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 741 participants including 299 (40.4%) acquiring OTC POPs and 442 (59.6%) by prescription. The cohort was predominantly White (70.7%), aged 18-24 (36.6%), employed (65.0%), and commercially insured (62.6%). The OTC group had increased odds of anticipating irregular bleeding or spotting compared to the prescription group (aOR 1.42; 95% CI 1.03, 1.96) but were less likely to anticipate lighter or absent periods (aOR 0.67; 95% CI 0.49, 0.92). The OTC group was less likely to expect decreased libido (aOR 0.47; 95% CI 0.31, 0.70). There was no significant difference in expectations of weight change between groups (aOR 0.78; 95% CI 0.56, 1.08).
CONCLUSION: Individuals acquiring their OCP OTC had similar or more accurate side-effect expectations than those obtaining their OCP by prescription, including less endorsement of decreased libido, a commonly held but unsupported belief. Neither group differed in its expectation of weight change.

articles.title: Hofbauer Cells and Placental Villous Inflammation in Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Spatial and Functional Analyses.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Weng J, Copple K, Bernier E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth is a major cause of neonatal morbidity/mortality strongly associated with pathological placental inflammation, but cellular mechanisms leading to this inflammation are poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE(S): Our objectives were to ascertain which immune cells are in the placental villi, understand cell-specific profiles through technologies maintaining cell localization within the tissue, and determine the role of Hofbauer cells in the dysregulated placental inflammation during preterm versus term birth with a focus on spontaneous preterm birth.
STUDY DESIGN: We first evaluated what cells (immune) are in the placental villi and which could be contributing to placental inflammation. We included 228 patients with preterm or term deliveries, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, and obtained placentas for histological analysis and performed imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on a subset of tissue (n=24). Fresh placentas were also obtained to determine the inflammatory mediator profile and cell-specific protein production by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and flow cytometry (n=8-11).
RESULTS: Imaging mass cytometry revealed that placental macrophages (Hofbauer cells) were the main immune cell in the placental villi. Furthermore, we observed that preterm placentas, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, had significantly increased CD163+ and CD68+ cells compared to term. Placental villi macrophages in spontaneous preterm versus spontaneous term analyses revealed a predominance of inflammatory genes and pathways with an involvement from trophoblast cells supporting inflammation, whereas stromal cells were primarily involved in extracellular matrix remodeling. Spontaneous vs non-spontaneous comparisons supported that even though both preterm birth groups are inflammatory, key inflammatory pathways such as TNF⍺ are enriched in spontaneous PTB, while in the term comparisons the pathways were either not related to inflammation or vastly different, with IL-2 being the top signaling pathway. In an ex vivo model of inflammation using placental explants, we found increases in pro-inflammatory mediators that coincided with our bioinformatic analyses. Primary cell experiments, using isolated cytotrophoblasts and Hofbauer cells, further supported that Hofbauer cells were a key contributor to pro-inflammatory mediator production.
CONCLUSIONS: This work showcases the cell-specific profile of placental macrophages and the inflammatory…

articles.title: Postoperative Hormonal Regimens and Two-Year Ovarian Endometrioma Recurrence Following Laparoscopic Cystectomy: A Weighted Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Lu W, Miao H, Liu M et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare 24-month imaging-defined ovarian endometrioma recurrence hazards across four postoperative hormonal regimens after laparoscopic cystectomy.
DESIGN: Single-center weighted retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Guangdong Women and Children Hospital.
PATIENTS: Women aged 18-45 years who underwent laparoscopic cystectomy for ovarian endometrioma from August 2015 to August 2023 with documented 6-month prescription coverage for one regimen.
INTERVENTIONS: Combined oral contraceptives (COC), gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists (GnRH-a), dienogest, or dydrogesterone initiated within 1 month without switching or sequential therapy.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Imaging-defined recurrence was a new endometrioma-compatible cyst >2 cm on at least two follow-up ultrasound examinations or confirmed by repeat surgery or pathology. Among 1121 women, 160 (14.3%) experienced recurrence within 24 months. Compared with COC, GnRH-a (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.405; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.253-0.649) and dienogest (adjusted HR, 0.417; 95% CI, 0.251-0.690) were associated with lower recurrence hazards. The dydrogesterone estimate had a wider 95% CI (adjusted HR, 0.504; 95% CI, 0.265-0.958). Higher baseline cancer antigen 125 (CA-125; adjusted HR per 1 U/mL, 1.002; 95% CI, 1.001-1.004) and deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE; adjusted HR, 2.358; 95% CI, 1.593-3.490) were associated with greater recurrence hazards.
CONCLUSION: Among women with documented 6-month prescription coverage, GnRH-a and dienogest were associated with lower 24-month hazards of imaging-defined ovarian endometrioma recurrence than COC. The dydrogesterone estimate was below 1 but less consistent across sensitivity analyses. These associations should not be extrapolated to overall endometriosis control or long-term pain outcomes.

articles.title: Video-Based Coaching in Essentials in Minimally Invasive Gynecologic Surgery (EMIGS): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Nolan W, Parikh S, Barbaresso R et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To determine the effect of video-based coaching on skill acquisition for Essentials in Minimally Invasive Gynecologic Surgery (EMIGS).
DESIGN: Single-site randomized controlled trial.
SETTING: Academic institution.
PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS: Obstetrics and Gynecology residents (PGY1-PGY4) and medical students (MS3-MS4).
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to a control cohort without video-based coaching or an intervention cohort with video-based coaching, where participants' surgical video was critiqued and the participant was given individualized strategies to improve performance. All participants underwent a baseline evaluation performing EMIGS tasks, followed by repeat testing after one month.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: After randomization, there were no significant demographic differences between cohorts with respect to level of training, prior laparoscopic experience, or days between completion of initial and final tasks. Baseline laparoscopic performance did not differ between cohorts. After the intervention, participants in the coaching cohort improved their time to complete the running suture task (Task 5) by a median of 250 seconds, compared with a 60-second improvement in the control cohort (p = 0.011). Medical students experienced a large effect, with a 361-second improvement in Task 5 performance compared with 80 seconds in controls (p = 0.032). Residents with coaching improved by 196 seconds compared with 60 seconds in resident controls (p = 0.083).
CONCLUSION: Video-based coaching improved EMIGS Task 5 acquisition. EMIGS curricula within residency programs may benefit from incorporating video-based coaching to improve task acquisition.

articles.title: Gender-stratified transmission model for multi-type HPV with multivalent vaccines: PINN calibration and optimal vaccination strategies for China.
articles.authors: Song M, Zhang K, Liu C et al.
articles.abstract: The transmission and prevention of human papillomavirus (HPV) require a rigorous mathematical framework reflecting multivalent vaccines and gender heterogeneous dynamics. This study establishes a gender-stratified multivalent HPV transmission model, including three core viral type groups and three vaccine valencies (bivalent, quadrivalent, nonavalent). To estimate complex time-varying epidemiological parameters, an MLP-based Physics-Informed Neural Network (MLP-PINN) is selected based on ablation experiments. By embedding governing ordinary differential equations as physical constraints in the loss function, this deep learning architecture is used for model calibration using Chinese demographic and cervical cancer prevalence data from 2010 to 2023. Theoretically, we rigorously prove the model's well-posedness, derive the basic reproduction number, and analyze the stability of the disease-free equilibrium and uniform persistence of the system. Numerical simulations confirm that vaccination reduces female infection burden and provides indirect protection to males. Using Pontryagin's Maximum Principle, we formulate an optimal control problem to evaluate multi-vaccine allocation strategies. The optimal control results show that the nonavalent vaccine plays a central role in protection across the three modeled HPV groups: the nonavalent-only strategy achieves the greatest disease burden reduction, whereas the bivalent-nonavalent combination provides a favorable balance between the two model-derived indicators under the assumptions of the present model.

articles.title: RRM2 Suppresses Ferroptosis via the MAPK-ERK1/2 Axis to Promote Uterine Leiomyosarcoma Progression.
articles.authors: Chen H, Lu R, Pan S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: 1. Employ bioinformatics and clinical sample analysis to determine the expression level of ribonucleotide reductase subunit M2 (RRM2) in uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) tissues. 2. Explore the impact of RRM2 on the biological behavior of uLMS cells. 3. Investigate the mechanism by which RRM2 contributes to uLMS progression.
METHODS: 1. Bioinformatics analysis of RRM2 expression in uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) using public databases. 2. Collect fresh clinical specimens of uLMS and normal uterine smooth muscle tissues, and culture uLMS cell lines. Detect the relative expression levels of RRM2 by RT-qPCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Examine the subcellular localization of RRM2 by immunofluorescence staining. 3. Establish RRM2 knockdown and overexpression uLMS cell lines using small interfering RNA (siRNA) and overexpression plasmids, respectively. Evaluate the effects of RRM2 on the biological behaviors of uLMS cells through CCK-8 assay, EdU incorporation assay, Transwell migration/invasion assay, flow cytometry, and tube formation assay. 4. Identify potential downstream signaling pathways regulated by RRM2 through transcriptome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis, followed by experimental validation. 5. Design rescue experiments to further verify whether RRM2 promotes uLMS progression by regulating the MAPK-ERK1/2 axis to inhibit ferroptosis. 6. Establish stable RRM2 knockdown uLMS cell lines and construct subcutaneous xenograft tumor models in nude mice to evaluate the effects of RRM2 knockdown, ERK inhibitors, and ferroptosis inhibitors on tumor growth in vivo. Detect the expression of Ki67, p-ERK, and GPX4 in tumor tissues by Western blot and IHC.
RESULTS: 1. Bioinformatics analysis using the GEPIA database revealed that RRM2 expression was significantly upregulated in uterine sarcoma. 2. RT-qPCR, Western blot, and IHC experiments demonstrated that RRM2 expression was markedly elevated in both uLMS tissues and cell lines compared to normal controls. 3. Cellular functional assays indicated that RRM2 knockdown significantly suppressed cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and angiogenic capabilities while promoting apoptosis, whereas RRM2 overexpression enhanced the malignant phenotype of uLMS cells. 4. KEGG and GSEA analyses of transcriptome sequencing data suggested that RRM2 may promote uLMS progression by inhibiting ferroptosis through the MAPK-ERK1/2 axis, which was further validated by Western blot experiments. 5.…

articles.title: Clinical readiness of first-trimester gestational diabetes prediction: From risk score to care pathway.
articles.authors: Mihoci EC, Socolov D, Socolov RV et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess whether first-trimester gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) prediction can improve clinical decisions, rather than merely predict a later abnormal glucose test.
METHODS: We critically reviewed targeted PubMed searches, independent validations, prospective implementation studies, randomized trials and guidelines. Searches were non-systematic and selection limitations are reported.
RESULTS: Routine clinical and glycemic predictors are feasible, but transportability, calibration, and strategy-level benefit are not established consistently. RESPECT 2 demonstrated implementation feasibility; a trial of nutrition support in 519 model-selected women did not significantly reduce GDM. TOBOGM investigated treatment after early biochemical diagnosis, not care guided by a risk score. Direct trials of the complete prediction-guided strategy remain limited.
CONCLUSION: First-trimester scores should not replace recommended diagnostic testing. Clinical adoption requires local validation, a prespecified beneficial action, evaluation of costs and harms, and comparative trials measuring maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Adnexal Torsion: A Case Report of Organ Loss and Clinical Overview of a Time-Sensitive Gynecologic Emergency.
articles.authors: Leonard CD, Anderson S
articles.abstract: Adnexal torsion is a time-sensitive gynecologic emergency requiring rapid surgical intervention to prevent organ loss. This manuscript presents an evidence-based overview of the condition and contextualizes a case of delayed diagnosis in a 20-year-old cisgender woman. The patient presented with acute abdominal pain and a large ovarian cyst with normal Doppler flow. Despite specialist consultation, torsion was not recognized until hospital day 5. Absent blood flow on repeated Doppler prompted emergency laparoscopy, which revealed complete right adnexal necrosis requiring salpingo-oophorectomy. A literature synthesis revealed that normal imaging often provides false reassurance and that timely surgical exploration guided by clinical suspicion achieves high organ salvage rates. The case demonstrates that clinical suspicion must guide surgical decision-making because imaging cannot reliably exclude torsion. Improved awareness of the variable presentations of torsion and lower thresholds for diagnostic laparoscopy are essential to prevent organ loss and preserve full reproductive function. Accepted October 13, 2026. Published online XXX.

articles.title: Bridging Evidence and Practice: Recent Advances in Hypothyroidism Management during Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.authors: Osman M, Sheikh Z, Ripa FA et al.
articles.abstract: Deficiency of thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxine and triiodothyronine, results in the clinical condition known as hypothyroidism, a prevalent endocrine disorder globally, particularly in women of childbearing age. Dynamic changes occur in thyroid function during pregnancy to provide adequate levels of thyroid hormones to the mother and the fetus. Hashimoto thyroiditis remains the most widespread reason for gestational hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and in mildly iodine deficient populations. Iodine plays a vital role in the synthesis and regulation of thyroid hormones; therefore, during pregnancy, iodine consumption must be increased by 50% to produce the required amount of maternal thyroid hormones and meet the increased demand of the developing fetus. Evidence-based studies have shown that even minor alteration in maternal thyroid function can cause pregnancy-related complications and adverse pregnancy outcomes (e.g. miscarriage, perinatal death, pre-eclampsia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, low birth weight and postpartum hemorrhage). Therefore, the timely assessment and appropriate management of gestational hypothyroidism is crucial to ensure optimal maternal and fetal outcomes. Levothyroxine remains the standard treatment for hypothyroidism, significantly reducing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with hypothyroidism. The present review provides an update on the diagnosis and management of hypothyroidism in pregnant women, highlighting the different types, causes, signs and symptoms of hypothyroidism, and the obstetric outcomes of each type of hypothyroidism along with the treatment strategy. Current key recommendations based on clinical evidence by health practitioners are also provided to assist in planning and choosing the individualized treatment regimen for patients with hypothyroidism before and during pregnancy.

articles.title: Brain health in children born extremely preterm: a multidimensional perspective.
articles.authors: Padilla N, Nivins S, Kvanta H et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational age and developmental stage of the brain at birth are major determinants of child health, and long-term consequences of preterm birth and altered brain maturation are inadequately understood simply through brain injury, survival rates, or diagnostic labels. In this Review, we conceptualise brain health in children born extremely preterm (before 28 weeks' gestation) as a developmental condition shaped by maturational timing, biological vulnerability, neonatal intensive care exposure, sensory and relational experiences, family circumstances, and social environments. We integrate evidence from research on early brain development and consciousness, long-term multidomain neurodevelopmental outcomes, neonatal intensive care practice, relational caregiving, early developmental interventions, and ethical, psychological, and social dimensions of care. Across these domains, extremely preterm birth emerges not as a single event but as a neuroplastic system that adapts to biological and environmental risks and protective factors that shape neurodevelopmental resilience and vulnerabilities and establish developmental trajectories. We argue that care for the infant born extremely preterm is optimised through a brain-health framework where care becomes a longitudinal, ethical process that integrates family support, minimises harmful exposures, promotes adaptive development, and fosters participation, wellbeing, and quality of life.

articles.title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Toumpe I, Masid M, Hatzimanikatis V et al.
articles.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a subset of these candidates. All 28 emerged directly from the mechanistic model structure and multi-omics constraints, with no calibration to known drug targets or cancer-dependency data. Simulations of thymidylate synthase, hexokinase, and triokinase inhibition predicted target- and physiology-specific changes in pathway use, energy metabolism, and a shared ceramide-linked stress response. Mapping predicted enzyme-activity shifts to BRCA1-associated transcription factors suggested regulatory routes underlying differences between the two states. These ensembles provide a reusable framework for time-resolved, mechanistic hypothesis generation across cancers and other diseases. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

articles.title: The promise and limitations of cell-free DNA fragmentomics for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance.
articles.authors: Parikh ND, Singal AG
articles.abstract: A phase 2 cell-free DNA fragmentomics signature biomarker validation study in two populations from Guatemala and Romania showed promising performance for early-stage HCC detection when combined with serum alpha-fetoprotein and demographic factors.1 In this Viewpoint, we critically appraise the study and contextualize the findings in the current early detection HCC biomarker landscape.

articles.title: Reproductive burden in women with central hypersomnolence disorders: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.authors: Houziaux H, Gauriau C, Labonne A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Women with narcolepsy or idiopathic hypersomnia face specific challenges in their reproductive lives, due to, (1) the potential teratogenic effect of several commonly prescribed therapies, (2) the reduced efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives with some agents, and (3) treatment discontinuation during pregnancy, which often impairs daily functioning. This study aims at evaluating those challenges.
METHODS: An 11-item survey was distributed to 91 women diagnosed with narcolepsy or idiopathic hypersomnia in one reference center. The first section covered diagnosis, treatments, and contraception. A second section addressed pregnancy history and outcomes. Finally, the patients were asked to assess the impact of their disorder on domains related to reproductive health and womanhood.
RESULTS: Responses from 91 women diagnosed with narcolepsy type 1, narcolepsy type 2 or idiopathic hypersomnia were analyzed. 84,6% of patients received an enzyme-inducing treatment as first-line therapy, although most (68.1%) were already using oral hormonal contraception at treatment initiation. Consequently, 42 (45.1%) changed their contraceptive method. 22 (24.2%) reported a pregnancy after diagnosis and provided pregnancy-related outcomes. Communication with primary care professionals was rated as difficult, with many respondents reporting challenges obtaining clear guidance. On a scale from 0 to 10, the negative effect of the disease on women-specific aspects of their life was 5.56/10.
CONCLUSION: Narcolepsy and idiopathic hypersomnia are rare diseases that are usually under-recognized among non-specialists. Women report unmet needs regarding their condition and its treatment. Structured therapeutic education programs should be implemented to support decision-making around medications, contraception, pregnancy planning, and perinatal care.

articles.title: Evaluation of semaglutide in an ex vivo human placental perfusion model to estimate maternal-fetal transfer.
articles.authors: Chan E, Zabek M, Balluku A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, is increasingly used in females of reproductive age for glycemic control and weight management, with emerging evidence suggesting benefits on fertility and obstetrical outcomes. However, pregnancy safety data remain limited, and current guidance advises discontinuation before conception due to uncertain fetal exposure risk. Since many pregnancies are unplanned, inadvertent exposures are inevitable-further data is needed to inform clinical counselling and risk assessment. This study aims to determine whether semaglutide crosses the human placenta using an ex vivo dual-perfused cotyledon model.
METHODS: Transplacental transfer of semaglutide was assessed at clinically relevant (222 ng/mL, n = 4) or at ten-fold higher (2220 ng/mL, n = 4) concentrations. Each perfusion included a 1-h control period followed by a 3-h experimental period with drug exposure. Perfusates samples were collected over time to measure semaglutide concentrations and quality control markers. Semaglutide was quantified via a validated enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kit. Paired Student's t-tests were used, with significance defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Placental viability was maintained throughout, supported by stable metabolic parameters and appropriate antipyrine transfer, confirming intact and functional cotyledons. Maternal semaglutide concentrations remained stable over the 180-min perfusion period in both conditions, with no significant time-dependent changes (p > 0.05). Fetal perfusate concentrations were all below the lower limit of quantification.
DISCUSSION: Semaglutide demonstrated minimal-to-no detectable transfer across the term human placenta, even at supratherapeutic concentrations. These findings suggest limited placental passage during term gestation and offer guidance for decision making regarding semaglutide use during pregnancy.

articles.title: Systemic influences on blood-brain barrier integrity - narrative review of insights from MRI.
articles.authors: Verstappen D, de Jong JJA, Staals J et al.
articles.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is vital for protecting the vulnerable neuronal microenvironment from harmful biomolecules. MRI is increasingly used to assess in vivo BBB integrity in various brain disorders. Thus far, extracerebral conditions that perturb the BBB via systemic pathways have received little attention. This narrative review synthesizes the available evidence for these extracerebral and systemic effects, focusing on human in vivo MRI measurements of BBB permeability. The most direct reproducible human evidence of BBB impairment was found in hypertension. Moderate evidence supports BBB involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus and long COVID. There is additionally suggestive evidence for an association with Sjögren's syndrome, HIV infection, diabetes, cardiac surgery (transient), and after pre-eclampsia. Evidence for BBB disruption is inconclusive for conditions like obstructive sleep apnea, sepsis, hyperlipidemia, obesity, alcohol abuse, and for smoking. In general, systemic inflammation emerges as a common mechanistic pathway that leads to BBB disruption and represents a target with therapeutic potential. Inflammation is amplified by a vicious cycle in which endothelial dysfunction and oxidative/metabolic stress further reinforce inflammatory signaling. Angiogenic factors also likely contribute in a subset of conditions. Heterogeneity in imaging and modeling methods and probed BBB transport pathways limits cross-study comparability. Furthermore, inherent confounding factors limit the power to detect subtle effects. Large-scale DCE-MRI studies are needed to be able to robustly map the influence of various extracerebral conditions on BBB integrity.

articles.title: HPV16 A4 sublineage and its characteristic E6/E7/E2/LCR polymorphisms is associated with LSIL persistence in eastern Chinese women.
articles.authors: Sun Y, Zhang L, Wang L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) sublineages exhibit differential oncogenic risks, but their effects on the prognosis of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) remain unclear. This study investigated the association between HPV16 sublineages and their characteristic single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and the outcomes of LSIL among eastern Chinese women.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: A total of 110 patients of LSIL with HPV16-positive colposcopy biopsy were enrolled and they have been followed up every six months for 2 years. Variant types were determined by bidirectional sequencing of HPV16 DNA E2, E6, E7, LCR and L1 from cervical exfoliated cells.
RESULTS: Among 110 HPV16-positive patients with LSIL, phylogenetic analysis identified four sublineages, including A1 (5.5%), A2 (10.0%), A3 (14.5%), and A4 (70.0%). A characteristic set of 15 SNPs across the E6, E7, E2, and locus control region (LCR) regions was identified in 77.9% (60/77) of A4 isolates. Compared with the combination of A1, A2, and A3 sublineages, the A4 sublineage exhibited a higher persistence rate (28.57% vs. 12.12%) and a lower regression rate (61.04% vs. 84.85%) (p = 0.016). After adjusting for age, the A4 sublineage was significantly associated with LSIL persistence (OR = 4.04, 95% CI = 1.50-10.91, p = 0.006). In silico, A4 LCR gained an activator protein 1 (AP-1)-binding site spanning 7170-7178.
CONCLUSIONS: The HPV16 A4 sublineage, defined by a characteristic 15-SNP signature and a gained AP-1 binding site in the LCR, represents the predominant high-risk variant in Eastern Chinese women with LSIL. Its strong association with lesion persistence (OR = 4.04) supports its utility as a clinically accessible molecular marker for early triage of LSIL patients, potentially reducing unnecessary interventions and enabling personalized surveillance.

articles.title: Exploratory biomarker analysis of ribociclib plus letrozole in recurrent low-grade serous carcinoma: A GOG-3026 correlative study.
articles.authors: Wong KK, Deng W, Tsang YTM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ribociclib plus letrozole demonstrated meaningful activity in recurrent low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSOC) in the phase II GOG-3026 trial. However, biomarkers associated with CDK4/6 inhibitor response remain undefined. We conducted an exploratory translational analysis to identify molecular and immune biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Archival FFPE tumors from 24 GOG-3026 patients were analyzed. Immunohistochemistry assessed ER, PR, p16, phosphorylated RB (pRB), and Ki-67. Whole-exome sequencing (n = 14) and RNA sequencing (n = 12) evaluated genomic alterations and immune transcriptional profiles. Associations between biomarkers and objective response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival were evaluated using 2-sided tests at a 5% significance level, without multiple testing adjustment.
RESULTS: Among 24 patients, ORR was 37.5% and CBR was 87.5%. Lower Ki-67 expression was significantly associated with CBR (r = -0.437, p = 0.0326). Higher p16 expression showed a trend toward shorter PFS (Cox proportional hazard regression: HR 2.8, 95% CI 0.96-9.20; Monte Carlo permutation log-rank test: p = 0.0633). ER, PR, pRB expression and MAPK pathway alterations were not associated with response or survival. The most common genomic alterations involved BRAF, KRAS, NRAS and FANCD2. RNA sequencing identified three immune phenotypes: immune-hot, intermediate, and immune-cold. No partial responders had an immune-hot phenotype, while four of five partial responders clustered in the intermediate group.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower Ki-67 expression may predict clinical benefit from ribociclib plus letrozole, while higher p16 expression may be associated with shorter PFS. Distinct immune phenotypes may also influence response, supporting prospective validation of proliferation-, cell-cycle-, and immune-based biomarkers to refine patient selection for CDK4/6-directed therapy in LGSOC.

articles.title: "Turn that down a few notches": A qualitative analysis of uncertainty and psychosocial burden among non-BRCA previvors.
articles.authors: Chess I, Holtzman S, Leschly J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Risk reducing decisions impact previvors' identity, family experiences, and relationships. These decisions are especially challenging for non-BRCA previvors, who face vague guidelines and limited evidence. This qualitative study explored non-BRCA previvors' attitudes toward family planning, relationships, and the burden of previvor status.
METHODS: Previvors with non-BRCA mutations (Lynch-related, PALB2, RAD51C, BRIP1, CHEK2) were recruited from an urban gynecologic oncology clinic. We conducted semi-structured telephone interviews which were transcribed verbatim. Two investigators independently coded a subset of interviews, resolved discrepancies with a moderator blinded to study background, and then refined the codebook and applied across all transcripts to identify themes.
RESULTS: Twenty-one previvors completed interviews (median age 39). Three overarching themes emerged: impact of previvor status on mental health, on personal identity, and impact of medical experience on decision making. Those considering future fertility worried about assisted reproductive technology (ART) cost and time pressure from risk reduction timelines; those not pursuing fertility worried about early menopause and mutation transmission to children. Previvor status impacted romantic relationships differently, with some describing strains caused by altered family planning and cancer prevention timelines, while others feeling no impact. Previvors emphasized the physician-patient relationship and shared decision-making. Many expressed frustrations regarding access to reliable data amid unclear guidelines. The lower penetrance of the non-BRCA did not lessen the psychosocial burden of previvor status in our cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Family planning, relationships, and previvor burden are central concerns for previvors. Ambiguity surrounding non-BRCA variants emerged as an independent source of distress shaping daily lives. Physicians can better partner with previvors by acknowledging these challenges to align medical and personal goals.

articles.title: Re-contextualizing embryo transfer: a multidimensional view of its value in IVF.
articles.authors: Vaiarelli A, Ruffa A, Cozzolino M et al.
articles.abstract: The value of embryo transfer per se in contemporary ART should be appraised based on its contribution to a live birth across multiple domains rather than as an independent end-point. Current advancements permit earlier identification of developmentally incompetent or aneuploid embryos, increasing cycle cancellations yet preserving scarce reproductive time, reducing futile transfers and potentially shortening the overall time to live birth when couples are properly counselled and supported throughout their journey. The worth of an embryo transfer is therefore relative: it depends on embryo competence, the couple's clinical and personal circumstances and the treatment context. When selection tools materially raise the probability of per‑embryo transfer live birth, performing an embryo transfer for its own sake when it is probably futile becomes questionable. Economically, strategies that reduce the number of futile transfers, despite higher per‑cycle expenses, can improve cumulative cost‑effectiveness; and psychologically, avoiding repeated futile transfers may limit cumulative emotional harm and reduce treatment discontinuation, also making patients more aware of treatment outcome. In poor‑prognosis individuals, prioritizing competence‑driven decisions and accepting early cancellation as a deliberate, time‑preserving strategy can maximize the couple's overall chance of success. The act of embryo transfer (and its value) should serve the pursuit of an optimal outcome and not be treated as an outcome itself.

articles.title: Phenotype-specific cardiometabolic risk in PMOS: an ovarian-endocrine perspective on reproductive and long-term health.
articles.authors: Kawuribi V, Adu-Amankwaah J, Yalley SK
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is the most common endocrine disorder in women of reproductive age, and a cause of ovulatory dysfunction, hyperandrogenism and infertility. It is a heterogeneous condition associated with insulin resistance, dysglycaemia, dyslipidaemia, metabolic syndrome, inflammation and vascular dysfunction. The Rotterdam criteria classify PMOS into four phenotypes based on hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Evidence suggests that these phenotypes differ in endocrine characteristics and cardiometabolic risk. Hyperandrogenic phenotypes, particularly phenotypes A and B, generally exhibit greater insulin resistance, visceral adiposity, atherogenic dyslipidaemia, chronic low-grade inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, whereas phenotype D typically has a milder, yet relevant, metabolic profile. This narrative review summarizes evidence on phenotype-specific cardiometabolic risk, and explores how ovarian-endocrine disturbances may contribute to metabolic and vascular dysfunction. This review also discusses implications for individualized assessment, reproductive counselling, and long-term follow-up. However, most evidence supporting a phenotype-specific risk gradient comes from cross-sectional studies using surrogate markers, while longitudinal data on cardiovascular events remain limited. Therefore, a phenotype-informed ovarian-endocrine framework may improve personalized care but should be considered hypothesis-generating until validated in prospective studies. Greater standardization of phenotype definitions and outcome measures is needed to strengthen future evidence and clinical translation.

articles.title: Design, synthesis, and evaluation of covalent HER2-targeting tracers with increased tumor uptake and prolonged retention for cancer theranostics.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Zhang X, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a classic theranostic target for breast and ovarian cancer. However, existing HER2-targeting tracers still exhibit suboptimal tumor uptake and retention time, limiting their PET imaging application. To address these limitations, we designed a series of irreversible covalent HER2-targeting ligands by incorporating different covalent linkers (-FSA-, -FSY-, -FSK-) into the DH6 peptide. NOTA-FSK-DH6 was selected from the virtual screening based on molecular docking, as it exhibited the most favorable binding mode to HER2 protein. MD simulations further confirmed that this ligand formed a stable complex with HER2 protein. The ligand was radiolabeled with 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu for systematic evaluation. In SKOV-3 and SKBR-3 xenograft-bearing mice, [18F]AlF-FSK-DH6 showed high tumor uptake and prolonged retention time, with superior specificity over [18F]FDG. [177Lu]Lu-FSK-DH6 also exhibited sustained tumor uptake over 24 h. These results indicate that NOTA-FSK-DH6 is a promising covalent theranostic candidate for HER2-positive cancers.

articles.title: Effects of sustained moderate to vigorous physical activity on late-life cognitive function: A target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Tang L, Qiu C, Liu F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia affects over 50 million people globally, with projections reaching 170 million by 2050. Nonpharmacological strategies targeting modifiable risk factors, particularly physical inactivity, offer scalable prevention. However, causal inference from observational studies remains limited, and randomized trials of long-term physical activity on cognitive outcomes are infeasible.
METHODS: We emulated a target trial using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (2011-2020). Participants aged ≥45 years without cognitive impairment at baseline were evaluated under four strategies based on the World Health Organization's recommendations regarding sustained moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA), classified in terms of metabolic equivalents (MET): no intervention, below (<7.5 MET-hours/week), meeting (7.5-15), and exceeding (>15)the recommendations. Cognitive outcomes over 9 years were estimated using the parametric g-formula, adjusting for baseline and time-varying confounders, with 50,000 Monte Carlo simulations and 500 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: Among 3307 participants, the >15 MET-hours/week strategy was associated with the highest global cognitive z-score (mean difference 0.043, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.009-0.077), followed by 7.5-15 MET-hours/week (mean difference 0.017, 95% CI 0.004-0.031), relative to no intervention. The <7.5 MET-hours/week strategy showed lower cognitive scores (mean difference - 0.009, 95% CI -0.016--0.002). Memory showed the strongest associations, while executive function was null. Estimated MVPA associations were directionally similar across age, sex, and BMI subgroups.
CONCLUSION: Sustained MVPA at or above the World Health Organization's recommended threshold was associated with higher cognitive scores over 9 years, with stronger associations at higher activity volumes.

articles.title: Knowledge and awareness of their condition among women with premature ovarian insufficiency: Exploring the link between health literacy and clinical behavior.
articles.authors: Ferreira SR, Silva PHRE, Ferreira PVE et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) significantly impacts women's health, yet gaps in patient health literacy often hinder optimal management. This study assessed knowledge, risk awareness, and treatment adherence among women with POI.
METHODS: A descriptive analytical study was conducted with a representative cohort of 101 women diagnosed with POI at a specialized tertiary center. Data were collected via structured questionnaires regarding symptoms, perceived risks, and therapy.
RESULTS: Participants (mean age 39.46 ± 8.44 years) reported hot flashes, night sweats, fatigue, lack of energy and vaginal dryness as primary symptoms. While 80% utilized hormone replacement therapy, symptoms such as fatigue, low energy, and lack of focus frequently persisted despite treatment. Bone loss and sexual dysfunction were the most recognized risks. Statistical analysis showed that higher-quality physician guidance (p = 0.001) correlated with greater self-reported disease knowledge, heightened awareness of health risks (p = 0.049), and significantly better treatment adherence (p = 0.032).
CONCLUSION: Better health literacy and disease understanding among women with POI are significantly associated with improved treatment adherence and proactive risk mitigation. Although hormone therapy mitigates vasomotor symptoms, the persistence of non-specific complaints requires a nuanced clinical approach. The clinician's role is pivotal in bridging information gaps; therefore, patient education must be integrated into therapeutic protocols to ensure improved clinical outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Rapid genotyping of FecB mutation in sheep using CRISPR-Cas12a orthology-assisted assay.
articles.authors: Li S, Shi S, Yang J et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate genotyping of the Fecundity Booroola (FecB) gene, a key determinant of ovine fecundity, is essential for effective breeding programs. However, current methods are largely constrained by their reliance on specialized equipment and high operational costs, which collectively limit their applicability for large-scale, on-site genetic screening. To address these challenges, we systematically evaluated five Cas12a orthologs and identified Gs12-19 as the optimal candidate. Based on this, we developed a novel detection platform integrating the CRISPR-Gs12-19 system with allele-specific amplification and fluorescence-based signal readout, which enables discrimination between homozygous wild-type sheep (AA) and FecB mutation carriers (AG or GG, collectively designated as RG). Coupled with a portable blue-light excitation device and a custom-designed Red Channel Quantification (RedQ) analytical program, the platform was field-tested on 153 randomly selected samples from a core crossbred sheep population. The method achieved 98% accuracy in mutation-carrier classification when benchmarked against Sanger sequencing. Collectively, this study offers a rapid, visually interpretable, and field-deployable platform for FecB mutation-carrier screening with high sensitivity and specificity, providing a practical solution to accelerate marker-assisted selection in sheep breeding.

articles.title: Management of presacral hemorrhage during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy using an autologous round ligament patch: a video case report.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Sepulveda CS, Ramirez IR, Rojas RG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Presacral hemorrhage during laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy is an uncommon but potentially serious complication that can be difficult to control using standard techniques. Autologous tissue may serve as a readily available adjunct in challenging intraoperative bleeding scenarios.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 66-year-old woman with symptomatic stage III pelvic organ prolapse underwent laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy. During suture placement at the sacral promontory, brisk presacral bleeding occurred that was not adequately controlled with bipolar coagulation and compression. A small fragment of the round ligament was harvested laparoscopically and applied directly over the bleeding site. Bipolar energy was delivered through the tissue, resulting in cessation of bleeding. The procedure was completed without conversion, transfusion, or use of commercial hemostatic agents. Postoperative recovery was uncomplicated, and no recurrent bleeding or prolapse was observed at 6-month follow-up.
CONCLUSION: The use of an autologous round ligament fragment as a tissue interface for bipolar coagulation may represent a feasible adjunct for controlling difficult presacral bleeding during minimally invasive pelvic surgery. This approach is immediately available and cost-neutral; however, its mechanism and generalizability remain uncertain. Further experience is needed to define its role relative to established hemostatic techniques.

articles.title: Health Professionals' Preferences for Genetic Prenatal Testing-An International Discrete Choice Experiment Survey.
articles.authors: Malmgren CI, Grauman Å, Johansson JV et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study explored healthcare professionals' preferences regarding prenatal genomic testing following the detection of a foetal anomaly and their attitudes towards uncertain results.
METHOD: HCPs involved in genetic prenatal diagnostics were asked to fill in a cross-sectional survey-based study using a discrete choice experiment to assess their preferences for prenatal genomic testing and attitudes towards uncertain results.
RESULTS: When ranking the different attributes, diagnostic yield was seen as the most important factor, followed by test safety, waiting time, and the professional responsible for communicating results. Regarding the DCE, respondents favoured tests with a higher probability of obtaining results and shorter turnaround times. The findings also revealed a consistent pattern of caution towards uncertainty, particularly among clinical geneticists compared to gynaecologists who preferred rapid return of test results. Clinical geneticists also assigned greater and almost equal importance to who was communicating the results, time to result, and the reporting of uncertain findings. In addition, respondents chose neither test option in approximately one third of choice tasks, suggesting that healthcare professionals were willing to forgo testing altogether when they perceived the balance between benefits and potential harms was unfavourable.
CONCLUSION: The cautious approach observed among healthcare professionals contrasts with findings from studies of prospective parents. Women generally preferred receiving as much information as possible from prenatal testing, including uncertain findings and secondary findings.

articles.title: The persistent multidomain health effects of the early-life exposome.
articles.authors: Anguita Ruiz A, Amine I, Luo C et al.
articles.abstract: The environments experienced early in life can shape health across multiple body systems, yet most research on exposome health effects has focused on isolated exposure windows and health outcomes, limiting understanding of their combined and enduring effects. Leveraging the Human Early Life Exposome (HELIX) European cohort-the largest exposome dataset from the general pediatric population-we studied 586 mother-child pairs with nearly 200 prenatal and childhood exposures, including air pollutants, chemicals, lifestyle (diet, physical activity, and toxic habits), and neighborhood outdoors factors. Associations between these exposures and 11 outcomes across mental health, cardiometabolic, respiratory, and allergic domains, assessed in both childhood (6 to 11 years) and adolescence (12 to 18 years) were sought using an outcome-wide exposure-wide analysis. We identified a set of "master regulator" exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence. By providing an atlas of exposome-health associations across developmental stages-available as an open-access interactive resource-this work pinpoints critical early-life risks and offers a platform to guide prevention and policy.

articles.title: Trends and causes of maternal mortality in Taiyuan, China, 2016-2024: A population-based observational study.
articles.authors: Wang F, Yang H
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016-2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR.
METHODS: We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports. MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Analyses were stratified by geographic region, cause of death, and place of death; the study period was divided into three phases (2016-2018, 2019-2021, 2022-2024) for subgroup analysis.
RESULTS: Between 2016 and 2024, Taiyuan recorded 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, yielding an overall MMR of 7.76 per 100,000 live births (95% CI 5.35 to 10.92). Urban MMR declined significantly (P < 0.0001), whereas rural MMR showed no significant temporal change (P = 0.313) and remained higher than urban levels (9.57 vs 7.58 per 100,000). Indirect obstetric causes accounted for 66.7% of maternal deaths, compared with 33.3% for direct causes, with no significant temporal trends in either category. Women aged 30-39 years accounted for 63.6% of maternal deaths, and 83.9% of deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals.
CONCLUSION: Taiyuan has maintained a low MMR through sustained investment in maternal healthcare; however, substantial urban-rural disparities remain. Indirect obstetric causes predominated among maternal deaths, suggesting a transition in the spectrum of maternal causes of death. Continued efforts to strengthen rural maternal health services and promote equitable, life-course-oriented maternal care are essential to further reduce preventable maternal deaths.

articles.title: Tissue factor-specific sdAb radiotracers for molecular imaging in solid tumors.
articles.authors: Dumas LS, De Groof TWM, Raes F et al.
articles.abstract: Tissue factor (TF) expression has been associated with tumor aggressiveness and poor prognosis in several cancers. With the recent FDA approval of an antibody-drug-conjugate targeting TF, tisotumab vedotin for recurrent metastatic cervical cancer, companion diagnostic tools capable of capturing tumor heterogeneity are increasingly critical. In this study, we developed and characterized single domain antibody (sdAb)-based radiotracers to non-invasively visualize tumors expressing either murine (m) or human (h) TF protein. SdAbs targeting hTF and mTF were obtained from an immune llama library. Seven candidates targeting each species' orthologue were selected, characterized in vitro and radiolabeled with 99mTc for in vivo screening in athymic nude mice bearing both mTF and hTF positive tumors. Lead anti-hTF sdAb was radiolabeled with 68Ga for PET imaging. In vitro, all sdAbs exhibited excellent affinities for their respective targets, reaching the picomolar range. When radiolabeled with 99mTc, the lead compounds showed strong uptake and specific binding in TF-positive tumors as confirmed by SPECT imaging. The lead sdAb 64B4 targeting hTF protein, demonstrated an uptake of 8.07±1.02% IA/g in BxPC-3 tumors and a tumor-to-blood ratio of 26.06±4.36. The best candidate for targeting mTF protein, sdAb 66A12, displayed an uptake of 3.30±0.22% IA/g in mTF positive tumors and a tumor-to-blood ratio of 10.70±2.83. Off-tumor uptake was detected in several organs, with unexpectedly the highest levels detected in brown adipose tissue, consistent with mTF protein expression levels determined by ELISA. We successfully developed and validated sdAb-based radiotracers targeting either mTF or hTF, enabling the noninvasive visualization of TF-expressing tumors.

articles.title: Validity and reliability analysis of the Korean version of the Partners in Health Scale for middle-aged women.
articles.authors: Lee H, Kim J
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Middle-aged women experience persistent and multifaceted health-related changes during the menopausal transition that require ongoing self-management. However, validated instruments for assessing self-management in this population are limited. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the validity and reliability of the Korean version of the Partners in Health Scale for middle-aged women (K-PIH-MW).
METHODS: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from 312 community-dwelling Korean women aged 45-64 years. Content validity was assessed by six experts. Construct validity was examined through confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), including factor-level convergent and discriminant validity. Convergent construct validity was also evaluated using theoretically related external measures. Internal consistency reliability was assessed using Cronbach's α, Spearman-Brown coefficients, and McDonald's ω, as appropriate.
RESULTS: The K-PIH-MW demonstrated good content validity (scale-level content validity index = .96). CFA supported the original four-factor structure, with acceptable model fit (comparative fit index = .97, Tucker-Lewis index = .96, root mean square error of approximation = .08, standardized root mean square residual = .03). Factor-level convergent and discriminant validity among the four domains were supported. Convergent construct validity was supported by significant positive correlations with self-care agency (r = .63, p < .001), physical health-related quality of life (r = .31, p < .001), and mental health-related quality of life (r = .40, p < .001). The overall internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = .92), with satisfactory domain-level reliability based on Spearman-Brown coefficients and McDonald's ω.
CONCLUSION: These findings support the validity and internal consistency of the K-PIH-MW as a multidimensional measure of self-management among middle-aged women. The instrument may be useful for assessing self-management across multiple domains and identifying areas that may require additional support in clinical and community settings.
