articles.title: Circulating inflammatory proteins mediate the causal relationship between blood alliin and cancer: A two-step, multivariable Mendelian randomization study.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Xiao S, Feng P et al.
articles.abstract: An association has been found between alliin and reduced risks of various cancers; however, evidence for these causal relationships remain limited. This study utilized Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to assess the potential causal relationships between circulating alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers. We selected instrumental variables from the latest and largest European genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets. First, we comprehensively assessed the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers through two-sample MR analysis. Subsequently, we repeated the validation of instrumental variables using cancer GWAS statistics from different studies and merged the results by meta-analysis. Two-step MR analysis was used to investigate whether 91 inflammatory proteins mediate the effect of alliin on the risk of cancer. Finally, multivariable MR analysis was conducted to determine the direct effects of alliin on the risk of cancer, with adjustment for potential mediators. Inverse variance weighted results were considered the primary observation outcome, and additional sensitivity analyses were conducted. Increased blood alliin levels were significantly causally associated with decreased risks of prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer, cervical cancer, lymphoma, and colorectal cancer, with the corresponding meta-analyses also showing significant associations. In the two-step MR analysis, chemokine ligand 23 (CCL23) and oncostatin M (OSM) as well as interleukin-12B (IL12B) were the key mediators of the inverse causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of prostate cancer as well as the risks of ovarian and colorectal cancers, respectively. STAM-binding protein was a key mediator of the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of lymphoma. The results of this study support that increased blood alliin levels can reduce the risks of multiple cancers, with circulating inflammatory proteins potentially mediating this association.

articles.title: Minimally invasive surgery improves surgical and analgesic outcomes in overweight or obese patients with borderline ovarian tumors: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Lee SM, Kim S
articles.abstract: This study aimed to compare surgical outcomes between minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and open surgery in overweight or obese patients with borderline ovarian tumor (BOT) and identify risk factors for additional analgesic use despite patient-controlled analgesia .We selected patients with a body mass index of 25 or more who underwent surgery for BOT at Korea University Anam Hospital from 2006 to 2023. Patients who underwent laparoscopic or robotic surgery were categorized into the MIS group, while those who underwent open surgery were categorized into the open surgery group. For statistical analysis, the Student t test, chi-square test, Fisher exact test, and logistic regression analysis were performed using SPSS. Of 128 patients, 90 were in the MIS group, and 38 were in the open group. Compared with the open surgery group, the MIS group had a shorter surgical time (P < .001), lower estimated blood loss (P < .001), a shorter hospital stay (P < .001), and a lower rate of additional analgesic use despite patient-controlled analgesia (P = .002). There was no significant difference in disease-free survival between the 2 groups. No deaths occurred during follow-up. MIS compared to open surgery was identified as a factor associated with significantly lower use of additional analgesics (adjusted odds ratio, 0.13; 95% confidence interval, 0.037-0.470; P = .002). In overweight or obese patients with BOT, MIS was associated with better surgical outcomes and a reduced need for additional analgesics during hospitalization compared with open surgery. These findings suggest that MIS may be a feasible surgical option for these patients.

articles.title: Construction of a nomogram for predicting pathological upgrading after LEEP in patients with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 based on colposcopic morphological features: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Chen L, Xie Y, Liu D et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) grade 1/2 diagnosed by colposcopy-directed biopsy may underestimate the final lesion grade found on excision. In patients who proceed to Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure (LEEP), postoperative pathology may show histopathological upgrading relative to the preoperative biopsy. Although HPV testing and ThinPrep Cytology Test (TCT) are standard screening tools, their differential value in this LEEP-selected CIN1/2 population remains unclear. This study aimed to identify factors associated with pathological upgrading after LEEP and to construct an internally validated nomogram based on colposcopic morphological features. We retrospectively analyzed 122 patients who underwent LEEP for clinical indications between 2020 and 2025 with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2. Pathological upgrading was defined as biopsy CIN1 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN2, or biopsy CIN2 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN3 (invasive carcinoma included). These 2 transitions were prespecified and are clinically distinct; event counts were, therefore, also reported by baseline biopsy grade. Multivariable logistic regression was used to develop a nomogram. Discrimination and calibration were assessed with ROC analysis and bootstrap internal validation; clinical utility was explored with decision curve analysis (DCA). Pathological upgrading occurred in 46/122 (37.7%) patients in this LEEP-selected cohort, including 4/15 (26.7%) with baseline CIN1 and 42/107 (39.3%) with baseline CIN2. In the multivariable model, Reid Colposcopic Index (OR = 1.41, P = .013) and number of involved quadrants (OR = 1.93, P = .018) were significantly associated with upgrading, whereas menopausal status (OR = 2.83, P = .059) and biopsy count (OR = 0.70, P = .068) did not reach conventional significance but were retained as candidate predictors. HPV genotype category and TCT were not significantly associated with upgrading. The nomogram showed apparent AUC 0.801 (95% CI 0.719-0.883) on internal evaluation; calibration and DCA supported exploratory clinical utility within this surgical cohort. In women with biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 who already had indications for LEEP, colposcopic morphological features (Reid score and lesion extent) were more informative than HPV/TCT for predicting histopathological upgrading after excision. The nomogram may assist risk stratification within this selected surgical population. An ROC-derived probability threshold of 43% is presented only as an…

articles.title: Disulfidptosis-related lncRNAs for establishing a new prognostic model of endometrial carcinoma and drug sensitivity prediction: A retrospective observational cohort study.
articles.authors: Cheng W, Zhang M, Jiang L et al.
articles.abstract: Disulfidptosis is a novel mode of regulated cell death, but the prognostic role of disulfidptosis-related lncRNAs (DRLs) in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) is unclear. Transcriptomic data from 552 UCEC tumor samples and 23 normal samples, together with clinical survival data, were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. DRLs were screened by correlation analysis, Cox regression, and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator. A prognostic model was constructed and validated. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, mutation profiling, and drug sensitivity analyses were performed. A total of 397 DRLs were identified, and a 7-lncRNA signature (AL078644.1, Z99572.1, LINC00645, AC092794.1, AC004596.1, CDKN2B-AS1, AC013486.1) was developed. Patients were stratified into high-risk (n=275) and low-risk (n=264) groups, with significantly poorer survival in the high-risk group (P < .001). The model achieved area under the curve values of 0.781 (1-year), 0.741 (3-year), and 0.706 (5-year), and remained an independent prognostic factor in multivariate analysis (P < .01).Immune profiling revealed P < .05 in CD4+ memory T cells, macrophages M1, and dendritic cells, alongside altered Type I IFN response, APC co-inhibition, and inflammation. Mutation analysis showed distinct distributions of PTEN and TP53 between groups. Enrichment analysis indicated pathways related to microtubule-based movement, extracellular matrix organization, Wnt signaling, and neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction. Drug sensitivity analysis identified 22 compounds with significantly higher sensitivity in the high-risk group. We established a 7-DRL signature that independently predicts UCEC prognosis, reveals immune and molecular heterogeneity, and suggests potential candidate compounds for precision management.

articles.title: Establishment of normal reference values for ultrasound measurements of fetal cerebellar vermis during mid-trimester: A prospective cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Zhou M, Lin Z, Zhou C
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop preliminary gestational age (GA)-specific reference ranges for ultrasonographic measurements of the fetal cerebellar vermis during mid-trimester at a single center. A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted at our hospital from March 2024 to December 2025. A total of 104 singleton pregnancies between 14 and 27 weeks of gestation were enrolled. The midsagittal plane of the posterior fossa was obtained using 2-dimensional transabdominal ultrasound. The anteroposterior diameter, craniocaudal diameter, vermian area, and brainstem-vermis (BV) angle were measured. Polynomial regression analysis and the generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape- lambda-mu-sigma method were applied to model the relationship between each parameter and GA and to construct percentile curves. The anteroposterior diameter, craniocaudal diameter, and vermian area demonstrated significant positive correlations with GA (all P < .001), with growth patterns best fitted by quadratic regression models (R2 = 0.961, 0.954, and 0.978, respectively). The BV angle remained stable throughout mid-trimester, with a mean of 1.67° ± 0.88°. Gestational age-specific percentile reference ranges (5th, 50th, and 95th) were established for all dimensional parameters. Intra-observer and inter-observer intraclass correlation coefficients exceeded 0.90 for all measurements except the BV angle. This single-center study provides preliminary reference data for fetal cerebellar vermis measurements during mid-trimester, offering a practical quantitative reference for prenatal screening of the posterior fossa. As no affected fetuses were studied and diagnostic performance was not assessed, the study establishes reference ranges rather than demonstrating clinical effectiveness. Fetal sex did not influence any parameter. External and multicenter validation with larger cohorts is warranted.

articles.title: Assessment of sleep patterns in third-trimester pregnant women: A cross-sectional latent profile analysis.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Cheng W, He D et al.
articles.abstract: This study seeks to categorize different sleep patterns in third-trimester pregnant women (≥28 weeks gestation) using latent profile analysis and to determine associated factors. A cross-sectional survey was carried out at a Shanghai hospital, where sleep information was gathered from 343 pregnant women via electronic questionnaires between June and August 2024. A total of 280 questionnaires were included (with a valid response rate of 81.63%). A 4-profile model was suggested as the optimum: good sleep quality (64.9%), high sleep efficiency-daytime dysfunction (19.3%), high sleep duration-low sleep efficiency (6.5%), and sleep disorder (SLD, 9.3%). Logistic regression analysis identified age, employment status, and anxiety as factors associated with poor sleep quality in pregnant women. Specifically, compared with the Good Sleep Quality group, women of older age (odds ratio [OR] = 1.186, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.072-1.313) were more prone to the High Sleep Efficiency-Daytime Dysfunction group classification. Older age (OR = 1.169, 95% CI = 1.028-1.331) and anxiety (OR = 1.075, 95% CI = 1.007-1.147) were associated with higher odds of SLD group membership, whereas employment (OR = 0.249, 95% CI = 0.102-0.604) was associated with lower odds of SLD group membership. Our study identified disparities in sleep quality among pregnant women based on various factors. Specifically, pregnant women with advanced maternal age or symptoms of anxiety were more likely to have poorer sleep quality. Employment was associated with lower odds of membership in the sleep-disorder profile. This indicates a need for tailored clinical care for different individuals.

articles.title: Reduced monocyte-to-HDL cholesterol ratio in intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy: A retrospective case-control study.
articles.authors: Topbas Selcuki NF, Karadeniz O, Batman A et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate whether the monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol ratio (MHR) is associated with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) and to explore its discriminative ability. This retrospective case-control study included 105 pregnant women (58 ICP; 47 controls) managed at a tertiary obstetrics center between March and August 2024. ICP was diagnosed based on pruritus and total bile acids ≥ 10 µmol/L. Monocyte counts, HDL levels, MHR, and pregnancy outcomes were compared between groups. Logistic regression, adjusted for maternal age and, in a sensitivity model, additionally for gestational age at blood sampling, assessed the association of each marker with ICP. Discrimination was explored using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Women with ICP had lower monocyte counts (median 0.68 [IQR 0.57-0.77] vs 0.80 [0.73-0.92] × 109/L; P < .001) and lower MHR (0.017 [0.012-0.022] vs 0.020 [0.016-0.026]; P = .006), whereas HDL levels did not differ (P = .842). After adjustment for age, lower MHR was associated with ICP (OR 0.50 per 0.01-unit increase, 95% CI: 0.28-0.90; P = .021). This association was attenuated after additional adjustment for gestational age at sampling (OR 0.64, 95% CI: 0.33-1.27; P = .200), whereas the association for monocyte count persisted (OR 0.69 per 0.1 × 109/L, 95% CI: 0.53-0.91; P = .009). MHR showed modest discrimination (area under the curve 0.658, 95% CI: 0.555-0.762), which did not exceed that of monocyte count alone (area under the curve 0.736). At a cutoff of ≤0.013, MHR had 31.0% sensitivity and 95.7% specificity. In this single-center, retrospective case-control study, MHR was lower in women with ICP, reflecting lower peripheral monocyte counts; the association was sensitive to adjustment for gestational age at sampling. Given its low sensitivity, MHR is not suitable for screening or diagnosis and does not replace serum bile acid measurement. These findings require confirmation in larger, prospective, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: How 37 Weeks Came to Define Preterm Birth and Why It Matters Today-Making of a Threshold.
articles.authors: Yu D, Norman M, Morin M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Preterm birth, defined as birth before 37 completed weeks of gestation, affects over 13 million births annually worldwide and remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. Despite the universal adoption of the 37-week threshold to define preterm birth, its historical origin and rationale remain unclear.
OBSERVATIONS: This review traces the evolution of the concepts of fetal maturity and gestational timing from ancient medicine to modern obstetrics. The idea of birth occurring too early can be traced to ancient Greek and Chinese medical writings, but the current 37-week threshold emerged in the mid-20th century, when definitions of prematurity shifted from birth weight-based criteria to gestational age. However, the basis for this threshold was not explicitly documented, and no clear evidence that its selection was based on a specific biological, clinical, or epidemiological justification was identified. Advances in obstetric dating and neonatal care have reshaped the clinical meaning of gestational age, with modern research and practice increasingly moving beyond a simple preterm-term dichotomy to the introduction of several subcategories of preterm birth. Growing evidence that infants born at 37 to 38 weeks face considerably higher short- and long-term health risks than those born later further challenges the assumption that 37 weeks represents a biologically sharp boundary.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The 37-week threshold for preterm birth has long been used in epidemiological surveillance, research, and clinical classification, although no clear documentation supporting its selection has been identified, and it may be insufficient for a better understanding of short- and long-term health of the offspring. A more precise assessment of gestational age, together with high-resolution clinical and population data, may support a more refined classification of different preterm birth categories and further advance clinical care, research, and public health.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Differences in County-Level Availability of Uterine Cancer Clinical Trials.
articles.authors: Felix AS, Meade CE, Wing JJ et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Racial and ethnic disparities exist in clinical trial enrollment, but whether such disparities exist in geographic availability of uterine cancer trials is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between race and ethnicity and county-level presence and rates of available uterine cancer clinical trials.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study linked Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Research Plus; Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov; and American Community Survey data of adult patients (aged ≥18 years) diagnosed with uterine cancer between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2021. The data analysis was performed between November 10, 2025, and September 9, 2026.
EXPOSURES: Race and ethnicity categorized as American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, Black, Hispanic (any race), Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, and White.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were county-level presence and rate of interventional uterine cancer trials. Hurdle models were used to estimate racial and ethnic differences in the odds of residing in a county with at least 1 trial and among patients in counties with trial availability, differences in rates of trials per person. Models accounted for county clustering and were adjusted for patient characteristics.
RESULTS: Among 155 811 patients in the cohort (median [IQR] age at diagnosis, 62 [55-69] years; 1055 identifying as American Indian or Alaska Native [0.7%], 12 753 as Asian [8.2%], 16 303 as Black [10.5%], 23 177 as Hispanic [14.9%], 2175 as Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander [1.4%], and 100 348 as White [64.4%] race and ethnicity), 121 525 (78.0%) resided in a county with at least 1 available trial. Trial availability was observed among 58.0% of American Indian or Alaska Native patients, 94.3% of Asian patients, 77.7% of Black patients, 86.1% of Hispanic patients, 90.3% of Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander patients, and 74.1% of White patients. Compared with White patients, higher odds of residing in counties with at least 1 available trial were found for Asian (odds ratio [OR], 5.83; 95% CI, 4.83-7.12), Black (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.07-1.30), Hispanic (OR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.80-2.63), and Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander (OR, 3.34; 95% CI, 2.17-5.66) patients, whereas American Indian or Alaska Native patients had lower odds (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39-0.61). Among patients in counties with at least 1 trial, fewer available trials per person were found for Asian…

articles.title: Neighborhood Exposome at Birth and Trajectories of Epigenetic Age Acceleration Across Childhood.
articles.authors: Yuan QE, Bozack AK, Paquin V et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) has been linked to increased disease risk in adults, yet its developmental trajectories and early-life neighborhood determinants remain poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether there are associations between the neighborhood exposome at birth and EAA trajectories from early childhood through adolescence.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This longitudinal cohort study used data from Project Viva, a prebirth cohort that enrolled pregnant women in eastern Massachusetts from April 22, 1999, to July 31, 2002. Participants included 570 children with available peripheral blood DNA methylation data, complete neighborhood characteristics, and complete covariates. Data were analyzed from August 19, 2024, to August 21, 2026.
EXPOSURES: Neighborhood exposome profiles at birth derived from 22 census tract-level characteristics across 4 domains (area deprivation, social fragmentation, population density, and environmental quality) using self-organizing maps.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: EAA was calculated at 3, 8, and 13 years of age using the Horvath, Skin & Blood, and Wu epigenetic clocks. Trajectories were identified using latent class linear mixed models. Associations between neighborhood profiles and EAA trajectories were estimated using multinomial mixed models.
RESULTS: Among 570 children (mean [SD] age at early childhood, 3.2 [0.4] years; 305 [53.5%] male), 3 EAA trajectory groups (stable, increasing, and decreasing for the Horvath and Skin & Blood clocks or low-baseline for the Wu clock) and 3 neighborhood profiles were identified. Compared with profile 1 (suburban, lowest adverse exposures [n = 278]), children born into profile 2 (urban, high residential instability and single-person households, and highway proximity [n = 168]) had greater odds of increasing EAA for the Wu clock (adjusted odds ratio, 1.67 [95% CI, 1.03-2.69]). Profile 3 (urban, high socioeconomic deprivation and pollution [n = 124]) showed no associations.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this longitudinal cohort study, birth into neighborhoods characterized by high residential instability and single-person households and highway proximity was associated with increasing Wu EAA trajectories across childhood. These findings suggest that early-life neighborhood conditions, encompassing both social and physical environmental factors, may represent targets for interventions aimed at reducing long-term disease risk. Further research is needed to…

articles.title: Real-world evaluation of the NHS testing criteria for glucokinase hyperglycaemia in pregnancy.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.authors: Jones O, Brackenridge A, Houghton J et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Criteria for Glucokinase-Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young (GCK-MODY) genetic testing are now being integrated into the National Health Service (NHS) services using fasting glucose, body mass index (BMI) and ethnicity. We aimed to assess the national screening criteria for GCK-MODY in a multi-ethnic population.
METHODS: GCK-MODY testing was offered to women with gestational diabetes that met criteria in a multi-ethnic cohort. Data from the national testing centre was used to compare patient characteristics in those positive and negative for GCK-MODY.
RESULTS: Fewer cases of GCK-MODY were found when testing using NHS criteria (0.14%) than expected (0.9%). Individuals testing positive for GCK-MODY had a higher HbA1c than negative individuals (p < 0.001). There was no difference in 2-h glucose increment (p = 0.829).
CONCLUSIONS: Current criteria may not effectively identify a high-risk cohort of individuals to test, given the prevalence of GCK-MODY in those tested, leading to over-testing. HbA1c may prove a useful additional screening parameter. Further studies are needed to improve the criteria's utility across different ethnicities.

articles.title: Cervical Cancer Knowledge, Misconceptions, and Educational Needs Among Women Undergoing Screening in Dodoma, Tanzania: A Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
articles.authors: Mmari EG, Lilungulu AG, Bintabara DF
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer prevention depends on women understanding that the disease is preventable and that screening is needed before symptoms develop. This study assessed cervical cancer knowledge and explored misconceptions, information sources, and educational needs among women undergoing screening at Dodoma Regional Referral Hospital, Tanzania. A concurrent mixed-methods study was conducted from January to March 2026. Quantitative data were collected from 422 women aged 25 years or older using a 25-item Cervical Cancer Awareness Measure-based composite incorporating 20 knowledge/awareness responses and five information-source indicators; 20 purposively selected women completed in-depth interviews. Composite scores were categorized as poor (0-14), moderate (15-19), or good (20-25). Quantitative data were summarized descriptively, qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and findings were integrated during interpretation. Overall, 211 (50.0%) participants were classified as poor, 184 (43.6%) as moderate, and 27 (6.4%) as good on the composite. Only 24.4% recognized that cervical cancer was preventable, 42.4% had heard of human papillomavirus vaccination, and 21.6% recognized the role of regular screening in early detection. Health workers were the most frequently reported information source (48.8%). Interviews revealed superficial awareness, misconceptions about causation, fear of severe illness and death, and a strong desire for education. These findings identify priority messages for culturally appropriate education at screening encounters and in community settings; effectiveness of such education requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Real‑World Treatment Patterns in Endometrial Cancer in the Post-Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor and Post-Platinum-Based Chemotherapy Setting in the United States.
articles.authors: Prabhu VS, Marupuru S, McClain KM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), either following or in combination with platinum chemotherapy (PT), are routinely used to treat endometrial cancer (EC). Subsequently, a post-ICI and post-PT patient population is emerging with no approved therapy or guideline-recommended treatment approach for this setting. As novel therapies are being explored, it is critical to understand the patient characteristics and real-world treatment patterns in this setting.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study used de-identified electronic health record data from the Flatiron Health database (2013-2026). Adult women with EC who had prior exposure to both ICI and PT and subsequently initiated a new regimen (the index line of therapy [LOT]) were included. The results were stratified by mismatch repair and microsatellite instability (MMR/MSI) status, and treatment patterns were summarized descriptively.
RESULTS: A total of 564 women met the selection criteria, including 34 (6.0%) treated in the first LOT, 188 (33.3%) in the second LOT, 189 (33.5%) in the third LOT, and 153 (27.1%) in the fourth LOT or later. Among patients with deficient MMR/MSI-High (dMMR/MSI-H) tumors, post-ICI and post-PT regimens usually included hormonal therapy (18.0%) and ICI monotherapy (14.0%). Among patients with proficient MMR and microsatellite stable (pMMR/MSS) tumors, chemotherapy monotherapy (25.7%) and ICI plus tyrosine kinase inhibitor combinations (11.9%) were most frequent. A total of 228 patients (40.4%) received an ICI-containing regimen at the index LOT or a subsequent line, of whom 179 (78.5%) received a pembrolizumab-containing regimen, 21 (9.2%) a dostarlimab-containing regimen, and 28 (12.3%) other ICI-containing regimens.
CONCLUSIONS: In EC, the post-ICI and post-PT patient population is growing, particularly in the second LOT and earlier settings. Treatment following ICI and PT exposure in EC was highly variable, with no dominant regimen identified regardless of MMR/MSI status.

articles.title: Patient and partner experiences of prostate cancer survivorship in Ireland: findings from the co-designed PRO-ACT study (CTRIAL-IE 24-45).
articles.authors: Flynn CR, Sweeney M, Sullivan J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy among men in Ireland, yet patient and partner experiences regarding sexual wellbeing, treatment preparedness, and survivorship needs remain poorly characterised.
METHODS: The PRO-ACT study employed parallel, co-designed online surveys for patients with PCa and their partners across the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland. Surveys were developed collaboratively with a patient previously treated for PCa and disseminated online between November 2024 and June 2025. Descriptive statistics summarised demographics, treatment preparedness, partner inclusion, sexual wellbeing, mental health, multidisciplinary consultation, and urinary/bowel toxicities.
RESULTS: A total of 598 patients and 538 partners participated. Preparedness for treatment-related sexual consequences was low: 66.3% of patients felt underprepared, and 53.1% of partners received no explanation. Sexual difficulties were widespread, with 85.4% of patients reporting erectile problems and 84.3% reporting decline in sexual wellbeing; 68.0% of partners also reported deterioration. Mental health impacts were substantial (patients: 58.7%, partners: 51.5%), yet psychological support was rarely offered. Urinary incontinence (63.7%), obstructive symptoms (40.4%), and bowel disturbances (40.1%) were common. Multidisciplinary involvement was inconsistent, with only 48.6% offered cross-specialty consultations.
CONCLUSIONS: This first all-island assessment demonstrates major gaps in information provision, partner inclusion, psychosexual support, and toxicity management. Findings highlight the need for structured, personalised, multidisciplinary survivorship pathways recognising sexual wellbeing and mental health as core components. Results provide actionable insights for Ireland's next National Cancer Strategy.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture at Front-Mu acupoint group attenuates stress urinary incontinence in rats by modulating oxidative stress and Nrf2 signaling.
articles.authors: Huang H, Chen B, Hu J et al.
articles.abstract: To investigate whether electroacupuncture (EA) at the Front-Mu acupoint group improves stress urinary incontinence (SUI) in rats through modulation of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway. Sixty-five female SD rats were randomized into sham (n = 10) and SUI model (n = 55) groups. SUI was induced by vaginal dilation and bilateral ovariectomy. Successfully modeled rats were randomly divided into model, DMSO, EA, ATRA (Nrf2 inhibitor), and EA + ATRA groups (n = 10 each). EA was applied at Zhongji (CV3), Guanyuan (CV4), and bilateral Dahe (KI12) once daily for three days. Urodynamic parameters (MBC, ALPP), antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, GSH-Px), oxidative stress markers (8-OHdG, 4-HNE), apoptosis (TUNEL, Bax/Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-3), and Keap1/Nrf2 mRNA and protein expression were assessed. EA significantly increased MBC and ALPP, enhanced SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px activities, and decreased 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) and 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) levels (all P < 0.05). EA also reduced the apoptotic index, Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, and cleaved caspase-3 expression (all P < 0.05). Furthermore, EA upregulated Keap1 and Nrf2 mRNA and protein expression (all P < 0.05). These protective effects were partially abrogated by ATRA co-treatment. EA at the Front-Mu acupoint group alleviates SUI, associated with modulation of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway, enhancing antioxidant defense and inhibiting apoptosis. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic support for further investigation of electroacupuncture in SUI treatment.

articles.title: Temporal trends in patients undergoing artificial urinary sphincter implantation: explantation outcomes and early failure patterns in a tertiary reconstructive referral center.
articles.authors: Roessler N, Vetterlein MW, Klemm J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Baseline characteristics and perioperative risk profiles in patients undergoing artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation have changed over time, potentially influencing clinical outcomes. This study assessed temporal trends in patient characteristics and explantation outcomes to inform preoperative counselling and risk stratification.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included male patients undergoing AUS implantation between 2009 and 2025, stratified into four implantation periods. Explantation-free survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Risk factors for explantation were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: A total of 491 patients were included (2009-2012: N = 177; 2013-2017: N = 159; 2018-2022: N = 107; 2023-2025: N = 48), with a median follow-up of 54 months (IQR 14-116). Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, with a relative increase in prior radiotherapy from 35% to 42% over time. Explantation rates were 36%, 27%, 22%, and 17%, respectively, predominantly due to erosion and infection. In multivariable analysis, prior radiotherapy (HR 1.88, 95% CI 1.30-2.70), prior BPH surgery (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.10-2.77), and prior bulbar urethroplasty (HR 2.10, 95% CI 1.12-3.93) were independent predictors of explantation. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant differences in explantation-free survival between periods (p = 0.8), although a numerical increase in early explantations within 24 months was observed (7.9% to 13%). In a supplementary analysis focusing on early explantation, prior radiotherapy (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.38-4.39) and prior urethral surgery (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.31-4.77) were independently associated with increased risk. Later implantation periods showed an increase in early explantation risk; however, this did not reach statistical significance. The study is limited by its retrospective single-center design.
CONCLUSION: The AUS remains a durable and effective treatment option for male incontinence, with stable outcomes across implantation periods. Careful preoperative counselling and structured follow-up remain essential, particularly in high-risk patients.

articles.title: Compartment-Resolved Profiling Identifies Shared Stromal Programs and Clarifies Molecular Subtype Origins in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Djirackor S, Heinze K, Beddows I et al.
articles.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancers (EOCs) comprise biologically distinct histotypes that arise within shared anatomical niches where tumor-stroma interactions shape tumor behavior and therapeutic response. However, most classification frameworks rely on bulk profiling that conflates epithelial and stromal contributions, limiting the understanding of crosstalk between the different compartments. Here, we performed compartment-resolved transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of matched carcinoma and stroma across clear cell (CCOC), endometrioid (ENOC), and high-grade serous ovarian cancers (HGSC). Carcinoma profiles segregated strongly by histotype, whereas stromal profiles showed minimal histotype specificity and instead resolved into four shared groups (S1-S4). The S4 subtype, marked by a desmoplastic, myofibroblast-rich program, was enriched in omental tumors and corresponded to the HGSC C1/Mesenchymal signature. This subtype largely reflected tumor-extrinsic programs and was present beyond HGSC. Compartment-resolved analyses also refined the interpretation of other molecular carcinoma subtypes and revealed distinct carcinoma-intrinsic EMT-like programs. Together, these findings define a histotype-agnostic stromal architecture across epithelial ovarian cancers, clarify the cellular basis of canonical high-grade serous molecular subtypes, and reveal carcinoma-intrinsic EMT programs. This study underscores the value of physically separating epithelial and stromal compartments before molecular analysis and position this dataset as a multi-purpose reference resource for the EOC research community.

articles.title: Patient acceptance and implementation of automated breast ultrasound in intensified breast cancer surveillance.
articles.authors: Hatzipanagiotou ME, Hartwig K, Fernandez-Pacheco M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Automated breast ultrasound (ABUS) is a standardized ultrasound technique that may reduce operator dependency compared with hand-held ultrasound. Evidence on patient acceptance and implementation in intensified breast cancer surveillance remains limited. This study evaluated patient acceptance and clinical implementation of ABUS within a certified center of the German Consortium for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center observational study, women enrolled in an intensified breast cancer surveillance program underwent ABUS examinations and completed standardized questionnaires. Patient-reported outcomes included examination-related discomfort, comparison with mammography, willingness to repeat the examination, and willingness to recommend ABUS. Workflow parameters and changes in acquisition time over repeated examinations were assessed prospectively.
RESULTS: 73 women contributed 162 ABUS examinations and corresponding questionnaires. Of these, 46/73 (63.0%) carried pathogenic variants in BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, or TP53, and 27/73 (37.0%) had a previous breast cancer diagnosis. Median pain score was 0 (IQR 0-1) for both breasts. Among women with previous mammography and an available comparative rating, 56/57 (98.2%) rated ABUS as more comfortable. All 73 participants (100%) were willing to undergo future ABUS examinations and recommend the procedure. Mean acquisition and interpretation times were 31.9 ± 6.2 and 9.95 ± 4.0 min, respectively. Acquisition time decreased significantly with increasing examination number (β = - 1.72 min/examination; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: ABUS was associated with high reported patient acceptance and was feasible to integrate into intensified breast cancer surveillance, with improving acquisition efficiency over time.

articles.title: Inflammation-driven epigenetic memory in infertility and chronic endometritis.
articles.authors: Chen R, Diao L, Markert UR et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic endometritis (CE) is a persistent, low-grade inflammatory condition of the endometrium, typically caused by microbial infections. CE is often asymptomatic, leading to frequent underdiagnosis. It is frequently identified during the assessment of causes for infertility. Even after resolving the infectious etiology by antibiotic treatment, infertility persists in a number of patients. Emerging evidence from chronic inflammatory diseases affecting epithelial tissues, e.g., in the gut, suggests that inflammatory conditions can induce long-lasting epigenetic changes, e.g., in innate immune cells. Notably, tissues outside the immune system can also retain memory of inflammatory events and environmental insults via epigenetic modifications. This review summarizes how epigenetic changes can affect endometrial function, drawing on current knowledge of CE. It also discusses how inflammation prompts these changes. We propose that persistent epigenetic memory in both immune and non-immune endometrial cells plays a crucial role in sustaining CE-associated adversities, such as infertility. Future research should focus on pinpointing specific epigenetic patterns in CE and exploring how inflammation-induced memory leads to cellular dysfunction in the endometrium. Understanding these mechanisms will advance CE diagnosis and open doors to new treatment options for infertility, focusing on reversing the inflammatory memory retained upon treatment of CE.

articles.title: Beyond Obliteration: Anatomical Characterisation of Residual Vaginal Length Following Colpocleisis.
articles.authors: Pandey D, Kottayam D, Arja K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Colpocleisis is an established obliterative procedure for advanced pelvic organ prolapse in women who no longer desire vaginal intercourse. This video demonstrates the surgical anatomy and key operative steps of Le Fort, total colpocleisis, and colpocleisis with hysterectomy, and correlates these techniques with the postoperative vaginal anatomy and residual vaginal length.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted between September 2024 and August 2025 in women undergoing colpocleisis for stage III or IV POP. Vaginal length was measured preoperatively, immediately after surgery, and at 6 months. Perioperative outcomes, complications, recurrence, and patient satisfaction were recorded. The accompanying video demonstrates Le Fort colpocleisis, total colpocleisis, and colpocleisis with hysterectomy, highlighting key operative steps and their relationship to postoperative anatomy.
RESULTS: Twenty-one women underwent surgery. All achieved successful anatomical correction without recurrence during follow-up and reported high postoperative satisfaction. Mean vaginal length decreased from 8.70 ± 1.98 cm preoperatively to 3.76 ± 0.41 cm immediately after surgery and 3.90 ± 0.45 cm at 6 months. The mean reduction in vaginal length from baseline to 6 months was 4.80 ± 1.90 cm. Thus, successful colpocleisis resulted in substantial shortening of vaginal length, with persistence of a short measurable vaginal segment at 6 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Colpocleisis provides effective prolapse correction with substantial reduction in vaginal length while leaving a measurable residual vaginal segment. Objective characterisation of this postoperative anatomy may improve understanding of the anatomical outcome of colpocleisis.

articles.title: Lipid-rich ascites reprograms the T cell lipid metabolic transcriptome to drive dysfunction.
articles.authors: Wan PK, Albayrak G, Bruchner PE et al.
articles.abstract: Malignant ascites is a lipid-rich, immunosuppressive environment that has recently emerged as a target for locoregional bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) therapy. However, the mechanisms by which ascites, particularly its lipid components, suppress antitumour immunity and limit therapeutic efficacy remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of ascites lipids on T-cell immunosuppression and assessed whether lipid modulation could enhance the efficacy of BiTE therapy. Transcriptomic profiling of T cells exposed to acellular ascites fluid revealed an enriched signature associated with cholesterol efflux and incomplete fatty acid oxidation, which are metabolic features often found in exhausted T cells. These alterations converged on a metabolically imbalanced state linked to impaired plasma membrane signalling. Meanwhile, anti-CD3/CD28-stimulated T cells showed marked lipid accumulation in ascites, which was attenuated by lipid depletion. Functionally, lipid removal was associated with enhanced TCR-associated signalling, as demonstrated by increased ZAP70 phosphorylation, and restored CD137 expression while leaving CD25 unchanged. To determine whether ascites lipids also affected BiTE efficacy, T cells were cocultured with ovarian cancer cells and an EpCAM-targeting BiTE in untreated or lipid-depleted ascites. Ascites suppressed BiTE-mediated T-cell activation and abolished tumour cell killing, whereas lipid depletion contributed to the restoration of T-cell activation, IFN-γ production and BiTE-mediated cytotoxicity. Together, these findings suggest that lipids contribute to T-cell dysfunction in ovarian cancer ascites and demonstrate that lipid depletion is associated with restored antitumour T-cell activity. Targeting this metabolic barrier may therefore provide a combination strategy to potentiate BiTE therapy in malignant ascites.

articles.title: Inflammaging and Cellular Senescence in Postmenopausal Depression: Linking Estrogen Deficiency, Immune Dysregulation, and Brain Aging.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.authors: Zhang L, Yao Y, Cai X
articles.abstract: Postmenopausal depression is clinically heterogeneous and cannot be explained by estrogen deficiency alone. We propose a conceptual, testable neuroimmune-aging model in which endocrine decline may interact with inflammaging, cellular senescence, and brain vulnerability in a subset of women. The evidentiary base is uneven: direct studies of senescence in well-phenotyped postmenopausal depression are lacking; clinical endocrine data come mainly from perimenopausal depression; molecular-senescence findings come from late-life depression or general major depressive disorder; and most cellular and brain mechanisms are supported by aging or preclinical models. Reduced estrogen signaling may weaken immune homeostasis, whereas peripheral cytokines or senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors could influence vascular and neural interfaces, glia, neurotransmitter metabolism, stress signaling, mitochondrial function, and neuroplasticity. These pathways are candidate mediators, not established causal mechanisms. Clinically established care remains diagnosis-based antidepressant treatment, evidence-based management of vasomotor and sleep symptoms, and individualized menopausal hormone therapy for appropriate candidates. Anti-inflammatory, microbiome-based, and senescence-targeted strategies remain investigational; no senolytic or senomorphic is approved for depression or menopause-related mood symptoms. Prospective studies integrating menopausal staging, prespecified confounders, senescence biomarkers, neuroimaging, and mood outcomes are needed to test this model.

articles.title: Prenatal stress alters the sexual differentiation of the neural circuits governing sex-typical behavior in male offspring.
articles.authors: Bentefour Y, Da Cruz LC, Bakker J
articles.abstract: Exposure to stress during pregnancy has been associated not only with adverse outcomes but also with lasting consequences on the offspring. In the present study, we investigated the effects of gestational stress on HPA axis reactivity, sexual behavior, and neural activation in adult male and female mouse offspring. The results showed that prenatally stressed males exhibited a blunted corticosterone response to stress and reduced baseline levels of dehydroepiandrosterone, whereas prenatally stressed females showed no clear alterations. Both males and females displayed markedly reduced sexual preference for opposite-sex conspecifics, while no changes were observed in sexual performance. However, orchiectomy and hormonal treatment of the males with estradiol and progesterone revealed increased lordosis behavior compared to control males. In addition, chemosensory-induced c-Fos in response to male bedding showed that prenatally stressed males displayed female-typical activation patterns in key brain areas involved in female reproductive behavior, including the ventromedial hypothalamus. Together, these findings indicate that gestational stress can impair opposite-sex preferences, as well as the defeminization of neural circuits governing sex-typical behavior in male offspring without disrupting normal male-typical sexual behaviors.

articles.title: Preimplantation genetic testing in Italy: a single-cycle retrospective analysis.
articles.authors: Conforti A, Faggionato C, Vigiliano V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) is a diagnostic procedure performed during assisted reproductive technology (ART) to detect chromosomal and monogenic abnormalities before embryo transfer. In Italy, the Italian ART Register (IARTR) monitors ART and PGT activity. Within a National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) project, entitled "Development of the Italian Preimplantation Genetic Testing (PGT) Network", we developed a monitoring system based on ART single-cycles in which PGT was performed.
METHODS: Data on ART-PGT cycles performed in 2024 were collected from 24 Italian ART centers. A relational database was developed including cycle-level and embryo-level variables. Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics, Version 29 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).
RESULTS: Overall, 2181 ART-PGT cycles involving 1358 patients were analyzed. Genetic testing was performed in 1195 cycles during 2024, and next-generation sequencing was the most frequent technology (96.5%). PGT for aneuploidies (PGT-A) was the most frequent procedure (1065 cycles), followed by PGT for monogenic/single gene defects (PGT-M) (114 cycles) and PGT for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR) (110 cycles). The main indication for PGT-A was advanced maternal age (59.4%), for PGT-M was beta-thalassemia (29.6%), for PGT-SR reciprocal chromosomal rearrangements (61.3%). A total of 3771 embryos were analyzed, of which 7% yielded no result. Most blastocysts were biopsied on day 5 or 6 and were classified as having good or optimal quality. Embryo transfer was performed in 761 cycles, most as single embryo transfer, resulting in a clinical pregnancy rate of 49.1%.
CONCLUSIONS: The single-cycle monitoring system for ART-PGT was feasible and effective in collecting detailed clinical and laboratory data. This approach represents an innovation in epidemiological surveillance and may be useful in quality assessment and standardization of ART-PGT practices in Italy.

articles.title: Do thyroid antibodies impact fertility outcomes in infertile women? An observational cohort study evaluating ART.
articles.authors: VAN DE Klashorst BP, VAN Wely M, Delprat CC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies (TPO-Abs) have been associated with infertility, implantation failure, early pregnancy loss, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. As TPO-Abs may interact with the zona pellucida, ICSI could bypass this mechanism. We therefore examined whether TPO-Abs influence pregnancy outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART), and whether ICSI offers higher pregnancy rates than IVF in women with TPO-Abs.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of women who underwent IVF/ICSI between January 2020 and December 2023. Thyroid function and TPO-Ab levels were measured. Baseline characteristics were collected. Univariable and multivariable Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) analyses were performed to assess associations between TPO-Ab status, fertilization method, and pregnancy outcomes, yielding adjusted odds ratios (ORadj).
RESULTS: Among 712 women, 115 (16.2%) women had TPO-Abs. These women had a longer duration of infertility and higher TSH levels. Cumulative ongoing pregnancy rates for women with TPO-Abs were 49.1% after IVF and 42.8% after ICSI. For women without TPO-Abs cumulative, ongoing pregnancy rates were 44.7% after IVF and 55.6% after ICSI. In multivariable GEE analyses, the presence of TPO-Abs was not associated with ongoing pregnancy (adjusted OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.59-1.51; P=0.80) or miscarriage (adjusted OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.50-1.35; P=0.43). No significant interaction was observed between TPO-Ab status, fertilization method, and ongoing pregnancy or miscarriage.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that TPO-Abs may not be associated with lower pregnancy rates after ART. Furthermore, no clear differences between IVF and ICSI outcomes were observed among women with TPO-Abs. These findings suggest that TPO-Ab status may have limited impact on ART treatment decisions in women with normal thyroid status at ART treatment initiation.

articles.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
articles.authors: Sufriyana H, Wu YW, Chiu HS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.
METHODS: We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.
RESULTS: The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).
CONCLUSIONS: Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

articles.title: Drug Repurposing in Pre-Eclampsia: Maternal Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Considerations for Clinical Trial Design.
articles.authors: Phogole CM, Algharably EA, Decloedt EH et al.
articles.abstract: Pre-eclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy affecting 3-8% of pregnancies worldwide, with no disease-modifying therapy currently available. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy, yet no candidate has been validated to date. Pregnancy-associated physiological changes alter drug pharmacokinetics (PK), and pre-eclampsia itself may further modify drug disposition, complicating dose selection and contributing to inconclusive clinical trial outcomes. A structured literature search identified six prospective or randomized controlled trials of repurposed drugs for established pre-eclampsia: esomeprazole, omeprazole, sulfasalazine, pravastatin, recombinant antithrombin, and metformin. All drugs were well tolerated, with metformin the one to show promising clinical benefit by prolonging gestation; the remaining five drugs yielded inconclusive or null efficacy outcomes. Critically, PK sampling was conducted in only three trials, and none systematically characterized exposure-response relationships using key pre-eclampsia biomarkers, including soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1, soluble endoglin, and placental growth factor. Further common methodological limitations included small sample sizes (12-120 participants), heterogeneous gestational age eligibility criteria, and dosing regimens extrapolated from non-pregnant populations without pregnancy-specific optimization. These shortcomings likely contributed to the translational gap between promising preclinical findings and positive clinical trial outcomes. Model-informed drug development (MIDD) approaches, including physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) and population pharmacokinetic (popPK) modeling, optimal sampling strategies, and simulation-based dose selection, offer a framework to improve pre-eclampsia trial design. Future studies should integrate these approaches with biomarker-guided exposure-response analyses and prediction of fetal exposure throughout pregnancy to enhance therapeutic development, optimize maternal-fetal safety, and accelerate the identification of effective disease-modifying therapies for pre-eclampsia.

articles.title: Associations between gestational weight gain and adverse pregnancy outcomes: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wang X, Zhang X, Zhang M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most studies on gestational weight gain (GWG) and pregnancy outcomes have focused on Western populations, leaving a gap in knowledge about the applicability of their findings to Asian women. Similarly, most investigations have utilised recommendations created by the US Institute of Medicine, with few using the Chinese GWG recommendations. We aimed to assess the associations between GWG, evaluated according to the Chinese recommendations, and adverse pregnancy outcomes, as well as to explore whether prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) or maternal age modified these associations.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we recruited pregnant women at 11-13 weeks of gestation from 13 hospitals in northern China between October 2020 and June 2024. We categorised GWG as insufficient, adequate, or excessive when it fell below, within, or above the Chinese recommendations, with the recommended GWG ranges being 11.0-16.0 kg (BMI < 18.5 kg/m2), 8.0-14.0 kg (18.5-23.9 kg/m2), 7.0-11.0 kg (24.0-27.9 kg/m2), and 5.0-9.0 kg (BMI ≥ 28.0 kg/m2). We used logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) for adverse pregnancy outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 10,638 pregnant women, 13.3%, 54.3%, and 32.4% had insufficient, adequate, and excessive GWG, respectively. After adjusting for confounders, excessive GWG was associated with higher odds for caesarean delivery (OR = 1.38; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.26-1.53), macrosomia (OR = 1.77; 95% CI = 1.44-2.17), being large for gestational age (OR = 1.66; 95% CI = 1.38-1.99), and neonatal ward admission (OR = 1.35; 95% CI = 1.09-1.67), while insufficient GWG was associated with increased odds of being small for gestational age (OR = 1.48; 95% CI = 1.17-1.88). There was a significant interaction between GWG and maternal age in relation to the odds of caesarean delivery (P-value for interaction = 0.034). Women aged ≥ 35 years with excessive GWG had the highest odds of caesarean delivery (OR = 2.72; 95% CI = 2.27-3.24), compared with women aged <35 years with adequate GWG.
CONCLUSIONS: Excessive GWG was associated with higher odds of caesarean delivery, macrosomia, large for gestational age, and neonatal ward admission, while insufficient GWG was associated to higher odds of small for gestational age.

articles.title: Physician Job Choice and Support for Abortion Access in the Post Dobbs Landscape: a Survey Study of High-Risk Specialty Trainees.
articles.authors: Douglas R, Brakke B, Bettini LM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physicians have always had to balance personal ethics, professional obligations, and legal constraints when providing abortion care; however, since the United States Supreme Court ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, the legal framework governing this care has shifted substantially, raising concerns about physician workforce stability. The primary aim in our pilot study was to assess how likely states' abortion laws will influence where physicians accept their first job after residency or fellowship. Our other objectives were to assess physician support for abortion access and well-being post Dobbs. We hypothesized that the majority of physicians would be likely to consider states' abortion laws when looking for first post training jobs, would support abortion access, and would have had their well-being affected.
METHODS: We surveyed anesthesiology, emergency medicine, and obstetrics-gynecology (OB-GYN) residents and fellows.
RESULTS: We achieved only a 1.2% response rate. In this small data set, a majority (65.6%) of residents and fellows said that they are likely to consider state abortion laws when deciding where to accept their first post-training job, with OB-GYNs (90.7%) having the greatest majority. Eight out of ten physicians were supportive of medical and surgical abortion access (87.2%; 86.1%). A majority of physicians were supportive of abortion across all demographics, even Catholics, deviating only when assessed by political party affiliation. A majority of physicians (56.5%) were negatively affected by the Dobbs decision, regardless of the abortion law where they practice. Cisgender women and OB-GYN trainees were most impacted.
CONCLUSIONS: The response rate limits any generalizability of our findings, and future research is needed. In this pilot study, the majority of physicians indicated that they will consider states' abortion laws when accepting their first job, and a minority of physicians may be willing to work in states with abortion bans. To promote physician retention and recruitment, future research should investigate how access to reproductive care impacts physicians' professional and personal well-being.

articles.title: From collision to conversion, the molecular renaissance of uterine carcinosarcoma in the era of antibody-drug conjugates: a scoping review.
articles.authors: D'Indinosante M, Giuliano MC, Parisi G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Uterine carcinosarcoma is a rare aggressive uterine malignancy increasingly regarded as a metaplastic endometrial carcinoma rather than a true collision tumor. Its marked molecular heterogeneity has important implications for classification, prognosis, and treatment.
AREAS COVERED: This scoping review summarizes histogenesis and molecular landscape of uterine carcinosarcoma and evaluates clinical evidence for immunotherapy, targeted therapies, and antibody-drug conjugates. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to 29 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and targeted searches. Most tumors exhibit a copy-number-high genomic profile or are classified as p53-abnormal, whereas mismatch repair-deficient and POLE-mutated tumors represent smaller but clinically relevant subsets. The clinical evidence base for immunotherapy remains extrapolated from broader endometrial cancer trials, although direct prospective evidence from small uterine carcinosarcoma cohorts is emerging. Earlier unselected targeted approaches showed modest activity, whereas biomarker-selected strategies, particularly HER2-directed trastuzumab deruxtecan, have produced encouraging signals.
EXPERT OPINION: Molecular profiling is likely to refine treatment selection and sequencing, especially in advanced or recurrent disease. However, progress depends on standardized biomarker assessment, international multicenter trials, and mandatory carcinosarcoma-specific outcome reporting. Surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy are likely to remain the therapeutic backbone, while future progress will depend on integrating validated biomarkers into disease-specific treatment algorithms.

articles.title: Molecular and Clinical Characterization of TRIM52, NF-κB, and PD-L1 in Breast Cancer Using Immunohistochemistry and Large-scale Transcriptomic Analysis.
articles.authors: Alfalah ME, Al-Keilani MS, Alqudah MA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Tripartite Motif (TRIM) family of E3 ubiquitin ligases regulates critical cancer-associated pathways. TRIM52, a less-characterized member, exhibits oncogenic roles in various solid tumors, often via Nuclear Factor Kappa-light-chain-enhancer of Activated B Cells (NF-κB) activation or Programmed Death-Ligand 1 (PD-L1).
METHODS: This retrospective study investigated the expression of TRIM52, NF-κB, PD-L1, and Ki- 67 (as a proliferation marker) in a retrospective cohort of 133 breast cancer tissues and 29 matched normal adjacent tissues from patients using immunohistochemistry on tissue microarrays. External transcriptomic validation was performed using the METABRIC cohort (n = 1,980), with patients classified into high- and low-TRIM52 mRNA expression groups according to the cohort median (n = 990 per group) for clinicopathological and survival analyses.
RESULTS: TRIM52 protein was not expressed across all 133 breast cancer specimens but was detected in 34.5% of histologically normal adjacent breast tissues. NF-κB was highly expressed in 88.6% of tumors and was significantly associated with ER-positive status (p = 0.018). PD-L1 expression was infrequent (9.8%) but correlated with ER and PR status (p = 0.040 and 0.010, respectively), pT stage (p = 0.048), pN stage (p = 0.034), TNM stage (p = 0.014), and Ki-67 expression (p = 0.029). In METABRIC, high TRIM52 mRNA expression was associated with age ≥50 years, menopausal status, tumor grade, NPI, ER/PR positivity, HER2 negativity, Ki-67, and molecular subtype (p < 0.004). High TRIM52 expression was also associated with poorer overall survival (log-rank P < 0.001; overall HR = 1.25, 95% CI, 1.11-1.41).
DISCUSSION: This study showed a complete TRIM52 protein loss in breast cancer and the adverse prognostic association of high TRIM52 mRNA expression, challenging its presumed oncogenic role and pointing to a potential breast-specific tumor-suppressive function. The distinct profiles of NF- κB, PD-L1, and Ki-67 underscore the molecular heterogeneity of BC.
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest a negative prognostic value of TRIM52 gene expression level in breast cancer despite its negative protein expression in the analyzed tissues.

articles.title: ONC201 (Dordaviprone/TIC10) Variably Modulates Autophagy Response in HPV-Positive Cervical Cancer Cell Lines in a CLPP-Independent Manner.
articles.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
articles.authors: Pathak SO, Shah I, Khedekar T et al.
articles.abstract: ONC201, also known as dordaviprone or TIC10, a first-in-class member of the imipridone family, has recently received fast-track FDA approval for recurrent diffuse midline glioma. It has shown therapeutic promise and a suitable safety profile in both solid and hematologic malignancies. We recently reported in vitro efficacy of ONC201 in cervical cancer cell lines despite its differential effects on its targets viz. caseinolytic protease (CLPP), TRAIL and DR5 in each of these cell lines. In the current study, we show that ONC201 treatment leads to distinct phenotypic outcomes i.e. significant apoptosis in HeLa cells vs. autophagy in SiHa cells. We further show opposing outcomes upon inhibition of autophagy in both of these cell lines i.e. enhanced apoptosis-inducing potential of ONC201 against SiHa cells and restrained apoptotic response in the case of HeLa cells. Knockdown studies using siRNA suggest that the autophagy modulation by ONC201 in HeLa cells is independent of its well-known target CLPP which is widely reported to play a role in cytoprotective autophagy. This is the first report on the ability of ONC201 to modulate the autophagy pathway in cancer cells.

articles.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
articles.authors: Vahab N, He E, Sarwar T et al.
articles.abstract: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM (Length-efficient sUbword-based Nucleic Acid Foundation Model), an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling of long RNA transcripts. We systematically evaluate tokenization strategies and vocabulary sizes to investigate the trade-offs between sequence compression, representation granularity, computational efficiency, and downstream performance. Across multiple RNA prediction tasks, including transcript classification, subcellular localization, and RNA-protein interaction prediction, LUNA-FM achieved competitive performance compared with existing RNA FMs while reducing effective input length and fine-tuning cost. We also found that frequency-based subword tokenization generally produced more stable and effective representations than likelihood-based approaches, although the optimal vocabulary size remained task dependent. Training-set motif discovery identified candidate motifs enriched relative to matched low-attribution and dinucleotide-shuffled controls of preeclampsia-associated lncRNAs. Overall, our findings highlight the task-dependent effects of subword tokenization and vocabulary size, extend RNA FM evaluation to longer transcript inputs, and establish LUNA-FM as a competitive model with favourable recorded fine-tuning times.

articles.title: Technical difficulty of levonorgestrel 52-mg intrauterine device placement and six-month clinical outcomes among women with and without isthmocele: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception
articles.ta: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
articles.authors: Laporte M, Marcelino AC, Juliato CRT et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare pain and difficulty during levonorgestrel 52-mg intrauterine device (LNG 52-mg IUD) insertion in women with and without isthmocele and, secondarily, to assess changes in uterine bleeding, and chronic pelvic pain six months after insertion.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Our prospective study was conducted at the Universidade Estadual de Campinas, Brazil. Women aged 18-43 years with at least one caesarean delivery ≥6 months previously, with or without ultrasound-diagnosed isthmocele, were included. Insertion pain, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain were assessed using a 100-mm visual analogue scale (VAS). We included 260 women (103 with and 157 without isthmocele), providing 80% power at α = 0.05 to detect differences in insertion outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with insertion difficulty and severe pain.
RESULTS: Insertion success was similar in women with and without isthmocele (99.0% vs. 98.7%; p = 1.000), as were pain intensity (p = 0.80) and insertion difficulty (p = 0.19). Of 224 women reporting at least one symptom at baseline, 89 (39.7%) had isthmocele and 135 (60.3%) did not. At six months, both groups showed significant reductions in heavy menstrual bleeding, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain (all p < 0.001). Prolonged menstrual bleeding (≥8 days) decreased significantly among women with isthmocele; however, the group-by-time interaction was not significant (p = 0.21).
CONCLUSION: Isthmocele was not associated with greater insertion pain or difficulty. Six months after LNG 52-mg IUD insertion, both groups showed improvements in heavy menstrual bleeding, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain.
SHORT CONDENSATION: Isthmocele was not associated with greater insertion pain or difficulty of the LNG 52-mg IUD. Six months after IUD insertion, both groups showed improvements in heavy menstrual bleeding, menstrual pain, and chronic pelvic pain.

articles.title: Plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA sequencing identifies clinically unsuspected cases of Toxoplasma gondii infection in immunocompromised patients: a single-centre experience.
articles.authors: Goren LR, Lehman AC, Drozdov D et al.
articles.abstract: Toxoplasmosis can be challenging to diagnose, particularly in immunocompromised patients with nonspecific clinical presentations. We present a retrospective, single-centre case series of eight Toxoplasma gondii infections identified by plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing in allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Nested within a larger cohort evaluating cfDNA utilization, this case series highlights a positive clinical impact of cfDNA testing in 5 out of 8 (62.5%) patients, including earlier diagnosis and changes in clinical management. These findings illustrate the potential utility of plasma cfDNA sequencing as a complement to conventional diagnostics across diverse clinical presentations of toxoplasmosis.

articles.title: "You're not necessarily pregnant": Confusion about emergency contraception.
articles.authors: Mueller J, VandeVusse A, Lindberg LD
articles.abstract: Misconceptions about what emergency contraception does are common and have resulted in policy efforts to restrict access. Understanding the beliefs and reasoning behind people's uncertainty and lack of knowledge about emergency contraception helps shed light on key misconceptions and how advocates, providers, and researchers can improve clarity. We conducted a secondary analysis using previously collected qualitative data from card sort and vignette activities focused on scenarios related to emergency contraception and if participants considered these scenarios abortions (N = 64). We identified three major themes related to participants' classification of emergency contraception: uncertainty and pregnancy liminality; timing and mechanism of action; and the role of intention and overlap with medication abortion. Our study demonstrates that people lack a consistent, coherent understanding of what emergency contraception does, which has implications for contraceptive access and service provision. Furthermore, these misconceptions can become politicized and undergird the rationale for restrictions on sexual and reproductive health care.

articles.title: Low platelets, high stakes: pregnancy after a diagnosis of immune thrombocytopenia.
articles.authors: Beltrami-Moreira M, Masias C
articles.abstract: Many patients live with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) during their reproductive years and may desire to become pregnant or may unexpectedly become pregnant. Although patients should be educated about potential risks to both the mother and child in such cases, a healthy pregnancy with good outcomes is still possible. In this review, we address topics spanning the pregnancy journey from preconception through the postdelivery period for patients with ITP. We recommend that reproductive plans be addressed proactively to allow for ITP treatment optimization for pregnancy. This may involve discontinuation of therapies with known fetal toxicity risks, such as fostamatinib, determining the timing of rituximab use or splenectomy, and adjusting for chronic therapies, such as thrombopoietin receptor agonists. The risk of bleeding with ITP is not higher during pregnancy, but thrombocytopenia often requires treatment to minimize delivery-related hemorrhagic risk or allow neuraxial anesthesia. Prednisone and IV immunoglobulin are effective for these purposes in most patients. There is evolving evidence to support the role of rituximab and romiplostim. We lack biomarkers to predict the severity of thrombocytopenia in both mothers and fetuses/neonates and to predict response to treatment. Similarly, there are limited data on patient-reported outcomes and mental health needs among patients who are pregnant and caring for their infant while managing their ITP. Care standardization and harmonization among different specialists for pregnant patients with ITP remains an unmet need.

articles.title: Screening performance and optimal threshold of the American Diabetes Association Diabetes Risk Score in a large multistate Sudanese population: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Noor SK, Ali HSAHM, Eldouma MYM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Validated non-invasive risk stratification tools can support diabetes prevention in resource-constrained settings. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) Diabetes Risk Score is widely used but has not been rigorously evaluated in sub-Saharan African populations. This study assessed the screening utility and optimal score threshold of the ADA Diabetes Risk Score in the population in Sudan.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, population-based study was conducted in 2023 across eight Sudanese states, using multistage cluster random sampling from 32 community health centres. Sudanese adult ≥18 years completed the self-administered ADA Diabetes Risk Test questionnaire (7-item, maximum score 10). Among the 1855 eligible participants, 203 with a prior physician diagnosis of diabetes were retained as the reference group for diagnostic performance analysis. Associations were evaluated using χ² tests and multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic analysis with Youden index optimisation was used to derive the optimal score threshold. All inferential analyses were performed using R (V.4.4.3).
RESULTS: Among participants (64.3% female; 80.3% aged <40 years), 10.8% (n=200) were classified as high-risk by the standard ADA threshold (score ≥5). Using physician-diagnosed diabetes (n=203) as the reference, the Youden-optimal threshold of 3.5 achieved sensitivity 59.6% (95% CI 52.2% to 66.0%) and specificity 79.7% (95% CI 77.8% to 81.5%), with area under the curve 0.744 (95% CI 0.707 to 0.781, p<0.001). The overall number needed to screen was 9.3, ranging from 43.8 in adults aged <40 years to 1.1 in those aged >60 years. On multivariable logistic regression, hyperlipidaemia (OR: 5.33, 95% CI 3.43 to 8.17) and gestational diabetes (OR: 4.50, 95% CI 1.62 to 11.8) were the strongest independent predictors of high-risk ADA classification.
CONCLUSION: The ADA Diabetes Risk Score demonstrated moderate screening utility in this Sudanese population. A threshold of 3.5 may improve sensitivity for identifying at-risk individuals compared to the standard cut-off of ≥5. These findings are hypothesis-generating; external validation against biochemical endpoints is required before clinical adoption.

articles.title: MRPL47 as a mitochondrial biomarker for early detection and therapeutic response in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Pradeep M, Kadamberi IP, George J et al.
articles.abstract: The MRPL47 (mitochondrial ribosomal protein large subunit 47) gene in chromosome 3q26 encodes a protein that is part of the large subunit of the mitochondrial ribosome. We observed that MRPL47 is frequently amplified and overexpressed in ovarian cancer samples. Importantly, increased expression of MRPL47 mRNA is associated with high levels of MRPL47 protein in patients with ovarian cancer. High expression of MRPL47 is also associated with poor overall and recurrence-free survival of patients with ovarian cancer. Gene set enrichment analysis and target-specific knockdown assays revealed that the cMYC transcription factor regulates MRPL47 expression. Furthermore, MRPL47 was identified at very high levels in the plasma samples of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer compared to those of healthy volunteers. MRPL47 was also associated with cisplatin resistance, whereas its expression predicted sensitivity to cisplatin therapy. Notably, MRPL47 improved metabolic fitness in cancer cells by promoting mitochondrial translation, cellular respiration, and glycolysis. Taken together, our results demonstrate that MRPL47 can serve as a diagnostic biomarker for ovarian cancer and potentially for other cancers that exhibit 3q26 locus chromosomal amplification.

articles.title: Sepsis-related hospitalisation risk in preterm-born and term-born children and adolescents: a nationwide registry study.
articles.authors: Valand J, Nilsen SM, Asheim A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The burden of severe infections in children remains inadequately characterised. Preterm birth is a risk factor for neonatal sepsis, but whether this risk persists beyond the neonatal period is unclear. We examined the risk of sepsis-related hospitalisation during childhood and adolescence in term-born and preterm-born children.
METHODS: Norwegian nationwide birth registry data (Jan 1, 1992-Dec 31, 2021) were linked with hospital discharge data (Jan 1, 2008-Dec 31, 2021). Using a standardised definition, sepsis-related hospitalisations were classified as explicit (sepsis diagnosis code) or implicit (infection plus organ dysfunction diagnosis codes).
