We estimated rate ratios (RRs) using adjusted negative binomial regression and sibling-controlled odds ratios (ORs) using conditional logistic regression by completed weeks of gestation (23-27, 28-31, 32-33, 34-36, 37-38, and 39-41 weeks), stratified by age (3-11 months, 1-5 years, and 6-15 years).
FINDINGS: Following 1,672,009 births, 13,158 sepsis episodes were available in the data. Hospitalisation rates for sepsis-related admissions were highest at ages 3-11 months (84.4 per 1000 person-years [95% CI 62.2-106.7] for 23-27 weeks gestation and 3.2 per 1000 person-years [95% CI 3.0-3.4] for 39-41 weeks gestation). Compared with term-born children, rates of sepsis-related hospitalisations increased by lower gestational age groups in both population and sibling analyses. Comparing extremely preterm versus term-born children, RRs were 26.5 (95% CI 20.2-34.7) at ages 3-11 months, 14.8 (11.2-19.6) at ages 1-5 years, and 6.7 (3.9-11.4) at ages 6-15 years. Sibling ORs were 24.9 (10.8-57.4), 29.7 (11.3-77.8), and 3.1 (1.2-8.0), respectively.
INTERPRETATION: Lower gestational age was robustly associated with an increased risk of sepsis-related hospitalisation throughout childhood and adolescence, supporting that low gestational age at birth should be recognised as a persistent risk factor for severe infections beyond the neonatal period.
FUNDING: The Regional Cooperation Body for Education, Research and Innovation between the Central Norway Regional Health Authority (Helse Midt-Norge RHF) and the universities and university colleges in the region (phd funding for Jonas Valand) and the joint research committee of St. Olavs University Hospital and Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (grant no. 2024-38542).

articles.title: Iron phenotypes and reports of menses, pregnancies, and live births in females with HFE p.C282Y homozygosity and HFE wt/wt: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Barton JC, Barton JC, Acton RT
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare iron phenotypes and questionnaire reports about menses, pregnancies, and live births in females with HFE p.C282Y (rs1800562) homozygosity (Y/Y) and HFE wt/wt (absence of p.C282Y and p.H63D (rs1799945) (wt/wt)).
METHODS: We compared post-screening iron phenotypes and questionnaire reports of self-identified non-Hispanic white females aged ≥25 y in a cross-sectional study.
RESULTS: There were 426 females (153 Y/Y, 273 wt/wt). Median ages were 50 y (25, 86) and 55 y (25, 92), respectively (p=0.0019). Median transferrin saturation, median serum ferritin, and provisional iron overload prevalence were greater in Y/Y (p ≤0.0001, each comparison). Prevalences of documented iron overload (3.3% Y/Y vs. 0.7% wt/wt), iron overload-related disease (2.0% vs. 0.4%, respectively), and iron deficiency (3.9% vs. 2.6%, respectively) did not differ significantly. Median ages at menarche (13 y Y/Y vs. 13 y wt/wt) and menopause (50 y vs. 49 y, respectively) did not differ significantly. Reports of "in-between bleeding?" (24.2% Y/Y vs. 25.2% wt/wt), "early stopping of periods?" (11.8% vs. 13.9%, respectively), and "had a hysterectomy?" (30.1% vs. 35.9%, respectively) were not significantly different. Respective percentage pairs of females with Y/Y and wt/wt who reported 0, 1, 2, 3, or ≥4 pregnancies (or live births) did not differ significantly. Live births/pregnancies were 287/363 (79.1%, Y/Y) and 534/673 (79.3%, wt/wt) (p=0.7549).
CONCLUSION: Median transferrin saturation, median serum ferritin, and provisional iron overload prevalence are greater in females with HFE p.C282Y homozygosity than those with HFE wt/wt, although iron deficiency prevalence and reports of menses, pregnancies, and live births are similar.

articles.title: Endometrial Cavity Fluid Before Frozen Embryo Transfer: A Critical Review of Prognostic Significance and Evidence for Cycle Cancellation.
articles.authors: Ma Y, Fu J
articles.abstract: Endometrial cavity fluid during preparation for frozen embryo transfer creates uncertainty about proceeding, reassessing, or deferring treatment. This critical narrative review examines how assessment timing, fluid trajectory, and underlying pathology influence prognosis and the interpretation of cancellation studies. Focused searches were updated through October 20, 2026; this was not a systematic review or meta-analysis. In a cohort of 1034 frozen blastocyst transfers, live birth rates after fluid resolution and without fluid were 35.2% and 34.2%, respectively (adjusted risk ratio 1.00, 95% confidence interval 0.70-1.50). In 4308 single euploid transfers, fluid persisting at the decision for progesterone initiation or ovulation triggering was associated with a lower live birth rate than no fluid (38.3% vs 58.5%; adjusted odds ratio 0.50, 95% confidence interval 0.28-0.88). These assessments are not interchangeable with transfer-day fluid. Subsequent-transfer analyses after cancellation exclude patients who never reach another transfer and cannot establish a cumulative live birth benefit. Deferral can add visits, costs, and distress; any effect on treatment discontinuation or cumulative live birth remains unquantified specifically for cavity fluid. A practical assessment should distinguish resolved fluid, diagnosed tubal or uterine pathology, and persistent unexplained collections. Cause-specific treatment has a different evidence base from empirical aspiration or hormonal changes. No direct randomized comparison of proceeding with vs canceling frozen embryo transfer was identified. Multicenter trials should evaluate cumulative live birth and time to live birth from a common decision point, retaining all assigned patients.

articles.title: Spatial Multi-Omics Integration with Mass Spectrometry Imaging: Decoding Metabolic Landscapes and Disease Mechanisms.
articles.authors: Bu X, Wang L
articles.abstract: Spatial multi-omics links molecular measurements to tissue architecture, but integrating spatial transcriptomics with mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because the modalities differ in sampling unit, spatial resolution, data structure, and molecular-identification certainty. This review synthesizes the enabling technologies and presents an evidence-calibrated workflow spanning tissue acquisition, spatial registration, modality-specific preprocessing, cross-modal annotation, mechanistic modeling, and orthogonal validation. We examine how MSI can complement single-cell and spatial transcriptomic or proteomic measurements in studies of tumor-host interfaces, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, adipose-tissue organization, and decidualization at the maternal-fetal interface. Across these applications, spatial colocalization is most informative when annotation confidence is reported and key chemical identities are validated, registration error is quantified, and candidate cell-metabolite relationships are tested by isotope tracing or perturbation. We further discuss molecular ambiguity, resolution-sensitivity-throughput trade-offs, 3-dimensional reconstruction, interlaboratory reproducibility, and requirements for clinical translation. The central conclusion is that spatial multi-omics is best used to formulate anatomically explicit, falsifiable hypotheses rather than to infer causality from aligned maps alone.

articles.title: Integrating hormonal analyses into the development of hormonal male contraception: geographic centre as a determinant of individual response.
articles.authors: Zitzmann M, Schlatt S, Nieschlag E et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Are the geographic recruitment centre and dynamic sex-steroid profiles, particularly for dihydrotestosterone, associated with inter-individual differences in libido and mood-related adverse events during hormonal male contraception?
SUMMARY ANSWER: In this multinational analysis of the WHO testosterone undecanoate/norethisterone (TU/NETE) enanthate trial, geographic cluster was associated with distinct androgenic profiles and clinical responses; lower dihydrotestosterone exposure emerged as a consistent predictor of decreased libido and mood-related adverse events.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Combined testosterone-progestin regimens can suppress spermatogenesis effectively, but the WHO TU/NETE trial was discontinued prematurely because of mood-related adverse events despite high contraceptive efficacy. The endocrine mechanisms underlying these adverse effects remain incompletely understood.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: This secondary analysis used serial hormone and adverse-event data from the multinational WHO/CONRAD trial, which enrolled 320 men. However, 255 participants had serum samples available for centralized steroid analysis and constituted the present analytical cohort, as the samples from Jakarta, Indonesia (65 subjects) were not sent to the Central Laboratory.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Healthy male participants were recruited across European/Australian, South American, and Asian centres and grouped into geographic clusters. Serum testosterone, calculated free testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, estradiol, and norethisterone were analysed centrally by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Longitudinal mixed-effects models and time-to-event analyses were used to evaluate associations between hormone trajectories, geographic cluster, age, libido changes, and mood disorders.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Marked cluster-dependent heterogeneity was observed. Participants from Chile showed higher total and free testosterone and persistently higher dihydrotestosterone concentrations over time, accompanied by a higher incidence of increased libido. Participants from India showed lower dihydrotestosterone exposure and higher norethisterone concentrations and no libido and mood changes. European/Australian participants showed comparatively lower dihydrotestosterone concentrations and the highest cumulative incidence of mood disorders. Declining dihydrotestosterone concentrations were associated with decreased libido…

articles.title: SGLT2 inhibitors for peripartum cardiomyopathy: A call for a dedicated trial.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.authors: Acharya B
articles.abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) accounts for more than 60% of pregnancy-related cardiogenic shock in the United States, yet specific evidence-based therapies remain limited. Despite guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, left ventricular ejection fraction recovery is incomplete in up to 50% of patients, and mortality reaches 20% in high-risk populations. A recent propensity-matched cohort of 10,907 PPCM patients found that sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use was associated with reduced all-cause mortality (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.25-0.92), heart failure exacerbation (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.76-0.90), and all-cause re-hospitalization (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.93), corroborated by two independent case reports showing rapid left ventricular ejection fraction recovery on empagliflozin-containing regimens. However, residual confounding, notably a significant baseline left ventricular ejection fraction imbalance despite matching (35.0% vs. 45.0%; P < 0.01) and unreported bromocriptine use, limits causal inference. The convergence of real-world evidence, case reports, and mechanistic plausibility supports early SGLT2i consideration in appropriately selected PPCM patients. A dedicated randomized controlled trial, stratified by disease severity, lactation status, and race, and designed with careful ethical consideration, is now scientifically justified and ethically imperative.

articles.title: Biologic therapies for atopic diseases during pregnancy: A World Allergy Organization survey.
articles.authors: Chiarella SE, Novoa-Caicedo I, Jenkins SM et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Biologic therapies are an increasingly important treatment option for atopic diseases, which commonly affect women of reproductive age. However, global barriers to prescribing biologic therapies to pregnant patients remain poorly understood.
METHODS: The World Allergy Organization (WAO) Junior Members Steering Group conducted a global, web-based survey of healthcare professionals to evaluate prescribing patterns and barriers to the use of biologic therapies for atopic diseases during pregnancy.
RESULTS: From 322 total participants representing 71 countries, 77 of 314 (24.5%) reported prescribing biologic therapies for atopic diseases during pregnancy. The most frequently prescribed biologic therapies during pregnancy were omalizumab (79.2%) and dupilumab (32.5%), followed by benralizumab (7.8%), mepolizumab (7.8%), tralokinumab (3.9%), tezepelumab (2.6%), and reslizumab (1.3%). Twenty-three respondents encountered barriers to prescribing biologic therapies to pregnant patients, including patients' concerns about the impact on pregnancy (82.6%), adverse reactions (47.8%), difficulty securing insurance coverage (13.0%), and high patient costs (8.7%). Reported biologic therapies discontinued due to pregnancy included dupilumab (39.1%), mepolizumab (26.1%), omalizumab (26.1%), and benralizumab (13.0%). Twelve of the 23 healthcare professionals who discontinued biologic therapies reported that their pregnant patients experienced worsening symptoms after stopping. Seven respondents (9.9%) reported adverse maternal or fetal outcomes in pregnant patients receiving biologic treatment for atopic diseases, including allergic/immune disorders (3), congenital defects (2), miscarriage (1), and preeclampsia (1). Only 42.3% of respondents who prescribed biologics to pregnant patients reported enrolling these patients in a pregnancy registry.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant barriers limit the prescriptions of biologic therapies for atopic diseases during pregnancy. Multidisciplinary collaboration among clinicians, researchers, and the pharmaceutical industry is essential for developing strategies to overcome these barriers and improve access to biologic therapy for pregnant patients.

articles.title: Beyond geographic access: Rural disparities in gynecologic oncology across the care continuum.
articles.authors: Schultz B, Hutchcraft ML
articles.abstract: Rural patients in the United States face disproportionate gynecologic cancer mortality compared to urban patients, driven by overlapping geographic, socioeconomic, and structural barriers that vary across cancer types and the care continuum. This review synthesizes the literature on rural disparities in cervical, endometrial, and ovarian cancers from prevention through survivorship. Rurality is defined variably across the literature, most commonly using government classification systems such as Rural-Urban Continuum Codes or Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Rural women experience lower Human Papillomavirus vaccination rates and reduced uptake of guideline-concordant cervical cancer screening, higher rates of late-stage ovarian cancer diagnosis, and delayed endometrial cancer diagnosis. Even when rural patients access subspecialist care, treatment quality gaps persist, including higher rates of open surgical staging for endometrial cancer and reduced access to brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer. Survival disparities remain even among rural patients treated at tertiary centers with subspecialist involvement, underscoring that geographic access alone is insufficient. Insurance status, health literacy, financial hardship, and limited social support compound these barriers throughout the continuum. Interventions including telehealth, shared care models, community-based navigation, and Medicaid expansion show promise but remain incompletely evaluated in gynecologic oncology. Most existing literature documents disparities without evaluating interventions, and variability in how rurality is defined limits generalizability. Rural women deserve more than documentation of the disparities they face, and closing these gaps will require both coordinated action across clinical, institutional, and policy levels and a stronger evidence base for targeted interventions.

articles.title: Pelvic floor knowledge and unhealthy habits related in female athletes: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Bosch-Donate E, Vico-Moreno E, Romero-Franco N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe pelvic floor (PF)-related knowledge and unhealthy habits among female athletes, and to examine their associations with PF dysfunction (PFD) symptoms, sports characteristics, academic level and help seeking attitudes.
METHODS: A total of 538 female athletes (36.7 ± 11.3 years) completed an anonymous online questionnaire covering age, academic level, sports experience, unhealthy PF-related habits, PFD symptoms, professional healthcare-seeking attitude and knowledge about urinary incontinence (UI), anorectal incontinence (ARI), pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and female sexual dysfunction (FSD). Adequate knowledge was considered as ≥70% correct responses.
RESULTS: Female athletes demonstrated adequate knowledge regarding UI, ARI and POP, but insufficient knowledge about FSD (52.6%). Several PFD symptoms were associated with lower knowledge levels and a higher number of unhealthy habits compared with athletes without these symptoms (p<0.05). Younger athletes showed lower knowledge about ARI (p=0.033) and POP (p=0.003), while older athletes showed lower knowledge about FSD (p<0.001). Athletes who rejected professional healthcare showed lower knowledge across all PFD domains (p<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Female athletes reporting symptoms suggestive of PFD showed lower levels of knowledge and a higher number of unhealthy PF habits compared with those without symptoms. Although athletes generally demonstrated an appropriate level of knowledge regarding PFD, important gaps were observed in the FSD domain and in unhealthy toileting and sport-related habits, particularly among athletes without university studies. Differences in knowledge were also observed according to age and healthcare-seeking attitudes, highlighting areas that may be considered in future educational initiatives.

articles.title: Distinct Associated Factors for Numerical and Structural Chromosomal Abnormalities in Products of Conception Following IVF/ICSI.
articles.authors: Wenxiu Z, Jingjing Z, Yujie Z et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the factors associated with different types of embryonic chromosomal abnormalities in miscarried tissues from patients undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (IVF/ICSI), with particular attention to whether maternal, paternal, and treatment-related factors are differentially associated with numerical and structural abnormalities.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 670 patients with spontaneous abortion after IVF/ICSI. Chromosomal abnormalities were detected by copy number variation sequencing combined with short tandem repeat analysis. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Chromosomal abnormalities were detected in 430/670 cases (64.18%). Multivariate analysis showed that maternal age (OR = 1.165, p < 0.001), high sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI) (OR = 1.649, 95% CI: 1.120-2.427, p = 0.011), maternal body mass index (BMI) (OR = 0.955, 95% CI: 0.915-0.997, p = 0.036), and blastocyst transfer (OR = 0.842, 95% CI: 0.710-0.999, p = 0.049) were independently associated with overall chromosomal abnormalities. In subtype analysis, maternal age and high sperm DFI were associated with numerical abnormalities, whereas gestational age and frozen embryo transfer were associated with structural abnormalities.
CONCLUSIONS: In separate models, maternal age and sperm DFI were associated with numerical abnormalities, whereas gestational age and cycle type were associated with structural abnormalities. However, in the direct comparison between subtypes, only gestational age, gonadotropin duration, and cycle type significantly distinguished structural from numerical abnormalities.

articles.title: Tuberculous Salpingo-Oophoritis Mimicking Ovarian Malignancy: A Case Report of a Diagnostic Dilemma.
articles.authors: Habte YM, Kebede HD, Tachibel KG et al.
articles.abstract: Female genital tuberculosis (FGTB) is an uncommon form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis that poses a significant diagnostic challenge because it frequently mimics ovarian malignancy clinically, radiologically, and biochemically. We report the case of a 34-year-old multiparous woman who presented 66 days after cesarean delivery with progressive lower abdominal pain and a tender pelvic mass. Pelvic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a complex left adnexal mass suspicious for ovarian malignancy, while serum CA-125 was elevated, further reinforcing the presumptive diagnosis. The patient subsequently underwent exploratory laparotomy with left salpingo-oophorectomy. Histopathological examination revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid granulomas, Langhans giant cells, and caseous necrosis, confirming tuberculous salpingo-oophoritis without evidence of malignancy. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient completed a standard 6-month anti-tuberculosis regimen with complete clinical recovery and progressive normalization of CA-125 levels during follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic dilemma posed by FGTB, particularly in tuberculosis-endemic regions where the disease may closely resemble ovarian cancer. Elevated CA-125 should therefore be interpreted cautiously in premenopausal women, as it is a nonspecific marker that may also reflect benign inflammatory conditions. A high index of suspicion for FGTB, coupled with careful integration of clinical, radiological, and epidemiological findings into preoperative decision-making, is essential to facilitate timely diagnosis, appropriate management, prompt initiation of anti-tuberculosis therapy, and avoidance of unnecessary extensive surgical intervention while minimizing long-term reproductive morbidity.

articles.title: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus (Hakim's syndrome): A cerebrovascular disorder. The contributions of Salomón Hakim (1922-2011).
articles.authors: Román GC, Jackson RE, Pardo-Turriago R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In 1957, Salomón Hakim MD (1922-2011), a Colombian neurosurgeon, discovered normal-pressure hydrocephalus (NPH), a cerebrovascular disorder that involves cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, cerebral arterial and venous blood flow, as well as the glymphatic circulation.
METHODS: We review the contributions of Hakim beginning with the initial 7 cases of NPH he studied and treated in Bogotá, Colombia, and the original articles published in 1965 in association with colleagues from neurology, neuropathology, and neurosurgery at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School in Boston, USA. We present Hakim's experimental studies on the pathophysiology of NPH that led him to successfully design CSF shunting valves for the surgical treatment of NPH.
RESULTS: The epidemiological measurement of NPH is affected by underdiagnosis despite the typical clinical features centered on ventriculomegaly and Hakim's triad of abnormal gait, urinary incontinence and cognitive decline. Earlier difficulties in visualizing the cerebral ventricles were solved by computerized tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain images, particularly after frequent falls in the elderly, allowing the quantification of the ventriculomegaly by measuring the Evans index, the callosal angle and the ALVI index. The recent introduction of Arterial Spin-Labeled Magnetic Resonance Imaging (ASL-MRI) to quantify cerebral blood flow (CBF) after the CSF tap test has simplified the diagnosis of NPH. Denying the existence of NPH was based on the lack of randomized, placebo-controlled trials but this has been answered by international trials demonstrating the benefit of CSF shunting.
INTERPRETATION: We confirm the existence of NPH-the clinical syndrome discovered by Salomón Hakim-a curable cerebrovascular disorder, grossly underdiagnosed, and we emphasize the overall poor prognosis of the untreated NPH patients in contrast with the usual return to normal life resulting from surgical treatment. Given the extensive and valuable contributions of Salomón Hakim to the discovery, pathogenesis, clinical and surgical treatment of this neurological condition, 70 years after his discovery we propose renaming idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus as Hakim's syndrome.

articles.title: A cross-sectional study of contraception and abortion utilization among female sex workers in the democratic Republic of Congo, Kenya, and Nigeria: preferences, access, and barriers.
articles.authors: Moss RA, Danel I, Kamau G et al.
articles.abstract: Female sex workers (FSW) report high rates of unintended pregnancy and unmet need for contraception. Using convenience sampling, this cross-sectional study included 853 FSW recruited from eight cities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Kenya, and Nigeria, where proportionate mortality from unsafe abortion is high. The study examined contraceptive prevalence, preferences, access, and barriers, and abortion history, methods and complications. Non-condom modern contraceptive prevalence was higher among FSW in Kenya (73.2%) than in the DRC (40.8%) and Nigeria (26.9%). A greater proportion of FSW in Kenya reported no abortion in the past five years (82.8%) compared with the DRC (54.0%) and Nigeria (33.9%). Among those reporting abortion, the mean number was lower in Kenya (1.5) than in the DRC (1.7) and Nigeria (2.2). Cost was a common barrier to accessing contraceptives in the DRC and Nigeria (approximately one-third of respondents) but less common in Kenya (9%). Contraceptive preferences differed. The majority of FSW in Kenya preferred long-acting reversible contraception (LARC). Although the majority of FSW in the DRC and Nigeria preferred condoms, client dynamics in criminalized settings may limit consistent condom use making them ineffective. Improving access to free or affordable non-condom modern contraceptives, particularly LARC, is critical to reducing unintended pregnancies and preventing morbidity and mortality from unsafe abortion among FSW. Increased education and counseling on LARC methods may further support uptake.

articles.title: The developing fetal immune landscape and congenital viral infection.
articles.authors: Chima SC, Sun SJ, Duell T et al.
articles.abstract: Fetal development is a complex process that can lead to adverse health consequences when impaired, such as congenital anomalies, fetal growth restriction, preterm birth, and stillbirth. Although there is a well-developed literature on the timing of adaptive immune cell appearance in the fetus, comparatively little is known about the ontogeny and functional maturation of the innate immune system over gestation. This knowledge gap limits our understanding of how intrauterine infections influence fetal development and contribute to adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Thus, the goal of this review is to summarize existing knowledge of the ontogeny of the fetal adaptive and innate immune systems throughout gestation, and how they are impacted by infection. We examine the emergence of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, while highlighting changes in immune lineages across the fetal brain, liver, thymus, bone marrow, spleen, and placenta, which play critical roles in immune competency and tolerance. The role of innate immunity in immunocompetence and pathogen responses is highlighted when known. Finally, we address how vertically transmitted and teratogenic viral infections disrupt normal immune and tissue development. Collectively, these studies demonstrate the dynamic, tissue-specific immune landscape that evolves throughout gestation.

articles.title: Reproductive Implications of a Rare Paternal Dicentric Rearrangement 45,XY,dic(5;13)(p15;p12) in an IVF Cycle With Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Structural Rearrangements: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Do VN, Tran HP, Van Nguyen T et al.
articles.abstract: This case highlights the counseling challenges associated with a rare paternal dicentric rearrangement. PGT-SR identified only one transferable balanced/normal copy-number profile among four biopsied blastocysts, underscoring the need to discuss the possibility of few or no transferable embryos and the limitations of PGT-SR.

articles.title: Circulating tumor DNA in Hodgkin lymphoma: biological classification, molecular residual disease, and integration with PET response.
articles.authors: Bednarek M, Komossa M, Bidzińska J
articles.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and its tumor-derived fraction, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), enable non-invasive tumor genotyping, longitudinal disease monitoring, and molecular residual disease (MRD) assessment. Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is particularly suitable for ctDNA-based analysis because malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells usually constitute only a small fraction of the tumor mass, whereas plasma may contain a strong tumor-derived DNA signal. This narrative review summarizes the potential applications of cfDNA-based ctDNA analysis in hematologic malignancies, with a focused emphasis on cHL. We discuss pre-analytical and analytical requirements, including plasma processing, tumor-informed and tumor-naive sequencing, error suppression, droplet digital PCR, and control for clonal hematopoiesis. We then synthesize evidence for ctDNA as a dual-readout biomarker: a baseline tool for non-invasive biological classification and a dynamic measure of molecular response. Published studies identify cHL genomic subtypes, associations with the tumor microenvironment, and prognostic information complementary to PET and conventional risk factors. Age-specific evidence is uneven, and most studies demonstrate analytical feasibility or prognosis rather than benefit from a ctDNA-triggered intervention. ctDNA-MRD should complement FDG-PET/CT; it cannot localize disease or currently replace established staging and response criteria. Routine implementation will require harmonized sample handling, validated assays and reporting thresholds, external quality assessment, and prospective trials demonstrating that ctDNA-guided treatment improves disease control, toxicity, or quality of life.

articles.title: Autologous platelet-rich gel activated by calcium gluconate for postoperative endometrial repair in moderate-to-severe intrauterine adhesion: a retrospective preliminary evaluation of efficacy.
articles.authors: Li Y, Han Y, Cao J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the effect of calcium gluconate-activated autologous platelet-rich gel (APG) on endometrial repair in patients with moderate-to-severe intrauterine adhesion (IUA).
METHODS: In this study, 60 patients with moderate-to-severe IUA who were undergoing hysteroscopic transcervical resection of adhesion surgery were recruited and grouped based on whether they underwent APG treatment (APG group) or not (non-APG group; n = 30 each). Hysteroscopy examination and transvaginal ultrasonography were performed after surgery to evaluate adhesion recurrence and endometrial thickness. Simultaneously, patients self-recorded the menstrual volume using a menstrual diary.
RESULTS: There was no significant difference in baseline characteristics, preoperative uterine adhesion grade, endometrial thickness, or menstrual pattern between the APG and non-APG groups (p > 0.05). After treatment, compared with the non-APG group, the postoperative adhesion recurrence rate (13.3% vs. 36.7%) and adhesion grades (75% mild and 25% moderate vs. 72.7% mild and 27.3% moderate) were significantly decreased in the APG group (p = 0.039). The endometrium thickness in the APG group was greater than that in the non-APG group (6.29 ± 0.24 mm vs. 5.10 ± 0.16 mm, p = 0.000), and the endometrial thickness increment was substantially higher in the APG group than that in the non-APG group (2.82 ± 0.17 mm vs. 1.84 ± 0.12 mm, p = 0.000). Furthermore, more participants in the APG group experienced significant recovery in menstrual volume at 3 months after surgery (p = 0.031), and participants from the APG group maintained improved menstrual volume 6 months after surgery (p = 0.029). Multivariate analysis confirmed the beneficial effect of APG in promoting endometrial repair.
CONCLUSION: Calcium gluconate-activated autologous platelet-rich gel has the potential to reduce postoperative recurrence and improve menstrual properties in patients with moderate-to-severe IUA.

articles.title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation versus sham stimulation and dexamethasone versus amisulpride for preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic gynecologic surgery: protocol for a randomized 2 × 2 factorial trial.
articles.authors: Li Y, Zhang J, Xu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains a common complication after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Although multimodal prophylaxis is recommended, clinical practice still relies largely on pharmacologic interventions. Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) at the P6 acupoint may have potential benefit for PONV prevention. However, its effectiveness when incorporated into pharmacologic prophylaxis, and whether its effect varies according to the antiemetic used, remain unclear. This trial aims to evaluate the effect of P6-TEAS on PONV prevention in patients receiving dexamethasone or amisulpride.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial will enroll 212 women undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive one of four treatment combinations: TEAS plus dexamethasone, TEAS plus amisulpride, sham stimulation plus dexamethasone, or sham stimulation plus amisulpride. TEAS or sham stimulation will be delivered at the P6 acupoint in two 1-h sessions, before surgery and at 24 h after surgery. The primary outcome will be the incidence of PONV within 48 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include PONV-related symptoms and severity, use of rescue antiemetics, opioid consumption, pain scores, recovery milestones, patient satisfaction, QoR-15 scores, and length of hospital stay. Safety outcomes will include adverse events related to TEAS or study drugs and perioperative hemodynamic events requiring treatment.
DISCUSSION: This trial will evaluate P6-TEAS versus sham stimulation as the primary comparison and provide exploratory estimates for the dexamethasone-versus-amisulpride comparison and the TEAS-by-drug interaction. The findings may inform integrated prevention strategies for PONV after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07631910, identifier NCT07631910.

articles.title: Risk factors for surgical site infection in women undergoing hysterectomy for gynecological cancers: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Tang L, Yang M, Hu J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hysterectomy is a common surgery performed in women. Most patients with gynecological cancers (GCs) undergo hysterectomy along with extensive resection and are prone to surgical site infections (SSIs). However, the risk factors for SSIs in this population remain unclear. This study focuses on this issue.
METHODS: Patients who underwent hysterectomy for GCs between January 2021 and December 2025 were selected from the electronic medical records of a single institution. The patients were classified into the non-SSI and SSI groups based on the occurrence of SSIs. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to evaluate risk factors among patient demographics and clinical characteristics.
RESULTS: In total, 558 patients were included in this study. The non-SSI and SSI groups included 468 and 90 patients, respectively. Univariate analysis indicated significant differences in six factors: diabetes mellitus (DM), intraoperative blood transfusion (IBT), intraoperative blood loss (IBL), surgical time, cervical cancer surgery, and ovarian cancer surgery (P < 0.05). Further multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that DM, IBT, IBL, surgical time, cervical cancer surgery, and ovarian cancer surgery were independent risk factors for SSIs. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis of IBL and surgical time showed areas under the curve of 0.9420 and 0.8984, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: DM, IBT, greater IBL, extended surgical time, cervical cancer surgery, and ovarian cancer surgery were found to be risk factors for SSIs in patients undergoing hysterectomy for the treatment of GCs. The accurate identification of high-risk patients is critical to guide perioperative care and reduce SSI-related morbidity.

articles.title: Association of viral load values with cervical lesion severity and exploratory genotype analysis in HPV-positive Indian women.
articles.authors: Singh N, Zakiya Z, Singhal S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hybrid Capture 2 (HC2) provides a semi-quantitative estimate of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) burden as relative light units/cutoff (RLU/CO), and HPV genotyping may add value to triage assessment. We evaluated the association of RLU/CO with cervical lesion severity and explored whether genotype information improves diagnostic performance in HPV-positive Indian women.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted in two sequential phases. In the initial phase, 217 consecutive HPV-positive women underwent HC2 HPV DNA testing, colposcopy-guided biopsy, and histopathological assessment. In a subsequent phase, an additional group of 111 HPV-positive women underwent the same clinical and histopathological assessment and also provided specimens for HPV genotyping. The genotype-enriched group was analysed separately for genotype distribution, co-infection patterns, and exploratory genotype-integrated prediction models. Age, Histopathology, and viral load (HC2 RLU/CO) were analysed in the full cohort. The genotyped subset was additionally evaluated for HPV genotype distribution and genotype-integrated ROC models. Descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis testing with Holm-adjusted Dunn's post-hoc comparisons, and ROC analyses with 95% confidence intervals and paired DeLong comparisons were performed.
RESULTS: RLU/CO values differed across study-specific histopathological severity categories, with higher median values in LSIL, HSIL, and invasive cervical cancer than in normal histology and chronic cervicitis. In the cohort of 328 women, RLU/CO discriminated HSIL or invasive cervical cancer (severity score ≥3) with an AUC of 0.798 (95% CI, 0.726-0.868). A study-derived Youden-index cutoff of 12.08 RLU/CO yielded a sensitivity of 81.1% (95% CI, 69.5%-90.9%) and specificity of 73.1% (95% CI, 68.0%-78.0%). Among 111 genotyped participants, HPV16 was the most frequently detected genotype, and multiple-genotype infections occurred in 64 participants (57.7%). In the genotyped subgroup, comparative ROC analysis for HSIL or invasive cervical cancer showed AUCs of 0.659 for RLU/CO alone, 0.608 for RLU/CO plus HPV16/18, and 0.461 for RLU/CO plus other high-risk HPV. Neither genotype-integrated model improved discrimination compared with RLU/CO alone; these exploratory estimates require validation in larger independent cohorts.
CONCLUSION: HC2 RLU/CO showed potential for identifying HSIL or invasive cervical cancer. The study-derived cutoff requires…

articles.title: Effects of butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) metabolites on sperm quality in adult males: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Yan W, Yao W, Xu Q et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the associations between urinary concentrations of BHT and its metabolites and sperm quality parameters in adult males.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 282 adult males seeking fertility care were enrolled. Urinary concentrations of BHT metabolites (BHA, BHT-CHO, BHT-COOH, BHT-OH, BHT-Q, and BHT-quinol) were measured by HPLC MS/MS. Sperm quality parameters included sperm count, sperm concentration, progressive motility, normal morphology rate, and DNA fragmentation index (DFI). Multiple linear regression and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) were used to evaluate individual and joint associations, adjusting for age, BMI, household income, and smoking status.
RESULTS: In multiple linear regression, higher tertiles of urinary BHA were significantly positively associated with higher sperm concentration (P for trend < 0.05). Similarly, higher tertiles of BHT-COOH were significantly positively correlated with more total sperm count (P for trend < 0.05). Higher tertiles of BHT-OH, BHT-Q, and BHT- quinol were significantly positively associated with normal sperm morphology rate (all P for trend < 0.05). BKMR model did not reveal a monotonic overall joint effect of the metabolite mixture on total sperm count, sperm concentration, or normal morphology rate, but individual metabolite trends were consistent with the linear regression results.
CONCLUSIONS: The overall elevated concentrations of BHT and its metabolites showed no significant correlation with sperm quality, while increased levels of certain metabolites were positively associated with improved sperm quality. Further in-depth investigations are still required to systematically clarify the effects of BHT on sperm quality, so as to provide solid scientific evidence for the comprehensive improvement of male reproductive health.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and treatment strategies of ovarian teratomas associated with anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor encephalitis based on a case series.
articles.authors: Yang H, Fang C, Wang S
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (anti-NMDAR) encephalitis is a potentially life-threatening yet reversible complication associated with ovarian teratoma. This study aims to systematically analyze the clinical features of anti-NMDAR encephalitis related to ovarian teratoma, with the goal of enhancing our understanding of the disease.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 17 patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis associated with ovarian teratomas, who were admitted to Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, from August 2015 to August 2025. A systematic analysis was performed on their complete clinical data, including demographic characteristics, prodromal symptoms, typical neurological and psychiatric manifestations, cerebrospinal fluid and neuroimaging findings, anti-NMDAR antibody in cerebrospinal fluid, pathological features of the ovarian teratomas, comprehensive treatment strategies and follow-up outcomes.
RESULTS: In this study, the age of the included patients was 25 years (21, 29). The time from symptom onset to diagnosis was 16 days (10.5, 27). The time from hospital admission to diagnosis was 4 days (2.5, 7). Two patients had a history of teratomas and methotrexate treatment. 15 patients (15/17, 88%) were directly admitted to the intensive care unit, while only 2 (2/17, 12%) were treated in general wards. The patients predominantly presented with multiple neurological abnormalities without clinical signs of teratoma compression. All patients received immunotherapy and tumor resection, and all patients achieved clinical improvement. At 3 months after surgery, mRS ≤ 2 was achieved in patients (4/17, 24%), mRS 3-4 in 5 paitents (5/17, 29%), and mRS 5 in 8 patients (8/17, 47%). Although all patients met the pre-defined criterion of clinical improvement in at least one neurological symptom, functional recovery remained limited.
CONCLUSION: A history of teratoma and methotrexate treatment may be associated with a higher risk of teratoma-associated anti-NMDAR encephalitis; however, this observation was based on only two patients and warrants further investigation. The disease is characterized by acute onset and rapid progression, and clinical improvement can be achieved through multidisciplinary collaboration combined with prompt immunotherapy and tumor resection.

articles.title: Home-based exercise in postmenopausal and older women: effects on body composition, physical function, cardiometabolic health, and quality of life-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Gu S, Tang S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Home-based exercise (HBE) has received increasing attention as a low-cost and accessible strategy, although the durability of its effects and of long-term participation remains uncertain. Postmenopausal women frequently experience unfavorable changes in body composition, muscle strength, physical function, and cardiometabolic health. This review evaluated the effects of HBE on these outcomes and on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in postmenopausal and older women.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials of home-based exercise in postmenopausal and older women were included. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 statement, was retrospectively registered in INPLASY, and used the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool; data were synthesized in R using the meta package.
RESULTS: Nineteen randomized controlled trials involving 1,128 postmenopausal and older women were included. Pooled results showed that home-based exercise significantly reduced body mass index (BMI) (MD = -0.57 kg/m2, 95% CI: -0.71 to -0.43; I2 = 0%) and significantly improved health-related quality of life (HRQoL) (SMD = 0.51, 95% CI: 0.08 to 0.94; I2 = 76%). Effects on the Timed Up-and-Go test (TUGT) (MD = -0.64 s, 95% CI: -1.57 to 0.30), the five-times sit-to-stand test (5 × STS) (MD = -1.92 s, 95% CI: -4.36 to 0.52), handgrip strength (MD = 1.43 kg, 95% CI: -1.02 to 3.88), the six-minute walk test (MD = 35.16 m, 95% CI: -59.96 to 130.29), body fat percentage (MD = -0.31%, 95% CI: -0.65 to 0.03), and triglycerides (MD = -8.96 mg/dL, 95% CI: -19.45 to 1.52) did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Home-based exercise may reduce BMI and improve HRQoL in postmenopausal and older women, although the certainty of this evidence was moderate and very low, respectively. Effects on physical function and cardiometabolic markers remain inconclusive, with prediction intervals crossing the null for the most heterogeneous outcomes. Given the small number of trials per outcome, further well-designed randomized controlled trials with standardized prescriptions, longer follow-up, and routine adherence and adverse-event monitoring are needed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://inplasy.com/inplasy-2026-4-0094/, identifier INPLASY202640094.

articles.title: Early pregnancy weight gain in pregnant women and the risk of gestational diabetes: a dose-response meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Li J, Yang M, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus is the most common metabolic disorder of pregnancy, and its global prevalence continues to rise. Although excessive gestational weight gain has been linked to an increased risk of gestational diabetes mellitus, the precise dose-response relationship during the early pregnancy remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the association between early pregnancy weight gain (defined as first-trimester weight gain, approximately 12-13 weeks) and the risk of developing gestational diabetes mellitus and to quantify the dose-response relationship.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, China Biology Medicine disk, VIP Database for Chinese Technical Periodicals, WanFang Data, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure was conducted from database inception to December 2025 to identify studies examining the association between first-trimester weight gain and the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus. Two reviewers independently performed literature screening, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment. A traditional meta-analysis was performed using Stata 17.0 with a random-effects model using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and Knapp-Hartung adjustment. The dose-response relationship was examined using restricted cubic spline regression and generalized least squares estimation. Subgroup analyses by GDM diagnostic criteria were performed.
RESULTS: Nine cohort studies, encompassing 66,673 participants and 13,130 incident cases of gestational diabetes mellitus, were included in the meta-analysis. In the primary analysis restricted to seven studies with strict first-trimester weight gain, insufficient weight gain was associated with a lower risk of GDM (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79-0.90), whereas excessive weight gain was associated with a 32% higher risk (RR 1.32, 95% CI 1.20-1.45). Each 1-kg increment in first-trimester weight gain was associated with a 19% increase in GDM risk (RR 1.19, 95% CI 1.15-1.23). No statistically significant departure from linearity was observed (P for non-linearity = 0.973). Subgroup analysis by GDM diagnostic criteria showed no significant between-subgroup difference for excessive weight gain (p = 0.810) and a borderline difference for insufficient weight gain (p = 0.082).
CONCLUSION: Current evidence indicates that excessive first-trimester weight gain is associated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes mellitus, and no…

articles.title: Evaluation of machine learning-based prediction of pregnancy complications and adverse birth outcomes using routine data.
articles.authors: Parent C, Moraitaki C, Ngo A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality rates in the United States are higher than any other high-income nation, with a disproportionate burden on marginalized groups who often lack access to specialized care. We investigate whether machine learning models have the capacity to predict pregnancy and birth complications using only routinely obtained health information.
METHODS: Using a population-based cohort of 442,760 pregnancies from Kaiser Permanente Northern California occurring between January 1, 2011 and October 31, 2021, we train separate XGBoost prediction models for each to predict seven pregnancy and birth complications in six-week intervals. We analyze performance by comparing to historical studies, examining top features of the model, and assessing clinical utility through a cost-effectiveness analysis.
RESULTS: Here we show that only three pregnancy complications (gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, and pre-eclampsia) are predictable at early intervention points within the first trimester (at 12 weeks, AUC values are 0.789 [0.782, 0.706], 0.800 [0.794, 0.806], and 0.740 [0.734, 0.747] respectively), and demonstrate the cost-effectiveness of model-based interventions with no specialized data. This is compared to the at-birth complications of preterm birth, stillbirth, placental abruption, and small for gestational age at 24-weeks which demonstrated limited interventionable performance (AUCs of 0.683 [0.676, 0.690], 0.667 [0.624, 0.708], 0.622 [0.606, 0.638], and 0.654 [0.647, 0.660] respectively). We validate whether such screening models can transfer to an additional cohort of 6105 pregnancies, and find that transfer must be supplemented with local model tuning.
CONCLUSIONS: While some predictive models showcase opportunities in prenatal care, this is not uniform across complications and time periods. Our work demonstrates both the potential for, and challenges of, early risk assessment and intervention in personalized perinatal healthcare.

articles.title: Placental Glycolysis-Related Transcriptional Features in Early-Onset Preeclampsia Complicated by Fetal Growth Restriction.
articles.authors: Zhang R, Peng Y, Gao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia (PE) is a severe obstetric complication characterized by the new onset of hypertension and proteinuria after 20 weeks of gestation. However, bulk transcriptomic approaches cannot resolve cell type-specific alterations within the heterogeneous placenta. Single- cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at individual-cell resolution, thereby revealing cellular heterogeneity and identifying cell populations and pathways potentially involved in disease processes.
METHODS: This exploratory study integrated scRNA-seq data from one EOPE-FGR placental sample and one healthy control sample with bulk RNA-seq data. The Seurat and limma packages were used for single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses, respectively. Gene set enrichment analysis and differential expression analysis were performed to identify candidate pathways and genes. RT-qPCR was used to examine candidate gene expression, whereas the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay was used to assess the effect of FLT1 knockdown on cell viability under hypoxia/reoxygenation conditions.
RESULTS: Exploratory scRNA-seq analysis identified ten major placental cell types. In the two analyzed samples, the EOPE-FGR sample showed a higher observed EVT proportion, whereas EVT cells displayed sample-specific glycolysis-, interferon-, and immune-related expression patterns. These single-cell observations were treated as exploratory. An exploratory intersection of bulk disease- versus-control differentially expressed genes with genes identified from the EVT high- versus low-glycolysis-score comparison prioritized 11 candidate genes: FLT1, PROCR, INHA, CST6, HTRA1, C12orf75, FSTL3, INHBA, CDA, EBI3, and PRG2. In supportive in vitro experiments, eight selected genes showed increased expression under hypoxia/reoxygenation conditions, and FLT1 knockdown was associated with an increased CCK-8 signal. The CCK-8 assay did not directly assess glycolytic activity.
DISCUSSION: Bulk RNA-seq analysis identified glycolysis-related enrichment in EOPE-FGR placentas, whereas the single-cell datasets provided exploratory observations of EVT-associated expression patterns. Given the limited scRNA-seq sample size, these observations should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger independent cohorts.
CONCLUSION: The integrated analyses prioritized candidate genes associated with bulk disease-related and within-sample EVT glycolysis-score-related expression patterns. These…

articles.title: The breast at perimenopause.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Rousset-Jablonski C, Gompel A
articles.abstract: Perimenopause, defined as the transition between regular menstrual cycles and confirmed menopause, is characterized by erratic hormonal secretions and metabolic disorders which can have potential consequences for breast health. During this period, benign breast diseases may worsen, adversely affecting quality of life and possibly increasing the risk of breast cancer. These aspects have implications for the clinical management of these women. Breast cancer has different characteristics and risk factors for women in premenopause, perimenopause and postmenopause. This narrative review analyzed available data on these risk factors during perimenopause, including the impact of hormonal contraception and menopause hormone therapy. Incidence and mortality, and subtypes of breast cancer differ in women according to the stage of menopause, ethnicity, the level of income of countries and public health resources. These inequalities in risk levels, breast cancer types and prognosis may affect screening and preventive strategies - an issue clinicians should be aware of. Among breast cancer survivors, the menopausal transition raises the question of a shift from tamoxifen, usually used in perimenopausal women, to aromatase inhibitors, indicated after menopause; the treatment may complicate the diagnosis of menopause. Women in the perimenopause may experience differences in the frequency and severity of endocrine therapy side effects.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) in Cardiovascular Disease: Integrating Epidemiology, Clinical Guidelines, Molar Measurement, and Emerging Therapies.
articles.authors: Thomas PE, Vedel-Krogh S, Kronenberg F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD = myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, peripheral artery disease) and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma concentrations of Lp(a) are >90% genetically determined. Multiple drugs in development reduce lipoprotein(a) by 80% to 98%. While the recently announced topline results, the phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial of pelacarsen did not meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint despite lowering Lp(a), and 3 other cardiovascular outcomes trials remain ongoing. Lipoprotein(a) testing is currently increasing rapidly in many countries.
CONTENT: Most guidelines on dyslipidemia and prevention of cardiovascular disease worldwide now advise that Lp(a) should be measured once in all adults, ideally jointly with the first lipid profile ordered. If previous lipid profiles were taken, then Lp(a) should be included in the next lipid profile. Lipoprotein(a) should ideally be measured in nmol/L, and repeat measurements are relevant if drugs are given to lower Lp(a) concentrations, initially at suspected acute coronary syndrome or stroke and again after 1 month, and sometimes in women after menopause. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial assessment of a patient's overall cardiovascular risk. Clinical chemistry laboratories that measure lipid profiles should therefore also offer Lp(a) testing. This is easily done as Lp(a) assays can be run on most major clinical chemistry platforms. High Lp(a) is >105 nmol/L (>50 mg/dL).
SUMMARY: As use of Lp(a) testing is increasing rapidly worldwide, more clinical chemistry laboratories will likely offer this test locally. Measuring Lp(a) levels alongside a standard lipid profile provides a more comprehensive initial lipid assessment of a patient's cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Risk factors for seizures in patients with brain metastases: integrating clinical features and molecular markers.
articles.authors: Malanga OM, Pellerino A, Bertero L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain metastases (BM) affect nearly 30% of patients with solid tumors. Despite this prevalence, the mechanisms underlying brain tumor-related epilepsy (BTRE) in this population remain incompletely elucidated. This study aims to investigate risk factors associated with seizure occurrence in patients with BM, focusing on histology and molecular markers of the primary tumor.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study on 325 patients who underwent surgical resection of BM between 2014 and 2019. Clinical, radiological, and molecular data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable regression models to assess seizure risk factors. Overall Survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models.
RESULTS: Seizures occurred in 32% of patients. Frontal (P<0.001) and parietal (P=0.05) locations were significantly associated with seizure occurrence. Ovarian cancer exhibited the highest seizure prevalence (80%, P=0.001), followed by melanoma (44%), breast (35%), and colorectal cancer (34%). Regarding molecular status, we found a significant association between seizures and both BRAF mutations in melanoma (P=0.03) and HER2 positive subtype breast cancer (P=0.01). Seizure occurrence at onset correlated with improved OS (P=0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest an association between seizure risk and molecular status of the primary tumor, specifically BRAF mutations in melanoma and HER2+ breast cancer subtype. Additionally, we found an improved OS in BM patients experiencing seizures at onset of disease. These findings are exploratory and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts; this could help refine seizure-risk estimation and prognostic assessment in surgically treated patients with brain metastases.

articles.title: Transperineal Ultrasound Assessment of Fetal Head Descent and Successful Manual Rotation in Women Undergoing Labor With Neuraxial Analgesia.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Suzuki Y, Takita H, Matsuoka R et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Manual rotation is commonly used to correct fetal head malrotation during labor. This study assessed the effectiveness of manual rotation under neuraxial analgesia and evaluated whether transperineal ultrasound (TUS)-derived parameters were associated with procedural success and could provide additional information when considering manual rotation.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 59 women with fetal rotational abnormalities during labor under neuraxial analgesia at a tertiary care center. Rotational abnormalities were defined as occiput posterior or occiput transverse positions with a midline angle (MLA) ≥ 45°, assessed 1 h after full cervical dilation. Manual rotation success was defined as correction to an MLA < 45°. Delivery, maternal, neonatal, and TUS-derived parameters were compared between successful and unsuccessful cases.
RESULTS: Manual rotation was successful in 44 of 59 cases (74.5%). The vaginal delivery rate was significantly higher in the successful group than in the unsuccessful group (90.9% vs. 46.7%, p < 0.001). No significant differences were noted in maternal or neonatal outcomes. Among TUS parameters, only the TUS-station was significantly associated with procedural success. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified a cutoff of 14.3 mm, above which the likelihood of successful rotation was 95.8%. In exploratory logistic regression models, TUS-station remained associated with successful manual rotation after adjustment for clinically relevant covariates.
CONCLUSIONS: Manual rotation performed under neuraxial analgesia was associated with a high-procedural success rate. A TUS-station ≥ 14.3 mm was associated with a high likelihood of successful manual rotation and may provide complementary information when considering the procedure, although further validation is required.

articles.title: Second-Trimester Assessment of Lower Uterine Segment Microvascular Flow and Residual Myometrial Thickness for Predicting Pregnancies at Low Risk for Developing Uterine Scar Dehiscence After Cesarean Delivery: A Prospective Preliminary Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Muto M, Horinouchi T, Kawakami K et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To determine whether second-trimester assessment of lower uterine segment microvascular blood flow using superb microvascular imaging complements residual myometrial thickness for predicting pregnancies at low risk of developing uterine scar dehiscence, a precursor lesion of uterine rupture after previous cesarean delivery.
METHODS: This prospective study included 77 women with singleton pregnancies and at least one previous cesarean delivery. Transvaginal ultrasonography was performed at 19-21 and 25-27 weeks of gestation to measure residual myometrial thickness and assess lower uterine segment microvascular blood flow using superb microvascular imaging. Uterine scar dehiscence was diagnosed by macroscopic findings at cesarean delivery. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Seventeen women developed uterine scar dehiscence. Residual myometrial thickness was thinner and microvascular blood flow was detected less frequently in women with than without uterine scar dehiscence at both gestational periods. At 25-27 weeks of gestation, combining microvascular blood flow assessment with residual myometrial thickness improved discrimination over residual myometrial thickness alone (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.77 vs. 0.65; p = 0.02), improving exclusion of uterine scar dehiscence. After adjustment for residual myometrial thickness, microvascular blood flow remained independently associated with the absence of uterine scar dehiscence (odds ratio, 11.1; 95% confidence interval, 2.74-61.0; p = 0.0005).
CONCLUSIONS: Superb microvascular imaging provides information complementary to residual myometrial thickness. Combined second-trimester assessment, particularly at 25-27 weeks of gestation, may improve prediction of pregnancies at low risk for developing uterine scar dehiscence.

articles.title: Comparison of DHEA- and Letrozole-Induced Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Phenotypes in Rats Under Simulated High-Altitude Hypoxia.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.authors: Wang R, Fang T, Yang Z et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Exposure to high altitudes and low oxygen levels has been associated with female reproductive system damage and increased polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) incidence. This study compared the effects of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) injection and letrozole gavage on development of PCOS-like phenotypes in rats under simulated high-altitude hypoxic (HH) conditions. MATERIAL AND METHODS Eighty late-adolescent Sprague-Dawley rats received subcutaneous DHEA injections or letrozole gavage under simulated HH conditions at 6000 m (pressure: 47.2 kPa) or local ambient altitude (LA; 2200 m; pressure: 77.2 kPa) for 21 days. Body weight, serum reproductive hormone levels, ovarian histomorphology, and estrous cycles were evaluated. RESULTS Under HH conditions, DHEA-treated rats had higher body weights than letrozole-treated rats (mean difference=-8.367, P=0.040). DHEA injection increased testosterone levels (adjusted P<0.001), while decreasing estradiol (adjusted P<0.001) and progesterone levels (adjusted P<0.001). Letrozole gavage increased only testosterone levels (adjusted P=0.008); there were no significant changes in estradiol or progesterone levels. The DHEA group exhibited more severe follicular atresia and a greater reduction in the healthy-to-cystic follicle ratio than the letrozole group (adjusted P=0.046). DHEA injection also produced more complete estrous cycle disruption than letrozole gavage under both LA and HH conditions by day 21 (100% vs 30% under LA and 100% vs 60% under HH; P=0.003 and P=0.011, respectively). CONCLUSIONS Under simulated HH conditions, DHEA injection produces a more severe PCOS-like reproductive phenotype than letrozole gavage. Further studies are needed to expand these findings across altitudes, exposure durations, and age groups.

articles.title: Prevalence and Determinants of Underweight Among Children Aged 6-10 Years in Urban and Rural Areas of Central Ethiopia: A Community-Based Comparative Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: Journal of primary care & community health
articles.authors: Abera M, Geda YF, Yasin HZ et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesThe evidence revealed that underweight is a major public health concern affecting school-aged children in low and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia. Underweight affects children aged 6-10 years, growth and development, which leads to poor physical, cognitive, and social performance. Thus, this study aimed to assess the prevalence and determinants of underweight among children aged 6-10 years old in urban and rural areas of Central Ethiopia.MethodsA community-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 541 children from January 2 to May 2, 2023. Participants were selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and anthropometric measurements. Children's nutritional status was assessed using weight-for-age z-scores calculated with WHO AnthroPlus software. Factors associated with underweight were identified using binary logistic regression analysis. Statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05, and associations were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).ResultsIn this study, 501 children were enrolled, yielding a response rate of 92.6%. Underweight was more common in rural areas than in urban areas, with prevalence rates of 24.9% (95% CI: 21.2, 26.3) and 17.5% (95% CI: 14.0, 19.0), respectively. Among urban children, maternal age at first birth (AOR = 4.4; 95% CI: 1.63, 12.2), handwashing after latrine use (AOR = 0.16; 95% CI: 0.12, 0.46), use of treated drinking water (AOR = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.18, 0.51), and family planning use (AOR = 0.12; 95% CI: 0.10, 0.47) were determinants of underweight. In contrast, among rural children, maternal age at first birth (AOR = 2.4; 95% CI: 1.34, 8.91), no antenatal care (ANC) follow-up (AOR = 2.3; 95% CI: 1.27, 6.53), diarrhea in the previous month (AOR = 2.8; 95% CI: 1.63, 9.35), dietary diversity (AOR = 6.0; 95% CI: 2.79, 13.2), and a history of illness in the preceding two weeks (AOR = 3.4; 95% CI: 1.91, 7.23) were identified as determinants of underweight.ConclusionUnderweight was more prevalent among rural children (24.9%) than among urban children (17.5%), highlighting the need for context-specific nutritional interventions. Interventions addressing the identified factors should be strengthened to improve the nutritional status of school-age children in both rural and urban settings.

articles.title: Placental angiogenic biomarkers for triage of suspected preeclampsia and prediction of maternal and neonatal morbidity in a high-risk population.
articles.authors: Lodewijks EJ, Hendrix MLE, Suiters MJM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Placental angiogenic biomarkers, including soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and placental growth factor (PlGF), are used to predict preeclampsia (PE) and related adverse outcomes . This study aimed to assess differences in sFlt-1/PlGF ratios among high-risk women according to PE, maternal and neonatal morbidity, and to evaluate the predictive performance of thresholds > 38 and > 85, including time to delivery.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 289 high-risk singleton pregnant women (2015-2019) were included. sFlt-1/PlGF ratios were measured after 24 weeks of gestation and compared across outcome groups.
RESULTS: sFlt-1/PlGF ratios were significantly lower in the reference group compared to the confirmed and the suspected PE group. Ratios > 38 were associated with PE (OR 12.2 (95% CI 4.9-30.7; p < 0.001)), maternal morbidity (OR 22.5 (95% CI 8.9-56.7; p < 0.001)), neonatal morbidity (OR 4.0 (95% CI 2.0-8.0; p < 0.001)) and delivery within one, two, and three weeks (OR 20.0, 9.2, and 14.6; all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The sFlt-1/PlGF ratio supports individualized management in high-risk pregnancies.

articles.title: Spatial distribution of short birth intervals and associated factors among reproductive-age women in Somalia, 2020: a spatial and multilevel analysis.
articles.journal: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique
articles.authors: Kahie AM, Hassan MS, Omer NM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short birth interval (SBI) is a major contributor to maternal and child morbidity and mortality. In Somalia, a nation experiencing high fertility rates alongside protracted conflict and humanitarian crises, evidence on birth spacing patterns is scarce. This study investigates the prevalence, determinants, and spatial distribution of SBI to guide evidence-based policy and targeted health interventions.
METHODS: This study analyzed data from a weighted sample of 26,990 reproductive-age women (aged 15-49 years) from the 2020 Somalia Demographic and Health Survey. To ensure national representativeness, the analysis incorporated complex survey design elements, including individual sample weights, clustering, and stratification. We employed multilevel logistic regression to assess individual and community-level factors associated with SBI (defined as a birth-to-birth interval < 33 months). Spatial analysis using Global Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi statistics was performed to identify significant geographic clustering and regional hotspots.
RESULTS: The national prevalence of SBI was 77.50%. Multilevel analysis revealed that older maternal age was a significant protective factor (AOR = 0.47; 95% CI: 0.43-0.51 for ages 30-39; AOR = 0.31; 95% CI: 0.28-0.34 for ages 40-49) compared to those under 30. Conversely, and paradoxically, women with higher education had significantly increased odds of SBI (AOR = 1.88; 95% CI: 1.07-3.30) compared to those with no formal education. Spatial analysis confirmed significant clustering of SBI (Moran's I = 0.50, p = 0.003), with hotspots concentrated in southern Somalia, specifically in the Gedo, Jubbada Hoose, Bay, and Bakool regions.
CONCLUSION: SBI in Somalia is a widespread public health crisis with a prevalence of 77.50%, showing distinct geographical patterns driven by a complex interplay of demographic and community factors. Health interventions should prioritize young women (< 30 years) and be geographically targeted toward the identified southern hotspots. The counterintuitive finding on education highlights the need for context-specific research to inform effective reproductive health programming in post-conflict settings.

articles.title: Prevalence and associated factors of symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress in pregnant women in Mozambique: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Barros EPJ, Fumo AMT, Moçambique MATM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental disorders represent a major public health burden worldwide, disproportionately affecting women in low- and middle-income countries. The perinatal period is a time of increased biological, psychological, and social vulnerability, heightening the risk of depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms. Despite the high relevance, data on maternal mental health in Mozambique remain scarce.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in two health centers in Maputo. Pregnant women aged ≥ 18 years were systematically recruited. Psychological symptoms were assessed using the DASS-21. Prevalence ratios for depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms were estimated using Poisson regression with robust variance.
RESULTS: Clinically significant symptoms (moderate to extremely severe) were observed in 38.9% of participants for depression, 57.6% for anxiety, and 14.4% for stress. Additional factors significantly associated with symptoms included household composition, marital status, family history of mental illness, occupational status, religion, and family planning practices.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight substantial psychosocial and structural vulnerabilities among pregnant women in Maputo. Systematic screening integrated into prenatal care, policies addressing economic and occupational insecurity, and further research exploring protective factors and culturally relevant interventions are warranted.

articles.title: Surgical opportunities for primary prevention of high-grade serous ovarian cancer: a procedure-level analysis of opportunistic salpingectomy.
articles.authors: Shaalan W, Schmidt C, Fischer K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most common and lethal subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, is now recognized to originate predominantly from the distal fallopian tube. This paradigm shift has established opportunistic salpingectomy (OS) as a promising strategy for primary prevention during otherwise indicated abdominal or pelvic surgery. However, the frequency, timing, and surgical distribution of previous opportunities for OS among patients subsequently diagnosed with HGSOC remain insufficiently characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To quantify previous surgical opportunities for OS before HGSOC diagnosis using complementary patient-level and procedure-level analyses.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with histologically confirmed HGSOC who underwent primary debulking surgery or interval debulking surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy between 2016 and 2025. Clinicopathological characteristics, family and personal cancer history, germline genetic testing results, and previous abdominopelvic procedures were reviewed. A procedure was considered eligible for OS if it was elective, had been performed at least 12 months before HGSOC diagnosis, and occurred after completion of childbearing.
RESULTS: Among 426 patients, 165 (38.7%) had undergone at least one previous abdominal or pelvic operation that fulfilled the predefined eligibility criteria for OS. At the procedure level, 210/469 previous operations (44.8%) represented potential opportunities for OS. Of these, 112/210 (53.3%) were sterilization procedures and 98/210 (46.7%) were non-sterilization procedures. Gynecologic surgery accounted for 135/210 (64.3%) eligible procedures, whereas 75/210 (35.7%) occurred during non-gynecologic surgery. Hysterectomy was the most common gynecologic procedure, and cholecystectomy was the most frequent non-gynecologic procedure. Eligible procedures were performed at a median age of 46.0 years (IQR, 40.0-53.0) and preceded HGSOC diagnosis by a mean interval of 17.9 years. Among 116 genetically tested patients meeting the OS-eligibility criteria, 32 (27.6%) carried a pathogenic germline variant.
CONCLUSION: More than one-third of patients with HGSOC had at least one previous surgical opportunity during which OS could have been considered, nearly two decades before HGSOC diagnosis. Although gynecologic surgery remains the principal setting for implementing OS, more than one-third of eligible procedures occurred during…

articles.title: Menstrual-related conditions are associated with optimal menstrual cycle timing for sports performance in female athletes.
articles.authors: Nose-Ogura S, Kawabe R, Kashiwagi Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the effects of menstrual cycle phases on objective exercise performance are generally trivial, athletes frequently report substantial subjective impairment. We examined 14-year temporal trends in menstrual-related conditions in elite Japanese athletes and tested whether perceived optimal menstrual cycle timing for sports performance is explained by menstrual-related conditions.
METHODS: We analyzed 9,130 records from 3,693 female athletes (2008-2021) derived from a standardized retrospective questionnaire, excluding records indicating the use of hormonal preparations (e.g., combined oral contraceptives or progestin preparations). Temporal trends in menstrual-related conditions (dysmenorrhea, premenstrual syndrome (PMS), heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB)) were assessed using multivariate logistic regression. We also evaluated associations between the number and type of menstrual-related conditions and the self-reported optimal menstrual cycle timing for sports performance.
RESULTS: From 2008 to 2021, the prevalence of dysmenorrhea (AOR: 1.040, p < 0.001) increased, and PMS (AOR: 0.934, p < 0.001) decreased. The self-reported optimal menstrual cycle timing for sports performance was strongly influenced by menstrual-related conditions: athletes with three conditions predominantly reported "Post-Menstruation" (68.4%), whereas those with no conditions most frequently reported "No Relation" (51.1%). A clear dose-response pattern was observed; having three conditions increased the odds of reporting "Post-Menstruation" by 3.54-fold versus no conditions (p < 0.001).
