In models including all three conditions, PMS was the strongest predictor of reporting "Post-Menstruation" (AOR: 2.53), exceeding HMB (AOR: 1.51) and dysmenorrhea (AOR: 1.15).
CONCLUSIONS: Athletes' perceived optimal timing of the menstrual cycle for sports performance is strongly influenced by menstrual-related conditions-particularly PMS.

articles.title: Incidence, predictors, and mortality of necrotizing enterocolitis among neonates admitted to two regional referral hospitals in Uganda: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Moalim MA, Turyasiima M, Lopez DC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening gastrointestinal condition affecting neonates, characterized by abdominal distension, feeding intolerance, and bloody stools, with or without radiological signs such as pneumatosis intestinalis, portal venous gas, or pneumoperitoneum. Despite its significant contribution to neonatal morbidity and mortality, most epidemiological data originate from high-income countries, leaving a gap in evidence from low-resource settings.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the incidence, associated risk factors, and mortality of NEC among neonates aged ≤ 28 days in two regional referral hospitals in Uganda.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted among neonates admitted to Mubende and Fort Portal Regional Referral Hospitals between April 2025 and June 2025. NEC was diagnosed using modified Bell's criteria and participants were followed until discharge or 28 days of life. Neonates with major gastrointestinal malformations or referred to other facilities were excluded. NEC diagnosis was based on modified Bell's criteria. A total of 424 neonates were enrolled, comprising 38.9% term and 61.1% preterm infants.
RESULTS: Thirty neonates developed NEC, yielding an incidence proportion of 7.1%, significantly higher among preterm neonates (p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression identified the following independent risk factors (p < 0.05 for all): maternal chronic illness (particularly HIV), history of preeclampsia, presentation after 14 days of life, very preterm birth, extremely low birth weight, very low birth weight, and neonatal sepsis. Mortality was markedly elevated in neonates with NEC compared to those without (26.8% vs. 2.3%, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: NEC incidence in this low-resource setting is notably high, especially among preterm neonates. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted interventions to reduce neonatal sepsis, prevent preterm births, address intrauterine growth restriction, and strengthen maternal HIV control measures to improve neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Integrating mental health support into care for placenta accreta spectrum: a qualitative analysis of patient perspectives.
articles.authors: Feldman N, Nathan MD, Lipschitz JM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with high-risk pregnancies due to placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) are at high risk of morbidity and mortality, which may increase risk for childbirth related mental health sequelae including postpartum post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and trauma symptoms. However, there has been limited investigation into these patients' mental health needs. We aimed to use qualitative data to understand PAS patients' mental health experiences through their obstetric course, and to generate recommendations for the delivery of mental health support to these patients.
METHODS: This exploratory study used a focus group format with patients who had a history of PAS. General questions about patient's pregnancies, births, and postpartum experiences were asked by mental health professionals. Using a rapid qualitative analysis approach, transcriptions of these focus groups were coded by three psychiatrists and core themes were extracted.
RESULTS: We conducted four focus groups with a total of 22 women. Major emotional themes included fear and isolation during the antepartum period, and grief, anxiety, and trauma in the postpartum period. Both periods were associated with a negative emotional impact on relationships with family members. Sadness & depression were less prominent among participants' experiences. Participants felt that mental health care resources needed to be integrated with their obstetric care, extend further into the postpartum period, and should be as specific as possible to their medical condition.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on the results of these focus groups, we propose that patients with high-risk pregnancies and/or a history of traumatic birth should have access to expert mental health care that is integrated with their obstetric care. These patients may benefit from extended obstetric follow-up. Mental health screening in these populations should focus on anxiety and trauma symptoms rather than only screening for depression. Future studies should continue to examine these factors in a broader group of women with high-risk pregnancies beyond PAS.

articles.title: Variation of the uterine flexion angle before and after voiding in nulliparous women with anteverted uterus: FLEXIMIX study.
articles.authors: Chiron B, Aujoulat P, Gergaud L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resistance during intrauterine device insertion (IUD) may be influenced by the uterine flexion angle. While bladder filling has been used to facilitate catheter insertion for hysteroscopy and embryo transfer, the only study assessing this strategy for IUD insertion found no benefit. However, the physiological effect of bladder filling on uterine alignment has not been rigorously evaluated. This effect may be particularly relevant in nulliparous women with anteverted uteri. The study aimed to evaluate the variation in uterine flexion angle between full and empty bladder conditions in nulliparous women, and to determine the prevalence of uterine anteversion in a European population.
METHODS: Prospective single-center study included 250 nulliparous women aged 18 years or older. Participant underwent two transabdominal ultrasounds: with a full bladder / after voiding. Uterine version and flexion were assessed by measuring the angles formed by the uterine body, cervix, and vaginal axis.
RESULTS: Among the 215 participants with uterine anteversion (87.0%), paired flexion angle measurements were available for 212 (84.8% of the total cohort). Among these 212 women, the mean change in flexion angle was 48.0° (SD 36.7°, p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.31). In 60.8% of cases, bladder filling changed an acute flexion angle to an obtuse one. The point of uterine flexion was located approximately 20-21 mm from the external cervical os, just beyond the internal os, suggesting a mechanical effect of bladder distension on uterine alignment.
CONCLUSIONS: Bladder filling significantly modifies uterine flexion in nulliparous women with anteversion. This physiological effect provides a plausible anatomical mechanism that may facilitate IUD insertion. Further interventional studies are needed to determine its clinical applicability.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, trial registration number: NCT06669845, registration date: 2024-10-31.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes, surgeon-rated fatigue, and scar satisfaction after dual-port versus single-port laparoscopic myomectomy: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Li Y, Su Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic myomectomy is commonly used for women with symptomatic uterine fibroids who wish to preserve the uterus. Single-port laparoscopy reduces the number of abdominal incisions but may increase instrument crowding and ergonomic difficulty during myometrial dissection and suturing. Dual-port laparoscopy may provide a practical balance between reduced-port access and operative maneuverability. This study compared perioperative outcomes, surgeon-rated fatigue, and patient-reported scar satisfaction between dual-port and single-port laparoscopic myomectomy.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women who underwent elective laparoscopic myomectomy for solitary uterine fibroids at a tertiary center between January 2024 and November 2025. Propensity scores were estimated using age, body mass index, fibroid diameter, fibroid location, pelvic adhesion grade, medical comorbidity, and number of previous pelvic surgeries. One-to-one nearest-neighbor matching without replacement was performed with a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score. Primary multivariable models in the matched cohort additionally adjusted for operating surgeon and year of surgery and used matched-pair clustered robust variance estimation. Alternative-model sensitivity analyses and regression diagnostics were also performed.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 190 women were included, with 95 patients in each group. Estimated blood loss was lower in the dual-port group (mean ± standard deviation, 45.53 ± 38.12 vs. 76.32 ± 69.94 mL; median [interquartile range], 30.0 [20.0-50.0] vs. 50.0 [30.0-100.0] mL). In the fully adjusted matched-cohort model, dual-port surgery remained associated with lower blood loss (β = -23.07 mL, 95% CI - 39.14 to - 7.01; P = 0.005), whereas the operative-time association was attenuated (β = -0.13 h, 95% CI - 0.27 to 0.00; P = 0.053). Surgeon-rated fatigue was available for 110 of 190 patients (57.9%) and scar satisfaction for 78 of 190 patients (41.1%); both were analyzed as exploratory complete-case outcomes. Postoperative recovery outcomes showed no consistent between-group pattern, and only one postoperative complication occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In this propensity score-matched cohort, dual-port laparoscopic myomectomy was associated with lower estimated blood loss after adjustment for operating surgeon and year of surgery. The operative-time finding was suggestive but not independently confirmed…

articles.title: Not all days are equal after preterm prelabor rupture of membranes: a time-dependent analysis of adverse perinatal outcomes.
articles.authors: Hentschke ES, Rahn A, Treier A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM) is associated with significant perinatal morbidity and mortality. Clinical management is typically based on inpatient monitoring, although the optimal duration and the potential role of outpatient care remain unclear.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, all women with PPROM between 15 + 0 and < 37 + 0 weeks' gestation managed as inpatients at a tertiary center (07/2019-04/2024) were included. The primary outcome was a composite severe adverse perinatal outcome (SAPO), comprising fetal or neonatal death, neonatal sepsis, intrauterine inflammation or infection, and major obstetric complications. Time-dependent risk was analyzed using latency stratification and landmark analyses. Independent predictors were identified via multivariable logistic regression. Longitudinal clinical and laboratory changes in the five days before delivery were assessed, and predictive performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: A total of 300 women were included, of whom 46 (15.3%) experienced SAPO. Lower gestational age at PPROM, non-cephalic presentation, and estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile were independently associated with SAPO, while inflammatory markers at admission showed no statistically significant independent association. The highest adjusted odds of SAPO were observed in the 6-7-day latency group (adjusted OR 6.10, 95% CI 1.45-25.62), although this subgroup comprised only 11 pregnancies. No statistically significant increase was detected in the group with latency exceeding seven days. Longitudinal increases in C-reactive protein (CRP) and leukocyte levels preceded delivery in complicated cases, but predictive performance remained limited (AUC 0.59-0.61).
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the importance of gestational age, fetal condition, and dynamic selection during expectant management of PPROM. Prospective studies are needed to evaluate individualized monitoring strategies and the potential role of outpatient management in carefully selected patients.

articles.title: Effect of exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in early pregnancy on blood glucose levels.
articles.authors: Yang Y, Zhu Z, Lin L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given the limited evidence on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposure and glucose metabolism in pregnancy, this study evaluated the associations of first-trimester exposure to individual and multiple PFAS with mid-pregnancy blood glucose levels and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
METHODS: This study recruited 314 pregnant women from the Changsha Maternal and Child Health Hospital, Hunan Province, China. Serum samples were collected at 11-13 weeks of gestation, and the concentrations of 25 PFAS compounds were measured. At 24-28 weeks of gestation, all participants underwent a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test. Multivariate logistic regression was applied to estimate associations between individual PFAS and GDM, whereas multivariate linear regression was utilized to assess their associations with fasting blood glucose (FBG), as well as 1-h and 2-h post-load glucose levels. Associations were stratified by maternal age and pre-pregnancy body mass index, and mixed effects were estimated using Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR).
RESULTS: In the multivariate logistic regression analysis, compared with the lowest tertile, early-pregnancy exposure to the second tertile of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA; OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.04, 3.73), and the highest tertile of perfluoroheptane sulfonic acid (PFHpS; OR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.15, 4.10) was positively associated with the risk of GDM. In the multivariate linear regression analysis, the second tertile of PFOA exposure was positively associated with 1-h glucose levels (β = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.19, 1.08). The second (β = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.06, 0.86) and highest (β = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.03, 0.85) tertiles of PFOA, as well as the highest tertile of PFHpS (β = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.31, 1.12), were significantly associated with increased 2-h glucose levels. In contrast, inverse associations or null associations were observed for certain other PFAS. Exposure to certain PFAS was associated with an increased risk of GDM and glucose intolerance, particularly in women of normal weight and women aged ≥ 30 years. The BKMR model results indicated that the PFAS mixture was negatively associated with FBG. Specifically, when the natural logarithm of the PFAS mixture increased from the median to the 60th percentile, FBG levels significantly decreased (β = -0.03, 95% CI: -0.05, -0.01), with N-ethylperfluoro-1-octanesulfonamide (N-EtFOSA-M) contributing most to this association.
CONCLUSION: Early pregnancy PFAS exposure was…

articles.title: MYOCD-associated congenital megabladder: novel variants and insights into prenatal phenotypic diversity.
articles.authors: Li G, Han X, Cao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardin, encoded by MYOCD, is a key transcriptional coactivator of serum response factor that is essential for smooth muscle cell differentiation and contractility. Loss-of-function variants in MYOCD have been reported to cause congenital megabladder (MGBL), a rare and severe developmental defect. To date, only six pathogenic variants across five families have been documented worldwide.
METHODS: Four unrelated Chinese families presenting with fetal urinary tract malformations were recruited. Amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling was performed, followed by conventional cytogenetic karyotyping, chromosomal microarray analysis, and trio-based exome sequencing (trio-ES). The ClinGen gene curation framework was employed to evaluate the clinical validity of the relationship between MYOCD and MGBL.
RESULTS: Trio-ES identified four novel heterozygous variants in the MYOCD gene, including two nonsense variants [p.(Gln434Ter) and p.(Gln307Ter)], one canonical splice-site variant (c.1125 + 1G > A), and one frameshift variant [p.(Gly191ValfsTer42)]. Marked phenotypic variability was observed, ranging from isolated prenatal bilateral hydronephrosis with postnatal survival to severe MGBL leading to pregnancy termination or intrauterine fetal demise. By integrating evidence from our study and previously reports, the MYOCD-MGBL association was classified as "Definitive" under the ClinGen framework.
CONCLUSIONS: This study expands the mutational and phenotypic spectrum of MYOCD-related MGBL and highlights substantial prenatal phenotypic heterogeneity. The findings underscore the complexity of prenatal diagnosis and the importance of careful genetic counseling.

articles.title: Gestational diabetes mellitus and risk of long-term cardiometabolic disease.
articles.authors: Shen Y, Perng W, Dabelea D et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), or hyperglycaemia first diagnosed during pregnancy, is associated with adverse outcomes for the mother and offspring. In this narrative review, we first summarize the epidemiological evidence regarding long-term maternal and offspring cardiometabolic consequences of GDM, including the role of heterogeneity in the aetiology of GDM in shaping the long-term effects of GDM exposure. Next, we discuss established mechanistic processes, such as β-cell stress, vascular dysfunction and developmental programming, that link GDM to long-term maternal and offspring outcomes and, accordingly, hold potential to be therapeutic targets. We also discuss emerging evidence for connections between other processes, such as placental signalling, and cardiometabolic risk after GDM. Finally, we discuss the role of potential avenues for cardiometabolic risk mitigation following GDM exposure, including lactation and breastfeeding, postpartum monitoring and lifestyle interventions.

articles.title: Risk prediction for neonatal resuscitation and intensive care admission after cesarean under general anesthesia.
articles.authors: Liu C, Zhao L, Yin M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates delivered by cesarean under general anesthesia (GA) may require resuscitation or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. This study aimed to develop and validate clinical prediction models for these outcomes.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included singleton cesarean deliveries under GA at four tertiary centers from January 2009 to August 2023. Patients were randomly split into development and validation cohorts (7:3). Candidate clinical and anesthesia-related variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, decision curve analysis, and risk stratification.
RESULTS: Among 1523 neonates, 1067 were assigned to the development cohort and 456 to the validation cohort. Neonatal resuscitation occurred in 212 neonates (13.9%), and NICU admission occurred in 482 (31.6%). The resuscitation model yielded development/validation AUCs of 0.834/0.682, versus 0.810/0.773 for NICU admission. Earlier gestational age was a major predictor of both outcomes, with anesthetic regimen, dexamethasone exposure, and gestational diabetes also contributing to risk estimation.
CONCLUSION: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related variables may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and NICU admission risk after cesarean under GA. These models may support neonatal team preparedness and delivery-room resource planning.
IMPACT: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related data may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission risk after cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. This multicenter study focuses on neonates already exposed to general anesthesia rather than comparing anesthetic techniques. The models incorporate maternal, obstetric, fetal, and anesthesia-related variables, including the induction-to-delivery interval, for individualized pre-delivery risk estimation. The NICU admission model showed more consistent validation performance than the neonatal resuscitation model. These tools may support neonatal team notification, delivery-room readiness, and multidisciplinary planning in high-acuity cesarean deliveries.

articles.title: Non-invasive esophageal cancer screening in high-risk populations: a multi-omics integration model.
articles.authors: Li W, Cui Y, Wu J et al.
articles.abstract: Esophageal cancer (ESCA) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in China, with over 95% of patients diagnosed at advanced stages, resulting in low survival rates. Early detection is critical for improving outcomes, yet current screening methods are invasive or lack sensitivity. We developed a non-invasive early-detection model by integrating circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation and fragmentomics features. Using a three-layer stacked ensemble machine learning framework, we analyzed multicenter blood samples from 309 participants, including ESCA patients and high-risk individuals. The integrated model called ESim-seq (Esophageal Cancer Screening with Integrated Model) achieved an AUC of 0.994 (95% CI: 0.979-1.000) in validation. At 99% specificity, sensitivity reached 87.3%, with simulated screening showing a 24.8% increase in stage I detection. Stratified analyses confirmed robustness across demographics, risk factors, and tumor stages. Clinical benefit modeling projected a 56.3% stage I detection rate under ideal conditions, significantly improving survival outcomes compared to standard care. This study developed a cfDNA-based analytical framework and demonstrated the advantage of multi-feature integration for early detection of ESCA.

articles.title: Neonatal sepsis.
articles.authors: Dramowski A, Bekker A, Bielicki J et al.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis and preterm birth are leading contributors to childhood death and disability in sepsis survivors. Whereas deaths from infectious diseases of childhood have declined substantially worldwide, progress in reducing neonatal sepsis burden and impact has stagnated in many low-income and middle-income countries. Efforts to track and prevent neonatal sepsis are hampered by the lack of a universally accepted case definition, gaps in global surveillance programmes, varied clinical presentations, and paucity of accurate and affordable sepsis diagnostics. The changing epidemiology of neonatal sepsis with predominance of Gram-negative pathogens, antimicrobial resistance, scarcity of and inequitable access to novel antibiotics, and under-representation of neonates in antibiotic clinical trials, are key issues impeding optimal treatment. Research and programmatic interventions to accelerate neonatal sepsis prevention and treatment should be prioritized alongside preterm birth prevention. Key actions include improving clinical care and infection prevention practices, and developing new diagnostic tests and vaccines that target the most common neonatal sepsis pathogens, particularly those responsible for the greatest morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Personalised mobile health coaching from early pregnancy to 12-months postpartum for females at risk of gestational diabetes (Bump2Baby and Me): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: O'Reilly SL, McAuliffe F, Teede H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal overweight and obesity increase the risk of gestational diabetes and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Digital health interventions offer scalable, personalised support, but evidence for interventions spanning both pregnancy and postpartum remains scarce. We evaluated the effectiveness of a personalised mobile health (mHealth) coaching intervention for females at increased risk of gestational diabetes.
METHODS: This multicentre, randomised controlled trial conducted in Australia, Ireland, Spain, and the UK enrolled pregnant females aged 18 years and older between 12-24 weeks of gestation with increased risk of gestational diabetes (Monash GDM risk tool score ≥3; tool risk factors were maternal age, BMI, ethnicity, family history of diabetes, and past history of gestational diabetes). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using computer-generated block randomisation (block size 200; stratified by site) to receive either personalised mHealth coaching via smartphone providing synchronous and asynchronous support through pregnancy to 12 months postpartum alongside usual maternity care, or usual maternity care alone. Usual maternity care, including gestational diabetes screening and management, continued unchanged in both groups, and both groups received Bluetooth-enabled scales. Participants and health coaches could not be masked to allocation; clinical staff providing usual care, laboratory staff, and trial statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was the between-group mean difference in BMI at 12 months postpartum among females at risk of gestational diabetes. The trial was registered at Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trials Register, ACTRN12620001240932.
FINDINGS: Between Feb 9, 2021, and Oct 22, 2023, 4386 females were screened, 3521 were excluded, and 865 were randomly assigned (437 to the mHealth intervention group and 428 to the control group). The mean age of participants was 35·2 years (SD 4·3), and most participants were White (588 [73%] of 804). Mean BMI change did not differ between groups (intervention, -0·04 kg/m2 [SE 0·12] vs control, 0·04 kg/m2 [0·13]). Adverse events were recorded in 18% (79 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 25% (106 of 428) of participants in the control group; serious adverse events occurred in 6% (28 of 437) of participants in the intervention group and 9% (40 of 428) of participants in the control group. No adverse or serious adverse events were considered related to the…

articles.title: Key Determinants and Clinical Impact of Male Factor Infertility: From Etiology to Treatment.
articles.authors: Dinkelman-Smit M, Antonio L, Jorgensen N et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Male factor infertility (MFI) contributes to a substantial proportion of couple infertility, yet the male partner is often incompletely evaluated, particularly when medically assisted reproduction is pursued. New clinical, hormonal and genetic classification systems, and evidence linking MFI to broader male health, are changing how these men should be assessed.
OBJECTIVE: To summarise the key determinants, classification systems, diagnostics and treatments of MFI, and the environmental, nutritional and lifestyle factors influencing male fertility, with their implications for personalized therapy and for men's reproductive and general health.
EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: A narrative review was conducted based on expert consensus and a focused review of the literature. Key publications were identified from major international guidelines, high-impact reviews, and original studies relevant to MFI. Evidence was selected to reflect clinically relevant developments in diagnostics, classification systems, and management.
EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Genetic variants, environmental exposures and lifestyle choices are key determinants of male fertility. Three complementary classification systems - pathophysiological, endocrine (APHRODITE) and phenotypic (Human Phenotype Ontology) - aid diagnosis, standardized communication and gene discovery. Hormonal and surgical treatments are effective but should be personalized, and evidence for several add-on diagnostics and empirical therapies remains limited. The limitations of current diagnostics, such as semen analysis, are critically evaluated. As a consensus-based narrative review without a systematic search, selection bias cannot be excluded.
CONCLUSIONS: MFI is multifactorial, requiring a holistic approach to diagnosis and treatment. Comprehensive andrological assessment, alongside personalized treatment strategies, is essential for optimizing fertility outcomes and addressing comorbidities in subfertile men.

articles.title: Prehabilitation before cytoreductive or debulking surgery for peritoneal malignancies: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Sand O, Graf W, Cashin P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To map the extent, characteristics and findings of research on prehabilitation interventions including at least one component of physical exercise for patients undergoing surgery for peritoneal malignancies and to identify research gaps.
DESIGN: We conducted a scoping review following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology.
DATA SOURCES: Six databases were systematically searched from inception to November 2025. Reference lists of the included articles were also screened.
ELIGIBILITY: Quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods studies published in English or Swedish were eligible if they included adults undergoing cytoreductive surgery (CRS) or debulking surgery with/without hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) for peritoneal malignancies and evaluated prehabilitation interventions comprising at least one component of physical exercise.
SCREENING AND DATA EXTRACTION: Sources were screened in Rayyan and data were extracted using a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet. Data were synthesised descriptively.
RESULTS: 15 articles from 14 studies published between 2021 and 2025 were included. Most studies were conducted in Europe and predominantly involved ovarian cancer patients. Studies were mainly small, non-randomised and feasibility-focused. Most combined resistance training and aerobic exercise within multimodal interventions. Prehabilitation was commonly described as feasible and acceptable, and within-group improvements in functional-capacity measures were commonly reported, although evidence from between-group comparisons was limited. Findings related to postoperative, nutritional and psychological outcomes and setting were heterogeneous.
CONCLUSIONS: The current body of research on prehabilitation in patients undergoing CRS or debulking surgery with/without HIPEC is recent, limited and heterogeneous in study design, intervention content and outcome measures. Furthermore, it is heavily dominated by ovarian cancer, limiting generalisability of findings to males and patients with non-gynaecological peritoneal malignancies. Future research should prioritise adequately powered randomised controlled trials, transparent reporting of intervention components and controls, and carefully select outcome measures to enable accurate evaluation of prehabilitation in this population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: An a priori protocol was registered in Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/R2BH8).

articles.title: Impact of Prior Bisphosphonates Exposure on the Efficacy of Denosumab in Patients with Osteoporosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.authors: Chen L, Han D, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether prior bisphosphonates (BPs) use for ≥ 12 months affects the efficacy of denosumab (DEN) in the treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, postmenopausal women aged over 50 years were recruited and divided into two groups based on prior BPs use: the BPs-DEN group comprised patients with ≥ 12-month prior BPs use and the DEN group comprised antiosteoporotic treatment-naïve patients. Endpoints included percentage change from baseline in bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers (BTMs) at month 24. Propensity score matching (PSM) was employed for sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Of 132 patients, 41 were in the BPs-then-DEN group, and 91 in the DEN-only group. At baseline, BTMs in the DEN-only group were significantly higher than in the BPs-then-DEN group (P < 0.001). There was no difference in the baseline BMD between the two groups. After adjusting for age at menopause, ALP, AST, UA, 25(OH)D, corrected calcium, and phosphorus, the DEN-only group demonstrated superior suppression of BTMs than the BPs-then-DEN group at months 12 and 24 (P < 0.05). The DEN-only group showed a greater BMD increase in total hip (TH) at month 24 compared with the BPs-then-DEN group (median: 2.43% [IQR, -1.13% to 6.06%] vs 0.42% [IQR, -1.18% to 3.01%]; P = 0.031). PSM analysis further confirmed the results.
CONCLUSION: Compared with the BPs-then-DEN group, the DEN-only group demonstrated superior suppression of BTMs and greater improvement in THBMD, which may be partially attributable to the higher baseline BTMs in the DEN-only group.

articles.title: Epigenetic Divergence Distinguishes Molecularly and Histologically Distinct Subtypes of Small Cell Carcinoma of the Ovary Hypercalcemic Type.
articles.journal: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
articles.authors: Diwan SS, Akiki G, Kommoss FKF et al.
articles.abstract: Small cell carcinoma of the ovary, hypercalcemic type (SCCOHT) is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy defined by inactivation of the SWItch/Sucrose Non-Fermentable (SWI/SNF) chromatin remodeling complex, specifically SMARCA4. It predominantly affects adolescent and young women, with poor survival despite radical surgery and multi-agent chemotherapy. Novel targeted agents have emerged with variable success. Here, we show that DNA methylation profiling stratifies SCCOHT (n= 63) into two distinct clusters with different morphologies: SCCOHT-1 exhibits typical features, including small cells and follicle-like spaces, while SCCOHT-2 exhibits large cells and rhabdoid morphology. Despite these differences, both clusters showed low copy number variation burden, reinforcing SWI/SNF deficiency as the central oncogenic driver. Differential methylation analysis revealed CpG island hypermethylation and open sea hypomethylation in SCCOHT-2, consistent with reprogramming of promoter and enhancer compartments. These epigenetic states were mirrored by distinct chromatin regulator signatures, differentiation programs, and calcium-regulatory networks. Immunohistochemistry further delineated the subtypes: WT1 was negative in SCCOHT-2, whereas it was diffusely expressed in SCCOHT-1. Keratins and cyclin D1 showed the opposite profile and were absent in SCCOHT-1. p16 was abnormal in both clusters: it was diffusely expressed in SCCOHT-2 and absent in SCCOHT-1. Clinically, both subtypes presented at a young age and were aggressive; however, hypercalcemia was restricted to SCCOHT-1. These findings establish SCCOHT heterogeneity despite uniform SWI/SNF ATPase loss, with implications for lineage specification and therapeutic stratification.

articles.title: Different strategies for medical management before frozen embryo transfer in patients with adenomyosis.
articles.authors: Cozzolino M, Roncarati I, Garcia Velasco JA
articles.abstract: Adenomyosis is associated with reduced implantation and live birth rates after in vitro fertilization, and medical pretreatment is widely used before frozen embryo transfer, although its benefit remains debated. This narrative review, informed by a systematic literature search, appraises the evidence on gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (GnRHa) pretreatment, alternative medical strategies, and frozen embryo transfer management, grading each strategy by study design and certainty of evidence and separating crude from confounder-adjusted estimates. Meta-analyses restricted to frozen embryo transfer and the only randomized trial comparing GnRHa pretreatment with no pretreatment did not show improved live birth, and adjusted cohort studies yielded inconsistent results; the overall certainty of evidence is low. However, adenomyosis is a heterogeneous disease: junctional-zone involvement, particularly when combined with outer-myometrial disease, carries the poorest prognosis, and pooling different phenotypes may conceal a benefit in selected women. Because GnRHa does not suppress estrogen production within adenomyotic lesions, combined suppression with an aromatase inhibitor is biologically plausible, but clinical data are limited to case series and one retrospective cohort and remain hypothesis-generating. Letrozole monotherapy was comparable with GnRHa in one randomized trial, whereas progestin-based strategies and oral GnRH antagonists lack robust reproductive data. Randomized trials stratified by standardized phenotype are needed to identify the women who benefit from pretreatment.

articles.title: Vericiguat attenuates cardiac inflammation and oxidative stress in an obese postmenopausal rat model with concurrent modulation of PKG-I, TGF-β1, and NF-κB.
articles.authors: Raeini AS, Khaksari M, Bashiri H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation and oxidative stress are implicated in cardiometabolic changes associated with menopause and obesity. This study investigated the effects of Vericiguat (VER) alone and in combination with estradiol (E2) on oxidative, inflammatory, atherogenic and fibrosis-related markers in cardiac tissue in an ovariectomized rat model of diet-induced obesity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Female Wistar rats were divided into sham and ovariectomized (OVX) groups and fed a standard diet (SD) or high-fat diet (HFD) for 4 months, followed by 4 weeks of treatment with E2, two doses of VER, or their combination. Body weight, malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), plasma atherogenic index (AIP), cardiac risk indices I and II (CRI-I and CRI-II), cardiac hydroxyproline, and expression of cardiac PKG-I, NF-κB, and TGF-β1 proteins were assessed.
RESULTS: OVX and HFD were associated with increased body weight, AIP, CRI-I, CRI-II, MDA, cardiac NF-κB and TGF-β1 expression, and hydroxyproline content, along with decreased TAC, TAC/MDA ratio, and PKG-I expression. E2 and VER treatments improved these alterations, as evidenced by reductions in AIP, CRI-I, CRI-II, MDA, NF-κB, TGF-β1, and hydroxyproline, as well as increases in TAC, TAC/MDA ratio, and PKG-I expression. Combined treatment with E2 and VER, compared to treatment with E2 alone, significantly improved all these parameters, with the exception of CRI-I and CRI-II. There were significant interactions between E2 and VER treatments were observed for TAC/MDA, hydroxyproline content, and TGF-β1 expression.
CONCLUSION: VER and E2 ameliorated several oxidative, inflammatory, atherogenic, and fibrosis-related changes in this model.

articles.title: Cervical cancer screening uptake and associated behavioral factors among female primary health care providers in Georgia: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Topuridze M, Shiukashvili N, Todua T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary health care (PHC) providers are instrumental in promoting cervical cancer screening, yet little is known about their own screening practices. This study assessed screening uptake and associated behavioral factors among female PHC providers in Georgia.
METHODS: A national cross-sectional survey was conducted in December 2023 among 1613 female PHC providers participating in a state-funded continuing medical education program on cancer screening. A self-administered questionnaire adapted from an International Agency for Research on Cancer screening barriers tool, tailored to the Georgian context, and informed by the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model assessed screening behavior and associated factors. Lifetime screening uptake was examined using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: 57% reported ever undergoing cervical cancer screening; among those ever screened, 42% had been screened within the previous three years. In bivariate analysis, recommending/referring ≥ 6 patients weekly was associated with higher screening uptake (OR=1.49; 95% CI: 1.16-1.90). In multivariable analysis, screening uptake was associated with urban practice (aOR=1.28; 95% CI: 1.02-1.60), screening-frequency knowledge (aOR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.01-1.54), sufficient information (aOR = 1.53; 95% CI: 1.22-1.93), confidence in accessing screening (aOR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.24-2.00), previous screening-related training (aOR = 1.32; 95% CI: 1.04-1.69), partner support (aOR = 1.92; 95% CI: 1.24-2.99), family support (aOR = 1.83; 95% CI: 1.34-2.51), perceived importance of screening (aOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.01-1.70), and definite future screening intention (aOR = 2.25; 95% CI: 1.75-2.87).
CONCLUSION: Screening uptake among female PHC providers remains suboptimal and was associated with factors across psychological capability, social opportunity, and reflective motivation.
POLICY SUMMARY: Findings identify screening knowledge, practical guidance, and social support as targets for future interventions to increase eligible female PHC providers' own participation in Georgia's national cervical cancer screening program, with effectiveness requiring prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Perillaldehyde (PAE) regulates ovarian cancer by modulating HSP70 and regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
articles.authors: Liu Z, Xu Z
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Perillaldehyde (PAE), a major active component of Perilla frutescens, possesses potential anti-tumor activity. However, its effects and mechanisms in ovarian cancer remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of PAE on ovarian cancer cells and a subcutaneous xenograft model, and explore the possible mechanisms involved.
METHODS: The effects of PAE on proliferation, migration, and invasion of SKOV3 and A2780 cells were assessed using CCK-8, colony formation, EdU, wound healing, and Transwell assays. Expression levels of HSP70, EMT-related proteins (E-cadherin, Vimentin, N-cadherin, MMP2/9), and PI3K/AKT pathway proteins were detected by Western blot. The role of HSP70 was validated by shRNA knockdown and plasmid overexpression. A nude mouse xenograft model was established to evaluate the in vivo anti-tumor effect.
RESULTS: PAE reduced cell viability, colony number, and EdU-positive cells in a concentration-dependent manner. PAE downregulated HSP70, Vimentin, N-cadherin, MMP2/9, decreased the ratios of p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT, while upregulating E-cadherin. HSP70 knockdown enhanced these effects, whereas overexpression weakened them. In vivo, PAE decreased tumor volume and weight, reduced Ki67-positive cells, and increased necrotic areas; protein changes were consistent with cell experiments.
CONCLUSION: PAE inhibits proliferation, migration, and invasion of ovarian cancer cells and slows tumor growth. The mechanism may involve HSP70 downregulation, PI3K/AKT inhibition, and EMT reversal, providing evidence for PAE as a candidate anti-ovarian cancer agent.

articles.title: Evidence-Based Guidance and Expert Recommendations to Address Preanalytical Variability in Urine Cell-Free DNA Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
articles.authors: Greytak SR, Murtaza M, Engel KB et al.
articles.abstract: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) analysis of urine specimens has shown great promise as a noninvasive means for biomarker detection in patients with cancer. However, the transition from experimental to clinically viable assays has been hindered by low sensitivity and low reproducibility among studies. The accurate assessment of urine cfDNA is critically affected by preanalytical handling of the urine specimen. The recommendations developed by a National Cancer Institute multidisciplinary working group include strategies to mitigate the impact of preanalytical factors on urinary cfDNA end points. Through review of published literature and experience-based discussions, the working group developed a National Cancer Institute Biospecimen Evidence-Based Practice (BEBP) document for Cell-Free DNA: Urine Collection and Processing, adaptable, fit-for-purpose guidance that implements a data-driven, decision-making approach. Like other published BEBPs, this BEBP contains step-by-step procedural guidelines, as well as summaries of the literature and expert recommendations on which they are based. Recommendations in the BEBP are applicable for the study of transrenal cfDNA and cfDNA originating from the genitourinary tract and are suitable for implementation in research and clinical settings ranging from large institutions to resource-limited laboratories. The findings, along with the BEBP, can serve as a template to generate evidence-based, standard operating procedures to improve the sensitivity and reproducibility of urinary cfDNA assays.

articles.title: The association between state abortion policies and fertility: A legal epidemiology analysis.
articles.authors: Berglas NF, Baumle D, Ghorashi AR et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: State abortion policies have shaped access to abortion care across the United States for decades, yet their associations with fertility outcomes are not fully understood. We examined associations between multiple state-level abortion policies and fertility outcomes, with a primary focus on births.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study linking legal epidemiology data on 11 abortion policy types to U.S. birth certificate data from 2005 to 2021. The primary outcome was monthly counts of live births by month and year of conception for each state. We used Poisson regression models with robust standard errors to estimate associations between abortion policies and births while adjusting for state-level covariates, state and year fixed effects, and state-specific time trends.
RESULTS: The sample included 65,915,535 births across 10,404 state-month-year observations. In adjusted models including all policies, six-week/fetal heartbeat gestational bans (IRR 1.14, 95% CI 1.11-1.18), 20-week/fetal pain bans (IRR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), 22-to-24-week/viability bans (IRR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and restrictions on in-person medication abortion (IRR 1.02, 95% CI 1.01-1.03) were associated with increased birth rates.
CONCLUSIONS: Specific types of abortion policies, particularly gestational bans and restrictions on in-person medication abortion, were associated with increased birth rates, even after accounting for other abortion policies and the broader socioeconomic and political environment. As states continue to enforce a range of abortion restrictions and policymakers consider future abortion protections, these findings highlight the importance of understanding how individual policy types may shape population-level fertility outcomes.
IMPLICATIONS: Policies restricting abortion later in pregnancy and in-person medication abortion may contribute to measurable increases in births. These findings suggest that variation in state abortion policies can influence reproductive outcomes and should inform discussions about the consequences of specific abortion policy approaches.

articles.title: Abortion information, awareness of methods, and self-efficacy among U.S. adolescents and young adults.
articles.authors: Larsen C, Whitfield B, Carpenter E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Characterize receipt of abortion information, awareness of abortion methods, and abortion self-efficacy among young people in the US. Examine associations between receipt of abortion information and awareness of abortion methods and self-efficacy.
STUDY DESIGN: We analyzed national, population-based data from the 2024 YouR HeAlth Survey, administered online via Ipsos KnowledgePanel among adolescents and young adults (AYA) ages 15-29 assigned female at birth (n=1,203). We assessed receipt of abortion information in the past year, awareness of abortion methods, and abortion self-efficacy. We conducted weighted bivariate analyses and multivariable linear regressions to assess associations with sociodemographic characteristics and policy environment.
RESULTS: Overall, 20.3% of AYA received abortion information in the past year. On average, AYA knew of 2 out of 4 abortion methods, with lower awareness of telehealth medication abortion (teleMAB) and self-managed abortion (SMA) than procedural or medication abortion. Mean self-efficacy for obtaining an abortion was 10.1 out of 20. AYA who received abortion information were aware of more methods (aβ=0.37, 95% CI=0.16, 0.59) and had higher self-efficacy (aβ=0.92, 95% CI=0.02, 1.83) than those who did not. Policy environment was not associated with awareness, but AYA living in protective environments had higher self-efficacy scores than those residing in restrictive policy environments (aβ=2.15, 95% CI: [1.37, 2.93]).
CONCLUSIONS: Receipt of abortion information, awareness of methods, especially teleMAB and SMA, and abortion self-efficacy are low among AYA, although AYA who received abortion information had higher awareness and self-efficacy.
IMPLICATIONS: Given that receiving abortion information was associated with higher awareness and self-efficacy, providing AYA information about navigating the complex legal landscape and their various options may help improve access to abortion care.

articles.title: The association between antiretroviral therapy regimen and contraceptive failure among Malawian women living with HIV using injectable, progestin-based hormonal contraception.
articles.authors: Diepstra K, Westreich D, Cottrell M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Drug-drug interactions between antiretroviral therapy (ART) and hormonal contraceptives are critical to understand for women with HIV (WWH) who do not desire pregnancy. One hormonal contraceptive commonly used among WWH in sub-Saharan Africa is depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA). We aimed to estimate the effect of efavirenz- versus dolutegravir-based ART on pregnancy incidence among Malawian WWH using DMPA contraception and ART as prescribed.
STUDY DESIGN: Using Family Planning and Antiretroviral Therapy (FP-ART) cohort data, we identified participants who initiated DMPA at enrollment and followed participants until DMPA or ART discontinuation, occurrence of first pregnancy, self-reported pregnancy intention of "now" or "in the next year", study dropout, or administrative censoring. We examined the time-varying exposure of ART regimen type (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and lamivudine, with either efavirenz or dolutegravir). The outcome was clinically-detected pregnancy. We used inverse probability weights to fit marginal structural Poisson regression models to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs).
RESULTS: 689 participants initiated DMPA at enrollment; 41 pregnancies were captured during 827 person-years of follow-up (crude incidence rate: 5.0/100 person-years, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.7, 6.7; crude efavirenz rate: 6.1 conceptions per 100 person-years, 95% CI: 4.3, 8.7; crude dolutegravir rate: 3.3 conceptions per 100 person-years, 95% CI: 1.8, 5.9). Restricted to person-time where DMPA was taken as prescribed, the crude incidence rate was 4.4/100 person-years (95% CI: 3.1, 6.2). The weighted IRR for consistently using efavirenz-based ART versus dolutegravir-based ART among those taking DMPA as prescribed was 1.90 (95% CI: 0.67, 5.40).
CONCLUSIONS: Among WWH who were taking DMPA as prescribed, we did not find evidence of an elevated pregnancy rate with continuous efavirenz- versus dolutegravir-based ART use, however the 95% confidence intervals were wide. Further understanding causes of contraceptive failure among WWH who use DMPA and ART is essential.
IMPLICATIONS: This work contributes to the growing evidence of possible drug-drug interactions between depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) and antiretroviral medications, such as efavirenz. This analysis underscores the safety of dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy.

articles.title: The PELICANS Registry: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Extended Longitudinal Investigation of Clinical Outcomes-Adverse Events, Nonrecovery, and Survival.
articles.authors: Santana AUL, Singh M, Pachariyanon P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) disproportionately affects Black women, yet long-term outcome data in socially vulnerable, predominantly Black cohorts remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to characterize long-term outcomes and baseline predictors of survival, major adverse events (MAEs), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) recovery in a U.S. PPCM cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective-prospective registry included 159 women with PPCM (1982-2024). Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, MAEs, and LVEF recovery (≥50%). Multivariable and extended Cox models evaluated predictors, adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy.
RESULTS: The cohort was 80.5% Black. Over a median 9.0-year follow-up (IQR: 3.4-15.5), 41 patients (25.8%) died and 64 (40.3%) had MAEs. Among 148 patients with echocardiographic follow-up, 69 (46.6%) had sustained LVEF recovery, though 23 (25.0% of initially recovered) declined to LVEF <50%. Independent mortality predictors included elevated creatinine (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.86; 95% CI: 1.37-5.97), lower index LVEF (aHR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.98), family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure (aHR: 3.27; 95% CI: 1.41-7.56), and non-O blood type (aHR: 2.36; 95% CI: 1.04-5.33), retaining significance after adjusting for LVEF recovery and subsequent pregnancy (n = 62). Elevated creatinine increased MAE odds (adjusted OR: 7.09; 95% CI: 1.98-32.9), while higher LVEF, parity, and obesity reduced them. Baseline LV dilation (≥60 mm), Black race, older age, and family history of cardiomyopathy or heart failure predicted lower LVEF recovery odds.
CONCLUSIONS: This long-term predominantly Black PPCM cohort had high mortality, low LVEF recovery, and frequent late relapse. These findings highlight the importance of baseline risk stratification and sustained echocardiographic surveillance to guide clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Metabolomic signatures and pathways linking maternal PFAS concentrations to gestational age at birth: a meet-in-the-middle and high dimensional mediation analysis.
articles.authors: Hoffman SS, Dunlop AL, Barr DB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth disproportionately affects Black and African American populations. Greater exposure to environmental toxicants driven by environmental racism may contribute to these disparities. We aimed to identify metabolic intermediates linking maternal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure to gestational age at birth (GA).
METHODS: We analyzed participants from the Atlanta African American Maternal Child Cohort (2014-2018) with maternal serum collected during early pregnancy (8-14 weeks; n = 307) and late pregnancy (24-30 weeks; n = 238). PFAS concentrations were measured using targeted exposure assessment, and untargeted metabolomics was conducted on maternal serum. GA was abstracted from medical records. We applied two complementary mediation frameworks, Meet-in-the-Middle (MITM) and High-dimensional Mediation Analysis (HIMA), to identify metabolites and pathways linking PFAS exposure with GA outcomes.
RESULTS: Higher maternal concentrations of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) were associated with increased risk of earlier GA. MITM identified 47 candidate metabolites in early pregnancy and 25 in late pregnancy. HIMA identified palmitoleic acid in early pregnancy and cortisol and N-acetyl-D-galactosamine in late pregnancy. Findings across the two approaches highlighted candidate metabolic signals and pathways, including the tricarboxylic acid cycle, bile acid biosynthesis, steroid hormone biosynthesis, and purine metabolism.
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal PFAS exposure was associated with metabolic perturbations that may represent putative biological pathways related to gestational age at birth. This study offers new insights into the potential pathways by which maternal PFAS levels shape the maternal metabolome and influence GA using cutting-edge, targeted exposure assessment, untargeted metabolomics technologies, and high-dimensional mediation techniques.

articles.title: A peritoneal cancer index above 14 is associated with incomplete cytoreduction in cytoreductive surgery with HIPEC for high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.authors: Bertolucci A, Rreka E, Piccini L et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The peritoneal cancer index (PCI) is used both to predict resectability and to estimate prognosis in ovarian cancer. We aimed to identify the PCI threshold predicting incomplete cytoreduction at cytoreductive surgery (CRS) with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC), and to describe its relation to survival.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective single-centre cohort of 112 consecutive patients with high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma treated with CRS and cisplatin HIPEC (2016-2023): 87 at interval CRS after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (primary population) and 25 at secondary CRS. PCI was related to residual disease (CC-1/2) with bootstrap-corrected ROC analysis and Firth regression, and to survival with Cox models and restricted mean survival time (RMST).
RESULTS: At interval CRS, residual disease occurred in 10/26 patients (38%) with PCI > 14 and in 2/61 (3%) with PCI ≤ 14 (AUC 0.82; optimism-corrected 0.82). PCI > 14 was associated with shorter overall survival (median 27 vs 57 months; HR 2.15 (1.11-4.16)) and progression-free survival (RMST difference at 36 months -7.1 months, 95% CI -12.9 to -1.2). Small-bowel or mesenteric involvement, abstracted blind from operative reports, did not predict residual disease independently of PCI > 14. With complete cytoreduction (n = 75), each PCI point was associated with shorter overall survival (HR 1.07 (1.01-1.12)).
CONCLUSION: At CRS-HIPEC for high-grade serous ovarian cancer, PCI > 14 identifies patients in whom complete cytoreduction is uncertain, reflecting total disease burden rather than small-bowel involvement alone. PCI retained prognostic information after complete cytoreduction. The threshold should guide surgical planning and counselling rather than exclusion, and requires external validation.

articles.title: Performance of HPV-test screening in young women: Results from a population-based study in Brazil.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Vale DB, Rego RM, Discacciati MG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brazil is transitioning to HPV-based cervical cancer screening. In this context, this study aimed to analyze outcomes in young women during the first five years of a population-based HPV-testing screening program.
METHODS: We followed a prospective cohort of women screened in the first round of the program in the city of Indaiatuba, São Paulo state. The subjects were all women screened through the public health system in the period (2017-2023). We analyzed two groups: women aged 25-29 and 30-34. The main outcome was cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or above (CIN3 + ). We estimated risk using relative risk with a 95 % confidence interval (RR).
RESULTS: In this five-year study, we screened 2,742 women aged 25-29 and 2,552 women aged 30-34. The prevalence of HPV-positive tests (HPV + ) was 23.2 versus 16.6 per 100 women, respectively (RR 1.40, 1.26-1.57). The risk in women 25-29 was higher for 16/18+ (RR 1.40, 1.13-1.74); other high-risk types and abnormal cytology (RR 1.27, 1.01--1.61); and colposcopy referrals (12.7 % versus 9.4 %, RR 1.34, 1.15-1.57). The risk of CIN3 + was lower in women 25-29 (RR 0.58, 0.38;0.90) and in those 16/18+ (RR 0.53, 0.32-0.87).
CONCLUSIONS: A lower detection capacity in detecting precursor lesions was observed in women aged 25-29. The colposcopy referral rate was higher but not clinically significant. Genotyping was crucial for triaging higher-risk women.
POLICY SUMMARY: It seems reasonable to recommend isolated HPV testing for women aged 25 to 29 years and withdraw cytology-based screening from primary health care to avoid resource overuse.

articles.title: The impact of non-radical hysterectomy on urinary functions: urodynamic assessment - a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Arseni RM, Angelis E, Cuccu I et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-radical hysterectomy is among the most frequently performed gynecological surgical procedures worldwide; nevertheless, its potential implication as an etiological factor of urinary dysfunction remains a matter of ongoing debate. The present meta-analysis is designed to systematically evaluate the impact of non-radical hysterectomy, stratifying by surgical access, on urodynamics dysfunction.
METHODS: A systematic search of the literature was conducted up to October 2025 using predefined keywords related to urodynamics and urinary incontinence. Randomized controlled trials and prospective observational studies evaluating patients undergoing simple hysterectomy with both pre- and postoperative urodynamic assessments were included. Case reports, reviews, editorials, and studies involving radical hysterectomy or prolapse surgery were excluded. Six studies met the inclusion criteria.
RESULTS: A total of 738 patients from six studies were included. No significant postoperative changes were observed in Q-max (MD -0.33 mL/s; 95% CI: -3.28 to 2.62), total bladder capacity (MD 7.55 mL; 95% CI: -13.68 to 28.78), residual urine volume (MD 1.27 mL; 95% CI: -1.98 to 4.52), maximal urethral closure pressure (MD 12.73; 95% CI: -11.21 to 36.67), voided volume (MD 9.99; 95% CI: -5.66 to 25.63) or bladder volume at first desire (MD 18.07; 95% CI: -6.81 to 42.94).
CONCLUSION: The present meta-analysis suggests that non-radical hysterectomy non-radical hysterectomy is not associated with significant postoperative changes across key urodynamic parameters.

articles.title: Depressive symptoms, possible sarcopenia, and functional disability among Chinese adults aged 50 years or more: A five-wave longitudinal study.
articles.authors: Mai T, Chao G
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine separate and joint associations of baseline depressive symptoms and possible sarcopenia with repeatedly assessed functional disability among Chinese adults aged 50 years or more.
STUDY DESIGN: Five-wave longitudinal cohort analysis, 2011-2020.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The presence of depressive symptoms was defined as a score ≥ 10 on the 10-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale. Possible sarcopenia was defined as low handgrip strength determined using the 2025 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia age- and sex-specific thresholds because directly measured muscle mass was unavailable. We assessed disability in terms of basic and instrumental activities of daily living, separately and jointly. Modified Poisson generalized estimating equations estimated risk ratios; logistic models provided standardized risks and risk differences with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Of 9346 eligible participants, 8790 contributed 30,366 complete-case person-wave observations. Compared with neither exposure, adjusted risk ratios were 1.38 (95% confidence interval 1.32-1.44) for depressive symptoms only, 1.27 (1.18-1.37) for possible sarcopenia only, and 1.46 (1.38-1.56) for both. Standardized risks were 30.7%, 41.3%, 38.0%, and 46.0%, respectively. The risk difference for both versus neither was 15.3 percentage points (12.6-18.1). Additive interaction was -2.6 percentage points (-6.2 to 1.2), and the multiplicative interaction ratio was 0.84 (0.77-0.91). After multiple imputation, the contrast between the two single-exposure groups attenuated (risk ratio 1.06, 0.99-1.13).
CONCLUSIONS: Participants with both exposures had the highest standardized risk, but there was no evidence of positive additive interaction and the joint association was less than multiplicative. The clinical usefulness of joint assessment requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Investigation of the effects of myricetin on ovarian and oocyte quality against experimental ischemia-reperfusion damage with microscopic and biochemical analysis.
articles.authors: Aydın S, Özbek Kurtul B, Şahin E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Ovarian torsion is a gynecological emergency in which detorsion-associated ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury poses a significant threat to ovarian reserve and follicular integrity. Myricetin, a naturally occurring flavonoid with well-characterized antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties, represents a promising pharmacological candidate for mitigating IR-induced ovarian damage. This study aimed to evaluate the protective efficacy of myricetin against IR injury following detorsion in an experimental rat model of ovarian torsion, with particular emphasis on ovarian morphology, follicular dynamics, oocyte quality, and markers of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty-two female Wistar albino rats were randomly allocated to four experimental groups: Control, Ischemia, Ischemia-Reperfusion (IRG), and Myricetin Treatment. Bilateral ovarian torsion was induced in all groups except the Control. Detorsion was performed after 3 h of ischemia in the IRG and Treatment groups, whereas torsion was left in place without detorsion (permanent ischemia) in the Ischemia group; animals in the Treatment group received a single dose of intraperitoneal myricetin (20 mg/kg) immediately at the onset of reperfusion. Following a controlled ovarian stimulation protocol, all animals in all four groups were sacrificed on day 20. Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), glutathione (GSH), nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) levels were quantified. Left ovarian samples were assessed histologically and immunohistochemically using Hematoxylin & Eosin (H&E), Masson's trichrome, and antibodies against Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) and Caspase-3. Right ovaries were processed for oocyte count and maturation assessment.
RESULTS: Histological evaluation revealed severe vascular dilatation, hemorrhage, interstitial edema, and advanced follicular degeneration in the Ischemia and IRG groups compared with Controls (p < 0.001). Myricetin treatment significantly attenuated these structural alterations, with histomorphological findings comparable to the Control group (p > 0.05) and significantly superior to both the Ischemia and IRG groups. VEGF and Caspase-3 immunoreactivity were markedly upregulated in the Ischemia and IRG groups (p < 0.001), whereas myricetin treatment resulted in moderate yet significant downregulation of both markers (p < 0.05…

articles.title: Evidence of metabolic-redox impairment and a disulfidptosis-like phenotype induced by zearalenone in GC-2 mouse spermatocyte-derived cells.
articles.authors: Zavaglia L, Venditti M, Biasi A et al.
articles.abstract: Alterations in the balance between cell proliferation and death during spermatogenesis, which may contribute to infertility, are influenced by several factors, including exposure to environmental mycotoxins. Among these, zearalenone (ZEN) impairs spermatogenesis through poorly understood mechanisms. Here, we investigated the toxic effects of ZEN in GC-2 mouse spermatocyte-derived cells. ZEN significantly inhibited cell growth and caused metabolic dysfunction. Bioenergetic profiling by Seahorse XF analysis revealed a marked decline in mitochondrial respiration and glycolytic reserve, reflecting impaired metabolic flexibility. Consistent with these findings, ZEN-mediated reductions in PPARγ and GLUT1 protein expression further supported dysregulation of mitochondrial metabolism and glucose homeostasis. These metabolic alterations disrupted cellular redox balance, resulting in increased oxidative stress. Indeed, ZEN enhanced reactive oxygen species production and upregulated HO-1 mRNA and protein expression. NAC treatment attenuated these effects and restored TOMM20 expression, as assessed by immunofluorescence analysis, suggesting a role for oxidative stress in mitochondrial structural alterations. Furthermore, ZEN induced ferroptosis-associated features, including membrane lipid peroxidation and intracellular Fe²⁺ accumulation. Nevertheless, ferroptosis inhibitors failed to restore cell viability, indicating that ferroptosis is not the primary mechanism of cell death. Conversely, ZEN upregulated both Slc7a11 and Slc3a2 expression and promoted disulfide stress, as evidenced by reduced free protein thiol content, associated with altered F-actin organization. Importantly, NAC restored intracellular thiol pools, mitigated actin disorganization, and rescued cell viability. Collectively, these findings support the involvement of a disulfidptosis-like phenotype in ZEN-treated GC-2 cells, providing new insights into the metabolic and redox dysregulation underlying ZEN-mediated germ cell toxicity.

articles.title: Effects of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus on the Offspring's Neurodevelopment.
articles.authors: Estudillo E, Hernandez-Zarate A, Lazo-de-la-Vega-Monroy ML et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a major global health concern that affects up to 14% of pregnancies. Traditionally, it has been characterized by hyperglycemia and insulin resistance. However, GDM can also lead to long-term health consequences in offspring, particularly affecting neurodevelopment. It has been associated with an increased risk of cognitive deficits, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and emotional dysregulation in GDM-exposed offspring. Findings from human and experimental studies suggest that GDM disrupts cortical and hippocampal architecture, impairs synaptic plasticity, and induces epigenetic alterations in key neurodevelopmental genes. These mechanistic pathways include oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and altered neurotrophin expression and receptor signaling. Maternal metabolism, diet, and genetic background may negatively affect neurotrophin expression, which could impact fetal brain development. Lower levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and nerve growth factor (NGF) in maternal blood, placental tissue, and cord blood have been linked to poor neurodevelopmental outcomes. This suggests that neurotrophins could be considered potential biomarkers. This narrative review compiles the latest evidence on the effects of GDM on fetal brain development, emphasizing the role of neurotrophins, especially BDNF and NGF, as critical mediators in this process. Emerging data also suggest that glycemic control during pregnancy may partially restore neurotrophin levels and improve neurodevelopmental outcomes. Understanding the interaction between maternal glucose metabolism and fetal brain signaling pathways is essential for pregnancy care and the design of neuroprotective strategies.

articles.title: Translational science in modern gynecologic oncology trials.
articles.authors: Arend RC, Dave D, Cosgrove CM et al.
articles.abstract: Translational science is integral in deciding who would benefit the most from novel therapeutics in gynecologic oncology, yet the specimens, assays, and the data behind them are often handled inconsistently as the translational endpoints are planned late. Clinical trials involving PARP-inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), and antibody-drug conjugates in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancer show that a biomarker can serve as an eligibility criterion, a stratification factor, a pharmacodynamic measure, or an exploratory tool. This review presents an operational framework for integrating translational science into the trial designs from the outset. We define exploratory, integrated, and integral biomarker tiers and tie each to analytical validation, clinical validation, and level of evidence. It proposes minimum standards for tissue and blood biospecimen collection, adequacy, sampling schedule depending on specimen type, pre-analytical variables, clinical annotation, and reporting with BRISQ, SPREC, and the BloodPAC technical data elements. We also cover newer techniques like ctDNA, addressing their intended use, tumor-informed versus tumor-naive assays, and sampling for minimal residual disease. We then review genomic, transcriptomic, spatial, single-cell, proteomic, metabolomic, and functional platforms, and why discovery should not be treated as validation for modern gynecologic oncology trials. Additionally, maintaining standards for data integration, reproducibility, NIH data sharing in NCI-sponsored, industry-sponsored, and institutional trials is crucial. Ultimately, adaptive master protocols and ctDNA-guided trial designs are discussed as future directions as translational endpoints deserve the same prospective planning as the primary clinical endpoint.

articles.title: Racial and ethnic differences in ovarian cancer survival across SEER registry states.
articles.authors: Dunlap CE, Meade CE, Sinnott JA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether racial and ethnic differences in ovarian cancer survival exist across states, represented in National Cancer Institute's Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, and assess whether racial and ethnic differences in ovarian cancer survival differed by factors associated with ovarian cancer prognosis.
METHODS: Using SEER 17 data (2000-2022), we constructed a cohort of 103,554 epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, and primary peritoneal cancer cases. Self-reported race was cross-classified with the NAACCR Hispanic Identification Algorithm variable to create racial and ethnic groups. Multivariable adjusted Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for ovarian cancer-specific survival by race and ethnicity, overall and stratified by registry state, histotype, stage, and treatment, adjusting for a priori covariates. Geographic heterogeneity was assessed using the I-statistic. Sensitivity analyses were restricted to high-grade serous tumors.
RESULTS: Hispanic cases had similar ovarian cancer-specific survival, while Non-Hispanic (NH) Asian cases exhibited better ovarian cancer-specific survival than NH White cases across SEER registry states (I2 = 40.2%, p-het 0.08; I2 = 0.0%, p-het 0.52; respectively). NH Black cases generally had worse survival than NH White cases, except in Kentucky (HR: 1.01; 95%CI: 0.84-1.23) and Iowa (HR: 0.82; 95%CI: 0.55-1.22). NH Native Hawaiian/PI cases also had worse survival compared with NH White cases across SEER registry states (I2 = 0.0%; p-het 0.60).
CONCLUSION(S): Racial and ethnic disparities in ovarian cancer-specific survival are persistent and geographically consistent, suggesting broad, multi-level determinants rather than state-specific factors underscoring the need for national efforts to ensure uniform access to high-quality healthcare.

articles.title: Hormonal Birth Control Misinformation and Disinformation Online: Rebuilding Young Women's Trust.
articles.authors: Siegel JA, Chadwick SB, Brown RL et al.
articles.abstract: In recent years, social media content has increasingly portrayed hormonal birth control as harmful or unnecessary. Emerging evidence indicates that such content is shaping contraceptive decision-making among young women. Addressing this public health issue requires understanding the factors contributing to medical mistrust. We argue that negative attitudes toward hormonal birth control may be fueled by a legacy of harm in reproductive science and health care, which has historically led women to rely on one another for knowledge about their health. Social media has transformed women's long-standing peer knowledge sharing by amplifying sensationalized personal experiences and spreading misleading claims widely with limited opportunities for correction or clarification. Rather than asking why women do not trust science and medicine, we must ask what science and medicine can do to earn young women's trust. We offer multilevel suggestions for individuals, scientific and medical organizations, social media companies, medical professionals, funding bodies, health departments and public health practitioners, and lawmakers. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(12):1886-1893. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308746).

articles.title: Compliance to National Cancer Grid of India Guidelines for Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer: Results From a Multicentric Observational Cohort in India.
articles.authors: Chopra S, Hande V, Gupta A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cervical cancer is a major cause of mortality among Indian women. Concurrent chemoradiation and brachytherapy is the standard care for locally advanced cancer. This multi-institutional implementation audit evaluated adherence to National Cancer Grid (NCG)-recommended treatment guidelines.
METHODS: In the first phase, seven academic and private cancer centers registered consecutive patients treated with chemoradiotherapy and brachytherapy during a 6-month period (2019-2023). Infrastructure, equipment, staging, and treatment data were collected. Compliance to NCG guideline-defined metrics for external-beam radiation therapy, chemotherapy, brachytherapy, and overall treatment time was assessed using prespecified deviation criteria. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with deviations.
RESULTS: Of 697 patients, 569 received radical treatment. Stage IIB (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018) was most common. Almost 60% of patients traveled >100 km, 67.7% were nonobese, and 73.1% were younger than 60 years. Over 80% received three-dimensional conformal radiotherapy. For brachytherapy, computer tomography imaging was most frequent (66%). Although intracavitary applicators were used in 83%, hybrid intracavitary-interstitial brachytherapy was limited (6%). Prescription remained point A-based in 69%, although volume-based prescriptions increased through 2019-2022. Cisplatin was the commonest chemotherapy agent (80%). Only 36.6% of chemotherapy-eligible patients completed ≥5 cycles and 47.5% completed treatment <8 weeks. Obesity status, center type, and travel distances were associated with compliance deviations. Multivariable analyses confirmed private centers had lower odds of major/unacceptable overall treatment time-related deviations (odds ratio [OR], 0.39 [95% CI, 0.22 to 0.68]).
CONCLUSION: This audit highlights deviations from guideline-recommended practice, including prolonged treatment times, incomplete chemotherapy delivery, and limited use of advanced techniques. Prospective phase of this study will focus on implementation of quality indicators.

articles.title: HPV knowledge and willingness to vaccinate among unvaccinated female college students: A cross-sectional comparison between a comprehensive university and a health vocational college in Fujian, China.
articles.authors: Liao M, Guo Y, Li J et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a significant burden in China, and HPV vaccination is key to prevention. Female college students are a crucial target, yet knowledge and willingness may vary across institution types.
