To compare HPV knowledge and vaccination willingness between female students from a comprehensive university and a health vocational college, and identify associated factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted from May to June 2026 among 2,761 female undergraduate students (first- and second-year) recruited from one comprehensive university and one health vocational college in Fujian, China. An electronic questionnaire collected data on demographic characteristics, HPV knowledge, vaccination willingness, vaccine preferences, and reasons for unwillingness. The overall HPV vaccination willingness rate was 78.7% (2,173/2,761). The mean HPV knowledge score was 6.17 ± 2.66 (out of 10), with only 37.0%(1,021/2,761) achieving high knowledge. Non-healthcare majors scored higher than healthcare majors (6.28 vs. 5.97, p = .003). Six independent factors were identified: healthcare major (OR = 0.65), higher income (OR = 0.58), maternal vaccination (OR = 2.28), friend vaccination (OR = 1.89), sexual history (OR = 1.74), and higher knowledge (middle level OR = 1.80; high level OR = 2.02). Among willing participants, 66.3% (1,441/2,173) preferred the nonavalent vaccine, and 56.1% (1,218/2,173) were unsure about domestic vs. imported vaccines. Main reasons for unwillingness were adverse reaction concerns, cost, and a wait-and-see attitude. HPV vaccination willingness was relatively high among unvaccinated female college students in Fujian, China, but knowledge gaps persisted, particularly regarding the recommended vaccination age. Willingness was significantly associated with academic major, household income, social influences, and knowledge level. Targeted educational interventions, financial support, and peer-based strategies are needed.

articles.title: The p38α MAPK-MK2 axis drives chemotherapy-mediated nuclear actin remodeling to promote ovarian cancer progression.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Xing X, Zhang Z, Li L et al.
articles.abstract: Nuclear F-actin facilitates DNA damage repair and contributes to cancer chemoresistance. However, the regulatory mechanisms controlling its dynamic polymerization in response to genotoxic stress remain poorly defined. A major barrier in nuclear actin research is the lack of tools for precise, high-throughput analysis. To systematically investigate nuclear F-actin assembly in DNA damage response, we developed a deep learning pipeline, named nFANet, for high-throughput detection and analysis of nuclear F-actin. Here, using ovarian cancer-a malignancy where chemoresistance is a major clinical obstacle-as a model, we showed that platinum-based chemotherapy robustly induces nuclear F-actin assembly. A subsequent kinome screening, in combination with the application of nFANet, identified the kinase p38α MAPK as a critical upstream regulator of platinum-induced nuclear F-actin assembly. Mechanistically, the p38α MAPK-MK2 signaling pathway promotes formin-mediated nuclear F-actin assembly in response to chemotherapy. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition or genetic knockout of the p38α MAPK-MK2 pathway sensitized ovarian cancer cells to platinum-based therapy. Our work uncovers a key mechanism governing nuclear actin remodeling under genotoxic stress and lays the foundation for identifying a patient subgroup likely to benefit from therapeutic targeting of this pathway.

articles.title: Egg freezing - meeting social and clinical needs.
articles.authors: Khalifeh J, Sunkara S, Beebeejaun Y
articles.abstract: Egg freezing allows women to store their eggs for use at a later stage in life. It was originally developed for patients facing cancer treatment that could cause infertility, but today many women choose egg freezing because they have not yet found a partner, want more time to build a family, or are concerned about the natural decline in fertility with age. Thanks to advances in laboratory technique, most eggs now survive the freezing and thawing process. However, the chance of achieving a pregnancy in the future is strongly influenced by the woman's age at the time of egg collection. This review brings together current evidence on who benefits from egg freezing, what outcomes are realistic to expect, and the ethical and counselling considerations that should inform clinical practice.

articles.title: Anti-inflammatory effects of metformin in gestational diabetes: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials and preclinical animal pregnancy models study protocol.
articles.authors: Ogra IO, Oyibo A, Kernyuy FB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a significant complication that can occur during pregnancy. It is characterized by glucose intolerance that first arises during pregnancy and is associated with insulin resistance, which is linked to elevated inflammatory markers. Metformin has emerged as a promising treatment option for GDM, with growing evidence supporting its anti-inflammatory effects. These effects are thought to be mediated by activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and inhibition of NF-κB signaling. This systematic review aims to assess the anti-inflammatory effects of metformin in GDM, considering both clinical and preclinical studies.
METHODS: A systematic review of all randomized controlled trials and controlled in vivo experiments for animals published until 2026 will be carried out. A comprehensive search of all published articles indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, CINAHL (EBSCOhost), Embase, and Web of Science will be performed. Studies will be screened for eligibility by title, abstract, and full text in duplicate by two independent reviewers. For data where meta-analysis is not possible, a narrative analysis will be conducted using themes derived from the data. For data that allow meta-analysis, a random-effects meta-analysis will be conducted. This systematic review will be reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA).
DISCUSSION: The study will utilize meta-analysis to establish the anti-inflammatory effects of metformin in GDM, potentially influencing clinical practice and guidelines. Additionally, validating metformin's anti-inflammatory effects has important implications beyond immediate management of GDM, extending to long-term adverse outcomes for both the mother and the offspring.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261337881.

articles.title: Differential age-related patterns of Human Papillomavirus infection among women in Western Province, Zambia.
articles.authors: Liamba MA, Chisompola D, Mukutuma C et al.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection remains a major global public health concern and is the leading cause of cervical cancer, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Zambia has one of the highest cervical cancer burdens worldwide, yet evidence on age-specific determinants of HPV infection remains limited. This study assessed the prevalence and determinants of HPV infection among women aged ≤40 years and ≥41 years in Western Province, Zambia. A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 2025 and January 2026 among women attending cervical cancer screening clinics in Western Province. A total of 1,132 participants were recruited using consecutive sampling. Sociodemographic, behavioural, and reproductive data were collected using structured questionnaires. Exfoliated cervical samples were collected and tested for high-risk HPV genotypes using the Hologic Panther platform with transcription-mediated amplification (TMA). Mixed-effects logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with HPV infection while accounting for clustering at the health facility level. Overall, HPV prevalence was 33.6%. HPV prevalence was comparable between women aged ≤40 years and those aged ≥41 years (33.6% vs. 33.4%). Among women aged ≤40 years, multiple lifetime sexual partners, high parity, lack of HPV vaccination, contraceptive use, low income, single marital status, and rural facility location were independently associated with HPV infection (P < 0.05). Among women aged ≥41 years, high parity, low HPV knowledge, unemployment, low income, and geographic location were independently associated with HPV infection (P < 0.05). Spatial variation was also observed, with significantly higher infection rates in Mwandi district. HPV infection remains highly prevalent across, in both younger and older women. Although the determinants differ by age group, the substantial HIV burden and ongoing HIV transmission may contribute to the persistence of HPV infection. These findings support age-specific prevention strategies that integrate HPV vaccination, cervical cancer screening, health education and treatment services to reduce the burden of HPV infection.

articles.title: Unintended pregnancy and associated factors among women on antiretroviral therapy in selected public hospitals, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A mixed-method study.
articles.authors: Ageze AA, Yusuf KM, Alamdo AG et al.
articles.abstract: Unintended pregnancy remains a public health concern among women living with HIV, despite expanded access to antiretroviral therapy (ART) and reproductive health services. Evidence on its prevalence and associated factors among women receiving ART in Ethiopia is limited. This study assessed the prevalence of unintended pregnancy and associated factors among women receiving ART in selected public hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. A facility-based mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted among 384 women from June 12 to July 18, 2025. Quantitative data were collected using an interviewer-administered questionnaire and clinical record review. Participants were selected through systematic random sampling, while 14 participants were purposively selected for in-depth interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using binary logistic regression, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The prevalence of unintended pregnancy was 38.8% (n = 149). Higher odds of unintended pregnancy were observed among women who did not use contraception after HIV diagnosis (AOR = 4.77; 95% CI: 2.85-8.04), had been diagnosed with HIV for ≥5 years (AOR = 2.77; 95% CI: 1.44-5.34), had inadequate sexual and reproductive health counseling (AOR = 1.86; 95% CI: 1.08-3.20), or had not disclosed their HIV status to partners (AOR = 1.92; 95% CI: 1.11-3.31). Compared with women with no formal education, those with primary, secondary, and higher education had lower odds of unintended pregnancy (AOR = 0.31; 95% CI: 0.17-0.56; AOR = 0.24; 95% CI: 0.11-0.51; and AOR = 0.11; 95% CI: 0.02-0.66, respectively). Qualitative findings highlighted fear of side effects, partner opposition, contraceptive misconceptions, inadequate counseling, and fragmented services as contributors to contraceptive non-use and unintended pregnancies. More than one-third of women receiving ART experienced unintended pregnancy, highlighting gaps in integrated reproductive health services. Strengthening family planning integration into ART care and improving reproductive counseling may help reduce unintended pregnancy.

articles.title: Leveraging ultrashort echo time magnetic resonance imaging to quantify sex-specific adaptations to the glenoid labrum across the lifespan.
articles.authors: Vogel CM, Jung KJ, Hutzelmann DM et al.
articles.abstract: The glenoid labrum is a collagen‑rich fibrocartilage structure critical to shoulder stability yet susceptible to age‑related degeneration. Quantitative, in‑vivo assessment of its composition remains limited. Ultrashort echo time MRI with magnetization transfer (UTE‑MT) enables estimation of macromolecular fraction (MMF), a biomarker sensitive to the collagen‑rich matrix content of the glenoid labrum. This study investigated the effect of age, sex, menopause status, and arm dominance on the glenoid labrum MMF. Forty‑two healthy adults (25 females, mean age: 47 ± 15 years; 17 males, mean age: 38 ± 15 years) underwent bilateral shoulder MRI on a 3T system using a double echo steady state sequence (DESS) for segmentation and a custom UTE‑MT protocol to quantify MMF. Labra were segmented from DESS images, and voxel‑wise MMF was computed. Mean MMF was calculated for each arm. A linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept for subject to account for within-subject dependence tested the effects of age, sex, arm dominance, and their respective interactions. A linear mixed effect model with a random intercept for subject tested the effect of menopause status among females on mean MMF. Males exhibited higher mean labral MMF than females (male: 40.4 ± 7.3%, female: 39.6 ± 7.2%; p = 0.016). Age showed no main effect on mean MMF. However, a significant sex‑by‑age interaction indicated a steeper age‑related decline in males (p = 0.0113). There was no significant effect of arm dominance on mean MMF (dominant: 41.1 ± 7.6%, non-dominant: 38.8 ± 6.9%; p = 0.412), and there was no significance found for the interactions of dominance and sex, dominance and age, or dominance, sex, and age. Among females, mean MMF did not differ by menopause status (premenopausal 39.4 ± 7.4% vs. postmenopausal 39.7 ± 7.1%; p = 0.761). UTE‑MT MRI detects sex‑specific differences in glenoid labrum MMF, with a significant sex‑by‑age interaction despite no main effect of age. These findings support MMF's potential as a non‑invasive quantitative marker of labral composition and motivates longitudinal studies to define clinically meaningful thresholds and regional variation.

articles.title: Copper sulfate-lactic acid combinations exhibit broad-spectrum microbicidal activity against viral and bacterial sexually transmitted pathogens in vitro and in vivo.
articles.authors: Visciano ML, Asowata OE, Verma N et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and unintended pregnancy remain critical global public health concerns affecting millions of women worldwide. To support the development of new multipurpose products offering non-hormonal contraception and activity against sexually transmitted pathogens, we evaluated copper sulfate, zinc lactate, L-(+)-lactic acid and their combinations as candidate pharmaceutical actives. We determined virucidal (HIV-1, HSV-2) and bactericidal (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis) activity in vitro followed by in vivo efficacy testing against HSV-2, N. gonorrhoeae, and C. trachomatis in mice. In vitro, zinc lactate alone showed no inhibitory activity. In contrast, copper sulfate and lactic acid alone and in combination demonstrated activity against all tested pathogens. Furthermore, these combinations remained potent in the presence of vaginal and seminal fluids. Importantly, the actives - alone or combined - at concentrations that inhibited STI pathogens did not inhibit the growth of Lactobacillus crispatus, bacteria associated with an optimal vaginal microbiota. Further, copper sulfate and lactic acid alone and in combination inhibited vaginal HSV-2 and N. gonorrhoeae infection in mice. The combination conferred limited protection against vaginal C. trachomatis infection. These data demonstrate the advantages of combining copper sulfate and lactic acid and support further evaluation and development of this combination as a multipurpose prevention product.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-65145-9.

articles.title: Compartment-specific soluble immune profiles associated with preterm birth, perinatal death, and low birthweight in pregnant individuals living with HIV.
articles.authors: Corry J, Zotova N, Tabala M et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pregnant people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PPLWH) face elevated risks of preterm birth (PTB), perinatal death (PND), and low birthweight (LBW). While antiretroviral therapy (ART) effectively suppresses viral load, it neither prevents these adverse pregnancy outcomes nor resolves underlying inflammation. Since circulating maternal markers may not fully capture local immune dysregulation, this observational cohort study identified compartmentalized immune factors associated with adverse outcomes. We analyzed 45 immune factors in paired maternal, placental, and cord plasma from 118 ART-treated PPLWH in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Among these pregnancies, 30% resulted in PTB, 9% in PND, and 8% in LBW. Compared to term births, PTB (n = 35) was associated with discordant spatio-temporal signaling of T-cell-associated chemokines CCL20, CXCL9, and CXCL10. PND (n = 10) correlated with the largest inflammatory signature and was associated with factors that signal neutrophil recruitment and activation, including CXCL1, CXCL5, MPO and S100A8/A9. LBW (n = 9) was associated with higher concentrations of inflammatory factors at enrollment IL-18 and S100A8/A9, alongside increased postdelivery and postpartum SAA. In ART-treated PPLWH, distinct outcomes were characterized by time- and compartment-specific immune pathways. These pathways may provide mechanistic insights into adverse birth outcomes in PPLWH and highlight potential compartment-specific biomarkers for risk stratification.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-75643-5.

articles.title: A randomized controlled trial of zoledronate and oral magnesium in post-menopausal women with osteoporosis.
articles.authors: Pickering ME, Morel V, Delay M et al.
articles.abstract: Bisphosphonates are recommended to enhance bone mineral density (BMD) and reduce the risk of fracture in women with post-menopausal osteoporosis. Magnesium (Mg) has a beneficial effect on BMD, but no trial has so far addressed its additive effect with bisphosphonate treatment. Our objective was to explore whether Mg supplementation could have an additive beneficial effect with bisphosphonate on the concentration of serum carboxy-terminal collagen crosslinks (CTX), as a surrogate of bone status. A pilot randomized controlled trial (NCT05328154) included 44 women with post-menopausal osteoporosis at the University Hospital, Clermont-Ferrand, France. Patients were randomized after zoledronate infusion into 200 mg/day oral Mg carbonate (n=22, "BMg") for three months or standard care (n=22, "BMg0"). The primary endpoint was comparison of variation in CTX at one year in both groups. Other bone markers and quality of life were also assessed. Responder analysis was post-hoc. All statistical tests were two-tailed with type-I error set at α=0.05. CTX substantially decreased in both groups, but without significant difference between groups. A subgroup analysis in 30%, with both high CTX and low serum Mg levels at baseline, showed that these patients had the largest decrease in CTX levels (≥89%). DKK1 demonstrated the greatest difference between the BMg0 and BMg group, suggesting an osteogenic effect of Mg. No other significant differences were observed. This innovative pilot randomized trial suggests that in clinical practice, the subgroup of post-osteoporotic women with high CTX values and low serum Mg concentrations might benefit from Mg supplementation in addition to zoledronate. A larger randomized trial targeting this subgroup is warranted. Trial registration: NCT05328154; first registration date: 29/03/2022; first inclusion: 28/06/ 2022.

articles.title: Publicly Available Information on Insurance Coverage for Maternal-Fetal Surgery.
articles.authors: Wilpers A, Zapolin B, Francis K et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Maternal-fetal surgery has expanded rapidly in the US, but how insurance coverage supports delivery of this specialized, high-cost care has not been systematically characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize publicly ascertainable information about how Medicaid programs and large commercial insurers cover procedures used in maternal-fetal surgery.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional descriptive study analyzed insurance coverage policies in the US from March through August 2025. Medicaid programs and large commercial insurers were selected based on national market share.
EXPOSURE: Insurance coverage policies for maternal-fetal surgery-related procedures were assessed using publicly available fee schedules and structured outreach to payer representatives.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Coverage status (covered, not covered, or data not available) for 19 maternal-fetal surgery-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes and 5 comparator codes.
RESULTS: The study included 50 state Medicaid programs and 30 large commercial insurers. Among Medicaid programs, coverage was high for nonspecific or individual components of procedures (eg, intrauterine transfusion: 49 of 49 available determinations [100%]) but incomplete and highly variable for codes specific to comprehensive interventions (eg, 6 of 36 available determinations [16.7%] for in utero sacrococcygeal teratoma resection). Among 44 states with available determinations for both code types, mean (SD) coverage was higher for CPT codes than S-codes (86.3% [14.1%] vs 53.0% [37.0%]; P < .001), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses. The median (range) proportion of MFS-related codes covered per state was 14.5 (0-19) of 19 codes (76.3%). Among 5 commercial insurers with data, all 5 (100.0%) reported coverage of all 4 S-codes representing comprehensive interventions.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, coverage of maternal-fetal surgery-related codes was incomplete and variable, and transparency in commercial coverage policies was limited. These findings suggest that coverage uncertainty may complicate health-system planning and financing for this increasingly used, high-cost care.

articles.title: Temporal influences in non-elective cesarean sections and indication patterns.
articles.authors: Windhorst AC, Tönnies FS, Wolter A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Elective (pre-labour) cesarean sections are, by design, concentrated during staffed hours, limiting the interpretability of overall temporal patterns. We examined whether the proportion of documented discretion-susceptible indications for non-elective (intrapartum) cesarean sections shifts with time of day and weekday, using the Robson classification for stratification.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 5,850 cesarean sections at University Hospital Giessen and Marburg, 2015-2021, classified as elective (n=2,851) or non-elective (n=2,998) by documented decision timepoint. Among non-elective cases, we assessed threshold-susceptible ("soft") indications (protracted labour/arrest, non-reassuring fetal heart rate) by shift and weekend, adjusted for Robson group and gestational age. Guideline-defined absolute ("hard") indications served as a supportive comparison, with Holm correction for exploratory comparisons.
RESULTS: Among non-elective cesarean sections, the proportion with documented discretion-susceptible indications was significantly higher during evening/night shifts (OR 2.63, 95%CI 2.20-3.14, p<0.001) and, less markedly, on weekends (OR 1.37, 95%CI 1.12-1.67, p=0.002), consistent across all five individual indicators for shift, and across two of five for weekend. Indications with limited clinical discretion showed no comparable variation (shift OR 0.99, p=0.92; weekend OR 0.77, p=0.16), except for placenta previa (Holm-p=0.023), discussed as a qualification rather than a validation of the primary interpretation.
CONCLUSION: The proportion of non-elective cesarean sections with documented discretion-susceptible indications was higher during evening/night shifts and weekends, while guideline-defined indications with limited discretion showed comparatively little variation. Because a population-based at-risk denominator was unavailable, these findings describe differences in documented indication composition among cesarean deliveries that occurred, rather than evidence that the intervention threshold itself changed. Whether this reflects clinical decision-making, documentation practice, or unmeasured case-mix factors warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Group exercise interventions and their impact on patient-reported outcomes in urologic, gynecologic, and breast cancers.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.authors: Ibilibor C, Denton AH, Armbruster SD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Patients with urologic, gynecologic, and breast malignancies experience unique treatment-related side effects that can be socially isolating. While group-based exercise can provide social support, its impact on these patients remains unclear. This review aims to examine patient-reported outcomes related to participation in group exercise in these patients.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review of randomized control trials and prospective cohort studies that compared group-based exercise to usual care or individual exercise in patients with a urologic, gynecologic, or breast malignancy and examined patient-reported metrics. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, SPORTDiscus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews were searched between January 2005 and December 2025.
RESULTS: We identified 973 studies and 14 met inclusion criteria. Of the included articles, 9 included breast, 4 included prostate, and 1 included bladder cancer patients, representing 1128 patients. Group exercise was performed in supervised groups or teams of 3-14 participants in a community or hospital facility. Compared to individual exercise, a group exercise intervention showed an improvement in patient-reported quality of life in 1 study where group dynamics were measured.
CONCLUSION: This review was unable to show an advantage in group-based exercise compared to individual exercise with regard to patient-reported quality of life for patients with a breast, prostate, or bladder cancer. However, our study is limited by the absence of measured positive group dynamic in each study. Future investigations will include qualitative and quantitative measures of group dynamic and group cohesion to determine the potentially socially supportive role of group-based exercise interventions.

articles.title: The effects of saffron and crocin in enhancing male fertility: insights from clinical and preclinical studies.
articles.authors: Khazdair MR
articles.abstract: ABSTRACTSInfertility is a disorder of the male or female reproductive system characterised by the failure to achieve a clinical pregnancy after twelve months or more of regular, unprotected intercourse. Crocus sativus L. (saffron), a widely used spice and food additive, is also recognised for its diverse medicinal properties. This review evaluates current literature regarding the effects of saffron and its active constituent, crocin, on male infertility. The search of electronic databases was conducted for articles published through April 2025, extracting data from both basic and clinical studies. Evidence from animal models indicates that saffron and crocin extracts enhance sexual behaviour, including mounting and intromission, while reducing latency for mounting, intromission and ejaculation. In clinical settings, daily supplementation with 200 mg of saffron has been shown to improve quality of life, urinary symptoms and sexual function in male subjects. Furthermore, both saffron and crocin significantly improve sperm parameters-including count, viability and motility-as well as seminiferous tubule diameter and serum testosterone levels. These therapeutic effects appear to be mediated by the alleviation of psychiatric symptoms, enhancement of antioxidant status and modulation of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) levels.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Benzimidazole Derivatives as Dual PI3K/HDAC8 Inhibitors with Potent Anti-Cervical Cancer Activity InVivo.
articles.authors: Chen J, Wang W, Qi X et al.
articles.abstract: The dual inhibition of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) has emerged as a promising strategy for cervical cancer (CC) therapy. We synthesized 34 novel benzimidazole derivatives and evaluated their anti-CC cell line proliferation. The compound 50 exhibited equivalent antiproliferative effect to cisplatin (Pt) in CC cell lines SiHa, Ca Ski, and HeLa, especially in HeLa cells with an IC50 value at 1.42 ± 0.50 μM (Pt 1.70 ± 0.28 μM). Further assessment in the HeLa cell xenograft mouse model, the intraperitoneal medium- (30 mg/kg) and high-dose group (60 mg/kg) and and intragastric high-dose group (100 mg/kg) exhibited antitumor efficacy no less than that of Pt (i.p. 5 mg/kg) but much more safe during the experiment period. Mechanism studies demonstrated that 50 could inhibit the PI3K/Akt pathway and HDAC8 expression and function. These findings prove that the PI3K/HDAC8 dual inhibition may be an efficient way in cervical cancer treatment and compound 50 deserved for further development.

articles.title: ENPP1 deficiency in siblings with apparently discordant phenotypes: case report and a review of the literature.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.authors: Wada T, Miyahara Y, Hasegawa Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ENPP1 deficiency encompasses a phenotypic spectrum from generalized arterial calcification of infancy (GACI) to autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 (ARHR2), and phenotypic variability has been reported even among individuals carrying the same variants; however, the extent of intrafamilial phenotypic concordance remains unclear.
CASE PRESENTATION: Case 1, a 20-month-old boy, presented with genu varum and fibroblast growth factor 23-mediated hypophosphatemic rickets. Genetic testing identified compound heterozygous ENPP1 variants, c.937_938insT (p.Gln313LeufsTer18), and a deletion involving exons 8-13. Ultrasonography revealed valvular calcifications, carotid intimal irregularity, and nephrocalcinosis. Case 2, his younger brother, developed fetal hydrops, diffuse cardiovascular calcification, and severe cardiac dysfunction in late gestation and died shortly after preterm birth. Postmortem examination demonstrated extensive vascular calcification consistent with GACI; genetic testing identified the same variants. A sibling-based literature review of genetically confirmed cases with shared biallelic ENPP1 variants identified 21 publications describing 26 unrelated families. Including the present family, 27 families comprising 61 affected individuals were analyzed; 24 families (88.9 %) had concordant phenotypes, whereas three (11.1 %) had discordant phenotypes. Among 19 individuals who presented with hypophosphatemia or ARHR2 without a documented history of GACI and underwent cardiovascular, calcification, and/or hearing assessment, 14 had abnormal findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Documented GACI status was generally concordant among affected siblings. Frequent cardiovascular, calcification-related, and/or hearing abnormalities in patients presenting with hypophosphatemia or ARHR2 without a documented history of GACI highlight the importance of multisystem assessment and support GACI and ARHR2 as overlapping manifestations within the ENPP1 deficiency spectrum.

articles.title: Perivascular epithelial remodeling is reflected in circulating cfDNA methylation signals as detection markers for early esophageal tumorigenesis.
articles.authors: Yi Y, Li D, Zhang S et al.
articles.abstract: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is hindered by a lack of noninvasive biomarkers for precancerous lesions. Here, we report a circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation approach for early esophageal neoplasia detection. In prospective community screening, the assay achieved standardized sensitivity of 78% at 79% specificity for the clinically actionable endpoint of high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (HGIN) or ESCC, with stage-specific sensitivities of 76% for HGIN and 86% for ESCC. Genome-wide methylation profiling reveals HGIN as an early epigenetic reprogramming stage. Integrative spatial and single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pronounced remodeling of the endothelial-proximal epithelial cell population, whose methylation signatures are detected in cfDNA. Guided by these findings, we develop an 11-gene cfDNA methylation panel that shows robust discrimination of early-stage ESCC across three retrospective case-control sets and an independent screening-derived case-control set. Together, these results demonstrate that our cfDNA methylation panel has promising utility for early ESCC detection.

articles.title: A Clinico-Sonographic Scoring System for Diagnosing Placenta Accreta Spectrum and Predicting Peripartum Hysterectomy Risk.
articles.authors: Keikha S, Zadehmir M, Razavi M et al.
articles.abstract: To develop and evaluate a clinico-sonographic scoring system combining prenatal ultrasound findings and maternal clinical history for diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) and predicting peripartum hysterectomy. We analyzed clinical and ultrasound data from 77 pregnant women with persistent placenta previa and prior cesarean delivery evaluated at a tertiary referral center between 2022 and 2024. Five patients were excluded because of incomplete data or loss to follow-up, leaving 72 patients in the final cohort. Multivariable logistic regression and clinical weighting were used to model PAS risk based on sonographic features (placental lacunae, retroplacental myometrial thickness, placental thickness, and bridging vessels) and maternal symptomatology (third-trimester bleeding). Surgical findings and histopathologic examination served as the reference standard. Peripartum hysterectomy was performed in 30 patients (41.7%; 15 percreta, 10 increta, 4 accreta, and 1 non-PAS). The clinico-sonographic score yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.907 (95% CI: 0.840-0.975) for diagnosing PAS. A score cutoff of ≥3.5 had a sensitivity of 85.1% and a specificity of 87.2%. For predicting peripartum hysterectomy, the same cutoff yielded a sensitivity of 96.7% and a specificity of 61.9% (AUC: 0.875, 95% CI: 0.795-0.955). A cutoff of ≥5.5 predicted placenta percreta with 69.2% sensitivity, 76.9% specificity, and an AUC of 0.806 (95% CI: 0.687-0.924). A clinico-sonographic scoring system combining prenatal ultrasound markers with third-trimester bleeding stratifies PAS risk and identifies patients at increased risk of peripartum hysterectomy. Prospective external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Sonographic Characteristics and Key Diagnostic Signs of Interstitial Ectopic Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Horrow MM, Rodgers SK
articles.abstract: Forty surgically proven cases of interstitial ectopic pregnancy (IEP) were reviewed for several signs and grayscale and color Doppler appearances, as well as for prospective interpretations by the interpreting radiologists. Prospectively, IEP was reported in 62.5%, with all reporting or describing a claw sign. The claw sign was identified on retrospective review in 100% of cases, thereby distinguishing the IEP from the more common tubal ectopic pregnancy (EP), which is separate from the uterus. The myometrial bar sign (myometrium between IEP and endometrium) was present in 100% of cases, allowing differentiation from an eccentric intrauterine pregnancy, which is peripherally located though completely surrounded by endometrium. The interstitial line sign was present in 22.5% of cases, considerably less frequent than prior studies, and was rarely used by the interpreting radiologists. The most common qualitative appearance of an IEP was a round mass (92.5%) with color Doppler flow (97.5%). An empty gestational sac (tubal ring) was present in 21 (52.5%), an embryo in 15 (37.5%), and a solid mass in 4 (10%). No cases of hematosalpinx were observed. Thus, the typical grayscale and color Doppler appearance of an IEP differs from the tubal EP, which most commonly presents as a mass without a visible gestational sac. In conclusion, IEP, a rare form of EP but with greater morbidity and mortality, is distinguished from a tubal EP and an eccentric intrauterine pregnancy by a combination of the claw and myometrial bar signs, use of which may potentially improve the diagnosis.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Obstetric Causes of Critical Illness in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Kuppusamy P, Kale DP, Manjrekar MR et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence, risks, and outcomes of obstetric causes of critically ill pregnant women admitted to the ICU.
DATA SOURCES: We searched the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid, and ScienceDirect databases up to May 15, 2026.
STUDY SELECTION: We included studies reporting primary data on critically ill pregnant and postpartum women (up to 48 d post-delivery) admitted to an ICU, with relevant obstetric risk factors and maternal outcomes.
DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects model with 95% CIs.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Of the 3,735 total records, 50 studies met the eligibility criteria, encompassing 7,756,232 women receiving obstetric care in tertiary hospitals across 20 countries, with 49,299 ICU admissions. Globally, 1.0% (95% CI, 0.8-1.3%) of pregnant and postpartum women experience critical illness and require admission to an ICU. The frequency varies according to the country's income levels, with the highest in low-income countries (4.1%) and the lowest in high-income countries (0.5%). Notably, 72.3% of ICU admissions were attributed to known obstetric causes, primarily obstetric hemorrhage (23.3%) and hypertension in pregnancy (26.9%). Nearly 33.3% of ICU patients required either respiratory or transfusion support, and the maternal mortality rate among ICU-admitted obstetric women was 8.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in 100 pregnancies require admission to intensive care due to critical illness, and nearly three-quarters of these admissions were due to direct obstetric causes, with high maternal morbidity and mortality. Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders account for the majority of ICU admissions. Strengthening obstetric care in resource-limited settings through the expansion and optimization of intensive care services is essential for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes and reducing preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Maternal-fetal health in arboviral diseases: clinical outcomes following prenatal dengue and chikungunya virus infections.
articles.authors: Salem GM, Tang KH, Familiar-Macedo D et al.
articles.abstract: SUMMARYArthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) are an increasingly important cause of global infectious disease, yet their effects during pregnancy and early life remain incompletely understood. In the context of declining fertility and birth rates globally, infectious threats to successful pregnancy and neonatal health warrant greater attention. Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), two of the most prevalent mosquito-borne viruses, are underrecognized contributors to maternal-fetal health. Although these infections rarely result in classical congenital syndromes, accumulating clinical, epidemiological, and experimental evidence indicates that prenatal exposure can impair placental function, drive maternal immune dysregulation, and influence fetal and neonatal immune development. This review summarizes current knowledge on the maternal, placental, and pediatric consequences of DENV and CHIKV infection during pregnancy. We outline the immunological features of the maternal-fetal interface and discuss how pregnancy-associated immune modulation shapes antiviral responses and placental homeostasis. We then review epidemiological and clinical evidence linking prenatal arboviral infection with adverse pregnancy outcomes, neonatal disease, and potential long-term neurodevelopmental effects. Mechanistic insights, including viral immune evasion, placental inflammation, and antibody-mediated immunopathology, are examined. Finally, we discuss clinical considerations for monitoring arboviral-exposed pregnancies and progenies, alongside emerging strategies to reduce maternal infection and improve neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Understanding pharmacokinetics of novel prolonged release dienogest 2 mg / ethinyl-estradiol 0.02 mg oral contraceptive formulation: clinical applications.
articles.journal: Expert opinion on drug metabolism & toxicology
articles.authors: Barretta M, Versailles JBE, Bahamondes L et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) have traditionally evolved through changes in estrogen and progestin type and dose. More recently, drug-delivery technology has emerged as an additional strategy to modify pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles without altering hormonal components.
AREAS COVERED: A structured search of MEDLINE and regulatory sources was conducted to review the PK and pharmacodynamic characteristics of a prolonged-release COC containing dienogest (DNG) 2 mg and ethinylestradiol (EE) 0.02 mg, and to explore their clinical implications. Compared with immediate-release formulations, prolonged-release DNG/EE produces delayed peak concentrations, lower plasma peak levels, and reduced intra-day hormonal fluctuations while maintaining comparable overall exposure.
EXPERT OPINION: Clinical evidence indicates contraceptive efficacy comparable to other COCs, with improved bleeding control compared with an immediate-release formulation. Both the intrinsic endometrial effects of DNG and more stable hormonal exposure may contribute . The formulation also provides antiandrogenic effects that may benefit hirsutism in women with PCOS. The safety profile appears broadly consistent with other low-dose COCs, although the effect on thromboembolic risk remains uncertain. Prolonged-release technology adds a new dimension to contraceptive choice. Further comparative and post-marketing studies are needed to establish its clinical advantages and long-term safety.

articles.title: Does reducing the number of intradetrusor botulinum toxin type A injection sites affect efficacy and safety in patients with spinal cord injury?
articles.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
articles.authors: Zheng H, Huang T, Yang X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical effect and safety of different numbers of botulinum toxin type A (BTX-A) bladder injections in the treatment of neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO).
DESIGN: A single-blind randomized control trial.
SETTING: A single spinal cord injury (SCI) rehabilitation center in China.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 44 patients with spinal cord injury and neurogenic detrusor overactivity who underwent intradetrusor injection of 200 U BTX-A were enrolled. The cohort included 34 men and 10 women.
INTERVENTIONS: They were randomly divided into two groups of 30 vs. 20 sites of injection with 200 U BTX-A.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Urodynamic parameters such as maximum detrusor pressure at first DO (PdetmaxDO), volume at the first involuntary detrusor contraction, were measured at baseline and week 12 after injection. Mean urine volume per catheterization(V-CIC), scores of the Incontinence Specific Quality of Life Instrument (I-QoL) were also recorded before and after treatment.
RESULTS: At the endpoint, both the urodynamic parameters and volume of catheterization improved significantly, without a significant difference between the two groups. Mean decreases in the maximum detrusor pressure were -31.95 and -25.77 cmH2O in the 20- and 30-injection groups. The increases in volume at the first involuntary detrusor contraction from baseline were +130.86 and +122.73 ml, respectively. There was no significant difference in the change in incontinence severity or I-QoL improvement between the two groups. The urinary incontinence episodes per week decreased from 48.41 ± 6.71-17.50 ± 16.17 and from 53.27 ± 11.33-22.91 ± 18.94 in the 20- and 30-injection groups, respectively (all P < 0.001). There were eight and seven patients with complete dryness after treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: When the total dose of 200 U was maintained, reducing the number of injection sites from 30 to 20 had a similar therapeutic effect in NDO without compromising safety. Clinically, this approach may be advantageous in terms of reducing the operating time and improving patient comfort.

articles.title: Thirty-Day All-Cause Readmissions After Pregnancy-Associated Hospitalizations With Heart Failure in the United States: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmissions Database.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.authors: Barry E, Kim MJ, Goldstein S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the United States. There is a paucity of data regarding pregnancy-associated heart failure readmissions. This study aims to characterize the 30-day heart failure readmission patterns in pregnancy-associated admissions.
METHODS: The National Readmission Database from 2016 to 2021 was used to identify women aged 13 to 49 with an index hospitalization with heart failure as the primary or secondary diagnosis during a pregnancy-related admission, identified by diagnosis-related group codes and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression were used to characterize readmission patterns and identify independently associated factors.
RESULTS: Among 19 452 eligible index hospitalizations, 2659 were followed by a 30-day readmission; the survey-weighted readmission rate was 13.5%. In the fully adjusted model, Medicare and Medicaid coverage, residence in a small metropolitan area, greater All Patient Refined Diagnosis-Related Group severity, discharge with home health care, and discharge against medical advice were associated with higher odds of readmission. Deficiency anemia, chronic pulmonary disease, diabetes without chronic complications, renal failure, solid tumor without metastasis, and cardiovascular or respiratory disorders complicating pregnancy were also independently associated with increased readmission.
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 7 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations complicated by heart failure was followed by a 30-day all-cause readmission. Readmission risk reflected a combination of illness severity, discharge disposition, payer status, geographic location, and selected medical and pregnancy-related comorbidities. These findings support the development and evaluation of individualized, multidisciplinary transitional-care strategies for patients at highest risk.

articles.title: When reproductive care ends: the cardiometabolic continuity gap in PMOS in low- and middle-income countries-a mini-review.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Yusuf AA, Abdi DA, Mohamed Hassan A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the potential cardiometabolic continuity gap after reproductive care among women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), particularly in low- and middle-income countries.Methods This mini-review synthesizes evidence on persistent glycaemic, adiposity-related, blood-pressure, lipid, and cardiovascular risk and examines where responsibility for follow-up may become fragmented in low- and middle-income countries.
RESULTS: PMOS, formerly polycystic ovary syndrome, is a lifelong multisystem condition whose cardiometabolic implications persist beyond fertility treatment, pregnancy, and childbirth. Yet care often remains organized around reproductive goals, creating a potential continuity gap when women transition from fertility, maternity, or postpartum services to primary or noncommunicable disease care. This review proposes a minimum continuity pathway: Identify, Document, Transfer, Reassess, and Retain.
CONCLUSIONS: The pathway defines essential functions rather than a fixed service model and requires local adaptation and prospective evaluation. Reproductive care may end, but cardiometabolic responsibility should not; every woman leaving reproductive care should have a documented risk profile, a clearly identified next service, and an accessible route to continuing follow-up.

articles.title: Menopausal symptom burden in postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia.
articles.authors: Derhem B, Kültür T, Çobankaya Ş
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to compare menopausal symptom severity between postmenopausal women with and without fibromyalgia syndrome, and to estimate the independent association of fibromyalgia syndrome with menopausal symptom burden.
METHODS: Comparative cross-sectional study of 80 postmenopausal women: 40 with fibromyalgia syndrome and 40 without. The primary outcome was the Menopause Rating Scale total score; pain, fatigue and sleep disturbance were rated on 0-10 visual analog scales. The association of fibromyalgia syndrome with Menopause Rating Scale total score was estimated by multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, body mass index, education and route of menopause.
RESULTS: Menopause Rating Scale total score was 26.2±9.7 with fibromyalgia syndrome versus 12.9±6.1 in controls (mean difference 13.3 points, 95%CI 9.6-16.9; Hedges' g=1.63; p<0.001). Severe symptoms (Menopause Rating Scale ≥17) occurred in 85.0% versus 27.5% (risk ratio 3.1; 95%CI 1.8-5.2). Fibromyalgia syndrome remained independently associated with Menopause Rating Scale total score after adjustment (β=13.13; 95%CI 9.32-16.94; p<0.001); further adjustment for pain, fatigue and sleep visual analog scales attenuated but did not abolish this association (β=10.11; 95%CI 6.07-14.16).
CONCLUSION: Postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia syndrome carry a substantially greater menopausal symptom burden than women of comparable age and body mass index. This association was independent of measured demographic and reproductive characteristics, but its independence from the core features of fibromyalgia syndrome could not be established, given the overlap between the two symptom sets.

articles.title: Association between lesion location and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia.
articles.authors: Yavuz ÖM, Şimşek E, Taşkum İ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to determine the clock-face distribution of cervical lesions in women undergoing colposcopy for high-risk human papillomavirus positivity and to evaluate the association between lesion localization and high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+; cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 298 women who underwent colposcopy because of high-risk human papillomavirus positivity between January 2024 and March 2026. Demographic characteristics, human papillomavirus genotypes, cervical cytology, colposcopic biopsy localization, and histopathological findings were retrospectively reviewed. Cervical lesions were classified according to the clock-face system and grouped into anterior, right lateral, posterior, and left lateral regions. The primary outcome was the presence of CIN2+.
RESULTS: The mean age was 42.5±9.2 years, and CIN2+ lesions were identified in 54 women (18.1%). Lesions were most frequently located at the 12 and 6 o'clock positions. Compared with the normal/CIN1 group, patients with CIN2+ had a higher frequency of abnormal cytology (48.1 vs. 23.8%; p=0.001) and anterior cervical localization (88.9 vs. 66.8%; p=0.002). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, abnormal cytology (adjusted OR 2.84; 95%CI 1.43-5.63; p=0.003) and anterior cervical localization (adjusted OR 3.67; 95%CI 1.46-9.21; p=0.006) were independently associated with CIN2+.
CONCLUSION: Cervical lesions in high-risk human papillomavirus-positive women showed a nonuniform clock-face distribution. Anterior cervical localization was independently associated with high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+), suggesting that careful assessment and documentation of lesion location during colposcopy may improve the identification of clinically significant lesions.

articles.title: Same margin, different lesion: margin subtype, glandular involvement, and endocervical curettage status as predictors of residual CIN2+ at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure: An 11-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Purut YE, Gercik İ, Tutal AD et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess how initial loop electrosurgical excision procedure margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and specimen size relate to re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology and receipt of further surgery.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 287 patients undergoing re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure at a tertiary center (2015-2025) were reviewed. Initial margin status was classified as margin continuity, margin adjacency, or non-evaluable margin. Associations with re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology, residual CIN2+ disease, and receipt of a third surgical intervention were assessed using chi-square/Fisher-Freeman-Halton tests, Cohen's kappa, and multivariate logistic regression.
RESULTS: Initial and re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology showed a significant group-level association (p=0.039) but no case-by-case agreement beyond chance (kappa=-0.009, p=0.754); most patients with initial CIN2/3 had CIN1 at re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure. Margin adjacency independently predicted residual CIN2+ disease at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure (OR 11.045, p=0.049), as did glandular involvement (OR 1.938, p=0.035). Among patients with negative re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure margins, residual CIN2+ disease was identified within the specimen in 27.1%, and human papillomavirus test negativity at the first follow-up visit was 88.2%, varying by genotype. Positive margin (OR 333.33, p<0.001) and positive endocervical curettage (OR 41.67, p<0.001) at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure were the strongest predictors of receiving a third surgical intervention.
CONCLUSION: Margin adjacency and glandular involvement independently predicted residual CIN2+ at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure, whereas positive margins and positive endocervical curettage at re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure were strongly associated with receipt of a third surgical intervention. Post-loop electrosurgical excision procedure follow-up should integrate margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and human papillomavirus surveillance rather than rely on margin status alone; genotype-specific differences in human papillomavirus test negativity require confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Maternal oncostatin M levels in gestational diabetes mellitus: associations with metabolic dysfunction and pregnancy outcomes.
articles.authors: Kapudere B, Akdemir Y, Guven B
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gestational diabetes mellitus is characterized by metabolic dysfunction and altered inflammatory signaling. The aim of this study was to evaluate maternal serum oncostatin M levels in pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus and explore their associations with metabolic and pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: In this prospective case-control study, 40 women with gestational diabetes mellitus and 40 healthy pregnant controls were enrolled. Maternal serum oncostatin M concentrations were measured during the third trimester using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.
RESULTS: Maternal serum oncostatin M levels were significantly lower in women with gestational diabetes mellitus than in controls (28.7 vs. 64.0 ng/L, p=0.001). Oncostatin M levels were negatively correlated with body mass index, insulin, hemoglobin A1c, and Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance, and positively correlated with gestational age at delivery (all p<0.05). Pregnancy outcomes were similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: Maternal oncostatin M levels are reduced in gestational diabetes mellitus and are associated with markers of metabolic dysfunction, supporting a potential association with the immunometabolic adaptations of diabetic pregnancy.

articles.title: Benign-appearing endometrial cells on Papanicolaou test in women aged 45 years or older: a retrospective study from a large academic institution and meta-analysis of comparable cohorts.
articles.authors: Burke O, Zhao J, Adeniran AJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Benign-appearing endometrial cells (BECs) are reported on Papanicolaou tests in women aged 45 years or older per the 2014 Bethesda System, and current American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology guidelines recommend endometrial evaluation for postmenopausal women with BECs. However, the clinical significance of BECs across age groups and menopausal status varies among published studies.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified Papanicolaou tests reporting BECs in women aged 45 years or older at our institution (2021-2023). Histologic follow-up diagnoses were analyzed by age and menopausal status. A random-effects meta-analysis combined our cohort with 6 comparable published series.
RESULTS: Among 133 280 Papanicolaou tests, BECs were reported in 2030 women aged at least 45 years (1.5%). Of 604 women with histologic follow-up, clinically significant pathology (atypical endometrial hyperplasia or endometrial carcinoma) was identified in 6.0% (36/604). Endometrial carcinoma risk increased with age, from 0.9% (45-49 years) to 6.9% (≥60 years; P < .001) and was higher in postmenopausal than in premenopausal women (5.2% vs 0.6%; P <0.001). Clinically significant pathology risk remained at or below 5% through age 59 years but rose to 12.8% at or beyond 60 years of age. Meta-analysis of 7 cohorts (4989 women) yielded a pooled estimate of 4.5% (95% CI, 3.3%-6.0%; I2 = 75%), with our cohort toward the upper end of the range.
CONCLUSIONS: The risk of atypical endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial carcinoma increases substantially after age 60 years and in postmenopausal women while remaining low in younger, premenopausal women. Meta-analysis confirmed a modest but clinically meaningful overall risk. Incorporating both age and menopausal status into clinical triage may improve risk stratification beyond age alone.

articles.title: From reproductive access to family sustainability: lessons from single-father families formed through surrogacy.
articles.authors: Pereira H
articles.abstract: Single-father families formed through oocyte donation and surrogacy provide a revealing, but not uniquely problematic, case for considering responsibilities after assisted reproduction. Early studies report reassuring parenting and adjustment, yet samples are small and selective, direct accounts from children are sparse, and adolescence and adulthood remain largely unstudied. Family-sustainability planning must therefore complement, not displace, child-centred longitudinal research. This Opinion uses single-father surrogacy to examine four treatment-related domains: portable legal parenthood, identity stewardship, continuity of care, and developmentally timed support. Their relevance extends to other donor-conceived, surrogacy and one-legal-parent families when comparable risks arise. A parent-held Family Sustainability Plan is offered as one testable handover tool, not a fitness assessment or mandatory global document. Its content should be tailored through shared decision-making and paired with navigation, affordable legal and psychosocial support, durable record systems, and structural reform. To avoid surveillance or discriminatory gatekeeping, its preparation should be proportionate, offered on a universal route- and risk-based basis, kept outside treatment-eligibility decisions, and open to refusal or later re-entry without penalty. Cross-border legal disagreement, unequal resources, provider fragmentation, and the possibility of added burden limit what any plan can achieve. Assisted reproduction should nevertheless be accountable for preventable legal and informational discontinuities beyond live birth, while evaluating whether proposed supports are useful, equitable, and acceptable to fathers and children themselves.

articles.title: Informed consent and timely emergency obstetric care in Somalia: Ethical, clinical, and policy perspectives.
articles.authors: Elmi AH, Ahmed MM, Ibrahim FH
articles.abstract: Maternal mortality remains a major public-health concern in Somalia, where timely access to emergency obstetric care is affected by referral difficulties, shortages of skilled staff, limited blood and surgical capacity, financial barriers, and weaknesses in facility-level processes. One insufficiently studied contributor to in-facility delay is the way consent for urgent obstetric interventions is discussed, obtained, and documented. In some maternity settings, clinicians may seek approval from husbands or other relatives before proceeding, even when an adult woman is able to make her own healthcare decision. However, direct Somalia-specific evidence measuring the frequency, duration, and maternal consequences of consent-related delays remains limited. Available evidence from Somalia, Somaliland, and the wider sub-Saharan African region suggests that consent practices may be influenced by provider communication, health literacy, family involvement, gender norms, financial constraints, and uncertainty about institutional procedures. This evidence-informed perspective examines the ethical, clinical, and policy implications of consent practices in Somali emergency obstetric care. It emphasizes that competent adult women should be supported to make their own healthcare decisions, while clear emergency protocols are needed for patients who temporarily lack decision-making capacity. Family involvement should support, rather than replace, the decisions of women who retain capacity. Respectful communication, documentation of capacity and consent, separation of financial authorization from clinical consent, and routine review of decision-to-treatment intervals may help reduce avoidable delays. Prospective research is needed to determine how frequently consent-related barriers occur and whether they independently influence maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Toward Precision Andrology: Advancing Semen Testing to Resolve the Enigma of 'Idiopathic' Male Infertility.
articles.authors: Sengupta P, Dutta S, Elsuity MAE et al.
articles.abstract: Despite decades of advancements, conventional semen analysis continues to leave nearly 40% of infertile men labeled as 'idiopathic', denoting abnormal semen parameters in the absence of remarkable abnormalities in genital examination. The emerging discipline of precision andrology attempts to bridge this diagnostic gap by integrating advanced semen examinations that cross-examine molecular, oxidative, and structural extents of sperm function. This review critically synthesizes evidence from recent experimental and clinical studies outlining how oxidative stress assays, sperm DNA fragmentation testing, chromatin packaging evaluation, epigenetic alteration assessment, and, proteomic and metabolomic profiling, collectively redefine male infertility diagnostics. These approaches expose mechanistic defects, redox imbalance, genomic and epigenomic instability, and subtle inflammatory or immune perturbations that remain invisible to traditional microscopy. We discuss their clinical translation, standardization challenges, and interpretive drawbacks while proposing a tiered framework that couples basic and advanced assessments for stepwise phenotyping. By reclassifying 'idiopathic' infertility into detectable categories such as redox-deficient, genomic-unstable, or immune-inflammatory subtypes, such precision diagnostics promise individualized interventions, optimized assisted reproduction strategies, and improved prognostic accuracy. The review underscores the urgent need for consistent reference ranges, validated cut-offs, and phenotype-based clinical trials to translate these research-grade tools into routine andrology practice, ultimately transforming the notion of 'idiopathic' male infertility from a diagnosis of exclusion to one of measurable functional insight.

articles.title: Bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) extract alleviates insulin resistance in gestational diabetes mellitus by modulating the AKT/LRRFIP1/GLUT4 pathway in skeletal muscle.
articles.authors: Sun J, Zhang R, Yan K et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is characterized by progressive insulin resistance (IR), with skeletal muscle representing a primary site of this pathology. This study investigated the potential of anthocyanin-rich bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) extract (VME) to ameliorate skeletal muscle IR in a high-fat diet (HFD) induced rat model of GDM. We integrated proteomics and bioinformatics approaches to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.UHPLC-MS/MS analysis identified cyanidin-3-O-galactoside (C3Gal) as the principal anthocyanin constituent of VME. Daily oral administration of VME (400 mg per kg bw) during pregnancy ameliorated hyperglycemia, IR, and dyslipidemia, and improved oral glucose tolerance in GDM rats. Proteomic analysis of gastrocnemius muscle identified VME associated differentially expressed proteins as candidate targets for further investigation. Gene set enrichment analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis implicated AKT signaling and highlighted Lrrfip1 as a hub gene correlated with HOMA-IR. Cross-species comparison with human type 2 diabetes skeletal muscle transcriptomes (GSE55650, GSE7014) supported target prioritization, with LRRFIP1 showing concordant regulation at both mRNA and protein levels. Molecular docking predicted binding of C3Gal to AKT and LRRFIP1, and a cellular thermal shift assay supported cellular target engagement of C3Gal with these proteins. C3Gal restored p-AKT and GLUT4 levels both in vivo and in palmitate-induced C2C12 myotubes. siRNA mediated knockdown of Lrrfip1 attenuated these effects, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AKT abolished them. Collectively, these findings support LRRFIP1 as a downstream mediator of AKT associated GLUT4 regulation. Together, our data propose LRRFIP1 as a candidate molecular target associated with skeletal muscle IR and support further investigation of VME as a potential dietary intervention for GDM associated IR.

articles.title: Early-life reproductive success predicts lifespan: intrinsic quality, not reproductive trade-offs, explains heterogeneity in a short-lived vertebrate.
articles.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
articles.ta: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci
articles.authors: Cattelan S, Valenzano DR
articles.abstract: Individuals of the same species often display extensive lifespan heterogeneity. However, the factors underlying such heterogeneity remain largely elusive. Here, we examined whether lifespan variation in the naturally short-lived turquoise killifish (Nothobranchius furzeri), an annual teleost with a limited reproductive window, is caused by reproductive trade-offs. To examine the individual covariation in reproduction and lifespan, we focused on males and performed in vitro fertilization using ejaculates collected longitudinally throughout life. We found that lifespan and reproduction do not trade off: early-life reproductive success positively predicts male lifespan and reflects intrinsic quality (IQ). A causal model, where IQ affects both survival and reproduction, recapitulates the empirical patterns. Together, our results show inter-individual variation in IQ explains lifespan heterogeneity in a short-lived vertebrate, challenging the view that reproductive costs drive inter-individual lifespan variation. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Prenatal Medicine: Current Evidence, Clinical Validation and Implementation.
articles.authors: Recker F
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly entering obstetrics and prenatal medicine, particularly in prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal magnetic resonance imaging, genomic screening, risk prediction and clinical decision support. The aim of this review was to summarize current evidence, recent developments and implementation requirements for AI-based applications in prenatal care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative review was performed with emphasis on peer-reviewed and clinically relevant literature published from 2021 to 2026, supplemented by landmark methodological, regulatory and reporting guidance. Priority was given to systematic reviews, diagnostic accuracy studies, external validation studies, prospective evaluations, randomized educational or clinical studies, regulatory documents and reporting standards relevant to AI in medicine.
RESULTS: The strongest current evidence supports AI-assisted standard-plane recognition, image-quality assessment and fetal biometry, followed by emerging applications in fetal cardiac screening, blind-sweep ultrasound, fetal MRI segmentation, placental phenotyping, prediction of fetal growth restriction, preterm birth and preeclampsia, and machine learning-enhanced cfDNA analysis. Generative and multimodal AI systems may support report drafting, guideline retrieval and education, but remain insufficiently validated for autonomous clinical decision-making.
DISCUSSION: AI has the potential to improve access, standardization, efficiency and quality assurance in prenatal medicine. However, most applications remain limited by retrospective design, enriched datasets, insufficient external validation, unclear calibration, limited fairness analyses and incomplete workflow evaluation. Clinical adoption should therefore follow a human-in-the-loop model with prospective validation, transparent reporting, regulatory oversight, bias monitoring and post-market surveillance. AI should augment rather than replace specialist expertise in obstetrics and fetal medicine.

articles.title: PD-L1 expression in epithelial ovarian cancer and survival: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Locks-Coelho LD, Ferreira CF, Capp E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate PD-L1 expression, measured by the Combined Positive Score (CPS), and its association with overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with EOC from southern Brazil. PD-L1 immunostaining was performed on tissue microarrays, and expression in tumor and inflammatory cells was assessed using CPS. Patients were classified as PD-L1 positive (CPS ≥1) or negative. Associations with clinicopathological variables, OS, and PFS were analyzed. Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank testing were used for the primary time-to-event comparisons, and multivariable Cox regression was performed to assess independent prognostic associations.
RESULTS: Among 75 patients, 21(28%) were PD-L1 positive and 54(72%) were negative. Clinicopathological characteristics did not differ significantly between groups. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 185 months. In descriptive analyses, PD-L1-positive patients had longer median OS (66 vs. 36.5 months) and PFS (38 vs. 20.5 months). However, Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing showed no statistically significant differences in OS or PFS between groups. In multivariable Cox regression, PD-L1 positivity was independently associated with a lower risk of death (adjusted HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.24-0.99; p = 0.047), but not with recurrence.
CONCLUSION: PD-L1 positivity was associated with a lower risk of death in adjusted analysis, although no significant differences were observed in Kaplan-Meier survival curves. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and considered exploratory. Larger prospective multicenter studies with standardized PD-L1 assessment are needed to validate these results.

articles.title: Addressing the challenges of tuberculosis in pregnancy and postpartum: a question-and-answer-based review.
articles.authors: Rodrigues CS, Gonçalves LI, Sant'Anna CC et al.
articles.abstract: In 2023, tuberculosis (TB) regained its position as the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent worldwide. Despite its global relevance, TB during pregnancy remains insufficiently understood, hindering the development of specific strategies for its diagnosis, treatment, and prevention in this population. Pregnant women with TB are at increased risk of maternal complications such as preterm birth, anemia, and postpartum hemorrhage, as well as higher mortality rates. Fetal complications include low birth weight, intrauterine growth restriction, and perinatal death. Transmission of TB from mother to child can occur via the transplacental route (resulting in congenital TB) or through close contact after birth (resulting in perinatal TB), especially when the mother has disseminated TB or smear-positive pulmonary TB, respectively. Early diagnosis is essential to minimize risks, interrupt transmission, and optimize clinical outcomes. For drug-sensitive TB, the standard treatment regimen is considered safe; however, treatment of drug-resistant TB requires the use of potentially teratogenic drugs. Prophylaxis with isoniazid and rifampicin has proven effective and safe in preventing TB in exposed neonates. The lack of clinical trials involving pregnant women with TB limits the available scientific evidence regarding the safest and most effective diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. This review, presented in a question-and-answer format, aims to contribute to improved management of TB during pregnancy and reduce the risk of adverse outcomes for both mother and child.

articles.title: Clinicopathologic ımpact and prognostic value of lymphovascular space ınvasion within the MMRd molecular subgroup of endometrial carcinoma.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Keles E, Maraşlı M, Taşyurek M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinicopathological significance and prognostic impact of lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) within the mismatch repair-deficient (MMRd) molecular subgroup of endometrial cancer.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on patients with histologically confirmed endometrial carcinoma who underwent primary surgical staging between January 2017 and December 2020. Immunohistochemical analysis of mismatch repair proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2) was performed to classify tumors into MMR-proficient or MMR-deficient (MMRd) subgroups. LVSI status was independently reviewed and classified as absent, focal, or substantial by two gynecologic pathologists. Clinicopathologic findings and follow-up data were extracted from the institutional electronic medical records.
RESULTS: A total of 214 patients with a mean age 60.61±9.70 years were included, with a median follow-up of 24.6 months (IQR: 24.7 months). Fifteen death events (7.0%) were recorded during the study period. LVSI was identified in 42 patients (19.6%), including 26 with focal and 16 with substantial involvement. LVSI-positive tumors were significantly associated with larger tumor size (p<0.001), high-grade histology (p<0.001), non-endometrioid subtype (p<0.001), lymph node metastasis (p<0.001), and advanced FIGO stage (p<0.001). Among the 70 patients (32.7%) with MMRd tumors, LVSI was observed in 14 cases (20.0%) and remained significantly associated with aggressive features, including larger tumor size (p <0.001), high-grade histology (p = 0.010), advanced stage (p = 0.011), and lymph node involvement (p <0.001). However, overall survival did not differ significantly between LVSI-positive and LVSI-negative MMRd patients (log-rank p = 0.213).
CONCLUSION: LVSI is associated with adverse clinicopathologic features in endometrial cancer, including within the MMRd molecular subgroup. However, its presence does not appear to independently influence overall survival in MMRd patients.

articles.title: Should glucose screening be repeated for large-for-gestational-age fetuses in the third trimester of non-diabetic pregnancies? A scoping review.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Leal CRV, Corrêa MD
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map and synthesize global evidence regarding the clinical utility, diagnostic yield, and perinatal impact of repeating third-trimester glucose screening in previously screen-negative, non-diabetic pregnancies complicated by ultrasound-suspected large-for-gestational-age (LGA) fetuses or macrosomia, evaluating whether late dysglycemia explains accelerated growth.
METHODS: Following defined criteria for singleton pregnancies with normal mid-trimester testing and late-onset suspected fetal overgrowth, a systematic search was performed in June 2026 across PubMed, Embase, and SciELO for peer-reviewed articles in English, Portuguese, and Spanish. Two independent reviewers handled selection, rigorous critical appraisal, and data extraction for qualitative narrative synthesis.
RESULTS: Fifteen observational studies met inclusion criteria (nine retrospective cohorts, four prospective cohorts, two case-controls). Diagnostic yield for late-onset gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) ranged from 2.9% to 24.6%. Diagnosing late GDM consistently changed clinical management, driving higher rates of labor induction and cesarean deliveries. Active standard-of-care maternal interventions initiated after retesting effectively curtailed excessive growth trajectories, producing no statistically significant differences in acute neonatal morbidities, such as shoulder dystocia or neonatal intensive care unit admissions, compared to non-diabetic controls.
CONCLUSION: Indiscriminate repeat third-trimester glucose testing for isolated LGA fetuses cannot be routinely recommended due to high methodological heterogeneity and no randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Fetal overgrowth remains predominantly multifactorial, mediated by maternal obesity and dyslipidemia. Clinical management warrants careful individualization, and robust interventional RCTs are needed.
OPEN SCIENCE FRAMEWORK: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/TFH7A.
