articles.title: Endometrial Microbes, Systemic Inflammatory Markers, and In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes Among Infertile Women: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Panigrahi K, Acharya M, Sahoo JP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Infertility among couples of the reproductive age group is a global healthcare concern. Imbalance in the neuro-immune-endocrine network leads to altered pro- and anti-inflammatory markers and endometrial dysbiosis. These two factors collectively cause infertility, despite the advancements in in vitro fertilization (IVF). Indian studies exploring this aspect are scarce. Therefore, we planned to evaluate endometrial microbes, interleukin-10 (IL-10), and IL-17 among infertile women seeking IVF.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2025 to June 2026 at Kalinga Institute of Medical Sciences (KIMS), Bhubaneswar, India. Infertile women aged 31-40 years seeking treatment with IVF were included in this study. Those with active vaginal or cervical infection, any autoimmune disease, or use of antimicrobials, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressive agents were excluded. The endometrial and blood samples were obtained in the peri-implantation window. Cultivable isolates were identified using matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS; BioMérieux, France). Serum IL-10 and IL-17 levels were detected using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). We used R software (version 4.6.2) for data analysis.
RESULTS: Our study population comprised 50 infertile women. The study population's median age was 37 (35-38) years. The median body mass index (BMI) of the study participants was 26.75 (24.20-30.80) kg/m2. Of the study participants, 32 (64%) had primary infertility. Of the 50, 17 (34%) had a tubal cause of infertility. Lactobacillus spp. (23, 46%) was the most common microbe in the endometrial cultures, followed by Enterococcus faecalis (5, 10%) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (5, 10%). A total of 20 (40%) participants became pregnant following IVF treatment. The remaining 30 (60%) had IVF failure. The median IL-10 values for participants with IVF failure and success were 14.93 (13.87-15.96) pg/mL and 35.60 (32.53-39.94) pg/mL, respectively (p < 0.001). The corresponding median IL-17 values were 40.02 (34.84-44.29) pg/mL and 23.57 (21.06-24.36) pg/mL (p < 0.001). The 20 participants who were pregnant with IVF had lower IL-17 levels and higher IL-10 levels. The differences were statistically significant. The IVF success rates were seen among those aged 31-35 years (8 of 15, 53.3%), secondary infertility (9 of 18, 50%), those with Lactobacillus spp. (14 of 23, 60.9%), and those with…

articles.title: Discriminative Performance of the C-Reactive Protein-Triglyceride-Glucose Index for Endometriosis: A Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Rokhgireh S, Salehi Z, Mohazzab A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endometriosis, a common gynecologic disorder, causes pain and fertility problems. Since laparoscopy, as a definitive diagnostic procedure, is considered invasive, finding reliable and noninvasive biomarkers is a clinical priority. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) for endometriosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this case-control study, 153 participants with surgically confirmed endometriosis and 112 participants without visible endometriosis at laparoscopy were included. Fasting glucose, triglycerides (TG), total cholesterol, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured, and CTI was calculated using a previously described formula. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was carried out to assess diagnostic discrimination and identify an exploratory threshold for CTI cutoff. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the independent relationship between CTI and endometriosis. Nested models were also assessed to examine the incremental contribution of TG and glucose beyond CRP.
RESULTS: Women with endometriosis exhibited higher levels of TG, total cholesterol, ESR, CRP, and CTI than controls (all P<0.001), whereas fasting glucose did not differ significantly between groups. CTI showed good discrimination for endometriosis, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.900 (95% CI, 0.858-0.942). An exploratory cutoff of 9.686 yielded a sensitivity of 92.16% and specificity of 83.93%. CTI was independently associated with endometriosis after adjustment for age, body mass index, systolic and diastolic blood pressure (adjusted OR per 0.5-unit increase, 2.598; 95% CI, 2.079-3.245; P<0.001). However, CTI's discriminatory performance was not significantly different from CRP's. (AUC 0.898; P=0.827). Addition of TG to a CRP-based model significantly improved model fit (P=0.007), whereas addition of glucose did not (P=0.095); the overall difference in AUCs across the nested models was not statistically significant (P=0.719).
CONCLUSION: CTI showed good discrimination for endometriosis but did not significantly outperform CRP. It may serve as a complementary biomarker alongside clinical and imaging assessment.

articles.title: Prenatal genomics and autism: detectable susceptibility without validated individual-level prediction.
articles.authors: Shateri A
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a behaviorally defined, biologically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with high heritability, estimated at 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.87) in Swedish population data. Large-scale exome sequencing, copy-number variant analysis, and genome-wide association studies have implicated a growing number of genes and genomic loci in autism liability, and functional genomic work has repeatedly converged on mid-gestational cortical development. In parallel, prenatal genetics has moved from karyotyping to chromosomal microarray analysis, exome and genome sequencing, and screening based on cell-free DNA in maternal plasma. This review asks how far these developments allow genetic susceptibility to autism to be identified before birth, and what prevents such identification from constituting prediction or diagnosis of autism in an individual fetus. It organizes the evidence in four steps - analytic validity (can the variant be detected in fetal DNA)?, variant interpretation (can it be classified under ACMG/AMP and ACMG-ClinGen standards)?, clinical validity (how far does it shift the probability of autism)?, and clinical utility (does knowing it improve outcomes)? - which makes explicit the classification step within the conventional three-stage sequence and locates where translation breaks down. A second distinction, between molecular diagnosis of a genetic condition and diagnosis of autism itself, runs alongside it. Recurrent copy-number variants such as 16p11.2 and 15q11-q13 rearrangements, and pathogenic variants in genes such as CHD8, SCN2A, SHANK3, and PTEN, are technically detectable by currently available prenatal diagnostic genomic platforms when such testing is clinically indicated. Their interpretation is frequently incomplete, their clinical validity for autism specifically is limited by incomplete penetrance, variable expressivity, and pleiotropy, and their clinical utility for neurodevelopmental prediction is unestablished. Common polygenic variation contributes substantially to population-level liability, but individual-level discrimination is poor and ancestry portability is limited. Prenatal diagnostic genomic testing is additionally largely indication-driven rather than a population screen for neurodevelopmental risk. Prenatal sequencing may therefore establish a molecular diagnosis of a condition associated with an increased likelihood of autism; this is not prenatal diagnosis of autism. Progress will require…

articles.title: Identification of m6A-Associated mRNAs, lncRNAs, and m6A Regulators in Endometriosis.
articles.authors: Ren C, He Y, Qu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis (EMs), which causes significant pain and infertility, continues to affect women of reproductive age, yet its molecular mechanisms remain inadequately defined. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification is the most prevalent post-transcriptional modification in mammalian mRNA, and recent studies have increasingly focused on elucidating the relationship between m6A and EMs, to provide theoretical insights for clinical prevention and treatment.
METHODS: Using human m6A-mRNA and lncRNA epigenomic microarray techniques, functional and pathway enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction network (PPI), and R packages, we conducted exploratory analyses to identify mRNAs and lncRNAs with differential methylation, as well as important m6A regulators associated with EMs. These findings were verified using external databases, along with RNA extraction and quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR), immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence techniques.
RESULTS: Specifically, our analysis revealed 1631 hyper-upregulated, 219 hypo-upregulated, and 6483 hypo-downregulated differentially methylated and expressed genes (DMEGs). Additionally, we identified 8 candidate hub genes-RHOA, KCNA2, BDNF, CACNA1C, FGFR1, IL18, KCNIP2, and RPL17-and characterized their enriched pathways. Furthermore, we observed 6 significantly hypermethylated and 14 significantly hypomethylated lncRNAs in EMs. Our screening identified two key m6A regulators, WTAP and RBM15, which may represent candidate molecules worthy of further investigation in the context of EMs.
CONCLUSION: This exploratory screening analysis delineates aberrant expression signatures of m6A regulators and their associated mRNAs and lncRNAs in endometriosis tissues, yielding preliminary molecular profiles that merely reflect correlations rather than causal or definite functional relationships.

articles.title: Maternal safety outcomes following bilateral hypogastric artery ligation in placenta accreta spectrum and severe obstetric hemorrhage: a retrospective tertiary-center cohort.
articles.authors: Hanulikova P, Krofta L, Halaj M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The hemostatic efficacy of bilateral hypogastric artery ligation (HAL) remains controversial, whereas its procedure-related maternal safety has been insufficiently investigated. This study evaluated procedure-related maternal morbidity and long-term patient-reported outcomes following prophylactic or therapeutic HAL.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 137 women with complete outcome data who underwent bilateral hypogastric artery ligation (HAL) at a tertiary referral center between 2005 and 2023. Women were stratified according to PAS status (PAS group, n = 45; non-PAS group, n = 92); all PAS cases had been suspected antenatally. The primary outcome was early non-transfusion major maternal morbidity, defined as disseminated intravascular coagulation, urinary tract injury, or reoperation within 7 days after delivery. Secondary analyses evaluated PAS severity (FIGO grades 1-2 vs. 3a/b), long-term patient-reported outcomes, and the independent association between PAS status and major maternal morbidity.
RESULTS: Women with PAS delivered earlier (35 vs. 37 weeks, p < 0.001) and underwent hysterectomy more frequently (84.4% vs. 34.8%, p < 0.001). Despite substantially greater surgical complexity, early procedure-related maternal morbidity was comparable between groups (24.4% vs. 23.9%, p = 1.000). Urinary bladder injury occurred more frequently in the PAS group (17.8% vs. 3.3%, p = 0.006), whereas rates of disseminated intravascular coagulation and reoperation were similar. Within the PAS group, FIGO grade 3a/b was associated with higher rates of overall complications and massive transfusion. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that PAS status was not independently associated with early major maternal morbidity after adjustment for gestational age, previous uterine surgery, maternal age, BMI, and parity. There were no ischemic complications in long-term patient-reported outcomes (n = 63).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide clinically relevant evidence on procedure-related maternal outcomes following HAL when performed within an experienced multidisciplinary tertiary-center setting. Although PAS was associated with substantially greater surgical complexity, early procedure-related maternal morbidity remained comparable between groups, and no severe long-term ischemic complications were reported in women who completed the structured follow-up questionnaire.

articles.title: Voices of Families: Enhancing Antenatal Consultations for Preterm Births.
articles.authors: Chelabi K, Germain A, Treherne S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Antenatal consultations (ANCs) are offered to families in the context of potential preterm birth and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. For gestational ages ≥ 26 weeks, no decision regarding levels of care is required, positioning the ANC primarily as an opportunity for families' preparation and information sharing. However, limited data describe how families retrospectively perceive these encounters after experiencing the NICU. We aimed to explore parental perspectives on ANCs for preterm birth outside of the periviable period after NICU hospitalization.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted an exploratory qualitative study in 2 tertiary-quaternary NICUs in Montreal, Canada. Parents of infants born between 26 + 0 and 34 + 6 weeks of gestation who had received an ANC were recruited once their infant had been hospitalized for >1 week. Semistructured interviews were conducted and analyzed using thematic content analysis with independent coding and consensus resolution.
RESULTS: Twenty-three families participated. Parents reported limited recall of medical information and described emotional overload antenatally. Few expressed a desire for detailed medical information. Meanwhile, families emphasized the importance of honest reassurance about prognosis, trust in the NICU team, and feeling accompanied through uncertainty. Relatable and concrete supports, including visual materials and personal stories, helped externalize prematurity and rendered information more tangible and emotionally accessible.
CONCLUSIONS: After NICU experience, parents described ANCs primarily as relational encounters centered on reassurance, trust, and accompaniment rather than as information-driven discussions. Reframing ANCs to prioritize relational support and staged information delivery may better align counseling practices with family needs for preterm births beyond 26 weeks of gestation.

articles.title: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles delivering CERS1 promote squamous differentiation in HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia via remodeling sphingomyelin metabolism.
articles.authors: Yang H, Chen W, Liu L et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), a precursor of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven cervical cancer, poses a severe threat to women's health. High-risk HPV infection drives CIN progression, whereas well-defined intervention targets and effective non-invasive therapies remain lacking. Herein, Using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), specifically HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids as a human-relevant disease model, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of engineered cell-free small extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSC-sEV). We found that hucMSC-sEV significantly promoted squamous differentiation in S12 cells and HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids. Mechanistically, integrated multi-omics analyses within this NAMs platform revealed that hucMSC-sEV delivered ceramide synthase 1 (CERS1) to upregulate C18 ceramide (C18 Cer) synthesis, activating the non-canonical p53 signaling to drive squamous differentiation. In NCG mice bearing subcutaneous xenografts of S12 cells, hucMSC-sEV effectively inhibited S12 xenograft growth and modulated squamous differentiation via regulation of C18 ceramide metabolism, while this therapeutic effect was abrogated in CERS1-knockdown hucMSC-sEV. This study delineates the molecular mechanism by which hucMSC-sEV remodel sphingolipid metabolism to promote cervical squamous epithelial differentiation and suppress S12 xenograft development, providing novel potential targets and therapeutic strategies for CIN intervention.

articles.title: The hidden genome of high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma: repetitive DNA, extrachromosomal DNA, and complex structural variation.
articles.authors: Xu X, Ren X, Yuan Z
articles.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) is marked by extensive genomic instability, characterized by near-universal TP53 mutations, frequent homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), widespread copy-number alterations, and complex structural rearrangements. However, much of our current understanding of this molecular landscape has been derived from exome sequencing, microarrays, and short-read whole-genome sequencing, which are limited in their ability to resolve repetitive and structurally complex genomic regions. Long-read sequencing, together with telomere-to-telomere reference assemblies, is beginning to reveal previously inaccessible aspects of HGSOC genome architecture. Exploratory studies have reported centromeric and transposable-element hypomethylation, chromosome-arm-specific telomere shortening, and complex extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) architectures associated with enhancer regulation and transposable-element activity. Complementary studies have also identified ongoing LINE-1 retrotransposition in HGSOC. Together, these observations suggest that repetitive DNA, epigenetic instability, and complex genome architecture may contribute to HGSOC heterogeneity and tumor evolution, although their causal relationships remain uncertain. Nevertheless, genome-wide long-read evidence in HGSOC currently derives primarily from two small studies involving six and 12 patients, respectively, underscoring the need for validation in larger, independent cohorts.

articles.title: Spectrum of FGFR2 Mutations and Plausible Phenotypic Modifiers Contributing to the Etiology of Syndromic Craniosynostosis in Sub-Saharan Africans.
articles.authors: Gowans LJJ, Asante MD, Sabbah DK et al.
articles.abstract: Craniosynostosis, the premature fusion of cranial sutures resulting from disrupted molecular and cellular mechanisms of suture patency, ranks as the second most common craniofacial birth defect. It manifests as syndromic (15%-30%) or nonsyndromic (70%-85%) forms and has multifactorial etiology. This cross-sectional, observational, family-based study is aimed at elucidating the genetic basis of syndromic craniosynostosis in a Ghanaian cohort presenting with characteristic phenotypes of FGFR2-related syndromes. Eight case-parent trios with syndromic craniosynostosis were recruited, and saliva/buccal swab samples were collected for DNA extraction. Whole exome sequencing (WES) of DNA samples was performed on the Illumina HiSeq platform at 100x read depth in a paired-end configuration. Quality control, read alignment, and variant calling followed the Sentieon V202112.01 workflow, with variant annotation utilizing Ensembl VEP V104. Variants were filtered for minor allele frequency < 0.01 across databases, and pathogenicity was evaluated using 11 dbNSFP-embedded tools and SpliceAI. ClinVar and LOVD were used to verify the pathogenicity of variants. Gene expression, enrichment and interaction analyses, and associated phenotype ascertainment utilized various databases such as DECIPHER and OMIM. Five probands harbored de novo pathogenic variants in FGFR2 (p.Asp336Gly, p.Cys342Ser, p.Pro253Arg, p.Gly272del, and p.Ser252Trp). However, lack of paternal samples limited the determination of the de novo status of two variants (p.Ser252Trp and p.Cys342Gly) in three probands. These variants affected multiple cranial suture types, including coronal, sagittal, metopic, and lambdoid, and were associated with the clinical diagnoses of Apert and Crouzon syndromes. Additional likely pathogenic variants in other genes that may plausibly contribute to phenotypic variability were also observed. In silico functional analysis buttressed the role of FGFR2 and plausible variants contributing to phenotypic variability. Thus, FGFR2 variants contribute to syndromic craniosynostosis among Ghanaians, with additional genetic variants plausibly influencing phenotypic variability among probands. This study may impact genetic counseling (prenatal testing and recurrence risk) and other clinical management of craniosynostosis.

articles.title: Ultrasound Evaluation of Varicoceles: A Closed-Loop Audit of Compliance With European Society of Urogenital Radiology Guidelines.
articles.authors: Khan HA, Paramesparan K
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate ultrasound reporting practices for varicoceles at a district general hospital in London against the European Society of Urogenital Radiology Scrotal and Penile Imaging Working Group (ESUR-SPIWG) standards and measure the impact of a structured reporting intervention.
BACKGROUND: Varicoceles are common and may cause infertility and chronic scrotal discomfort. Ultrasound is the gold standard imaging modality for investigation. The ESUR-SPIWG guidelines, based on the Sarteschi grading system, mandate documentation of testicular volume, vein location and diameter (supine and erect), and duration of venous reflux. Previous audit data suggested poor compliance with these standards.
METHODS: Retrospective closed-loop audit of ultrasound reports for 40 patients per cycle, investigated for varicoceles (Cycle 1: July 2023; Cycle 2: October 2024). Data were extracted from the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) and CERNER (electronic health records). Three key reporting criteria were assessed per ESUR-SPIWG guidelines. A structured reporting template was introduced as an intervention between audit cycles.
RESULTS: Full compliance with all three criteria improved from 0% in Cycle 1 to 22.5% (9/40 cases) in Cycle 2. Cases documenting at least one criterion increased from 47.5% (19/40) to 82.5% (33/40). While the intervention demonstrated improvement, substantial gaps in adherence remain.
CONCLUSIONS: The implementation of a structured reporting template showed measurable improvement in ESUR-SPIWG compliance; however, current practice still falls well short of the 100% target. This represents an audit cycle requiring continued quality improvement efforts. Further initiatives, including in-person education, intranet-accessible reporting pathways, and sustained reinforcement, are necessary to achieve guideline compliance and improve clinical decision-making for varicocele management.

articles.title: Association of obstetric factors with maternal morbidity and mortality in patients who gave birth preterm.
articles.authors: Des Jardin MK, McGee PL, Sibai BM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth is associated with an increased rate of serious maternal complication compared with those who deliver at term. However, data are limited on risk factors for maternal morbidity and mortality specifically in the setting of preterm birth. Improved understanding of risk factors for morbidity in patients with preterm birth can help optimize interventions to best support patients experiencing preterm birth.
OBJECTIVE: To assess associations between obstetric factors and maternal morbidities and mortality among patients who gave birth less than 35 weeks' gestation.
STUDY DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of a multicenter registry of gravidas carrying singletons or twins who gave birth at 16 0/7 to 34 6/7 weeks' gestation January through August 2019. The primary outcome was a maternal morbidity and mortality composite (blood transfusion, postpartum hemorrhage, maternal sepsis, stroke, thromboembolism, intensive care unit admission, or death) during the delivery hospitalization. Factors were compared between those with and without the composite outcome to identify statistically significant variables. Those factors were then used to create a parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model with adjusted odds ratio (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a backward strategy. We estimated area under the curve to quantify the predictive ability of these factors for the primary outcome.
RESULTS: The analysis was based on 6660 patients, of whom 15.1% experienced the primary composite outcome. Factors associated with increased odds of the outcome included increasing maternal age, use of assisted reproductive technology, twin gestation, preeclampsia, placental abruption and cesarean delivery-aOR ranged from 1.02 [1.01-1.04] for maternal age (continuous) to 2.55 [2.08-3.14] for abruption. In contrast, nulliparity, gestational diabetes, preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM), and later birth gestational age were associated with decreased odds of the primary outcome-aOR ranging from 0.96 [0.95-0.98] for gestational age (continuous) to 0.54 [0.44-0.66] for PPROM. The model with these factors had low to moderate predictive ability (AUC 0.68 [0.66-0.69]).
CONCLUSION: Among individuals who experienced preterm birth before 35 weeks, multiple factors were associated with maternal morbidity and mortality. The factors together modestly discriminate maternal morbidity or mortality.

articles.title: Perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended virtual and in-person prenatal care model in integrated healthcare systems.
articles.authors: Fassett MJ, West EV, Gibson EC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional US prenatal care typically includes 12-14 standardized in-person visits. COVID-19-related barriers accelerated adoption of blended virtual/in-person prenatal care, but evidence from large, diverse populations is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To compare perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended prenatal care model versus traditional in-person care in a large health maintenance organization.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study in Kaiser Permanente Northwest and Southern California comparing blended care (cases, July 22, 2022 to December 31, 2024) with traditional in-person care (controls, January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019). Groups were compared using t-tests/Wilcoxon and chi-square tests; multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Among 47,577 patients (473 cases; 47,104 controls), cases were older at delivery (mean = 32.0 [SD = 4.6] vs. 30.4 [4.9] years, p < 0.0001), more likely to be non-Hispanic White (68.9% vs. 26.5%, p < 0.0001), had higher median household income, and higher rates of publicly funded coverage (15.9% vs. 9.1%, p < 0.0001). Cases had fewer nulliparous women (20.9% vs. 47.5%, p < 0.0001), higher smoking rates (9.5% vs. 2.7%), and less likely to initiate prenatal care in the first trimester (92.6% vs. 96.8%). Cases had fewer in-person visits (mean = 6.2 [2.7] vs. 15.7 [6.2], p < 0.0001), more virtual visits (3.2 [1.4] vs. 1.0 [1.4], p < 0.0001), and fewer total visits (9.4 [3.2] vs. 16.7 [6.5], p < 0.0001). Depression screening was more frequent in cases (84.1% vs. 45.9%, p < 0.0001). Compared to controls, cases had lower odds of preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) (aOR, 0.17; 95% CI, 0.05-0.58), preterm birth <37 weeks (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.22-0.61), and stillbirth (aOR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.03-0.70), but higher odds of non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing (aOR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.06-1.60), gestational diabetes (aOR, 3.75; 95% CI, 2.80-5.01), and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR; aOR, 2.46; 95% CI, 1.42-4.25). No significant differences were observed in placenta previa, chorioamnionitis, cesarean birth, postpartum hemorrhage, macrosomia, placental abruption, preeclampsia/eclampsia, or maternal length of stay more than 2 days.
CONCLUSIONS: Blended virtual/in-person prenatal care was associated with comparable perinatal outcomes despite fewer visits. Lower odds of preterm birth, PPROM, and stillbirth and higher odds of…

articles.title: Lactate metabolic plasticity across the menopausal transition: a hypothesis-generating framework linking ovarian hormone variability, exercise, and skeletal muscle remodeling.
articles.authors: Duan X, Du D
articles.abstract: The menopausal transition combines marked ovarian-hormone variability with changes in body composition, insulin sensitivity, vascular function, skeletal muscle, and exercise substrate use. Established lactate-shuttle, maximal-lactate-steady-state, metabolic-flexibility, and Lactate-Carbohydrate models already explain that lactate is an oxidative fuel, a gluconeogenic precursor, and an informative but protocol-dependent marker of substrate use rather than a waste product. The unresolved menopause-specific question is whether changing ovarian status alters the coordination of systemic lactate appearance and disappearance during exercise and recovery. This Mini Review therefore distinguishes evidence from natural perimenopause from evidence in established postmenopause and other populations, defines testable stage-specific hypotheses, and proposes a component measurement profile for future studies. The profile combines standardized absolute and relative exercise workloads, serial blood lactate concentrations, stable-isotope estimates of lactate rate of appearance, rate of disappearance, oxidation and recycling, repeated estradiol and follicle-stimulating hormone measurements, and muscle or vascular phenotyping. A structured narrative search identified no study that directly measured lactate flux or whole-body metabolic clearance during natural perimenopause. The novelty of the proposed framework therefore lies in its menopause-specific evidence hierarchy and study design, not in reclassifying lactate biology. Longitudinal studies are needed before any component can be treated as a menopausal biomarker or used to individualize exercise prescription.

articles.title: The PGE2-EP receptor axis in urinary tract smooth muscle: one signaling system, three organ-specific strategies.
articles.authors: Su H, Zhou W, Ao F et al.
articles.abstract: Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) is the dominant lipid mediator generated within the urinary tract wall, yet the direction of its action reverses from organ to organ: it excites the bladder, suppresses the ureter, and relaxes the prostate and urethra. This review asks why one signaling system produces three opposite outputs and what that organization offers for therapy. Synthesizing 115 publications, from classical organ-bath studies to current clinical trials, we first outline the molecular toolkit-an inducible biosynthetic arm and four EP receptor subtypes with asymmetric G protein coupling-that makes divergent deployment chemically possible. We then assemble the organ-specific evidence. In the bladder, EP1/EP3-driven contraction and afferent sensitization are distributed across a chimera of smooth muscle, urothelium, interstitial cells, and nerves, and are amplified by obstruction, inflammation, denervation, and aging. In the ureter, EP2-mediated inhibition of peristalsis-with the EP4 component still an inference from coupling logic-is the property that NSAIDs, the first-line analgesics for renal colic, act upon, although whether their benefit arises from restoring motility, reducing edema, or dampening nociceptors remains unresolved. In the outflow tract, the weakest-evidenced arm, EP-dependent relaxation is supported by rodent pharmacology and by a single clinical association between pathway activation and BPH that fails medical therapy. Within this PGE2-centered frame, receptor-subtype repurposing across organs is consistent with rules that pathology reweights but does not erase-weights inferred from function rather than measured receptor abundance-and much of the literature's apparent contradiction dissolves under five methodological variables. We propose the axis as one system deployed in three organ-specific strategies-a testable working hypothesis, with the outflow tract currently a plausible third member, under which choosing a receptor subtype would approximate choosing an organ. The hypothesis maps onto therapy as one established success, two credible prospects-EP2/EP3 agonism for underactive bladder and EP2 agonism for stone expulsion-and one open frontier, and we define the maps, conditional knockouts, verified ligands, and computational tools needed to convert it into organ-directed pharmacology.

articles.title: Second-trimester fetal thymic-thoracic ratio in pregnancies treated with levothyroxine for elevated first-trimester TSH: a retrospective case-control study.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Demir FN, Cevval ZK, Kayıkçı U
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maternal thyroid dysfunction during pregnancy has been associated with adverse fetal and obstetric outcomes; however, the relationship between early pregnancy TSH elevation, levothyroxine treatment, and fetal thymic development remains unclear. This study aimed to compare second-trimester fetal thymic-thoracic ratio (TTR) values between pregnancies receiving levothyroxine after elevated first-trimester thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels and healthy controls.
METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 109 pregnant women who underwent second-trimester obstetric ultrasonography between February 2023 and December 2024. Pregnancies treated with levothyroxine after first-trimester TSH levels ≥2.5 mIU/L (n=43) were compared with healthy controls without thyroid disease or pregnancy-related complications (n=66). Fetal thymic-thoracic ratio measurements were obtained from stored ultrasound images using the method described by Chaoui et al. Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test.
RESULTS: No statistically significant difference was observed in fetal thymic-thoracic ratio values between the levothyroxine-treated group and the healthy control group (median TTR: 0.420 [0.345-0.445] vs. 0.395 [0.323-0.450], respectively; p=0.483). Similarly, no significant differences were found between the groups regarding maternal age, gestational age at examination, thymic diameter, thoracic diameter, BMI, or smoking status (all p>0.05).
CONCLUSION: Second-trimester fetal TTR values did not differ significantly between healthy controls and pregnancies treated with levothyroxine after elevated first-trimester TSH. These preliminary findings suggest that early-treated maternal TSH elevation may not be associated with measurable alterations in fetal thymic size during the second trimester. However, the retrospective design, incomplete characterization of thyroid status (including free T4, thyroid antibodies, levothyroxine dose, and confirmation of euthyroidism), and limited statistical power preclude definitive conclusions regarding the effect of treatment. Further prospective, adequately powered longitudinal studies with complete thyroid function data are needed to clarify this relationship.

articles.title: Endometrial preparation for embryo transfer: reproductive outcomes of modified natural cycle versus hormone replacement therapy.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: de Sá LC, Fagundes LS, Lamaita RM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Compare reproductive outcomes between modified natural cycle (mNC) and hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for endometrial preparation in embryo transfer.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study (2020-2024) including 180 cycles that reached embryo transfer at a tertiary center. Primary outcome was biochemical pregnancy (β-hCG positivity), and clinical pregnancy was secondary. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for baseline imbalances (age, infertility duration, endometriosis, unexplained infertility) and embryonic factors (developmental stage, PGT-A status) was performed. Sensitivity analyses assessed embryonic heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Cohort comprised 68.9% HRT and 31.1% mNC cycles. Baseline differences were observed: mNC had higher rates of endometriosis (41% vs. 25%; p = 0.029), unexplained infertility (30% vs. 9.7%; p < 0.001), and longer infertility duration (median 5 vs. 3 years; p = 0.003), while anovulation was more frequent in HRT (22% vs. 5.4%; p = 0.006). No statistically significant difference in biochemical pregnancy rates was observed between groups (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.45-1.65; p = 0.682). After adjustment, endometrial preparation protocol was not independently associated with biochemical pregnancy (aOR 1.31; 95% CI 0.51-3.35; p = 0.568). Sensitivity analyses showed consistent results despite blastocyst transfer predominance (75%).
CONCLUSION: After adjustment for clinical and embryonic confounders, no statistically significant association was observed between endometrial preparation protocol and β-hCG levels or clinical pregnancy among cycles that achieved embryo transfer. Despite retrospective design, limited progesterone data, and exclusion of canceled cycles, mNC may represent a feasible physiological alternative in selected ovulatory patients, although prospective studies are needed.

articles.title: Clinical Factors Associated With Failure of Uterine Compression Sutures in Postpartum Hemorrhage During Cesarean Delivery: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Abusin FY, Ebaid Mahdi Gabreldaar A, Olaleye AA et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine compression sutures can preserve the uterus during refractory postpartum hemorrhage, but clinical factors associated with failure are less well established than overall success rates. This review examined evidence specifically applicable to cesarean delivery. PubMed/MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online), Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched without a lower publication-date restriction. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed primary investigations of therapeutic uterine compression sutures with cesarean-specific clinical-factor information linked to treatment outcomes. Additional hemostatic treatment and hysterectomy were considered separate endpoints. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool, and findings were synthesized narratively, supplemented by study-level effect estimates and an exploratory pooled analysis of event proportions. Of 1,010 identified records, 374 remained after deduplication; of these, 76 reports underwent full-text assessment, and finally four studies were included. Their original cohorts contained 105 women, of whom 102 underwent cesarean delivery. Two studies were rated at low overall risk of bias and two at high risk. Placental pathology was the principal directly evaluable clinical factor, although placenta previa and suspected placenta accreta spectrum represented distinct exposures; escalation was more frequent with suspected placenta accreta spectrum. Evidence for other factors was sparse, and factor-specific estimates were not pooled. In an exploratory random-effects analysis, immediate hemorrhage-related hysterectomy occurred in 21.7% (95% CI 14.7-30.8%) of treated cesarean cases. The evidence supports attention to hemorrhage etiology and a distinction between escalation of treatment and loss of the uterus. It does not establish a validated cesarean-specific prediction model or a reliable threshold for abandoning compression sutures.

articles.title: Patient Willingness-To-Pay and Preferences for Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidy (PGT-A) Provision Models in Japan.
articles.authors: Wakui N, Takiuchi T, Shen J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantify Japanese infertile couples' willingness to pay (WTP) for preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) and to identify preferences for key service-delivery attributes to inform improved models.
METHODS: We conducted an online survey using a discrete choice experiment among couples who participated in a PGT-A clinical study under Japan's Advanced Medical Care B program. The primary outcome was the WTP for an additional embryo submitted. Secondary outcomes included preferences for service characteristics influencing the examination plan choice.
RESULTS: The mean WTP for an additional embryo submitted was JPY 84,072 for women and JPY 87,295 for men. Preferences were significantly influenced by the distance to the medical facility, the number of embryologists, and the duration of PGT-A and results explanations. The mean WTP for a 1-minute extension of the PGT-A explanation time was JPY 7023 for women and JPY 6778 for men, while that for test-result explanation was valued at JPY 8571 and JPY 8662, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: In Japan, infertile couples are willing to pay approximately JPY 85,000 (USD 541) per additional embryo submitted, and service components-particularly the time devoted to explaining results-substantially affect PGT-A plan preferences. Building a delivery model based on these findings is crucial.

articles.title: Sex differences in atrial fibrillation incidence among individuals with metabolic syndrome: a narrative mini review.
articles.authors: Bonapace S, Molon G, Tosi P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex differences influence the development and clinical expression of many chronic cardiometabolic diseases. Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common sustained arrhythmia, frequently coexists with metabolic syndrome (MetS), yet whether MetS confers different AF risk in men and women remains incompletely understood.
CONTENT: Epidemiological evidence consistently demonstrates that MetS increases the risk of incident AF by approximately 1.4- to 1.9-fold. Among MetS components, elevated blood pressure and abdominal obesity show the strongest associations with AF onset. Most studies also reveal that men have higher rates of AF than women across all age groups, although AF incidence in women rises sharply after menopause. In individuals with MetS, similar sex-related trends are observed: men typically exhibit a higher and earlier AF incidence, whereas women experience a delayed but steep increase in older age.Biological differences-particularly sex hormone-driven variations in fat distribution, lipid metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and inflammation-may underlie these patterns. Premenopausal women tend to accumulate subcutaneous, metabolically benign fat, whereas men preferentially store visceral fat, promoting earlier metabolic dysfunction and AF susceptibility. After menopause, declining estrogen levels shift women toward central adiposity and cardiometabolic deterioration, narrowing the AF incidence gap. Sex-related differences in autonomic balance and adiposity-related sympathetic activation may further modulate AF risk.
CONCLUSION: While MetS increases AF risk in both sexes, accumulating evidence suggests that the magnitude, timing, and underlying mechanisms of this risk differ between men and women. Better integration of sex-specific biological pathways into AF prevention strategies is warranted.

articles.title: Long-chain acyl-CoA synthetases in female reproductive diseases: isoform-specific regulation of lipid metabolism, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling.
articles.authors: Jin S, Guo L, Wu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Female reproductive diseases (FRDs) substantially affect women's health and fertility, with lipid metabolic reprogramming emerging as a shared pathological feature. Long-chain acyl-CoA synthetases (ACSLs) activate long-chain fatty acids and direct lipid flux toward β-oxidation, lipid synthesis, and phospholipid remodeling, thereby influencing oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and inflammatory signaling. Unlike previous reviews centered on broad ACSL biology, selected isoforms, or pathway-based ferroptosis mechanisms, this review adopts a disease-spanning, isoform-specific framework. We compare ACSL1, ACSL3, ACSL4, ACSL5, and ACSL6 across cervical, ovarian, and endometrial cancers, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, and preeclampsia. By integrating isoform-specific substrate preference, subcellular localization, and lipid-channeling functions, we examine how individual ACSLs differentially regulate fatty acid oxidation, lipid synthesis and phospholipid remodeling, ferroptosis sensitivity, and inflammatory signaling across reproductive disease contexts. We further distinguish disease-specific experimental evidence from bioinformatic associations and mechanistic extrapolations from other disease models. Current evidence most consistently supports a disease-relevant role for ACSL4 in ferroptosis regulation, whereas ACSL1, ACSL3, ACSL5, and ACSL6 show greater context dependence. This integrated framework identifies shared metabolic mechanisms, disease-specific differences, and priorities for cell-resolved validation and future isoform-selective therapeutic development.

articles.title: The developmental, genetic, and epigenetic basis of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.authors: Mahdi A, Qannan A, El Hajj N
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the most common reproductive and endocrine disorder affecting women in their reproductive age. PCOS is characterized by clustering of reproductive disturbances, including, but not limited to, hypothalamus-pituitary-ovarian axis dysfunction, chronic anovulation, excess androgen, and subfertility. PCOS extends beyond reproductive dysfunction to involve metabolic, endocrine, and cardiometabolic abnormalities. Therefore, it has recently been redefined as polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Despite the evolution of diagnostic criteria for PMOS in recent decades, there persists a knowledge gap regarding its origins and pathophysiology. Genetic studies have identified candidate genes associated with PMOS, but genetic factors alone cannot account for its varied phenotypes. The diverse phenotypes observed in PMOS instead point to a complex gene-environment interaction, thereby paving the way for epigenetic mechanisms to explain this heterogeneous trait. Emerging evidence suggests that epigenetic alterations during critical developmental periods, particularly in utero and during puberty, may contribute to the reproductive, metabolic, and endocrine manifestations of PMOS. These observations may re-frame PMOS as a developmental disorder that follows the developmental origin of health and disease (DOHaD) theory. In this review, we propose a comprehensive framework to address the complexity of PMOS pathogenesis and phenotypes. We investigated how environmental exposures during critical windows may shape the epigenome and contribute to PMOS development. The review also examines the biological rationale of the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS, including the use of anti-Müllerian hormone, postponing diagnosis until after puberty, and recommendations for healthy lifestyle behaviors.

articles.title: A processed dietary pattern is associated with gestational diabetes mellitus and altered APOM and SAA4 proteomic signatures in Miao women.
articles.authors: Zhang W, Liu C, Sun Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study integrated dietary pattern analysis with serum proteomics to identify diet-related molecular signatures associated with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in Miao pregnant women.
METHODS: A 1:1 matched case-control study was conducted among 78 Miao pregnant women (39 GDM cases and 39 controls). Dietary patterns were derived using principal component analysis. Serum proteomics was performed using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. Associations were evaluated using conditional logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models. LASSO penalized logistic regression was used for exploratory feature selection, followed by nested cross-validation to assess internal discriminative performance and an exploratory multivariable analysis.
RESULTS: Higher adherence to a processed dietary pattern was associated with higher odds of GDM (OR = 2.33, 95% CI: 1.08-5.04). Proteomic analysis identified 34 candidate differentially expressed proteins enriched in lipid metabolism and inflammatory pathways. The processed dietary pattern was inversely associated with APOM (β = -0.308, p = 0.036) and showed a borderline inverse association with SAA4 (β = -0.285, p = 0.052). A leave-one-matched-pair-out nested LASSO feature-selection analysis using all 344 quality-controlled proteins yielded an internal AUC of 0.953 (95% CI: 0.894-0.992). SAA4 was selected in all 39 outer iterations, whereas selection frequencies varied across other proteins. APOM was retained for subsequent exploratory integrative analysis based primarily on its association with the processed dietary pattern, PPI-hub status, and biological relevance.
CONCLUSION: A processed dietary pattern was associated with GDM and altered circulating APOM/SAA4 profiles in Miao pregnant women. Nested cross-validation provided an exploratory assessment of proteomic feature stability using all 344 quality-controlled proteins. The resulting internal discrimination should be interpreted cautiously because the upstream QC correction/normalization incorporated GDM group information and was completed before cross-validation. The APOM/SAA4-diet model was developed as a proof-of-concept analysis only and should not be interpreted as a clinically applicable prediction model. Larger independent and prospective cohorts are required for external validation.

articles.title: Advances in platinum-based drug development for cervical cancer therapy.
articles.authors: Shao D, Gao P, Wang Q et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a predominant malignancy of the female reproductive system and a critical global health challenge. Traditional platinum-based agents such as cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin, are cornerstones in postoperative adjuvant therapy, management of locally advanced cases, and systemic treatment of recurrent/metastatic disease. However, their clinical efficacy is frequently hampered by severe systemic toxicities and the emergence of chemoresistance. To address these bottlenecks, diverse nano-delivery platforms have been engineered to enhance bioavailability and mitigate adverse effects. This review systematically delineates the evolution of first-to third-generation platinum drugs, elucidating their molecular mechanisms of action specifically within the landscape of cervical cancer. Furthermore, we critically evaluate the clinical application of these agents and provide a comprehensive synthesis of recent advances in nano-delivery systems, including targeted and stimuli-responsive carriers. By bridging traditional pharmacology with cutting-edge nanotechnology, this review offers strategic insights into achieving precise delivery and controlled release, potentially defining new paradigms for the next-generation of cervical cancer therapeutics.

articles.title: High prevalence of adverse drug reactions among oral contraceptive pill users in Western India: a prospective observational study.
articles.authors: Dhakne AN, Rajopadhye B, Londhe VA et al.
articles.abstract: Oral contraceptive (OC) pills are among the most widely prescribed hormonal preparations globally, yet prospective adverse drug reaction (ADR) surveillance data from the Indian subcontinent remain sparse. This prospective observational study aimed to estimate the prevalence, spectrum, and temporal pattern of ADRs among OC pill users at a tertiary care gynecology outpatient department and affiliated private clinics in Pune, Western India. A total of 201 women aged 18-60 years prescribed OC pills for contraceptive or non-contraceptive indications were enrolled; 130 were new initiators and 71 were existing users. Participants were followed for 3 months, with ADRs documented at three pre-specified time points anchored to the date of OC pill initiation. Of 201 participants, 179 (89.05%; 95% Wilson confidence interval: 83.98%-92.66%) experienced at least one ADR, with a mean of 1.87 ± 1.06 ADRs per participant. Nausea was the most frequently reported ADR (62.69%), followed by weight gain (25.87%), breast pain (24.88%), vomiting (22.39%), and headache (19.90%). A notable 87.06% of participants used OC pills for non-contraceptive therapeutic purposes, with polycystic ovary syndrome as the predominant indication (36.82%). Among new initiators, a distinct biphasic temporal pattern was observed: early-onset gastrointestinal ADRs-particularly nausea and vomiting-resolved completely by the third month, while weight gain emerged as a persistent late-onset effect. On multivariable analysis, reported weight gain was independently associated with baseline overweight/obese status rather than with polycystic ovary syndrome or OC pill formulation. Serious ADRs were rare, with no thromboembolic events recorded. These findings demonstrate a high ADR burden among OC pill users in an Indian clinical setting, predominantly driven by transient gastrointestinal symptoms, and highlight the importance of anticipatory counseling on the biphasic ADR trajectory, and prospective pharmacovigilance in guiding individualized prescribing.

articles.title: Lower Uterine Segment Compression Sutures for Hemorrhage During Cesarean Delivery in Women With Placenta Previa: A Systematic Review of Hemostatic Success and Uterine Preservation.
articles.authors: Marfani J
articles.abstract: Bleeding from the lower uterine segment is difficult to control during cesarean delivery for placenta previa, and conventional compression sutures were designed mainly for uterine atony. We systematically reviewed comparative studies of lower uterine segment compression sutures, focusing on hemostatic success and uterine preservation. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched through 12 September 2026. Original comparative studies from the last five years that included women with placenta previa undergoing cesarean delivery were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed with the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Because techniques and comparators differed, results were synthesized narratively without pooling. Of 183 records identified, four retrospective comparative cohorts (91-346 women) were included. In the two studies reporting mean blood loss, suture groups lost less blood than comparators (2152.6 versus 2960.5 mL; 792.5 versus 1220.8 mL). Operative times were shorter, and fewer additional procedures were needed. Hysterectomy was infrequent: none occurred with double-row transfixion versus two with aortic balloon plus sutures. Two studies had a low overall risk of bias and two a serious risk. Lower uterine segment sutures appear to be a useful, low-cost hemostatic option in placenta previa, but the evidence is limited to four retrospective cohorts. Prospective comparative studies with standardized outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Parental determinants of blastocyst euploidy in a predominantly recurrent-pregnancy-loss PGT-A cohort: limited predictive value of female age, BMI, AMH and sperm DNA fragmentation.
articles.authors: Tan C, Wang X, Tong D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Embryonic aneuploidy is a major factor affecting clinical outcomes in assisted reproduction. PGT-A improves embryo selection, but the clinical factors associated with euploidy remain debated.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 588 PGT‑A cycles. We used embryo‑level GLMMs to evaluate the associations of female age, female BMI, AMH, male age, male BMI, and sperm DFI with embryo euploidy. We performed univariable and multivariable analyses, assessed model performance (AUC, R2, calibration), and conducted internal validation via patient-clustered bootstrap (200 replicates). Subgroup analyses by female age were performed with FDR correction.
RESULTS: Among 2,357 blastocysts, 1,299 (55.1%) were euploid. In univariable analysis, female age, male age, and male DFI were significantly associated with euploidy. After multivariable adjustment, only female age (OR = 0.87, p = 0.011) and male DFI (OR = 0.89, p = 0.006) remained independent predictors. Model performance was poor (apparent AUC = 0.571; bootstrap-corrected AUC = 0.574; apparent marginal R2 = 0.018 and conditional R2 = 0.036; apparent calibration slope = 0.985; bootstrap-corrected calibration slope = 0.913), indicating weak signal strength and limited generalizability. Subgroup analyses showed some nominal associations, but none survived FDR correction (all q > 0.05). Among 588 cycles with complete covariate data, 90.3% had at least one euploid blastocyst; among all 613 biopsied cycles and 637 started cycles, the rates were 89.89% and 86.50%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Female age and male DFI were independently associated with euploidy, but the model's discrimination remained poor after optimism correction (bootstrap-corrected AUC = 0.574; apparent calibration slope = 0.985, bootstrap-corrected calibration slope = 0.913), and these variables therefore lack sufficient value for clinical use. Subgroup analyses by female age were exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and no statistically significant age-modified association between male DFI and euploid embryos persisted after FDR correction. Future models incorporating embryo-specific data and larger samples are needed.

articles.title: Trigger-day progesterone-to-mature-oocyte ratio, cycle-level blastocyst yield, and recorded embryo-transfer outcomes: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wei Y, Xu Y, Wei N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The progesterone-to-metaphase II oocyte ratio (P/MII) combines trigger-day progesterone with mature oocyte count after retrieval. Its associations may reflect ovarian response and embryo allocation.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 7,778 in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (IVF/ICSI) cycle records. Existing pregnancy analyses used 4,273 positive-transfer records. A linked clinical and laboratory source export enabled post hoc analyses using recorded extended culture counts, retrieval order, transfer dates, thawing records, and source-identifier grouping.
RESULTS: The original high-versus-low P/MII rate ratio for blastocysts per recorded 2PN zygote was 0.796 (95% CI 0.762-0.831). Among the same 5,821 culture-positive records, the adjusted rate ratio was 0.934 (0.902-0.968) with a 2PN denominator and 0.974 (0.945-1.005; P = 0.101) with the recorded culture denominator. The continuous culture-count association remained small (aRR 0.993 per 0.01, 0.989-0.997). The source recorded 6,148 first and 1,630 later retrievals. In 3,526 first-retrieval, date-consistent records without thawing evidence, the ratio term after inclusion of progesterone and MII was associated with clinical pregnancy flags (aOR 0.952, 0.919-0.986; P = 0.006) but was uncertain for live birth flags (0.968, 0.935-1.002; P = 0.067). Source-identifier-grouped live birth areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.623 with the components, 0.623 with P/MII, and 0.624 with all three.
CONCLUSIONS: Recorded associations depended on the culture population, denominator, and outcome. Incremental clinical usefulness was not established. These data do not support a physiological ratio mechanism or a clinical cutoff for trigger-day or freeze-all decisions.

articles.title: A cross-sectional study of routine hematological and biochemical parameters with age- and sex-specific analyses in mid-to-high-altitude regions of southwestern China.
articles.authors: Li J, Ji Y, Zhuang S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete blood count (CBC) and biochemical parameters (liver function, renal function, Blood glucose, and lipid profile) are the most routinely used tests in clinical laboratory practice, and serve as critical evidence for disease diagnosis. This study aimed to characterize the distribution patterns of age- and sex-related differences in CBC and biochemical indicators, identify the age-related inflection points of these indicators, and analyze their correlation patterns across different sexes and age groups.
METHODS: A total of 83,945 individuals physical examination in mid-to-high-altitude areas of Yuxi City, southwestern China (1,500-1,800 m above sea level), were enrolled in this study. All subjects were stratified into seven age groups by sex. Age trend inflection plots, correlation analysis, and mediation models were applied to explore indicator trajectories, inter-association patterns, and the mediating role of triglyceride (TG) in the age-uric acid (UA) relationship.
RESULTS: After FDR correction, most hematological and biochemical parameters remained statistically significant in sex comparisons within each age group. For indicators with an absolute relative median difference |RMD| > 10%, total bilirubin (TBIL), direct bilirubin (DBIL), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), creatinine (CREA), and uric acid (UA) consistently exhibited clinically meaningful sex differences across all age groups. Most included CBC and biochemical indicators included in this study showed generally synchronous age trend in both male and female populations, the age inflection points were also generally concordant between sexes. However, four indicators alkaline phosphatase (ALP), globulin (GLB), triglyceride (TG), and uric acid (UA) showed pronounced sexual dimorphism in their age-dependent trajectories. The CBC indicators showed that the levels of red blood cell count (RBC), hemoglobin (Hb), and hematocrit (HCT) were higher in males from 18-25 to 56-65 years, but females surpassed males by the 66-75 years group. Sex-stratified correlation analysis revealed that in young males (18-25 years), lipid metabolism indicators had the strongest correlations with liver enzymes and liver enzyme ratios, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.31 to 0.39; these correlations gradually attenuated with advancing age. In females, only transient moderate correlations of UA with TG and VLDL emerged during the perimenopausal period (36-45 years). After Bonferroni correction, all…

articles.title: Perceptions of overactive bladder treatments among women, caregivers, and healthcare professionals: a systematic review and meta-synthesis.
articles.authors: Roman MP, Mihu D, Rus D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a common condition that substantially impairs quality of life yet remains underreported and undertreated. Understanding how women, caregivers, and healthcare professionals (HCPs) perceive OAB treatments may help improve patient-centered care. This systematic review and meta-synthesis aims to synthesize qualitative evidence on experiences and perceptions of OAB treatment.
METHODS: MEDLINE, Scopus, Google Scholar and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 2026 for qualitative studies exploring treatment experiences among women with OAB, their caregivers, and HCPs. Three reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and performed line-by-line coding. Data were synthesized using thematic synthesis. Methodological quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) checklist. A GRADE-CERQual assessment was performed to evaluate confidence in the synthesized qualitative findings.
RESULTS: Thirteen qualitative studies were included. Forty-five codes were identified and synthesized into five analytical themes: (1) the burden of treatment vs. the burden of illness, reflecting the tension between symptom burden and treatment-related challenges; (2) erosion of trust in the therapeutic alliance, driven by poor communication and unmet expectations; (3) the knowledge gap and desire for agency, highlighting unmet informational needs and preferences for shared decision-making; (4) psychosocial barriers to treatment engagement, encompassing stigma, embarrassment, isolation, and emotional distress; and (5) preference for low-burden treatments and resistance to behavioural change, reflecting preferences for convenient therapies and difficulties sustaining long-term behavioural interventions.
CONCLUSIONS: Experiences of OAB treatment extend beyond symptom control and are shaped by psychosocial burden, healthcare interactions, treatment expectations, and the need for autonomy. Patient-centered communication, shared decision-making, and individualized support may improve treatment engagement, satisfaction, and adherence.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261289760, Identifier: CRD420261289760.

articles.title: Childhood trauma and PMOS-related quality of life: perceived stress statistically accounts for part of the association.
articles.authors: Santantonio MMM, Preiss M, Levcik D
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is among the most prevalent endocrine disorders, and it is associated with substantial impairment in quality of life. Emerging evidence suggests that childhood trauma and stress-related processes may contribute to psychological burden in women with PMOS, but these links are poorly understood. The present study examines the relationship between childhood trauma, perceived stress, and PMOS-related quality of life.
METHODS: In a cross-sectional online survey, 206 adult women reporting a prior PMOS diagnosis completed three validated questionnaires: the Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Quality of Life Questionnaire (PCOSQ), the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), and the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form (CTQ-SF).
RESULTS: The results indicate significant correlations: higher levels of childhood trauma are associated with poorer PMOS-related quality of life (ρ = -0.38, ρ < 0.001) and increased perceived stress (ρ = 0.40, ρ < 0.001). Regression analyses showed that higher perceived stress was significantly associated with lower PCOSQ scores (βs = -0.54, p < 0.001). Additionally, an indirect-association analysis showed that perceived stress statistically accounted for part of the association between childhood trauma and PMOS-related quality of life (β = -0.18, ρ < 0.001).
DISCUSSION: Women with greater trauma histories reported higher perceived stress, and higher perceived stress was associated with poorer quality of life. These findings support further prospective and intervention research examining whether assessment of trauma history and perceived stress may help identify women at greater risk of poorer PMOS-related quality of life and whether trauma-informed approaches can improve psychosocial outcomes.

articles.title: Differential DNA methylation profiling of spermatogenesis-associated genes in patients with idiopathic hypospermatogenesis: a hospital-based case-control study.
articles.authors: Sharma N, Singh S, Kumar V et al.
articles.abstract: Hypospermatogenesis is a histopathological subtype of non-obstructive azoospermia and is characterized by a decrease in the total number of germ cells within the seminiferous tubule as a result of spermatogenic failure. Germ cell epigenetic reprograming during development shows that the methylation status of testicular DNA is highly distinct in which hypomethylated foci predominates. A unique testicular DNA methylation pattern needs to be established for various clinical and histopathological subtypes of azoospermia, in order to delineate the epigenetic factors associated with the condition. This study aim to explore the differential methylation profile in idiopathic hypospermatogenesis patients using methylation microarray technique from testicular tissue DNA. A comprehensive clinical history, blood sample, semen analysis parameters, and reproductive endocrine evaluation reports of 51 hypospermatogenesis patients were collected. The known genetic causes were investigated for exclusion using XY fluorescent in-situ hybridization and Yq microdeletion techniques. DNA methylation microarray was performed, on 40 idiopathic hypospermatogenesis and 10 normospermatogenesis patient to identify differential DNA methylation patterns in spermatogenesis associated genes. A genome-wide differential DNA methylation profiling of 40 hypospermatogenesis patients identified 1,666 differentially methylated regions localised predominantly at promotor regions. A significant proportion (70%) of these differentially methylated genomic regions exhibited hypermethylation, suggesting widespread transcriptional repression of spermatogenesis-associated genes. The transcription factor protein-protein interaction analysis identified six clusters viz., TBP, AR, SP3, TP53, CCNT2 and SIN3A, indicating their potential role in the epigenetic mechanisms of the clinical condition of male infertility. Differential methylation burden analysis showed 4/29 high burden and 5/29 intermediated burden patients. Functional enrichment analysis of promoter-associated differentially methylated spermatogenic genes were found implicated in crucial molecular functions including RNA binding, DNA binding, transcription regulation, and spermatid differentiation. The findings suggest that male infertility may, in part, be driven by the silencing of genes that are not just transcriptionally active, but that also act as nodal regulators in transcription factor complexes essential for germ cell viability, hormone…

articles.title: Clinical and sonographic characteristics of gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma: a descriptive case series of 13 patients.
articles.authors: Li T, Jiang M, Luo Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma (G-EAC) is a distinct human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent subtype of cervical adenocarcinoma for which early diagnosis continues to pose a clinical challenge. We set out to characterize the clinical and sonographic features of G-EAC and to provide hypothesis-generating observations to guide future research.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis comprised 13 patients with histopathologically confirmed G-EAC who underwent surgery at our center between August 2017 and September 2024. We reviewed and descriptively summarized the clinical presentation, HPV and cytology results, cervical biopsy findings, tumor markers, and ultrasonographic and cross-sectional imaging findings, together with all available pathological and surgical records.
RESULTS: The patients were aged 39-76 years (mean, 53.4 years), and all were parous. Vaginal discharge was the most common presenting symptom (8/13, 61.5%), followed by irregular vaginal bleeding (4/13, 30.8%) and postcoital bleeding (1/13, 7.7%). HPV testing was negative in 11/13 patients (84.6%); 1/13 (7.7%) tested positive for HPV 58, and another 1/13 (7.7%) carried a different high-risk HPV type. ThinPrep cytologic testing (TCT) was negative in 12/13 patients (92.3%), whereas atypical squamous cells were detected in 1/13 (7.7%). Among the 11 patients who underwent colposcopy with cervical biopsy, histopathological findings were negative in 8/11 (72.7%), mild glandular atypia was identified in 2/11 (18.2%), and rare adenocarcinoma cells were identified in 1/11 (9.1%). All 13 patients underwent preoperative ultrasound. Ultrasound findings raised suspicion of cervical malignancy in 9/13 patients (69.2%), were suggestive of benign cervical cystic lesions in 2/13 (15.4%), and were unremarkable in the remaining 2/13 (15.4%). A honeycomb sonographic pattern was present in 7/13 patients (53.8%), and abundant intralesional vascularity (Adler grade III) was present in 9/13 patients (69.2%). Preoperative MRI was performed in 10/13 patients (76.9%), 1 of whom also underwent CT, whereas the remaining 3/13 patients (23.1%) underwent neither MRI nor CT. A barrel-shaped cervix was documented in the pathological or surgical records of 4/13 patients (30.8%).
CONCLUSION: G-EAC may come to attention through a combination of clinical and imaging findings that together raise diagnostic suspicion. In this series, HPV negativity was common, and vaginal discharge was the most frequent…

articles.title: Sexually transmitted co-infections as biological modifiers of HPV-driven cervical carcinogenesis: a systematic integrative review.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Alqassim E, Al-Qahtani AA, Alqassim AY et al.
articles.abstract: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is necessary but not sufficient for cervical cancer, which caused approximately 350,000 deaths in 2022. Co-infections with Chlamydia trachomatis (CT), herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2), and HIV may modify cervical carcinogenesis, but causal inference is constrained by confounding, study heterogeneity, and limited mechanistic validation in human tissue. This systematic integrative review (PRISMA 2020) searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library (January 2015 to March 2026); risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. HIV co-infection shows the strongest evidence: approximately 6-fold risk elevation, a confirmed CD4 dose-response, and residual risk that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (GRADE: high). CT is associated with 2-4-fold elevations in observational studies, but substantial heterogeneity, residual sexual-behavior confounding, funnel-plot asymmetry suggesting publication bias, and attenuation of the HPV-adjusted independent effect (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.03-3.01) leave causality uncertain (GRADE: Low-Moderate). HSV-2 associations are inconsistent: pooled cervical cancer risk was elevated (OR 3.01, 95% CI 2.24-4.04), but most estimates were unadjusted for HPV status, prospective studies are non-significant, and mechanistic evidence derives from non-human models (GRADE: low). A context-dependent syndemic effect appears in HIV co-infected populations. In conclusion, HIV meets criteria for a probable causal modifier of HPV-driven carcinogenesis, supporting WHO-endorsed intensified screening for women living with HIV; CT's role remains uncertain pending rigorous confounder control; and HSV-2 does not meet the threshold for independent co-factor classification. Priorities include prospective cohorts and human cervical-tissue mechanistic validation.

articles.title: Maternal age-related thyroid changes during pregnancy: implications for isolated hypothyroxinemia patterns.
articles.authors: Wang S, Zhang Y, Zhu A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations between maternal age and thyroid function in early and late pregnancy, as well as their changes, with a focus on the impact of age on the longitudinal patterns of isolated hypothyroxinemia.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 43,545 women with singleton pregnancies. Serum free thyroxine (FT4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels were measured in early and late pregnancy, along with their changes. Linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), and piecewise linear regression were used to assess non-linear associations and threshold effects. Isolated hypothyroxinemia was categorized into euthyroid, transient, and persistent patterns. Ordinal logistic regression was used to examine the association between maternal age and these patterns, as well as the relationships between the patterns and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preeclampsia, preterm birth, macrosomia, and low birth weight (LBW).
RESULTS: Maternal age showed significantly stronger negative associations with FT4 levels and their changes than with TSH. Maternal age was positively associated with the risk of isolated hypothyroxinemia in a dose-response manner. Compared with women aged 18-24 years, those aged 35-39 years (OR = 1.89) and 40-49 years (OR = 3.01) had higher risks of persistent isolated hypothyroxinemia. Risks of preeclampsia, macrosomia, and LBW increased progressively from transient to persistent patterns (all P for trend <0.01).
CONCLUSION: Maternal age is an important factor influencing FT4 during pregnancy. Increasing age is associated with a higher likelihood of persistent isolated hypothyroxinemia, which is linked to a broader range of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: How law legitimized and later recharacterized forced sterilization in Peru: the juridical laundering of biopower.
articles.authors: Aguirre-Lanegra AJ, García Enríquez JR
articles.abstract: Between 1996 and 2000, a Peruvian family planning program sterilized hundreds of thousands of people, most of them poor, rural and Indigenous women, many without free consent. The program operated under the cover of a law, a ministerial resolution, numerical sterilization targets and signed consent forms. Since 1997, Peruvian prosecutors and courts, Congress and international human rights bodies have classified the same facts in contradictory ways, for example as an accident, as ordinary crimes barred by time limits, as a lawful health program and as serious human rights violations. This raises a question for the sociology of law: how do legal documents make state control over reproduction look legitimate, and how do they shape later disputes over it? Existing research explains either how such policies were legitimized or how they were contested, but not the link between the two. To connect them, this article proposes the juridical laundering of biopower, a category with two phases. Biopower here means the state's power over a population's life and reproduction. First, legal documents present the state's intervention as lawful, technical and, when framed as voluntary, consented to. Later, prosecutors, courts and other institutions place the same facts in different legal categories, and the category that prevails determines whether anyone can be held responsible. We test four propositions against the program's documents and 34 decisions and other official acts issued between 1997 and 2026. The evidence supports three of them: the program's own documents later served as grounds for not prosecuting its architects, the facts were classified in contradictory ways, and none of its architects was convicted. It is consistent with the fourth, on the conditions for accountability. Classifying the facts as human rights violations led to accountability only when domestic and international institutions agreed on that classification, when a binding court decision enforced it, and when time limits did not bar prosecution. The Peruvian case thus shows how a policy that the State presented as lawful can end in a finding that the State itself violated human rights, while no official is held criminally responsible. We call this outcome deferred impunity.

articles.title: Nonlinear associations of bone age and basal luteinizing hormone with uterine volume in girls with central precocious puberty: a segmented regression analysis.
articles.authors: Yuan X, Cai C, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationships between basal luteinizing hormone (LH), bone age (BA), and uterine volume in girls with precocious puberty are conventionally treated as linear in clinical practice. Whether these associations exhibit nonlinear, threshold-dependent patterns has not been formally investigated.
