METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 1, 617 girls with breast development before 8 years of age, of whom 1, 008 had central precocious puberty (CPP) and 609 had premature thelarche (PT). Restricted cubic spline regression was used to test for nonlinearity in the associations of BA and ln-transformed basal LH with ln-transformed uterine volume. Where nonlinearity was confirmed, piecewise linear regression identified breakpoints at which uterine growth accelerated. CPP girls were then cross-classified by the identified thresholds to evaluate their complementary value.
RESULTS: CPP girls had significantly greater BA advancement than PT girls (1.87 ± 1.11 vs. 1.58 ± 1.02 years, P < 0.001). In CPP girls, both BA and basal LH exhibited significant nonlinear associations with uterine volume (both P < 0.0001). A BA breakpoint was identified at 10.6 years: below this threshold, each additional year was associated with a 0.067-unit increase in ln(uterine volume); above 10.6 years, the slope increased to 0.550 (8.2-fold acceleration, P < 0.001). A basal LH breakpoint was identified at 0.67 IU/L, below which the slope was 0.107 per ln-unit and above which it rose to 0.421 (3.9-fold acceleration, P < 0.001). In PT girls, no clinically meaningful breakpoints were found. When CPP girls were stratified by both thresholds, the "Both High" subgroup (16.5%) had a median uterine volume of 2.76 mL (47.6% exceeding 3.0 mL), compared with 1.22 mL (1.4%) in the "Both Low" subgroup (58.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: The associations of BA and basal LH with uterine volume in CPP are distinctly nonlinear, with identifiable thresholds beyond which uterine growth accelerates substantially. These breakpoints are proposed as quantitative descriptors of uterine maturation tempo rather than as diagnostic cutoffs; they have high specificity but limited sensitivity, and girls with values below the thresholds require clinical follow-up. These two indicators provide complementary information for characterizing the tempo of uterine maturation.

articles.title: Testosterone-Modulating Medicinal Plants Used in the Management of Male Infertility in Uganda: A Mechanistic and Evidence-Based Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Ikuomola EO, Shehu UU, Adeniyi IA et al.
articles.abstract: Male infertility contributes to approximately 40-50% of infertility cases worldwide and poses a substantial public health challenge, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa. In Uganda, where access to conventional fertility treatments remains limited by cost and availability, traditional medicinal plants are widely used as a therapeutic option for managing male reproductive disorders. However, the scientific evidence supporting their efficacy and mechanisms of action remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on medicinal plants used in Uganda for the management of male infertility, with particular emphasis on their testosterone-modulating mechanisms and the strength of available evidence. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar to identify studies evaluating medicinal plants used in Uganda and the broader East African region. The review identified 171 medicinal plant species traditionally used for sexual and reproductive health across the East African Community, of which 66 are documented in Uganda. Frequently cited Ugandan-native species include Mondia whitei and Warburgia ugandensis; Withania somnifera is included as a comparative benchmark. Available preclinical evidence suggests that some of these plants may enhance testosterone production through stimulation of Leydig cell steroidogenesis, modulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, antioxidant activity, and other phytochemical-mediated mechanisms. Although these findings suggest potential therapeutic avenues, the clinical evidence base remains extremely limited, with no randomized controlled trials for Ugandan-native medicinal plants, and current evidence is insufficient to recommend these plants for clinical use outside of research settings. Future well-designed clinical and pharmacological studies are essential to validate efficacy, establish safety, and facilitate integration into evidence-based reproductive healthcare.

articles.title: Sequential ejaculated- and testicular-sperm ICSI cycles in couples with prior ICSI failure: a within-pair analysis of embryo quality, euploidy, and live birth.
articles.authors: Yücetürk A, Peker N, Tığlı E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Persistent poor outcomes after intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) occur in a clinically significant subset of couples despite reassuring conventional semen analysis. In such couples, testicular sperm aspiration (TESA) may be undertaken in a subsequent cycle on clinical and embryological grounds. We assessed whether TESA-ICSI improves embryo-quality indicators and live birth rates compared with EJAC-ICSI in couples whose initial EJAC-ICSI cycle did not result in a live birth.
METHODS: This retrospective paired cohort study included 58 sequential ICSI cycle pairs at a single tertiary IVF center. Each pair comprised an initial ICSI cycle with ejaculated sperm (EJAC-ICSI) that had not resulted in a live birth, followed by a subsequent TESA-ICSI cycle in the same couple; the cycle pair was the unit of analysis. The primary outcome was live birth rate per cycle; secondary outcomes included fertilization, blastulation, Grade A blastocyst formation, PGT-A, clinical pregnancy, miscarriage, and live birth per embryo transfer. Paired comparisons used McNemar exact and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
RESULTS: Total oocyte, mature oocyte, 2PN, and blastocyst counts were similar between paired cycles (all p > 0.05), while the fertilization rate was lower in TESA-ICSI cycles at the oocyte level (71.3% vs. 79.7%; p = 0.001). By contrast, the blastulation rate per 2PN was higher in TESA-ICSI cycles (p = 0.008), as was the Grade A blastocyst rate both at the per-embryo level (EJAC: 2.4% vs. TESA: 8.9%; p = 0.0006) and at the per-patient level (p = 0.0032). PGT-A euploidy increased from 27.9% to 65.0% (p = 0.0009), the clinical pregnancy rate from 6.9% to 31.0% (p = 0.0026), and the live birth rate from 0% to 29.3% (absolute risk difference 29.3%; number needed to treat 3.4) (p = 1.5 × 10-5), while the miscarriage rate per clinical pregnancy fell from 4/4 to 1/18 (p = 0.0007).
CONCLUSIONS: In couples whose prior EJAC-ICSI cycle had not resulted in a live birth, a subsequent TESA-ICSI cycle in the same couple was associated with significant improvements in embryo quality, euploidy, and live birth without change in embryo numbers. These findings support TESA-ICSI as a reasonable therapeutic option in this clinical scenario.

articles.title: Associations between age at first calving, productivity, survival, and economic performance in US Holsteins.
articles.authors: Overton MW
articles.abstract: Age at first calving (AFC) influences raising costs, future milk production, cow survivability, and herd profitability. This retrospective observational study examined associations between AFC and productivity, survival, and economic performance through 305 d of the second lactation in US Holstein dairy cows. Data from 74 US dairies included 128,252 Holstein cows born from January 2020 to June 2021 with AFC of 21 to 27 mo. Production outcomes included projected 305-d milk in first lactation (P305M), cumulative milk through 305 d of first lactation (CUML1), and cumulative milk through 305 d of second lactation (CUML1&2). Replacement risk, stillbirth risk, and cumulative DIM were also assessed. Linear mixed models (with herd and mo-yr of birth as random effects) and multivariable logistic regression were used. Although P305M was highest at 26 mo AFC, both CUML1 and CUML1&2 were maximized at 23 mo, driven partly by lower removal risks in younger-calving cohorts. First-lactation replacement risk increased progressively from 17% (21 mo AFC) to 35% (27 mo AFC). An integrated economic model incorporating milk revenue, calf value, feed, replacement, and raising costs showed comparable net income among 21- to 23-mo AFC cohorts, with a progressive decline beginning at 24 mo. Despite potential first-lactation production advantages for older-calving heifers, delaying first calving beyond 23 mo carries meaningful economic consequences. Results support targeting 22 to 23 mo AFC in US Holstein herds, provided adequate growth and BW at first calving are achieved.

articles.title: Association of mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities with embryo transfer success.
articles.authors: Waymire A, Niesen AM, Rossow HA
articles.abstract: Mitochondria produce energy vital for health, reproduction, and metabolism and contain their own DNA, which is inherited exclusively from the dam. The objective of this study was to assess the association of mitochondrial enzyme activities of Complex I (C-I), Complex IV (C-IV), and Complex V (C-V) with pregnancy outcome and other physiological and management factors influencing reproductive efficiency. Forty Holstein recipients were assigned either embryo A (Donor 1/Sire 1, n = 20) or embryo B (Donor 2/Sire 2, n = 20) based on donor embryo production and recipient availability. Crude mitochondrial extracts were isolated from peripheral blood mononuclear cells and analyzed for mitochondrial enzyme activities of C-I, C-IV, and C-V. Pregnancy outcome was checked at ∼32 d carried calf, confirmed at 45 and 90 d carried calf, and by live calf birth. Mitochondrial enzyme activities were regressed on management, genomic, embryo source, and pregnancy outcome and confirmed through birth. Performance data were collected from the herd management software DairyComp 305 (VAS, Tulare, CA), and hematological variables were measured at the time of embryo transfer. The mitochondrial enzyme activity of C-I was associated with C-IV, C-V, and mean corpuscular hemoglobin. Complex IV was associated with C-I, C-V, and platelets, and C-V was associated with C-I, C-IV, lymphocyte number, and genomic Dairy Wellness Profit Dollars (Zoetis). Embryo source also tended to influence C-I and C-IV activities. This effect was replaced with genomic daughter pregnancy rate when embryo was not included in the regressions. Associations between C-I and C-IV reflect their joint role in creating the proton gradient in the electron transport chain and relationship with oxygen supply and immune function. Mitochondrial enzyme activities were shaped by genetic and physiological factors but, in this study, were not a definitive marker for reproductive success of recipients via embryo transfer. But further examination of the relationship between mitochondrial function and nuclear-encoded genes to find markers of success of pregnancy via embryo transfer is warranted.

articles.title: Transplantation in the rat of enzymatically and genipin-modified decellularized uterine tissue after mesenchymal stem cell recellularization; a proof-of-concept study.
articles.authors: Bandstein S, Sehic E, De Miguel-Gómez L et al.
articles.abstract: Uterus transplantation can restore fertility in women with uterine factor infertility, but donor shortage, surgical complexity, and immunosuppression limit its wider use. Bioengineered uterine grafts may offer an alternative, yet animal studies have shown that large decellularized uterine scaffolds often lack sufficient mechanical durability and may not support complete tissue regeneration. This study used the rat model to investigate whether enzyme-treated genipin-crosslinked decellularized uterine patches could support long-term repair after full-thickness uterine wall injury. The patches were transplanted either alone or after mesenchymal stem cell recellularization, with particular focus on identifying the molecular profile during tissue remodeling and regeneration one and four months after transplantation. Methods included histology, collagen quantification, immunohistochemistry, biocompatibility testing, and digital droplet polymerase chain reaction analysis of genes linked to uterine identity, angiogenesis, proliferation, extracellular matrix turnover, fibrosis, and immune response. Genipin treatment increased scaffold stiffness and improved surgical handling without impairing scaffold biocompatibility or recellularization. Regeneration improved over time in recellularized grafts, but glandular regeneration remained absent and cellularity was sparse in parts of the graft. Gene expression indicated a continued remodeling state rather than mature uterine restoration. Reduced epithelial cadherin expression, increased mesenchymal vimentin expression, persistent transforming growth factor beta upregulation, and elevated proliferation and matrix-remodeling markers suggested an ongoing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition repair process that may explain the incomplete epithelial and glandular regeneration. Immune-related gene expression further suggested that recellularized grafts showed signs of improved immune resolution. These findings suggest that genipin-crosslinked uterine scaffolds provide a robust structural platform for large uterine wall repair, but functional regeneration may be limited by a delayed epithelial maturation. By identifying the incomplete mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition and the glandular lineage commitment as key barriers, this study defines actionable targets for the next generation of bioengineered uterine grafts.

articles.title: Maternal mean arterial pressure and serum inhibin A as early predictors of hypertensive disorders in low-risk pregnant women attending a University Teaching Hospital in Lagos, Nigeria: A prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Kuku OJ, Okunade KS, Olorunfemi G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the role of maternal mean arterial pressure (MAP) and serum inhibin-A level as early predictors of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) among low-risk pregnant women attending a University Teaching Hospital in Lagos, Nigeria.
METHODS: This was a prospective cohort study of 254 consecutively consenting, low-risk, normotensive, and non-proteinuric pregnant women at 13-19 weeks of gestation. Receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curves and validity tests were used to determine the performance of serum levels of inhibin A, MAP, and a combination of both in predicting HDP (gestational hypertension and preeclampsia).
RESULTS: The mean age and parity of the participants was 30.3 ± 4.9 years and 1 (0-2), respectively. The area under the ROC curves of serum inhibin A (0.9981, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.9946-1.000) was higher than for MAP (0.7531, 95% CI 0.6641-0.8421), in predicting the composite endpoint of HDP. The optimum cut-offs for predicting HDP as calculated from Youden's index were 476.8 pg/mL (sensitivity = 100% and specificity = 98.7%) for serum inhibin A and 81.3 mm Hg (sensitivity = 100% and specificity = 50.1%) for MAP. There was no statistically significant difference between the combined predictive ability of inhibin A and MAP compared to that of serum inhibin A alone for predicting HDP (AUC of 0.9984 vs. 09981, P-value = 0.7259.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated that serum inhibin A alone and MAP have good and moderate performance, respectively, in predicting HDP in the low-risk cohort of Nigerian pregnant women. The combination of serum inhibin A and MAP has a similar predictive performance as serum inhibin A alone.

articles.title: Detection of Silent Carriers of Spinal Muscular Atrophy: A Survey of Clinical Practice and Recommendations for Screening.
articles.journal: Twin research and human genetics : the official journal of the International Society for Twin Studies
articles.authors: Wood-Chvalkovsky J, Martinez NN, McLean A
articles.abstract: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive disorder with a carrier frequency of approximately 1 in 50, with an estimated 3-9% of carriers being 'silent' (2+0 configuration) and therefore undetectable by standard assays, complicating reproductive genetic counseling and risk assessment. Implementation of Medicare-funded reproductive genetic carrier screening (RGCS; MBS items 73451 and 73452) in Australia in November 2023 has increased the urgency of addressing this diagnostic gap. This study aimed to characterize current practices and perceptions regarding silent SMA carrier detection among genetics professionals in Australia and New Zealand and to identify strategies to improve detection and counseling. A cross-sectional REDCap survey distributed via the Human Genetics Society of Australasia newsletter yielded 62 responses, 95% from Australia and 5% from New Zealand. Genetic counselors comprised 60% of respondents and clinical geneticists 24%. Silent carrier awareness was high (92%), and 53% reported clinical encounters with silent carriers, most commonly identified through family history with affected offspring or through results indicating the presence of high-risk single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with silent carrier status. However, most respondents had counseled fewer than five cases. Management approaches frequently included counseling on residual risk, segregation studies, and prenatal testing. Thematic analysis identified laboratory support limitations, challenging SNP interpretation, counseling complexity, and workforce constraints as major challenges. A model of care was proposed to address these challenges. This study highlights the need for advanced detection methods, workforce education, and development of guidelines for silent carrier management with the increasing uptake and mainstreaming of RGCS.

articles.title: Reconfiguration of clinical training delivery in a family planning and post-abortion care quality assurance programme in Sierra Leone, 2018-2022: a retrospective programme evaluation.
articles.authors: Onunkwor FI, Abiodun OP, Aguolu R
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health programmes often use both centralised courses and embedded clinical training, but longitudinal descriptions of how training arrangements change - and how competency safeguards are maintained - remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To characterise training-delivery configurations and their implementation context across centre, outreach and public-sector strengthening (PSS) channels in Sierra Leone from January 2018 to June 2022.
METHODS: We undertook a retrospective descriptive programme evaluation of the complete 472-event training register (380 clinical training, seven competency-assessed training-of-trainers and 85 non-competency activities), with event-level stratification by period and service-delivery channel. We interpreted register patterns alongside programme supervision reports, PSS strategy and quality-assurance documents. We did not conduct a controlled effectiveness evaluation.
RESULTS: The register contained 286 events in 2018, 52 in 2019, 39 in 2020, 76 in 2021 and 19 in January-June 2022; 209 occurred in outreach, 172 in centres and 91 in PSS. Across 3,817 participant-episodes, 2,571 were recorded in 387 competency-assessed activities; 2,559 had L1-L3 outcomes and 2,013/2,559 (78.7%) attained Level 1. The 2019 workforce-expansion period featured longer residential courses (median 10 days), whereas other periods featured short, service-linked instruction and refreshers. An external 2020 PSS assessment documented quality safeguards and remaining gaps; no pre-implementation QTA baseline was available.
CONCLUSIONS: Training configurations evolved with programme expansion, changing staffing needs and pandemic adaptation rather than a simple linear classroom-to-workplace shift. Competency-based restrictions, supervised practice and a developing government-linked trainer network formed the clinical governance context. Descriptive programme records and external assessment do not isolate the causal effects of training modality.

articles.title: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy and perinatal outcomes in twin pregnancies: a propensity score matching analysis.
articles.authors: Huang Y, Li X, Cao X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) tends to be more severe in twin pregnancies and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. However, data on the specific effects of ICP in twin gestations remain limited. This study aimed to investigate comprehensively the maternal and neonatal consequences of twin pregnancies complicated by ICP.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 3,109 twin pregnancies delivered at Northwest Women's and Children's Hospital in China from January 2018 through December 2022. Pregnancy and delivery data were extracted from the medical records of women with twin pregnancies who delivered at the hospital. Women were allocated into two groups: ICP (n = 244) and non-ICP (n = 2,865). ICP was diagnosed based on the presence of pruritus together with serum total bile acid (TBA) concentrations ≥10μmol/L. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized estimating equations (GEE) were applied to evaluate the associations between ICP and adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: After matching, ICP increased the risk of maternal outcomes, including preterm labor (early preterm birth: OR = 2.87, 95% CI 1.95-4.23; preterm birth: OR = 4.30, 95% CI 2.11-8.77; very preterm birth: OR = 2.97, 95% CI 1.50-5.87) and hypoproteinemia (OR = 2.83, 95% CI 1.12-7.14), as well as adverse neonatal outcomes, including low birth weight (OR = 2.66, 95% CI 1.99-3.55), small vulnerable newborns (OR = 5.30, 95% CI 2.34-12.00), respiratory distress syndrome (OR = 2.43, 95% CI 1.61-3.67), and necrotizing enterocolitis (OR = 5.71, 95% CI 2.34-13.92).
CONCLUSION: Twin pregnancies complicated by ICP were associated with increased risks of adverse perinatal outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, and neonatal morbidity. These findings highlight the importance of heightened clinical awareness and individualized risk assessment in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Concordance of flow cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection with human papillomavirus DNA testing and cervical cytology in a cervical cancer screening cohort.
articles.journal: Journal of pathology and translational medicine
articles.authors: Ngo DQ, Ha TK, Tran MNT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overexpression of viral oncogenes E6 and E7 of high-risk (HR)-human papillomavirus (HPV) plays a key role in the progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and cancer. Detection of E6/E7 mRNA may help distinguish between transient and transforming infections, thus improving cervical cancer screening accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the association of E6/E7 mRNA expression with HR-HPV infection, cervical cytology, and histologically confirmed cervical lesions and to compare its agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology.
METHODS: A total of 526 women undergoing cervical cancer screening between January 2023 and May 2025 were enrolled. E6/E7 mRNA expression was assessed using flow cytometry with the HPV OncoTect 3Dx E6/E7 mRNA assay and compared with HR-HPV DNA testing, cervical cytology, and available histopathologic findings from biopsy specimens.
RESULTS: Among 526 samples, eight (1.5%) tested positive for E6/E7 mRNA, compared to 30 (5.7%) HR-HPV DNA-positive and 17 (3.2%) abnormal cytology results. Median E6/E7 mRNA expression was higher in HR-HPV- positive cases and in cytologically abnormal cases. Almost perfect agreement was observed between E6/E7 mRNA results, HR-HPV DNA testing, and cytology. Histopathologic follow-up was available for nine women with cytological abnormalities ≥low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, including four CIN2 and five CIN1 cases. E6/E7 mRNA expression was markedly elevated in one CIN2 case associated with HPV16 infection (37.51%), while two CIN1 cases demonstrated high mRNA expression despite negative HPV DNA results.
CONCLUSIONS: Flow-cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection showed high overall agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology in this screening cohort. Larger prospective studies with comprehensive histologic follow-up are needed to determine its clinical utility.

articles.title: Large language model responses about PMOS : information quality, readability, transparency and perceived empathy.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Chen Y, Xiong YJ, Yu P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Freely accessible large language models provide health information, but their communication characteristics require evaluation. We compared information quality, transparency, readability and perceived empathy for questions about polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; formerly PCOS).
METHODS: Thirty-three clinician-formulated English questions using PCOS terminology were submitted once to each of three free-access configurations during 20-25 July 2026. Two clinicians rated DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmarks, global quality and perceived empathy. Six readability indices were calculated. Matched comparisons used Friedman tests, paired signed-rank permutation comparisons and Holm correction.
RESULTS: Across 99 archived responses, the DeepSeek-V4 configuration received higher final ratings than GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.5 on all five clinician-rated measures (Holm-adjusted pairwise P < 0.05). Median DISCERN scores were 67.0, 62.0 and 61.0, respectively. DeepSeek-V4 had higher median ARI, GFI, FKGL and SMOG values, whereas GPT-5.5 had the highest median Coleman-Liau score. FRES showed no overall difference (adjusted P = 0.100). Initial empathy agreement was low (ICC 0.05-0.43).
CONCLUSION: Ratings differed for the specific configurations and single responses examined in this treatment-heavy question set. The findings neither establish stable model rankings nor demonstrate clinical correctness, safety or effectiveness for patients.

articles.title: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of FTO-Related Developmental Disorder Caused by Biallelic Variants in FTO.
articles.authors: Periyasamy R, Narayanan GK, Narayanan DL et al.
articles.abstract: Fat Mass and Obesity-Associated (FTO) gene encodes a versatile RNA-modifying enzyme that regulates gene expression, RNA processing, and protein synthesis by demethylating different RNA substrates. FTO has a wide range of effects on mammalian physiological functions in regulating fat mass, adipogenesis, and energy homeostasis. Bi-allelic variants in FTO cause growth failure, developmental delay, and facial dysmorphism. Earlier reported individuals carried variants at critical catalytic sites and had severe developmental phenotypes with early childhood lethality. We report 13 additional individuals from nine families with variable prenatal and postnatal phenotypes with variants in FTO (NM_001080432.3). We add a presumably founder variant c.608 T>C in seven individuals from four Indian families with milder clinical and neuroimaging findings compared to earlier reports. We reviewed genotype-phenotypes of the current series and previous individuals with FTO-related developmental disorders. We also document the prenatal phenotypes of FTO variants, thereby expanding the spectrum of FTO-related developmental anomalies.

articles.title: Prevalence, Incidence, Clinical Presentation, and Treatment of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome in Primary Care in the United Kingdom Between 1998 and 2025.
articles.authors: Shapiro SB, Yu OHY, Dahan MH et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a multisystemic disorder with a wide range of health consequences. We sought to describe temporal trends in the prevalence and incidence of PMOS and to characterize its clinical presentation, comorbidity burden, and pharmacological management in primary care in the United Kingdom (UK) between 1998 and 2025.
DESIGN: Population-based matched cohort study using primary care records from the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink.
PATIENTS: Females newly diagnosed with PMOS between the ages of 15 and 49 matched on age, general practice, calendar year of cohort entry, and duration of medical history to population controls without PMOS.
MEASUREMENTS: Annual prevalence and incidence of diagnosed PMOS; baseline prevalence and incidence of cardinal PMOS features and various comorbidities; and pre- and post-cohort entry prevalence of hormonal contraceptive, anti-androgen, ovulation-inducing drug, and metformin use.
RESULTS: The prevalence of diagnosed PMOS increased from < 0.1% in 1998 to 2.0% in 2025, with incidence rising from 0.1 to 3.6 per 1,000 person-years over the same period. Among 125,482 patients with newly diagnosed PMOS matched with an equal number of controls, patients with PMOS had higher baseline prevalence and incidence of cardinal features of PMOS, as well as diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, sleep apnea, thyroid disorders, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, chronic pain, depression, and anxiety. Use of anti-androgens, ovulation-inducing drugs, and metformin was substantially higher in patients with PMOS, especially in the year following diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: PMOS is increasingly diagnosed in UK primary care and is associated with substantial multimorbidity and pharmacotherapy.

articles.title: Fertility-sparing surgery for early-stage epithelial ovarian cancer: evolving criteria for patient selection.
articles.authors: Shikama A, Satoh T
articles.abstract: Fertility-sparing surgery (FSS) is an important treatment option for young women with early-stage epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). Stage IA, grade 1-2, non-clear-cell carcinoma is the most established indication, but whether FSS can be safely extended beyond this population remains uncertain. In 2010, Satoh et al. proposed a patient-selection framework based on stage, histologic subtype, and tumor grade, identifying stage IA clear-cell carcinoma (CCC) and unilateral stage IC non-clear-cell grade 1-2 disease as candidates for expanded FSS beyond this reference group (termed "favorable histology" in the original terminology). This review reassesses that framework using evidence accumulated through 2026. Only FSS cases with classifiable stage, histologic subtype, and grade were included in the descriptive oncologic synthesis, with CCC evaluated as a separate histologic category. Available evidence continues to support FSS for stage IA non-clear-cell grade 1-2 disease and, in carefully selected patients, unilateral stage IC non-clear-cell grade 1-2 disease. Increasing evidence supports considering FSS in appropriately staged stage IA CCC, although counseling should address the potentially poor salvageability of extra-ovarian recurrence. Evidence remains insufficient for routine FSS in high-grade disease or stage IC CCC. Retrospective evidence is limited by selection bias, historical staging systems, heterogeneous pathology, treatment variability, and overlapping cohorts. Further, a recent nationwide Japanese survey demonstrated substantial institutional variation in FSS practice. Prospective validation is therefore required to establish reproducible criteria for expanded indications. JCOG1203 is expected to determine whether FSS can safely be extended to these groups without compromising survival or increasing lethal recurrence.

articles.title: Extended-Dose Letrozole Regimen versus Standard-Dose Regimen for Ovulation Induction and Biochemical Pregnancy in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of the College of Physicians and Surgeons--Pakistan : JCPSP
articles.authors: Munir SI, Tariq R, Raana G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the extended-dose letrozole regimen with the standard-dose regimen for ovulation induction and biochemical pregnancy in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
STUDY DESIGN: A randomised controlled trial. Place and Duration of the Study: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Sir Gangaram Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, from April to September 2025.
METHODOLOGY: A total of 174 women with PCOS were randomised into extended-dose (n = 87; letrozole 5 mg, cycle days 2-10) and standard- dose (n = 87; letrozole 5 mg, cycle days 2-6) groups. Ovulation was triggered with human chorionic gonadotropin (5000 IU) upon detecting mature follicles (18-22 mm). Ovulation induction was confirmed by measuring mid-luteal serum progesterone levels on day 21, and biochemical pregnancy by urine pregnancy test on day 28. Statistical analysis was performed using both univariable and multivariable logistic regression frameworks to estimate odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Baseline demographics and endocrine parameters were comparable, with no statistically significant differences between groups (all p >0.05). The extended-dose letrozole regimen achieved significantly higher rates and odds of successful ovulation induction (69.0% vs. 51.7%, p = 0.020; aOR = 1.995, p = 0.035) and positive biochemical pregnancy (33.3% vs. 16.1%, p = 0.008; aOR = 2.500, p = 0.014) than the standard protocol. Conversely, secondary subfertility independently reduced the likelihood of successful ovulation induction (aOR = 0.472, p = 0.026). None of the other evaluated covariates showed a significant association in both univariable and multivariable analyses.
CONCLUSION: Extended-dose letrozole regimen demonstrated better efficacy in achieving successful ovulation induction and biochemical pregnancy compared with the standard-dose regimen. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution in light of the study's inherent limitations.
KEY WORDS: Letrozole, Infertility, Ovulation induction, Polycystic ovary syndrome, Pregnancy.

articles.title: Under-recognition of endometriosis in general surgery: A national review of Freedom of Information data.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.authors: Mills L, Herschel P, Jicol A et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEndometriosis affects 10% of women of reproductive age; however, diagnostic delay remains common, with an average delay of 7 years. Although general surgeons frequently perform pelvic procedures, recognition of endometriosis within this specialty remains limited. This study compares diagnostic practices between general surgery and gynecology to identify missed opportunities for earlier detection of endometriosis.MethodsFreedom of Information requests were submitted to 143 National Health Service organizations across the United Kingdom to collect data on diagnostic laparoscopies in women aged 16-35 years between 2013 and 2023. Outcomes included rates of initial and delayed endometriosis diagnoses, laparoscopic volumes, and patient complaints. Comparative analysis was performed according to specialty.ResultsOf the 143 hospitals contacted, 52 provided data for analysis. Between 2013 and 2023, there were 1,419,366 admissions for abdominal pain in general surgery and gynecology, with 4356 endometriosis diagnoses established per annum. General surgeons diagnosed endometriosis in 255 of 8305 (3.1%; 95% confidence interval: 2.7%-3.5%) laparoscopies, whereas gynecologists diagnosed endometriosis in 4825 of 21,456 (22.5%; 95% confidence interval: 21.9%-23.1%) laparoscopies. Delayed diagnoses following inconclusive procedures occurred in 8.2% of general surgery cases compared with 15.5% of gynecology cases. Complaint rates were comparable between general surgery and gynecology among the four trusts that reported data (p = 0.49).ConclusionsGeneral surgeons recorded substantially lower rates of endometriosis diagnosis than gynecologists during diagnostic laparoscopy. Although case mix, coding, and follow-up differences may contribute, the magnitude of this disparity supports the need for improved endometriosis recognition, training, documentation, and cross-specialty diagnostic pathways.

articles.title: Diet-induced obesity disrupts hypothalamic- testicular NF-κB signaling axis and impairs spermatogenesis: an integrated transcriptomic analysis and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Du G, Chen J, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a recognized risk factor for male infertility, yet the involvement of the hypothalamic-testicular axis and nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB)-mediated inflammation remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to investigate whether diet-induced obesity is associated with alterations in the hypothalamic-testicular NF-κB signaling axis and spermatogenesis through integrated transcriptomic analysis and clinical meta-analysis.
METHODS: Testicular single-cell RNA-seq and hypothalamic transcriptomic data from diet-induced obese mice were integrated to identify cell-type-specific transcriptional changes. The analyses included differential expression, pathway enrichment, and NF-κB activity scoring based on target gene expression. Mechanistic findings related to steroidogenesis and germ-cell maturation were elucidated via integrated transcriptomic analysis, and a systematic clinical meta-analysis was further performed to validate these mechanistic insights and assess the association between obesity, sperm quality, and NF-κB-related inflammation in humans.
RESULTS: Integrated analysis revealed marked NF-κB transcriptional activity in testicular germ cells (predominantly round spermatids, adjusted p = 0.00134), whose median score was 1.82-fold higher than that of the control group. This activity inversely correlated with genes essential for steroidogenesis (Hsd3b1: r = -0.47 to -0.62), blood-testis barrier (BTB) integrity (Cldn11: r ≈ -0.55), and germ-cell maturation (Tnp1: r = -0.42 to -0.58; all adjusted p < 0.05). Concurrently, a high-fat diet was associated with hypothalamic NF-κB signaling (log2FC = 1.32, adjusted p = 0.012) and upregulated Protein Phosphatase 2 Catalytic Subunit Alpha (Ppp2ca; log2FC = 1.57, adjusted p = 0.008). Meta-analysis of 7 clinical studies confirmed obesity-associated reduced sperm concentration (standardized mean difference = -0.24, 95% CI: -0.37 to -0.12, p < 0.001) and 3.24-fold higher azoospermia risk (95% CI:1.18-8.88, p = 0.023).
CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings suggest that NF-κB-mediated inflammation along the hypothalamus-testis axis may contribute to obesity-related male infertility and highlight NF-κB as a potential therapeutic target. However, further interventional studies using NF-κB inhibitors or germ cell-specific genetic models are required to establish causality and validate NF-κB as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Neuromodulation with microcurrents versus posterior tibial nerve stimulation in the treatment of overactive bladder: a prospective comparative study.
articles.authors: Arrabal-Martin M, Martinez-Sanchez MI, Jerez-Fernandez L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) using the Urgent PC device has been shown to improve symptoms of overactive bladder (OAB). In this context, non-invasive autonomic nervous system neuromodulation using microcurrents (NESA), delivered via the NXsignal device, has emerged as a potential alternative therapy. The study aimed to evaluate the initial efficacy of NESA in patients with an overactive bladder.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, non-randomized study comparing microcurrent neuromodulation (NESA) with PTNS in 60 consecutively recruited patients, evaluating changes in clinical bladder diary parameters and urodynamic findings after 12 treatment sessions. The main variables measured were clinical (collected from a 3-day bladder diary), including: daytime urinary frequency (DUF); nocturnal urinary frequency (NUF); urgency episodes (EU); urgency urinary incontinence episodes (UUI) and urodynamic (first urge to void; maximum bladder capacity; urgency-related voiding; detrusor overactivity). Various parametric and non-parametric statistical tests were used, and statistical significance was considered at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Favorable outcomes were observed across all clinical and urodynamic variables with both treatments (NESA vs. PTNS). A significant reduction in urgency episodes (EU) was observed in patients treated with PTNS (p = 0.006), while a significant reduction in detrusor overactivity was found in patients treated with NESA (p = 0.008). In the NESA group, the bladder tolerated a greater urine volume before the first desire to void, whereas significant differences in increased bladder capacity were observed in patients treated with PTNS. No adverse effects were detected in either treatment group.
CONCLUSION: Both treatments were effective, with no statistically significant differences between NESA and PTNS in the management of OAB. Further studies are warranted to investigate the long-term effects of microcurrent neuromodulation, as well as to better define its optimal, patient-specific application.

articles.title: Robotics in functional and reconstructive urology: evolutionary institutional experience and current attitudes amongst practicing urologists.
articles.authors: Bhalla RG, Vereecken SJ, Coddington N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of robotic-assisted laparoscopic (RAL) surgery in functional and reconstructive urology (FRU) has exponentially grown and has become standard of care over the past decade. We aimed to compare our experience adopting RALsurgery in FRU with current practice patterns and to discuss the implications of the RAL platform for the future of genitourinary reconstructive surgery (GURS) training.
METHODS: We reviewed case logs of two GURS urologists and identified RAL cases from 2012 to 2024. Cases were categorized into: lower urinary tract (LUT), upper urinary tract (UUT), urogynecology and reconstructive pelvic surgery (URPS), fistula, extirpative, and gender affirmation. Changes in volume and distribution were evaluated over time. A REDCap survey was circulated amongst practicing urologists, asking about their experience regarding RAL-FRU surgery.
RESULTS: A total of 1083 surgeries were captured: 165 LUT, 314 UUT, 437 URPS, 16 fistula, 94 extirpative, and 57 gender affirmation. The annual number of RAL-FRU cases increased from 23 (2012) to 158 (2024), with the biggest change seen in UUT reconstruction (4.3% to 36.1%). A total of 108 surveys were completed. The majority of respondents had been practicing for less than 10 years (59%) and in academia (57%). Of the respondents, 31% performed at least 10 RAL-FRU cases annually. The most common cases were robotic pyeloplasty (55%) and ureteral reconstruction (54%). Surgeons involved in post-graduate training reported they strongly agreed or agreed with reporting RAL-FRU cases for GURS fellows.
CONCLUSIONS: The RAL platform was rapidly adopted in FRU surgery over the past decade, particularly in UUT reconstruction. Educators should aim to incorporate robotics training for the next generation of GURS surgeons.

articles.title: Does Aquablation wash away holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP)?: a comparison of the techniques and outcomes.
articles.authors: Helfand BT, Quintas JJ, Park G et al.
articles.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is the most prevalent urological condition in aging men and often requires surgical treatment. While traditional procedures such as open simple prostatectomy (OSP) and transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) have been widely used, newer modalities, including holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP)/anatomic endoscopic enucleation of the prostate (AEEP), initially described in 1997, and Aquablation robotic waterjet therapy (RWT) with FDA approval in 2018, have emerged as modern contenders as a new gold standard. This review study aimed to compare HoLEP and Aquablation RWT across various clinical domains, including symptom relief, quality of life (QoL), sexual function, perioperative outcomes, durability, and learning curves, to guide evidence-based surgical decision-making for BPH treatment. A comprehensive analysis of published randomized trials, registry data, and institutional experience was conducted and outcomes were compared. Both techniques result in significant improvements in LUTS and QoL. HoLEP remains a durable treatment, especially for large prostates, with <2% retreatment rates; however, it is associated with a steep learning curve, temporary or permanent stress urinary incontinence (SUI), and high rates of ejaculatory dysfunction. In comparison, Aquablation RWT is associated with a shorter learning curve, comparable improvements in LUTS, minimal SUI, and superior preservation of antegrade ejaculatory function. Same-day discharge is feasible for both techniques. Both HoLEP and Aquablation offer superior urinary outcomes compared to TURP for prostates of all volumes. However, given the low learning curve, minimal risk of stress incontinence and ejacultory function preservation, Aquablation is an increasingly attractive option for both physicians and patients.

articles.title: Tracking Tumorigenesis Through Cell-Free DNA Analysis: From Premalignant Evolution to Multimodal Surveillance and Early Detection.
articles.authors: Sun Y, Zhang G, Xu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Conventional tissue biopsy remains the clinical standard for diagnosing many cancers, but it provides only a spatially restricted and temporally limited view of disease. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a minimally invasive source of molecular information that may reflect temporal changes in tissue injury, clonal evolution, and epigenetic remodeling. This review distinguishes early tumorigenesis, premalignant states, preinvasive disease, and early-stage cancer, and examines how mutational profiling, fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and extracellular vesicles can be used to investigate molecular events across this continuum. The conceptual contribution is to frame cfDNA as a longitudinal readout of somatic evolution rather than solely a one-time cancer detection assay, while distinguishing direct measurements from computational inferences. We also discuss clonal hematopoiesis, signal dilution, the lack of validated reference standards, and the mismatch between dynamic tumor evolution and static biomarker assays. Longitudinal and multimodal analyses are biologically promising; however, current evidence does not yet demonstrate that cfDNA can directly or continuously monitor malignant transformation. In the near term, its value may lie primarily in risk stratification, mechanistic research, and rigorously validated surveillance of selected high-risk populations.

articles.title: Social and Structural Forces Shaping Reproductive Decision-Making in Hispanic Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Wise L, de Oca AM, Delgado M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects women of reproductive age, making pregnancy timing and contraception use central to care. Although clinical counseling is vital to reproductive planning, less is known about the sociocultural and structural influences shaping reproductive decision-making among Hispanic women with SLE in the United States. This study explored patient perspectives on multi-level factors influencing reproductive health decision-making.
METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 30 Hispanic women with SLE recruited from a safety-net rheumatology clinic and a community lupus support organization. Participants were aged 18-45 years, sexually active or considering pregnancy within three years, and fluent in English or Spanish. Interviews were conducted virtually, transcribed, and analyzed using a grounded theory-informed approach, with the Socioecological Model retrospectively applied to guide analysis.
RESULTS: Four major themes aligned with the Socioecological Framework. Reproductive decision-making was shaped by structural stability, including financial security, career readiness, and confidence managing SLE during pregnancy. Culture and religion were present but variably integrated into reproductive health considerations, while partners and family members influenced how risks and decisions were discussed and supported. Participants also relied on informal information networks, including peer experiences and online resources, to interpret reproductive risks and contraception options.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive planning among Hispanic women with SLE is influenced by structural, relational, and informational factors extending beyond the clinical encounter. These findings highlight the need for supportive interventions or resources beyond the clinical encounter, including supportive networks, trusted information, and peer-informed support tailored to young women living with SLE.

articles.title: Sex differences in neurogenic hypertension: estrogen modulation of NADPH oxidase signaling in the rostral ventrolateral medulla.
articles.authors: Jin J, Kalsoom UE, Su Y et al.
articles.abstract: Neurogenic hypertension is characterized by sustained sympathetic activation arising from dysregulation within the central autonomic network. The rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM) is a major sympathetic premotor region that integrates reflex, neurohumoral, inflammatory, and metabolic signals. Oxidative stress within the RVLM can increase neuronal excitability, enhance glutamatergic transmission, weaken nitric oxide-dependent GABAergic inhibition, and promote sympathetic activation. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidases are important sources of reactive oxygen species in this region. Direct anatomical evidence is the strongest for components of the NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) complex, whereas the cellular distribution and functional roles of Nox1, Nox4, and other isoforms remain less clearly defined. Current evidence more strongly supports RVLM Nox-related oxidative stress as a mechanism that amplifies and maintains established hypertension than as an independent initiator of chronic hypertension.Sex and ovarian hormone status modulate these redox and autonomic mechanisms. Estrogen signaling can influence neuronal excitability, inflammation, and oxidative balance, but its effects depend on receptor subtype, endocrine state, exposure pattern, age, and hypertensive background. Estradiol replacement after ovarian hormone loss may reduce RVLM oxidative stress, whereas prolonged exposure in intact cycling animals may increase superoxide production and Nox-related gene expression. Human studies also associate menopause with altered blood pressure, arterial stiffness, sympathetic activity, and baroreflex regulation, although direct evidence for estrogen receptor and Nox signaling within the human RVLM remains lacking. This review summarizes current evidence and highlights priorities for mechanistic and translational research.

articles.title: Herd-, sow-, parity- and service-level risk factors for sow mortality at different reproductive stages: an analysis of production data.
articles.authors: Huang J, Fonseca O, Pailler L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sow mortality has been increasing in recent years, posing significant challenges to commercial pig production. High mortality affects animal welfare, farm productivity, and causes substantial economic losses. While previous studies have identified risk factors such as high parity, seasonal effects, and farrowing-related complications, limited research has quantified mortality risk at different reproductive stages in Spain. This study aims to analyze sow mortality patterns and identify associated risk factors.
RESULTS: Analysis of production records from 16 Spanish farms revealed that 55.59% of sow deaths occurred before farrowing, while 44.41% occurred after farrowing. Mortality risk peaked during late gestation (105-118 days) and again during the first and after the fourth weeks post-farrowing. Several risk factors were identified at farm and individual levels. Internal gilt replacement was associated with increased mortality risk. Before farrowing, sows with parity ≥ 3 and single-service sows exhibited higher mortality. After farrowing, increased mortality was observed in parity 1 sows and those with repeat breeding. Seasonal effects showed highest mortality rates in sows bred in spring and farrowing in summer. Matched case-control analysis revealed that parity 0 sows had a younger age at first service, and deceased sows had shorter gestational length, fewer piglets born, born alive, and a higher incidence of stillbirth fetuses at their last litter before their death. Comparing their lifetime performance, dead sows had younger gilt age at first service, fewer parity at removal, higher average number of piglets born, born alive, born still and born mummified per parity, but they had fewer weaned piglets and nonproductive days.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies late gestation and the first week postpartum as critical windows for sow mortality risk. Internal gilt replacement and parity extremes emerged as key herd- and sow-level risk factors, while mortality was also higher among sows farrowing in summer. Repeat breeding prior to farrowing was associated with lower mortality. These findings support integrating reproductive history and herd-level replacement strategy into sow management and culling decisions.

articles.title: Association between anatomical correction and bladder emptying after robotic sacrocolpopexy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Nishiyama S, Kadota C, Hyodo R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between anatomical correction and bladder emptying after robotic sacrocolpopexy remains unclear. This study evaluated early postoperative changes in postvoid residual volume (PVR) and examined their association with changes in anterior compartment support.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients who underwent robotic sacrocolpopexy for pelvic organ prolapse between April 2025 and April 2026. PVR was measured by transurethral catheterization on the day before surgery and on postoperative day 3. Anterior compartment support was assessed using pelvic organ prolapse quantification point Ba before surgery and approximately 1 month postoperatively. Changes were calculated as postoperative minus preoperative values (ΔPVR and ΔBa). The association between ΔBa and ΔPVR was evaluated using Spearman's rank correlation, and an exploratory linear regression analysis adjusted for preoperative PVR was performed.
RESULTS: Of 37 consecutive patients, 36 were included in the primary analysis. Median ΔBa was - 4.0 cm (interquartile range [IQR], - 5.0 to - 3.0; p < 0.001). Median PVR decreased from 28.0 mL (IQR, 15.0-96.3) preoperatively to 11.0 mL (IQR, 4.5-30.3) on postoperative day 3 (p < 0.001), although individual changes varied widely. No statistically significant correlation was observed between ΔBa and ΔPVR (Spearman's ρ = - 0.155; 95% confidence interval [CI], - 0.462 to 0.185; p = 0.367). In the baseline-adjusted regression analysis, ΔBa was not significantly associated with postoperative PVR (regression coefficient, - 1.345; 95% CI, - 13.270 to 10.580; p = 0.820).
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic sacrocolpopexy was associated with improved anterior compartment support and an overall reduction in early postoperative PVR. However, the magnitude of anatomical correction was not significantly associated with the change in PVR. Given the small sample size and wide confidence interval, these findings should be considered exploratory. Anatomical and bladder emptying outcomes should therefore be assessed separately after robotic sacrocolpopexy.

articles.title: Association between vitamin D levels, hormonal profile, and ovarian reserve in infertile women.
articles.authors: Azizi Kutenaee M, Roozbeh N, Taghvaei E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The potential influence of vitamin D on female reproductive function has recently gained considerable attention, yet its connection with hormonal dynamics and ovarian reserve remains uncertain. This study explored how circulating vitamin D concentrations relate to reproductive hormones and ovarian reserve indices among infertile women.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on medical records of 880 infertile women aged 18-45 years. Participants were grouped by serum vitamin D status as sufficient (≥ 30 ng/mL), insufficient (21-29 ng/mL), or deficient (≤ 20 ng/mL). Hormonal factors (FSH, LH, AMH, E2, TSH) and antral follicle count (AFC) were analyzed using Kruskal-Wallis and multinomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: Nearly half of the women (47.4%) were vitamin D deficient. Those with deficiency exhibited significantly greater BMI values and lower LH concentrations compared with women having sufficient vitamin D (p < 0.05). Regression modeling indicated that BMI positively predicted both insufficiency (OR = 1.045, p = 0.029) and deficiency (OR = 1.058, p = 0.001), whereas LH showed an inverse association with deficiency (OR = 0.964, p = 0.040). In adjusted analysis, higher AMH was associated with vitamin D insufficiency, whereas no significant association was observed for vitamin D deficiency.
CONCLUSION: Vitamin D deficiency was common among infertile women and was associated with higher BMI and lower LH levels. These findings support a possible link between vitamin D status and selected metabolic and hormonal parameters; however, longitudinal studies are needed before clinical implications can be established.

articles.title: Anxiety in preschool children with ADHD symptoms: associations with ADHD dimensions and perinatal risk factors.
articles.authors: Fan Z, Chu S, Shen J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) commonly co-occurs with anxiety, but the relative contributions of inattention (INA) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (HI) to anxiety severity in preschool children remain unclear. The role of perinatal risk factors is also insufficiently understood.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 6,188 preschool children who screened positive for ADHD symptoms based on SNAP-IV cutoffs. ADHD symptom dimensions were assessed using the Swanson, Nolan, and Pelham Rating Scale, Fourth Edition (SNAP-IV), and anxiety severity was measured with the Spence Preschool Anxiety Scale (PAS). Perinatal depression, fetal growth restriction (FGR), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), and gestational diabetes mellitus were obtained from parent-reported questionnaires. Multivariable regression, restricted cubic spline, subgroup, and interaction analyses were performed after adjustment for sociodemographic and perinatal covariates.
RESULTS: Both INA and HI were independently associated with anxiety severity, with a stronger association for INA. INA showed a nonlinear association with anxiety, with a steeper increase at low-to-moderate levels followed by a plateau at higher levels. Children with inattentive and combined symptom presentations had higher anxiety scores than those with the hyperactive-impulsive presentation. Perinatal depression and FGR were independently associated with greater anxiety severity. A significant interaction suggested a stronger association between INA and anxiety severity among children exposed to HDP.
CONCLUSIONS: INA may be more strongly associated with anxiety severity than HI in preschool children with ADHD symptoms. ADHD symptom dimensions and perinatal context should be jointly considered in the early identification of anxiety risk.

articles.title: Linking dietary-derived arsenic exposure to blood serum arsenic burden, potential food sources, and breast cancer risk in the EPIC-Heidelberg cohort.
articles.authors: Kipkoech M, Beck CM, Jaeger A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women worldwide, yet the role of environmental toxicants remains unclear. Arsenic is an International Agency for Research on Cancer classified carcinogen linked to skin, lung, and bladder cancers. The relationship between dietary arsenic intake levels and blood arsenic concentrations, particularly across sexes, and the association between dietary arsenic intake and breast cancer remain understudied. This study aimed to address these gaps.
METHODS: Measurements of arsenic in foods collected from 1995 to 2022 in the German monitoring programme were used to estimate long-term dietary intake. Serum arsenic levels were measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. Participants were aged 35-65 years; 2,674 non-cases were included in the arsenic intake-serum arsenic analysis, and 631 incident cases and 1,708 non-cases in the breast cancer analysis. Partial spearman's rank correlation and logistic regression models assessed the association between dietary arsenic intake and serum arsenic levels. Prentice-weighted Cox proportional hazards models with age as underlying time scale were used to assess associations between dietary arsenic intake and breast cancer risk.
RESULTS: No association was observed between total or estimated inorganic arsenic intake and breast cancer risk (HR 1.1, 95% CI: 0.93-1.31; HR 0.9, 95% CI: 0.76-1.07), including in subgroup analyses by menopausal status (pre- and post-menopausal), estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status. Weak positive correlations were observed between total and estimated inorganic arsenic intake and serum arsenic concentrations (ρ = 0.20 and ρ = 0.07). However, regression analyses showed that total arsenic intake was associated with serum arsenic in both sexes (men: OR 3.48, 95% CI 2.33-5.22; women: OR 2.60, 95% CI 1.84-3.68), whereas estimated inorganic arsenic intake were associated only among women in the second and fourth quintiles (OR 1.53 [95% CI 1.10-2.14] and 1.90 [1.33-2.73], respectively).
CONCLUSION: Dietary arsenic intake was not significantly associated with serum arsenic levels or incident breast cancer.

articles.title: Percutaneous transvenous mitral commissurotomy during pregnancy: a contemporary Southeast Asian experience.
articles.authors: Sricholwattana S, Kosum P, Theerasuwipakorn N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis during pregnancy is associated with substantial maternal and fetal morbidity because physiological hemodynamic changes may precipitate heart failure and pulmonary hypertension. Percutaneous transvenous mitral commissurotomy (PTMC) is the recommended intervention for carefully selected symptomatic patients who remain refractory to medical therapy. Although PTMC during pregnancy has been widely reported, contemporary data describing procedural characteristics, radiation exposure, and maternal-fetal outcomes from Southeast Asia remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the procedural, hemodynamic, radiation, maternal, and neonatal outcomes of PTMC performed during pregnancy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of consecutive pregnant women with rheumatic mitral stenosis who underwent PTMC at a tertiary referral center in Thailand between 2002 and 2022 according to the institutional eligibility criteria used during the study period. Given the limited sample size, all analyses were considered exploratory. Hemodynamic, echocardiographic, procedural, radiation, maternal, and neonatal outcomes were evaluated.
RESULTS: Eighteen pregnant women underwent PTMC at a mean gestational age of 24.6 ± 5.7 weeks. Procedural success was achieved in 94% of patients. Mitral valve area significantly increased from 0.98 ± 0.23 cm² to 1.50 ± 0.34 cm² (p < 0.001), while mean transmitral gradient decreased from 15.98 ± 5.97 mmHg to 7.26 ± 3.92 mmHg (p = 0.001). Mean left atrial pressure also significantly decreased from 31.94 ± 5.95 mmHg to 17.41 ± 4.29 mmHg (p < 0.001), and most patients improved from New York Heart Association functional class III-IV to class I-II (p < 0.001). Among the 12 patients with available radiation data, the median fluoroscopy time was 3.76 min and the median cumulative air Kerma was 21 mGy. Among patients with available obstetric follow-up (n = 12), no maternal deaths, neonatal deaths, or congenital anomalies were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small retrospective single-center study, PTMC was associated with significant immediate hemodynamic and symptomatic improvement in carefully selected pregnant women with rheumatic mitral stenosis. Among patients with available follow-up, maternal and neonatal outcomes were generally favorable; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, prolonged recruitment period, retrospective design, and…

articles.title: Prevalence of hepatitis E virus in pregnant women in Northeast Brazil.
articles.authors: Melo JHL, Júnior JVJS, Cunha GG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection remains underrecognized in many low- and middle-income settings, particularly among pregnant women, a population potentially vulnerable to adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. We investigated HEV seroprevalence, molecular detection, and epidemiological characteristics among pregnant women attending antenatal care services in northeastern Brazil.
METHODS: Serum samples from 900 pregnant women were screened for anti-HEV IgG. Reactive samples were further tested for anti-HEV IgM using two commercial immunoassays and for HEV RNA by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Demographic, environmental, and obstetric variables were analyzed using appropriate statistical tests.
RESULTS: Anti-HEV IgG was detected in two pregnant women (0.22%; 2/900), whereas no samples were positive for anti-HEV IgM. Both IgG-positive women tested positive for HEV RNA by RT-qPCR, were asymptomatic at the time of sampling, and reported exposure profiles compatible with recognized fecal-oral transmission routes. No statistically significant associations were observed between HEV positivity and the variables evaluated.
CONCLUSIONS: This study reports the seroprevalence and molecular detection of HEV among pregnant women attending antenatal care services in northeastern Brazil. Beyond providing epidemiological data, these findings highlight the importance of combining serological and molecular approaches for HEV investigation and reinforce the need for further epidemiological studies to better define the public health relevance of HEV infection during pregnancy.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Sequential method for determining the effective dose of remimazolam combined with sufentanil for cervical dilation in hysteroscopic surgery.
articles.authors: Yan Q, Wang H, Wu L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the 50% and 95% effective doses (ED50 and ED95) of remimazolam combined with sufentanil for cervical dilation during hysteroscopic surgery.
DESIGN: Prospective single-center dose-finding study using a modified Dixon up-and-down sequential method.
METHOD: Twenty-five patients who underwent hysteroscopic surgery were enrolled in 2024. All patients received an intravenous injection of sufentanil at 0.15 μg/kg for intraoperative analgesia. We used a modified Dixon sequential method. The initial dose of remimazolam was 0.15 mg/kg. The dose of remimazolam administered to each patient was determined by whether hysteroscope placement had failed. Failure was defined as inadequate cervical dilation and difficulty in hysteroscope placement, accompanied by patient manifestations such as limb movements, frowning, or a Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (MOAA/S) score ≥1. If cervical dilation failed (i.e., a positive response), the dose of remimazolam was increased by 0.02 mg/kg for subsequent subjects. Conversely, in the case of a negative response, the dose was decreased by the same gradient. Formal testing started from the first crossover point and continued until the eighth crossover point appeared.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: The probit method was used to calculate the 50% and 95% effective doses (ED50 and ED95) of remimazolam combined with sufentanil for cervical dilation during intravenous anesthesia, along with their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs).
RESULTS: The ED50 and ED95 of remimazolam combined with 0.15 μg/kg sufentanil for cervical dilation were 0.18 mg/kg (95% CI: 0.17-0.20) and 0.22 mg/kg (95% CI: 0.19-0.25), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Administering 0.22 mg/kg remimazolam combined with 0.15 μg/kg sufentanil is safe and effective for intravenous anesthesia during cervical dilation in hysteroscopic surgery.

articles.title: Primary Care Engagement and Acute Care Utilization by Interpreter Use in an Urban Resident Clinic: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Mathews P, MacKay M, Elias G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients who prefer a language other than English (LOE) experience well-documented differences in health care access and quality. How care delivery and utilization differ for those requiring professional interpreter services in resident continuity clinics is not well characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To compare primary care delivery, preventive screening, chronic disease management, and utilization between patients who did and did not require interpreter services.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data, October 2022 to October 2024. Setting and Participants An urban internal medicine resident continuity clinic in St. Louis, MO, with in-person interpreter services; 14,457 adults, of whom 1058 had documented interpreter use (LOE; > 50 preferred languages) and 13,399 did not (English-proficient). Main Measures Demographics, area-based socioeconomic indicators, comorbidity burden, screening adherence, clinic attendance, emergency department (ED) visits, and hospitalizations. No primary outcome was pre-specified. Key Results LOE patients were older and more often uninsured or Medicaid-insured, yet resided in less-deprived, higher-income areas (median ADI national percentile 71 vs 85) and had lower comorbidity burden. Colorectal, breast, and cervical cancer screening did not differ. Among those with diabetes, glycemic control was worse (A1c < 7%: 49.3% vs 56.8%; difference - 7.5%, 95% CI - 12.9 to - 2.1), as were tetanus vaccination and HIV screening. They had lower no-show rates (14.0% vs 21.0%; difference - 7.1%, 95% CI - 7.9 to - 6.2), more completed visits (mean 4.6 vs 3.9; difference + 0.7, 95% CI 0.5 to 0.9), fewer ED visits (36.2% vs 56.3%; difference - 20.1%, 95% CI - 23.1 to - 17.1), and fewer hospitalizations (26.5% vs 37.3%; difference - 10.8%, 95% CI - 13.6 to - 8.0).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single clinic, LOE patients had greater primary care engagement and lower acute care utilization, with residual gaps in glycemic control and vaccination. These descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings may reflect who reaches care as well as language-access supports and warrant prospective study.

articles.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China.
articles.authors: Meng L, Yang H, Miller G et al.
articles.abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline1-10. Notably, even China's total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China's one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China's total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research.

articles.title: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 across cell types improves interpretation of variant pathogenicity.
articles.authors: Dace P, Forrester NM, Zanti M et al.
articles.abstract: Germline pathogenic BRCA1 variants predispose women to breast and ovarian cancer. Despite accumulation of functional evidence, over half of reported single-nucleotide variants in BRCA1 lack a definitive clinical interpretation. Furthermore, the consistency of variant effects across cell types remains largely unexplored. Here we performed saturation genome editing (SGE) of BRCA1 in HAP1 cells to score 4,113 previously unassayed variants. Additionally, we developed an SGE assay in human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs), allowing comparison of effects across cell lines, drug treatments and genetic backgrounds. We identified 538 variants impacting gene function through distinct mechanisms. HAP1 function scores discriminate between known pathogenic and benign variants with near-perfect accuracy. Intriguingly, however, nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants scored neutrally in HMECs. We show that discordantly scored variants are hypomorphic and confer intermediate cancer risk. Overall, this work demonstrates how performing SGE across cell models improves the functional interpretation of rare variants.

articles.title: P53-assisted METTL14-mediated m⁶A modification of SLC7A11 drives ferroptosis and inflammation in polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.authors: Chen X, Lin J, Ning P et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by chronic inflammation and follicular arrest, yet the molecular drivers linking these pathologies to granulosa cell (GC) death remain elusive. Here, we identify a ferroptosis-inflammation cascade as a critical determinant of ovarian dysfunction in PCOS. We demonstrate that the N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) methyltransferase METTL14 is aberrantly upregulated in human PCOS GCs, correlating with oxidative damage. Mechanistically, we uncover a non-canonical paradigm where upregulated P53 functions as an essential RNA-binding cofactor, recruiting METTL14 to the SLC7A11 transcript. Validated by AlphaFold3 modeling, this METTL14-p53 complex catalyzes SLC7A11 m⁶A hypermethylation and mRNA destabilization. The resulting SLC7A11 deficiency dismantles antioxidant defenses, driving ferroptosis and amplifying local inflammation. Crucially, in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model, genetic ablation of Tp53 severed this pathogenic axis, restoring redox balance, suppressing inflammation, and reversing the polycystic phenotype. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal epigenetic mechanism linking m⁶A reprogramming, iron-dependent cell death, and inflammation, highlighting the METTL14-p53-SLC7A11 axis as a therapeutic target in PCOS.

articles.title: Toxicity, health-related quality of life and sexuality after molecular profile-based adjuvant treatment in high-intermediate risk endometrial cancer, PORTEC-4a.
articles.authors: Van den Heerik ASVM, Post CCB, Haverkort MAD et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PORTEC-4a was the first to incorporate molecular-integrated profile-guided adjuvant treatment in early-stage high-intermediate-risk endometrial cancer (EC), demonstrating non-inferiority. Here, adverse events (AE), health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and sexual health are reported.
METHODS: 564 patients were randomised to molecular-based adjuvant treatment (n = 367) or standard vaginal brachytherapy (VBT, n = 197). In the molecular-profile arm, patients underwent observation, VBT or pelvic radiotherapy according to molecular-integrated profile. HRQoL and sexual functioning were assessed with EORTC QLQ-C30 and EN24 modules and compared with age-matched normative data.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 58.1 months; 523 (92.7%) patients were evaluable. Grade 1-2 AEs were less frequent in the molecular-profile arm at treatment completion compared with the standard arm (28.3% vs. 45.2%, p < 0.01), without differences in grade 3-4 AEs (p = 0.46). Throughout follow-up, treatment-related grade 3-4 AEs were rare (1% vs. 2%). HRQoL remained comparable to normative data over time. Sexual interest/activity was similar between arms, but lower than normative values. 75.5% of patients reported ≥1 reason for sexual inactivity; disease-related sexual inactivity decreased from 24.2% to 9.2% at 3 years.
CONCLUSION: Molecular-guided adjuvant treatment for patients with high-intermediate riskEC is associated with low toxicity, preserved HRQoL and slightly reduced sexual activity due to personal factors (no partner, sex not important in their relationship or partner-related medical issues) rather than their own illness.

articles.title: Hypermethylation in CpG-rich cfDNA fragments enables accurate detection of circulating tumor DNA in BRCA1- and BRCA2-associated breast and ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Sekar A, Broche J, Bursic V et al.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic BRCA1 and BRCA2 germline variants confer an increased risk of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC). In this high-risk cohort, novel biomarkers are needed to support patient management. While circulating cell-free DNA-based conventional CpG-level averaging is promising, it dilutes tumor-specific signals in samples with low circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) fractions. Here, we developed a targeted ultra-deep NGS assay for detecting tumor-derived ctDNA based on fragment-level hypermethylation of CpG-rich cfDNA. A panel of 360 cancer-specific CpG-rich regions derived from 450k methylation array datasets from TCGA breast cancer and GEO ovarian cancer, was applied to plasma from 31 breast cancer, 16 ovarian cancer patients, and 26 healthy controls using enzymatic methylation sequencing. Hypermethylated ctDNA (hm-ctDNA) fragments, were significantly enriched in cancer cases, identifying 62.5% of ovarian and 38.7% of breast cancers at 100% specificity. Elevated hm-ctDNA was observed across different tumor stages, with higher burden in BRCA1-associated cases. This approach enables highly specific, non-invasive hypermethylated ctDNA detection in HBOC populations.

articles.title: Delayed brain network energy development in preterm youth impairs cognitive function: evidence from the longitudinal ABCD study.
articles.authors: Li Q, Jensen D, Jakim T et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth disrupts early brain development, increasing the risk of cognitive difficulties. However, its long-term effects on functional brain network energy, a metric of large-scale network stability and adaptability, remain poorly understood. Using resting-state fMRI data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, we examined how prematurity influences brain network energy across late childhood and early adolescence. Our sample included 818 preterm-born youth and 2,149 matched full-term controls.
