Compared to full-term adolescents, preterm individuals exhibited altered multiscale functional connectivity and persistent reductions in functional network energy, specifically within the sensorimotor (SM) and higher-cognitive temporoparietal (HC-TP) networks, at both baseline and 2-year follow-up. These findings suggest diminished functional flexibility and network integration in preterm-born individuals. To further contextualize these results, we incorporated data from 1,633 participants in the Human Connectome Project (HCP) and HCP-Development studies, confirming that network energy increases with age in typically developing youth and is consistently reduced in preterm individuals. Notably, lower energy in the HC-TP network was specifically associated with deficits in crystallized cognition, but not with behavioral problems. Meta-analytic decoding further linked the HC-TP network to language and social cognition, providing a mechanistic explanation for its relationship with crystallized cognitive abilities. These findings highlight the persistence of neurodevelopmental alterations in preterm individuals, particularly affecting higher-order cognitive functions, and position network energy as a potential marker of altered neurodevelopment following preterm birth.

articles.title: Biomarker-led advances in renal cell carcinoma diagnosis, progression monitoring and therapeutic decision-making.
articles.authors: Lasorsa F, Pandolfo SD, Claps F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) diagnosis and management remain challenging due to asymptomatic presentation and limitations in accurately characterizing small renal masses. Noninvasive liquid biopsy biomarkers, including circulating proteins, metabolites, cell-free DNA, microRNAs, and inflammatory markers, have emerged as promising tools for RCC detection, prognostic stratification, and treatment monitoring.
AREAS COVERED: Here we review recent advances in blood- and urine-based biomarkers, highlighting key findings such as the diagnostic accuracy of kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1), CA15-3, metabolomic signatures, and urinary protein panels, alongside the prognostic relevance of circulating tumor DNA and systemic inflammatory indices.
EXPERT OPINION: Despite encouraging analytical and clinical validity, no biomarker has yet demonstrated clinical utility due to biological, methodological, and regulatory challenges. Continued efforts focusing on standardized protocols, prospective validation, and integration with imaging and clinical data are essential to translate these biomarkers into personalized RCC management strategies.

articles.title: Placental-Neural Cross Talk: Biological Mechanisms Shaping Brain Architecture.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.authors: Penn AA, Mir IN, Bonnin A et al.
articles.abstract: Impact of placental function on normal and pathological brain processes and supported behavior is an integrative research area dubbed "neuroplacentology." Placental functional genetics, structure, and vascular function have been discovered to have links to multiple clinical outcomes: autism, schizophrenia, and developmental cognitive impairment in offspring and postpartum depression and cognition in mothers. There are significant data showing that long-term impacts of preterm birth, diseases of pregnancy (preeclampsia), and maternal stress and depression may all be mediated by placental mechanisms, providing clinical and translational insights. Here, we will provide an up-to-date introduction to this emerging field. Mechanistic links between variations in placental structure and function and features of human and animal brain development and function will be discussed, clarifying basic biological connections and highlighting new targets to prevent clinical impairments.

articles.title: Maternal Immune Activation and Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Cross-Species Perspective.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.authors: Mukherjee A, Bauman MD, Hill RA et al.
articles.abstract: Prenatal exposure to infection increases the likelihood of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). This association is attributed largely to the maternal inflammatory response, maternal immune activation (MIA), rather than to single pathogen. In this review, we discuss the molecular, cellular, and behavioral consequences of MIA and their contribution to NDDs in clinical cohorts and preclinical models across different species. We first trace the pathophysiology linking maternal infection to altered fetal neurodevelopment, describing how diverse immune challenges converge on shared nodes including cytokine signaling, oxidative and nutritional stress, placental dysfunction, and epigenetic modification. We then describe how these perturbations affect neural circuits and behavior, focusing on the disrupted social development. Next, we consider sources of individual variation, including gestational timing, fetal sex, and later-life "second hits," that may contribute to the greater vulnerability. Finally, we discuss the translational implications of this work in terms of maternal cytokine and epigenetic signatures as candidate biomarkers for risk stratification and potential therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: Hormonal Effects during the Reproductive Years on Brain and Behavior: Molecular Discovery to Promising Therapeutics for Women's Mental Health.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.authors: Wijtenburg SA, Shansky R, Sacher J et al.
articles.abstract: Beginning at puberty and throughout the lifespan, women experience greater rates of depression, anxiety disorders, eating disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, and hormone-linked mood disorders relative to men. How these disorders relate to hormonal fluctuations and associated changes in physiology and brain circuitry in women during the reproductive years is only partially understood. In this review, the molecular, structural, and functional brain changes during the reproductive years are discussed, with a specific focus on transitional changes during the perinatal period. Preclinical and clinical models of neuroplastic change are also discussed, along with neuromodulatory approaches that account for the contextual, spatial, and temporal parameters of interventions delivered during the postpartum period. Future directions may consider how hormonal fluctuations during reproductive years may improve preclinical and clinical models for women's mental health while acknowledging that greater work is needed to understand the role of a broader range of hormonal and environmental factors linked to mental health including lactation, trauma, contraceptive use, menstruation, and perimenopause.

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in Chinese perimenopausal women: a retrospective observational study.
articles.authors: Yang CM, Liu YF, Gao HY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the predictive performance of different machine learning (ML) models for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in perimenopausal women and to interpret the optimal model using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP).
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
SETTING: A health management centre of China.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 5637 perimenopausal women aged 45–55 years who underwent health examinations were included between February 2022 and August 2023.
METHODS: Physical examination data were collected from perimenopausal women at the Health Management Center of the First Affiliated Hospital of the University of Science and Technology of China. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was employed for feature selection. Eight ML models were developed with hyperparameter tuning. The optimal model was selected based on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), which was calculated on the training set and was subsequently interpreted.
RESULTS: Among 5637 participants, 1324 (23.5%) were diagnosed with NAFLD. The Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model exhibited the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.907 and an accuracy of 0.822 in the validation set. SHAP analysis identified that body mass index, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein, random blood glucose, alanine aminotransferase, hyperuricaemia, platelet count and albumin were the most influential predictors of NAFLD in this population.
CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated superior NAFLD prediction performance compared with other ML methods in the perimenopausal women and might improve health management for this population.

articles.title: Effective dose for successful insertion of a laryngeal mask and impact on discharge time of alfentanil combined with remimazolam besylate in ambulatory hysteroscopic surgery: study protocol for a single-centre, prospective, randomised, controlled clinical trial in China.
articles.authors: Huang X, Liu H, Lie J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alfentanil, a μ-opioid receptor agonist, offers a rapid onset of action, quick recovery and stable haemodynamics, making it an ideal agent for ambulatory surgery anaesthesia. However, the optimal dosing regimen of alfentanil in combination with remimazolam besylate—a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine—for laryngeal mask airway (LMA) insertion has not yet been investigated. This study aims to assess the effective dose of alfentanil and whether alfentanil provides non-inferior discharge times and other relevant outcomes compared with remifentanil in patients undergoing ambulatory hysteroscopic surgery.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-centre, prospective, randomised controlled trial enrolling 160 patients undergoing hysteroscopic surgery. The study consists of two phases. In the first phase, the modified Dixon up-and-down method will be used to determine the median effective dose (ED₅₀) and 95% effective dose (ED₉₅) of alfentanil and remifentanil, each in combination with remimazolam, for successful LMA insertion. In the second phase, patients will be randomised to receive alfentanil or remifentanil and postoperative discharge time and recovery profiles will be compared between groups. The primary outcomes are the ED₅₀ and ED₉₅ for successful LMA insertion and the non-inferiority of discharge time in the alfentanil group compared with the remifentanil group. Secondary outcomes include induction-related safety, postoperative adverse events and the overall safety and efficacy of alfentanil for LMA-based general anaesthesia in ambulatory hysteroscopic surgery.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This randomised controlled trial was reviewed and approved by the Ethics Committee of the Guangzhou First People’s Hospital (Approval number: S-2023-219-01). The results will be published in peer-­reviewed journals.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2600121808.

articles.title: Reproductive Outcomes Associated With Discordance Between Gardner Morphology and KIDScore D5 in Euploid Embryo Transfer Cycles.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Ban M, Ihana T, Takahashi K et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate reproductive outcomes associated with discordance between Gardner morphology and KIDScore D5 in frozen-thawed single euploid embryo transfer cycles and explore developmental-timing features associated with discordance.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 217 frozen-thawed single euploid blastocyst transfer cycles from February 2020 to September 2024. Generalized estimating equations logistic regression models accounted for patient-level clustering. Incremental value was assessed from model discrimination. Outcomes were compared among concordant and discordant Gardner morphology and KIDScore D5 classifications. Exploratory analyses examined developmental timing associated with classification patterns.
RESULTS: Gestational sac formation, fetal heartbeat confirmation, and live birth occurred in 65.9% (143/217), 58.1% (126/217) and 53.9% (117/217) of cycles, respectively. Morphology was independently associated with all three outcomes; the adjusted odds ratio for live birth per one-category increase was 1.95 (95% confidence interval, 1.35-2.84). KIDScore D5 was not independently associated with outcomes and did not significantly improve discrimination beyond morphology and clinical factors. Among 177 cycles with available KIDScore D5, live birth rates were 60.0% in the concordant group (105 cycles), 65.7% in the morphology-higher-than-KIDScore group (35 cycles), and 29.7% in the KIDScore-higher-than-morphology group (37 cycles). The latter had lower adjusted odds of live birth than the concordant group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.25; 95% confidence interval, 0.10-0.62). Exploratory analyses linked blastocyst formation timing with KIDScore D5 category and two-cell and three-cell timing with discordance contrasts.
CONCLUSIONS: In single euploid embryo transfers, morphology remained associated with outcomes, whereas KIDScore D5 provided limited incremental prognostic information. Discordance findings require independent validation.

articles.title: Clinical Signals of Hypothalamic-Pituitary Dysfunction in Patients with Severe Motor and Intellectual Disabilities : A Case Series from a Long-Term Care Facility in Japan.
articles.journal: The journal of medical investigation : JMI
articles.authors: Uemura O, Otobe Y, Miyashita T et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore the clinical features and potential relevance of hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction in patients with severe motor and intellectual disabilities (SMID).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 15 residents with SMID (9 males, 6 females;median age 36 years) who were suspected of hypothalamic or pituitary dysfunction based on recurrent hypothermia, bradycardia, paralytic ileus, vomiting, or stress intolerance. Basal endocrine profiles were evaluated, and cases with hormonal findings suggestive of central endocrine dysfunction were assessed for clinical response to hormone replacement therapy. Because dynamic endocrine testing is often infeasible in this population, the analysis focused on basal hormone levels, characteristic clinical features, and treatment responses.
RESULTS: Six patients (40%) showed hormonal findings suggestive of central endocrine dysfunction, including possible central adrenal insufficiency and/or central hypothyroidism. Other pituitary hormones were within reference ranges;however, comprehensive endocrine evaluation was not performed, and broader hypothalamic-pituitary involvement cannot be excluded. Four patients received hormone replacement therapy. Detailed longitudinal treatment-response assessment was available in three patients, in whom clinical improvement was observed.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that some patients with SMID and unexplained systemic instability may exhibit clinical and biochemical features compatible with possible hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 462-466, August, 2026.

articles.title: In Vitro Fertilization versus Intrauterine Insemination for Cumulative Live Birth and Cost-Effectiveness in Older Low-Prognosis Women with Diminished Ovarian Reserve.
articles.authors: Ma Y, Yang X, Liu S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare cumulative live birth, direct medical costs, and cost-effectiveness of initial intrauterine insemination (IUI) versus in vitro fertilization (IVF) among women in Patient-Oriented Strategies Encompassing Individualized Oocyte Number (POSEIDON) group 4.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study with 20 multiply imputed datasets, 1:1 propensity score matching, and economic evaluation from a healthcare sector perspective.
SUBJECTS: Women in POSEIDON group 4 aged 35-50 years initiating treatment during 2014-2023: 2,675 undergoing IVF and 921 undergoing IUI; 914-920 matched pairs per imputed dataset.
EXPOSURE: Up to three IUI cycles versus one IVF stimulation cycle and all fresh and frozen-thawed transfers of embryos from that retrieval, until first live birth, pathway completion or discontinuation, or follow-up end.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE(S): Cumulative live birth rate, mean direct assisted reproductive technology medical costs per patient in 2025 Chinese yuan, and incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per additional live birth.
RESULT(S): IVF was associated with a higher cumulative live birth rate (21.9% vs. 7.6%; odds ratio, 3.45; 95% confidence interval, 2.49-4.78; P<.001). Mean costs per patient were 21,588 versus 3,802 yuan, with an ICER of 124,322 yuan per additional live birth. At exploratory willingness-to-pay thresholds of 99,665 and 199,330 yuan per additional live birth, the probabilities that IVF was cost-effective were 3.35% and 99.90%, respectively. ICER were 86,859 and 469,582 yuan among women aged 35-<40 and 40-<45 years, respectively; estimates were unstable at ages 45-50 years. The second and third insemination cycles added 1.81 and 0.11 percentage points to the cumulative live birth rate, with ICER of 44,068 and 249,622 yuan, respectively. Among clinical pregnancy cycles, twin pregnancy rates were 15.5% with IVF and 3.9% with IUI (P=.006).
CONCLUSION: (s): In POSEIDON group 4, initial IVF was associated with higher cumulative live birth, costs, and twin pregnancy rates. Cost-effectiveness depended on willingness to pay and was less favorable at older ages. A third IUI cycle offered limited additional benefit and less favorable cost-effectiveness. Treatment decisions should consider prognosis, previous treatment, and patient preferences.

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes associated with influenza-related hospitalization during pregnancy: a population-based matched cohort study in Suzhou, China, 2018-2024.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.authors: Wang R, Sun J, Wang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physiological and immunological changes render pregnant women susceptible to influenza, leading to increased risks of severe illness and adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes are major causes of perinatal mortality and morbidity, and fetal deaths (including miscarriage and stillbirth) pose a major public health challenge. However, population-based cohort studies on this topic, particularly from China, remain scarce. Therefore, clarifying the association between influenza infection and adverse pregnancy outcomes is critical for optimizing antenatal care and reducing maternal-neonatal risks.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based matched cohort study among pregnant women in Suzhou, China, from October 2018 to September 2024, based on active surveillance of influenza-related acute respiratory or febrile illness (ARFI) hospitalizations. Exposed groups were RT-PCR-confirmed influenza infections among hospitalized ARFI pregnant women, excluding those with delivery outside Jiangsu Province, miscarriage or stillbirth in the current pregnancy, repeated ARFI-related hospitalizations during the same pregnancy, multiple gestations, or already postpartum at ARFI admission. Unexposed groups were selected from the same source population, matched 1:4 by age, last menstrual period, gravidity, and parity, excluding those with any ARFI hospitalization, delivery outside Jiangsu Province, miscarriage or stillbirth in the current pregnancy, or multiple gestation. For preterm birth analysis, we included only exposed women with gestational age 28-37 weeks and their matched controls. For term outcomes (macrosomia, term low birth weight (TLBW), small for gestational age (SGA), large for gestational age (LGA), high-risk infants, frail infants, 1-min Apgar < 7, and neonatal resuscitation), we excluded preterm births and their matched group to avoid confounding. Associations were estimated using generalized estimating equations (GEE) with logit link, clustering by matched-set identifier, and stratified by infection trimester, reporting odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: A total of 4275 pregnant women were enrolled in this study, including 855 in the exposed group and 3420 in the unexposed group. In the full cohort, influenza-related hospitalization during pregnancy was significantly associated with increased risks of preterm birth (aOR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.42-2.66), TLBW (aOR = 2.40, 95% CI: 1.08-5.37), LGA (aOR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.13-1.65),…

articles.title: Synthetic cannabinoid exposure and the male reproductive system: A review of disruptive mechanisms in preclinical models.
articles.authors: Ajayi AF, Amos VO, Ojetunde AO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Synthetic cannabinoids (SCBs) are structurally and pharmacologically heterogeneous compounds. Although their acute toxicities are well described, evidence concerning male reproductive effects remains limited. This review synthesizes compound-specific preclinical findings and available human evidence, emphasizing exposure validity, study quality, and measured versus inferred mechanisms.
METHODS: A narrative review was conducted using Google Scholar, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Web of Science, and CrossRef. Studies evaluating male reproductive endpoints following exposure to defined SCBs or relevant street preparations were prioritized. Given the limited and heterogeneous evidence, a structured qualitative appraisal incorporating relevant SYRCLE risk-of-bias domains and exposure-model applicability was undertaken without quantitative scoring or meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Reproductive evidence was identified for HU-210, JWH-018, AB-FUBINACA, CUMYL-4CN-BINACA, and the incompletely characterized street preparation Strox. Reported findings included alterations in sperm parameters, testosterone, testicular histology, redox and inflammatory biomarkers, apoptosis-associated proteins, and mitochondrial-complex protein expression. Findings varied by compound, dose, duration, and model. Most purified compounds were administered intraperitoneally to rodents, limiting translation to typical human exposure. No included study demonstrated infertility using mating, pregnancy, fertilization, embryo development, litter size, or live birth outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence indicates preliminary, compound-specific signals of male reproductive toxicity in preclinical models but does not establish a uniform SCB class effect, a linear causal mechanism, greater reproductive toxicity than Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol, or male infertility. Analytically confirmed human studies and more representative exposure models are required before clinical or regulatory fertility recommendations can be supported.

articles.title: Targeted Probe-Capture Sequencing of Maternal Plasma Cell-Free DNA for Noninvasive Fetal ABO Blood Group Prediction.
articles.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
articles.authors: Hao H, Shen J, Lou C et al.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive fetal ABO blood group prediction can be performed by using cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from maternal plasma, which contains a fetal-derived fraction known as cell-free fetal DNA. However, accurate analysis of cell-free fetal DNA is challenging because fetal-derived fragments are short, low in abundance, and diluted within a predominant maternal DNA background. A targeted probe-capture next-generation sequencing workflow was developed by using magnetic bead-purified maternal plasma cfDNA for fetal ABO prediction in maternal type O singleton pregnancies. The assay combines liquid-phase hybridization capture of ABO-defining regions with 1090 autosomal single-nucleotide polymorphisms for fetal fraction estimation, maternal background discrimination, and internal sequencing quality control. Maternal FUT1 and FUT2 genotyping was additionally incorporated in available residual samples as an auxiliary quality control step to assess potential interference from H-deficient phenotypes. Among 51 enrolled pregnancies, neonatal heel-prick serologic validation was available for 33 cases. Complete concordance was observed between next-generation sequencing-based fetal ABO prediction and neonatal serology, including 9 type A, 11 type B, and 13 type O neonates. The mean fetal fraction was 9.23% (range, 5.05% to 16.34%), and all validated samples exceeded the 4% quality control threshold. In 28 maternal residual samples, FUT1/FUT2 genotyping provided no genetic evidence suggestive of Bombay or para-Bombay phenotypes. Together, these results support targeted capture next-generation sequencing of maternal plasma cfDNA as a feasible module for fetal ABO prediction within the NIPT2.0 framework.

articles.title: Deep learning-based estimation of multi-tracer PET phenotypes from structural MRI for A/T/N-related analysis and progression prediction in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.authors: Xie W, Pan X, Zhan Y et al.
articles.abstract: Early identification and staging of Alzheimer's disease (AD) require integrated assessment of amyloid deposition, tau pathology, and neurodegeneration. PET provides spatially resolved in vivo imaging biomarkers, but its routine use is constrained by cost, tracer availability, and radiation exposure, limiting access to complete A/T/N imaging profiles. We propose a conditional flow matching-based framework that estimates SUV-space PET-derived phenotypes related to 18F-FDG, 18F-florbetapir and 18F-flortaucipir from a single T1-weighted MRI scan. To address limitations in SUV-level quantitative fidelity, single-tracer applicability, and external generalization, the framework combines a PET prior network with a time-conditioned velocity network and uses multi-constraint losses to preserve SUV accuracy, regional uptake consistency, and anatomical boundaries. The model was developed using 1978 paired ADNI MRI-PET records from 991 participants and evaluated in a predefined ADNI test set and an independent hospital PET/MR cohort of 514 participants. In ADNI, voxel-level MAEs were 0.012, 0.034, and 0.021 SUV, with representative ROI Pearson correlations of 0.978, 0.842, and 0.781. In the hospital cohort, corresponding MAEs were 0.014, 0.037, and 0.024 SUV, with ROI correlations of 0.952, 0.803, and 0.834. In OASIS, generated PET-derived features improved CDR stratification and future cognitive decline prediction, increasing AUCs from 0.662 to 0.739 and from 0.569 to 0.643. These findings suggest that the method can provide PET-derived phenotypes related to A/T/N analysis from structural MRI when PET is unavailable, but should not be interpreted as a replacement for molecular PET assessment.

articles.title: Interpregnancy interval and the risk of adverse perinatal outcomes of singleton pregnancies: a retrospective analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Bu X, Ye W, Zhang M et al.
articles.abstract: This retrospective study analyzed 3,568,957 singleton live births from the US National Vital Statistics System (2021-2022) to evaluate adverse perinatal outcomes (preterm birth, low birth weight, small for gestational age) using interpregnancy interval (IPI) as a continuous variable. Departing from conventional categorical classifications, we treated IPI as a continuous monthly variable to precisely delineate the full risk trajectory. Spline smoothing and logistic regression revealed that an IPI of 20 months had the lowest risk. Compared to this nadir, IPI <6 months increased odds by 44% (adjusted odds ratio=1.44, 95% CI 1.40-1.48) and IPI >120 months increased odds by 74% (aOR=1.74, 95% CI 1.70-1.78). Risk and incidence charts were generated for IPI as a continuous measure, including subgroups by prior preterm birth or cesarean section. Our findings confirm that both short and long IPIs are associated with elevated perinatal risks, with 20 months emerging as the optimal interval for subsequent pregnancy planning. These continuous-risk charts offer an evidence-based, practical resource to enhance prenatal counseling and family education.

articles.title: Association of age at menopause with incident depressive disorders in women: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wu N, Wang Z, Zhang H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the association between age at menopause and the subsequent development of depression.
METHODS: This study included 37,754 postmenopausal women from the UK Biobank. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between age at menopause and depression risk, and multivariable-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to evaluate the dose-response relationship. Sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 14.91 ± 3.04 years, 698 participants developed depression. RCS analysis showed a significant linear dose-response relationship between age at menopause and the risk of depressive disorders; each 1-year increase in age at menopause was associated with a 3.5% lower risk of incident depressive disorders (HR = 0.965, 95% CI: 0.947-0.983, P < 0.001). With 50 years as the reference, women who experienced menopause at age 45 years had a 17.3% higher risk (HR = 1.173, 95% CI: 1.031-1.333, P = 0.015), whereas those who experienced menopause at age 55 years had a 20.3% lower risk (HR = 0.797, 95% CI: 0.642-0.989, P = 0.039). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings. Stratified analyses showed that the protective association of age at menopause was more pronounced among participants with hypertension, whereas hormone replacement therapy did not significantly modify the association.
CONCLUSIONS: Age at menopause was significantly associated with the risk of new-onset depression in a linear dose-response manner, with a younger age at menopause associated with a higher risk of depressive disorders.

articles.title: Increased stillbirth risk associated with heatwave exposure in late pregnancy: evidence from a 3.8 million mother-infant birth cohort.
articles.authors: Fang J, Liu Y, Jiang Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite growing evidence linking extreme temperature to adverse birth outcomes, the nexus between heatwaves and stillbirth remains unstudied in low- and middle-income settings. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the effects of different heatwave types on stillbirth risk in an Iranian birth cohort.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis using national data from Iran, encompassing 3.84 million singleton birth records across 749 hospitals in 31 provinces (2013-2018). Heatwaves based on mean temperature (MeanT-HW), maximum temperature (daytime heatwave, DHW), minimum temperature (nighttime heatwave, NHW) and day-night compound heatwave (CHW) were defined as combinations of multiple durations (2, 3, and 4 days) and temperature percentile thresholds (P90, P92.5, P95 and P97.5). The cumulative excess heatwave index (CEHWI) was used to assess the cumulative intensity of heat exposure by summing the daily deviations of mean temperature above the predefined threshold during heatwave events. Logistic regression models were employed to separately investigate the associations of stillbirth risk with distinct heatwave exposures under multiple gestational exposure windows. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify population-specific susceptibility stratified by maternal characteristics including age, educational level and residence as well as infant gender.
RESULTS: Among 3.84 million singleton births (maternal age 28.1 ± 5.8 years), 27,778 stillbirths were identified (28.8 ± 6.5 years). We observed consistent evidence for the effects of MeanT-HW and CEHWI on elevated stillbirth risk in late pregnancy, and the estimated odds ranged from 1.013 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.001-1.025) under P92.5_2d to 1.040 (95% CI: 1.011-1.070) under P97.5_4d for each additional MeanT-HW day and from 1.012 (95% CI: 1.000-1.025) under P95_3d to 1.034 (95% CI: 1.001-1.069) under P97.5_4d for each 1-°C increase in CEHWI during the last week before delivery. Moreover, CHW was associated with greater odds of stillbirth than both DHW and NHW. During the last week before delivery, the excess risks per 1-day increase in exposure reached up to 3.4% (95% CI: 0.5%-6.4%) for DHW under P97.5_3d, 4.3% (95% CI: 1.0%-7.8%) for NHW under P97.5_4d, and 14.2% (95% CI: 4.7%-24.6%) for CHW under P97.5_4d. Subgroup analysis suggested a greater heatwave-related estimates among urban residents compared with rural counterparts.
CONCLUSIONS: This birth cohort study suggested…

articles.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics exposure impairs human trophoblast cell functions and induces miscarriage via activating circRHOBTB3/miR-135a/EGR1 axis.
articles.authors: Wang X, Zhao L, Gou J et al.
articles.abstract: Plastic pollution has become a global environmental problem, leading to the widespread presence of nanoplastics (NPs) in the natural environment, which poses a potential threat to human reproductive health. However, the toxic effects and underlying mechanisms of polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) on unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion (URSA) remain largely elusive. In this study, we exposed human trophoblast HTR-8/SVneo cells and pregnant CD-1 mice to 50 nm PS-NPs to explore reproductive toxic effects and molecular mechanisms. In vivo, maternal exposure to 100 mg/kg PS-NPs via oral gavage significantly increased fetal resorption rate and reduced placental weight in mice. In vitro, PS-NPs inhibited proliferation, migration and invasion of HTR-8/SVneo cells, while promoting apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. Transcriptomic analysis and validation revealed that circRHOBTB3 was significantly upregulated in villous tissues of URSA patients and PS-NPs-exposed trophoblast cells. Mechanistically, PS-NPs activated the circRHOBTB3/miR-135a/EGR1 signaling axis in trophoblast cells: circRHOBTB3 may serve as a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) and potentially interact with miR-135a, thereby possibly relieving the post-transcriptional repression of EGR1 and ultimately inducing trophoblast cell dysfunction. Functional rescue experiments confirmed that knockdown of circRHOBTB3 reversed PS-NPs-induced trophoblast cell damage. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that environmental PS-NPs exposure is a potential risk factor for URSA, and uncover a novel circRHOBTB3-mediated regulatory mechanism underlying PS-NPs-induced trophoblast reproductive toxicity, providing potential therapeutic targets for NP-related unexplained miscarriage.

articles.title: Arsenic exposure in association with reproductive hormones, kisspeptin, and age at menarche in European teenagers.
articles.authors: Cox B, Iszatt N, Hassen HY et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arsenic is a widespread environmental contaminant with known toxic effects, but its impact on adolescent reproductive development, a critical window for endocrine regulation, is not well understood.
OBJECTIVES: We studied associations between arsenic species levels and reproductive development markers in European teenagers, focusing on reproductive hormones, kisspeptin, and pubertal timing.
METHODS: Harmonized biomonitoring data from five European countries within the Human Biomonitoring for Europe (HBM4EU) initiative included 1139 teenagers (12-18 years) with data on at least one arsenic species and one reproductive marker. Urinary arsenic species, arsenite [As(III)], arsenate [As(V)], monomethylarsonic acid [MMA], dimethylarsinic acid [DMA], arsenobetaine [AsB], total arsenic [TAS] and toxicologically relevant arsenic [TRA], were measured and normalised for specific gravity. Reproductive markers included serum levels of luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), and total testosterone (TT) in boys only, kisspeptin in both sexes, and age at menarche in girls. Associations were estimated using linear regression, adjusting for confounders.
RESULTS: In boys, pooled analyses based on two studies (n = 191) showed a nominal positive association between As(V) and FSH (geometric mean ratio [GMR] for detectable versus non-detectable As(V): 1.24; 95% CI: 1.02, 1.51), while higher DMA and TRA concentrations were associated with higher SHBG (GMRs per interquartile fold change [IQFc] in exposure: 1.09-1.10). A similar association was observed for TAS measured, although this estimate was based on a single study only (n = 140). A suggestive positive association was observed between As(V) and TT based on three studies (n = 239). Serum kisspeptin levels were 70.0 pg/mL (95% CI: 6.4, 133.6) and 80 pg/mL (95% CI: 18.7, 141.3) higher per IQFc in AsB and TAS sum, respectively, based on two studies (n = 192). In girls, higher DMA was associated with later menarche (three studies; n = 312; +0.18 years per IQFc; 95% CI: 0.01, 0.36), and a similar trend was observed for TRA (two studies; n = 200). A suggestive positive association was also noted between As(V) and kisspeptin (three studies; n = 268).
CONCLUSIONS: Several arsenic biomarkers showed nominal associations with reproductive hormone concentrations, kisspeptin levels and age at menarche. However, none of these associations remained statistically…

articles.title: Vertical homogenization and legacy sinks of phthalate esters in arid artificial oasis agricultural soils: Implications for long-term management.
articles.authors: Zhai H, Yang X, Liu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Intensive plastic mulching and agrochemical use in arid oasis agroecosystems exacerbate phthalate ester (PAEs) pollution. However, conventional topsoil monitoring (e.g., 0-20 cm) systematically underestimates deeper soil burdens. This study investigated the occurrence, source apportionment, and health risks of nine PAEs across the 0-60 cm soil profile at 107 agricultural sites in Northwest China. Σ9PAEs exhibited consistent vertical homogenization (averaging 154-159 μg/kg) across the 0-60 cm profile, dominated by di-n-butyl phthalate (DBP) and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP). Regional practices like deep tillage and mulched drip irrigation likely facilitate this downward migration, which may contribute to a deep-profile legacy sink. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed strong within-site clustering across the profile (ICC = 0.83), with substantially greater variation among sites than among depth layers within a site; although current single-season mulching was associated with a detectable concentration elevation (P < 0.001), its contribution remained small relative to long-term cumulative accumulation. Positive matrix factorization (PMF) further identified agricultural activities (agrochemicals and agricultural plastic) accounting for 73.82% of the total pollution inventory. Although current health risks remain within regulatory thresholds, PAEs accumulation in the 20-60 cm subsurface colocalizes with the deep-rooted crop uptake zones, which may shift the primary human exposure route from direct soil contact to food-chain pathways under this deterministic framework. Supported by sensitivity analysis, dietary exposure was the dominant relative pathway in the screening model, accounting for >99.9% of the total estimated risk under the deterministic BAF-based framework. These findings indicate that while halting plastic film usage is indispensable for preventing new inputs, it must be paired with deep-soil remediation strategies to effectively mitigate the entrenched legacy burden. A paradigm shift from topsoil monitoring to comprehensive deep-profile regulation and long-term source reduction is imperative to safeguard agricultural sustainability in arid regions.

articles.title: Applications of intravenous magnesium Sulfate in the emergency department: A narrative review.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.authors: Santiago R, Krenz J, Szczesniak P et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intravenous (IV) magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) has a variety of indications within the emergency department (ED) with evidence for its use continuing to evolve. It is used for common presentations such as headache/migraine, arrhythmias, severe respiratory exacerbations, and refractory hypokalemia while remaining the mainstay of treatment for preeclampsia/eclampsia. Evidence also supports its use for the management of shivering during targeted temperature management and a potential role for analgesia.
OBJECTIVE: The focus of this review is to provide an update on the literature regarding the use of IV MgSO4 for common presentations in the ED for adults and provide an evidence-based approach to its utilization.
DISCUSSION: The most robust trials suggest that IV MgSO4 serves a supporting role in the management of headache/migraine and may be used as an adjunct for rate control in patients with atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate. Magnesium sulfate should be reserved for patients experiencing severe respiratory exacerbations who fail to respond to initial therapy and may have a role in patients experiencing shivering during targeted temperature management. Routine empiric use in the management of hypokalemia is not suggested and evidence supporting its use for analgesia is limited. Intravenous MgSO4 remains first-line for preeclampsia/eclampsia and is the drug of choice in Torsades de Pointes. There was a low risk of adverse events across all studies evaluated with no serious events reported.
CONCLUSION: Intravenous MgSO4 is an adjunct for a myriad of indications in the ED. Additional high-quality research is needed to identify patients who benefit most from IV MgSO4.

articles.title: Sociodemographic predictors of postpartum anticoagulant selection in pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism.
articles.authors: Ladha A, Pugliese M, Skeith L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) requires anticoagulation into the postpartum period that overlaps with breastfeeding initiation. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) and vitamin K antagonists (VKA) are compatible with breastfeeding, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are currently not recommended. Postpartum anticoagulant selection may be influenced by safety, convenience and access, potentially contributing to racial and socioeconomic inequities in care. We evaluated the impact of race and sociodemographic factors on postpartum anticoagulant selection in a publicly funded healthcare system.
METHODS: This is a population-based cohort study using linked administrative health data in Ontario, Canada. We included Ontario Drug Benefit (ODB) recipients with pregnancy-associated VTE diagnosed between 2012 and 2022 who received ≥1 anticoagulant prescription within 6 months postpartum. Primary outcome was the exclusive receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulants (LMWH/VKA). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) were determined to identify factors associated with breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant use.
RESULTS: Of 113 ODB-eligible individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE, 62.8% received ≥6 weeks of postpartum anticoagulation. During the 6-month postpartum period, 25.7% transitioned to a DOAC. No significant association was observed between race and receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulation. However, individuals in the most materially deprived neighbourhoods were significantly less likely to receive a breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant compared with those in less deprived areas (aOR 0.20, 95% CI 0.07-0.58).
CONCLUSIONS: In this population-based cohort, 1 in 4 individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE received a DOAC within 6 months postpartum. Postpartum anticoagulant selection was affected by socioeconomic status. These findings highlight the need to explore structural factors influencing anticoagulant selection to advance equitable postpartum care.

articles.title: Applications of peptide-drug conjugates in paclitaxel delivery: New perspectives for Cancer therapy and drug design.
articles.authors: Pan W, Chen X, Li M et al.
articles.abstract: Paclitaxel (PTX) is a classical chemotherapeutic agent widely used for breast cancer, ovarian cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and other malignancies. However, its clinical application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, non-specific biodistribution, systemic toxicity, and drug resistance. Peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs) have attracted increasing attention as a promising strategy to improve PTX delivery. In peptide-PTX conjugates peptides are linked to PTX through rationally designed linkers. Targeting peptides recognize specific receptors on tumor cell surfaces and enhance tumor selectivity, whereas cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) promote transmembrane transport, intracellular uptake, and tissue penetration. In addition, enzyme-sensitive peptides and optimized linkers enable selective drug release within the tumor microenvironment, whereas bifunctional peptides integrate multiple delivery functions and improve pharmacological efficacy. This review summarizes recent advances in peptide-PTX conjugates, focusing on the roles of peptide moieties, linker design, receptor-mediated targeting, intracellular delivery, and controlled PTX release. Current challenges, including peptide sequence optimization, release control, drug resistance, and clinical translation, are also discussed to provide guidance for the rational development of PTX-based PDCs.

articles.title: Electrochemical aptasensor for the detection of placental growth factor protein as a biomarker of preeclampsia using a boron-doped diamond electrode.
articles.authors: Nevada BAN, Zakiyyah SN, Swara RR et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a serious pregnancy complication associated with hypertension and endothelial dysfunction caused by impaired placental vascularization. Early detection is essential to reduce maternal and fetal risks. Placental growth factor (PlGF), a pro-angiogenic biomarker that decreases significantly in preeclampsia, is a promising target for early diagnosis. This study develops a gold-modified boron-doped diamond (BDD/Au) electrochemical aptasensor for sensitive and selective PlGF detection. The selected aptamer is determined based on 3D structure modeling and molecular docking results, followed by electrode fabrication, aptamer immobilization, and characterization using SEM, XPS, CV, EIS, and DPV. The selected aptamer exhibits a docking score of -288.41 and a confidence score of 0.9155. The aptasensor shows a signal-off response, with current decreasing as PlGF concentration increases. It demonstrates excellent linearity (R2 = 0.9952) over 1-10,000 fg/mL, with limits of detection of 2.10 fg/mL in PBS and 2.58 fg/mL in spiked human serum. Selectivity studies against various interfering species show 96.85% selectivity and 83.94% specificity toward PlGF, confirming specific aptamer-target recognition. These findings demonstrate that the BDD/Au aptasensor is a highly sensitive and selective platform with strong potential for early preeclampsia diagnosis.

articles.title: Peripartum echocardiographic findings in preeclampsia and their association with subsequent hypertension.
articles.authors: Alhuneafat L, Puttur A, Williams BA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia, a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, predisposes women to long-term cardiovascular risk, especially future hypertension. We examined whether peripartum echocardiographic measures were associated with subsequent hypertension among women with preeclampsia without pre-pregnancy chronic hypertension.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective study of 252 women with preeclampsia and 222 normotensive pregnant controls who underwent echocardiography between 20 weeks' gestation and 30 days postpartum within a single integrated health system (2016-2022).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Incident hypertension during follow-up (through mid-2023), defined by a new diagnosis of hypertension, systolic blood pressure (BP) >135 mmHg on a recorded visit, diastolic BP >85 mmHg, or initiation of antihypertensive medication. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify echocardiographic and clinical predictors of subsequent hypertension.
RESULTS: Among 474 pregnant women followed for a mean of 2.3 years, 119 of 252 (47.2%) preeclampsia women and 9 of 222 (4.1%) controls met criteria for hypertension. Among women with preeclampsia, 85% had severe features. Eighteen of 26 echocardiographic measures differed significantly between preeclampsia and control groups. In adjusted models limited to women with preeclampsia, both interventricular septal thickness at end-diastole (IVSd) and left ventricular mass index (LVMi) were independently associated with the development of hypertension (IVSd OR = 1.37 per 0.1 cm, p < 0.01; LVMi OR = 1.15 per 10 g/m2, p = 0.04). LVMi greater than 95 g/m2 was associated with a more than threefold higher odds of developing hypertension.
CONCLUSION: Peripartum echocardiography may provide additional insight for identifying women at higher risk for future hypertension, allowing for closer follow-up and early intervention.

articles.title: Variation in baseline estrogen levels, menopause-related adverse events and early study discontinuation among women on the placebo-controlled MAP.3 exemestane prevention trial.
articles.authors: Ho V, Pasquet R, Singh RJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer prevention has been demonstrated using aromatase inhibitors (AIs) including exemestane, but menopause-related adverse events can limit adherence. We hypothesized that estrogens are potential biomarkers that could be measured at baseline to predict the probability of AI-related adverse events.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Estrone (E1) and estradiol (E2) levels were measured from Mammary Prevention 3 trial baseline serum samples (n = 4111) using liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry. Hot flashes, fatigue, and joint pain were assessed using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v4.0. Severe toxicity (grade ≥3) and moderate toxicity (grade ≥2) were contrasted with less severe toxicity. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) for each symptom (years 1 and 5) and baseline E1 and E2 levels.
RESULTS: Women on exemestane with the highest levels of E1 or E2 at baseline were significantly more likely to develop severe hot flashes (E1: ORyr-1 = 3.8, 95% CI 1.6-10.5) and (E2: ORyr-1 = 4.2, 95% CI 1.6-13.1) compared with women in the lowest quartile, with a clear dose-response observed at year 1. Severe joint pain was associated with higher baseline E1 and E2 levels in women on exemestane at year 1 but was only statistically significant for E1 (quartiles 2 and 3). There were no significant associations in the placebo group. Women in the highest quartile of E1 or E2 were significantly more likely to discontinue protocol therapy within the first 12 months, independent of assigned treatment, compared with women in the lowest quartile.
CONCLUSIONS: Postmenopausal women with elevated estrogen levels who initiate exemestane are at greater risk for the development of severe hot flashes and joint pain and may benefit from measures to limit early discontinuation.

articles.title: Early and premature menopause and brain health across the adult lifespan: a scoping review of neuroimaging and neuropathological outcomes.
articles.authors: Watts A, Lewis G, McDaniel M et al.
articles.abstract: Early-onset menopause may have detrimental impacts on brain health, yet mechanisms underlying this association are poorly understood. This scoping review synthesizes findings linking early and premature menopause to brain health across adulthood, including brain volume, function, and pathology. We conducted a scoping review using Covidence literature review software with a comprehensive search strategy using search terms related to early and premature menopause and brain health. The authors independently mapped study details onto a data-extraction tool to ensure inter-rater agreement. We reviewed 21 studies sorted into two categories by primary exposure: 1) early age at menopause (n = 10), and 2) premenopausal bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (PBSO) (n = 11). Nine of the 10 papers that focused on early age at menopause reported at least one association with poorer brain outcomes, including smaller volumes and greater pathology. Brain regions reported to be associated with earlier menopause in multiple studies included the medial temporal lobe (i.e., hippocampus and parahippocampus). Multiple studies observed associations with lower total gray matter volume and poorer white matter integrity. Among papers that focused on PBSO, 7 reported worse brain outcomes and 4 originating from the same parent study reported results that were not easily characterized in terms of our hypothesis (i.e., group differences were attributable to the interactions of estrogen use, age, or other factors with PBSO). Despite inconsistency in definitions, methodologies, and populations of interest, over three-quarters of papers we reviewed reported poorer brain health associated with premature and early menopause. Studies did not consistently evaluate or interpret these associations in terms of potential confounders or mechanistic explanations. Future research would benefit from studies designed to evaluate underlying neural mechanisms and increased measurement accuracy for menopause type and timing.

articles.title: Recovery and SNP genotyping of nuclear DNA from hair shafts using hybridization capture.
articles.authors: Lewis EJ, Ostojic A, Millis GL et al.
articles.abstract: Hair strands are frequently recovered from crime scenes but rarely undergo nuclear DNA analysis because shed hair shafts contain low quantities of highly degraded DNA. This study evaluated a workflow designed to improve DNA recovery from rootless human hair, enrich targeted single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) through hybridization capture, and generate accurate genotypes following massively parallel sequencing. A modified cell-free extraction method was selected for its efficiency and reliability. The recovered DNA fragments were larger than previously reported for hair shafts and exhibited a multimodal size distribution similar to that observed in plasma-derived cell-free DNA. Sequencing libraries were prepared from 20 to 700 pg of hair shaft DNA collected from 21 donors. Libraries underwent two rounds of hybridization capture using a custom oligonucleotide panel targeting SNPs informative for forensic investigations. Following sequencing, autosomal SNP coverage was proportional to DNA input and ranged from 7% to 90% of targeted loci. Hair shaft genotypes were compared with corresponding buccal reference genotypes using both threshold-based methods and likelihood ratio analyses with FamLink2. In all comparisons, the likelihood ratios provided extremely strong support for the correct hypothesis, supporting the same-source hypothesis for true donor comparisons and the unrelated-source hypothesis for non-donor comparisons, including samples prepared from less than 50 pg of hair shaft DNA. These findings demonstrate that cell-free DNA-based extraction combined with targeted hybridization capture and sequencing can generate accurate and highly informative nuclear genotypes from shed human hairs.

articles.title: BEHOLD phase 3 clinical development program of mocertatug rezetecan in ovarian and endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Hurteau J, Grayeski M, Dixon J
articles.abstract: Mocertatug rezetecan (Mo-Rez; GSK5733584) is a B7-H4-targeting antibody-drug conjugate comprising a humanized anti-B7-H4 monoclonal antibody linked to the topoisomerase I inhibitor rezetecan. In the Phase 1 BEHOLD-1 study (NCT06431594), Mo-Rez demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (objective response rate [ORR], 62%) and recurrent/advanced endometrial cancer (ORR, 67%), supporting further clinical evaluation in Phase 3 studies. The global BEHOLD Phase 3 clinical program consists of five randomized studies evaluating Mo-Rez across ovarian and endometrial cancer treatment settings, with approximately 3,070 patients planned for enrollment. The ovarian cancer studies evaluate platinum-resistant disease (BEHOLD-Ovarian01, NCT07286266), platinum-sensitive disease (BEHOLD-Ovarian02, NCT076684612), and first-line maintenance for non-homologous recombination deficient disease (BEHOLD-Ovarian03, NCT07694427). The endometrial cancer studies evaluate previously treated advanced/recurrent disease (BEHOLD-Endometrial01, NCT07286331) and first-line maintenance for mismatch repair proficient disease (BEHOLD-Endometrial02, NCT07684599). Primary endpoints include progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), depending on study design. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include safety, pharmacokinetics, biomarkers, immunogenicity, and quality-of-life assessments. Collectively, the BEHOLD program evaluates three therapeutic strategies: replacement of conventional chemotherapy with a B7-H4-directed ADC, combination approaches with bevacizumab or immune checkpoint inhibitors, and use of Mo-Rez as maintenance therapy. Tumor tissue collection across studies enables prospective evaluation of B7-H4 expression and other biomarkers as predictors of clinical benefit. The BEHOLD program represents a comprehensive Phase 3 clinical development effort designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Mo-Rez across multiple ovarian and endometrial cancer settings and to further characterize the clinical relevance of B7-H4 as a therapeutic target in gynecologic malignancies.

articles.title: Maternal and fetal anesthetic management during in utero embolization for fetal vein of Galen malformation: a case series.
articles.authors: Seifert SM, Roth J, Guidugli T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In utero embolization for fetal vein of Galen malformation is a novel ultrasound-guided transuterine, transcranial fetal neurointervention. We describe the anesthetic management for this procedure.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of the anesthetic management of patients undergoing in utero vein of Galen malformation embolization at a fetal surgery program. Maternal and fetal anesthetic techniques and perioperative complications were assessed using descriptive statistics.
RESULTS: Nine patients underwent attempted embolization. Combined spinal-epidural anesthesia was employed in all cases, with conversion to general anesthesia in one. Fetal anesthesia consisted of intramuscular fentanyl, rocuronium, and atropine. Complications included fetal bradycardia and emergent delivery.
CONCLUSIONS: Fetal vein of Galen malformation embolization can be performed under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia with general anesthesia in reserve. Direct fetal anesthesia provides analgesia and immobility. Multidisciplinary maternal-fetal anesthetic coordination and preparedness for emergent delivery are essential. These findings provide guidance for anesthetic management of this novel procedure.

articles.title: Measuring the Utility of Prenatal Exome Sequencing Using the Clinician-Reported Genetic Testing Utility InDEx for Prenatal Care: A Retrospective Multicentre Study.
articles.authors: Hayeems RZ, Luca S, Xiao B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the diagnostic and clinical utility of prenatal exome sequencing (ES) in a cohort of pregnancies using the Clinician-reported Genetic testing Utility InDEx for Prenatal Care (C-GUIDE Prenatal).
METHODS: Cases that met criteria for prenatal ES in Ontario, Canada were identified in 5 clinics. Clinicians assessed the utility of ES using C-GUIDE Prenatal, a clinician-reported measure of how genetic testing informs pregnancy and neonatal management. Case characteristics were summarized descriptively. C-GUIDE Prenatal total scores were calculated and regressed against clinically important variables using generalised estimating equations.
RESULTS: Among 115 cases, the diagnostic yield was 41.7%. The mean C-GUIDE Prenatal score was 9.48 (SD 11.51). Compared with negative results, informative positive results were associated with an increase in C-GUIDE Prenatal score of 17.6 (p < 0.001). Compared to meeting one criterion for ES, meeting ≥ 3 criteria was associated with an increase in C-GUIDE Prenatal score of 3.8 (p < 0.05). Compared with pregnancies that were not ongoing at result disclosure, ongoing pregnancy was associated with an increase in the C-GUIDE Prenatal score of 2.8 (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Findings address a knowledge gap in the clinical value evidence base that informs policy and funding decision-making for prenatal genetic testing.

articles.title: The Content and Role of an Online Support Group for Parents of an Unborn Baby With a Diagnosis of Spina Bifida Considering Fetal Surgery: A Qualitative Analysis.
articles.authors: Gallagher K, David AL, Marlow N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore concerns discussed in a closed online support group for parents considering open fetal surgery for their unborn baby diagnosed with open spina bifida.
METHODS: Thematic analysis was used to analyze data from a UK-based closed Facebook (Facebook.com) parent support group. Two researchers were granted access to the group for two weeks (commencing 18/11/2021 and 18/1/2022) and manually extracted posts and comments from consenting participants from the group's inception (04/2019) until October 2021.
RESULTS: We extracted 659 unique posts from 41 members. Thematic analysis using inductive coding identified three overarching themes representing discussions relating to (1) maternal physical and psychological support; (2) navigating ongoing child health and development; and (3) decision-making and preparation for fetal surgery. Subthemes within each were related to (1) preoperative and postoperative maternal health, finances, emotional support, and community building; (2) preoperative planning and support, information needs, and decision-making; and (3) child development, health concerns, and access to resources.
CONCLUSION: Parental concerns when considering or opting for fetal surgery encompass topics beyond current counseling. Our observations should enhance pre-surgical counseling and prompt the provision of additional information to support families throughout their pregnancy, before and after surgery, and in the ongoing care of their child.

articles.title: Sociodemographic Variation in Prenatal Aneuploidy Screening and First-Line Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing: A Multicentre Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Pynaker C, Marzan M, Lewis S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine prenatal aneuploidy screening uptake and modality in a high-income setting where non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is recommended but remains self-funded, and to investigate variation by sociodemographic and clinical characteristics.
METHOD: We conducted a retrospective multi-centre study of women who gave birth at ≥ 20 weeks' gestation across 11 public hospitals in Melbourne, Australia from 2022-2024. Maternity and pregnancy covariates were collected from routine maternity hospital databases.
RESULT: Of 102,729 women, screening data were available for 80,355 (78.2%); 66,343 (82.6%) had aneuploidy screening, 12,632 (15.7%) declined, and 1380 (1.7%) were not offered screening. Women who declined screening were more likely to be younger (< 30 years), multiparous, or migrants from specific regions. Among screened women, NIPT was the predominant modality (80.6%, n = 53,475), followed by combined first trimester screening (16.6%, n = 10,991) and second trimester serum screening (2.5%, n = 1634). NIPT uptake increased from 75.3% in the most disadvantaged regions to 88.9% in the most advantaged regions and remained associated with socioeconomic advantage after adjustment (aIRR 1.09, 95% CI 1.06-1.13 for most advantaged vs. most disadvantaged regions).
CONCLUSION: NIPT was the predominant screening modality; however, its uptake was strongly associated with socioeconomic advantage, suggesting variation in uptake of the most accurate aneuploidy screening test in Australia.

articles.title: Healthy Lifestyle Score and the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease, Cancer, and Mortality in an Asian Population: Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Park SH, Ho PJ, Liang X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthy lifestyle behaviors are key modifiable factors for the prevention of chronic diseases and premature mortality. Composite lifestyle scores provide a practical framework for capturing the combined impact of multiple health behaviors, but prospective evidence from multiethnic Asian populations remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the associations between a composite healthy lifestyle score and the risk of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and all-cause mortality in a multiethnic Asian population.
METHODS: We analyzed prospective data from 9920 participants of the Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort who were free of major chronic diseases at baseline. A healthy lifestyle score was constructed from 5 components: BMI, smoking, physical activity, diet quality, and screen time. Scores ranged from 0 to 10, with higher scores reflecting healthier lifestyles. An expanded score, including mental well-being, was examined in a subset. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs were estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), stroke, cancer, and all-cause mortality, adjusting for sociodemographic factors, energy intake, family history of cancer or heart disease, and menopause status.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 14 years, 457 AMI cases, 322 stroke cases, 707 cancer incident cases, and 631 deaths were identified. More favorable lifestyle scores were associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes and mortality, consistent with a dose-response relationship. Compared to participants scoring 8 to 10, those with the lowest score (0-3) had more than 2 times the risk of AMI (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.47-3.07), stroke (HR 3.21, 95% CI 2.12-4.85), and all-cause mortality (HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.46-2.78). In contrast, no significant associations were observed for cancer incidence. Incorporating mental well-being into the lifestyle score yielded similar results.
CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to a healthy lifestyle was associated with a lower risk of AMI, stroke, and mortality in a multiethnic Asian cohort, highlighting the importance of integrated lifestyle approaches for chronic disease prevention.

articles.title: Short-term additive effect of posterior tibial nerve stimulation in neurogenic detrusor overactivity among incomplete spinal cord injury patients on antimuscarinic therapy: A prospective study.
articles.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
articles.authors: Sajeev A, Kataruka M, Ghosh N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the short-term additive effect of transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) in patients with incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI) with neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) receiving antimuscarinic therapy.
DESIGN: All 29 patients with urinary incontinence underwent a baseline cystometry followed by a 15-session therapy of PTNS. Stimulation was delivered with a pulse width of 200 microseconds, a frequency of 20 Hz, and a current intensity of 10-40 mA for 15 min. After completion of the intervention, patients were reassessed with a repeat cystometry.
SETTING: The study was conducted in the department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation of a tertiary care center.
PARTICIPANTS: SCI patients with NDO.
INTERVENTIONS: Transcutaneous stimulation of the posterior tibial nerve to alleviate detrusor overactivity.
OUTCOME MEASURES: UDS parameters comparing pre- and post- intervention.
RESULTS: The mean age of the study group was 44.5 ± 12.9 years. Significant improvements were observed following intervention, with an increase in the reflex volume (ΔRV = -111 mL, p < 0.001) and maximum cystometric capacity (ΔMCC = -134 mL, p < 0.001), alongside a reduction in maximum detrusor pressure (ΔMDP = 14.9cmH2O, p < 0.001). Level of injury demonstrated a significant association with changes in reflex volume (p = 0.001), but the changes in maximum cystometric capacity (p = 0.105) or maximum detrusor pressure (p = 0.138) did not suggest any statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Transcutaneous PTNS improved urodynamic parameters in incomplete spinal cord injury with neurogenic detrusor overactivity undergoing prolonged antimuscarinic therapy.

articles.title: Naloxone and emergency contraceptives health vending machines across residential and nonresidential university locations (October 2025-April 2026): an observational study.
articles.journal: Journal of American college health : J of ACH
articles.authors: Chahal H, Paa A, Ngo G et al.
articles.abstract: Background:Health vending machines are an emerging strategy to improve access to naloxone, emergency contraceptives, and other health products in university settings. However, there are limited data that compare utilization across multiple vending machines to guide ideal placement.Methods:This observational study evaluated the monthly mean and total items dispensed from health vending machines located in two nonresidential buildings and one residential dormitory, from October 1, 2025, to April 30, 2026.Results:The health vending machine located in the residential dormitory, Akers Hall, demonstrated the greatest utilization, with 1,083 total items dispensed compared to 319 and 366 items at the nonresidential sites-Multicultural Center and Union Building-respectively. Naloxone, emergency contraceptives, and pregnancy tests were the most dispensed products across all sites.Conclusion:Although the residential location, Akers Hall, showed higher utilization, multiple site-specific characteristics may contribute to the observed difference, highlighting the importance of strategic site selection in health vending machine implementation.

articles.title: Identifying Metabolic Pathways That Drive Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Protocol for a Prospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Jebasingh F, Harika LM, Anoop S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a disorder characterized by hyperglycemia that is first recognized during pregnancy due to a mismatch between placental insulin production and increased maternal need, exacerbating insulin resistance. Few studies have systematically examined the metabolic markers and pathways underlying GDM from diagnosis through the postnatal period, including placental metabolic changes through metabolomics studies.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the metabolite profiles identified through metabolomics, as well as the associated pathways responsible for hyperglycemia during pregnancy and the postpartum period, in mothers with GDM compared with mothers without diabetes during pregnancy.
METHODS: We plan to recruit an equal number of patients with GDM and age- and BMI-matched mothers without GDM. Anthropometric data are collected at the first visit. Samples are collected at 3 time points: serum or plasma samples at the time of GDM diagnosis or at the first visit after diagnosis (24-28 weeks of gestation), placental and cord blood samples during delivery, and postnatal serum samples 4 to 12 weeks after delivery. Macroscopic and microscopic features of the placenta will be noted, and a histological score will be derived. Using liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS) with an untargeted approach, metabolite profiles will be identified in serum samples collected at diagnosis and postpartum, cord blood samples, and placental samples from both groups. The raw mass spectrometry (MS) data will be analyzed using the company-provided MS operator software. After data normalization, univariate analyses will be performed. Subsequently, all statistical analyses will be performed using MetaboAnalyst. Through these analyses, differences in the metabolite profiles and their pathways between mothers with and without GDM across pregnancy, starting from the diagnosis of GDM, will be identified. Data will be analyzed using R software. Clinical and demographic data will be presented as percentages, means, or medians, as appropriate. Logistic regression will be performed to assess the association between biomarkers and the placental histological score.
RESULTS: Ethics approval for the study was obtained from the Christian Medical College Vellore Ethics Committee, along with an institutional research grant in January 2025 and an Endocrine Society of Tamil Nadu grant in May 2026. Recruitment for the study began in June 2025…

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Motherwort Injection for Hemostasis and Menstrual Regulation: Protocol for a Prospective, Observational, Multicenter Real-World Study.
articles.authors: Wang S, Li M, Guan S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Motherwort injection (MI) is a traditional Chinese medicine injection widely used for hemostasis and menstrual regulation in obstetrics and gynecology. Although clinical trials and systematic reviews have demonstrated its effectiveness for specific indications, comprehensive real-world evidence (RWE) regarding its safety, effectiveness, and use patterns across diverse clinical settings remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of MI in routine clinical practice and to generate RWE to support its rational use in women receiving treatment for approved obstetric and gynecological indications.
METHODS: This prospective, observational, multicenter real-world registry study plans to enroll 20,000 patients receiving MI for approved obstetric and gynecological indications in routine clinical practice in China. Treatment decisions, including whether to use MI and the dose and duration of treatment, as well as the use of concomitant medications, are made independently by treating physicians. Safety outcomes include the occurrence, type, severity, and incidence of adverse events and adverse drug reactions (ADRs). Effectiveness outcomes are assessed according to the clinical indication and include perioperative bleeding, postpartum hemorrhage, postabortion bleeding and menstrual resumption, uterine involution, menstrual regulation, and treatment satisfaction. Descriptive statistics will be used to characterize patient characteristics, MI use, and safety and effectiveness outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses will examine heterogeneity across major clinical groups. An exploratory nested case-control analysis with 1:4 matching and conditional logistic regression will be used to investigate factors associated with the occurrence of ADRs.
RESULTS: This study has received funding and obtained ethics approval in March 2024 (approval P24003-PJ03). Participant recruitment began on March 31, 2026. By September 2026, a total of 774 participants had been enrolled and included in the study database. The protocol specifies a target sample size of 20,000 participants, with data collection, monitoring, and quality control being conducted according to standardized study procedures. Data analysis has not yet commenced, and the study findings are expected to be published in October 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: This study will provide large-scale RWE regarding the safety and effectiveness of MI in obstetric and gynecological practice. The…

articles.title: Mindfulness-based stress reduction for sleep quality and emotional state in menopause-related insomnia symptoms.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Zhao J, Deng J, Liu H
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the efficacy and safety of mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) for menopause-related insomnia symptoms, with a focus on anxiety, depression, sleep quality, coping styles and quality of life.
METHOD: Eighty-two patients with menopause-related insomnia symptoms were randomized into an experimental group (n = 41, MBSR plus routine health intervention) and a control group (n = 41, routine health intervention) for a 12-week intervention. Emotional state, sleep quality, disease coping styles and quality of life were assessed using standardized scales, with intervention adherence and adverse events recorded as secondary outcomes.
RESULTS: Compared with routine care alone, the MBSR group achieved significantly larger decreases in Self-Rating Anxiety Scale and Self-Rating Depression Scale scores, lower Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores, more positive improvements in disease coping styles and more pronounced gains in several quality-of-life dimensions, particularly physical, psychological and social functioning (p < 0.01). The experimental group had high offline and online adherence rates, with no significant between-group differences in adherence (p > 0.05). The adverse event incidence was below 5% in both groups, with no serious adverse events reported.
CONCLUSION: This study confirms that 12-week MBSR is a safe and effective intervention for improving sleep quality, negative emotions, coping styles and quality of life in patients with menopause-related insomnia symptoms.

articles.title: Mail-in Semen Analysis Completion Among Men Seeking Fertility Evaluation.
articles.authors: Tolani AT, Belarmino A, Kenfield SA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: One in 6 couples experience infertility, and male partner evaluation is often delayed or incomplete. Mail-in semen analysis (SA) may reduce logistical barriers to testing, but completion among fertility patients who use this pathway is not well characterized.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 35,444 patients who obtained a mail-in SA kit from a single national commercial platform (Fellow Health) between April 2020 and October 2025 for fertility evaluation. Completion was defined as receipt and analysis by the laboratory within 16 weeks of kit activation, the step at which a kit is linked to an individual patient and standardized reminders begin. Age, geographic region, neighborhood socioeconomic deprivation (Area Deprivation Index [ADI] quintile), urbanization, and time point in the fertility journey were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression and complete-case sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Overall SA completion was 93% at 16 weeks (32,955/35,444), with 81% completed within 4 weeks and 89% by 8 weeks. Younger age was associated with higher completion (p<0.001). There was not a statistically significant association between completion and urbanization (p=0.24) or ADI quintile (p=0.79), and absolute differences across these categories were small. In multivariable analysis, men trying to conceive for 0-6 months and 7-12 months had 27% and 34% higher odds of completion, respectively, than men planning to start trying in 1 year or longer.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who activated a mail-in SA kit for fertility evaluation, completion was high across geographic, urbanization, and neighborhood socioeconomic categories. Nearly one-third of men sought testing before meeting guideline criteria for infertility evaluation, indicating interest in earlier information about fertility status.
