These findings describe completion within a single mail-in SA pathway and do not compare it with other testing options; this observational study does not establish causality compared with clinic-based testing and did not evaluate real-world analytical accuracy.

articles.title: Methotrexate use in ectopic pregnancy with baseline transaminase elevation.
articles.authors: Powers E, Nguyen A, Rashid Y
articles.abstract: Ectopic pregnancy is a common complication in early pregnancy and remains a leading cause of first-trimester maternal morbidity (0.5 deaths per 100,000 live births). In hemodynamically stable patients, methotrexate is widely used as a fertility-preserving alternative to surgery. However, clinically significant hepatic disease is considered an absolute contraindication for methotrexate therapy. Current guidelines lack clarity concerning the management of patients with elevated liver enzymes, particularly those with metabolic risk factors such as polycystic ovary syndrome and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, which are growing presentations in reproductive-aged women. We present a case of a tubal ectopic pregnancy managed with reduced-dose methotrexate in the setting of elevated liver enzymes, not seen previously in literature, followed by surgical intervention after medical management failure.

articles.title: Silent mourners: Disenfranchized paternal grief, continuing bonds, and meaning-making after perinatal loss.
articles.authors: Kariveliparambil A, Babu J, Rajan Philip S et al.
articles.abstract: Perinatal loss is a profound form of bereavement; however, fathers' grief is often socially and clinically unrecognized. This study examined meaning-making in bereaved fathers in Kerala, India. Using interpretative phenomenological analysis, one-to-one semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten fathers who had experienced miscarriage at or after 12 weeks, stillbirth, or neonatal death within 28 days of birth. Six superordinate themes were generated: the invisible mourner, performing strength while privately breaking, frozen in the moment, already a father, grief layered on grief, and faith as a paradox. Fathers described perinatal loss as a rupture in anticipated fatherhood, relational identity, family futures, and spiritual certainty. Their grief was hidden while continuing bonds were maintained through memory, prayer, symbolic imagination, and private remembrance. The findings theorize paternal perinatal grief as socially organized disenfranchized mourning and call for father-inclusive, culturally responsive bereavement care.

articles.title: Dual-action small-molecule VSP-51-2 ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome via PPARγ modulation and AKR1C3 inhibition.
articles.authors: Liu X, Zheng X, Ma L et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser273, thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.

articles.title: Cystic fibrosis: remarkable success but still not at the finish line.
articles.authors: Jung F, Rosenblatt R
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive, multisystem disease caused by variants in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene which leads to absent or decreased function of the CFTR protein and its regulation of ion flow through the epithelial cell channels. These channels are present in epithelial cells in multiple organs, and abnormal flow of chloride, bicarbonate, and sodium accounts for the bronchiectasis, malabsorption, diabetes, urolithiasis, liver disease, and infertility commonly seen in these patients. The development of compounds, referred to as highly effective modulators classified as potentiators and correctors, augment CFTR's role in the function of these ion channels and consequently have dramatically improved the life expectancy and quality of life in these patients. With the introduction of these modulators and earlier identification of the CF patient through newborn screening, median predicted survival is now 66 years of age; and there has been a marked decrease in the number of exacerbations, hospitalizations, and need for lung transplantation as well as a marked improvement in nutritional markers and fertility. Continued attention to and appreciation of a multidisciplinary approach, screening for complications, and further development of therapies for those individuals who do not benefit from the modulators are essential to further improve the outcomes of these patients. CF exemplifies and highlights the transformative potential of precision medicine but also illustrates the need to continue our efforts to develop a cure and further therapies to help those 8% who do not presently qualify for the modulators available today.

articles.title: A new concept for 'starting menopause hormone therapy' using an oral GnRH antagonist with an estrogen and a progestin (or an estrogen and a selective estrogen receptor modulator): why must we wait to treat women in perimenopause?
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Grandi G, Barretta M, La Marca A et al.
articles.abstract: The target population for menopause hormone therapy (MHT) comprises women who have not menstruated for 12 months or more. However, vasomotor symptoms (VMS) can affect perimenopausal women for some years before their final menstrual period. In this case, hormonal replacement with combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs) or sequential estro-progestin combinations may be proposed in appropriate cases with some drawbacks in terms of safety, tolerability and adherence. Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is a very common challenge across the menopause transition. Unfortunately, the hormonal management of women with VMS and bleeding problems may be difficult until the final shutdown of ovarian function and the absence of endometrial stimulation. In this proof of concept, we propose the use of oral gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonists under a new indication as 'starting MHT' (sMHT), initiated as soon as the first VMS appear in early or late perimenopause in combination with an estrogen and a progestin (or with an estrogen plus a selective estrogen receptor modulator [SERM]). sMHT could then be transitioned to conventional MHT some years later, when no risk of AUB is still present and ovarian function has definitively ceased. Indeed, the use of CHCs to achieve contraception and bleeding control in this life stage has some cardiometabolic and vascular contraindications that do not seem to absolutely apply to the use of sMHT regimens. Is the availability of oral GnRH antagonists therefore an opportunity for treating symptomatic women in the perimenopause earlier with sMHT.

articles.title: Electromagnetic FIELD-INDUCED oxidative stress, inflammation, and APOPTOSIS: A BIBLIOMETRIC and KNOWLEDGE-MAPPING analysis.
articles.authors: Arslan A, Parlak SN, Güney MN et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Public and occupational exposure to extremely low-frequency magnetic fields and radiofrequency electromagnetic fields has expanded over recent decades, while redox-mediated non-thermal mechanisms have become a major framework linking such exposure to biological effects. Despite extensive experimental research, the intellectual structure of this field remains insufficiently mapped. This study analyses global scientific production linking electromagnetic field exposure with oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Web of Science Core Collection was searched using exposure descriptors combined with redox, inflammatory, and cell-death terms. English-language original articles were included, yielding 2,169 documents published between 1989 and 2026 across 847 sources by 8,812 authors. Performance analysis, Bradford and Lotka modelling, h-, g-, and m-indices, co-word clustering, Callon-based thematic mapping, trend-topic detection, co-citation analysis, and collaboration network analysis were performed using the bibliometrix R package.
RESULTS: Annual output grew by 12.97% and peaked at 147 articles in 2025, with 21.63 mean citations per document. Twenty-one journals constituted the Bradford core, led by Electromagnetic Biology and Medicine (n = 141) and Bioelectromagnetics (n = 123). China (343), Türkiye (317), and Italy (193) led corresponding-author output, while international co-authorship was 15.72%. Co-word analysis identified three clusters: oxidative stress and apoptosis occupied motor-theme positions, whereas DNA damage formed a peripheral, declining cluster.
CONCLUSIONS: Inflammation, ROS, pulsed electromagnetic fields, nanoparticles, hypoxia, male infertility, and ferroptosis emerged as recent research fronts, indicating a shift from genotoxic endpoints toward regulated cell-death and inflammatory signalling pathways.

articles.title: The Skin-Mood Axis in Midlife: Neuro-Immuno-Endocrine Cross-Talk in Perimenopausal and Menopausal Aesthetic Dermatology.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Shaker G, Humphrey S, Aguilera SB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perimenopause and menopause may alter skin quality, repair capacity, sleep, mood, self-perception, and aesthetic motivation, yet midlife aesthetic aging is often framed primarily around estrogen and collagen loss.
OBJECTIVE: To propose a midlife skin-mood axis that integrates cutaneous biology, neuroendocrine signaling, immune activity, and psychosocial experience in perimenopausal and menopausal aesthetic dermatology.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes evidence regarding menopausal hormonal change, barrier and extracellular matrix remodeling, stress and sleep physiology, oxytocin-related signaling, body image, observer perception, and aesthetic motivation.
RESULTS: Midlife skin concerns may reflect interactions among reduced barrier resilience, altered repair capacity, neuroendocrine stress pathways, and changes in self-perception rather than isolated tissue aging. These relationships may influence tissue readiness, consultation goals, recovery counseling, patient-reported outcomes, and treatment satisfaction.
CONCLUSION: Recognizing the skin-mood axis may help aesthetic dermatologists individualize consultation, sequence treatments around tissue quality and recovery capacity, and align procedural choices with patient motivation and realistic patient-centered outcomes.

articles.title: Serum FT3/FT4 ratio may indicate the degree of T3 compensation in congenital hypothyroidism.
articles.authors: Yamauchi T, Keidai A, Tomobe Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical guidelines for hypothyroidism recommend measuring serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (FT4) levels as diagnostic and treatment efficacy indicators. However, they do not recommend measuring serum free triiodothyronine (FT3) levels because serum FT3 levels often remain within the normal range. However, serum TSH and FT4 levels alone make diagnosis and treatment decision-making difficult in conditions such as central hypothyroidism, suggesting the need for an additional indicator distinct from serum TSH levels. We investigated whether the serum FT3/FT4 ratio could be an indicator of congenital hypothyroidism (CH) severity, instead of serum TSH level.
METHODS: Thirty-seven newborns were diagnosed with CH (severe group (n = 13): serum TSH ≥ 30 mIU/L; moderate group (n = 24): serum TSH ≥ 5 to < 30 mIU/L). All infants in the severe group received thyroid hormone (TH) replacement therapy vs 13 infants in the moderate group (moderate group with CH). Serum TSH, FT4, FT3, and FT3/FT4 ratios were compared between each group and the two control groups of different ages at diagnosis and 2 months after treatment.
RESULTS: The serum FT3/FT4 ratio was elevated before treatment compared with the control group, reflecting CH severity. Two months after TH replacement, the serum FT3/FT4 ratio decreased significantly: severe group: at diagnosis, 0.48 vs 2 months, 0.27, p =<0.0001; moderate group with TH: 0.38 vs 2 months, 0.26, p < 0.0001. No change was observed in infants without TH replacement.
DISCUSSION: A high serum FT3/FT4 ratio in CH could reflect the degree of systemic T3 compensation and is an indicator of CH severity. This ratio may also be applicable in conditions in which serum TSH levels are not useful for diagnosis or when assessing treatment outcomes.
CONCLUSION: A high serum FT3/FT4 ratio may be an indicator of hypothyroidism severity.

articles.title: RE1 silencing transcription factor is reduced in endometriosis, and uterine deletion in mice alters progesterone responsiveness.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Minchella P, Vashisht A, Peterson R et al.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a steroid-dependent gynecologic disease characterized by progesterone (P4) resistance, subfertility/infertility, and pelvic pain; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying impaired P4 responsiveness in endometriosis tissue are not fully understood. RE1 silencing transcription factor (REST), a transcriptional regulator implicated in steroid hormone signaling, has emerged as a potential mediator of P4 responsiveness. Here, we investigated the role of REST in endometriosis using human tissues and a uterine-specific Rest conditional knockout mouse model. Immunohistochemical analysis of eutopic endometrium and ectopic lesions from patients with endometriosis revealed significantly reduced nuclear REST expression compared with control endometrium, suggesting loss of functional REST in disease. To assess the physiological consequences of REST deficiency, uterine-specific Rest knockout (Rest d/d) mice were generated. Rest d/d females exhibited progressive subfertility and hyperestrogenic uterine tissue characteristics that displayed a blunted responsiveness to P4 treatment. Loss of Rest selectively altered expression of P4-responsive genes associated with endometriosis pathology, despite preserved P4 receptor expression. Following induction of experimental endometriosis, female mice that developed endometriotic-like lesions using Rest-deficient donor tissue developed significantly larger lesions that were less responsive to P4 treatment compared to lesions induced using control tissue. Mechanical sensitivity was modestly increased in mice receiving Rest-deficient tissue, whereas vaginal hyperalgesia was unaffected. These findings identify loss of nuclear REST as a feature of endometriosis and support a role of REST in subfertility, lesion progression, and blunted response to P4. REST may represent a molecular contributor to altered P4 responsiveness and a potential therapeutic target in endometriosis.

articles.title: Tachykinin-like NLP-58 signaling through TKR-1 modulates thermotaxis behavior in Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.authors: Jang MS, Matsuyama HJ, Suzuki R et al.
articles.abstract: Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling plays a central role in mammalian thermoregulatory dysfunction associated with menopause, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Caenorhabditis elegans thermotaxis as a genetically tractable system for investigating conserved tachykinin signaling. We demonstrate that overexpression of nlp-58, the C. elegans ortholog of mammalian NKB, induces abnormal thermotaxis behavior without impairing the temperature response of the thermosensory neurons. NLP-58 is expressed in multiple neurons, including the AIY interneurons, a central integrative node of the thermosensory circuit. AIY-specific overexpression of nlp-58 is sufficient to reproduce the thermotaxis defect, identifying AIY as an important site of NLP-58-dependent behavioral modulation. Genetic analyses further demonstrated that the thermotaxis behavior is mediated primarily through the tachykinin receptor TKR-1, the homolog of mammalian tachykinin 3 receptor (NK3R), acting in ASG and/or ASJ sensory neurons. We also identified a genetic interaction between dhs-4, a lipid metabolic enzyme gene, and nlp-58, suggesting that lipid metabolic pathway modulate tachykinin-dependent thermotaxis behavior. Furthermore, endogenous NLP-58/TKR-1 signaling contributed to the age-dependent decline in thermotaxis behavior. Finally, treatment with fezolinetant, a selective NK3R antagonist used clinically for menopausal vasomotor symptoms, partially improved the thermotaxis defect caused by nlp-58 overexpression. Together, our findings identify the NLP-58/TKR-1 signaling pathway as a modulatory component of thermotaxis behavior and provide a framework for investigating conserved principles of tachykinin-dependent circuit modulation.

articles.title: Sumac (Rhus coriaria L.) Capsules for the management of hypermenorrhea: Protocol for a randomized triple-blind trial.
articles.authors: Mojahedi M, Rezaei A, Fili R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypermenorrhea is a common gynecological disorder adversely affecting women's quality of life. Conventional treatments, particularly hormonal therapies, are associated with side effects and contraindications. Rhus coriaria L. (sumac) has a historical basis in Persian medicine for its astringent and haemostatic properties, supported by modern phytochemical evidence of tannins and flavonoids. However, robust clinical evidence for its efficacy in hypermenorrhea is lacking. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of sumac capsules compared to a placebo in reducing menstrual blood loss in women with hypermenorrhea.
METHODS: A triple-blind, parallel-group, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial will be conducted. Sixty eligible women aged 18-45 years with hypermenorrhea (Pictorial Blood Loss Assessment Chart [PBAC] score ≥100) will be randomly allocated to either the intervention group (500 mg sumac capsule twice daily for the first 7 days of menstruation) or the control group (Avicel placebo capsule), over three consecutive menstrual cycles.
DISCUSSION: This protocol details a methodologically rigorous trial to generate high-level evidence on the potential of sumac as a complementary treatment for hypermenorrhea. If proven effective, sumac could offer a safe, accessible, and cost-effective therapeutic alternative, aligning with patient preferences for natural interventions. The results will inform future clinical practice and research in integrative women's health.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT), IRCT20180218038783N12, registered on 5 October 2025.

articles.title: Depression, anxiety, and stress and fulfillment of contraceptive preferences among young people in Texas and California.
articles.authors: Hecht HK, Yarger J, Hopkins K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young people face both increased mental health concerns and growing barriers to accessing reproductive healthcare.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the association of depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms with preferred contraceptive method use, a measure of healthcare access and reproductive autonomy.
METHODS: We used baseline data (April 2018-May 2023) from a cluster randomized trial at 29 community colleges in Texas and California. Participants were 2,065 sexually active, first-year community college students ages 18-25. We used multivariable mixed effects multinomial logistic regression for clustered data to examine the association of depressive (CESD-10) or anxiety and stress symptoms (DASS-21) and fulfillment of participants' contraceptive preferences (unfulfilled, fulfilled or unknown), controlling for factors related to mental health and care access.
RESULTS: Overall, 51% of participants had an unfulfilled contraceptive preference, and 4% did not know what they preferred. Multivariable results showed elevated depressive symptoms (relative risk ratio [RRR]: 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.01, 1.71) or anxiety and stress symptoms (RRR: 1.31, 95% CI 1.03, 1.66) were associated with having an unfulfilled contraceptive preference versus a fulfilled preference. Additionally, elevated depressive symptoms were associated with having an unknown preference versus fulfilled preference (RRR: 2.98, 95% CI: 1.78, 4.99). Participants with mental distress were also significantly more likely to report cost or insurance barriers as reasons for having an unfulfilled preference (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Young people experiencing mental distress were less likely to realize their contraceptive preference. Future interventions should focus on providing mental health support and improving contraceptive access for young people, including addressing insurance barriers. A primary care model integrating both mental and reproductive healthcare will help to address important health needs of young people.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03519685.

articles.title: Hidden struggles of postmenopausal women in the informal sector: A biopsychosocial assessment.
articles.authors: Ahmed S, Kushwaha N
articles.abstract: Menopause, being a critical stage in women's life, is associated with social stigma and many biopsychosocial challenges. Its complications are associated with poverty, illiteracy, lack of knowledge, and social acceptance. For marginalized women working in the informal sector in India, these challenges become even more strenuous as their experiences are never documented. Literature too reveals a significant gap in understanding menopausal experiences of women in the informal sector, where they are facing challenges of limited healthcare access and support management concerning policy rights and legislative safeguards. This study aims to explore the neglected and lived experiences of informal workers who experienced menopause. It highlights their workplace struggles and coping strategies by focusing on biopsychosocial dimensions through the biopsychosocial model.The study employed a qualitative phenomenological approach, in which 20 postmenopausal women working in the construction sector of the Kishangarh Marble Industry in Rajasthan, India, were purposively chosen. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, which revealed lived experiences in terms of themes including challenges ranging from biological, psychological and social challenges to their coping mechanisms and resilience. The findings highlight that postmenopausal women in the construction sector are facing all of these challenges during the menopausal phase. Women are also expressing resilience through self-care and peer support. However, policy support, gender-sensitive approaches and rights-based perspectives are essential to empower these women.

articles.title: RETRACTION: Clomiphene Citrate Plus Tamoxifen Versus Laparoscopic Ovarian Drilling in Women with Clomiphene-Resistant Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract: M.S. Zakherah, A. Nasr, A.M. El Saman, O.M. Shaaban, and A.Y. Shahin, "Clomiphene Citrate Plus Tamoxifen Versus Laparoscopic Ovarian Drilling in Women with Clomiphene-Resistant Polycystic Ovary Syndrome," International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics 108, no. 3(2009): 240-243, 10.1016/j.ijgo.2009.10.004. The above article, published online on 26 November 2009 in Wiley Online Library (wileyonlinelibrary.com) has been retracted by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Michael Geary; and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. Concerns were raised by a third party regarding the short time frame during which this study and five others, involving recruitment of clomiphene-resistant PCOS women out of one single center, were undertaken by the authors. The editorial team assessed the reported data and results and found additional issues, including numerical anomalies and inconsistencies. The reported p-values of the different categorical variables in Table 2, such as live birth, could not be reproduced using reasonable variations of statistical tests. The reported relative risks were also unable to be reproduced. The authors were contacted with a request for their original data and a comment, but they did not respond. With a considerable number of critical errors in the results, the Editor-in-Chief considers the data and conclusions of the article to be unreliable. Therefore, a retraction is warranted.

articles.title: RETRACTION: Prognosis and Determinants of Pregnancy Outcome among Patients with Post-Hepatitis Liver Cirrhosis.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract: S.M. Rasheed, A.M. Abdel Monem, A.H. Abd Ellah, and M.S. Abdel Fateh, "Prognosis and Determinants of Pregnancy Outcome among Patients with Post-Hepatitis Liver Cirrhosis," International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics 121, no. 3(2013): 247-251, 10.1016/j.ijgo.2012.12.020. The above article, published online on 19 March 2013 in Wiley Online Library (onlinelibrary.wiley.com), has been retracted by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Michael Geary; and John Wiley & Sons Ltd. UK. Concerns were raised by a third party regarding the distribution of women with liver cirrhosis between Tables 1 and 3 in the study, as they and the Child-Pugh scores all differ between these tables when the numbers should remain the same. The publisher asked the authors to clarify these inconsistencies and provide the raw data for the study. The authors did not provide the requested data but responded to the concerns. Upon review of their response, the editorial team and publisher did not feel it explained these serious concerns adequately. Subsequently, further concerns were identified, including irreproducible odds ratios, lack of a reference category, and contradictions between the confidence intervals and p-values in the tables. In addition, the journal sought a clinical opinion from an expert in the area who felt that some of the clinical findings and outcome were not consistent with the typical clinical course of the condition. As a result, the data and conclusions are considered unreliable, and therefore the article must be retracted.

articles.title: Resource-constrained rolling-horizon scheduling optimization for male fetal NIPT testing timing: a memetic algorithm-based study.
articles.authors: Liu C, Qin H, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract: In male fetal non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT), the success of result interpretation depends strongly on the gestational age at blood draw, which makes "when to test" both a clinical and an appointment-management issue. We propose a rolling-horizon scheduling framework that integrates patient-specific success-probability curves with capacity, no-show, retest, and execution dynamics. Using a public cohort of 5,543 singleton male fetal samples, a polynomial-feature logistic regression was fitted to 3,880 records and evaluated in 1,663 held-out patients. The held-out area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.799 (95% confidence interval, 0.736-0.856), with calibration intercept - 0.020  and slope 1.018. The operational layer was evaluated as a prospective operational-feasibility simulation on a constructed 105-day timeline. Across ten common random seeds, the Memetic Algorithm (MA) achieved eligible-patient completion of 99.09 % ± 0.23  percentage points, mean success probability among completed tests of 98.44 % ± 0.03  percentage points, and eligible-patient risk coverage of 98.86 % ± 0.78  percentage points. Under prespecified weights, its composite fitness and custom load-distribution score with a front-loading penalty exceeded those of six executable rules, which retained advantages in waiting time, completion, mean success probability, or risk coverage. On four reduced instances, the mean gap from exact mixed-integer linear programming was 3.37 % ± 1.94  percentage points under the common linearized surrogate objective. The framework offers an integrated and interpretable approach to coordinating individualized testing timing with dynamic appointment capacity in NIPT services.

articles.title: Maternal fish or n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid intake during pregnancy and risk of impaired kidney function at 6 years of age: the Japan environment and children's study.
articles.authors: Nakamura M, Yamazaki C, Tsuchida A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic kidney disease in children causes kidney failure and growth impairment, making its prevention an urgent clinical and public health priority. Experimental animal studies have suggested that maternal intake of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) during pregnancy may have kidney-protective effects in offspring; however, evidence in humans remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the association between maternal fish or n-3 PUFA intake during pregnancy and kidney dysfunction in children.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study, a nationwide prospective birth cohort. A total of 2,679 mother-child pairs were included. Kidney dysfunction was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate < 90 mL/min/1.73 m² at 6 years of age. Maternal fish or n-3 PUFA intake during pregnancy was categorized into quintiles. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate the associations.
RESULTS: At 6 years of age, 262 children (9.8%) had decreased kidney function. In the adjusted model, maternal fish intake in the highest quintile was associated with a significantly lower risk of kidney dysfunction compared with the lowest quintile (odds ratio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval, 0.41-0.99). Maternal n-3 PUFA intake showed a similar trend, although the association was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Higher maternal fish intake during pregnancy was associated with a reduced risk of kidney dysfunction in offspring, whereas maternal n-3 PUFA intake showed no significant association. These findings suggest that higher maternal fish intake during pregnancy may be associated with a lower risk of impaired kidney function in children.

articles.title: Effect of Sacral Neuromodulation in Women with Prior Pelvic Floor Surgery: A Systematic Review of the Literature.
articles.authors: Ghazi A, Alamri O, Alsehli A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: To evaluate sacral neuromodulation (SNM) outcomes in women with overactive bladder (OAB) following pelvic floor surgery (PFS).
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through January 2026 for any studies reporting SNM outcomes in women with prior PFS. The primary outcomes were progression to permanent implantation after test stimulation and overall clinical success rates, as defined by each study (≥ 50% symptom improvement, resolution of OAB symptoms, or moderate/marked improvement on the Global Response Assessment). Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE.
RESULTS: Six articles involving 308 patients (189 with prior PFS) met inclusion criteria. Two studies were reported separately because of poor quality, different indications, or a single treated patient. The remaining four studies (175 patients) demonstrated progression to permanent implantation of 85.1% (149/175) and overall success of 77% (91/118). One retrospective cohort showed a decrease in daily pad use by 73.8% (4.2 to 1.1 pads, p < 0.001), with 24% achieving pad-free status. A single comparative study revealed no short-term differences based on surgical history, but at 24 months, success rates decreased significantly (42% vs. 66%, p = 0.031). In a small subgroup of women with prior urethrolysis, six out of eight patients progressed to permanent implantation. In a single study, factors associated with success included age < 55 years, SNM within 4 years of surgery, and preserved pelvic floor activity. Prior surgery type did not predict response. GRADE certainty of evidence was low to very-low.
CONCLUSIONS: Within the current limited evidence, SNM appears to be a reasonable treatment option for OAB following PFS, with short outcomes comparable to those reported in general OAB patients. Previous PFS should not preclude potential candidates from undergoing SNM; yet, long-term effectiveness may be reduced, and these findings should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Intersphincteric prosthetic implants for faecal incontinence: a systematic review and exploratory pooled analysis of clinically meaningful response.
articles.authors: Gupta MS, Muhibullah N, Yusufi M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intersphincteric prosthetic implants have emerged as a minimally invasive treatment option for faecal incontinence (FI), positioned between conservative therapies and more invasive surgical or neuromodulatory interventions. However, evidence supporting their effectiveness remains fragmented and largely nonrandomised.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review with exploratory quantitative synthesis was conducted. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to August 2025, with an updated search in January 2026 for nonrandomised studies evaluating intersphincteric prosthetic implants (GateKeeper® or SphinKeeper®) in adults with FI. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving a clinically meaningful response, defined as a ≥ 50% reduction in Vaizey (St Mark's) score at ≥ 12 months. Where feasible, exploratory pooled analyses of binary responder outcomes were performed using random-effects models. Secondary outcomes, including continence severity, quality of life and complications, were synthesised narratively. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Fourteen observational studies were included. Two studies reporting comparable binary responder outcomes at approximately 12 months (n = 75) contributed to the primary exploratory synthesis, yielding a pooled responder proportion of 49.3% (95% CI 38.2-60.5%). A sensitivity analysis incorporating three studies reporting study-defined clinical success (n = 129) produced a similar pooled estimate (51.9%, 95% CI 43.3-60.4%). Given the very small number of contributing studies, measures of statistical heterogeneity were uninformative, and interpretation was further limited by the nonrandomised study designs. Quality-of-life outcomes and complication rates were heterogeneous and could not be pooled quantitatively. No procedure-related mortality was reported.
CONCLUSION: Exploratory quantitative synthesis suggests that intersphincteric prosthetic implantation may be associated with clinically meaningful symptom improvement in a subset of patients with faecal incontinence. However, the certainty of evidence is low, and pooled estimates should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. Prospective comparative studies with standardised outcome reporting are required to more clearly define the role of these implants within the treatment pathway. What does this paper add to the literature? This review brings together the fragmented evidence on intersphincteric prosthetic…

articles.title: Smooth muscle tumors of uncertain malignant potential of the uterus: A single-center 9-year retrospective cohort study with a record-based diagnostic consistency audit.
articles.authors: Ekmez F, Cim N
articles.abstract: Uterine smooth muscle tumors of uncertain malignant potential (STUMP) are diagnosed by integrating cytological atypia, mitotic activity, and coagulative tumor cell necrosis, yet retrospective series often rely on historical reports that document these features incompletely. This study aimed to describe an institutional STUMP cohort and to determine whether its recorded category labels were supported by the pathological variables recorded for each case. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 20 patients who underwent surgery between January 2017 and March 2026 and received an institutional diagnosis of STUMP, epithelioid STUMP, or STUMP/leiomyosarcoma (LMS) interface. In a post hoc, record-based audit, the 18 labels recorded as Criterion A, B, or C were compared with explicit operational definitions adapted from a published 3-pattern formulation and classified as discordant, indeterminate, or consistent on record. Slides were not reexamined, and original diagnoses were retained. Exact 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and 3 sensitivity analyses were calculated. The mean age was 41.6 ± 7.2 years. All patients underwent surgery for presumed leiomyoma, 11 by hysterectomy and 9 by uterus-sparing procedures. All 7 Criterion C labels were accompanied by recorded mitotic counts below 15 per 10 high-power fields (7/7; 95% CI, 59.0-100.0%). Of the 18 audited labels, 10 were discordant (55.6%; 95% CI, 30.8-78.5%), six were indeterminate, and two were consistent on record. No recorded mitotic-count range crossed an audit threshold; lower range bounds and a stricter mitotic threshold changed no audit status, whereas 14 labels were discordant when only absent atypia was accepted as nonsignificant. One STUMP/LMS interface case was subsequently managed as LMS. Sixteen patients had no recorded recurrence or progression during a median follow-up of 11 months; the outcome was unknown in 3. STUMP was not recognized preoperatively in this cohort, but without a leiomyoma comparator, no conclusion about clinical distinguishability is possible. The audit demonstrates discordance between recorded labels and recorded variables rather than diagnostic error, and the affected cases remain provisional pending slide-level gynecological pathology review. The data support no inference about recurrence risk, the safety or reproductive benefit of uterus-sparing surgery, or biomarker-based prognosis.

articles.title: Correlation between endometriosis and chronic endometritis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Fan H, Liu B, Wu X et al.
articles.abstract: This single-center retrospective cohort study included infertile patients treated between October 2019 and December 2024, comparing an endometriosis (EMS) cohort (n = 250, laparoscopically and histopathologically confirmed) with a control cohort (n = 750, tubal-factor infertility only, EMS excluded by laparoscopy). All patients underwent laparoscopy, hysteroscopy, and endometrial biopsy; chronic endometritis (CE) was diagnosed by cluster of differentiation 38/cluster of differentiation 138 immunohistochemistry, and EMS was staged by revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine. CE detection rate was significantly higher in the EMS cohort than in controls (P < .001). Within the EMS cohort, CE prevalence was 45.1% in moderate-to-severe (stage III-IV) disease versus 24.0% in mild (stage I-II) disease (P = .001). Factors independently associated with concurrent CE were moderate-to-severe EMS, repeated intrauterine procedures, infertility duration ≥ 3 years, chronic pelvic pain, and higher gravidity (all P < .05). At 1 year, the EMS cohort had a lower clinical pregnancy rate (70.0% vs 80.0%), higher persistent infertility rate (30.0% vs 20.0%), and higher early pregnancy loss rate (16.0% vs 9.2%) than controls (all P < .05). Within the EMS cohort, concurrent CE was associated with a lower clinical pregnancy rate (56.0% vs 76.0%), higher persistent infertility rate (44.0% vs 24.0%), and higher early pregnancy loss rate (31.0% vs 11.3%) than EMS alone (all P = .002). These findings demonstrate a significant cross-sectional association between EMS and CE, with higher CE detection in advanced-stage EMS; however, causality and temporal sequence cannot be determined, reproductive outcomes were exploratory and unadjusted, and this single-center retrospective dataset is insufficient to support universal diagnostic or therapeutic guidelines.

articles.title: Causal effects of genetically predicted CCL25 signaling on ovarian cancer risk: A 2-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Tang L, Chen J et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a common and highly malignant neoplasm in women, characterized by a poor prognosis and posing a significant threat to both health and quality of life. Despite the unclear pathogenesis of OC, there is growing evidence suggesting an association between OC and inflammatory cytokines. Nevertheless, this potential causal relationship remains insufficiently explored. To enhance early clinical diagnosis and inform therapeutic strategies, we conducted a bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to evaluate the causal relationship between inflammatory cytokines and OC. We identified genetic instrumental variables for inflammatory cytokines and OC utilizing publicly accessible genome-wide association study data. Causal relationships between inflammatory cytokines and OC were assessed using inverse variance weighting as the primary analytical approach. The robustness and validity of the observed causal relationships were further substantiated through multiple sensitivity analyses, including Cochran Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, MR pleiotropy residual sum and outlier, and leave-one-out analysis. Additionally, a random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to enhance statistical power and further identify causal proteins. Finally, colocalization analysis was employed to reinforce the evidence regarding the sharing of common etiological variants. MR analysis indicated that genetically predicted elevated levels of serum C-C motif chemokine 25 (CCL25) were inversely correlated with the risk of developing OC (inverse variance weighting: odds ratio = 0.95, 95% confidence interval = 0.91-0.99, P = .038). The direction of the beta coefficient was consistent across all MR methodologies. There was no evidence of horizontal pleiotropy (Egger intercept = 0.016, P = .145) or heterogeneity (Cochran Q = 8.857, P = .635). A meta-analysis confirmed that the inverse causal relationship between CCL25 and OC remained statistically significant (odds ratio = 0.94, 95% confidence interval = 0.90-0.99, P = .001). Colocalization analysis revealed no shared genetic factors between CCL25 and OC (the sum of the posterior probabilities of hypothesis 3 and hypothesis 4 is equal to 0.05.). Combined MR and meta-analyses indicate that CCL25 functions as a protective factor for OC. Future research should therefore conduct more comprehensive investigations into this relationship.

articles.title: Cervicography for cervical cancer screening: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Kim SN, Shim SH, Bae J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervicography (CVG) has been proposed as a low-cost adjunct to Papanicolaou (Pap) cytology, but its added value as a co-test is uncertain. We evaluated the accuracy of CVG and Pap cytology, alone and as a parallel combined test, for histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse.
METHODS: Five databases were searched for studies published through December 31, 2024, without geographical or language restriction. The reference standard was histopathology of colposcopy-directed biopsy. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled with a bivariate random-effects model. Because both index tests were applied to the same participants in every study, they were compared within a single paired model yielding relative sensitivity, relative specificity and the relative diagnostic odds ratio (rDOR).
RESULTS: Eight cross-sectional studies were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.69 (95% confidence interval 0.59-0.77) and 0.90 (0.83-0.95) for CVG, and 0.69 (0.56-0.80) and 0.96 (0.91-0.98) for Pap cytology. In the paired comparison, relative sensitivity was 1.01 (0.92-1.11; P = .87), relative specificity 0.94 (0.91-0.98; P = .002) and the rDOR 0.43 (0.31-0.60; P < .001). In the 3 studies also reporting the combination, its rDOR versus Pap cytology was 1.48 (0.72-3.08; P = .29). Heterogeneity was substantial, but the comparison was stable on leave-one-out analysis (relative specificity 0.93-0.96).
CONCLUSIONS: CVG did not improve sensitivity over Pap cytology, and both its specificity and its overall accuracy were lower. Adding CVG raised sensitivity, but this follows from the parallel testing rule: the gain in overall accuracy was not statistically significant, while false positives increased approximately 3-fold. Given the very low certainty of the evidence, routine addition of CVG to Pap cytology cannot be recommended. Prospective studies of digital tele-CVG against human papillomavirus-based strategies are required.

articles.title: Exploring the Association Between Cannabis Use and Male Reproductive Parameters: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: International braz j urol : official journal of the Brazilian Society of Urology
articles.authors: Marquardt N, Felkl OR, Veiga DM et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between cannabis use and male reproductive function, specifically sperm parameters and serum hormone levels.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library (August-September 2025) for studies assessing cannabis exposure and male fertility outcomes. Data were pooled using random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed by I²/Q statistics and publication bias by funnel plots/Egger's test, following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251132635).
RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (5,766 patients, 6,231 samples; mean age 36.5 ± 9.9 years) were included for sperm outcomes, and 21,066 patients (mean age 37.4 ± 10.4 years) for hormonal outcomes. All cannabis users reported smoking more than one joint per week in the preceding months. Cannabis users showed a significant reduction in sperm morphology compared to non-users (MD = -1.02; 95% CI: -1.93 to -0.10; p < 0.05), which persisted even when restricted to studies strictly following WHO criteria. No significant differences were found for sperm concentration, ejaculate volume, total sperm count, or progressive and total motility. Hormonal analysis revealed no differences in testosterone, FSH, or LH, but SHBG levels were significantly higher in cannabis users (MD = 3.90; 95% CI: 1.67-6.13; p <0.05).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that cannabis use should be considered in the lifestyle assessment of men evaluated for subfertility and infertility. Although causality could not be established, cannabis should be considered a potential lifestyle factor, particularly in cases of abnormal sperm morphology or unexplained infertility. Further studies on sperm function are needed to clarify its effects on testicular function and fertilizing capacity.

articles.title: Endometrial thickness and risk of endometrial pathology in women with postmenopausal bleeding: the influence of hormone therapy.
articles.authors: Okoror CEM, Sen S, Hazbun S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between endometrial thickness (ET) and histopathologically confirmed endometrial cancer or atypical hyperplasia in postmenopausal women presenting with vaginal bleeding, stratified by menopausal hormone therapy (HT) status, and to assess diagnostic performance across therapy groups.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of postmenopausal women referred to an urgent cancer pathway between September 2022 and August 2023 at a United Kingdom district hospital. ET was measured by transvaginal ultrasonography as double-layer thickness. Histopathologic diagnosis from endometrial biopsy or hysteroscopy-directed sampling served as the standard. Diagnostic discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals; sensitivity and specificity were calculated at prespecified thresholds. Multivariable logistic regression assessed predictors including age, ET, recurrent bleeding, and HT status.
RESULTS: Among 1,082 women with histopathologic outcomes, 32 had clinically significant endometrial pathology. ET demonstrated excellent discrimination in women not using HT (AUC: 0.925) but markedly reduced discrimination in women using continuous combined HT (AUC: 0.597). At a 4 mm threshold, negative predictive value exceeded 99% in both groups, while positive predictive value remained low in HT users. Age and ET were independent predictors in adjusted models.
CONCLUSIONS: ET performs well as a triage test in women not using HT, but is less informative as a standalone measure in women using continuous combined HT; HT status should inform interpretation and referral decisions.

articles.title: Validation of the Perimenopause Symptom Scale (Peri-SS) for digital self-assessment: psychometric evaluation among US women aged 35 to 59 years.
articles.authors: Xu Y, Ilyich I, Prentice C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Perimenopause is an under-recognized transition poorly measured by existing tools, which often overlook symptoms characteristic of this phase. To address this, we developed and validated the Perimenopause Symptom Scale (Peri-SS): a concise, phase-specific, psychometrically robust instrument for digital self-assessment and research use among US women aged 35-59 who self-reported being in perimenopause.
METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal validation study with 1,255 US women aged 35-59 (633 self-identified as perimenopausal) recruited via Prolific. Participants completed the Peri-SS, Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), and EuroQol 5-Dimension, 5-Level (EQ-5D-5L) questionnaire at baseline and 7-14 days later. Following COSMIN guidelines, we assessed structural validity, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, criterion and construct validity, and responsiveness to change.
RESULTS: The Peri-SS demonstrated strong psychometric performance. Confirmatory factor analysis confirmed a four-domain structure (vasomotor, psychological, sexual, physical), with excellent model fit (CFI=0.932, RMSEA=0.069). Internal consistency was excellent (α=0.90 overall; domain range 0.73-0.86), and test-retest reliability was high (ICC=0.82). Criterion validity was strong, with Peri-SS scores highly correlated with Menopause Rating Scale (r=0.88). Construct validity was supported through moderate correlations with EQ-5D-5L utilities (ρ=-0.50) and effective discrimination between groups by age, reproductive stage, and hormone therapy use. The scale was also responsive to symptom changes over time (η²=0.277).
CONCLUSIONS: The Peri-SS is a reliable, valid, responsive tool for assessing perimenopausal symptom burden. Its concise format and strong psychometric performance make it well-suited for research, clinical care, and digital health applications.

articles.title: An exploration of the physical and mental health impact among a diverse population in the United Kingdom experiencing perimenopause and menopause (MARIE UK-WP2a).
articles.authors: Delanerolle G, Sun J, Taylor J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Menopause is associated with diverse physical, psychological, and cognitive symptoms, yet variation across menopausal stages and modes of onset remains poorly characterized in the United Kingdom-based populations. This study aimed to evaluate symptom burden and quality of life across perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal individuals, including those with natural and surgical menopause.
METHODS: A mixed-methods, prospective cohort study was conducted to explore perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal experience in cis-trans gender and LGBTQ+ populations in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland using the digital XM Qualtrics platform, using psychometric and clinical scales including the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), Greene Climacteric Scale (GCS), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Burnout Assessment Tool (BAT), Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), and Health-related Quality of Life (HrQoL) assessments. Quantitative data were gathered following informed consent at two time points, and qualitative interviews were conducted in a selected sub-cohort.
RESULTS: Among 845 baseline and 538 follow-up participants (median age 52), anxiety severity was significantly higher in perimenopause compared with post-menopause (baseline: P=0.013; follow-up: P=0.013), while depressive symptoms were markedly greater in those with surgical menopause, as shown by both HADS (baseline: P=0.001; follow-up: P<0.001) and GCS scores (baseline: P=0.004; follow-up: P=0.003). People experiencing surgical menopause displayed increased insomnia, back pain, vasomotor symptoms, and reduced quality of life. Cognitive symptoms, including forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating, were most pronounced among the perimenopausal cohort. Insomnia and burnout were moderately prevalent among employed people, especially when coexisting with conditions such as endometriosis. Regional differences were minimal, though participants from Scotland reported higher pain scores.
CONCLUSION: Symptom severity and variability are dependent on menopausal stage and vary with the mode of onset. The study findings highlight the need for targeted, stage-specific clinical pathways and workplace adaptations, particularly for those with complex medical histories such as endometriosis. A stratified, inclusive approach to menopause care is urgently required across policy and practice settings.

articles.title: Periodontitis and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Evidence for a Potential Biological Link.
articles.authors: Jiang L, Li S, Luo M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the potential association between gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and periodontitis (PD) and to explore possible biological mechanisms underlying this link.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In the first part of this study, a two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) analysis was conducted to evaluate the potential effect of PD on the risk of GDM, and vice versa. In the second part, transcriptomic data and network-based bioinformatics analyses were integrated, including differential expression analysis and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, to screen for common differentially expressed genes and significantly enriched biological pathways. In the third part, a simplified in vitro β-cell challenge system was established using the human pancreatic β-cell line EndoC-βH1. Cells were exposed to high-glucose and progesterone conditions with or without Porphyromonas gingivalis to examine inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. Differences in the expression of MR-genes, inflammatory cytokines, and reactive oxidative species were evaluated. All analyses were performed using R version 4.2.2 (R CoreTeam, Vienna, Austria).
RESULTS: The forward MR analysis showed evidence consistent with a modest positive association of genetically predicted PD with GDM risk (OR = 1.14, P = 0.006), whereas the reverse analysis did not provide evidence for an association of genetically predicted GDM with PD risk (OR = 1.08, P = 0.222). Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the MR results. Transcriptomic bioinformatic analyses identified multiple key genes that were dysregulated in both PD and GDM, including inflammatory mediators (IL1RN and TGFB1) and metabolic regulators (AKT1, NOS3, and TCF7L2). Functional enrichment revealed that the overlapping genes were mainly involved in critical biological processes like apoptotic signalling, cell adhesion, and inflammatory responses. The PPI network suggested a synergistic role of PD and GDM in inflammation and metabolic regulation. Compared with the GDM model, β-cells in the GDM+PD model exhibited significantly enhanced inflammatory responses and oxidative stress. Additionally, the MR-genes showed significant expression changes in the GDM+PD model: HSPBAP1, APBA1, and SHC4 were upregulated, whereas CDH1, NDUFAF6, and DGKB were downregulated.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide evidence consistent with a potential biological link between PD and GDM, in which periodontal…

articles.title: Preimplementation Factors for a Mobile Decision Support Tool for Cervical Cancer Screening Among Dominican Women Living With HIV: Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: The Journal of the Association of Nurses in AIDS Care : JANAC
articles.authors: Gerchow L, Baez P, Rodriguez K et al.
articles.abstract: Women living with HIV (WLH) have a sixfold greater risk of cervical cancer. In the Dominican Republic, cervical cancer and HIV remain prevalent, yet screening rates are low. The World Health Organization recommends a same-day screening, triage, and treatment protocol for WLH, but implementation faces persistent barriers. This study examined barriers and facilitators to implementing iSTAR, a mobile clinical decision support tool designed to guide providers through the screening, triage, and treatment protocol through rapid human papillomavirus DNA testing and results interpretation. We conducted a secondary qualitative analysis guided by the Health Equity Implementation Framework of transcripts from 16 providers and 25 WLH across formative interviews and usability testing. Societal, clinic-level, patient, and provider factors intersected during clinical encounters to shape implementation, indicating that neither protocol adoption nor technology alone will sustain implementation. Findings support multilevel strategies for successful initial and sustained implementation.

articles.title: Regimens of vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: Trak-Fellermeier MA, Palma Molina XE, Huey SL et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Vitamin D deficiency is common in pregnancy and has been associated with adverse health outcomes for the mother and infant, including pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and low birthweight. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a vitamin D intake of 200 international units (IU) per day during pregnancy. Vitamin D supplementation is recommended for women with suspected vitamin D deficiency, but it is not universally recommended. The effects of different doses (regimens) of vitamin D during pregnancy have not been established. This is an update of a Cochrane review first published in 2019, which concluded that vitamin D supplementation (at any dose) may have little or no beneficial effects on maternal or neonatal outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of different doses of vitamin D supplementation (alone or in combination with calcium or other micronutrients) during pregnancy: more than 600 IU/day versus up to 600 IU/day, and 4000 IU/day or more versus less than 4000 IU/day.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), ClinicalTrials.gov, the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, and relevant databases in April 2026.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised trials evaluating the effects of different vitamin D regimens during pregnancy on maternal and infant health outcomes. Trials of pregnant women with pre-existing conditions or multiple pregnancies were excluded.
OUTCOMES: The critical maternal outcomes were pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and any adverse events. The critical infant outcomes were preterm birth and low birthweight.
RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 1 tool to independently assess the risk of bias in included studies.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two review authors independently assessed study eligibility and extracted data from included studies. We conducted fixed-effect meta-analyses in RevMan where it was reasonable to assume that studies were estimating the same underlying treatment effect. If substantial heterogeneity was detected, we conducted random-effects meta-analyses, using the Mantel-Haenszel method for dichotomous outcomes and inverse-variance method for continuous outcomes. We used the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of the evidence.
INCLUDED STUDIES: This review update included 25 studies with 7008 pregnant women. The included studies were conducted in 14 countries between 2004 and 2024. We excluded 29 studies,…

articles.title: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) for treating advanced epithelial ovarian cancer.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: El-Shakankery KH, Shawky M, Grainger T et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Ovarian cancer is the eighth most common cancer in women worldwide. Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the most common type; three-quarters of cases present with advanced disease (stage III or IV). Treatment consists of combinations of surgery and chemotherapy. Although initial responses to chemotherapy are good, most women with advanced disease relapse. Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) prevent cancer cells from repairing DNA damage, especially in those with breast cancer susceptibility gene (BRCA) mutations (BRCA-mutant), thereby offering a different mechanism of action for anticancer treatment compared to conventional chemotherapy. This is an update to a review first published in 2010 and previously updated in 2015 and 2022.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) versus placebo or other anti-cancer treatments for women with newly diagnosed or recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC).
SEARCH METHODS: We identified randomised controlled trials (RCTs) by searching the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials MEDLINE, and Embase up to 2 December 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included trials randomising women with EOC to PARPi versus no treatment/placebo, PARPi versus conventional chemotherapy, or PARPi together with conventional chemotherapy versus conventional chemotherapy alone.
OUTCOMES: We extracted data on overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS), severe adverse events, and quality of life.
RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane tool RoB 1 to assess the risk of bias in the included studies.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We conducted meta-analyses using the random-effects model to calculate hazard ratios (HR), risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the certainty of evidence using GRADE.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We identified 10 new studies. We included a total of 24 studies (8961 participants) in this 2026 version of the review: eight (4801 participants) with newly-diagnosed, advanced EOC and 16 (4160 participants) with recurrent EOC.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: The studies evaluated different PARPi against various comparators. Below we present four key comparisons. Most participants had BRCA mutations, either in their tumour (sBRCA-mutant) and/or germline (gBRCA-mutant), or homologous recombination deficiencies (HRD) in their tumours. Newly diagnosed EOC PARPi versus placebo maintenance after chemotherapy PARPi maintenance…

articles.title: Redox and Inflammatory Mechanisms in PMOS and Endometriosis: A Critical Review of Microbial and Plant-Derived Interventions.
articles.authors: Hussain AA, Ali SM, Naser RSA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) or polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and endometriosis arise from different endocrine and tissue disturbances, yet oxidative stress (OS) and inflammation connect their initiating processes to reproductive dysfunction.
OBJECTIVE: In PMOS, redox-inflammatory signaling intersects with insulin resistance, androgen excess, and follicular dysfunction; in endometriosis, it supports estrogen-dependent lesion persistence, angiogenesis, and fibrosis. This narrative review examines these interactions and evaluates microbial and plant-derived interventions according to their mechanistic targets and clinical evidence.
KEY FINDINGS: Selected probiotic, synbiotic, and phytochemical trials in PMOS report improvements in metabolic, endocrine, and oxidative-inflammatory measures. In endometriosis, human intervention findings are concentrated in pain outcomes, while evidence for modulation of lesion biology remains predominantly experimental. Across both disorders, formulation, biological compartment, baseline phenotype, and concomitant treatment influence interpretation of therapeutic effects. Microbial metabolism offers a potential link between the two intervention classes by modifying phytochemical exposure and generating bioactive metabolites.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence-informed comparative framework identifies where mechanistic findings have reached clinical evaluation and where further translation is needed. Future trials should connect standardized interventions and disease-specific clinical outcomes with measurements of microbial function and redox signaling to establish which patients benefit and through which pathways.

articles.title: Five years of nationwide use of whole genome sequencing in ongoing pregnancies: Diagnostic yield, timing, and implementation.
articles.authors: Vogel I, Andreasen L, Tørring PM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We describe timing, diagnostic yield, secondary findings of prenatal whole genome sequencing (pWGS) in ongoing pregnancies during the first 5 years of implementation within a publicly funded healthcare system. Moreover, we discuss our collective clinical experiences implementing pWGS in prenatal care.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a historical cohort study, including all singleton pregnancies undergoing pWGS after a normal chromosomal microarray between 2019 and 2023. Data on sample type, gestational age at test ordering, turnaround time, diagnostic yield, and secondary findings were extracted from all four Danish clinical genetics laboratories.
RESULTS: A total of 207 cases were analyzed, including 85 chorionic villus samples and 122 amniotic fluid samples; trio sequencing was performed in 204/207 (98.6%). Median gestational age at ordering was 20 weeks (IQR 17-21). Median turnaround time for ongoing pregnancies was 11 working days (IQR 8-17). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants explaining the phenotype were identified in 33/207 pregnancies (15.9%, 95% CI 11.6-21.5). Yield was highest in hydrops (25.0%, 95% CI 12.0-44.9) and multiple anomalies (24.3%, 95% CI 13.4-40.1), and lowest in isolated increased nuchal translucency (7.1%, 95% CI 2.0-22.6). Secondary findings were reported in 18/207 cases (8.7%, 95% CI 5.6-13.3).
CONCLUSIONS: pWGS was delivered within clinically relevant turnaround times. Applied after normal chromosomal microarray, the yield represents incremental diagnostic value in a chromosomal microarray-negative population. In clinical practice, both normal and abnormal pWGS results form a central component of counseling in ongoing pregnancies with unresolved fetal risk. However, the impact of such results on parental decision-making or pregnancy outcomes was not assessed in this study.

articles.title: Toward Germline-Like Differentiation of Human Mesenchymal Stem Cells: Induction Strategies, Signaling Pathways and Current Limitations.
articles.authors: Seyyedin S, Rezaei M
articles.abstract: The generation of human gametes from somatic cells represents a major goal in reproductive medicine, with significant implications for infertility treatment and disease modeling. Among candidate sources, mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have emerged as a promising platform due to their multipotency, accessibility, and immunomodulatory properties. Increasing evidence indicates that MSCs can be directed toward germline- and gamete-like phenotypes; however, differentiation efficiency, reproducibility, and functional competence remain major challenges. The present narrative review analyzes current advances in the differentiation of human MSCs into germline- and gametelike phenotypes, integrating findings from 36 studies published between 2000 and 2026. Key chemical and biological drivers, including retinoic acid and bone morphogenetic proteins, are highlighted for their roles in meiotic initiation and primordial germ cell specification. Importantly, germline induction depends on the coordinated interplay of biochemical signals, genetic and epigenetic regulators, and microenvironmental cues. Niche-mimicking strategies, such as co-culture systems, gonadalconditioned media, three-dimensional scaffolds, and in vivo transplantation, enhance differentiation by partially recapitulating the native germline environment. Emerging approaches, including microRNA modulation, gene overexpression, and photobiomodulation, further improve lineage commitment. Despite these advances, most MSC-derived cells remain at early or pre-meiotic stages, with limited evidence of complete meiosis or functional competence. Major barriers to clinical translation include low differentiation efficiency, lack of standardized protocols, incomplete epigenetic reprogramming, and insufficient functional validation. Addressing these challenges will require the development of integrative, stage-specific differentiation systems that better replicate human germline development, advancing the goal of generating functional human gametes in vitro.

articles.title: Yangjing Granules Ameliorate Cyclophosphamide-induced Spermatogenic Dysfunction via the miR-322/RASSF8/Wnt-β-catenin Signaling Axis.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Guan Y, Liu C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Male infertility, specifically Non-obstructive Azoospermia (NOA), is a major reproductive health issue, and impaired spermatogenesis is a key pathological feature. Yangjing Granules (YJG) have shown therapeutic potential, but molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates whether YJG ameliorates Cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced spermatogenic dysfunction by modulating the miR-322/RASSF8/Wnt-β-catenin signaling axis.
METHODS: Network pharmacology identified YJG- and male infertility-associated targets. A CTXinduced mouse model of spermatogenic dysfunction was developed. Animals were assigned to the control, model, positive control (Wuzi Yanzong Pills), and low-dose (0.63 g/kg), medium-dose (1.26 g/kg), and high-dose (2.52 g/kg) YJG groups. Sperm count and motility were assessed by semen analysis, histopathology by H&E staining, pathway components by qRT-PCR and Western blotting, and miR-322 expression and distribution by FISH.
RESULTS: Network pharmacology identified 78 core targets associated with the therapeutic effects of YJG on male infertility. Medium-dose YJG (1.26 g/kg) improved sperm count and motility and showed more significant effects than the positive control (p < 0.01). Histological examination showed that medium-dose YJG upregulated miR-322 (p < 0.001), suppressed RASSF8 (p < 0.001), and increased PLZF, Cyclin D1, and β-catenin (p < 0.01). FISH confirmed miR-322 upregulation.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that YJG, a multi-component herbal formula, protects spermatogenesis through coordinated regulation of the miR-322/RASSF8/Wnt-β-catenin axis, which is involved in spermatogonial proliferation and differentiation. This pathway may be a therapeutic target for NOA, though clinical studies are needed.
CONCLUSION: YJG may improve CTX-induced spermatogenic dysfunction, in part, by modulating the miR-322/RASSF8/Wnt-β-catenin pathway, providing a molecular basis for its potential clinical application in male infertility.

articles.title: Three-year survival rate and prognostic factors among women with vulvar cancer treated at Ocean Road Cancer Institute in Tanzania: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Almada NJ, Oneko O, Masenga G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Vulvar cancer accounts for approximately 5% of gynecologic malignancies worldwide. Global incidence remains low (0.85 per 100 000 women). Vulvar cancer is under-reported in low- and middle-income countries, and survival data from sub-Saharan Africa remain limited. This study evaluates the 3-year survival rate and associated prognostic factors among women diagnosed with vulvar cancer at Ocean Road Cancer Institute in Tanzania.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 127 women with histologically confirmed vulvar cancer diagnosed between January 2019 and December 2021 was conducted. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox proportional hazards regression identified mortality predictors. Analyses were performed using STATA 17.
RESULTS: Among 127 patients, 61.4% were aged >45 years and 62.2% were HIV-positive. Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was the predominant histological subtype (89%). The 1-, 2-, and 3-year survival rates were 76.0%, 51.3%, and 39.1%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, factors associated with mortality were age greater than 45 years (P = 0.047), lymph node involvement (P = 0.046), advanced FIGO (the International Federation of Gynecology & Obstetrics) stage (P < 0.001), lack of surgical treatment (P = 0.010), and suboptimal treatment (P = 0.004) In multivariate analysis, advanced stage (adjusted hazard ratio, aHR = 2.93, P < 0.001) and suboptimal treatment (aHR = 1.91, P = 0.031) were independent predictors of mortality, with age greater than 45 years showing marginal significance (aHR = 1.62, P = 0.054).
CONCLUSION: Three-year survival among women with vulvar cancer at Ocean Road Cancer Institute was poor (39.1%). SCC was the predominant histology. Advanced FIGO stage, older age, and suboptimal treatment independently predicted mortality.

articles.title: Determinants of non-utilization of cryotherapy among cervical cancer screening-positive women in public health facilities of West Shoa Zone, Oromia, Ethiopia: An unmatched case-control study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Dube DL, Debele R, Yilma D
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer is largely preventable through vaccination, screening, early detection, and treatment of precancerous lesions. Cryotherapy is a simple, effective, and affordable treatment, particularly in low-resource settings. However, some women who screen positive do not receive recommended treatment. Evidence on factors associated with non-utilization of cryotherapy in Ethiopia is limited. The present study identified factors associated with non-utilization among women who screened positive for cervical precancerous lesions in public health facilities in West Shoa Zone, Oromia, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A facility-based unmatched case-control study was conducted from September 1 to November 30, 2022. Cases were screening-positive women who did not receive cryotherapy, while controls were screening-positive women who received cryotherapy. A total of 297 women (74 cases and 223 controls) participated. Data were collected using a pretested interviewer-administered questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS version 26. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with non-utilization. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated.
RESULTS: Non-utilization was significantly associated with being single (aOR = 3.06, 95% CI: 1.12-8.45), no formal education (aOR = 6.70, 95% CI: 2.40-18.72), fewer than three children (aOR = 6.10, 95% CI: 2.38-15.63), poor knowledge (aOR = 5.16, 95% CI: 1.98-13.31), unfavorable attitudes (aOR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.13-6.83), inadequate counseling (aOR = 2.96, 95% CI: 1.41-6.33), and dissatisfaction with screening (aOR = 4.51, 95% CI: 2.03-10.05).
CONCLUSION: Strengthening counseling, health education, and screening services may reduce non-utilization of cryotherapy among women with positive screening results.

articles.title: The impact of mild fundal pressure during vacuum extraction on labor and perinatal outcome.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Dominsky O, Gilboa I, Dangot A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Failed vacuum extraction (VE) is associated with increased adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Mild fundal pressure (MFP) is sometimes applied during VE to assist vaginal delivery and to potentially lower the VE failure rate. We aimed to determine whether the addition of MFP during VE reduces failure rates and its impact on perinatal outcomes.
METHODS: This was a retrospective study at a single tertiary medical center (January 2022 to March 2024). All term singleton VEs were included and stratified by whether or not MFP was applied. MFP was added at the physician's discretion when initial traction was insufficient to achieve adequate fetal descent. The primary outcome was the rate of failed VE and subsequent cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included composite maternal adverse events (obstetric anal sphincter injury, shoulder dystocia, postpartum hemorrhage, or hemoglobin drop ≥3 g/dL) and composite neonatal adverse events (neonatal intensive care unit admission, Apgar score <7 at 5 min, umbilical artery pH <7.1, or birth trauma).
RESULTS: Of 2015 VEs, 555 (27.5%) included MFP. Extraction failed in 0.2% with MFP versus 2.2% without (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.08; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.01-0.61, P = 0.014). Composite maternal outcomes were similar between the groups (19.5% vs. 18.3%; aOR 1.02; 95% CI 0.79-1.32). No difference in composite neonatal outcome was observed (15.7% vs. 12.9%; aOR 1.28; 95% CI 0.97-1.69).
CONCLUSION: The application of MFP during VE was associated with reduced failure of operative vaginal delivery without significantly increased maternal or neonatal morbidity.

articles.title: Implementation of opportunistic salpingectomy during cesarean delivery: Temporal adoption and surgeon-related determinants.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Delli Carpini G, Montanari M, Cicoli C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the implementation of opportunistic salpingectomy for permanent contraception during cesarean delivery, assessing temporal adoption, the association between specialist training and adoption, and surgical feasibility.
