METHODS: A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted on all consecutive patients requesting permanent contraception during cesarean delivery between January 2010 and December 2025. Temporal adoption of bilateral salpingectomy was evaluated using logistic regression and structural change analysis. The correlation between each surgeon's residency completion year and proportion of bilateral salpingectomies performed was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation.
RESULTS: Among 12 648 cesarean deliveries, 801 patients requested permanent contraception. The procedure was completed in 777 (97.0%) cases. Bilateral salpingectomy progressively replaced tubal ligation during the study period, accounting for 90.9% of sterilization procedures in 2025 (odds ratio per calendar year 1.35, 95% confidence interval 1.28-1.42; P < 0.001). No temporal breakpoint in adoption was identified. Adoption varied among surgeons and was associated with the year of completion of residency training (Spearman's ρ = 0.77; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Opportunistic salpingectomy was progressively implemented as the preferred technique for permanent contraception during cesarean delivery without compromising the feasibility of the procedure. Adoption occurred gradually over time and was strongly associated with the period of specialist training, suggesting that differences in training context may influence the implementation of ovarian cancer prevention strategies.

articles.title: Child Abuse and Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Gemma L, Bonerba G, Antonietti M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: About 25% of children will encounter child abuse throughout their lifetime. Child abuse, one of the main components of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), is associated with a variety of physical and mental health problems, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, self-injurious behavior, personality disorder, psychosis, sexually transmitted diseases, and lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). The aim of this systematic review was to evaluate prevalence and pattern of LUTS both in childhood and adulthood associated to a history of child abuse.
METHODS: The systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA statement. A literature search of the Medline, Scopus, and Web of Science databases was performed in May 2026 and included studies published in English up to April 2026. Relevant studies to the review reported the prevalence and urinary symptoms in child and adult patients who have experienced abuse in childhood primarily. The quality of the studies and risk of bias were evaluated using version 2 of ROBINS-I tool.
RESULTS: Out of 676 studies, 19 papers met the inclusion criteria. Six studies explored LUTS in children with past child abuse and neglect, while 13 studies evaluated LUTS in adults with a history of child abuse. Up to 12 years after sexual abuse, abused girls had 2.1 times more diagnoses of urinary problems compared to the general population. In children evaluated for suspected sexual abuse, nocturnal enuresis increased with age, from 13% in 5-9 years to 18.2% in 17-18 years. Childhood traumatic event score was significantly associated with overall LUTS severity and frequency, urgency, and incontinence severity, while ACEs predicted the total number of LUTS. In one study, formal mediation analysis suggested that depression, anxiety, and perceived stress partly mediated the association between childhood trauma and LUTS severity, whereas another study found no mediating effect of negative affect. Limitations of the review are the low quality of studies (13 of 19 retrospective; serious overall risk of bias in 13) and the lack of standardized assessment of abuse and LUTS; overall, the certainty of the evidence is low.
CONCLUSION: A history of childhood abuse appears to be associated with LUTS during childhood, which could also manifest in adulthood. However, given the predominantly retrospective design of the included studies and the heterogeneity of abuse definitions and urinary outcomes, the strength of this evidence…

articles.title: Ruptured Hemorrhagic Ovarian Cyst Mimicking Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy in a Post-Transplant Patient: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Journal of education & teaching in emergency medicine
articles.authors: Shah S, Lewis K, Hseuh A
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The incidence of syncope in the setting of ruptured ectopic pregnancy can vary widely; however, data specifically focusing on syncope as the primary presenting symptom without accompanying abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding are scarce.1,2 Our 23-year-old female patient, who is post-liver transplant and currently on immunosuppressive therapy, experienced syncope without significant pain or bleeding and presented to the ED with stable vital signs. Initial investigations revealed mild left lower quadrant tenderness, a serum beta-hCG of 95 mIU/mL, and moderate free pelvic fluid with a 28 mm left ovarian "cyst" on transvaginal ultrasound. These findings raised concerns for a ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Diagnostic laparoscopy, however, ultimately revealed a ruptured ovarian hemorrhagic cyst. Subsequent negative urine beta-hCG tests confirmed the initial serum beta-hCG as a false positive likely due to heterophile antibody interference, which is common in immunosuppressed patients. This case represents a rare mimic of a ruptured ectopic pregnancy which can occur in post-transplant patients and a nuanced interpretation of clinical workup.
TOPICS: Syncope in reproductive-age women, ruptured ovarian cyst, ectopic pregnancy mimics, false-positive beta-hcg, heterophile antibody interference, emergency ultrasonography, diagnostic laparoscopy, immunosuppression and diagnostic challenges, atypical presentations of gynecologic emergencies.

articles.title: Amniotic Fluid Embolism Successfully Managed With Extracorporeal Life Support and Damage Control Surgery: A Case Report.
articles.authors: Nagano T, Shimono K, Hamada T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amniotic fluid embolism can lead to severe complications, including cardiac arrest, a significant cause of maternal mortality.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 36-year-old woman with postpartum hemorrhage was transported to our hospital. Shortly after her arrival, she experienced cardiac arrest and required immediate extracorporeal life support. A hysterectomy was performed, but persistent bleeding necessitated open abdomen management for damage control to stabilize the patient's condition. On the second day, she was successfully weaned from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, followed by catheter removal and complete abdominal closure. The patient was discharged with no neurological sequelae. Pathological examination of the hysterectomy specimen confirmed amniotic fluid embolism.
CONCLUSION: Extracorporeal life support may be effective as a last resort for cardiac arrest due to amniotic fluid embolism, and damage control surgery may be beneficial for managing intractable bleeding.

articles.title: Urodynamic predictors of daytime and nighttime urinary incontinence in FloRIN and Padua intracorporeal robotic neobladders: Results from two tertiary-care centers at mid-term follow-up.
articles.authors: Anceschi U, Di Maida F, Chiacchio G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional results of intracorporeal orthotopic ileal neobladders (iOINs) may vary depending on the selected neobladder technique. Standardization in reporting continence outcomes is lacking, as objective measurements based on urodynamic assessment remain limited. The aim of this series was to identify urodynamic predictors of daytime and nighttime urinary incontinence for robotic iOINs performed at 2 high-volume centers.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively pooled data from two prospectively maintained institutional robot-assisted radical cystectomy databases covering the period from June 2017 to May 2023. The pooled dataset was queried to identify patients who underwent iOIN reconstruction and completed urodynamic evaluation, yielding a final study population of 94 patients. Baseline data and complete urodynamic profiles were collected. Urodynamic assessment was performed between 6 and 9 months after surgery. Frequencies and proportions were reported for categorical variables, while medians and interquartile ranges were reported for continuous variables. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify predictors of daytime and nighttime urinary incontinence at last follow-up. Multicollinearity among covariates initially considered for multivariable modeling was assessed using variance inflation factor analysis. A 2-sided p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Overall, at a median follow-up of 25 months (interquartile range, 15.5-37.5), 94 patients achieved a complete urodynamic evaluation. On multivariable analysis, female gender (OR, 4.14; 95% CI, 1.37-12.5; p = 0.01) was the only independent predictor of daytime urinary incontinence, whereas cystometric capacity <250 mL showed an association at univariable analysis only and was not retained after multivariable adjustment. Residual peristaltic neobladder activity (OR, 3.44; 95% CI, 1.02-11.5; p = 0.04) was the only independent predictor of nighttime urinary incontinence.
CONCLUSIONS: At urodynamic evaluation, female gender emerged as the only independent predictor of daytime urinary incontinence, whereas residual peristaltic neobladder activity was the only independent predictor of nighttime urinary incontinence. Urodynamic assessment may provide clinically relevant insights into continence evolution after iOIN at mid-term follow-up.

articles.title: Characterization of preoperative patient-reported outcomes in men undergoing benign prostatic hyperplasia surgery.
articles.authors: Song DY, Hines L, Ceraolo C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the literature on benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) often focuses on postoperative patient-reported outcomes (PROs), less attention has been paid to preoperative symptom burden and PROs of men who ultimately undergo surgical treatment. This study provides a detailed descriptive analysis of preoperative PROs across the urinary, sexual, and quality of life domains in a large surgical cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a single-institution BPH database from 2021 to 2024 assessed preoperative International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), Michigan Incontinence Symptom Index, and Sexual Health Inventory for Men score. Descriptive statistics and Mann-Whitney tests were applied to total and subgroup PRO scores.
RESULTS: A total of 1874 patients underwent BPH surgery (average age 71.1). The mean IPSS score was 16.60 (of 35), with a quality-of-life score of 3.89 (of 6). When standardized as a percentage of maximum possible score, storage symptoms were significantly more prominent than voiding symptoms (51.3% vs. 45.4% of maximum, p < 0.0001). The distribution of IPSS severity was 15.6% mild (1-7), 44.2% moderate (8-19), and 40.2% severe (20-35). The mean Michigan Incontinence Symptom Index score was 5.81 (of 32), with 34.9% of patients meeting criteria for preoperative incontinence (total score ≥ 7). Preoperative urge urinary incontinence scores were higher than stress urinary incontinence scores (3.55 vs. 1.48, p < 0.0001). The mean Sexual Health Inventory for Men score was 15.05 (of 25), with 27% severe, 10% moderate, 14% mild-to-moderate, 24% mild, and 25% no erectile dysfunction. Preoperative IPSS storage and total scores were significantly lower in patients who underwent simple prostatectomy, and IPSS quality of life scores were significantly lower in patients who underwent holmium laser enucleation of the prostate, relative to transurethral resection of the prostate.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative BPH patients reported moderately lower urinary tract symptoms, worse storage than voiding symptoms, more urge urinary incontinence than stress urinary incontinence, and mild-to-moderate erectile dysfunction. Understanding baseline PROs enables clinicians to better contextualize postoperative outcomes and manage patient expectations, thereby supporting both optimal care and medicolegal protection in the event of postoperative dissatisfaction.

articles.title: Against All Odds: Repeated Successful Pregnancies in Two Women with Unrepaired Single-Ventricle Physiology.
articles.journal: European journal of case reports in internal medicine
articles.ta: Eur J Case Rep Intern Med
articles.authors: Sugralimova M, Togyzbayeva K, Mukarov M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy in women with unrepaired single-ventricle physiology is rare and associated with substantial maternal and foetal risk. Evidence regarding pregnancy outcomes in this population remains limited.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We report three successful pregnancies in two women with unrepaired double-inlet left ventricle, transposition of the great arteries and valvular/sub-valvular pulmonary stenosis. Both women were classified as modified World Health Organization class IV and received multidisciplinary care throughout pregnancy. Despite complex congenital heart disease, systemic ventricular function and oxygen saturation remained stable. All three pregnancies resulted in live births. However, foetal growth restriction, oligohydramnios, placental insufficiency, prematurity and prolonged neonatal hospitalisation occurred in all pregnancies. One patient successfully completed two consecutive pregnancies without maternal cardiovascular deterioration.
DISCUSSION: Pulmonary outflow obstruction, relatively preserved oxygen saturation and stable systemic ventricular function may have contributed to maternal haemodynamic stability. However, substantial foetal and neonatal morbidity in all three pregnancies underscores that favourable maternal outcomes do not establish pregnancy safety in this population.
CONCLUSION: Carefully selected women with unrepaired single-ventricle physiology and balanced circulation may tolerate pregnancy better than expected, although foetal complications remain common. Multidisciplinary management in specialised congenital heart disease centres is essential.
LEARNING POINTS: Successful pregnancy may be possible in selected women with unrepaired single-ventricle physiology and balanced circulation.Favourable maternal outcomes do not preclude foetal complications, including foetal growth restriction, prematurity and prolonged neonatal hospitalisation.Multidisciplinary management in specialised congenital heart disease centres is essential.

articles.title: Biochemical basis of cervical remodeling in preterm and term labor revealed by Raman spectroscopy.
articles.authors: Gautam R, O'Brien CM, Haugen EJ et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB), affecting approximately 15 million infants annually, is the leading cause of neonatal mortality. However, the underlying mechanisms driving preterm labor (PTL) remain poorly understood. Early detection of biomolecular changes associated with both term and PTL is critical but challenging with current methods. Here, we utilize in vivo Raman spectroscopy (RS) to non-invasively investigate cervical remodeling in mouse models of PTL induced by inflammatory (lipopolysaccharide 'LPS') and hormonal (RU486) pathways, compared with term labor (TL). In vivo RS results revealed etiology-specific biochemical differences associated with cervical remodeling. LPS-induced PTL exhibited increased carbohydrate-associated spectral features, whereas the RU486 model exhibited a distinct protein remodeling pattern that diverged from both LPS-induced PTL and TL. These biochemical signatures aligned with ex vivo imaging and biomechanical assessments of collagen, elastin, and vascularity. RS differentiated PTL from TL with 86% accuracy, outperforming existing techniques. Collectively, these results demonstrate that PTL is not a single biochemical process but comprises distinct remodeling trajectories that can be detected in vivo prior to labor onset. This work establishes a translational framework for Raman-based cervical phenotyping, supporting the future development of non-invasive tools for early PTL detection, etiological stratification, and targeted clinical intervention, to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Comparison of Pregnancy Outcomes from Fresh Transfer of High-Quality Single Blastocysts in Women of Different Ages: A Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Wu Y, Wu S, Chen H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare pregnancy and neonatal outcomes following fresh high-quality single blastocyst transfer (SBT) across different maternal age groups.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 4352 women who underwent fresh high-quality SBT and were divided into three age groups: <30 years (Group A, n = 1939), 30-34 years (Group B, n = 1801), and 35-37 years (Group C, n = 612). Baseline characteristics, pregnancy outcomes, and neonatal outcomes were compared across the groups. Non-live birth was the prespecified primary outcome. For secondary and exploratory outcomes, P values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Bonferroni method.
RESULTS: Women in Group A had a significantly higher live birth rate than those in Group C (56.88% vs 43.79%; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between Groups A and B. The miscarriage rate in Group C (20.94%) was significantly higher than that in Group A (11.48%; P < 0.001); however, the difference compared with Group B (14.06%) did not remain significant after Bonferroni correction. Exploratory differences in preterm birth, gestational diabetes mellitus, and birth defects were also not statistically significant after correction. Multivariable analysis showed that maternal age 35-37 years was independently associated with higher odds of non-live birth (OR = 1.539, 95% CI 1.220-1.942) and adverse pregnancy outcomes (OR = 1.515, 95% CI 1.135-2.024), whereas age 30-34 years was not.
CONCLUSIONS: Among women undergoing fresh high-quality SBT, those aged 30-34 years achieved pregnancy outcomes comparable to those of women aged <30 years, whereas women aged 35-37 years had significantly lower live birth rates and higher miscarriage rates. These findings reflect age-related differences within the SBT population rather than a comparison between transfer strategies. Large-scale prospective multicenter randomized trials are warranted.

articles.title: From Awareness to Practice: Barriers and Facilitators to Saudi Men's Engagement with Pelvic Floor Muscle Training as Conservative Rehabilitation-A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Alghamdi W
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore how Saudi men interpret pelvic floor-related symptoms and perceive pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT), and to identify barriers and facilitators influencing help-seeking and engagement with conservative rehabilitation support.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative explanatory follow-up study was conducted in Al-Baha, Saudi Arabia, with 19 Saudi men recruited from a previous PFMT knowledge, attitudes, and practices study. One-to-one semi-structured interviews were conducted in Arabic, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Four interrelated themes were generated: normalizing or minimizing symptoms; awareness of PFMT without practical understanding; embarrassment and privacy as central barriers; and trust, explanation, and professional support, including physiotherapy, as conditions for potential engagement with PFMT.
CONCLUSION: Limited practical understanding of PFMT, embarrassment, delayed help-seeking, and lack of trusted guidance helped explain why awareness did not translate into practice. Male-sensitive education, practical skills training, privacy-conscious communication, and follow-up may support men's engagement with physiotherapy-led conservative pelvic health care.

articles.title: Nanocarrier-Mediated Immunotherapy for Gynecological Malignancies: Mechanisms, Clinical Translation, and Emerging Nucleic Acid-Based Strategies.
articles.authors: Fu M, Zhao R, Cao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Gynecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, remain major contributors to female morbidity and mortality worldwide. Conventional treatments-surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy-have improved outcomes, but advanced or recurrent disease is still associated with poor prognosis, chemoresistance, and tumor heterogeneity. Immunotherapy has emerged as a transformative strategy because of its specificity and potential for durable responses. However, the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and inefficient delivery of immunotherapeutic agents limit clinical benefit. Nanocarriers, including organic, inorganic, and biomimetic platforms, can improve targeted delivery, sustained release, biocompatibility, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, thereby enhancing immunotherapy. This review summarizes major immunotherapeutic modalities for gynecological cancers-immune checkpoint blockade, CAR-T cell therapy, tumor vaccines, and oncolytic viruses-and the classification and characteristics of commonly used nanocarriers. We focus on nanocarrier-mediated immunotherapeutic mechanisms in ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, and further highlight emerging lipid nanoparticle/mRNA and programmable RNA delivery strategies. Finally, we analyze challenges in clinical translation and provide perspectives for future development, aiming to support fundamental research and clinical application of nano-immunotherapy in gynecological malignancies.

articles.title: Family planning knowledge and practices among physicians in academic centres in Johannesburg, South Africa.
articles.journal: Journal of the colleges of medicine of South Africa
articles.authors: Rothman AB, Bhoora SA, Zamparini J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Specialists in Internal Medicine may manage women of childbearing age, but data regarding their family planning knowledge and prescribing practices are lacking. This study aimed to assess the family planning knowledge and prescribing practices of Consultants and Trainee Physicians (Registrars) in three academic hospitals in Johannesburg and to identify barriers to effective contraceptive counselling for women with chronic medical conditions.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Consultants and Registrars in Internal Medicine at the University of the Witwatersrand. Likert-scale items assessed attitudes to contraceptive prescribing, and single-best-answer questions assessed contraceptive knowledge. Descriptive statistics summarised demographics, and Poisson regression identified factors associated with higher scores; p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Of the 82 respondents (35% response rate), with a median age of 32 years (interquartile range 30-37), 47 (57.3%) were female, and 54 (65.9%) were Registrars. Fifty respondents (61%) had high attitude scores, but the median knowledge was 53.8%, and only 34/82 (41.5%) respondents achieved the pragmatic threshold of ≥ 10/13 for adequate knowledge. Key barriers were high workload and lack of sexual and reproductive health training. Married respondents were more likely than single respondents to have high attitude scores (PRR 1.83, 95% CI 1.05-3.17), while male doctors had higher practice scores than female doctors (PRR 1.92, 95% CI 1.14-3.26). No variables were associated with high objective assessment scores.
CONCLUSION: Gaps in contraceptive knowledge and decision-making amongst Consultants and Trainee Physicians highlight the need for improved education to support comprehensive care for women of childbearing age, especially those with medical comorbidities.
CONTRIBUTION: This study highlights the importance of collaboration between Internal Medicine and Gynaecological specialities in a combined effort to reduce unwanted and high-risk pregnancies to promote the overall health of women, especially those living with medical conditions.

articles.title: Endometrial microbiota in IVF patients: Lactobacillus dominance, pathogen prevalence and recurrence after treatment.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Campos D, Diez-Tercero L, Berenguer C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The endometrial microbiota has been recently described as a Lactobacillus dominant environment and lower levels of this genus have been associated with a decrease in implantation and pregnancy rates. Moreover, the detection and overgrowth of several types of microorganisms in the female reproductive tract including bacterial, fungal and viral pathogens have been associated with complications in pregnancy such as miscarriage or preterm birth. Nevertheless, the prevalence of alterations in the endometrial microbiota of patients undergoing infertility treatment has not been thoroughly described yet.
METHODS: The presence of 36 microorganisms including bacteria, fungi and viruses with relevance in reproductive outcome was quantified in endometrial biopsies by Real-Time qPCR. Moreover, a second biopsy was performed in 86 patients after personalized antimicrobial and/or probiotic treatment to evaluate the efficacy of the treatment.
RESULTS: An altered microbiota was detected in 87.52% of the samples analyzed. A significantly higher presence of pathogens was detected in dysbiotic samples (Lactobacillus < 90%, p<0.01). More precisely, opportunistic bacterial pathogens were more frequently associated with dysbiosis (p<0.0001). Ureaplasma parvum and Gardnerella vaginalis were the most frequently detected bacterial pathogens, both individually and in combination, while Candida spp and Cytomegalovirus were detected in 8.2% and 1.6% of the samples. In patients that performed a second biopsy after personalized antimicrobial and probiotic treatment, a significant decrease in pathogen presence was observed (p<0.001), although Ureaplasma parvum showed recurrence in some patients.
DISCUSSION: Our findings suggest that imbalances in the endometrial microbiota are frequent in patients undergoing IVF treatments. Identifying these imbalances and treating them accordingly could potentially improve endometrial environment in these patients.

articles.title: FemTech and the equity imperative: no woman left behind.
articles.authors: Mfeka-Nkabinde NG
articles.abstract: FemTech, a rapidly expanding sector of technologies focused on women's health, is an emerging global health megatrend. These technologies impact how menstrual health, fertility, contraception, pregnancy, menopause, and sexual wellbeing are understood and managed. From a health systems perspective, FemTech is best conceptualised as a digitally enabled women's health sector that predominantly operationalises personalised, data-driven care. Most commercial FemTech platforms rely on user-generated data, behavioural analytics, and symptom tracking to individualise recommendations. Using insights from research on young women's sexuality, gendered power relations, and reproductive experiences in low- and middle-income countries, I argue that FemTech can realise its full potential when embedded within equity-driven care models. The paper contrasts the creation and utilisation of FemTech in high-income countries and low- and middle-income countries, and concludes by providing strategies for equity-oriented FemTech.

articles.title: Association of antenatal perceived stress and depressive symptoms with birth weight and gestational age: a prospective cohort study within the Action Against Stunting Hub, India.
articles.authors: Thomas J, Fernandez Rao S, Dasi T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on the association of pregnancy specific perceived stress and depressive symptoms with adverse birth outcomes, including preterm birth (PTB) and low birth weight (LBW), remains limited and inconsistent in India.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of elevated perceived stress and elevated depressive symptoms during the third trimester of pregnancy and examine their associations with birth weight, gestational age, low birth weight (LBW), and preterm birth (PTB) in an Indian cohort.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted within the Action Against Stunting Hub mother child cohort in Hyderabad, India between June 2021 and December 2022. Of the 717 pregnant women enrolled in their third trimester, 616 with available psychosocial data were included in the analysis. Perceived stress, depressive symptom scores and social support were assessed using Perceived Stress Scale 10(PSS-10), Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and Multidimensional Scale for Perceived Social Support (MSPSS) respectively. Gestational age was determined using a hierarchical approach and birth weight was measured within 12 h of delivery. Associations between maternal perceived stress and depressive symptoms scores with birth outcomes were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses (p < 0.05).
RESULTS: The prevalence of elevated perceived stress and elevated depressive symptoms among pregnant women during the third trimester was 17.4 and 21.4%, respectively. After adjusting for covariates, each one-point increase in maternal perceived stress score (β = -5.84 g (95%CI -11.49, -0.19, p = 0.04)) and depressive symptom scores (β = -7.45g (95%CI -13.72, -1.17, p = 0.02)) was significantly associated with lower birth weight, but not with gestational age. However, no association between maternal perceived stress and depressive symptom scores was observed with either LBW and PTB using multivariable logistic regression.
CONCLUSION: Third trimester maternal perceived stress and depressive symptom scores were associated with modest reductions in birth weight but not with gestational age, LBW, or PTB. Although the observed effect on birth weight was small, these findings highlight the importance of recognizing and addressing maternal psychological well being during antenatal care.

articles.title: Endocrine life after breast cancer: navigating hormonal challenges from treatment to survivorship.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.authors: Soroush MG, Badamchizadeh S, Sarvari M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the hormonal challenges that breast cancer survivors encounter, with a particular emphasis on endocrine treatment side effects and how they affect survivorship.
RECENT FINDINGS: Endocrine therapy is the mainstay for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, and improvements in detection and treatment have improved survival. Premature menopause, bone loss, metabolic dysfunction, and sexual health problems are examples of treatment-induced side effects that have been shown to impair adherence and quality of life.
SUMMARY: Long-term endocrine problems that profoundly impact health and well-being are experienced by breast cancer survivors. Pharmacological, non-hormonal, and lifestyle interventions are among the multidisciplinary approaches necessary for effective management, aiming to increase adherence, reduce recurrence, and improve overall survivorship outcomes.

articles.title: The improvement effect of androgen priming on fertility in patients with diminished ovarian reserve and its impact on in vitro fertilization outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Li X, Sui C, Zhang B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the effect of using androgen supplements (including transdermal testosterone gel and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)) to priming androgens in the body and improve fertility in patients with diminished ovarian reserve (DOR).
METHODS: Electronic searches were conducted on seven databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Springer, VIP Information, Wanfang, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), to search for studies published as of July 5, 2026. Randomized controlled trails (RCTs) and non-randomized controlled trails of using androgen supplements (i.e. dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and transdermal testosterone gel (TTG)) to intervene in improving fertility and IVF outcomes in patients with DOR were embodied. The study applied systematic review and meta-analysis methods to systematically summarize the main outcome measures, including FSH, AMH, AFC, retrieved oocytes, and clinical pregnancy rate. In addition, indicators such as the number of fertilized embryos, top-quality day-3 embryos, live birth rate and miscarriage rate were also evaluated.
RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 14 studies with 2132 participants. Analyses of RCTs and non-randomized controlled trials were conducted separately. A comprehensive analysis of existing evidence indicated that androgen supplementation, including DHEA and TTG, can improve count of retrieved oocytes [RCTs (MD = 0.79, 95% CI [0.50,1.09], p<0.00001)]. A retrospective analysis of non-randomized controlled trials showed that androgen supplementation can significantly increase the number of Top-quality day-3 embryos (MD 0.47, [95% CI: [0.28, 0.66], p < 0.00001), the count of fertilized embryos (MD 0.78, [95% CI: [0.49, 1.06], p < 0.00001), and clinical pregnancy rate (OR = 2.23, 95% CI [1.49,3.36], p = 0.0001). Besides, androgen supplementation showed Intervention with androgen supplements for 2 months was beneficial for retrieving more oocytes (p < 0.05) through the results in RCT. And also showed a more significant improvement in retrieved oocytes and metaphase II oocytes in DOR patients with an average age of over 40 years (p < 0.05). The subgroup analysis results indicated that the application of GnRH antagonists as IVF stimulation protocol was more beneficial in increasing the number of retrieved oocytes than the adopt of GnRH agonists.The sensitivity analysis concludes that our conclusion is robust.
CONCLUSIONS: Androgen priming (including DHEA and TTG) may be beneficial for…

articles.title: GnRH antagonist-induced ovarian suppression does not protect the ovarian reserve from cyclophosphamide chemotherapy in tumour-bearing mice.
articles.authors: Lewis YM, Herszberg D, Fowler K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues are used clinically to induce ovarian suppression during chemotherapy treatment and are proposed to protect the ovaries from chemotherapy-induced damage, yet their efficacy and underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. While most preclinical and clinical studies have focused on GnRH agonists, far less is known about the effects of GnRH antagonists in this context, despite their more rapid and direct suppression of gonadotrophin signaling.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used the GnRH antagonist degarelix to induce ovarian suppression in an orthotopic tumour-bearing mouse model. We then evaluated whether degarelix protected against cyclophosphamide-induced ovarian damage in reproductively young and aged mice receiving one or two chemotherapy doses. Ovarian function was assessed by quantifying ovarian volume, corpora lutea number (a marker of ovulation), and serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels, as well as follicle enumeration and histological assessment of ovarian fibrosis.
RESULTS: Degarelix suppressed ovulatory activity, as indicated by reduced corpora lutea number and ovarian volume. However, degarelix was associated with increased ovarian fibrosis in young mice treated with single-dose cyclophosphamide and failed to protect the ovarian reserve following either single or two doses of cyclophosphamide in both age groups. Moreover, degarelix did not prevent reductions in circulating AMH, with all treatment groups displaying reduced AMH levels compared with controls in young mice.
CONCLUSIONS: Together, our findings do not support a protective effect of GnRH antagonist treatment against cyclophosphamide-induced ovarian damage.

articles.title: A study on the correlation between serum anti-Müllerian hormone levels in male participants of pre-pregnancy genetic health checkup in Qingyang District, Chengdu City.
articles.authors: Kou H, Gui C, Liu F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the relationship between serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels and semen quality in men undergoing preconception health checkups.
METHODS: A total of 145 male preconception patients were enrolled. Semen parameters, including sperm kinetics, were measured via computer-aided sperm analysis (CASA), and serum AMH levels were detected using chemiluminescence immunoassay. Spearman's correlation and multivariate linear regression analyses were used for statistical analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 145 men were included in the study. The median serum AMH level was 8.79 ng/ml, with an interquartile range of (5.25- 11.25) ng/mL. Spearman's rank correlation analysis showed that serum AMH levels were positively correlated with total sperm count (r = 0.268, P = 0.001), sperm concentration (r = 0.219, P = 0.008), total PR count (r = 0.225, P = 0.006), VCL (r = 0.196, P = 0.018), VSL (r = 0.179, P = 0.032), VAP (r = 0.164, P = 0.049), and STR (r = 0.165, P = 0.047). Multivariate linear regression analysis showed that after adjusting for confounding factors, such as age and abstinence days, serum AMH remained independently associated with total sperm count (β = 0.549, P< 0.001), total PR count (β = 0.584, P< 0.001), and VCL (β = 0.572, P = 0.005).
CONCLUSION: Serum AMH levels in men showed weak but statistically significant positive correlations with total sperm count (r = 0.268), total PR count (r = 0.225), and selected sperm kinetic parameters (r = 0.164-0.196). After adjusting for confounders, AMH remained independently associated with total sperm count, total PR count, and VCL, although the overall explanatory power was limited. These findings suggest that serum AMH may have a limited role as an adjunctive biomarker in male fertility assessment; however, its clinical utility is uncertain, given the weak strength of the associations. Large-scale prospective studies are required to validate these findings and determine whether AMH provides incremental value beyond conventional semen analysis.

articles.title: CRISPR-enabled biosensing of cancer-associated DNA methylation in cell-free DNA: molecular architectures, molecular sampling constraints, and translational biosensor engineering.
articles.authors: Luo H, Huang X, Yu Q et al.
articles.abstract: DNA methylation in circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) provides cancer-associated and tissue-of-origin information complementary to mutation-based liquid biopsy. Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based sensing is challenging because 5-methylcytosine (5 mC) generally preserves Watson-Crick base pairing and is not inherently resolved by sequence-programmed CRISPR-associated (Cas) proteins. This targeted narrative review examines how methylated and unmethylated molecules are distinguished and converted into Cas-readable outputs under fragmented, low-input cfDNA conditions. We organize the literature into four discrimination routes comprising sequence conversion, enzymatic gating, affinity-assisted recognition, and native-state Cas modulation. Engineered molecular transduction is considered separately as a downstream enabling layer. We compare readouts in terms of quantitative fidelity and integration requirements. Sequence-conversion and enzymatic-gating systems have the broadest analytical evidence among the identified studies, largely from in vitro experiments. Direct affinity-assisted 5 mC-to-Cas sensing remains sparsely studied, and evidence for native-state sensing in patient-derived cfDNA is limited to exploratory observational comparisons. No native-state Cas methylation assay identified in this review has established clinically usable diagnostic performance. Reported analytical limits of detection and methylation-fraction discrimination cannot be extrapolated to clinical sensitivity without accounting for input, recovery, fragmentation, background, and decision thresholds. Translation requires validated biomarkers, fragment-matched calibration, orthogonal reference testing, reproducible device integration, and independent evaluation of locked assays in intended-use populations.

articles.title: Predictors of Preterm Delivery in the COVID-19 Era: A Retrospective Cohort Study of a Large, Integrated HealthSystem.
articles.authors: Raisler K, Jefferson CR, Kim S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preterm delivery is the leading cause of perinatal mortality and long-term neonatal morbidity in the United States, and rates are rising. Research has shown that COVID-19 infection may increase the possibility of preterm delivery. However, these studies disproportionately focus on third trimester and iatrogenic cases, often overlooking risk across the entire pregnancy or without adjusting for prior preterm delivery and sociodemographic factors. To address these gaps, the authors investigated the association between COVID-19 at any point in pregnancy and preterm delivery while exploring other predictors of preterm delivery.
METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study of members pregnant between March 2020 and March 2021, comparing odds of preterm delivery for those with and without COVID-19. Using logistic regression and χ2 tests, the authors explored associations between preterm delivery and other sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Data were abstracted from electronic medical records.
RESULTS: Of 14,250 participants, 994 (7%) experienced COVID-19 infection during pregnancy. Overall, 1313 (9%) had preterm delivery. In univariate logistic regression analyses, those with COVID-19 were more likely to be < 35 years old, Hispanic or Black, non-English-speaking, obese, and multiparous. COVID-19 infection during pregnancy was associated with increased odds of preterm delivery in the authors' unadjusted model but not in the multivariable adjusted model. Being ≥ 35 years old, Hispanic, Black, nulliparous, hypertensive, immunocompromised, or having a prior preterm delivery or gestational or chronic diabetes were significantly associated with higher odds of preterm delivery in the authors' multivariable model.
CONCLUSION: COVID-19 infection throughout pregnancy was not associated with increased odds of preterm delivery. Racial disparities and other key covariates like history of preterm delivery may confound the reported increase in preterm delivery.

articles.title: Early Postpartum Oral Glucose Tolerance Testing During Delivery Hospitalization in Women With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Watanabe T, Ikehata E, Kamoshida T et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Because completion of the guideline-recommended postpartum oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) remains low, we evaluated the feasibility of inpatient 75-g OGTT among women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and described abnormal glucose tolerance and associated factors.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 248 singleton pregnancies complicated by GDM delivered between January 2021 and December 2025. The primary outcome was inpatient OGTT completion. Abnormal glucose tolerance was defined by Japan Diabetes Society criteria as either borderline type or diabetic type. Secondary outcomes were the distribution of glucose tolerance categories and factors associated with an abnormal result.
RESULTS: Inpatient postpartum OGTT was completed in 236/248 eligible pregnancies (95.2%). Of those, 171 (72.5%), 61 (25.8%), and 4 (1.7%) had normal-type, borderline-type, and diabetic-type results, respectively; 65 (27.5%) were classified as abnormal. In the multivariable complete-case model (n = 223), maternal age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.11 per year, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-1.20), number of positive antepartum OGTT points (aOR 1.75 per point, 95% CI 1.05-2.92), light-for-dates birth (aOR 3.89, 95% CI 1.11-13.62), and heavy-for-dates birth (aOR 3.28, 95% CI 1.43-7.55) were independently associated with an abnormal result.
CONCLUSIONS: Inpatient postpartum OGTT was feasible in this Japanese tertiary-center setting and identified early dysglycemia. Inpatient testing may support counseling and follow-up planning. However, this study did not evaluate whether it improved completion compared with conventional care or whether inpatient results predicted subsequent glucose tolerance. Timely postpartum reassessment remains necessary.

articles.title: Selective miRNA network modulation by quinolone derivative CF5 is associated with potent anti-ovarian cancer activity.
articles.authors: Servillo G, Di-Iacovo N, Pieroni S et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a leading cause of gynaecological cancer mortality, largely due to late diagnosis and limited options for recurrent disease. Dysregulation of microRNAs (miRNAs) contributes to tumour progression, highlighting the potential of pharmacological strategies that restore miRNA-mediated control. Here, we describe CF5, a fluoroquinolone derivative developed from enoxacin, the first-in-class small-molecule enhancer of miRNA processing (SMER), as a potent anticancer agent with a favourable selectivity profile. CF5 consistently inhibits proliferation and migration in ovarian cancer cells, restricts long-term clonogenic survival, and retains activity following TRBP knockdown, indicating reduced dependence on canonical SMER-associated pathways. Differential miRNA profiling identifies a CF5-associated miRNA expression pattern involving a discrete subset of upregulated miRNAs. Integrative bioinformatics and functional analyses reveal convergence on oncogenic regulatory processes, with downstream target genes including ALDOA, NACC1, VAV3, and PRRG4. Analysis of transcriptomic datasets shows that these genes are overexpressed in tumours and treatment with CF5 is able to restore levels to those found in healthy tissues. Together, these findings demonstrate that CF5 orchestrates targeted post-transcriptional regulatory networks involving proliferation, survival, metabolic and migratory programs. By combining enhanced biological activity with a distinct response to TRBP depletion, CF5 represents a new generation of miRNA-modulating compounds capable of exploiting molecular vulnerabilities in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma. These results support further development of CF5 and related fluoroquinolone derivatives as promising therapeutics targeting post-transcriptional regulatory networks in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Age-related changes in the expression of human endometrial receptivity factors osteopontin, CD44, and HOXA10 at the window of implantation.
articles.authors: Makrygiannakis F, Marmara M, Saare M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Embryo quality is well established as a factor of infertility with increasing age. Blastocyst implantation receptivity is highest during the window of implantation (WOI). Although the expression of receptivity factors at the WOI is critical for optimal embryo implantation, the impact of female aging on their expression remains unclear.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Endometrial tissue slides from healthy fertile women aged 25-46y, at the WOI (day 7-8 post-LH surge), were stained and analyzed by immunohistochemistry for receptivity factors OPN, CD44, and HOXA10. The analysis was also performed by dividing the samples into two age groups: 25-32 years and 33-46 years.
RESULTS: Data showed a statistically significant linear decrease in the expression of the proteins OPN, CD44, and HOXA10 (p < 0.0001, p = 0.0001, and p = 0.0002, respectively) when plotted against women's age. OPN, CD44, and HOXA10 showed linearity with increasing age (R2 = 0.3209, R2 = 0.1265, R2 = 0.1257). Furthermore, a significant decrease in the three proteins was observed between the two age groups, 25-32 years and 33-46 years (OPN: p = 0.0002; CD44: p = 0.0011; HOXA10: p = 0.0273, respectively).
CONCLUSION: Endometrial receptivity factors present a negative correlation with increasing age in human endometrial stromal cells, in vitro, at the WOI.

articles.title: Modifiable Factors Associated with Trajectories of Health-Related Quality of Life in Women from Midlife to Older Adulthood: The Study of Women's Health Across the Nation (SWAN).
articles.authors: Avis NE, Miller RG, Colvin A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Midlife health and psychosocial status impact health-related quality of life (HRQL), but few studies have examined these associations from midlife to older adulthood. The current analyses aimed to (1) identify HRQL trajectories in women from midlife to older adulthood, (2) determine factors associated with HRQL trajectories, and (3) examine whether these associations change over time.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey Physical (PCS) and Mental Component Summaries (MCS) from 2002 to 2023 (ages 48-79 years) in 2,636 women from The Study of Women's Health Across the Nation (SWAN). We used locally weighted scatterplot smoothing to estimate PCS and MCS mean trajectories as a function of age and group-based trajectory models to identify trajectory subgroups. Associations between trajectory group membership and sociodemographic, health-related, menopausal, lifestyle and anthropometric, and psychosocial variables were estimated through mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Mean PCS declined 6.6 points (51.6-45), and MCS increased 3.0 points (50-53) with age. We identified four PCS groups (one stable and three decreasing) and three MCS groups (two stable and one increasing). Compared to the high-stable groups, other PCS and MCS groups were associated with worse health factors. Most associations were stable over time, but financial strain worsened faster in more adverse trajectories. Positive affect and social support increased in the high-stable PCS and MCS groups, while negative affect improved faster in the low, late-increasing MCS group.
CONCLUSIONS: These results extend previous research by characterizing heterogeneous HRQL trajectories and identifying potentially modifiable behavioral and health targets for physical and mental HRQL in women from midlife to older adulthood.

articles.title: Single-Particle ICP-MS Enabled Multiplex Digital Detection of Nucleic Acids via Feedback Recombinase Polymerase Amplification.
articles.authors: Dai F, He M, Yuan G et al.
articles.abstract: Digital droplet assays, with their single-molecule sensitivity, hold great promise for early disease diagnosis by enabling precise biomarker quantification and the generation of patient-specific molecular profiles. Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) has shown its great potential in the quantification of biomolecules with elemental labeling strategies. However, the development of ICP-MS-based digital assays has been limited, primarily due to the challenge of efficiently anchoring elemental labels within droplets. To address this, we developed a feedback recombinase polymerase amplification (F-RPA)-based digital analyzer via a facile droplet generator and combined it with single particle (sp)-ICP-MS for the quantitative analysis of human papillomavirus (HPV) genetic markers. In this system, HPV DNA molecules are randomly partitioned across tens of thousands of agarose droplets, following a Poisson distribution. Individual encapsulated target DNA molecules initiate on-demand F-RPA amplification and anchoring of elemental tags for subsequent signal transduction. Leveraging the discrete event counting characteristics and multi-element analytical capabilities of sp-ICP-MS, the digital F-RPA assay achieved highly sensitive and multiplexed analysis, with detection limits as low as 20 copies/μL for HPV16 and 9 copies/μL for HPV18 DNA. The method was validated by quantifying the HPV DNA load in cervical cancer cell lines and further applied to clinical cervical swab samples, where it identified 26 HPV16-positive and 20 HPV18-positive cases with 100% precision. This digital F-RPA sp-ICP-MS system emerges as a robust diagnostic platform for trace biomarker analysis, significantly advancing the role of sp-ICP-MS in digital droplet detection and clinical diagnosis.

articles.title: Cyclic Electro-Hydrodynamic Stacking Enables fg/μL-Level DNA Sizing for Ultra-Sensitive Cell-Free Nucleosome Analysis in Liquid Biopsy.
articles.authors: Toublanc M, Boutonnet A, Mano M et al.
articles.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) analysis in blood plasma provides valuable diagnostic information for cancer detection, transplant rejection monitoring, and prenatal screening. However, the low abundance of cfDNA remains a major analytical challenge that can limit sensitivity and reproducibility across studies. Here, we present an improved BIAbooster platform for DNA sizing that incorporates up to 10 cycles of sample loading and electrohydrodynamic stacking, achieving a limit of detection of 3 fg/μL, corresponding to a 15-20-fold lower detection limit than highly sensitive commercial platforms such as FemtoPulse. This enhanced sensitivity, achieved through repeated loading/electrohydrodynamic stacking cycles that enable processing of ∼8 μL in a single run, allows direct quantification of immunocaptured epigenetically modified cfDNA. Using this approach, we show that immunocaptured fractions are enriched in higher-molecular-weight fragments, suggesting that enrichment workflows may deplete diagnostically relevant cfDNA populations. These findings demonstrate the value of high-sensitivity DNA sizing for cf-nucleosome analysis and establish its utility for liquid biopsy workflows.

articles.title: Comparative safety of dolutegravir-based and second-line antiretroviral therapy on adverse birth outcomes: a retrospective cohort study of HIV-positive women in Nigeria.
articles.authors: Hedima EW, Aliyu AI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) has shown to reduce mother child transmission of HIV. This necessitates robust evidence on the comparative safety of different regimens on birth outcomes. There is paucity of evidence on specific cART regimens and adverse birth outcomes in the Nigerian context.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 420 HIV-positive pregnant women. The participants received antenatal and delivery care from 2018 to 2023 at the State Specialist Hospital in Gombe State, Nigeria. Participants were categorized based on their antenatal cART regimen: first-line (Dolutegravir-based regimen (DTG-based)) or second-line (Protease inhibitor (PI)-based regimen). The primary outcomes were neonatal death, low birth weight (LBW), preterm birth, and stillbirth. Adjusted odd ratios were estimated to compare risk of adverse outcomes across HIV regimens, and multivariate logistic regression was used to identify predictors of adverse outcomes. A p-value less than 0.05 (95% confidence interval) was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The analyses revealed no evidence of a significant association between PI-based ART and adverse birth outcomes compared with DTG-based ART while number of pregnancies (p = 0.02), delivery mode (p = 0.03), virological status during pregnancy (p < 0.005) and occupation (p =0.018) were significantly associated with adverse birth outcomes. Crucially, an unsuppressed maternal viral load (>1000 copies/mL) was the strongest independent predictor of adverse outcomes (adjusted Odds Ratio [aOR]=31.22; 95% CI: 10.29-94.72).
CONCLUSION: This study provided evidence on the safety of first-line and second-line cART regimens among Nigerian women. Infants born to mothers on these regimens have no risks for adverse birth outcomes. The most critical modifiable risk factor was unsuppressed viral load during pregnancy. These findings underscore the paramount importance of achieving viral suppression for optimizing birth outcomes and suggest that regimen choice should be carefully considered alongside maternal virological status.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Risk factors for metabolic syndrome: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
articles.authors: Cui A, Xiong W, Huang T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) - a cluster of conditions including hypertension, dyslipidemia, insulin resistance, and central obesity - affects 20-30% of adults globally and elevates risks for type 2 diabetes mellitus and cardiovascular disease. Although extensive research has been conducted on individual risk factors, a comprehensive synthesis of existing evidence is urgently required to guide the development of targeted, multi-component prevention strategies.
METHODS: To identify observational studies which assessed the association between MetS development and risk factors, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Database were searched from inception to May 2025. A random or fix-effects model was utilized to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs), relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). Statistical heterogeneity across included studies was quantified using the I² index, where values > 50% were considered indicative of substantial heterogeneity. The Egger's test or funnel graph was used to assess the methodological quality.
RESULTS: This umbrella review systematically analyzed 72 meta-analyses from 7,367 unique articles to evaluate associations between 101 factors and MetS development. 76 positively correlated factors and 25 negatively correlated factors were identified from the included studies and categorized into five distinct domains: lifestyle behaviors, pre-existing diseases, individual characteristics, environmental exposures, and occupational factors. From the selected studies, the most significantly positive correlation with MetS was overweight and obesity. Parental history of MetS, gestational diabetes mellitus, high screen time, and shift work were also exhibited high degrees of correlation with MetS. In our study, we also identified several modifiable dietary factors exhibited negative correlations with MetS. High-fiber diet consumption, regular nut intake, and adherence to a Mediterranean diet had higher association with MetS.
CONCLUSIONS: MetS pathophysiology is multifactorial. Comprehensive evidence shows that multiple distinct factors performed significantly associations with MetS. Unhealthy dietary patterns, sedentary behavioral patterns, and adverse occupational patterns are the primary modifiable associated factors for MetS. Despite the limited quality of current supporting evidence, targeted intervention strategies for these factors should be prioritized in public health policies to mitigate MetS at the…

articles.title: Breast density and risk factors for interval and screen-detected breast cancers: a case-case analysis of the Breast Cancer Now Generations Study, UK.
articles.authors: Johns L, Brayley M, Frost R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interval breast cancers (IBC), diagnosed between routine screening rounds, tend to have a worse prognosis than screen-detected breast cancers (SDBC). Identifying risk factors for IBCs is critical for improving early detection and developing risk-stratified screening strategies to reduce their incidence. We evaluated associations of breast density, reproductive, hormonal, lifestyle and medical factors with IBC compared to SDBC in a large UK cohort.
METHODS: Analyses included 1,940 women diagnosed with breast cancer between 2004 and 2018 after enrolment in the Breast Cancer Now Generations Study, a prospective UK cohort linked to the National Health Service Breast Screening Programme. Pre-diagnostic risk factors were collected at enrolment, and breast density was estimated from pre-diagnostic mammograms using Cumulus in a subset of 1,191 cases. Risk factor associations with density were estimated using linear regression models. We identified 1,185 SDBCs and 755 IBCs included in logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for associations between risk factors and IBC, adjusting for age at diagnosis, time since recruitment and year of diagnosis, breast density and tumour characteristics.
RESULTS: Higher breast density was associated with later age at menarche, nulliparity, breastfeeding, history of benign breast disease (BBD), alcohol consumption, lower body mass index (BMI) at recruitment and at age 20, and current use of menopausal hormone therapy (MHT). In a fully-adjusted model, IBC risk was lower for overweight women (OR (95% CI ) = 0.74 (0.58-0.93) vs. normal weight), and higher for high breast density (2.13 (1.44-3.17) for Q4 vs. Q1), later age at menopause (1.60 (1.02-2.50) 55 + vs. < 50), current MHT use (1.41 (1.04-1.91) vs. never users), history of BBD (1.36 (1.11-1.68)), being underweight at age 20 (1.65 (1.14-2.38) vs. normal weight), family history of breast cancer (1.26 (1.00-1.58)) and ever using oral contraceptives (1.25 (0.93-1.69) vs. never). These risk factor associations were independent of tumour characteristics.
CONCLUSIONS: Breast density and several risk factors independently increase the likelihood of IBC, highlighting opportunities for tailored screening strategies to enhance early detection and reduce IBCs incidence.

articles.title: Before-and-after evaluation of an IDEA-based standardized ultrasound image documentation protocol for deep endometriosis ultrasound assessment.
articles.authors: Wei N, Li X, Sun R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between implementation of a standardized endocavitary sonography image-documentation protocol, developed in accordance with the International Deep Endometriosis Analysis (IDEA) consensus, and the diagnostic performance for compartment-specific deep endometriosis (DE) lesions, and to explore its feasibility as a component of routine ultrasound quality assurance.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective before-and-after controlled study included 783 patients who underwent dedicated ultrasound examination for DE at Peking University Shenzhen Hospital between January 2023 and September 2025 and subsequently underwent laparoscopic surgery within 6 months with complete surgical and pathological confirmation. According to the implementation of the standardized image documentation protocol in November 2024, patients were divided into a pre-implementation group and a post-implementation group. The protocol was developed based on the four-steps scanning framework of the IDEA consensus and required mandatory documentation of 19 standard sections and standardized recording of procedural information. The documentation rate of standard sections, examination duration, and diagnostic performance indices were compared between groups.
RESULTS: A total of 783 patients were included (pre-implementation, n=267; post-implementation, n=516), with comparable baseline characteristics. Following protocol introduction, documentation rates significantly improved for 15 of 19 core ultrasound sections after Bonferroni correction (P<0.0026), with absolute gains of 47.9%-63.3% for previously underreported sections including the uterovesical pouch, ureters, rectovaginal septum, and lower rectum. Median examination duration remained unchanged (719 vs. 723 seconds; P=0.529).For deep endometriosis at posterior compartment sites, specificity increased significantly for pouch of Douglas obliteration (80.0% to 93.9%, P<0.001) and rectosigmoid colon involvement (79.9% to 90.0%, P<0.001), with both differences remaining robust after multiple comparison correction. Sensitivity for the uterine sliding sign improved from 74.0% to 95.1% (P<0.001). Although adenomyosis detection sensitivity also rose (82.5% to 94.9%, P=0.003), adenomyosis and ovarian endometrioma are considered endometriosis-related manifestations rather than DE-specific anatomical sites.In a subgroup analysis of 14 patients with ureteral DE, the mean ureteral diameter near the bladder orifice…

articles.title: Knowledge of and preferred legal grounds for abortion in Kenya: a national cross-sectional telephone survey.
articles.authors: Juma K, Mutuku E, Athero S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inadequate knowledge of abortion law in restrictive settings impedes women's access to safe services and engenders poor abortion perception and stigma among the general population. There is limited understanding of the public's knowledge and support for abortion in Kenya. This study aimed to assess public knowledge of the current abortion law, factors associated with accurate knowledge, and to characterize the preferred conditions under which abortion should be legally permitted in Kenya.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey using mobile phones to collect data from adults aged 18 or older. The sample was drawn from a database maintained by a mobile survey provider, with over 12 million telephone numbers across Kenya. We used a random digit dialing approach to select and recruit participants. Trained research assistants administered telephonic interviews using a structured questionnaire that had questions assessing knowledge of conditions for legally sanctioned abortion and legal conditions under which they would support abortion. We summarized continuous variables into means (standard deviations) and medians (interquartile range), while categorical variables (including for the outcomes) as proportions. We performed a survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression model to assess associations between sociodemographic variables (such as age, sex, marital status, education among others) and the knowledge levels of abortion laws. We also conducted latent class analysis to characterize the preferred legal grounds around abortion by the Kenyan population.
RESULTS: Of the 8,942 respondents, 76%, 74%, and 33% knew that the Kenyan law permits abortion when a woman's life or health is at risk and when the pregnancy results from rape, respectively. Relative to males, females had 2% higher knowledge of abortion law (score ratio 1.02; 95% CI: 1.01-1.03), while those with secondary and university education were associated with 6% (score ratio 1.06; 95% CI: 1.01-1.12) and 8% (score ratio 1.08; 95% CI: 1.03-1.14) higher knowledge of abortion law respectively, compared to those with no education. Most respondents indicated support for abortion when a woman's life (71%), health (64%), or mental health (43%) is at risk. About one-third would support abortions when pregnancy results from rape (29%) or incest (28%). The latent class analysis showed that most respondents (41%) preferred legalization of abortion for health and life reasons, whereas…

articles.title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting endometrial polyp recurrence after hysteroscopic polypectomy.
articles.authors: Li L, Lin M, Lin Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial polyps (EP) are common, and hysteroscopic polypectomy is the reference treatment, but recurrence is frequent. This study aimed to identify risk factors for recurrence and to develop and internally validate a nomogram for individual postoperative risk stratification.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, women with a histologically confirmed benign EP treated by hysteroscopic polypectomy between May 2023 and May 2025 and followed for at least 12 months were analyzed. The primary outcome was recurrence within 12 months. Variables were selected by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and entered into multivariable logistic regression to build a nomogram. Performance was assessed by discrimination (area under the curve, AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA), with internal validation by 1000 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: Of 240 women (median follow-up 18.0 months), 43 (17.9%) had recurrence. Multiple polyps (odds ratio [OR] 3.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.73-8.11), higher body mass index (BMI; OR 1.17, 95% CI 1.05-1.29), and uterine leiomyoma (OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.04-5.45) were independently associated with increased recurrence, whereas postoperative medical management was associated with lower odds (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.17-0.75). The nomogram showed an apparent AUC of 0.784 (bootstrap-corrected 0.750), good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.304), and positive net benefit on DCA.
CONCLUSION: Multiple polyps, higher BMI, and uterine leiomyoma were independently associated with recurrence after hysteroscopic polypectomy, whereas postoperative medical management was associated with a lower likelihood of recurrence. On internal validation the nomogram showed acceptable discrimination and calibration and might assist in postoperative risk stratification, pending external validation.

articles.title: Potential prognostic value of the free T3/T4 ratio in HR+/HER2 - metastatic breast cancer treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors.
articles.authors: Kavgaci G, Sahin TK, Guduk N et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The free triiodothyronine (fT3)/free thyroxine (fT4) ratio is an index estimating the peripheral activity of thyroid hormones. The prognostic role of the fT3/fT4 ratio in colorectal cancer, urothelial cancer, renal carcinoma, and lymphoma is well-recognized, but its effect in metastatic breast cancer remains unestablished.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of metastatic breast cancer patients treated with cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors at Hacettepe University Hospital. Baseline fT3 and fT4 levels were recorded, and patients were categorized into two groups based on the median fT3/fT4 ratio: Low and High fT3/fT4 Ratio Groups.
RESULTS: We included 162 h-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer patients. There were no significant differences between the Low and High fT3/fT4 Ratio Groups in terms of age, sex, tumor grade, histopathologic type, menopausal status, sites of metastases, lines of treatment prior to CDK4/6 inhibitors, type of CDK4/6 inhibitor, or endocrine backbone therapy. Of all patients, 47 (29.2%) received two or more lines of treatment before initiating CDK4/6 inhibitors. High fT3/fT4 ratios were associated with significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) compared to Low fT3/fT4 ratios (median, 9.7 vs. 6.9 months; HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; p = 0.035) and significantly longer overall survival (OS) compared to Low fT3/fT4 ratios (median, NR vs. NR months; HR: 0.30; 95% CI: 0.15-0.60; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study showed that high fT3/fT4 ratios were independent factors associated with longer PFS and OS in metastatic breast cancer patients treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors, supporting the role of high fT3/fT4 ratios as a prognostic marker.

articles.title: Assessment of unsuppressed viral load and its determinants among pregnant and breastfeeding women living with HIV in the prevention of vertical transmission programme in Bugesera District, Rwanda, 2023.
articles.authors: Ndabana D, Uwamahoro B, Mukamurigo J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prevention of vertical transmission (PVT) of HIV programs are designed to prevent the transmission of HIV during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Nevertheless, attaining viral suppression among mothers living with HIV remains a major challenge, especially in resource-constrained settings like Bugesera District, Rwanda. This study aim to determine the prevalence and determinants of unsuppressed viral load (VL) among pregnant and breastfeeding women living with HIV enrolled in the PVT of HIV program as of 2023.
METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study using retrospective record review was carried out using secondary data from 508 pregnant and breastfeeding women living with HIV enrolled in the PVT of HIV services in 15 health centres in Bugesera District between January 2023 and December 2023, Data were extracted from patient records and analysed using descriptive statistics, bivariate analysis, and multivariate logistic regression to identify factors associated with an unsuppressed VL (≥ 200 copies/mL).
RESULTS: Among the 508 pregnant and breastfeeding women living with HIV enrolled in the PVT of HIV services, the prevalence of unsuppressed VL was 8.5% (95% CI: 6.3-11.2). factors associated with unsuppressed VL were mental health problems (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.7, 95% CI: 2.3-9.5, p < 0.001), low attendance to antenatal care (ANC) (< 4 visits) (aOR = 2.2, 95% CI: 1.1-4.7, p = 0.025), a history of treatment interruption (aOR = 2.4, 95% CI: 1.1-4.9, p = 0.015) and being married or cohabiting (aOR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.0-4.1, p = 0.035).
CONCLUSION: The unsuppression viral load rate among women living with HIV in Bugesera District was high. This study highlights the need of strengthening psychosocial support, increase attendance of antenatal care consultations and improve antiretroviral (ART) retention in the PVT of HIV program, particularly among women who are partnered.

articles.title: Exploring the mechanism of phthalate esters and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons on gestational metabolic disorders based on network toxicology and molecular docking.
articles.authors: Fang J, Wang J, Chen F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phthalates (PAEs) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are environmental pollutants linked to metabolic disorders, yet their role in gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and gestational obesity remians unclear.
METHODS: This study employed network toxicology and molecular docking to investigate the potential mechanisms by which 21 PAEs and PAHs influence these gestational conditions. We first predicted pollutant target genes using TargetNet and SwissTargetPrediction and cross-referenced them with disease-related genes from established databases to identify overlapping targets. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were then constructed using the STRING database, followed by GO/KEGG enrichment analyses to determine the biological functions and pathways of these targets. Finally, molecular docking was performed to validate the interactions between key pollutants and identified hub proteins.
RESULTS: Our analysis identified 149, 214, and 149 overlapping targets for gestational hypertension, GDM, and gestational obesity, respectively. The PPI networks highlighted central hub genes, including TNF, CASP3, BCL2, and ESR1, which were significantly enriched in pathways crucial for metabolism and cellular response, such as MAPK, calcium signaling, and insulin resistance. Docking simulations revealed strong binding affinities of several PAHs-notably benzo(b)fluoranthene, benzo(k)fluoranthene, and benzo(ghi)perylene-to the hub proteins TNF (-8.5 kcal/mol), BCL2 (-9.4 kcal/mol), and CASP3 (-6.8 kcal/mol).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that PAEs and PAHs may contribute to gestational metabolic disorders through potential interactions with key regulators of inflammation, apoptosis, and metabolism. This research underscores the need for further investigation into the impact of environmental pollutants on maternal health during pregnancy.

articles.title: A cfDNA fragmentomics-based liquid biopsy assay for early detection of oral cancer.
articles.authors: Wang W, Ding T, Liu C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early detection of oral cancer improves outcomes, but remains limited by the invasiveness and low sensitivity of current screening methods.
METHODS: This study included 342 participants (200 in the training and 142 in the validation cohorts). Plasma cfDNA underwent low-depth whole-genome sequencing, with data normalized to a standardized 5× coverage via down-sampling to ensure consistent analysis. Three cfDNA-derived features, including fragment size ratio (FSR), copy number variation (CNV), and repetitive element profiles (REP), were extracted and integrated using a stacked machine learning ensemble to generate prediction scores. Model performance was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity with 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: In the training cohort, oral cancer patients had a median age of 53 years (91% male), while healthy individuals had a median age of 57 years (37% male). In the validation cohort, the median ages were 53 and 57 years, with male proportions of 83.1% and 38.0% in the cancer and healthy groups, respectively. Cancer samples exhibited shorter cfDNA fragments, recurrent CNV gains at 3q and 8q, and losses at 3p and 5q. The individual AUCs for FSR, CNV, and REP were 0.973, 0.983, and 0.979 in the training cohort, and 0.960, 0.982, and 0.972 in the validation cohort, respectively. The integrated stacked model achieved AUCs of 0.996 (95% CI: 0.991-1.000) and 0.988 (95% CI: 0.975-0.988) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. To prioritize high specificity for large-scale screening, a decision threshold was established in the training cohort to target 98.0% specificity, which yielded a corresponding sensitivity of 98.0%. When this pre-fixed threshold was blindly applied to the independent validation cohort, a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 95.8% were achieved. Prediction scores were not significantly associated with age, sex, or tumor site.
CONCLUSIONS: The cfDNA fragmentomics-based stacked model distinguished oral cancer from healthy individuals, including early stage disease, supporting its potential for noninvasive approach for oral cancer detection.

articles.title: Medicaid Value-Based Payment and Quality of Serious Mental Illness Care: Does the Association Vary Across Racial and Ethnic Groups?
articles.journal: Administration and policy in mental health
articles.authors: Parry G, Cook BL, McConnell J et al.
articles.abstract: While there is growing interest in the implementation of value-based payment (VBP) policies in Medicaid, there is little evidence on whether their impacts among high-need beneficiaries vary by race and ethnicity. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Oregon Medicaid data and a pre-experimental, treatment-only repeated cross-sectional panel design, to examine whether the association of Oregon's Medicaid VBP policy with quality varied by race and ethnicity among the state's beneficiaries with serious mental illness (SMI), that is, those diagnosed with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or severe major depressive disorder. We estimated changes in 12 quality measures, by race and ethnicity, pre (2010-2012) and post (2013-2019) VBP implementation. Seven of the 12 measures were designated as VBP performance metrics, with Follow-up after Hospitalization for Mental Illness, 7-day (FUH-7-day), also designated as a bonus-earning incentive metric. The cohort totaled 232,791 person-years (71,599 beneficiaries), with 89% self-described as White and the balance as Latinamerican or Black. The policy was associated with improved quality on FUH-7-day and FUH-30-day, and decreased quality on three physical healthcare measures. The quality impacts varied by race and ethnicity. The policy was associated with the elimination of a pre-existing schizophrenia-only Latinamerican-White FUH-7-day disparity due to the relatively larger Latinamerican post-VBP increase of 18.4 percentage points (95% CI, 2.2-34.6).
