However, the minority-White disparities in the Antidepressant Medication Management measures persisted post-VBP, and pre-existing advantages for Latinamerican beneficiaries in Cervical Cancer Screening and Avoidance of All-Cause Readmission disappeared because Latinamerican beneficiaries' performance worsened post-VBP. This study of Oregon's mature VBP policy contributes first evidence of the potential impacts of Medicaid VBP policies on quality disparities among beneficiaries with SMI. Findings suggest modest gains, potentially related to targeted financial incentives, while also revealing a potential for stagnant or worsening performance.

articles.title: Vibegron add-on therapy for persistent overactive bladder symptoms in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized comparisons and within-group changes.
articles.authors: Altamimi A, Aldayhani I, AlSughayyir Z et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate randomized comparative effects and descriptive symptom changes during vibegron add-on therapy in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and persistent overactive bladder (OAB).
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through April 2026. Randomized contrasts and within-group changes were pooled separately using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses varied imputed pre-post correlations, omitted individual studies, and used modified Hartung-Knapp intervals.
RESULTS: Five reports represented four cohorts (1,362 men), including two randomized trials. At 12 weeks, randomized pooled differences favored vibegron for daily micturitions (mean difference [MD] =  - 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI]: - 1.04 to - 0.53), urgency episodes (MD =  - 0.96; 95% CI: - 1.32 to - 0.61), and nocturia (MD =  - 0.28; 95% CI: - 0.44 to - 0.11). The randomized post-void residual urine volume (PVR) difference was MD = 3.13 mL (95% CI: - 0.72 to 6.99). Routine maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax) at 12-24 weeks showed no clear difference (MD = 0.21 mL/s; 95% CI: - 0.66 to 1.08). All two-trial modified Hartung-Knapp intervals crossed zero. Descriptive within-group Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS) and total International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) changes were MD =  - 2.36 (95% CI: - 3.47 to - 1.24) and MD =  - 3.48 (95% CI: - 4.45 to - 2.51), respectively. Adverse events were numerically more frequent with vibegron in both trials; urinary retention was uncommon.
CONCLUSION: Randomized estimates support short-term reductions in bladder-diary symptoms, although inference is sensitive to small-sample methods. Within-group score changes are descriptive. The 12-week comparative PVR estimate does not establish an increase, but longer-term safety and uncommon harms remain uncertain.
TRAIL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration number: CRD420261432844.

articles.title: Real-World Treatment Patterns and Unmet Needs of Patients with Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer in Mainland China.
articles.authors: Peng P, Goh JC, Domingo EJ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Given China's high disease burden, Chinese physicians have accumulated substantial real-world experience in managing locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). Accordingly, the study aims were to evaluate treatment patterns and decision-making drivers for Chinese patients with LACC and to identify unmet needs.
METHODS: Subgroup data from mainland China (n = 80) were analyzed from a broader Asia-Pacific study conducted across five regions. This prospective cross-sectional study used a two-phase approach (literature review and physician interviews). Outcomes included treatment regimens, patient characteristics, treatment choice drivers, and unmet patient needs.
RESULTS: Responses were obtained from 20 medical oncologists and 60 gynecologists/gynecologic oncologists. LACC accounted for approximately 37% of cervical disease cases, including precancerous lesions. Treatment patterns varied according to the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stage. For stage Ib3-II disease, surgery-based strategies predominated (65%), with the most frequent being surgery plus radiotherapy (21%), surgery plus radiotherapy and systemic therapy (18%), and surgery plus systemic therapy (14%). Although concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) is guideline-preferred for stage Ib3/IIa2, radiotherapy with systemic therapy (including CCRT) was reported in only 14% of cases. For stage III-IVa disease, radiotherapy with systemic therapy (including CCRT), was most commonly selected (39%), followed by radiotherapy alone (14%) and surgery plus radiotherapy and systemic therapy (13%). Cisplatin or carboplatin with paclitaxel were the most frequently used radiosensitizers. Treatment decisions were mainly influenced by the disease stage, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines, and drug efficacy/safety. Key unmet patient needs included affordability, poor outcomes with current options, and barriers to radiotherapy access.
CONCLUSIONS: Reported LACC treatment patterns in China differed from guideline-recommended approaches, with surgery used more frequently than CCRT. These patterns may reflect physician, patient, financial, and/or radiotherapy access-related factors. Addressing these practical considerations will help to optimize LACC care and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Wilhelm J, Kumar A, Vasiyani H et al.
articles.abstract: Flower-Win/Lose signaling underlies a tumor-host fitness conflict in ovarian cancer, in which tumor-derived exosomal Tu-stroma reduces the fitness of surrounding host cells, favoring tumor expansion within host tissues. High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most prevalent histotype of epithelial ovarian cancer and leading cause of ovarian-cancer-related mortality, arises from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), a noninvasive precursor typically identifiable only by histopathologic examination of excised fallopian tube tissue. Here we evaluated Tu-stroma, a tumor-associated long noncoding RNA enriched in serum extracellular vesicles (EVs), as a circulating biomarker in STIC and early-stage HGSC, representing the earliest histopathologically defined phases of disease. Tu-stroma was quantified in serum EVs from 506 individuals with histologically normal adnexa, benign-adnexal lesions, isolated STIC and HGSC across International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stages I-IV. Normalized EV Tu-stroma ΔCT values were elevated in STIC (n = 43) and HGSC (n = 232) versus controls (n = 143) and benign-adnexal lesions (n = 88), including premenopausal women (controls = 57, benign = 34, STIC = 32, HGSC = 88). In paired receiver operating characteristic analyses, Tu-stroma showed higher discrimination than cancer antigen 125 (CA125) for STIC versus controls (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.99 versus 0.59, P < 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.99 versus 0.31, P < 0.001), and for HGSC versus controls (AUC = 0.99 versus 0.96, P = 0.001) and benign-adnexal masses (0.98 versus 0.84, P < 0.001). Tu-stroma showed no systematic elevation across inflammatory or physiologic comparators (n = 116) or nonovarian malignancies (n = 160), each assessed against healthy controls (n = 100), supporting disease-context specificity. Modeled risk-enriched contexts yielded predictive values compatible with intended-use populations. These findings identify Tu-stroma as a candidate EV-RNA marker associated with pre-invasive and early HGSC biology. Prospective evaluation in consecutively enrolled real-world cohorts is required to validate diagnostic performance, predictive value and clinical utility.

articles.title: Association of Low Birth Weight with Bone Mineral Density and Fracture Occurrence in Postmenopausal Women.
articles.authors: Kuitunen I, Sankilampi U, Manninen EM et al.
articles.abstract: Low birth weight (LBW) has been associated with impaired skeletal development and low peak bone mass. However, the association between LBW and fracture risk in postmenopausal women remains un-clear. We analyzed prospectively collected data from the population-based Osteoporosis Risk Factor and Pre-vention (OSTPRE) cohort, including women aged >50 years. Birth weight was categorized as LBW (<2500 g) or normal birth weight (≥2500 g). Fracture outcomes were analyzed using standardized inci-dence ratios (SIRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bone mineral density (BMD) trajectories were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. There were 635 women in the LBW group and 9387 in the normal birth weight group. During follow-up, a total of 8453 fractures occurred. Women with LBW had an 18% higher risk of vertebral fractures (SIR 1.18, 95% CI 1.01-1.39), a 20% higher risk of vertebral or hip fractures combined (SIR 1.20, 95% CI 1.06-1.38), and an 11% higher risk of any osteoporotic fracture (SIR 1.11, 95% CI 1.01-1.22) compared with women with normal birth weight. Hip fracture risk was borderline increased (SIR 1.25, 95% CI 0.99-1.59). No significant differences in BMD levels or age-related BMD decline were observed between the groups. LBW was associated with increased fracture risk in postmenopausal women despite similar BMD trajecto-ries. These findings suggest that adverse early-life conditions may have long-term effects on skeletal fra-gility independent of later-life BMD.

articles.title: Differences in Placental Pathology Between COVID-19-Induced Preeclampsia-Like Syndrome and True Preeclampsia.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Serrano B, Garrido M, Bonacina E et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Women with COVID-19 may develop preeclampsia-like syndrome, which shares some of the clinical features of preeclampsia (PE) but lacks its characteristic angiogenic imbalance (elevated soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1-to-placental growth factor ratio (sFlt-1/PlGF ratio)), suggesting the absence of placental involvement. The aim of this study was to investigate whether pathological placental changes associated with PE, such as maternal vascular malperfusion (MVM), may be useful to discriminate true PE from COVID-19-induced PE-like syndrome.
METHODS: This is a prospective cohort study conducted from February 2020 to September 2021. Inclusion criteria were pregnancies with SARS-CoV-2 infection that met the diagnostic criteria for PE. Cases with a normal sFlt-1/PlGF ratio (≤ 38) were classified as PE-like syndrome and cases with an abnormal sFlt-1/PlGF ratio were classified as true PE. A perinatal pathologist blinded to group allocation performed the placental histopathological examination for signs of MVM.
RESULTS: During the study period, 106 pregnant women with severe COVID-19 were admitted to the Intensive Care Unit. Among them, 15 (14.2%) met the diagnostic criteria for PE, and 11 placentas (73.3%) were available for histopathological examination. Of the 5 true PE cases, 80.0% had placentas with MVM. In contrast, none of the 6 PE-like syndrome placentas met the MVM criteria.
CONCLUSIONS: The absence of MVM in PE-like syndrome supports the initial evidence based on angiogenic factors: PE-like syndrome and true PE are different conditions with similar clinical features but different etiologies.

articles.title: The association of intrapartum oral labetalol for preeclampsia with severe features and risk of cesarean delivery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Bronner BA, Schermerhorn M, Holod M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate if the use of intrapartum oral labetalol vs. no antihypertensive medication additions for severe preeclampsia (PreE with SF) for sustained oral blood pressure control decreases the risk of cesarean.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent a trial of labor of a non-anomalous, singleton gestation at ≥ 34 weeks gestational age with preeclampsia with severe features. The exposure was intrapartum oral labetalol compared to no oral antihypertensive medication. The use of intrapartum labetalol was defined as the initiation of labetalol in labor for preeclampsia with severe features. The primary outcome was the need for cesarean. Univariable analyses were performed to evaluate the association of oral labetalol therapy and need for cesarean. Variables that had an independent association with the outcome were determined a priori and included in the multivariable regression analysis. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: 642 patients met the inclusion criteria. A total of 134 patients (20.9%) received intrapartum oral labetalol, whereas 508 (79.1%) were not started on antihypertensive medications. Patients who were initiated on oral labetalol in labor for blood pressure control were significantly more likely to have a lower gestational age at delivery (35.0 vs 37.7 weeks gestation, p < 0.001) and have a higher risk of needing IV antihypertensives in labor (95.5 vs 80.6%, p < 0.001). There were no other statistically significant baseline differences between groups. 62 (46.3%) individuals in the labetalol group and 192 (37.8%) in the no antihypertensives group underwent cesarean section. In multivariable analysis of the primary outcome, patients who were started on oral labetalol in labor were not at an increased risk of cesarean (aOR 1.32, 95% CI 0.88-1.99). Composite adverse neonatal outcomes were higher in the oral labetalol group and more patients in the oral labetalol group required cesarean for worsening preeclampsia and abnormal fetal heart tones.
CONCLUSION: Intrapartum oral labetalol use was not associated with a significant difference in cesarean rates. Univariable analysis suggests a higher odds of composite adverse neonatal outcomes as well as differing indications for cesarean sections, however, this is likely secondary to confounding by indication.

articles.title: Digital Phenotyping, Remote Monitoring, and Risk Prediction of Heart Failure in Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review With Narrative Synthesis.
articles.authors: Mo L, Powell L, Yoo A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), particularly preeclampsia, are associated with acute cardiovascular morbidity and future heart failure (HF). Current surveillance relies largely on blood pressure, symptoms, laboratory abnormalities, and clinician-triggered evaluation. Digital phenotyping, remote monitoring, electronic health record-based prediction, and machine learning may enable earlier cardiovascular risk identification.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically identify and narratively synthesize studies evaluating remote monitoring, digital health, machine learning, or risk-prediction approaches for HF-related phenotypes or cardiovascular morbidity in HDPs.
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published from January 2020 through April 10, 2025. Studies evaluating prediction or monitoring approaches in HDPs underwent sequential assessment for HF-related or cardiovascular morbidity outcomes. Screening and full-text reviews were performed by 2 independent reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Given substantial heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Of 3366 records imported for screening, 6 studies met the inclusion criteria. Studies used clinical prediction models, electronic health record (EHR)-based models, and remote monitoring to evaluate acute cardiovascular morbidity, HFpEF, cardiac remodeling, and cardiovascular readmission. Model discrimination ranged from modest to strong (AUROC approximately 0.70-0.94). Recurrent predictors included severe hypertensive disease, earlier gestational age at delivery, kidney disease, pre-existing cardiac disease, pulmonary hypertension, maternal age, obesity-related measures, blood pressure, and postpartum volume retention. Most prediction models lacked external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Preliminary evidence suggests that clinical, EHR-derived, and remotely monitored data may support risk stratification for selected cardiovascular morbidity and HF-related phenotypes after HDPs. Prospective validation, physiological marker integration, and evaluation of risk-guided interventions are needed.

articles.title: Artificial Urinary Sphincter: Perioperative Complications.
articles.journal: The Urologic clinics of North America
articles.authors: Orcutt DJ, Johnsen NV
articles.abstract: The artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) is the gold standard for managing male stress urinary incontinence, offering excellent success rates and high patient satisfaction. However, despite decades of clinical experience and well-established long-term outcomes, AUS placement remains a technically demanding procedure with a range of potential perioperative complications. This article reviews the diagnosis and management of the most common AUS-related complications encountered in the perioperative period.

articles.title: Female Urethral Sling Surgery: Complications.
articles.journal: The Urologic clinics of North America
articles.authors: Wang CN, Cox LC, Rovner ES
articles.abstract: Slings as surgical treatment for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) can be associated with a spectrum of perioperative and postoperative complications. Although overall complication rates of slings are low, pelvic surgeons must recognize common sling complications including intraoperative injury to the urinary tract, postoperative mesh extrusion/erosion, and symptoms of early and late postoperative voiding dysfunction after sling placement. This article will review incidence and etiology of common sling-related complications, discuss preoperative patient workup and optimization, review surgical techniques to prevent intraoperative complications, and outline the recognition, evaluation, and management of early and late postoperative complications related to sling treatments for SUI.

articles.title: Complications of Surgery for Scrotal Conditions: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.journal: The Urologic clinics of North America
articles.authors: Nam CS, Shen J, Andino JJ
articles.abstract: Surgery for scrotal conditions encompasses a broad range of procedures performed for benign pathology, infertility, malignancy, trauma, and chronic pain, and represents one of the most common surgical domains in urology. This article provides a comprehensive review of complications associated with scrotal surgery, organized by procedure type and complication category, with emphasis on risk stratification, prevention strategies, and evidence-based management. Across all domains, microsurgical techniques consistently improve safety profiles and reduce procedure-specific morbidity. Optimization of modifiable risk factors and timely recognition of complications are essential to minimizing morbidity and preserving testicular function and quality of life.

articles.title: Nutrition Care Strategies at the Intersection of Menopause and Obesity Pharmacotherapy.
articles.authors: Christensen S, Hurtado Andrade MD, Sampson-Paine K et al.
articles.abstract: The premenopause to menopause transition, known as perimenopause, is a critical period of metabolic vulnerability, characterized by hormonal changes, shifts in body composition, and increased cardiometabolic risk. Concurrently, incretin mimetic pharmacotherapies have emerged as highly effective treatments for obesity, achieving weight reductions that are approximating those previously observed only after bariatric surgery. While these agents confer substantial benefits, their mechanisms-appetite suppression, delayed gastric emptying, and enhanced satiety-introduce nutritional risks that intersect with pre-existing vulnerabilities of women experiencing this transition. Reduced energy intake and inadequate micronutrient intake, combined with estrogen deficiency, heighten the risk for osteoporosis and sarcopenic obesity. Likewise, gastrointestinal adverse events further compromise dietary quality and hydration, while aging physiology amplifies susceptibility to malnutrition. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on nutritional risks during perimenopause in the context of incretin mimetic pharmacotherapy, highlighting overlapping pathways that influence musculoskeletal health, metabolic resilience, and quality of life. Clinical strategies to mitigate these risks, including protein optimization, micronutrient monitoring, menopausal hormone therapy (osteoporosis/musculoskeletal health), and multidisciplinary care, are discussed alongside research priorities to inform targeted nutrition frameworks. Addressing these gaps is essential to ensure safe, effective, and sustainable obesity management for women in midlife and beyond.

articles.title: Preferred clinical protocols for the management of LH/FSH deficiency: a practitioner opinion survey.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Labrosse J, Ranisavljevic N, Tsironis A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Today's clinical guidelines do not fully address clinical situations associated with combined functional luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) deficiencies linked to advanced maternal age, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist-related LH deficiency, low body mass index with eating disorders, or an unexpected hypo-response to ovarian stimulation. The objective of this fictional "case vignette" opinion survey was to characterize clinicians' treatment preferences in these contexts.
METHOD: An international, four-investigator panel developed four fictional but realistic case vignettes, which were presented to practitioners via an online chatbot from June to September 2024. Each case featured two or three clinical scenarios with predetermined assisted reproductive technology outcomes, based on the chosen protocol.
RESULTS: 132 gynaecologists and fertility specialists (primarily from France but also from 10 other European countries) completed at least one case vignette. Over 70% of practitioners included LH activity (primarily recombinant human LH (r-hLH)) at the first treatment opportunity, with the objective of increasing the oocyte yield and quality. r-hLH was preferred in 58-72% of instances, with the greatest preference for patients with a history of eating disorders or an unexpected hypo-response to ovarian stimulation (72% and 70%, respectively). Cost considerations were infrequently reported as a driver of treatment choices.
CONCLUSION: The results of this survey of practitioners' perceptions of fictional but realistic scenarios suggest that the management of LH/FSH deficiency is complex and varies from specialist to specialist. In complex clinical scenarios, co-treatment with LH (and particularly r-hLH) was primarily selected; the practitioners considered that this choice might improve both oocyte yield and quality.

articles.title: A one-day multidisciplinary pelvic floor program: an organizational model for comprehensive assessment and coordinated care.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Lamblin G, Miguet-Bensouda C, de Boisredon M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic floor disorders significantly affect women's quality of life but remain frequently underdiagnosed, leading to fragmented care pathways and delayed management.
OBJECTIVE: To describe the organization and feasibility of a one-day multidisciplinary pelvic floor program, focusing on access to specialist care, therapeutic management and patient acceptability.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study from February 2023 to February 2024. Patients underwent a one-day multidisciplinary assessment including validated symptom questionnaires, pelvic floor examination, urodynamic testing, pelvic floor ultrasound, therapeutic education, pessary fitting and training, and posterior tibial nerve stimulation when indicated. An individualized treatment plan was established at the end of the assessment.
RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 56.7 ± 0.9 years). The mean interval between symptom onset and first consultation was 4.2 ± 0.2 years, compared with 2.1 ± 0.1 months from referral to the program. Referrals came primarily from gynecologists (58.9%), general practitioners (28.4%), and midwives (6.3%). The main presenting complaints were urinary incontinence (51.9%) and pelvic organ prolapse (24.2%). Pelvic floor rehabilitation was recommended for 54.7% of patients, surgery for 41.0%, and posterior tibial nerve stimulation for 16.8%. The mean interval between assessment and surgery was 2.2 ± 0.1 months. Among the 262 patients who completed the satisfaction questionnaire, 92.3% rated the quality of examinations as excellent, and 91.0% rated their overall satisfaction as excellent. All respondents would recommend the program.
CONCLUSION: A one-day multidisciplinary pelvic floor program appears to be a feasible and well-accepted model for the coordinated assessment and management of women with pelvic floor disorders. It may facilitate timely care, improve multidisciplinary coordination, and achieve high patient satisfaction.

articles.title: Timing of continence assessment after radical prostatectomy in men receiving perioperative hormonal therapy.
articles.authors: Buhas BA, Finati M, Kasim RH et al.
articles.abstract: Perioperative hormonal intensification is entering practice for high-risk prostate cancer: in the PROTEUS substudy, perioperative apalutamide plus androgen deprivation improved event-free survival compared with surgery alone, but urinary incontinence was reported only as an adverse event. When hormonal therapy continues after surgery, continence at the conventional 6-month assessment is measured while patients are still androgen-suppressed. In a two-center cohort of 98 men, social continence at 6 months was lower after perioperative therapy than after upfront surgery (65.0% vs 87.1% by clinician report; 58.3% vs 81.3% by patient report) but similar at 12 months (95.0% vs 96.9%). Confounding cannot be excluded, but the pattern suggests a transient on-treatment delay, whereas neoadjuvant therapy ending at surgery has been associated with faster recovery. We discuss three non-exclusive hypotheses, their implications for counseling and rehabilitation, and a reporting framework anchoring functional outcomes to the end of treatment as well as to surgery.

articles.title: LHCGR disruption and downregulation by bisphenol PH impairs ovarian function and establishes a prioritization framework for endocrine disruptors.
articles.authors: Ji X, Wang W, Chen Z et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bisphenol analogs (BPs) are recognized endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) significantly threaten ovarian health; however, the characterization of high-risk compounds, molecular initiating events (MIEs), and toxicity mechanisms associated with specific diseases remains insufficient.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to systematically evaluate the ovarian hazards of BPs, identify high-risk compounds and their MIEs, and elucidate the underlying toxicity mechanisms.
METHODS: A tiered strategy integrating computational toxicology models, high-throughput in vitro screening, and in vivo validation using a murine exposure model was employed. Transcriptomic, immunoblotting, and immunohistochemical analyses were conducted to elucidate the mechanisms of BP-induced ovarian injuries. Molecular dynamics simulations, and cellular thermal shift assays were performed to investigate the direct target binding of BPs and MIEs.
RESULTS: High- throughput screening highlighted Bisphenol PH (BPPH) as a high-risk compound. Animal studies demonstrated that BPPH induced endocrine dysfunction and reduced ovarian reserve. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that both compounds disrupted steroidogenic pathways, pinpointing luteinizing hormone/choriogonadotropin receptor (LHCGR) as a critical target. Protein analyses corroborated the suppression of LHCGR expression. BPPH was shown to directly bind to and disrupt LHCGR. Agonist validation experiments affirmed that BPs disrupt steroid hormone biosynthesis by binding to LHCGR and dysregulating its expression.
CONCLUSION: Results delineate the molecular pathogenesis by which BPs, particularly BPPH, induce ovarian insufficiency through binding and dysregulation of LHCGR. This study establishes a translatable framework for prioritizing hazardous EDCs, providing critical insights for regulatory decision-making and intervention strategies.
SYNOPSIS: High-throughput screening identified Bisphenol PH (BPPH) as a high-risk compound. Both BPPH and BPA can directly bind to LHCGR, causing structural alternation and dysregulation of steroidogenic pathways, thereby resulting in diminished ovarian reserve.

articles.title: General anesthesia or Procedural sedation and analgesia for laparoscopic sterilization; a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Sluijter HMM, Huppelschoten AG, Braam L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to compare postoperative recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic sterilization under procedural sedation and analgesia (PSA) and those receiving general anesthesia (GA).
DESIGN: Single-center, single-blinded randomized controlled trial SETTING: Gynaecological unit in a general teaching hospital PARTICIPANTS: Patients scheduled for a laparoscopic sterilization.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to either receive GA or PSA during their laparoscopic sterilization.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome measure was the recovery 24 hours postoperatively assessed using the Quality of Recovery 40 questionnaire (QoR-40). In addition, peri-operative data were measured including vital parameters, complications, conversions, the times of induction and surgery, total operating room time and total recovery room time. Usage of analgesics and the recovery index 10 (RI-10) were measured one week postoperatively. A sample size of 46 participants was calculated, with an expected difference of 10 points of the QoR-40 and an alpha of 0.05 and a beta of 80%.
RESULTS: The study comprised a total of 46 patients, 23 per arm. No significant difference was found in the main outcome; QoR-40 (PSA; 170, GA; 167 p=0.471) or in the RI-10. The total operating room time was eighteen minutes shorter in the PSA group compared to those receiving GA (43 vs 61 minutes; p=0.001). There was no difference in pain medication usage. There were no anesthesia related complications in either group.
CONCLUSION: This study observed no difference in recovery after 24 hours and 7 days between PSA en GA. However, the operation times were significantly shorter, making PSA more cost effective. We therefore conclude that PSA is a promising option in patients undergoing a laparoscopic sterilization, especially for low-risk patients. More research should be performed into the safety for higher-risk patients, and for the use of PSA for other minimally invasive gynaecological procedures.

articles.title: Prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances exposure and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: fetal sex-specific associations.
articles.authors: DeBolt CA, Midya V, Andra SS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental chemicals associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, however their role in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the fetal sex-specific PFAS mixture associations with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
METHODS: Using data from 217 pregnant individuals from a prospective cohort study, we examined associations between maternal serum concentrations of 12 PFAS and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (gestational hypertension and preeclampsia) using weighted quantile sum regression stratified by fetal sex.
RESULTS: The PFAS mixture, which included 8 of the 12 assessed PFAS that met detection criteria, was not associated with odds of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (OR [95% CI]: 1.06 [0.73,1.53]) in the overall analysis sample. However, in pregnant persons carrying a male fetus, the PFAS mixture was marginally associated with higher odds of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (OR [95% CI]: 1.55 [0.88, 2.73]). In contrast, pregnant individuals carrying a female fetus exhibited negative associations between PFAS mixture and the odds of HDP (OR [95% CI]: 0.34 [0.16, 0.74]). Additionally, individual PFAS congeners contributed differently to each mixture model, with the highest contributions from PFNA and PFOS to the male mixture model whereas PFHxS and MeFOSAA contributed the highest weights to the female mixture model.
CONCLUSION: We found that PFAS associations with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy may differ by fetal sex, which may be an important source of heterogeneity in studies of environmental exposures and adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: State of the Reproductive Urology Workforce: Trends and Geographic Distribution of Reproductive Urologists from 2005 to 2024.
articles.authors: Nam CS, Gago LC, Park AC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the contemporary geographic distribution of reproductive urologists (RUs) across the United States (US) in the context of worsening urologic workforce shortage and increasing utilization of assisted reproductive technology (ART) over the past two decades.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional study with geomapping of the distribution of RUs in relation to males of reproductive age in the US and ART clinics.
SUBJECTS: RUs and their geographic distribution were identified by membership to the Society for Male Reproduction and Urology (SMRU) and the Society for the Study of Male Reproduction (SSMR) in 2024. US males of reproductive age were defined as males aged 20 to 49 years in the most recent US Census Bureau Application Programming Interface (API) in 2020. ART centers were identified from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National ART Surveillance system.
EXPOSURE: None MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The percentage of US males of reproductive age living within 60 miles of a RU in 2024, US males of reproductive age per RU, RUs per ART center, and in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles per RU.
RESULTS: 228 RUs were identified, an increase of 31 (15.7%) since 2005. There were 13 states without RUs in 2005 and 2024. Only 68.9% of males of reproductive age live within 60 miles of a RU in the US. The ratio of males of reproductive age to RU in 2024 improved by 28,691 males to RUs compared to 2005, which translates to 9.9% improvement. However, there was a 2.8-times increase in IVF cycles per RU compared to 2005 (+1,410 IVF cycle per RU).
CONCLUSION: Access to male infertility care continues to be limited by extensive care deserts due to the geographic sparsity of RUs. For geographic areas with availability of RUs, there has been a disproportionate increase in IVF cycles per RU since 2005. Targeted interventions are essential to improve access to infertility care for patients in the 13 states currently lacking any RUs and geographic areas with high utilization of IVF.

articles.title: Association between non-invasive PGT-A (niPGT-A) and live birth using spent embryo culture medium in donor oocyte cycles: a prospective non-selection cohort study.
articles.authors: Lledo B, Morales R, Ortiz JA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To study the association between non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (niPGT-A) performed on spent embryo culture medium and live birth in donor oocyte recipient IVF cycles.
DESIGN: Prospective, blinded, non-selection cohort study.
SUBJECTS: Women aged 30-50 years undergoing their first single fresh blastocyst transfer from their first donor-oocyte treatment cycle.
EXPOSURE: Embryos were selected exclusively based on morphological criteria. Spent culture medium was collected after embryo transfer and analyzed by next-generation sequencing (VeriSeq®, Illumina). niPGT-A results were blinded and not used for clinical decision-making.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE(S): Live birth rate (LBR). Secondary outcomes included biochemical pregnancy rate, biochemical pregnancy loss, clinical pregnancy rate and clinical miscarriage RESULTS: Of 154 transferred embryos, 135 (87.7%) yielded informative niPGT-A results and 19 (12.3%) were non-informative. Live birth occurred in 56.0% (42/75) of embryos classified as euploid and 36.7% (22/60) of those classified as aneuploid, including 32.6% (14/43) of embryos with whole-chromosome aneuploid calls. In adjusted analyses, the association between an aneuploid niPGT-A call and lower live birth was similar in magnitude and direction using ASEBIR morphology (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.22-0.93) and Gardner morphology (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.24-1.03). Addition of niPGT-A did not significantly improve prognostic discrimination under either morphological framework, and optimism-corrected AUCs indicated limited overall discrimination.
CONCLUSION: In donor oocyte IVF cycles, SCM-based niPGT-A classification was associated with live birth, although substantial live-birth rates were observed among embryos classified as aneuploid, including those with whole-chromosome aneuploid calls. Prognostic analyses showed limited incremental discrimination beyond conventional clinical and morphological variables. Further studies are required to establish its diagnostic performance, incremental prognostic contribution, and clinical utility.

articles.title: To Test or Not to Test? A Dilemma in Prenatal Testing for an Adult-Onset Genetic Condition.
articles.authors: Lowe C, Ross LF, Moore B et al.
articles.abstract: Pediatric genetic testing for adult-onset genetic conditions is controversial and generally not recommended because of concerns about protecting a future child's autonomy to decide as an adult whether to know their genetic status. Yet, preimplantation genetic testing of embryos and prenatal diagnosis of fetuses for adult-onset genetic conditions are routinely offered to at-risk prospective parents when parents intend to select unaffected embryos or terminate an affected pregnancy to avoid having a child with the condition. These commentaries consider a case in which expecting parents (1 of whom is at risk) request prenatal testing for Huntington disease (HD), a genetic, progressive, adult-onset neurological condition, but do not intend to terminate the pregnancy if affected. Such situations highlight the tension between protecting a potential child's interest in an open future and honoring prospective parents' reproductive autonomy and ability to make decisions that they determine to be in the best interests of their family and future child. The first commentary highlights ethical distinctions in the case from obstetric and pediatric perspectives. The second commentary considers the role of parental reason-giving in shifting ethical reasoning and deliberation between prenatal and pediatric frames of reference. The third commentary, from the perspective of an HD community member, offers reflections on the breadth of personal and family experiences of HD that may inform choices about prenatal testing. The fourth commentary considers clinicians' process-related obligations while counseling families about prenatal testing for adult-onset conditions to argue for a shared decision-making model.

articles.title: Hormonal Contraception Use and Changes in Body Mass Index: A Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Lund M, Andersen MP, Sørensen KK et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the potential association between hormonal contraceptive use and body mass index (BMI).
DESIGN AND METHODS: Linear regression model was used to assess change in BMI between adolescence and adulthood according to hormonal contraception use. Hormonal contraception (HC) use was categorized according to hormonal composition.
POPULATION: We included all Danish women with data on adolescence height and weight in the Danish National Child Health register and adult weight and height reported in the Safe Choice survey.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in BMI from adolescence to adulthood, based on the assessed height and weight in adolescence and adulthood.
RESULTS: We included 47 148 individuals with a median age of 21 years (1st-3rd quantile: 19-24) at the time of answering the Safe Choice survey. Regardless of HC use, BMI increased between the two measurements for all groups. Hormonal contraception containing oestrogen was associated with a larger BMI increase after 4-5 years of cumulated duration of use compared to participants who had never used HC (p-value < 0.001). After more than 5 years, among women with a history of HC use, BMI increased most in users of combined oestrogen-progestin contraceptives (3.14 BMI points; 95% CI: 2.98-3.30; p < 0.001) and least in progestin-only users (2.47 BMI points; 95% CI: 2.27-2.66; p < 0.001); in comparison, non-users experienced a BMI increase of 2.28 BMI points (95% CI: 2.10-2.45; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: This study shows that BMI increased between the two measurements in all groups. Hormonal contraception containing oestrogen was associated with a larger BMI increase after 4-5 years of cumulative HC use compared to never-users. Among those with a cumulative duration of HC use greater than five years, the largest BMI increase was observed for combined HC, and the smallest was observed for progestin-only methods.

articles.title: Maternal and perinatal outcomes in pregnant women with Lassa fever: analysis from the LASCOPE prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Serra B, Juchet S, Etafo IC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lassa fever, a viral haemorrhagic fever endemic in west Africa, is usually described as associated with severe maternal and perinatal outcomes. Previous studies reported maternal mortality of 33% (whereas overall mortality is about 14% in Nigeria for patients admitted to hospital) and fetal mortality is up to 60%. However, most evidence derives from small case series with substantial limitations. We aimed to assess maternal death and perinatal outcomes in a prospective cohort study with standardised medical care protocols.
METHODS: We analysed data from the LASCOPE cohort from the Federal Medical Centre Owo, Nigeria, which included all patients with PCR-confirmed Lassa fever. In this analysis, non-pregnant women of childbearing age (15-45 years) were compared with pregnant women, defined as having an ongoing pregnancy during Lassa fever. The primary maternal outcome was all-cause mortality 28 days after admission and the primary pregnancy outcome was fetal death. Mortality at 28 days was compared using Kaplan-Meier estimates and a Cox proportional-hazards model, the cumulative incidence of fetal death was estimated with livebirth as a competing event, and the association between gestational age at symptom onset and fetal death was assessed by logistic regression.
FINDINGS: Between April 4, 2018, and Feb 18, 2023, of 1006 patients in the LASCOPE cohort admitted with PCR-confirmed Lassa fever, 703 were excluded for not being of childbearing age, and 303 were women of childbearing age, of whom 45 were pregnant. The median age of pregnant women was 28 years (IQR 24-32). The 28-day mortality was comparable between pregnant and non-pregnant women (four [9%; 95% CI 2-21] of 45 vs 19 [7%; 95% CI 4-11] of 258; hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·41-3·50]; log-rank p=0·75). Fetal case-fatality rate was 60% (27 of 45), with higher risk of fetal death if infection occurred early in the pregnancy (100% for the first trimester, 82% for the second trimester, and 25% for the third trimester). Each additional week of gestation at symptom onset was associated with a reduction in the odds of fetal death (odds ratio 0·77 [95% CI 0·61-0·90]). Among 15 liveborn infants, three (20%) died within 30 days.
INTERPRETATION: Although the fetal prognosis was poor, as previously reported, maternal fatality was lower than previously indicated, potentially reflecting improved supportive care and patient monitoring. These findings suggest that maternal mortality might be lower than…

articles.title: Risovalisib for PIK3CA-mutated recurrent or persistent ovarian clear cell carcinoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 trial.
articles.authors: Li J, Yonemori K, Niimi K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is a rare but aggressive and biologically distinct subtype of ovarian cancer, in which PIK3CA mutations are common. Advanced ovarian clear cell carcinoma is very difficult to treat, and after failure of platinum-based chemotherapy, therapeutic options are limited. We aimed to evaluate the anti-tumour activity and safety of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, for treatment of patients with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma.
METHODS: We conducted a single-arm, phase 2 trial of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, in 27 centres in China and 12 centres in Japan. Eligible participants were adult patients (aged 18 years or older, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1) with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma and one to three lines of previous systemic anti-tumour treatment. Risovalisib was given orally at 40 mg daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other protocol-defined reasons for discontinuation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (version 1.1), among all treated patients with a confirmed PIK3CA hotspot mutation and baseline tumour assessments with measurable lesions per BIRC (efficacy analysis set). The primary endpoint was considered met if the lower 95% CI was greater than 8%. Safety analyses were performed in all patients who received at least one dose of risovalisib (safety analysis set). The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05043922) and is ongoing but no longer recruiting patients.
FINDINGS: Between Oct 6, 2021, and Jan 31, 2024, 93 patients were enrolled and received risovalisib. The median age was 49 years (IQR 43-58), all patients were female, 52 (56%) were from Japan, 41 (44%) were from China, and 63 (68%) had two or more previous lines of therapy. The median duration of follow-up was 14·5 months (IQR 8·6-18·3). The objective response rate was 29 (35% [95% CI 25-46]) of 84 patients in the efficacy analysis set. The most commonly reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 93 patients were rash (30 [32%]), hyperglycaemia (28 [30%]), and decreased weight (7 [8%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 36 (39%) patients, the most common being rash (eight [9%]), pneumonitis (six [6%]), and decreased appetite (four…

articles.title: Stillbirth Risk with Class II and III Obesity.
articles.authors: Herrera CL, Farid SI, Cohn ER et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We sought to analyze the rates of stillbirth at recommended gestational age epochs based on body mass index (BMI) at first prenatal visit.
STUDY DESIGN: A total of 79,148 births with optimal dating, BMI at first prenatal visit, and absence of maternal complications (chronic hypertension, pregestational diabetes) or fetal complications (aneuploidy, major fetal malformations, fetal growth restriction) were identified from January 2013 to September 2024. Of these, 33,108 (42%) delivered ≥ 34 weeks with a BMI classified as normal, class II, or class III obesity. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated due to differences in age, race/ethnicity, and parity.
RESULTS: Among patients with class II obesity, no difference in stillbirth was observed compared with normal weight individuals at either early term (370/7 -386/7 weeks) or term (≥ 39 weeks), with aHRs of 2.19 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67-7.17) and 0.86 (95% CI 0.17-4.34), respectively. Neither were differences found in stillbirth risk for patients with class III obesity compared with normal weight individuals in the late preterm (340/7 -366/7 weeks), early term, or term gestational ages with aHRs of 0.78 (95% CI 0.17-3.57), 2.44 (95% CI 0.61-9.84), and 2.81 (95% CI 0.7-11.28), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Based on our results, the utility of antepartum surveillance for the prevention of stillbirth in patients with class II or III obesity may be of limited benefit.
KEY POINTS: · There is no significant increased risk of stillbirth in class II obesity at term.. · The utility of antepartum surveillance may be of limited benefit.. · No significant increased risk of stillbirth in class III obesity beginning at preterm gestation has been found..

articles.title: Family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding care in familial hypercholesterolaemia (Taking ACTion to Improve Care of coupleS in FH (TACTICS)): a mixed methods study.
articles.authors: Mulder JWCM, Pang J, Klevmoen M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a common genetic condition causing premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding are important phases of care. We investigated awareness, knowledge and practices regarding these phases among individuals with FH, partners, and healthcare professionals (HCPs).
METHODS: An exploratory mixed-methods study was conducted in the Netherlands, Norway and Australia. Interviews with individuals with heterozygous FH (HeFH) explored experiences of care related to family planning and were analysed following reflexive thematic analysis. Partners completed an anonymous survey on the impact of FH on their relationship. HCPs were surveyed on family planning and pregnancy practices.
RESULTS: Twenty-six individuals with HeFH (62% women, median age 37 [IQR 33-42] years, 15% ASCVD) were interviewed. Experiences varied widely, with women reporting the greatest impact, particularly concerning pregnancy, breastfeeding and treatment interruption. Among 175 partners of subjects with FH (55% men, median age 48 [37-60] years, 82% with children), 25% reported a past and/or current negative impact of FH on their relationship. FH influenced family planning in 11% of couples, with a higher proportion among those aged 30-39 years (35%). 107 HCPs (median practice duration 21 [12-30] years, median FH-caseload 50 [15-128]) completed the survey. Most (89%) discussed family planning, mainly concerning inheritance (94%) and preconception medication advice (91%). Most HCPs recommended statin discontinuation during conception, pregnancy and breastfeeding; 46% recommended breastfeeding duration similar to that for general population.
CONCLUSIONS: Substantial heterogeneity exists in counselling practices, highlighting the need for standardised care pathways to improve guidance and support individuals with FH and their partners in family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding.

articles.title: BPA exposure from gestation through the post-weaning period increases susceptibility to allergic airway inflammation in female mouse offspring: Association with reduced mTOR phosphorylation, enhanced autophagy, and Foxp3 promoter methylation.
articles.authors: Yang Y, Wang S
articles.abstract: Early-life exposure to bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine disruptor, is associated with increased asthma susceptibility in offspring, yet the mechanisms remain poorly characterized. We examined whether BPA exposure spanning gestation, lactation, and the post-weaning period is associated with allergic airway inflammation in female offspring in relation to mTOR signaling, autophagy, and Foxp3 methylation. Dams received BPA (0.1 µg/mL in drinking water, ~25 µg/kg BW/day) from gestational day 6 to weaning; female offspring continued BPA or vehicle post-weaning and were assigned to control, BPA, ovalbumin (OVA), and BPA+OVA groups before OVA sensitization and challenge. Airway hyperresponsiveness, lung histopathology, BALF inflammation and Th2 cytokines, serum OVA-specific IgE, splenic Tregs, LC3/p62 and mTOR signaling, and Foxp3 methylation were assessed. BPA alone was associated with moderate asthma-like phenotypes approaching those induced by OVA; co-exposure produced the most severe phenotypes, with stepwise control-to-BPA+OVA trends in mucus, LC3 (increasing), and p62 (decreasing). BPA was associated with reduced mTOR phosphorylation (Ser2448) accompanied by PI3K/Akt inhibition and AMPK/TSC1/2 activation, increased Foxp3 methylation, and reduced splenic Tregs, most pronounced under co-exposure. Thus, BPA exposure from gestation through the post-weaning period is associated with exacerbated allergic airway inflammation in female offspring, accompanied by mTOR suppression, enhanced autophagy, Foxp3 hypermethylation, and Treg reduction; interventional studies are needed to establish causality.

articles.title: Association of exposure to the organophosphate flame retardant EHDPP with early pregnancy loss: An integrated case-control, population-based, and computational study.
articles.authors: Yifu P, Yaping J, Xian C et al.
articles.abstract: The association between 2-ethylhexyl diphenyl phosphate (EHDPP) exposure and early pregnancy loss (EPL) remains unknown. This study integrated targeted exposomics (n = 50), NHANES analysis (n = 860), network toxicology, Mendelian randomization, and single-cell RNA sequencing to investigate the association between EHDPP exposure and EPL and to explore potential biological mechanisms. In the targeted exposomics discovery cohort, EHDPP showed the largest fold change in plasma concentration among the 68 detectable chemicals when EPL cases were compared with controls (fold change = 2.12, q < 0.001). EHDPP concentrations were associated with shorter activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and higher fibrinogen levels, suggesting a procoagulant pattern. In an independent NHANES analytic sample, urinary DPHP, a non-specific biomarker reflecting exposure to multiple aryl-OPEs including EHDPP, was associated with self-reported pregnancy loss (n = 860; log2-transformed DPHP, P = 0.003). The association was directionally consistent in women aged 20-45 years, although not statistically significant. Network toxicology predicted putative EHDPP targets and pathways. Genetically predicted levels of five proteins-CA1, HSPA5, IGFBP2, IMPDH2, and PNKP-showed nominal associations with spontaneous abortion in Mendelian randomization analyses (all P < 0.05); however, these findings emerged from screening multiple candidate proteins and should be considered hypothesis-generating. These proteins also had favorable predicted docking scores (ΔG ≤ -5.0 kcal/mol) and cell-type-specific expression in placental and decidual cell populations in single-cell RNA sequencing analysis. Collectively, these findings support a potential association between EHDPP exposure and EPL and provide a hypothesis-generating mechanistic framework that warrants experimental validation.

articles.title: Associations between fatty acids and female reproductive disease risk: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.journal: Prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and essential fatty acids
articles.authors: Li J, Zhang C, Jin Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated associations between circulating fatty acids and female reproductive disorders using bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR).
METHODS: Genetic variants for circulating fatty acid traits and female reproductive disorders were obtained from publicly available genome-wide association study datasets. Bidirectional MR was performed using inverse variance weighted (IVW), MR-Egger, weighted median, and weighted mode methods. Steiger directionality testing and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Multivariable MR (MVMR) was performed for significant forward associations to account for BMI, triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, and LDL cholesterol. Phenome-wide association analysis (PheWAS) was used to assess potential horizontal pleiotropy.
RESULTS: After outlier removal and FDR correction, genetically predicted monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA) were associated with increased endometriosis risk (IVW OR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.02-1.29, P = 0.0206, FDR = 0.0412), and DHA was associated with increased infertility risk (IVW OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.04-1.29, P = 0.0072, FDR = 0.0289). The MUFA-endometriosis association was strengthened after removal of rs12212146, and the DHA-infertility association became significant only after removal of rs12639836. Neither association remained statistically significant after MVMR adjustment for BMI, triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, or LDL cholesterol. No reverse MR association remained significant after FDR correction.
CONCLUSION: This study identified associations of genetically predicted circulating MUFA with endometriosis and DHA with infertility after outlier correction. Both associations were sensitive to outlier handling and attenuated in MVMR analyses, indicating that these findings require further validation.

articles.title: Embryo donation in Canada: Ethical, moral, and legal considerations from specialists' perspectives.
articles.authors: Guerzoni CS, Côté I
articles.abstract: The proliferation of unused embryos at the end of IVF cycles has sparked ethical debates regarding their disposal, especially regarding their donation for family-building purposes. How do Canadian and US reproductive health professionals represent embryo donation for family-building purposes? Ethnographic research was conducted in Canada and the United States from August 2023 to April 2024. 21 reproductive health professionals were interviewed (one CAN lawyer, one CAN embryologist, two CAN social workers, one CAN psychologist, three CAN doctors, one CAN third-party coordinator, one US embryologist, three US doctors, one US nurse, and seven US embryo donation coordinators). An issue at the core of our interlocutors' concerns was the logistical difficulty associated with this practice. A pivotal issue was related to privacy, how much and which information should be disclosed to patients. Another important aspect concerned legal disputes around who is responsible in cases where either donors or recipients may change their minds. A crucial concern is the well-being of children born through embryo donation. In the absence of national guidelines, these issues were managed differently from clinic to clinic, pointing to the need for national standards and early counseling.

articles.title: Time to treatment initiation in cervical cancer in the United States: Trends by treatment modality and factors associated with delay.
articles.authors: Yen TT, Hsieh TYJ, Lee GY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate national trends in time to treatment initiation (TTI) for cervical cancer from 2004 to 2022, and to identify factors associated with treatment delay.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Cancer Database. Adult women with cervical cancer diagnosed between 2004 and 2022 were included and categorized by initial treatment as radiation-based, surgery, or chemotherapy. TTI was defined as the interval from diagnosis to first treatment. Multivariable quantile regression models evaluated temporal trends and factors associated with longer TTI. Covariates included patient sociodemographic and treating facility characteristics. Among patients receiving radiation-based treatment, secondary analyses evaluated the association between TTI and completion of radiation within 56 days.
RESULTS: A total of 73,233 patients were included: 43,995 in the radiation-based group, 26,735 in the surgery group, and 2503 in the chemotherapy-only group. Median TTI increased over time across all three modalities, from 29 to 45 days in the radiation-based group, 39 to 57 days in the surgery group, and 23.5 to 39 days in the chemotherapy-only group, corresponding to relative increases of 55.2%, 46.2%, and 66.0%, respectively. Longer TTI was consistently associated with treatment at high uninsured/Medicaid burden facilities, Medicaid insurance, Hispanic ethnicity, lower neighborhood educational attainment, and diagnosis-treatment facility discordance. Longer TTI was not associated with prolonged radiation duration beyond 56 days.
CONCLUSIONS: TTI for cervical cancer has lengthened nationally across treatment pathways. Delays reflect structural inequities and care fragmentation. Further work is needed to benchmark TTI cutoff and quantify harm.

articles.title: National cancer database analysis of uterine carcinosarcoma: An updated series in locally advanced stage patients.
articles.authors: Zitter R, Sivananthan AP, Son CH et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Uterine carcinosarcoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with high rates of distant failure, and the optimal sequencing of adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation in locally advanced disease is undefined. We evaluated whether the sequencing of adjuvant therapies is associated with overall survival (OS) in surgically managed FIGO stage III-IVA uterine carcinosarcoma.
METHODS: We identified 4593 patients with surgically treated FIGO stage III-IVA uterine carcinosarcoma in the National Cancer Database (2004-2020). Patients were categorized as chemotherapy only (CO), radiation only (RO), sequential chemoradiation (SCRT), concurrent chemoradiation (CRT), or no adjuvant therapy. CRT was defined as chemotherapy and radiation start dates within 14 days, with SCRT separated by more than 14 days. OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier and compared using Cox regression, with inverse probability of treatment weighting, propensity-score matching, and landmark analyses as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: SCRT had the highest 2-year OS (67.3%) versus CO (51.4%), CRT (52.8%), and RO (34.6%). On MVA, SCRT was associated with improved OS versus CO (adjusted HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.60-0.82; univariable HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.61-0.74), whereas CRT was not (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.80-1.57). SCRT benefit persisted across weighted, matched, and landmark analyses and after exclusion of stage IVA patients (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.59-0.80). Age and lymphovascular space invasion were independently prognostic.
CONCLUSIONS: In locally advanced uterine carcinosarcoma, SCRT was associated with superior OS compared with CO, while CRT was not. These data support prospective evaluation of adjuvant treatment sequencing in this histology.

articles.title: Surgical management of cervical cancer: A Society of Gynecologic Oncology evidence-based review.
articles.authors: Melamed A, Covens AL, Pfaendler KS et al.
articles.abstract: Surgical management of cervical cancer has changed substantially over the past decade as randomized and prospective data have refined the extent of resection, the role of fertility-sparing surgery, nodal assessment strategies, and the choice of surgical approach. This Society of Gynecologic Oncology evidence-based review addresses the upfront surgical management of cervical cancer. Surgery for recurrent disease, including pelvic exenteration and resection of oligometastatic recurrence, is outside its scope. A panel of gynecologic oncologists and subject matter experts identified twelve clinical questions spanning extent of resection, fertility-sparing surgery, lymph node assessment, surgical approach, and the integration of surgery with chemoradiation. Relevant literature was systematically collected and synthesized, and each recommendation was assigned a strength of recommendation and quality of evidence using a two-part rating system adapted from the ASCCP guidelines. Recommendations were approved by the SGO Clinical Practice Committee, Document Review Panel, and Board of Directors. Simple hysterectomy with nodal assessment is preferred for low-risk FIGO 2018 stage IA through IB1 disease. Fertility-sparing surgery is acceptable for appropriately selected patients with low-risk stage IA1 through IB1 tumors, with conization or simple trachelectomy preferred over radical trachelectomy. Sentinel lymph node biopsy may replace complete pelvic lymphadenectomy when an accepted algorithm is applied, with indocyanine green and near-infrared imaging the preferred mapping technique. When radical hysterectomy is indicated, the open approach is preferred outside of a clinical trial. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery is not recommended in place of chemoradiation, and hysterectomy after completion of definitive chemoradiation is not recommended in the absence of documented residual disease. Evidence quality varies considerably across questions, and several recommendations rest on observational data or expert consensus.

articles.title: Increasing Specialty Menopause Referrals for Premenopausal Breast Cancer Patients: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
articles.authors: Skelly EA, Stevenson E, Tsai M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer often develop severe menopausal symptoms from chemotherapy and endocrine therapy, reducing quality of life (QoL) and contributing to early treatment discontinuation. Referral to specialty menopause care remains inconsistent. This project evaluated whether an interdisciplinary educational intervention, combined with a structured referral pathway to a specialty menopause care clinic, could improve provider confidence and increase referrals.
METHODS: The project was conducted at the Swedish Gynecology Specialty Center and Swedish Breast Medical Oncology Clinic. Oncology providers and menopause-certified gynecology clinicians participated in a 60-minute hybrid workshop addressing menopause management and referral processes. Pre- and post-intervention surveys assessed provider awareness and comfort. Referral volume was tracked across Baseline (January-April 2025), Early Implementation (April-October 2025), and Post-Implementation (October 2025-January 2026).
RESULTS: Referrals increased from 22 (6.8/mo) at baseline to 104 (27.3/mo) post-implementation, representing a fourfold increase. Early implementation referrals (17.3/mo) suggested increased awareness contributed to uptake. Provider awareness of menopausal and sexual health issues rose from 80% to 100%, and comfort discussing these symptoms increased by 14%-16%. Patient surveys (n = 23) revealed a high symptom burden, including sleep disturbance (82%) and hot flashes (77%). Most patients (87.5%) found the specialty clinic helpful, and 95.7% intended to complete their endocrine therapy.
CONCLUSION: An interdisciplinary educational intervention with a structured referral pathway significantly improved provider confidence and increased menopause specialty referrals. Integrating menopause expertise into oncology care is feasible and may enhance symptom management, treatment adherence, and QoL.

articles.title: Pregnancy and classic Hodgkin lymphoma: real world outcomes from a single center in Egypt.
articles.authors: El-Ashwah S, Elashwah S, Najah MS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Association of pregnancy and Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (CHL) is rare, but clinically important scenario because the peak incidence of CHL overlaps with reproductive years. Management requires balancing maternal disease control with fetal safety. This article aims to explore the clinicopathological characteristics, management challenges, and survival outcomes of CHL female patients in relation to pregnancy.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This is a retrospective study analyzed forty-one female patients in their childbearing period diagnosed with de novo or relapsed/refractory CHL that occurred during pregnancy and treated between 2010 and 2024.
RESULTS AND OUTCOMES: Mean age at diagnosis was 25.2 years (SD; 4.9). Thirty-nine patients received ABVD, two received BEACOPP. Complete remission was achieved in 75.6% of patients, with relapse in 6.5%. Median overall survival (OS) for the cohort was 95.33 months (range, 7.1-199.7). Pregnancy outcomes were favorable; most patients delivered full-term infants with no reported congenital anomalies. It appears that CHL and its treatment did not affect fertility and pregnancy itself did not worsen the lymphoma outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Management of CHL during pregnancy is a real challenge and requires a multidisciplinary approach with the goal of maximizing the cure rate for the patient, minimizing the fetal risks and allowing delivery of a healthy newborn. ABVD remains safe and effective in pregnancy, with excellent maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Optimizing antiseizure treatment in women of reproductive age and during pregnancy: Nationwide practice versus specialized epilepsy care in Poland.
articles.authors: Wójcik-Kawa K, Sienkiewicz-Jarosz H, Słowik A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare antiseizure medication (ASM) treatment patterns among women with epilepsy (WWE) of reproductive age and pregnant WWE using nationwide administrative data and a university epilepsy referral center cohort in Poland.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed two complementary datasets. Nationwide data were obtained from the Polish National Health Fund, including 44,951 WWE aged 20-49 years in 2024 and 594 pregnant WWE who delivered in 2022. Referral center data were collected from medical records of 277 WWE aged 20-49 years treated in 2024 and 112 pregnancies managed between 2019 and 2026.
RESULTS: Levetiracetam and lamotrigine were the most frequently prescribed ASMs in both cohorts. Compared with the nationwide population, women of reproductive age treated at the epilepsy center were significantly less likely to receive valproate (18.4 % vs. 31.1 %, p < 0.001) or carbamazepine (6.5 % vs 16 %p < 0.001), while lacosamide, brivaracetam, and cenobamate were prescribed more frequently. The proportion of women receiving monotherapy was similar in both cohorts. Among pregnant WWE, non-valproate monotherapy predominated in both groups but was significantly more common at the referral center (77.7 % vs. 62.0 %, p < 0.001). Valproate use during pregnancy was markedly lower in the referral center than in the nationwide cohort (2.7 % vs. 16.0 %, p < 0.001), whereas levetiracetam and lamotrigine use was comparable.
CONCLUSIONS: Women managed at an epilepsy referral center were substantially less likely to receive potentially teratogenic ASMs, particularly valproate, despite representing a more clinically complex population. These findings highlight the contribution of specialized epilepsy care to optimizing pharmacological management for women of reproductive age and during pregnancy while supporting adherence to contemporary treatment recommendations.

articles.title: Risk of colorectal cancer and systemic menopausal hormone therapies: a Finnish cohort study.
articles.authors: Siitonen H, Joensuu JM, Savolainen-Peltonen H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We assessed the impact of menopausal hormone therapies (MHTs) on the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC) in Finnish women. In addition, we analysed various MHT characteristics in relation to risk and anatomic site of CRC.
METHODS: Users of MHT and age-matched non-users (both groups n = 364,304) in 1994-2019 were identified from the Finnish Medicine Reimbursement Register and the National Population Register. Cohorts were followed for the occurrence of primary CRC from the Finnish Cancer Registry. CRC risks were calculated as hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) with a Cox proportional hazards model.
RESULTS: Over a mean 18-year follow-up (13 million person-years), 4602 MHT users (1.3%) and 5103 non-users (1.4%) were diagnosed with CRC (p < 0.001). Ever use of MHT for 5 years or more was associated with a decreased CRC risk (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92). Estrogen-only therapy (ET) (0.81, 0.76-0.87) showed a larger risk reduction than combined estrogen-progestogen therapy (EPT) (0.92, 0.88-0.96). Tibolone was accompanied by the greatest risk decrease (0.54, 0.41-0.73), but the number of users was modest. Dydrogesterone EPT tended to confer 31-36% lower CRC risk than EPTs containing norethisterone or medroxyprogesterone acetate. Risk reductions were of similar magnitude for right- and left-sided colon cancer, but rectal cancer risk was decreased only with 10 or more years of MHT use. The risk falls persisted for over 5 years after the cessation of MHT use.
CONCLUSIONS: Use of ET or EPT for 5 years or more is associated with reduced CRC risk, likely mediated by estrogen, while some progestogens - but not dydrogesterone - may attenuate this effect.

articles.title: Associations of objectively measured daytime and nighttime light exposure with the severity of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome and all-cause mortality: Evidence from a national cohort and genetic analyses.
articles.authors: Yan Y, Zhang T, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Light exposure is an increasingly recognized modifiable environmental factor in cardiometabolic health, but its associations with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, as well as with mortality (from any cause), remain unclear.
METHODS: Adults with valid measurements of ambient light from wrist-worn devices from the 2011-2014 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey were included. Daily, daytime, and nighttime light intensity and duration were assessed. Survey-weighted regression and unweighted Cox models examined associations with CKM stage, advanced CKM syndrome, and all-cause mortality. Mediation analysis evaluated circulating levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]. Mendelian randomization assessed genetically predicted 25(OH)D level, ease of skin tanning, and outdoor time.
RESULTS: Higher daily and daytime light intensity was associated with lower CKM stage and lower odds of advanced CKM syndrome. Longer exposure to light >1000 lx was also associated with lower odds of advanced CKM syndrome, whereas nighttime light intensity showed no independent association. Among individuals with CKM syndrome, higher daily and daytime light intensity was associated with lower all-cause mortality. However, these associations were substantially attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for baseline CKM stage. Circulating 25(OH)D partially mediated associations between light intensity and mortality, but not advanced CKM syndrome. Mendelian randomization findings were mixed after multiple-testing correction.
CONCLUSION: Greater objectively measured daytime light exposure was associated with a more favorable CKM profile and lower all-cause mortality among individuals with CKM syndrome. The association with lower all-cause mortality was attenuated after adjustment for baseline CKM stage, suggesting that it may not be independent of CKM severity. Further prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Do parental questions and gestures support executive functions in toddlers born preterm and full-term?
articles.authors: Yılmaz B, Göksun T
articles.abstract: This study examined parental questions and gestures in the development of executive functions (EF) in preterm (PT) and full-term (FT) toddlers. Sixty-four Turkish-speaking parent-child dyads (32 girls, Mage = 26.1 months, SD = 1.33, 25 PT) were observed in free-play sessions. The form (i.e., WH, yes/no) and function (i.e., pedagogical, information-seeking, rhetorical) of parental questions and gestures accompanying them were coded. Children's working memory and cognitive flexibility skills were measured using Hide the Pots and Reverse Categorization (pre- and post-switch) tasks, respectively. Results showed that PT and FT children had similar EF skills. Parental WH questions were associated with PT children's working memory skills. Parental WH questions, not pedagogical ones, were related to children's cognitive flexibility skills, regardless of neonatal status. When accompanied by gestures, both WH and pedagogical questions were associated with PT children's working memory and cognitive flexibility skills. These results highlight the importance of specific parental input as a function of children's neonatal status in the development of EFs.

articles.title: First multicentre clinical results of human umbilical cord blood platelet-rich plasma for endometrial restoration.
articles.authors: Alonso-Frías P, Rodríguez-Eguren A, Bueno-Fernandez C et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Can human umbilical cord blood platelet-rich plasma (hUC-PRP) enhance endometrial growth, vascular remodelling and tissue regeneration in patients with Asherman syndrome, endometrial atrophy or thin endometrium?
DESIGN: This multicentre pilot study included 15 infertile individuals with Asherman syndrome or endometrial atrophy/thin endometrium despite repeated oestrogen exposure. hUC-PRP was characterized and compared with adult platelet-rich plasma (PRP) using proteomic and metabolomic analyses. Participants underwent hysteroscopic subendometrial hUC-PRP injection alongside oestrogen administration. Endometrial thickness, ultrasound patterns, vascular markers and transcriptomic changes were assessed before and after treatment.
RESULTS: hUC-PRP showed high homogeneity across donors in principal component analysis and a 1.89-fold increase in platelet concentration versus whole human umbilical cord blood. Proteomic profiling of hUC-PRP identified 138 growth factor-related proteins, and revealed enrichment of extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling pathways compared with adult PRP. Endometrial thickness did not significantly increase after two oestrogen-only cycles (P = 0.57), but rose significantly after hUC-PRP administration from a mean ± SD of 3.67 ± 0.72 mm to 5.59 ± 1.20 mm (P < 0.001). Seventy per cent (7/10) of patients with non-trilaminar or atrophic endometrium developed a trilaminar pattern post-treatment. Immunofluorescence demonstrated an 11.86 percentage-point increase in mean neoangiogenic vascular area, while transcriptomic analysis revealed activation of pathways related to proliferation, angiogenesis, immune response, hormone response and ECM remodelling.
CONCLUSIONS: hUC-PRP combines a distinctive regenerative molecular profile with meaningful endometrial regeneration, supporting its potential as a novel therapeutic strategy for infertile women with a compromised endometrium. As a proof-of-concept study, these findings support further investigation of hUC-PRP as a potential endometrial regenerative approach, while reproductive efficacy remains to be established.

articles.title: Chromosomal rearrangement type and pre-transfer outcomes after PGT-SR: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Hu J, Shi J, Jiang W et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Is chromosomal structural rearrangement (CSR) type associated with transferable-embryo acquisition, embryo prioritization, reported mosaic embryo detection, and early pregnancy outcomes in preimplantation genetic testing for structural rearrangement (PGT-SR) cycles?
DESIGN: This single-centre retrospective cohort study analysed 215 PGT-SR cycles from 150 patients: 145 reciprocal translocation (RecT), 43 Robertsonian translocation (RobT), and 27 inversion (Inv) cycles.
