Generalized estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression accounted for repeated cycles. Outcomes were acquisition of at least one total transferable embryo (TTE) or priority-transferable embryo (PTE), reported mosaic embryo detection, and transfer outcomes.
RESULTS: Compared with RecT cycles, Inv cycles had higher odds of at least one TTE [adjusted OR (aOR) 3.60, 95% CI 1.28-10.15; P = 0.015]. RobT (aOR 2.54, 95% CI 1.39-4.65; P = 0.002) and Inv (aOR 2.74, 95% CI 1.17-6.41; P = 0.020) cycles had higher odds of at least one PTE. Inv cycles also had higher odds of reported mosaic embryo detection (aOR 2.88, 95% CI 1.01-8.22; P = 0.048), but this was attenuated after adjustment for the number of diagnosed embryos (aOR 2.73, 95% CI 0.95-7.80; P = 0.061). Among 111 matched transfers, biochemical pregnancy rate differed nominally across CSR types (P = 0.041), but clinical pregnancy rate did not (P = 0.126), and transfer-level GEE detected no significant CSR-type association with clinical pregnancy.
CONCLUSIONS: CSR type may be associated with pre-transfer embryo acquisition and centre-defined genetic prioritization. The findings were hypothesis-generating, and the limited transfer cohort provided no consistent evidence of CSR-type-specific early pregnancy prognosis.

articles.title: The experience of sexuality during the postpartum period: a qualitative study in a city in southern Brazil.
articles.journal: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P
articles.authors: Silva VVD, Paris MDC, Velho MB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To understand the experience of sexuality during the postpartum period.
METHOD: This qualitative research was conducted using two distinct yet complementary data collection strategies-semi-structured interviews and a self-administered questionnaire with open-ended questions-, both developed from the same script. The study included 37 people who experienced the postpartum period between the second half of 2021 and the end of 2022 in the state of Santa Catarina. Thematic analysis of the data obtained was adopted.
RESULTS: It became evident that the people interviewed consider sexuality important; however, during the postpartum period they had difficulty engaging in it due to fatigue, lack of libido, pain during intercourse, and other factors related to the postpartum period.
CONCLUSION: It can be concluded that the topic of sexuality is not regularly addressed during postpartum consultations, with only contraceptive methods and the postpartum period being discussed.

articles.title: Improving Mental Health Support for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Mothers Through a Universal Screening Quality-Improvement Initiative.
articles.authors: Fleiss N, Schneider E, Buck CO et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To improve early perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) mothers and facilitate timely referral to mental health services through the integration of a dedicated mental health clinician at our level 3 NICU.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary team convened to address barriers to universal maternal mental health screening in our NICU. Key drivers were identified, focusing on appropriate screening tools, availability of a mental health clinician, and a robust referral process should a mother screen positive. The primary outcome measure was percentage of referrals made for mothers who screened positive for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders. The process measure was percentage of mothers screened. Clinical characteristics were compared between mothers who screened positive and those who screened negative to ensure that any disparities identified were addressed in real time.
RESULTS: Since implementation of our universal screening program, 95.0% of mothers in our NICU have been screened for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders (an increase from 29.5%). Of those, 59.9% required referral for additional psychosocial support (an increase from 25.3%). Mothers who screened positive were more likely to be Black non-Hispanic (P<.001), and mothers who screened negative were more likely to be White non-Hispanic (P=.021). No differences were identified in delivery mode or breastfeeding at discharge.
CONCLUSION: A dedicated NICU mental health clinician, with multidisciplinary buy-in, may allow the successful implementation and maintenance of a universal perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening and referral program.

articles.title: Clinical Predictors of Early Postpartum Depression Based on Screening during the Birth Hospitalization.
articles.journal: MCN. The American journal of maternal child nursing
articles.ta: MCN Am J Matern Child Nurs
articles.authors: Newcomb P, Allen M
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine documented clinical and demographic factors associated with positive depression screens during the immediate postpartum period.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic medical record data from 2017 through 2021 from a large private north Texas health care system.
METHODS: Health system informaticists extracted target variables from 23,598 records from 13 hospitals across the system. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics and regression analyses.
RESULTS: Variables identified as conferring significant risk for depression screening scores indicating possible or probable depression included race, parity, admission of their baby to the neonatal intensive care unit, cesarean birth, maternal blood transfusion, history of any mental disorder, stillbirth, race, and marital status.
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: It is likely that screening uncovers transient "baby blues," as well as possible depression, when used immediately following birth. Given the possibility that diagnosable depression may develop following the hospital admission for birth, it is critical that mothers access care after discharge, regardless of the score on a depression screen. Nursing activities to help ensure the continuity of maternity care, such as helping arrange appointments, transportation, and childcare, if necessary, are essential. Providing a coherent program of evidence-based interventions and referrals for mothers experiencing stillbirth should also be a routine part of every postpartum service.

articles.title: Association Between Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes and Postpartum Contraceptive Method Selection and Use.
articles.authors: Trompeter GA, Miller VE, Arora KS
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adverse pregnancy outcomes are associated with self-reported postpartum contraceptive use and method selection.
METHODS: We performed a secondary data analysis of data from the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (phase 8 cohort, 2016-2022). The exposures of interest were adverse pregnancy outcomes, including maternal hypertension, diabetes, preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, and infant death. Contraceptive methods were grouped into four categories: permanent contraception, long-acting reversible contraception, prescription-start methods (patch, ring, pill, or injectable), and patient-start methods (condoms, natural family planning, withdrawal, or abstinence) based on the level of clinical engagement required. We employed multivariable logistic regression to examine the association between adverse pregnancy outcomes and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, we used multinomial logistic regression to analyze whether adverse pregnancy outcomes influenced method selection.
RESULTS: In this analysis of 222,412 individuals, 32.7% of the study sample experienced at least one adverse pregnancy outcome and 77.4% of the sample reported using contraception. In weighted models, experiencing three or more adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraception usage (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.82-0.97). Patients who experienced infant death had lower odds of using any postpartum contraception than those who did not (aOR 0.39; 95% CI, 0.33-0.46). We observed no association between experiencing preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, gestational diabetes, or hypertension and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, experiencing at least one adverse pregnancy outcome was associated with a higher likelihood of using permanent contraception relative to patient-start methods.
CONCLUSION: Experiencing an increasing number of adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraceptive use. Adverse pregnancy outcomes were associated with permanent contraception use. Patient-centered contraceptive counseling and shared decision making to support patients in identifying and actualizing their postpartum reproductive goals are necessary in the wake of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Patient Report of Subsequent Uterine-Sparing Leiomyomata Procedures up to 10 Years.
articles.authors: Graham McNeil K, Sitarik AR, Vines AI et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine risk of subsequent treatment after uterine-sparing procedures for uterine leiomyomata.
METHODS: Study participants from two uterine leiomyomata procedure studies were recontacted. The baseline procedures studied included myomectomy, endometrial ablation, laparoscopic ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA), and uterine artery embolization (UAE). Participants reported all uterine leiomyomata procedures after their baseline uterine-sparing leiomyomata procedure. The subsequent treatment options analyzed included the baseline uterine leiomyomata procedures plus hysterectomy and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided focused ultrasonography. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate differences in retreatment risk according to baseline procedure by means of hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95% CIs. Fisher exact tests were used to examine the association between baseline procedure and retreatment procedure.
RESULTS: The total number of participants in the study is 817. Median age at baseline procedure was 39.7 years; participant median age at recontact was 46.8 years. Follow-up after baseline procedure was 4.0-10.5 years. Baseline procedure types included myomectomy (n=469, 66.0%), endometrial ablation (n=90, 12.7%), RFA (n=96, 13.5%), and UAE (n=56, 7.9%). Of the 204 participants (28.7%) who had retreatment for uterine leiomyomata, the most common subsequent procedure was hysterectomy (n=94, 46.1%), followed by myomectomy (n=57, 27.9%), UAE (n=26, 12.7%), endometrial ablation (n=12, 5.9%), MRI-guided focused ultrasonography (n=9, 4.4%), and RFA (n=6, 2.9%). Within 5 years after the baseline procedure, 79.1% (95% CI, 76.2-82.1%) had no additional uterine procedures; 64.1% (95% CI, 57.7-71.2%) had none within 10 years. When endometrial ablation, RFA, and UAE were compared with myomectomy, RFA was found to have a higher retreatment rate (HR 1.61, 95% CI, 1.08-2.40). Those who had undergone myomectomy at baseline were the least likely (10.9%) and those who had undergone endometrial ablation were most likely (22.2%) to have a subsequent hysterectomy.
CONCLUSION: The majority of women who have uterine-sparing uterine leiomyomata procedures can remain treatment free for 5-10 years.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06430320.

articles.title: Hospital-Level Variation in Antenatal Corticosteroid Use for Late Preterm Births.
articles.authors: Clapp MA, Lee D, Li S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether and to what extent hospitals across the United States vary in their use of late preterm steroids.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of singleton births with known gestational ages identified in the Premier Healthcare Database from 2015 to 2022. The primary variable of interest was hospital-level adoption of antenatal corticosteroid use for late preterm singleton deliveries, calculated as the proportion of late preterm singleton births (34-36 completed weeks of gestation) with any betamethasone exposure during the same late preterm period. Hospital adoption was defined as the weighted average rate of steroid administration among late preterm births across the entire postperiod. Hospitals were ranked by their late preterm steroid adoption rates and categorized by quartile based on the empirical distribution. Temporal trends were assessed using annual hospital-level adoption rates and visualized using time series plots and distributional plots. A logistic regression model was constructed to identify hospital characteristics associated with being a highest-quartile adopter.
RESULTS: The analysis cohort included 726 hospitals and 5,109,270 births, of which 309,837 (6.1%) were singleton late preterm births. Hospital steroid exposure rates ranged from 0% to 92% and were categorized into quartiles based on overall exposure rate, with cutoffs at 22.4%, 33.9%, and 45.1%. Median exposure rates increased progressively across quartiles, from 15.4% (IQR 10.0-18.9%) in the lowest-adopting hospitals (quartile 1) to 54.3% (IQR 49.1-61.0%) in the highest-adopting hospitals (quartile 4), with substantial within-quartile variation. In the multivariable model, urban location was a strong predictor of high adoption after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.03; 95% CI, 1.04-4.02, P=.04). Compared with Midwestern hospitals, Southern hospitals had significantly lower odds of being high adopters (aOR 0.32; 95% CI, 0.17-0.61, P<.001). Among clinical case mix variables, a higher proportion of late preterm births at 34 weeks of gestation was strongly associated with high adoption (aOR 2.39; 95% CI, 1.73-3.36, P<.001).
CONCLUSION: After the publication of the ALPS (Antenatal Late Preterm Steroids) trial, the adoption of late preterm steroid use was heterogeneous among U.S. hospitals. These findings highlight the need for a more in-depth exploration of local factors that drive the adoption of evidence-based practices outside of…

articles.title: Risk Factors for Seven Common Aneuploidies: Successes, Limitations, Missed and New Opportunities.
articles.authors: Cuckle H, Hook EB, Benn P
articles.abstract: Advanced maternal age is a risk factor for common autosomal trisomies, 47,XXY and 47,XXX, and rate schedules by age have been used in genetic counselling and screening protocol design. However, if there is a family history of an affected offspring, rates require adjustment, about which there are considerable uncertainties. These depend upon likely important additional factors, both genetic (e.g., cryptic parental mosaicism) and environmental, some independent of age whilst other age associated. The observed high recurrence risk of some aneuploidies, as well as heterotrisomic recurrence may result from currently unidentified hereditary predisposing factors. Pregnancy losses are not routinely karyotyped, and as most aneuploidies are non-viable, this has diminished awareness of such a possible etiological contribution in this group. Aneuploidy screening has led to early diagnosis of most affected pregnancies but has complicated the research process. The advent of cell-free DNA screening, which is simpler and maximal, could be an opportunity to refocus on understanding aetiology through epidemiology. We advocate cooperation between large population-based screening programs, revitalised birth defect registers, variant databases, and electronic medical record systems. There is a need to reap the benefits of advanced genomic technologies and combine them with traditional epidemiology to further understand aneuploidy origins.

articles.title: Factors associated with neonatal intensive care unit admission in preterm prelabour rupture of membranes: a retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Ay O, Bahçeci P, Taşkıran D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the independent associations of four prespecified variables readily available at the initial assessment (gestational age at preterm prelabour rupture of membranes [PPROM], admission C-reactive protein [CRP], white blood cell [WBC] count and oligohydramnios) with NICU admission in singleton pregnancies between 34 + 0 and 36 + 6 weeks. A secondary exploratory objective was to assess the discriminative performance of a multivariable logistic regression model incorporating these four variables.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 345 singleton pregnancies complicated by PPROM and managed at a tertiary care centre between January 2020 and December 2025. The four prespecified variables were entered simultaneously into a multivariable logistic regression model to evaluate their independent associations with NICU admission. Antenatal corticosteroid exposure was added in a sensitivity analysis. Model discrimination, calibration and bootstrap internal validation were assessed exploratorily.
RESULTS: NICU admission occurred in 89 neonates (25.8%). Gestational age at PPROM was independently associated with NICU admission (adjusted odds ratio 0.607, 95% confidence interval 0.445-0.830; p = 0.002), corresponding to a 39.3% reduction in the odds of NICU admission per 1-week increase. Admission CRP, WBC count and oligohydramnios were not independently associated with NICU admission. The association with gestational age persisted after adjustment for antenatal corticosteroid exposure. Model discrimination was modest (apparent AUC 0.611, 95% CI 0.541-0.681; optimism-corrected AUC 0.584); after bootstrap correction, the calibration slope was 0.796 and the Brier score was 0.191.
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational age at PPROM was the only prespecified variable independently associated with subsequent NICU admission, whereas admission CRP, WBC count and oligohydramnios were not independently associated with NICU admission. The exploratory model showed limited overall performance and should not be used for individual-level risk prediction.

articles.title: Evaluation of the performance of rapid diagnostic tests in point-of-care conditions for serological diagnosis of chagas disease in pregnant women in Colombia.
articles.authors: Marchiol A, Caicedo Díaz RA, Segura M et al.
articles.abstract: Between 2022 and 2024, the National Institute of Health of Colombia and DNDi conducted a performance evaluation study on rapid diagnostic tests under point-of-care conditions for the serological detection of T. cruzi infection in Colombia. The main objective was to assess the performance of four rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) under point-of-care conditions compared to Colombia's official serological diagnostic algorithm based on enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). To achieve this, the performance of each RDT and combined algorithms (parallel and serial configurations) was determined. This was a prospective, observational, and analytical diagnostic study involving 771 pregnant women residing in Colombia. Whole blood samples were collected for rapid tests and serum for reference tests under standardized protocols. All participants were enrolled within the framework of the implementation of the Comprehensive Health Care Route and the Maternal-Perinatal Route of the Ministry of Health, and clinical and laboratory follow-up was guaranteed for all newborns and their mothers. Key findings revealed that the evaluated tests (STAT PAK, ADBIO, BIOLINE, and WL Check Chagas) achieved point estimates of sensitivity ranging from 88.6% to 97.5% and specificity from 98.1% to 100%. STAT PAK showed the best individual performance, and combined algorithms demonstrated promising results. Modeling of the simultaneous (parallel) use of rapid diagnostic tests yielded point estimates of sensitivity between 92.4% and 98.7% and specificity between 97.5% and 99.6%. In turn, serial models, in which a rapid test is initially applied and, if the result is positive, a second test is performed, achieved point estimates of sensitivity between 86.1% and 96.2% and specificity between 99.7% and 100%. Based on the results of this study, RDTs may be considered a valuable tool for screening T. cruzi infection in pregnant women. Selected combinations of RDTs, modeled mathematically from individual RDT results rather than prospectively implemented as diagnostic workflows, showed promising diagnostic performance. The use of RDTs for screening, combined with locally validated simplified confirmation strategies, could significantly improve access to timely diagnosis in rural and remote areas. Furthermore, it could substantially contribute to the widespread implementation of initiatives aimed at universal screening of pregnant women for Chagas disease in Colombia, thereby improving the control…

articles.title: Prevalence and distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes among women living with HIV in Nigeria.
articles.authors: Ifeorah IM, Chinwendu J, Eneh SC et al.
articles.abstract: Women living with HIV (WLHIV) are at significantly higher risk of persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV), and consequently, cervical cancer. However, large scale data on the epidemiology of hrHPV genotypes among WLHIV are limited in Nigeria. The study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of hrHPV among WLHIV in Nigeria. We conducted a cross-sectional study among 1327 WLHIV aged 25-60 years receiving HIV care from six selected Nigeria Implementation Science Alliance-Model Innovation and Research Centers (NISA-MIRCs) across Nigeria. Cervical swabs were obtained, and HPV DNA genotype was determined using the Hybribio Genoarray assay that detects 37 HPV genotypes including 14 high-risk HPVs. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected using interviewer-administered structured questionnaire. Factors independently associated with hrHPV infection were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical analysis was performed using R statistical software (version 4.4.1) with significance set at p < 0.05. Among the 1105 participants with analyzable samples, the overall HPV and hrHPV prevalence were 30.9% and 22.1%, respectively, with regional differences. Non-HPV 16 and 18 accounted for nearly two-thirds (67.6%) of hrHPV infections. The top five most often detected hrHPVs were HPV-58 (14.2%), HPV-16 (12.7%), HPV-52 (12.4%), HPV-31 (10.6%), and HPV-18 (10.3%). In a multivariate analysis, ART usage for one year or less was associated with hrHPV infection (aOR = 8.2, 95% CI 4.3-16.0). This multi-site study showed a significant and genotype-diverse burden of hrHPV among HIV-positive women in Nigeria, with most infections caused by non-HPV16/18 variants. These findings emphasize the need for increased integration of cervical cancer screening within HIV care and support the call for HPV vaccines with broader genotype coverage beyond HPV 16 and 18 to address the prevailing genotype distribution in this population.

articles.title: Addressing barriers and facilitators to family planning uptake among adolescent girls and young women in the anticipated context of long-acting antiretroviral therapy (LA ART).
articles.authors: Hassan SA, Biegon W, Maju M et al.
articles.abstract: Adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) aged 15-24 years bear a disproportionate HIV burden globally, with nearly twice as many AGYW living with HIV as adolescent boys and young men. Despite a 63% reduction in new infections since 2000, 210,000 new infections occur annually among AGYW, four times higher than the 2025 global target of 50,000. Despite emerging opportunities for integrated service delivery, including now through long-acting antiretroviral therapy (LA ART), significant gaps remain in understanding barriers and facilitators to family planning (FP) access among AGYW living with HIV from adolescent and stakeholder perspectives. We conducted focus group discussions (FGDs) with four stakeholder groups in western Kenya (November 2021-April 2022): adolescents and young people living with HIV (AYPLHIV), healthcare providers, advocates, and policymakers. Participants were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling from Rafiki Clinic at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital in Eldoret, Kenya, and transcripts were analyzed using inductive and deductive approaches organized by the socioecological model (SEM). Seven FGDs were conducted with 58 participants total. Four themes emerged across SEM levels: at the policy level, parental consent requirements created policy-level implementation challenges; at the health systems level, barriers included provider stigma, inadequate youth-friendly services, and supply chain gaps; at the interpersonal level, peer mentors were trusted but could perpetuate misinformation, parental disapproval persisted, and male partner involvement was variable, and at the individual level, adolescents preferred discreet, low-maintenance methods, though myths, side effect fears, and procedural anxiety influenced choices. Effective interventions require comprehensive approaches combining policy clarification, provider training, service integration, male partner and parental engagement, evidence-based peer mentor programs, and removal of cost barriers to long-acting reversible contraceptives. Integration of FP within LA ART delivery platforms offers promising opportunities to normalize contraceptive use and improve reproductive health outcomes for AGYW living with HIV.

articles.title: Effects of infertility on relationship quality and mental health outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Juma K, Kairu C, Nungo MA et al.
articles.abstract: Infertility is associated with significant psychosocial challenges, and relationship strain yet remains underprioritized in sub-Saharan African policy and research. We conducted a scoping review to examine the effects of infertility on relationship quality and mental health outcomes among people experiencing infertility in sub-Saharan Africa. We utilized the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. We searched databases including PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, JSTOR, Scopus, Academic Search Complete, PsycINFO, and the Psychology and Behavioral Science Collection. Eligible articles focused on the effects of infertility on mental health and relationship quality in women, men, and couples experiencing infertility and were published between January 2000 and November 2025. We extracted data and conducted an iterative narrative synthesis. We included 70 articles: 36 quantitative, 5 mixed methods, and 29 qualitative. Four key themes emerged, which fit within the socio-ecological model: 1) infertility and relationship quality, 2) infertility and mental health, stigma and discrimination, 3) adaptive coping mechanisms, and 4) maladaptive coping mechanisms. Infertility was associated with anxiety, depression, and emotional distress. Studies revealed profound experiences of isolation and grief over unfulfilled reproductive goals, compounded by societal pressures. Diminished relationship quality was a common outcome among individuals with infertility, manifesting as intimate partner violence, verbal and emotional abuse, loss of intimacy, infidelity, and separation or divorce. Couples with infertility attempted multiple care pathways, including religious, biomedical, and traditional care. Lack of psychosocial support was common, and individuals often coped through substance and drug abuse, isolation, and active avoidance. Complexity of the relationship between infertility, mental health, and relationship quality, reinforces the need for urgent integrated individual and structural interventions that promote holistic fertility care and social support.

articles.title: Buying the 'Right' sperm: racialised appearance and social visibility in Chinese lesbian families.
articles.authors: Liu Y
articles.abstract: China's marital eligibility rules restrict Chinese lala (lesbian) families' access to authorised domestic assisted reproduction, leading some to purchase sperm through informal domestic or cross-border commercial channels. Drawing on 30 in-depth interviews conducted in 2024-2025 with members of 28 lala families, this article examines sperm-provider selection among the 25 families that purchased sperm and entered an IVF pathway. Families evaluated providers' health, education, occupation, ancestry and appearance when imagining their children's future lives. Some valued physical features associated with White ancestry but sought to avoid a conspicuously 'mixed-race' appearance. Anticipated attention to children's appearance or parentage sometimes altered the importance assigned to provider characteristics and, in some cases, the provider ultimately selected. Accounts after childbirth described differences between expected and actual appearances, alongside varied interpretations of comments about children's visible differences. Commercial channels differed in the candidates they offered, transaction costs and access to information for evaluating providers. The analysis shows how expectations of children's social reception shape the value that Chinese lala families attach to racialised appearance, while commercial arrangements affect which provider attributes families can assess and which preferences they can pursue.

articles.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among cisgender bisexual women: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Lawley KA, Kusuma K, Farquhar SA et al.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection in the United States, and a primary cause of cervical cancer. Although cervical cancer is largely preventable through HPV vaccination, vaccine coverage remains suboptimal. Research on HPV prevalence and vaccination among cisgender bisexual women is limited and inconsistent. This may be partly due to variation in how bisexuality is defined. Bisexuality may be operationalized based on sexual identity (e.g., self-identification as bisexual) or sexual behavior (e.g., sexual contact with more than one sex or gender), and these differing definitions may capture distinct populations and yield divergent health findings. This paper proposes a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine whether reported HPV prevalence and vaccination rates among cisgender bisexual women differ based on whether bisexuality is defined by identity or behavior. The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252015) and follows PRISMA-P guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses will estimate pooled HPV prevalence and vaccination rates by definition type. Findings will clarify how operational definitions shape observed HPV-related outcomes and inform tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies for cisgender bisexual women.

articles.title: Developing a digital knowledge-to-practice framework for urinary device management and CAUTI surveillance.
articles.journal: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)
articles.authors: Howcroft E
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inappropriate urinary device use and catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) contribute to preventable patient harm, antimicrobial resistance, incontinence-associated dermatitis (IAD) and prolonged hospitalisation.
AIM: To describe the development, implementation and evaluation of a digitally enabled urinary device knowledge-to-practice framework designed to strengthen clinical governance, improve CAUTI surveillance and support harm prevention.
METHODS: A practice-based implementation programme was led by the Continence Lead Nurse at University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust. Following an evidence review, the Continence Lead Nurse independently undertook a prospective clinical audit of CAUTI symptoms and microbiology findings. The audit informed the decision to embed CAUTI symptom prompts within electronic catheter care plans and develop CAUTIon+, a digital surveillance dashboard. Evidence-based urinary device pathways and digital care plans were integrated into trust-wide clinical policy. A female external catheter (FEC) pathway was evaluated through a 6-week feasibility study and a separate 6-month value-based procurement evaluation.
RESULTS: Implementation established daily prospective CAUTI surveillance through CAUTIon+, supporting earlier identification of suspected infection and structured clinical review. In the initial FEC evaluation, all nine patients reported positive experiences, while 19 of 21 staff respondents highly recommended the device. The subsequent procurement evaluation recorded a 93% reduction in IAD cases (43 to 3), with an estimated 132 bed days avoided and £67 896.30 in reported net savings.
CONCLUSION: Integrating digital urinary device care plans, trust-wide clinical policy and CAUTIon+ surveillance translated evidence into routine practice and strengthened urinary device stewardship. The framework supports earlier clinical intervention and antimicrobial stewardship, with the potential to contribute to prevention of urinary-source sepsis. It aligns with the NHS 10-year health plan's shift towards digital, preventive health care and offers a model for wider NHS evaluation.

articles.title: Neonatal Morbidity Across the Fetal Growth Spectrum in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.authors: Massalha M, DeFrance B, Malinowski K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is linked to fetal overgrowth and, less commonly, fetal growth restriction (FGR). Few studies have examined neonatal outcomes across the full birthweight spectrum while incorporating antenatal Doppler findings. We evaluated the association between birthweight/Doppler-defined growth category and neonatal outcomes in singleton GDM pregnancies.
METHOD: In a retrospective cohort (2011-2024) of singleton GDM pregnancies delivering at ≥32 weeks, growth categories were assigned after delivery using Hadlock birthweight percentiles and antenatal Doppler findings from the last ultrasound within 14 days of delivery. FGR was defined as birthweight <3rd percentile or 3rd-<10th percentile with an abnormal Doppler criterion; SGA was 3rd-<10th percentile without an abnormal available Doppler criterion. The primary outcome was a composite of arterial cord pH <7.1, 5-minute Apgar <7, neonatal hospital stay >2 days, or phototherapy. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal and obstetric factors.
RESULTS: Among 2,099 pregnancies, 7.7% were FGR, 7.5% SGA, 71.8% AGA, and 13.0% LGA. Composite morbidity occurred in 50% of FGR, 40.7% LGA, 29.3% SGA, and 29.1% AGA (p<0.001). FGR (aOR 1.97, 95% CI 1.32-2.92) and LGA (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 1.00-1.85) predicted increased morbidity; SGA did not. The FGR association persisted at term (aOR 1.72, 95% CI 1.10-2.68).
CONCLUSION: In GDM, FGR and LGA were associated with greater neonatal morbidity. SGA without an abnormal available Doppler criterion was not associated with increased morbidity compared with AGA. These findings support prospective evaluation of Doppler-based risk stratification among small fetuses.

articles.title: Three-in-One Injectable Hydrogel Orchestrating Host-Bacteria Targeting, Retention, and Autophagy for Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus-Infected Mastitis Therapy.
articles.authors: Fan X, Li Y, Xu X et al.
articles.abstract: MRSA mastitis is clinically refractory and characterized by progressive inflammation driven by intracellular bacteria that form persistent niches in mammary epithelial cells and macrophages to evade antimicrobial clearance. Conventional antibiotics, particularly β-lactams, are widely used but suffer from poor intracellular accumulation, failing to reach these reservoirs. Even nanocarrier-based strategies struggle to achieve efficient endosomal escape and precise intracellular targeting. Herein, we report a fibronectin-functionalized, fluorinated PLGA nanoparticle encapsulating amoxicillin and sulbactam (Fn-F-PLGA@A/S) engineered with a 2.5% (w/w) fluorinated core for efficient endosomal escape. The fibronectin decoration enables sequential targeting of both host integrins and bacterial fibronectin-binding proteins (FnBPs). Fn-F-PLGA@A/S achieved efficient intracellular delivery, clearing 90% of intracellular MRSA in macrophages and epithelial cells within 4 h in vitro. To prolong mammary retention, Fn-F-PLGA@A/S was loaded into a thermosensitive hydrogel. In a murine MRSA mastitis model, a single intramammary dose of the gel formulation achieved >90% bacterial reduction, attenuated TNF-α and IL-6, and preserved alveolar architecture and tight junctions. Proteomic analysis revealed upregulation of AMPK-mediated autophagy, suggesting that beyond direct antibiotic action, the potent intracellular clearance achieved by Fn-F-PLGA may involve the engagement of host autophagic machinery, potentially facilitating the sequestration of MRSA within degradative compartments. Collectively, by integrating sequential targeting, sustained local retention, and autophagic engagement, this platform provides a robust strategy to address the key limitations of conventional antibiotics against intracellular pathogens in refractory infections.

articles.title: Extracellular Vesicles at the Intersection of Environmental Exposure and Preterm Birth: A Research Agenda for an Emerging Field.
articles.authors: Corradetti B, Anderson B, Symanski E
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Preterm birth (PTB), defined as delivery before 37 completed weeks of gestation, affects approximately 10% of pregnancies in the United States and remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. Persistent disparities in PTB rates are not fully explained by traditional risk factors, highlighting the need for biomarkers of environmental exposures and their biological effects during pregnancy. While direct human evidence linking environmental exposures to extracellular vesicle (EV) alterations that contribute to PTB remains limited, this review examines whether EVs provide a plausible, testable framework linking environmental exposures with maternal-fetal signaling relevant to PTB risk.
RECENT FINDINGS: Maternal exposure to environmental pollutants and adverse neighborhood-level conditions, which disproportionately burden marginalized communities, has been associated with increased PTB risk. These exposures have been associated with inflammatory, metabolic, and epigenetic alterations, some of which are reflected in the cargo of circulating EVs, and profiling of maternal plasma EVs has identified signatures enriched for inflammatory and coagulation pathways among women who deliver preterm. Most of this evidence derives from non-reproductive toxicology, related pregnancy complications or biological plausibility, rather than from studies directly evaluating whether EVs mediate the effects of environmental exposures on PTB risk. Integrating EV biology with environmental health research offers a noninvasive framework for capturing the impact of environmental exposures on maternal-fetal signaling during pregnancy. Owing to the lack of direct human evidence, we present this as a forward-looking research agenda and outline the prospective, exposure-characterized studies needed to determine whether EV-based biomarkers can improve PTB risk stratification.

articles.title: Exosomal microRNAs in apoptosis and chemoresistance of ovarian cancer: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
articles.authors: Gong Y, Li J
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, largely because of late diagnosis, frequent recurrence, and acquired chemoresistance. Impaired apoptotic regulation is a central mechanism underlying tumor persistence and reduced sensitivity to platinum- and taxane-based chemotherapy. Exosomes are important mediators of intercellular communication within the ovarian cancer microenvironment and can transfer microRNAs (miRNAs) that reprogram gene expression and signaling pathways in recipient cells. Accumulating evidence indicates that exosomal miRNAs regulate apoptosis-related pathways, including Bcl-2 family signaling, caspase activation, p53 signaling, and PI3K/Akt signaling, thereby influencing tumor cell survival, immune escape, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and therapeutic response. Exosome-mediated miRNA transfer also contributes to chemoresistance by suppressing apoptosis, enhancing survival signaling, and disseminating resistant phenotypes among tumor and stromal cells. In addition, preclinical studies suggest that selected natural bioactive compounds may influence miRNA- and exosome-related signaling as well as apoptosis-associated pathways; however, direct evidence for modulation of ovarian-cancer exosomal miRNAs remains limited. This review summarizes current evidence on the roles of exosomal miRNAs in apoptosis regulation and chemoresistance in ovarian cancer, with emphasis on molecular mechanisms, biomarker potential, and therapeutic implications. Targeting the exosome-miRNA-apoptosis axis may provide a promising framework for improving treatment response in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Effect of pelvic floor reconstruction on postoperative urinary continence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Wu X, Lu H, Huang W et al.
articles.abstract: Urinary incontinence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) remains a common and burdensome complication. Whether pelvic floor reconstruction (PR) helps restore continence is still debated. We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to October 8, 2026, for controlled studies comparing PR with no reconstruction (nPR) during RARP. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Begg's, and Egger's tests. The certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach. Twenty-two studies (5 RCTs and 17 non-RCTs) with 6425 patients (4134 PR and 2291 nPR) were included. At postoperative weeks 1, 2, 4, 12, 24, and 52, continence rates were significantly higher in the PR group than in the nPR group (pooled ORs ranged from 2.58 at 24 weeks to 2.82 at 12 weeks; all 95% CIs excluded 1). Significant heterogeneity was found at all time points except week 2 (I² = 74.3%-87.5%); the 2-week analysis showed minimal heterogeneity (I² = 0.0%). No obvious publication bias was detected. The GRADE assessment indicated that the certainty of evidence was moderate at 2 weeks and low at all other time points, primarily due to the predominance of observational studies and high heterogeneity. Pelvic floor reconstruction during RARP may improve early urinary continence recovery. However, given the low certainty of evidence, considerable heterogeneity, and the predominance of observational data, the magnitude and durability of this benefit remain uncertain. PR should be considered a reasonable option rather than a standardized intraoperative adjunct. Further high-quality, multicenter RCTs with uniform endpoints are warranted.

articles.title: Colposcopic magnified scanning-assisted CO2 laser treatment (CMSLT) for vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (VaHSIL): A single-center prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Pieralli A, Venzi R, Maccarrone C et al.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of Colposcopic Magnified Scanning Laser Treatments (CMSLT), divided into laser excision (CMSLE) and vaporization (CMSLV), using a scanner-assisted CO2 laser as a singular outpatient therapeutic modality for patients affected by vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (vaHSIL). vaginal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (vaHSIL) is a rare condition associated with persistent high-risk HPV infection, carrying a concrete potential for progression into invasive carcinoma. Due to diagnostic complexities and the rarity of the disease, its optimal clinical management and treatment standardization remain controversial. This prospective non-randomized cohort study was conducted between January 2022 and June 2024 on 63 patients with histologically confirmed vaHSIL. Based on the 2011 IFCPC colposcopic terminology, patients were assigned to either the CMSLV group (n = 22) or the CMSLE group (n = 41). The outpatient protocol utilized a laser system implemented with a computerized surgical scanner-assisted micromanipulator. The two-year follow-up included semi-annual screenings with HPV testing, cytology, and colposcopy. Follow-up adherence was high, with a dropout rate limited to 11.3%. The cumulative recurrence risk for vaHSIL was 14.5%, with no statistically significant difference between the two modalities, although the CMSLE group showed a higher 2-year disease-free survival rate (70% vs. 57%). The progression rate to invasive carcinoma was 1.6% 1 cases in the CMSLE cohort), revealing a 2.4% rate of occult cancer missed at initial colposcopic assignment. Only one major complication occurred (vaginal perforation, 1.6% in a post-hysterectomy patient), with no minor complications or long-term sequelae (dyspareunia or pain) reported. CMSLT may represent feasible approach since it happened to be safe, effective and associated with patient compliance. The precision of the scanner-assisted technology minimizes thermal damage and the risk of undertreating occult cancer, allowing for tailored and efficient therapy.

articles.title: Synergistic antitumor activity of Napabucasin and Curcumin via ROS accumulation and apoptotic cell death induction in ovarian cancer cells.
articles.authors: Saruhan S, Özdemir D, Baydaş G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite therapeutic advances, ovarian cancer remains a formidable malignancy due to frequent chemoresistance and recurrence. Targeting STAT3 is promising, however Napabucasin monotherapy often shows limited efficacy due to activation of compensatory survival pathways. Combining Napabucasin with multi targeted agents such as Curcumin therefore offers a rational and innovative strategy to overcome these limitations. In this study, we examined the synergistic effects of Napabucasin and Curcumin in ovarian cancer cells and explored underlying mechanisms.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Cell viability and drug interactions were assessed in OVCAR 3 and SKOV 3 lines using heat map analysis. Intracellular ROS generation and MMP changes were monitored by fluorescence microscopy, while apoptosis and cell cycle distribution were quantified via flow cytometry. Long term proliferation and migration were evaluated through colony formation and scratch assays. The combination markedly reduced viability and proliferation compared to either agent alone. The combination treatment triggered robust apoptosis, as evidenced by the emergence of a sub-G0 apoptotic peak accompanied by a reduction in the S and G2/M phases. Mechanistically, it enhanced ROS production, disrupted MMP, and strongly suppressed migration.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight a potent synergistic interaction between Napabucasin and Curcumin, supporting this combination as a promising therapeutic approach for ovarian cancer. Further translational and in vivo studies are warranted to validate clinical relevance and accelerate progress toward clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Hematological trajectories and pregnancy complications in essential thrombocythemia and polycythemia vera.
articles.authors: Klok FR, Jørgensen FS, Nielsen CGS et al.
articles.abstract: Women with essential thrombocythemia (ET) and polycythemia vera (PV) are at increased risk of pregnancy complications. During pregnancy, hematologic parameters tend to approach normal values, and previous studies have reported that a greater decline in platelet counts in ET is associated with reduced risk of complications. In this study, we examined longitudinal trajectories of platelet count, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and leukocyte count during pregnancy, characterized pregnancy outcomes, and investigated the association between platelet trajectories and preeclampsia. We established a longitudinal cohort of pregnant women with ET and PV in the Capital Region and Region Zealand between 2010 and 2024, using data from regional laboratory information systems and Danish health registries. In total, 41 ET and 5 PV pregnancies in 35 women were included. The mean age at MPN diagnosis was 30.1 years in women with ET and 34.1 years in women with PV. In ET pregnancies, platelet counts, hemoglobin, hematocrit and leukocyte count changed by - 44%, - 5%, - 12% and + 55%, respectively, from baseline to delivery, and in PV pregnancies - 36%, - 26%, - 25% and + 47%, respectively. Overall, 29% of ET pregnancies had a maternal complication, with preeclampsia being the most common (12%). ET women who developed preeclampsia had significantly higher platelet counts before pregnancy and experienced a greater decline in platelet counts during pregnancy than women without preeclampsia. Thus, hematologic trajectories during pregnancy may help identify women at increased risk of preeclampsia.

articles.title: A Crisis in the Treatment of Osteoporosis - 10 Years Later, the US Care Gap is Still Open.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.authors: Walker MD, Khosla S, Shane E et al.
articles.abstract: A decade ago, we published an editorial in the Journal of Bone and Mineral Research describing a crisis in osteoporosis treatment. In this Perspective, we reassess osteoporosis care and progress addressing that crisis. Despite the availability of safe and effective medications that reduce fracture risk, the osteoporosis care gap persists and may have widened in the United States (US). Fewer than 15% of patients receive osteoporosis therapy within one year of a fragility fracture, and treatment rates declined between 2015 and 2022. Meanwhile, declining hip fracture rates plateaued around 2012 and remain stable, while clinical vertebral fractures have increased. Persistent barriers include limited patient awareness of bone health, low screening rates, reduced access to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), concerns regarding treatment-related adverse events, underutilization of fracture liaison services, as well as racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic disparities. Despite this, the tools available to address the crisis have expanded. Advances that can help narrow the current care gap include new osteoanabolic agents; improved understanding of atypical femur fracture risk-benefit profiles; goal-directed treatment; opportunistic screening and diagnosis; artificial intelligence-enabled vertebral fracture detection; and electronic medical record-based decision support. Other developments may reduce the future burden of osteoporosis and fracture, including growing evidence supporting primary prevention, evolving perspectives on menopausal hormone therapy, and U.S. Food and Drug Administration qualification of total hip bone mineral density as a surrogate endpoint for fractures, which may facilitate more efficient drug development. The challenge now is to implement available approaches for patients at high fracture risk while continuing to consider strategies that shift osteoporosis care toward earlier prevention. Progress will require coordinated action by healthcare systems, providers, payers, professional societies, and policymakers to improve equitable access to fracture prevention.

articles.title: Impact of in vitro fertilization on disease activity and pregnancy outcomes in women with inflammatory bowel disease.
articles.authors: Khanna R, Garcia NM, Fenton C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) increasingly utilize assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs) like in vitro fertilization and oocyte cryopreservation. Data regarding ART associated IBD flare risk are limited. We evaluated the risk of disease exacerbation among women with IBD undergoing ART.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study evaluated women with IBD undergoing ART. Electronic medical records were abstracted for demographics, IBD history, and fertility history. Disease activity was assessed via medication exposure, biomarkers, and healthcare utilization 6 months pre- and post-ART. The primary outcome was disease flare (therapy modification, steroid initiation, or IBD-related hospitalization) within 6 months of ART. Secondary outcomes included successful egg retrieval, biochemical pregnancy, and live birth. Demographics were analyzed at the patient level and outcome data at the ART encounter level.
RESULTS: We included 49 women (mean age 37.1 ± 4.01 years, body mass index 25.7 ± 4.72 kg/m2) who underwent 149 ART encounters. Most had Crohn's disease (63.3%) or ulcerative colitis (34.7%), with a mean disease duration of 13.4 ± 7.16 years. Pre-ART, therapies included ustekinumab (20.8%), anti-tumor necrosis factors (12.1%), and corticosteroids (6.7%), or no therapy (29.5%). In 149 ART encounters (86 oocyte retrievals and 63 embryo transfers), the overall disease flare rate was 3.4% (n = 5 of 149, representing 5 unique patients). Flares occurred after embryo transfer during established pregnancy (gestational week ≥8), with no flares occurring during or immediately following oocyte retrieval. Secondary endpoints showed low rates of new corticosteroid use (2.7%), IBD-related hospitalizations (0.7%), and medication dose escalation (0.7%). Among the 63 embryo transfers, biochemical pregnancy occurred in 63.5% (n = 40 of 63) and live births in 42.9% (n = 27 of 63).
CONCLUSIONS: Across all 149 ART encounters, patients with IBD demonstrated low flare risk and live birth rates comparable to the general population. Under multidisciplinary guidance, ART is a safe and viable option in IBD.

articles.title: Cerebrovascular mechanisms of stroke severity in offspring from pre-eclamptic pregnancy.
articles.authors: Savage-Hunt RD, Tremble SM, Brigl JC et al.
articles.abstract: Offspring from pre-eclamptic pregnancies face elevated ischaemic stroke risk throughout life, yet the mechanisms linking adverse intrauterine exposure to adult cerebrovascular vulnerability remain unknown. Distal leptomeningeal anastomoses (LMAs), which develop during late gestation are key determinants of stroke severity and represent a plausible target of prenatal programming. Here, we show that experimental preeclampsia (ePE) in rats establishes a persistent cerebrovascular structural and transcriptional phenotype in adult offspring. Following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion, ePE-exposed males exhibited increased infarct volume, oedema, enhanced perfusion deficit and smaller LMA diameters relative to normal pregnant offspring, and 83% had microvascular stasis after stroke. Female offspring were protected from stroke-induced brain injury despite sharing a similar transcriptional landscape. RNA sequencing and DNA methylation profiling revealed differentially expressed genes and discrete differentially methylated regions enriched for vascular development and VEGF-Notch signalling in ePE offspring. These findings support the possibility of a developmental origin of cerebrovascular stroke risk, implicating gestational programming of cerebrovascular gene expression as a sex modulated determinant of adult stroke outcome and a potential target for early intervention. KEY POINTS: Offspring born from pre-eclamptic pregnancies have a greater lifetime risk and death from ischaemic stroke, but why this occurs is unknown. Pial collaterals form during the late gestational period and are a key determinant of stroke severity. Using a rat model, we showed that compared to normal pregnancy, male offspring from pre-eclamptic pregnancies had smaller diameter pial collaterals which was associated with decreased collateral recruitment during ischaemic stroke and worsened stroke outcome. RNA analysis revealed altered expression of genes related to blood vessel development and function in adult offspring. These findings suggest that preeclampsia leads to lasting changes in cerebrovascular structure and gene expression which is associated with increased stroke severity in male offspring suggesting a potential window for early intervention.

articles.title: Non-invasive vascular assessment in gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Alkhurainej SE, Khan F, Murdoch CE
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate evidence on non-invasive vascular assessment techniques used during pregnancy and/or the postpartum period to identify vascular abnormalities associated with gestational hypertension and explore potential implications for long-term cardiovascular health.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and gray literature (to May-2024) identified studies assessing vascular structure or function using pulse-wave velocity, carotid intima-media thickness, flow-mediated dilation, ophthalmic artery Doppler, and retinal imaging. Forty-nine studies involving 32,683 participants. Due to the heterogeneity in study design and methodology, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Women with gestational hypertension generally demonstrated increased arterial stiffness (elevated pulse wave velocity and augmentation index), impaired endothelial function (reduced flow-mediated dilation), and increased intima-media thickness during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Several studies reported persistence of these abnormalities from weeks to years after delivery, although findings were inconsistent. Ophthalmic artery Doppler studies showed variable alterations in peak systolic velocity ratios and pulsatility index reported in hypertensive pregnancies. Retinal imaging identified alterations in retinal vessel caliber during pregnancy and the postpartum period, with some abnormalities reported up to six years postpartum.
CONCLUSION: Non-invasive vascular assessments can help identify macrovascular, microvascular, and endothelial abnormalities in women with gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Although some abnormalities persist beyond delivery and may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk, evidence remains insufficient to support their use as independent predictors of future cardiovascular events. Further standardized, prospective longitudinal studies are needed to determine their prognostic and clinical value.

articles.title: Psychometric performance of the perinatal bereavement care confidence scale among maternity healthcare workers in Lagos, Nigeria: A cross-sectional evaluation.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Lebimoyo A, Adewuya AO, Adewunmi AA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the internal structure, internal consistency, and score distributions of the 43-item Perinatal Bereavement Care Confidence Scale (PBCCS) among nurses and midwives working in public maternity services in Lagos, Nigeria.
METHODS: This secondary psychometric analysis used cross-sectional BEACON data from 215 participants. Six negatively phrased items were reverse-scored. Internal consistency, ordinal reliability, item performance, floor/ceiling effects, and exploratory construct validity were examined. Structural validity was assessed primarily by polychoric weighted least squares mean and variance adjusted (WLSMV) confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) of the published nine-subdomain model, with one-factor, four-factor, and bifactor alternatives; scale-specific exploratory factor analysis (EFAs) were secondary diagnostics.
RESULTS: Seven subdomains had Cronbach alpha values of 0.774-0.938; Functional Skills was lower, at  0.672 and Environmental/Workload lowest, at  0.591. The published nine-factor CFA fitted below conventional benchmarks (robust comparative fit index [CFI] = 0.869, Tucker-Lewis index = 0.856, root mean square error of approximation [RMSEA] = 0.097, 90% confidence interval [CI] 0.092-0.101, standardized root mean squared residual = 0.118) but better than one-factor (CFI = 0.564) and four-factor (CFI = 0.763) alternatives. A bifactor model yielded hierarchical omega = 0.78 and explained common variance = 0.53 but fitted worse than the nine-factor model. Exact ceiling effects were 26.0% for Emotional Knowledge and 37.7% for Continuous Education. Environmental/Workload (mean 2.71) and Institutional Support (2.93) were the lowest-scoring subdomains.
CONCLUSION: Most PBCCS subdomains showed acceptable or stronger reliability after corrected scoring, but the published structure was only partially supported. The nine-subdomain model preserved meaningful distinctions better than simpler alternatives, while wording effects and Environmental/Workload heterogeneity contributed to misfit. A total score might summarize some common variance, but domain profiles remain necessary for interpretation and service planning.

articles.title: Use of autologous hamstring tendon in laparoscopic hysterosacropexy: short term outcomes from a prospective pilot study.
articles.authors: Szepieniec WK, Bil A, Bilir E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive pelvic organ prolapse (POP) surgery is increasingly globally, particularly for uterus-preserving procedures. While laparoscopic correction with synthetic mesh remains the standard approach, growing concern over mesh-related complications has prompted increasing interest in native tissue alternatives. Our prospective pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and early clinical outcomes of laparoscopic hysterosacropexy using autologous tendon grafts for the correction of apical POP via patient reported outcomes (PROs).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We included women with symptomatic apical POP (≥ stage II, POP-Q).We excluded the patients with obesity, prior major abdominal or pelvic surgery, or prior knee procedures. Hamstring autografts (semitendinosus or gracilis) were harvested and used for apical suspension. Clinical evaluations were conducted preoperatively as well as at 6 weeks and 6 months postoperatively. In addition, PROs were measured using the PFIQ-7, UIQ-7, and CRAIQ-7 questionnaires.
RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 44.3 years (±10.75), and the mean body mass index was 21.72 kg/m² (± 2.4). At the 6-month postoperative follow-up, all patients achieved complete anatomical and functional success. Global PFIQ-7 scores demonstrated a marked reduction from a preoperative mean of 128.5 (± 82.06) to 23.0 (± 33.32) at 6 months (p value < 0.001).Significant changes were observed between the preoperative and 6-week assessments for UIQ-7 (p value = 0.008) and POPIQ-7 (p value = 0.012).
CONCLUSIONS: Laparoscopic hysterosacropexy using autologous tendon grafts appears to be a safe and clinically effective mesh-free alternative for apical POP repair in the short term. Further randomized studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up periods are warranted to validate long-term outcomes and to compare this approach more robustly with other techniques.

articles.title: Second-Stage Labor Duration and Risk of Postpartum Urinary Retention in Nulliparous Women With Epidural Analgesia.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Matsui H, Ichinose M, Iriyama T et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Postpartum urinary retention (PUR) is a clinically relevant complication after vaginal delivery; however, independent risk factors among nulliparous women receiving epidural analgesia remain unclear. To identify independent risk factors for PUR among nulliparous women undergoing vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of nulliparous women who underwent vaginal delivery at ≥ 37 weeks' gestation with epidural analgesia between January 2022 and June 2023 at our institution. PUR was defined as either absence of spontaneous voiding with no urge to void at 6 h postpartum, or diminished urge to void with a postvoid residual volume ≥ 150 mL measured by intermittent catheterization despite spontaneous voiding. Variables were compared between the PUR and non-PUR groups. Multivariable logistic regression was then performed with second-stage labor duration prespecified as the primary variable of interest. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using ROC analysis.
RESULTS: Among 215 women, PUR occurred in 26 (12.1%). Second-stage labor duration was significantly longer in women with PUR than in those without (228 [151-275] min vs. 127 [70-210] min; p = 0.0005). In multivariable models adjusting separately for pre-pregnancy body mass index, neonatal birth weight, operative vaginal delivery, or duration of continuous epidural infusion, each 1-h increase in second-stage labor duration remained independently associated with PUR. ROC analysis demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC 0.71; 95% CI, 0.61-0.81), with an optimal cutoff of 215 min (sensitivity 61%, specificity 76%).
CONCLUSIONS: In nulliparous women undergoing vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia, second-stage labor duration is independently associated with PUR. It may serve as a pragmatic marker for targeted postpartum bladder surveillance.

articles.title: Dose-Response Relationship Between Household Food Insecurity Severity and Lower Urinary Tract Symptom Subtypes: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Seto A, Yang A, Sheen M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether household food insecurity severity is associated with lower urinary tract symptom subtypes in a dose-response manner and to evaluate mediating pathways, in a nationally representative sample of US adults.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed pooled data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2005-2020, comprising 36 713 adults aged 20 years or older. Household food security (full, marginal, low, or very low) was defined by the United States Department of Agriculture Household Food Security Survey Module. Nocturia and urgency, stress, and mixed incontinence were ascertained by self-report. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios across four sequential models, with a test for linear trend. Secondary analyses evaluated mediation by systemic inflammation, cardiometabolic comorbidity, dietary intake, and depressive symptoms.
RESULTS: In fully adjusted models, very low food security was associated with higher odds of nocturia (odds ratio 1.52; 95% confidence interval, 1.31-1.77), urgency incontinence (1.60; 1.37-1.87), stress incontinence (1.37; 1.16-1.62), and mixed incontinence (1.86; 1.52-2.27), with a significant dose-response trend for all (all p for trend < 0.0001). Gradients were steepest for the overactivity-associated subtypes and persisted after adjustment for income. Inflammation and diet showed essentially no mediation; cardiometabolic comorbidity and depressive symptoms accounted for 9% to 18% and 24% to 30%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Household food insecurity was independently and dose-responsively associated with all subtypes examined, partly explained by depressive symptoms and cardiometabolic comorbidity but not inflammation or diet. These findings support recognizing food insecurity as a modifiable social determinant relevant to bladder health.

articles.title: Self-reported verbal assessment in the evaluation of urinary continence after 3D-laparoscopic prostatectomy: a single-centre prospective registered study.
articles.authors: Valli J, Kaipia A, Huhtala H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare self-reported verbal assessment of safety-pad use with scores on the urinary incontinence domain of Expanded Prostate Cancer Index Composite-26 (UI-EPIC-26) and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) in the evaluation of post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence (PPI).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 105 men underwent 3D-laparoscopic radical prostatectomy at Seinäjoki Central Hospital, Finland. Patients were classified into four urinary continence groups based on self-reported assessment of urinary continence (S-RUC): no pads, single daytime safety pad, ≥ 2 daytime pads (continent at night), or pads used day and night. Continence was assessed preoperatively and at 3, 12 and 24 months postoperatively using S-RUC, UI-EPIC-26 and VAS. Associations were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation.
RESULTS: Baseline data were available for all 105 patients. Among 103 patients with postoperative S-RUC data, full continence (no pads) rates were 24.8, 64.1 and 65.7% at 3, 12 and 24 months, respectively. S-RUC showed strong correlations with UI-EPIC-26 (ρ = -0.84, -0.84 and -0.80) and VAS (ρ = -0.80, -0.65 and -0.66) at 3, 12 and 24 months, respectively (all p < 0.001). Baseline correlations were weaker.
CONCLUSIONS: Simple verbal assessment of safety-pad use may provide a practical and clinically useful approach to assessing patient-perceived PPI in routine clinical follow-up.

articles.title: Serum estradiol, reproductive timing, and melanoma prevalence among women: population-based evidence and single-cell transcriptomic insights.
articles.authors: Zhao T, Xie R, Li C et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence linking female reproductive factors and circulating estradiol with melanoma has been inconsistent. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of US women in NHANES 2009-2023. Exposure-specific analytic samples were constructed for age at menarche, pregnancy history, natural menopause age, and serum estradiol. Associations with prevalent melanoma were examined using survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression. XGBoost with Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used as a complementary prediction analysis. Two melanoma single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets (GSE269936 and GSE115978) were analyzed to examine the patient-level association between inferred ESR2 activity and E2F/G2M proliferation-related transcriptional activity. Low estradiol levels (0-20 pg/mL) were associated with higher odds of prevalent melanoma [adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 3.382; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.304-8.773; P = 0.013], and late menarche (>14 years) was also associated with higher odds (adjusted OR = 2.074; 95% CI = 1.118-3.846; P = 0.021). Pregnancy history was not significantly associated with melanoma prevalence. The association for premature menopause could not be estimated because no melanoma cases occurred in this category. Low estradiol was the highest-ranked encoded feature by global SHAP importance (mean |SHAP| = 0.157). Across 10 patients inferred ESR2 activity was inversely correlated with the composite proliferation score (pooled r = -0.250; 95% CI = -0.392 to -0.095; P = 0.006). Lower estradiol levels and later menarche were associated with higher odds of prevalent melanoma. The single-cell finding requires prospective and functional studies are needed to determine the biological and clinical relevance of these findings.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Controlled-Release Nifedipine for Tocolysis in Normotensive Pregnant Women.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Ushida T, Fujito S, Shiraishi Y et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Nifedipine is widely used as a tocolytic agent for threatened preterm labor. However, its hemodynamic effects in normotensive pregnant women, particularly when administered as a controlled-release formulation, remain unclear. We evaluated changes in maternal hemodynamics and adverse effects after controlled-release nifedipine administration in normotensive pregnant women with threatened preterm labor.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included normotensive women with singleton pregnancies who received controlled-release nifedipine as maintenance therapy for threatened preterm labor between 2018 and 2025. Maternal blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure < 60 mmHg), tachycardia (≥ 120 beats/min), and adverse maternal and fetal effects were evaluated before and after nifedipine administration.
RESULTS: Overall, 38 women were included in the final analyses. Systolic blood pressure significantly decreased from 110.2 ± 9.1 mmHg to 107.5 ± 10.2 mmHg after administration (mean change, -2.7 mmHg; 95% confidence interval, -4.5 to -0.8; p < 0.01). Diastolic blood pressure did not change significantly (-0.7 mmHg; -2.2 to 0.8 mmHg; p = 0.35). Heart rate significantly decreased from 95.3 ± 14.5 to 90.9 ± 12.4 beats/min. The incidence of hypotension and tachycardia did not differ significantly after nifedipine administration. No emergency deliveries were attributed to maternal hypotension. Headache was the most commonly reported adverse effect (28.9%).
CONCLUSIONS: Controlled-release nifedipine was associated with a small decrease in systolic blood pressure without serious maternal or fetal adverse events. With appropriate monitoring, controlled-release nifedipine may be a feasible option for maintenance or adjunctive tocolytic therapy in normotensive pregnant women.

articles.title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models Incorporating TGFBIp Expression for Prognosis Prediction in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Guo Y, Li Z, Song W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) exhibits substantial heterogeneity in clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for diverse prognostic tools. Transforming growth factor-β-induced protein (TGFBIp) has been implicated in ovarian cancer progression, but its incremental prognostic value within machine learning frameworks remains unexplored.
AIMS: To develop and validate machine learning models incorporating TGFBIp expression to predict vital status and recurrence in EOC patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 155 EOC patients from a tissue microarray. TGFBIp expression in tumor cells and stroma was assessed by immunohistochemistry. Twelve machine learning algorithms were benchmarked across four feature inclusion strategies, with TGFBIp expression sequentially added to a baseline clinicopathological model. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, the area under the precision-recall curve, calibration intercept and slope, Brier score, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The incremental value of TGFBIp was formally tested by paired bootstrap comparison of test-set AUCs. SHAP analysis was performed for model interpretation. The support vector machine (SVM) with Strategy 4 (incorporating both tumor and stromal TGFBIp) was selected for vital status prediction, achieving a test-set AUC of 0.951 (95% CI 0.870-0.998), accuracy of 0.872, sensitivity of 0.920, specificity of 0.818, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.900. The random forest (RF) with Strategy 4 was selected for recurrence prediction, achieving a test-set AUC of 0.936 (95% CI 0.816-1.000), sensitivity of 0.974, and NPV of 0.800. Adding TGFBIp features significantly improved vital status prediction (ΔAUC +0.038, 95% CI +0.002 to +0.092 for Strategy 4 vs. baseline). Calibration was acceptable for the vital status model (test-set calibration intercept -0.24, slope 1.25, Brier score 0.071). SHAP analysis identified maximum tumor diameter, grade, stage, and TGFBIp expression as leading predictors; tumoral TGFBIp contributed to both outcomes, whereas stromal TGFBIp contributed mainly to vital status prediction. DCA suggested potential clinical utility across a broad range of threshold probabilities.
CONCLUSION: We established a machine learning framework incorporating compartment-specific TGFBIp expression for EOC prognosis. TGFBIp in tumor cells provided incremental prognostic information…

articles.title: Prospective Analysis of Breastfeeding History and Ovarian Cancer Risk: Results From the Ovarian Cancer Cohort Consortium.
articles.authors: Fest SN, Vitonis AF, Townsend MK et al.
articles.abstract: Breastfeeding has been found to be associated with decreased ovarian cancer risk, but prospective analyses are sparse and limited by insufficient sample sizes to assess associations by histotype and patient characteristics. To investigate the association between breastfeeding (ever/never, duration, and timing) and incident epithelial ovarian cancer risk overall and by histotype, we leveraged harmonized individual-level data from 11 prospective cohort studies participating in the Ovarian Cancer Cohort Consortium, including 620,645 parous individuals, among whom 3730 developed incident epithelial ovarian cancer. Using pooled logistic regression models, odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs were calculated for the association between breastfeeding and ovarian cancer risk. Ever versus never breastfeeding was associated with a 15% lower risk of ovarian cancer (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.75-0.96), with inverse associations observed for high-grade serous (OR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.81-0.98) and endometrioid tumors (OR = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.58-0.95). Compared to never breastfeeding, inverse associations were observed for breastfeeding for more than 12 months across total pregnancies (OR = 0.79, 95% CI = 0.68-0.92) as well as for durations of 1-3 months (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.74-0.98). Similar results were observed when stratified by parity. Although risk reduction persisted for up to 30 years since last breastfeeding (OR = 0.81, 95% CI = 0.72-0.91; p-trend < 0.0001), the inverse association was greatest for more recent breastfeeding (OR = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.47-0.66 for < = 20 years). This pooled prospective study provides further evidence that breastfeeding, even for less than 3 months, is associated with lower ovarian cancer risk overall and across most histotypes independent of parity.

articles.title: The role of reproductive health policies in shaping Women's well-being in the Middle East.
articles.authors: Almarzooqi M, Hussein FA, Alqassem A et al.
articles.abstract: Women's reproductive health in the Middle East remains shaped by a complex interplay of sociocultural norms, economic, and political determinants. Despite regional progress in healthcare, inequities persist in women's access to comprehensive reproductive services. Several Middle Eastern countries, including the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Jordan, have initiated national policies and awareness programs to promote women's health. In contrast, others, such as Afghanistan, Yemen, Libya, and Sudan, face systemic and policy-related challenges. This Perspective compares national strategies for women's reproductive health across Middle Eastern countries, highlighting policy frameworks, medical insurance coverage, and barriers to equitable care. We examine how socioeconomic, cultural, and legislative factors influence the accessibility and quality of reproductive health services. Furthermore, we assess the impact of insurance coverage and healthcare financing on women's well-being and examine how policy gaps perpetuate disparities in maternal, sexual, and reproductive health outcomes.

articles.title: Transcription factor 3 cooperates with CXXC finger protein 1 to regulate histone H3K4 trimethylation and developmental competence in mouse oocytes.
articles.authors: Qiu YX, Zhang C, Cao LR et al.
