articles.abstract: During oogenesis, the establishment of oocyte-specific gene expression relies on epigenetic and transcriptional remodeling. Both histone modifications and transcription factors are crucial for the oocyte to acquire developmental competence; however, the mechanisms involved remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify transcription factor 3 (TCF3), an E-protein family member, as a key maternal regulator of oocyte developmental potential. Oocyte-specific deletion of Tcf3 results in female infertility, characterized by impaired meiotic maturation and early embryonic arrest at the two-cell stage. These defects are associated with defective maternal mRNA clearance and disrupted establishment of the H3K4me3 landscape in maturing oocytes. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that TCF3 directs H3K4me3 deposition at target gene promoters through interaction with CXXC finger protein 1 (CXXC1), the core subunit of the SETD1 histone methyltransferase complex. Importantly, this TCF3-CXXC1 interaction depends on their DNA-binding activity, highlighting the specificity of TCF3 in coordinating with CXXC1 to regulate maternal target genes, such as Pabpn1l. Together, our findings uncover a transcription factor-driven mechanism of epigenetic reprogramming that is essential for the maternal-to-zygotic transition.

articles.title: Associations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) with muscle mass and function in women in midlife.
articles.authors: Rokoff LB, Rifas-Shiman SL, Lin PD et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous chemicals that disrupt hormonal and inflammatory pathways and may thereby influence body composition. Reduced muscle mass increases risk of frailty, a condition disproportionately affecting women.
METHODS: In the Project Viva cohort (N = 551), we assessed outcomes in midlife (2017-2024, mean age 50.7 years) including appendicular lean mass index (ALMI), a marker of muscle mass measured via dual X-ray absorptiometry, and plasma concentrations of PFAS at enrollment in pregnancy (1999-2002) and in midlife. We used covariate-adjusted linear regression of individual PFAS and the PFAS burden score and quantile g-computation (qgcomp) mixture models to examine PFAS-ALMI associations, and we explored effect modification by menopausal status, diet, and physical activity at midlife. In secondary analyses, we evaluated associations of midlife PFAS with midlife muscle function measures, and pregnancy PFAS with midlife ALMI.
RESULTS: Mean (standard deviation) ALMI was 6.93 (1.11) kg/m2, and PFAS concentrations compared well with those from contemporaneous National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles. Women with higher concentrations of perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA), perfluoroundecanoic acid (PFUnDA), and the qgcomp PFAS mixture in midlife had lower ALMI (e.g., -0.04 [95% confidence interval = -0.09, -0.0001]; kg/m2 per 0.2 ng/mL increment in PFNA). There was no consistent evidence of effect modification by menopausal status, diet, or physical activity. Associations of midlife PFAS with muscle function (grip strength, physical performance), and pregnancy PFAS with midlife ALMI, were null or positive.
CONCLUSION: Women with higher plasma concentrations of select PFAS had small decrements in ALMI, but muscle function measures were unchanged or slightly better.

articles.title: Anticancer activity of polycarpol from Uvaria siamensis roots against human cervical cancer cells in nude mouse xenograft models.
articles.authors: Pholdaeng K, Lekphrom R, Schevenels FT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cervical cancer treatment with cisplatin or 5-fluorouracil is often hindered by resistance and toxicity. This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms underlying polycarpol's antiproliferative activity in vitro and its potential anticancer effects in vivo.
EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Cell cycle arrest was evaluated by PI staining, and apoptosis was determined by Annexin V-FITC/PI staining, followed by flow cytometric analysis. In vivo antitumor activity was evaluated using TGI% in nude mouse xenograft models. Survival rate, BWC%, and hematoxylin and eosin staining were used to assess toxicity in nude mouse xenograft models.
FINDINGS/RESULTS: Polycarpol (25-50 μM) caused G2/M phase cell cycle arrest only after 24 h of exposure. In addition, polycarpol (25-200 μM) caused concentration- and time-dependent increases in the sub-G1 population, indicating apoptosis. Annexin V-FITC apoptosis assay confirmed that polycarpol (25-200 μM) caused a concentration-dependent increase in apoptotic HeLa cells at 24 h and a time-dependent increase across all tested concentrations at 24-72 h. In nude mouse xenograft models, polycarpol (50-100 mg/kg) significantly suppressed tumor growth, with the highest dose (100 mg/kg) showing the greatest effect compared with the vehicle control group. Polycarpol (50-100 mg/kg) showed no toxicity to the liver or kidneys; however, the 100 mg/kg dose caused spleen toxicity in a mouse model.
CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Polycarpol may inhibit cervical cancer cell growth by inducing G2/M phase cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, suggesting its potential as an anticancer drug.

articles.title: Trends and Inequalities in Demand for Family Planning Satisfied with Modern Methods in Indonesia: An Application of the WHO Health Equity Assessment Toolkit.
articles.authors: Permata YR, Adnani QES, Wibowo AFQ et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Demand for family planning satisfied with modern methods (DFPSm) is a core indicator of equitable reproductive health and Sustainable Development Goal indicator 3.7.1. Although the World Health Organization Health Equity Assessment Toolkit (HEAT) has been used to assess DFPSm inequalities in several settings, multi-round trend analyses in Indonesia remain limited. This study examined trends and inequalities in DFPSm among women in Indonesia between 2003 and 2017.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional study used aggregated estimates from the 2003, 2007, 2012, and 2017 Indonesia Demographic and Health Surveys, accessed through WHO HEAT. DFPSm estimates were assessed across age, economic status, education, place of residence, and subnational region. Inequalities were quantified using difference (D), ratio (R), population attributable risk (PAR), and population attributable fraction (PAF).
RESULTS: National DFPSm remained relatively stable at approximately 77%-79% between 2003 and 2017. Inequalities were dynamic and multidirectional, with subnational region the dominant axis throughout the period. Age inequality narrowed (D: -13.5 to -6.2). Economic inequality reversed direction, from favoring the richest group in 2003 (D=6.3) to favoring the poorest group in 2017 (D=-7.7). Educational inequality also reversed after widening in 2007. Rural-urban inequality widened in favor of rural areas (D: -1.9 to -6.1). Subnational region was the only dimension with consistently non-zero population-level measures, with PAF ranging from 9.6% to 14.3% and PAR from 7.6 to 11.0% points, meaning that closing this gap alone could raise national DFPSm by approximately 7.6-11.0% points (9.6%-14.3% of the national average).
CONCLUSION: Despite stable national estimates, DFPSm inequalities were dynamic and differed in direction across sociodemographic dimensions. Persistent subnational inequality indicates that geographically targeted interventions including province-level resource allocation and stronger JKN integration are needed to improve equitable access to modern family-planning methods in Indonesia.

articles.title: Hepatocellular Injury Markers, but Not Total Bile Acid Severity, are Associated with Fetal Growth Restriction in Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Qi C, Wang F, Mi C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal total bile acids (TBA) guide management of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP), but the relationship of hepatic injury markers with fetal growth restriction (FGR) remains uncertain.
METHODS: We analyzed 110 ICP and 110 non-ICP pregnancies in a retrospective single-center cohort. Clinically recorded FGR was verified against source medical records, including ultrasound reports, but not against standardized fetal-growth percentiles. TBA at ICP diagnosis and the highest TBA during pregnancy were analyzed separately. An exploratory Firth-penalized logistic model assessed alanine aminotransferase (ALT), IVF-coded conception and diagnostic TBA. Two induction-only records were excluded from the main preterm analysis.
RESULTS: Recorded FGR occurred in 16/110 ICP versus 1/110 control pregnancies (14.5% vs 0.9%; Fisher P<0.001). Mean birth weights were 2695 versus 3281 g (P<0.001). Within ICP, median ALT was 195 versus 46 U/L with and without FGR (P=0.016); AST showed a nonsignificant unadjusted difference (P=0.062). Recorded FGR rose across data-derived ALT quartiles (10.0%, 4.0%, 14.3% and 29.6%; ordinal trend P=0.030). In the exploratory Firth model (16 events), ALT had an odds ratio (OR) of 1.046 per 10 U/L (95% CI 1.018-1.079; P=0.001), but exclusion of the highest 5% of ALT values attenuated the association (P=0.079). FGR was 13/81 versus 3/29 across pregnancy-peak TBA strata (P=0.553). Preterm births were 33/80 versus 16/28 (OR 1.899, 95% CI 0.795-4.537; P=0.149); the diagnosis-time TBA preterm trend was also nonsignificant (OR 1.395, 95% CI 0.807-2.411; P=0.233).
CONCLUSION: Hepatocellular injury markers, primarily ALT with AST secondary, showed fragile, hypothesis-generating associations with recorded FGR in this selected cohort, whereas total bile acid severity did not track recorded FGR; absent TBA associations establish neither a null effect nor marker superiority. Larger prospective studies with standardized FGR ascertainment and timed blood tests are required.

articles.title: Association of Preoperative Systemic Inflammation Response Index and Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio with Cytoreduction Outcomes in Ovarian Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Azzahra DM, Suardi D, Nurdiawan W
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Optimal cytoreduction is essential for improving outcomes in ovarian cancer, but reliable preoperative biomarkers for predicting surgical outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of preoperative systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) with cytoreduction outcomes and assess their discriminatory performance in ovarian cancer.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study reviewed medical records of women who underwent debulking surgery at Hasan Sadikin General Teaching Hospital, Bandung, Indonesia, between January 2024 and December 2025. SIRI and NLR were calculated from preoperative complete blood count parameters. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age and histological group, with internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Surgical timing and prior systemic treatment status were not consistently documented, precluding reliable classification by surgical setting.
RESULTS: Among 107 patients, 57 had suboptimal and 50 had optimal cytoreduction. Median SIRI (2.34 vs 1.65, p = 0.047) and NLR (3.60 vs 3.01, p = 0.020) were higher in the suboptimal cytoreduction group. Individual biomarker AUCs were 0.611 (95% CI, 0.504-0.718) for SIRI and 0.631 (95% CI, 0.526-0.735) for NLR. In adjusted models, the estimated odds ratios per unit increase were 1.162 (95% CI, 1.001-1.349, p = 0.049) for SIRI and 1.188 (95% CI, 1.036-1.362, p = 0.014) for NLR. However, the overall likelihood-ratio test was significant only for the NLR model. The optimism-corrected AUCs of the multivariable models were 0.552 for SIRI and 0.587 for NLR.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative SIRI and NLR were associated with cytoreduction outcomes, but both demonstrated limited discriminatory performance. The findings do not establish the superiority or clinical utility of either biomarker. Limited adjustment for clinical confounders and the absence of external validation warrant further prospective multicenter studies before clinical application.

articles.title: Nanomaterials for endometriosis: a multimodal strategy integrating targeted delivery, immunomodulation, and physical ablation.
articles.authors: Inam M, Hayat M, Latif F et al.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory condition for which existing treatments, mainly hormonal therapy and surgical intervention, remain insufficient. These approaches are often limited by high recurrence rates, significant side effects, and an inability to effectively target underlying disease mechanisms. This review outlines emerging mechanism-oriented therapeutic strategies that combine targeted drug delivery, immunomodulation, and physical ablation. Advanced delivery systems, such as Lipid nanoparticle polymeric carriers, and nanomicelles, enable selective accumulation of therapeutic agents at endometriotic lesions, improving efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity. Immunomodulatory strategies pursue to re-establish immune balance by enhancing immune surveillance, driving macrophage polarization toward anti-inflammatory states, and suppressing pro-inflammatory signaling, often through nanocarrier-enabled localized delivery. Furthermore, physical ablation techniques including gold (Au) NPs-mediated photothermal therapy and magnetic hyperthermia offer minimally invasive approaches for precise lesion elimination while preserving adjacent healthy tissues. Collectively, integrating these strategies may advance preclinical efforts to improve disease management, patient stratification, and potentially fertility outcomes, although clinical validation is still required. Despite ongoing challenges in clinical translation, the convergence of nanotechnology, immunology and interventional therapy marks a conceptual shift away from symptom-centered management toward investigational strategies that, pending clinical validation, may confer disease-modifying potential in endometriosis.

articles.title: Gatekeepers of ovarian fate: the molecular landscape of diminished ovarian reserve.
articles.authors: Tang L, Zhou L, Cui G et al.
articles.abstract: Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is a major reproductive disorder characterised by accelerated follicular depletion and impaired ovarian responsiveness, yet its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This review integrates current evidence across the major biological processes that determine ovarian reserve and follicular competence. Primordial follicle activation governed by PI3K-AKT-FOXO3/PTEN-mTOR, Hippo-YAP, KIT/KITL and AMH signaling represents an upstream determinant of follicle-pool consumption, while bidirectional oocyte-granulosa cell communication and the stromal microenvironment sustain follicular development. Genomic instability, defective DNA repair, chromatin remodeling and epigenetic dysregulation further compromise cellular integrity and reproductive longevity. Mitochondrial bioenergetic failure, mtDNA instability, altered mitochondrial dynamics and oxidative stress form a central mechanistic hub linking metabolic dysfunction to follicular damage. Emerging evidence additionally highlights the autophagy-mitophagy-lysosome system, including stress-granule clearance and lysosomal proteostasis, as a context-dependent quality-control network rather than an intrinsically lethal pathway. Downstream cell-fate responses, particularly granulosa-cell apoptosis, cellular senescence and ferroptosis, together with immune-inflammatory and endocrine disturbances, further promote follicular attrition. Importantly, the strength of evidence varies substantially across mechanisms, with direct human DOR data available for only a subset of pathways and many proposed mechanisms remaining dependent on animal or cellular models. Clinically, AMH and antral follicle count remain the principal reserve markers, whereas molecular biomarkers and targeted interventions are largely investigational. By organizing these mechanisms into an integrated framework, this review identifies key evidence gaps and priorities for mechanistically informed biomarker development and therapeutic translation in DOR.

articles.title: Accuracy of the Final Growth Ultrasound in Predicting Birthweight Centile in Women With Class III Obesity: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Mahurkar S, Riaz S, Salovic B et al.
articles.abstract: Introduction This study evaluated agreement between final third-trimester ultrasound estimated fetal weight (EFW) centile and subsequent birthweight centile in singleton pregnancies among women with class III obesity (body mass index (BMI) ≥40 kg/m²). Secondary objectives were to assess antenatal detection of small-for-gestational-age (SGA) and large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infants and associations of maternal BMI and scan-to-delivery interval with centile prediction error. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of singleton pregnancies in women with booking BMI ≥40 kg/m². Agreement between final ultrasound EFW centile and birthweight centile was assessed using centile differences, correlation, SGA/appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA)/LGA categorical agreement, and weighted Cohen's kappa. Secondary analyses assessed diagnostic performance for SGA and LGA and associations of maternal BMI and scan-to-delivery interval with centile error. Results A total of 245 pregnancies had complete data. Mean maternal BMI was 44.8 kg/m², and mean scan-to-delivery interval was 14.4 days. EFW centile was positively correlated with birthweight centile (r = 0.732, p < 0.001). The median absolute centile difference was 13.1 centiles, and the mean signed difference was +3.6 centiles (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.0-6.2). Overall SGA/AGA/LGA category agreement was 82.4% (weighted κ = 0.502). Sensitivity was 26.9% for SGA and 46.9% for LGA, with specificities of 99.5% and 97.2%, respectively. Absolute centile error did not differ significantly across BMI or scan-to-delivery interval groups. Conclusions Final third-trimester ultrasound EFW centile was positively correlated with birthweight centile in women with class III obesity, but clinically important individual discrepancies remained. The final scan had high specificity but low sensitivity for identifying infants subsequently born SGA or LGA. Increasing BMI within the class III obesity range and scan-to-delivery interval were not significantly associated with greater centile error.

articles.title: Identification and Biological Evaluation of Fisetin as a Novel DYRK1B Inhibitor in Ovarian Cancer with Apoptotic and Ferroptotic Effects.
articles.authors: Sam A, Peng CH, Hsu KC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: DYRK1B kinase has emerged as an important regulator of tumor survival, quiescence, and chemotherapy resistance, making it an attractive therapeutic target. Natural compounds are well-known for their anticancer properties and are being studied extensively for their ability to modulate cancer-related signaling pathways.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to screen and identify a natural compound that functions as a DYRK1B inhibitor and evaluate its potential as a therapeutic candidate for ovarian cancer treatment.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We used virtual screening, in-silico molecular docking and in-vitro kinase assay to identify fisetin as a potential DYRK1B inhibitor exhibiting an IC50 of 1.2 μM. Subsequent validation through in-vitro analysis on ovarian cancer cell lines revealed a reduced phosphorylation of DYRK1B downstream targets, characterized by decreased p27 phosphorylation at (Ser 10) and increased cyclin D1 expression, indicating cell cycle re-entry of quiescent cells following effective inhibition of DYRK1B. This inhibition further triggered DNA damage and apoptosis by the accumulation of γ-H2AX, followed by the cleavage of caspase 3 and PARP. To further investigate the mechanistic role of fisetin, RNA-seq was performed, which showed an enrichment of the ferroptosis pathway. The validation of ferroptosis-associated RNA-seq data using qPCR and Western blot analysis confirmed the upregulation of transferrin receptor (TFRC) and downregulation of the iron exporter SLC40A1, leading to iron accumulation. In addition, GPX4, a crucial protein that inhibits ferroptosis by preventing lipid peroxidation, was also found to be decreased. Lipid Peroxidation assay by C11-BODIPY confirmed an increase in lipid ROS, which was effectively reversed by the treatment with ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1.
CONCLUSION: In summary, our results revealed that fisetin is an effective DYRK1B inhibitor that further induces ovarian cancer cell death via apoptosis and also modulates ferroptosis associated pathways, underscoring the therapeutic potential of fisetin in ovarian cancer treatment.

articles.title: Impact of Coexisting Adenomyosis on the Histopathological, Immunohistochemical, and Molecular Features of Endometrial Cancer and on Adjuvant Therapy Allocation: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: D'Asta M, Monaco C, Gulino FA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Adenomyosis is frequently found in hysterectomy specimens of women with endometrial cancer (EC), but its relationship with tumor characteristics remains debated. This study aimed to compare the histopathological, immunohistochemical (IHC) and molecular features of EC, and the allocation of adjuvant therapy, between patients with and without coexisting adenomyosis.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort study of consecutive women who underwent hysterectomy for EC at ARNAS Garibaldi Nesima, Catania, Italy, between January 2023 and September 2024, with complete IHC and molecular profiling. Adenomyosis was defined histopathologically. FIGO 2023 stage, histotype and grade, myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), nodal status, p53 and p16 expression, POLE, mismatch repair (MMR), KRAS and PIK3CA status, and adjuvant therapy were compared using Fisher's exact and chi-square tests, with odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: Of 87 patients, 27 (31.0%) had coexisting adenomyosis. Adenomyosis was associated with FIGO stage I (81.5% vs. 46.7%; OR 5.03, 95% CI 1.68-15.04; p = 0.003), myometrial invasion < 50% (66.7% vs. 35.0%; OR 3.71, 95% CI 1.42-9.70; p = 0.010), absent/focal LVSI (77.8% vs. 50.0%; OR 3.50, 95% CI 1.24-9.89; p = 0.019) and a lower proportion of grade 3 endometrioid tumors (3.7% vs. 26.7%; p = 0.017). No differences were observed in nodal status or in p53, p16, POLE, MMR, KRAS, or PIK3CA status. Fewer patients with adenomyosis received adjuvant therapy (29.6% vs. 58.3%; OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.11-0.80; p = 0.020). Multivariable adjustment was not feasible given the sample size.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, coexisting adenomyosis was associated with earlier-stage, less invasive EC and, consistently, with less frequent allocation to adjuvant therapy. These are univariate associations from a small, single-center retrospective series without survival data; they do not establish an independent or causal effect of adenomyosis and require confirmation in larger prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: Menopausal Hormone Therapy Decreases the Odds of Developing Soft-Tissue Disorders of the Shoulder in Perimenopausal Women.
articles.authors: Shah IK, Shah AK, Burkhart RJ et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether perimenopausal women receiving menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) have decreased odds of developing soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with women without an active MHT prescription, specifically adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, bicipital tendinitis, calcific tendinitis, atraumatic rotator cuff tear/rupture, and shoulder impingement syndrome and to quantify the impact of differing formulations and administration route.
METHODS: The TriNetX US Collaborative Research Network, a deidentified database of over 180 million patients, was queried on June 11, 2026. Women aged 40 to 60 years in a menopausal state were identified by International Classification of Diseases code N95.1 and primary ovarian insufficiency by International Classification of Diseases code E28.3. Patients were grouped by MHT prescription status. Patients were one-to-one propensity-matched on age, race, ethnicity, and metabolic disease status, with standardized mean difference less than 0.1. The odds of developing soft-tissue shoulder disorders were studied, with P values less than .05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: A total of 296,992 patients were included. The index the mean age was 49.1 years, 74.5% to 74.6% were White, 6% were Hispanic/Latino, 9% were African American, and 4.1% were Asian. Women prescribed any form of systemic MHT showed significantly lower odds of developing adhesive capsulitis (odds ratio [OR] 0.875, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.786-0.973; P = .014), bicipital tendinitis (OR 0.775, 95% CI 0.669-0.898; P = .001), calcific tendinitis (OR 0.829, 95% CI 0.706-0.974; P = .023), shoulder impingement syndrome (OR 0.873, 95% CI 0.792-0.962; P = .006), and rotator cuff tear/rupture (OR 0.892, 95% CI 0.804-0.991; P = .032). Topical estrogen specifically was associated with decreased odds of developing adhesive capsulitis, bursitis, bicipital tendinitis, shoulder impingement syndrome, and rotator cuff tear/rupture.
CONCLUSIONS: In peri- and postmenopausal women, MHT use was associated with decreased odds of soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with individuals not using MHT. Topical estrogen was more closely associated with reduced odds of soft-tissue shoulder disorders compared with oral estrogen and oral combined formulations.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, therapeutic retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Dual-action nanotheranostics targeting cell-free DNA rescues aberrant alternative polyadenylation to ameliorate periodontitis.
articles.authors: Gu B, Qu S, Wei Y et al.
articles.abstract: While periodontal pathogens (Porphyromonas gingivalis) are known to severely disrupt macrophage post-transcriptional homeostasis, the precise extracellular instigator remains elusive. Here, through comparative transcriptomic profiling, we identify cell-free DNA (cfDNA) as this fundamental pathogenic trigger. Comprehensive bioinformatic analysis uncovers that cfDNA governs macrophage fate by fundamentally rewiring the global alternative polyadenylation (APA) equilibrium. Specifically, cfDNA forces pro-inflammatory (M1) transcripts into translationally hyperactive short-3'-untranslated region (3'UTR) isoforms, while simultaneously suppressing anti-inflammatory (M2) programs via 3'UTR lengthening. To therapeutically intercept this cfDNA-APA pathogenic axis, we engineered a homologous nanotheranostic platform (DA-APAT). Addressing the unique clinical demands for early periodontitis screening, its polycationic PEI shell enables highly sensitive salivary cfDNA theranostic monitoring. Crucially, this monitoring readout directly calibrates the in situ enzymatic clearance load executed by the internally encapsulated DNase I. Synergized by the intrinsic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capability of the hollow mesoporous cerium oxide core, this monitoring nanoplatform decisively silences intracellular DNA-sensing pathways (cGAS-STING/TLR9), rectifies the disrupted APA, and contributes robust M2 macrophage repolarization. In an orthotopic murine periodontitis model, this nanotherapy effectively halts alveolar bone loss and facilitates profound periodontal regeneration with excellent biocompatibility. This work unveils a cfDNA-driven RNA regulatory paradigm in immune dysregulation and provides a monitoring precision nanotheranostic modality for inflammatory therapy.

articles.title: Assessment of socio-economic and demographic factors on child poverty: a case study of Northern Zone of Tanzania.
articles.authors: Mutalemwa LA, Miraji H
articles.abstract: Despite sustained national and international efforts, child poverty remains a persistent challenge in developing countries specifically Tanzania. Growing up in poverty can affect personal future wellbeing and negatively affect persons' life opportunities. This study examines the socio-economic and demographic determinants of child poverty among children aged 7-17 years in the Northern Zone of Tanzania. Using a cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 504 children selected through a multi-stage sampling procedure in Moshi District Council and Moshi Municipal Council. The multidimensional poverty outcome variable was constructed using average indexing, whereby the three dimensions were aggregated into a continuous composite index for each child. Fixed cut-off thresholds were then applied to this composite index to segment the population into three progressive, rank-ordered categories: Very Poor (high deprivation/low average scores), Poor (moderate average scores), and Not Poor (low deprivation/high average scores). Descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and an ordered logistic regression model were employed to examine variations in child poverty status. The results indicate that age of the child, household size, household structure, and employment status of the household head are significant predictors of child poverty. Older children and those residing in two-parent and non-agricultural households were less likely to experience poverty, while children from large households and households with unemployed heads faced substantially higher risks. The findings underscore the importance of livelihood diversification, household-level economic stability, and family planning interventions in reducing child poverty. The study contributes to the literature by incorporating children's self-reported experiences of deprivation into the analysis of multidimensional child poverty.

articles.title: Determining the Quality of Functional Evidence for Coding Variants in CYP1B1 for Use in Variant Classification.
articles.authors: Burdon KP, Hadler J, Graham P et al.
articles.abstract: Biallelic variants in the CYP1B1 gene are associated with primary congenital glaucoma and some instances of anterior segment dysgenesis and juvenile open-angle glaucoma. Genetic testing is increasingly used in the diagnosis of these conditions and to inform future family planning decisions. Variant-specific functional data play a critical role in variant classification during the interpretation of genetic test results. In this study, the ClinGen Glaucoma Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) evaluated published functional assays assessing CYP1B1 protein stability and enzymatic activity to determine which assays meet the recommended standards for use in variant classification, specifically when applying the PS3 or BS3 criteria from the ACMG/AMP variant interpretation guidelines. Following a comprehensive literature review, the panel identified assays that examined protein abundance and stability, as well as enzymatic activity across a range of substrates. The VCEP determined that BS3 (benign functional evidence) should not be applied to CYP1B1 as variants exhibit substrate-specific effects. After detailed review, the panel determined that two assays had an adequate number of validation controls and could distinguish between pathogenic and benign variants. The first measured 17β-estradiol activity using a commercially available luminescence kit in yeast microsomes. The second assessed benzo[a]pyrene activity via HPLC detection, also in yeast microsomes. A consensus review of additional assays recommends the inclusion of more clinical controls to either establish a significant OddsPath or to better define thresholds for applying pathogenic evidence. Incorporating validated functional data into the curation of CYP1B1 variants will enhance the accuracy of variant classification.

articles.title: Placental programming of metabolic diseases: molecular pathways from maternal pregnancy complications to offspring metabolic risk.
articles.authors: Zhou D
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The placenta is increasingly recognized as a dynamic regulatory organ that translates both maternal and paternal physiological and pathological states into developmental signals into developmental signals shaping offspring health across the lifespan. In the context of maternal metabolic and obstetric complications, placental function extends far beyond the regulation of fetal growth, influencing key aspects of development including endocrine set points, nutrient allocation, inflammatory responses, vascular adaptation, and molecular programming across fetal organs.
RESULTS: This review examines how maternal conditions -such as obesity, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, undernutrition, micronutrient imbalance, and maternal inflammatory stress -induce structural, endocrine, vascular, metabolic, and epigenetic alterations in the placenta. We further explore how these changes disrupt critical molecular pathways, including nutrient sensing and transport, oxidative stress responses, mitochondrial function, angiogenesis and glucocorticoid signaling, immune regulation, and gene expression. A central focus is the convergence of placental mechanisms across diverse maternal disorders, leading to shared offspring phenotypes such as insulin resistance, increased adiposity, dyslipidemia, impaired glucose regulation, altered appetite control, and elevated risk of cardiometabolic disease later in life.
CONCLUSION: Additionally, we address sex-specific placental adaptations, fetal tissue vulnerability, and the translational potential of placental biomarkers and omics-based approaches supported by mechanistic experimental models. By positioning the placenta as the primary biological interface linking maternal complications to offspring susceptibility to endocrine and complex metabolic diseases, this review provides an integrated framework for understanding developmental programming in metabolic health.

articles.title: Sexual and reproductive health of women living on illegal gold mining sites in French Guiana: a multicentric cross-sectional survey.
articles.authors: Douine M, Sanna A, Bardon T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women involved in illegal gold mining in French Guiana face intersecting vulnerabilities related to migration, informality, and precarious living and working conditions, which heighten their exposure to sexual and gender-based violence and undermine sexual and reproductive health. However, quantitative data on these issues in this population remain scarce. This study aimed to document the sexual and reproductive health of these marginalized women.
METHODS: A cross-sectional descriptive survey was conducted among women involved in illegal gold mining. Participants were recruited at logistical bases at the borders with Suriname and Brazil. After providing informed consent, participants were interviewed by trained field investigators using a standardized questionnaire. It collected information on sociodemographic characteristics, exposure to sexual and gender-based violence, engagement in transactional sex, obstetrical history, access to gynecological care, and testing for sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistical methods.
RESULTS: Among the 115 women included, 14.0% reported sexual assault or rape (95% CI: 8.2-21.8), and 19.1% reported intimate partner violence. Regarding transactional sex, 9.5% of women were currently engaged in sex work, and 8.7% reported past involvement, among whom 80.9% reported systematic condom use. Overall, 15.6% of women reported a history of induced abortion (95% CI: 9.5-23.6), and half were performed by a healthcare provider. Most participants (80.0%) reported up-to-date gynecological follow-up (95% CI: 71.5-86.8). Previous HIV testing was relatively common (65.2%), whereas testing for hepatitis B (33.9%), hepatitis C (28.7%), and syphilis (35.6%) were less frequent.
CONCLUSIONS: Women working in mining areas faced high levels of sexual and intimate partner violence, while transactional sex appeared less aligned with commonly held stereotypes. Despite relatively good access to gynecological care, abortion rates remained high and STIs screening coverage could be improved. Promoting systematic screening for gender-based violence within sexual and reproductive health services is essential.Clinical Trial Registration: NCT05540470.

articles.title: PC6 injection enhanced the preventive effect against postoperative nausea of granisetron compared with intravenous injection in gynecological laparoscopic patients: a randomized controlled study.
articles.authors: Song J, Tang J, Gu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate to severe postoperative nausea and vomiting significantly impedes recovery and is inadequately managed by current pharmacotherapy. This study investigates whether granisetron injection at the PC6 acupoint enhances prevention of postoperative moderate to severe postoperative nausea and vomiting compared to intravenous injection.
METHODS: 244 participants undergoing elective gynecologic endoscopic surgery under general anesthesia were randomly assigned to PC6 granisetron group, IV granisetron group, PC6 saline group and control group. All patients receive 5 mg dexamethasone during anesthesia induction. At the end of surgery, 2 mg granisetron was injected at the PC6 acupoint in PC6 granisetron group, 2 mg granisetron was injected intravenously in IV granisetron group, 2 ml saline was injected at the PC6 acupoint in PC6 saline group, no additional measures to prevent postoperative nausea and vomiting in control group.
RESULTS: The incidence of moderate-to-severe postoperative nausea in PC6 granisetron group was significantly lower than that in IV granisetron group, PC6 saline group and control group within 24 h after surgery. (14.8% [9/61] vs. 32.8% [20/61]; RR = 0.45, [95% CI: 0.22, 0.91]; P = 0.02 (14.8% [9/61] vs. 29.5% [18/61]; RR = 0.50 [95% CI: 0.24, 1.02]; P = 0.058, (14.8% [9/61] vs. 43.9% [25/57]; RR = 0.34 [95% CI: 0.17, 0.66]; P < 0.01.) These differences started from 2 h after surgery. There was no adverse events about PC6 acupoint injection was found.
CONCLUSION: Granisetron injection at the PC6 acupoint enhances prevention of moderate-to-severe postoperative nausea within 24 h after surgery in patients undergoing elective gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered at http://www.chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2400085300).

articles.title: Fatty liver index and breast cancer risk: age-stratified findings from a prospective electronic health record-based cohort.
articles.authors: Ma Y, Xie M, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The fatty liver index(FLI) is a validated noninvasive marker derived from routinely collected clinical parameters. It is widely used to assess hepatic steatosis and metabolic dysfunction. These conditions have been linked to cancer development. The association between the FLI and breast cancer risk remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis of a population based cohort with linked electronic health records. We classified participants into low, intermediate, and high FLI groups. We used modified Poisson regression with robust variance to estimate relative risks of incident breast cancer across index categories. We applied Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios while adjusting for demographic, metabolic, lifestyle, and reproductive factors. Lifestyle factors were measured using electronic biosensing devices. We used restricted cubic spline models to evaluate non linear dose response relationships. We also performed analyses stratified by age and menopausal status. Multiple sensitivity analyses assessed the stability of the results.
RESULTS: During follow-up, higher FLI levels were consistently associated with an increased incidence of breast cancer. Compared with women in the low FLI group, those in the intermediate FLI group had an adjusted RR of 1.09 (95% CI, 1.02-1.16) and an HR of 1.08 (95% CI, 1.01-1.15), while those in the high FLI group had an adjusted RR of 1.11 (95% CI, 1.01-1.21) and an HR of 1.11 (95% CI, 1.02-1.21). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated a non-linear association, with a steeper increase in breast cancer risk at higher FLI values. Associations were more pronounced among older and postmenopausal women.
CONCLUSIONS: An elevated FLI derived from routinely available electronic health record data is independently associated with a modest increase in breast cancer risk. This association is more evident among older and postmenopausal women. The FLI may serve as a practical marker for breast cancer risk stratification in population health settings. Further research is needed to clarify underlying mechanisms and to evaluate prevention strategies informed by the FLI.

articles.title: Immediate histopathological outcomes according to Aptima HPV E6/E7 mRNA genotype, age, and menopausal status in women with ASC-H/HSIL cytology.
articles.authors: Liu P, Liu Z, Yang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations of Aptima HPV E6/E7 mRNA genotype, age, and menopausal status with immediate histopathological outcomes in women with ASC-H/HSIL cytology.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 330 women aged 20-84 years with ASC-H/HSIL cytology who underwent Aptima HPV testing, colposcopy-guided biopsy, and histopathological examination. Histopathological outcomes were compared according to hrHPV genotype, age, and menopausal status. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the associations of hrHPV genotype, age, and menopausal status with CIN2 +.
RESULTS: Among women with ASC-H/HSIL cytology, 38.2% had cervical precancerous lesions and 24.5% had malignant lesions. HPV16 and the other 11 hrHPV types were associated with a higher prevalence of CIN2/3, while HPV16-positive women had the highest prevalence of SCC. Both AIS cases occurred in the HPV18/45-positive group, although this subgroup was small. CIN2/3 prevalence decreased with age, whereas SCC prevalence increased. In the multivariable analysis, HPV16, HPV18/45, and the other 11 hrHPV types were independently associated with CIN2+, whereas age and menopausal status were not.
CONCLUSIONS: Histopathological outcomes among women with ASC-H/HSIL cytology differed according to hrHPV genotype. HPV16 positivity was strongly associated with cervical precancerous and malignant lesions. Age and menopausal status showed differences in unadjusted analyses but were not independently associated with CIN2 +.

articles.title: Impact of surgical versus spontaneous fetal reduction on maternal and neonatal outcomes after assisted reproductive technology: a single-center cohort study of 1, 451 singleton live births.
articles.authors: Song J, Zhang T, Wang K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes among pregnancies with surgical reduction, spontaneous reduction, and initial singleton pregnancies following assisted reproductive technology (ART), and to identify independent risk factors for adverse obstetric outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,451 singleton live births after ART at a single center from January 2018 to December 2023. Participants were divided into three groups: surgical reduction (n=128), spontaneous reduction (n=156), and initial singleton control group (n=1,167). Baseline characteristics, maternal complications, and neonatal outcomes were compared. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Univariate analysis revealed significant intergroup differences in the incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preterm birth. The GDM rate was highest in the spontaneous reduction group (26.92%), followed by the surgical reduction group (19.53%) and singleton controls (15.94%, P = 0.003). Preterm birth also differed significantly across groups (19.23% vs 14.06% vs 11.83%, P = 0.024). No group differences were detected for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, placental complications, or congenital birth defects. After adjusting for maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, embryo type, No. of embryos transferred and embryo stage, multivariate logistic regression showed that surgical reduction (OR = 1.22, 95%CI 0.98-1.52, P = 0.069) and spontaneous reduction (OR = 1.39, 95%CI 0.98-1.98, P = 0.067) were not independent risk factors for GDM. Advanced maternal age (OR = 1.12, 95%CI 1.01-1.23, P = 0.028) and elevated pre-pregnancy BMI (OR = 1.11, 95%CI 1.01-1.21, P = 0.030) were the only independent predictors of GDM. For preterm birth, both surgical reduction (OR = 1.35, 95%CI 1.09-1.68, P = 0.007) and spontaneous reduction (OR = 1.72, 95%CI 1.20-2.45, P = 0.003) were independently associated with higher odds of preterm birth. Although the adjusted OR was numerically higher for spontaneous reduction than for surgical reduction, a direct comparison between the two methods showed no statistically significant difference.
CONCLUSION: In ART singleton live births, a history of fetal reduction (surgical or spontaneous) was not independently associated with GDM, but both reduction modalities were independently associated with higher odds of preterm birth.

articles.title: Abortion support in the USA after Dobbs: collaboration, radical acceptance, and the persistent norm of clinician-supervised care.
articles.authors: Kimport K
articles.abstract: In the USA, non-profit abortion support organisations provide resources to ameliorate abortion-related financial, logistical, informational, and psychosocial challenges, but do not provide abortion services. This sector developed under a regulatory environment in which clinic-based abortion was legal and abortion outside of clinician supervision was uncommon. The US Supreme Court's 2022 overturning of constitutional protection of abortion in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization and the rise of medication abortion without clinician supervision have substantially changed the US abortion access landscape. Post-Dobbs, abortion support does not have to be tethered to a clinician-managed provision model, prompting research questions about whether and how the sector's relationship to this model operates post-Dobbs. Drawing on findings from interviews with 32 abortion support organisation staff and volunteers from 17 organisations, this paper finds that abortion support organisations, both individually and as a group, operate in novel, collective ways that do not depend on a clinician-based model of abortion provision, including by prioritising resource sharing on behalf of clients and by incubating and instilling a philosophy of radical non-judgement of clients' circumstances. Despite this, however, their activities remain broadly constructed so as to privilege clinician-supervised abortion, leaving the sector deeply tied to the formal healthcare system.

articles.title: Epidemiology of gestational diabetes mellitus in Latin America and the Caribbean: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Granich-Armenta A, Rangel-Osuna F, Cantoral A et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a major maternal health concern associated with adverse outcomes for mothers and their offspring. In Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), its burden is heightened by socioeconomic inequalities, limited prenatal care, and high obesity rates, while evidence for other determinants remains fragmented and heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to identify, describe, and categorize existing research on the prevalence, incidence, determinants, and risk factors of GDM in LAC. We conducted a scoping review following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Embase, MEDLINE/PubMed, Web of Science, SciELO, and LILACS were searched from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies included observational studies reporting GDM prevalence, incidence, diagnostic criteria, or risk factors in LAC. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Findings were synthesized descriptively. Fifty‑six studies from nine LAC countries were included, mainly from Brazil and Mexico. Studies were predominantly cross-sectional, cohort, and case-control designs conducted in hospital or prenatal care settings. Diagnostic approaches varied, with IADPSG (39.3%), WHO (25.0%), and ADA (16.1%) as the most frequently used criteria. GDM prevalence ranged from 3.0% to 61.0%, and incidence estimates varied substantially. The most frequently reported determinants and risk factors were advanced maternal age, overweight and obesity, family history of diabetes, previous GDM, prior macrosomia, and hypertension. Behavioral and social determinants were less frequently assessed. Variability in GDM prevalence across LAC highlights the need for standardized regional screening and prospective, population-based research. Reducing the regional GDM burden requires integrating clinical interventions targeting modifiable risk factors and improved continuity of care.

articles.title: Estradiol via GPER Maintains Protection Against Arterial Stiffening During Midlife Hypertension in a Mouse Model of Menopause.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.authors: Imulinde Sugi A, Richard C, Blessinger SA et al.
articles.abstract: Endogenous estradiol is associated with cardiovascular protection, but whether menopausal hormone therapy provides protection in aging women with underlying cardiometabolic disease is still not known. Our previous work has shown that the membrane-bound G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) plays a crucial role in estradiol's protective vascular effects by promoting vasodilation, attenuating oxidative stress, and reducing arterial stiffness. In the current study, we designed a midlife mouse model of menopause with induced hypertension to more closely mimic the conditions of postmenopausal women in randomized clinical trials. We hypothesized that estradiol's vascular protection would be reduced in the presence of cardiovascular disease, especially when the disease was established before menopause, and that vascular GPER plays a role in the response. Middle-aged female C57Bl/6J mice, wildtype and global GPER knockout mice, and smooth muscle-specific GPER knockout mice were ovariectomized at 46 weeks of age and infused with Ang II to induce hypertension in combination with either estradiol or vehicle treatment. Estradiol did not significantly impact blood pressure but reduced arterial stiffness independent of the timing of hypertension. Either global or smooth muscle cell GPER deletion abrogated estradiol's protection from arterial stiffening. These studies are important for determining whether cardiovascular status should be a factor when considering menopausal hormone therapy and underscores GPER as an important mediator of estradiol's protective vascular effects, particularly with regards to arterial stiffness.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in the in vitro fertilization laboratory: A scoping review and SWOT-based evaluation of emerging applications.
articles.authors: Javar AA, Miresmaeili SM, Dehghanpour F
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) represents a potentially transformative tool in assisted reproductive technology (ART), particularly in vitro fertilization (IVF), for gamete assessment, embryo selection, non-invasive genetic testing, and laboratory automation. This scoping review synthesized recent evidence on AI applications in IVF laboratories and evaluated their translational maturity using an evidence maturity framework and a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis.
METHODS: This scoping review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from January 2020 to February 2025. Eligible studies evaluated AI, machine learning, or deep learning in laboratory components of ART. Data were charted on AI methods, dataset characteristics, validation strategies, clinical endpoints, and performance metrics.
RESULTS: Ninety-four studies were included. Most applications addressed embryo grading and implantation prediction using convolutional neural networks and were evaluated through internal cross-validation. Reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.75 to 0.92, depending on the endpoint and dataset size. AI applications in sperm analysis and oocyte assessment showed greater reproducibility than manual evaluation. Non-invasive genetic prediction models displayed promising but heterogeneous sensitivity and remained predominantly limited to internal validation. Few studies reported prospective evaluation or external validation using multicenter datasets.
CONCLUSION: AI applications in IVF are expanding, but most remain at early stages of clinical translation. Standardized datasets, external validation, interpretable algorithms, and regulatory oversight remain necessary for safe, equitable clinical integration. AI should function as a decision-support tool that supplements, rather than replaces, embryologists' expertise.

articles.title: Sperm DNA Fragmentation Index, Semen Quality, and Assisted Reproductive Technology Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies.
articles.authors: Bao T, Zhang S, Ou J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI) reflects nuclear DNA damage, but its association with assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes remains controversial.
OBJECTIVES: This meta-analysis evaluated associations between DFI, semen parameters, and ART pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: Four databases were searched through September 2025 for studies comparing reproductive outcomes between low- and high-DFI groups. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) or weighted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup, sensitivity, and publication bias analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: Eighty-seven studies were included. Low DFI was associated with higher clinical pregnancy rate (RR = 1.121, 95% CI:1.068-1.178), live birth rate (RR = 1.136, 95% CI:1.063-1.215), and embryo implantation rate (RR = 1.198, 95% CI:1.085-1.323), and lower miscarriage risk (RR = 0.731, 95% CI:0.652-0.820). No significant association emerged for biochemical pregnancy rate. After publication bias adjustment, clinical pregnancy and live birth associations lost significance, while embryo implantation and miscarriage associations remained robust. Semen parameters favored the low-DFI group.
CONCLUSION: DFI may serve as a supplementary indicator to routine semen analysis, providing information on sperm DNA integrity to complement the assessment of semen quality and ART reproductive outcomes; however, the current evidence primarily reflects population-level associations, and its routine clinical utility remains to be further clarified.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY: Registration number: CRD420261356371.

articles.title: Development and Preliminary Validation of a Male-Oriented Fertility Index in Infertile Men With Varicocele.
articles.authors: Shomarufov A, Bozhedomov V, Martinez M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male infertility is usually assessed using separate parameters, while a simple integrated male-oriented tool is lacking.
OBJECTIVES: To develop a Male Fertility Index (MFI), assess its association with natural conception after varicocelectomy, and perform preliminary external validation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This two-center cohort study included 149 infertile men with clinical varicocele: 99 in the development cohort and 50 in the validation cohort. Preoperative variables were analyzed against natural conception within 12 months. ROC-derived AUCs for total progressively motile sperm count, total motility, male age, and infertility duration were used to construct the MFI.
RESULTS: Natural conception occurred in 30/99 couples (30.3%). MFI values were higher in men whose partners conceived (1.44 [0.87-2.15] vs. 0.64 [0.25-1.31], p < 0.001). Conception was more frequent with MFI > 0.8 than with MFI ≤ 0.8 (44.4% vs. 13.3%, p = 0.0017). In validation, corresponding rates were 40.0% and 14.3%; AUC was 0.795 (95% CI 0.650-0.911).
DISCUSSION: The MFI showed a similar association with natural conception in both cohorts, although validation was limited by sample size and incomplete assessment of female factors.
CONCLUSION: The MFI may summarize male reproductive status in infertile men with clinical varicocele. Its weighting and cut-off require confirmation in larger cohorts, and its usefulness in other infertility settings remains to be established.

articles.title: Is Low Male Fertility Adaptive? Implications for Male Infertility Research.
articles.authors: Amory JK
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fertile human males produce significantly fewer sperm per gram of testes than most other animals, including primates. Human's low sperm output is associated with a lower pregnancy rate per episode of intercourse and a longer time to pregnancy than in most other species. This, coupled with the concealed nature of ovulation in women, means that human couples frequently require numerous acts of intercourse to achieve a pregnancy. The reason for the low fecundability of humans is unknown.
METHODS: I performed a literature review examining the efficiency of spermatogenesis and time to pregnancy in humans to estimate the period of time and average number of episodes of sexual intercourse required for pregnancy. These estimates were corroborated with mathematical models. Hypotheses are suggested to explain the low fecundity of humans.
RESULTS: The average, fertile human couple has sexual intercourse 17-35 times over 2-6 months to conceive, with some fertile couples requiring longer periods of time. These numbers and time period are greater than for most other species. Among the theories that could be advanced to explain the relatively low fecundability of humans compared with other species, two will be explored here: (i) a reduction in the risk of pre-eclampsia with repeated sexual intercourse with a single partner over several months and/or (ii) improved pair-bonding from repeated intercourse over time leading to improved outcomes for children.
CONCLUSIONS: Reduced sperm production in men may be evolutionarily adaptive. Lower fertility and longer time to conception is associated with a reduced risk of pre-eclampsia and improved outcomes for offspring. Greater understanding of the mechanism(s) involved in the relatively low sperm output in men might provide clues to explain some types of male infertility. Additional research into the reduced efficiency of sperm output in men is warranted.

articles.title: DNAH14 Variants Are Associated With Asthenozoospermia and Impaired Mitochondria.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Ma A, Dong F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male infertility affects approximately 15%-20% of couples worldwide, with asthenozoospermia accounting for about 19% of cases. Nevertheless, the genetic basis of many asthenozoospermia cases remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether DNAH14 variants cause asthenozoospermia and to explore the underlying mechanisms related to sperm motility and mitochondrial function.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Whole-exome sequencing was performed on six Chinese individuals with asthenozoospermia. Dnah14-disrupted male mice were generated to assess fertility phenotypes. Comprehensive kinetics analysis, quantitative proteomics, Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis, transmission electron microscopy, and Seahorse assays were utilized to investigate sperm function, protein alterations, and mitochondrial bioenergetics.
RESULTS: Six DNAH14 variants were identified in the affected individuals. Disruption of Dnah14 in male mice led to subfertility characterized by impaired sperm motility and fertilization capacity. Dnah14-deficient spermatozoa exhibited reduced flagellar beat amplitude but increased beat frequency. Quantitative proteomic analysis indicated substantial alterations in sperm protein composition, with GO analysis revealing associations with mitochondrial translation and mitochondrial inner membrane pathways. Transmission electron microscopy showed abnormal mitochondrial morphology, and Seahorse assays detected significantly reduced oxidative phosphorylation and glycolysis.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: DNAH14 is a critical regulator of sperm flagellar beat amplitude and mitochondrial bioenergetics, and variants in DNAH14 might be an important cause of asthenozoospermia.

articles.title: Study of Visceral Adiposity Index and Free Androgen Index in Indian Women With PCOS: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Adhikary P, Pramanik S, Choudhury S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: PCOS is a complex endocrine disorder associated with metabolic and hormonal dysregulation. The visceral adiposity index (VAI) and free androgen index (FAI) have emerged as predictive markers for PCOS. This study aims to evaluate the role of VAI and FAI from the aspect of metabolic and hormonal imbalance in PCOS women from urban and rural areas of India.
STUDY DESIGN AND SUBJECTS: Women within the reproductive age of 18-40 years from both rural and urban areas of India were recruited in the study between November 2018 and July 2022 for this cross-sectional study. 12,100 women were approached to participate in the study, of whom 8993 subjects were enroled. After clinical examination and all investigations according to the protocol, 795 were PCOS cases, while 2475 were non-PCOS cases as per Rotterdam criteria. The PCOS group was segregated according to obesity.
MEASUREMENTS: Hormonal profile and ovarian morphology were evaluated along with anthropometric parameters. VAI, FAI, and Lipid Accumulation Product (LAP) were calculated based on biochemical parameters.
RESULTS: VAI and FAI were significantly elevated in PCOS compared to non-PCOS. VAI, FAI, and LAP were significantly increased in obese PCOS. VAI, independent of BMI, was significantly associated with the Ferriman Gallaway (FG) score, FBG, fasting insulin, and LAP, whereas FAI was associated with BMI and LAP.
CONCLUSION: The study underscores that VAI may serve as the surrogate marker of PCOS, independent of obesity.

articles.title: The Association Between Paternal BMI and Semen Quality in Cohorts Undergoing IUI, IVF and ICSI Fertility Treatments: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Arivalagan A, Mathew G, Gugapriya TS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of obesity and overweight in reproductive age shows an upward trend globally, impacting fertility potential. Against this backdrop, infertility affects an estimated 17.5% of the global population. Intrauterine insemination (IUI) and assisted reproductive technology (ART) are advanced options in a structured fertility care pathway and ensuring semen quality remains a critical step in guiding fertility treatment decisions of these cohorts. Contradictory reports about the impact of paternal body mass index (BMI) on semen quality in these procedures necessitate confirmation of this influence.
OBJECTIVES: To critically analyse the literature and synthesise evidence on the impact of paternal BMI on semen quality among those seeking IUI or ART.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Systematic search in four databases: 'PubMed', 'Web of Science', 'Embase' and 'Scopus' was performed on 28th September 2025. Studies reporting comparison of semen parameters between BMI categories among IUI and ART cohorts were included and interventional studies were excluded. The pooled estimate of mean difference, 95% confidence interval (CI), prediction interval, I2 value, LFK, were estimated and Age and BMI classification sub-group analysis were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using 'JBI Cross-sectional tool'.
RESULTS: Twenty-two studies qualified for meta-analysis out of 34 included studies. The sperm total motility showed a statistically significant pooled mean difference -8.17 between the overweight and normal group with 95% CI = -15.15 to -1.20. Subgroup analysis as per BMI classification showed significant differences in sperm concentration between the overweight and normal groups (test for subgroup differences, p = 0.0206). Prevalence of paternal obese and overweight is 12.15% and 43.37% respectively.
CONCLUSION: Paternal obesity showed no significant association with semen parameters. However, paternal overweight had significant effect on total motility. Further studies on the impact of paternal BMI using novel anthropometric measures, ruling out metabolic and lifestyle factors on semen are warranted.

articles.title: Migration, Duration of Residence and Spontaneous and Iatrogenic Preterm Birth: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: El-Achi V, Dhamrait G, de Vroome M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether the 'healthy migrant' effect applies to PTB and its subtypes, iatrogenic (iPTB) and spontaneous (sPTB) and whether this association differs by length of residence.
DESIGN: Cohort study using electronic health records.
SETTING: New South Wales, Australia.
POPULATION: Singleton births between June 2020 and November 2023.
METHODS: Migrant status was categorised as Australian-born, new migrants (< 5 years residence) or established migrants (≥ 5 years residence). Logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for associations between migrant status and PTB, controlling for demographic, social and service factors.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Odds of PTB, iPTB and sPTB reported as aORs with 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Among 60 806 births, 4076 (6.7%) occurred preterm. Compared to Australian-born women, both new migrants (aOR 0.74, 95% CI 0.65-0.85) and established migrants (aOR 0.84, 95% CI 0.75-0.93) had lower odds of PTB, largely attributable to lower odds of iPTB (new migrants aOR 0.68, 95% CI 0.57-0.83; established migrants aOR 0.80, 95% CI 0.69-0.92). Lower odds of sPTB were observed only among new migrants after full adjustment (aOR 0.80, 95% CI 0.65-0.97). There was evidence that the association between migrancy duration and PTB varied by area-level socioeconomic status, with lower odds of PTB among migrants compared with Australian-born women most apparent in the most disadvantaged areas.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings may be consistent with a 'healthy migrant' effect for PTB, with lower odds observed among both new and established migrants and a larger reduction among new migrants. Lower odds of iPTB were observed among both migrant groups, whereas lower odds of sPTB were observed only among new migrants. Differences in baseline health, obstetric decision-making and health-system engagement may contribute to these observed associations.

articles.title: Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification-Assisted Rapid, Accurate, and Sensitive Photoelectrochemical Biosensing With CdIn2S4/SnS Heterojunction Quenched by Methylene Blue.
articles.authors: Shen Y, Jiang Y, Xi Z et al.
articles.abstract: Rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) is highly significant for early cervical cancer intervention. Herein, a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP)-assisted photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensor is rationally constructed with type II heterojunction CdIn2S4/SnS (CIS/SS) quenched by methylene blue (MB). With the superior charge separation of CIS/SS, an intense initial photocurrent is obtained. After intercalating into double-stranded DNA products of efficient LAMP, residual free MB is rapidly and directly immobilized on CIS/SS via electrostatic and chemical adsorption (15 min), causing remarkable photocurrent quenching. This finding not only circumvents tedious and time-consuming quenching probe modification, but also shortens the mutual distance with significantly improved quenching efficiency over traditional ones. More importantly, mechanistic investigations innovatively reveal that photogenerated electrons preferentially transfer from CIS to MB over SS, triggering MB reduction. Meanwhile, adsorbed MB exerts a light-shielding effect to reduce incident light reaching CIS/SS, collectively causing remarkable photocurrent quenching for enhanced sensitivity with a wide linear range from 1 fM to 1 nM and a detection limit of 0.70 fM. Besides constructing a reliable PEC sensing platform for rapid HPV-16 detection, this work profoundly clarifies the synergistic quenching mechanism of MB, offering theoretical support for various high-performance PEC quenching biosensors.

articles.title: Temporal Analysis of Gestation at Birth in Pregnancies Complicated by Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Wong C, Seeto K, Webb L et al.
articles.abstract: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is associated with maternal morbidity and adverse perinatal outcomes and has historically been managed with planned early birth. This retrospective study examined temporal trends in gestational age at birth among 943 ICP pregnancies at an Australian tertiary hospital between 2014 and 2024, spanning three local policy updates. There was a progressive shift in gestational age distribution from 37 weeks towards later gestations over time. Although the majority of cases were mild or severe disease, 18.1% of births were preterm, of which 84.2% were iatrogenic, suggesting an ongoing opportunity to improve adherence to guideline-recommended timing of birth.

articles.title: Trends and Factors Associated with the Use of Traditional Methods of Family Planning in South and Southeast Asian Countries.
articles.authors: Singh A, Upadhyay AK, Singh A et al.
articles.abstract: Limited research has examined trends and determinants of use of traditional methods of family planning (FP) in South Asia (SA) and Southeast Asia (SEA). This study analyzes data from the Demographic and Health Surveys conducted between 1990 and 2026 across 12 countries in these regions-Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Papua New Guinea, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Timor-Leste. Over the past three decades, the use of traditional FP methods in the pooled sample of 12 countries increased from 4.2 percent in the early 1990s to 8.8 percent in 2022, a pattern also noted in pooled samples of both SA and SEA countries. At the country level, most notable increases in traditional method use occurred in Cambodia, India, Nepal, and Pakistan-three of which are located in SA. Across the pooled sample, as well as region-specific samples, higher use was noted among women having any formal schooling, those whose husbands/partners had five or more years of schooling, and urban residents compared to their respective counterparts. Policies that focus solely on modern methods or on transitioning users from traditional to modern methods may not align with the evolving preferences of women in the region.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography in primary tumor localization and its impact on management in patients with metastases of unknown origin: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Mahmoud HA, Ibrahim EMA, Mekkawy MA et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Metastases of unknown origin (MUO) remain a diagnostic challenge, with identification of the primary tumor closely tied to treatment planning and survival. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) in detecting the primary tumor in MUO patients.
METHOD: This cross-sectional study included 73 patients with MUO who underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT at the Department of Clinical Oncology and Nuclear Medicine, Assiut University Hospitals, between November 2023 and December 2025. PET/CT findings were correlated with histopathological or clinical-radiological follow-up to classify results as true/false positive/negative.
RESULT: Median age was 64 years (37 males, 36 females). PET/CT suggested a primary tumor site in 76.7% (56/73) of patients. PET/CT correctly localized the primary in 50 patients (true positive), was falsely positive in 6, falsely negative in 2, and correctly excluded a detectable primary in 15 (true negative). Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy were 96.15, 71.4, 89.3, 88.2, and ~89%, respectively. Lung was the most common identified primary (20%), followed by lymphoma and ovarian cancer (10% each). PET/CT altered tumor, node, metastasis staging or diagnosis in 10 patients (13.7%): 3 (4.1%) were upstaged to M1b, 2 (2.7%) were downstaged to M0, and 5 (6.8%) were reclassified as nonmalignant based on PET/CT findings.
CONCLUSION: 18F-FDG PET/CT is a high-yield, single-step imaging tool for evaluating MUO, showing a primary tumor detection rate and diagnostic accuracy favorable relative to previously published series, and significantly influencing clinical management strategies. Given the modest sample size and heterogeneous reference standard, these findings should be regarded as preliminary pending validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Changes in central hemodynamics and heart rate variability across active and placebo phases in second-generation oral contraceptive pill users.
articles.authors: Stone JC, Chackal J, Badour MI et al.
articles.abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) is a popular, non-invasive measure of cardiovagal tone. Some research has found that HRV increases from the follicular to the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle, however limited studies investigate the oral contraceptive pill (OCP) cycle. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to determine the influence of second-generation OCP (OCP2) phase on HRV in the laboratory using electrocardiogram, and in a free-living situation using the OURA® smart ring. 19 females using an OCP2 underwent measurements of HRV in the morning during the placebo and active phase of their OCP2 cycle and wore an OURA® smart ring. All HRV parameters, including those in the time and frequency domain, were lower in the active phase (all p <  0.05) however, these differences did not persist after covarying for resting HR (all p > 0.05), except for ECG-derived root mean square of successive differences and the standard deviation of successive differences. Diastolic and mean arterial blood pressure were lower in the active phase compared to the placebo phase (p < 0.05). Therefore, we conclude that HRV is lower in the active phase compared to the placebo phase of the OCP2 cycle, reflecting the integrative regulation of cardiovascular homeostasis.

articles.title: Oliceridine vs Sufentanil Combined With Ondansetron for Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting and QTc Interval in Hysteroscopic Surgery: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.authors: Guo Z, Wu Y, Sang Y
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) is common after hysteroscopic surgery, and opioid use can raise concerns regarding cardiac safety. This prospective study aimed to compare the effects of oliceridine plus ondansetron versus sufentanil plus ondansetron on 24-hour PONV incidence and perioperative changes in the corrected QT interval (QTc) in patients undergoing non-intubated hysteroscopy under general anesthesia. MATERIAL AND METHODS In this randomized, double-blind, controlled study, 62 patients undergoing hysteroscopic surgery under general anesthesia were analyzed. Patients received propofol 2 mg/kg with either oliceridine 0.039 mg/kg plus ondansetron 4 mg (O group) or sufentanil 0.1 μg/kg plus ondansetron 4 mg (S group). The primary endpoint was 24-hour PONV. Secondary endpoints included emergence time, post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) pain scores, and change in QTc from baseline (ΔQTc) measured by 5-lead electrocardiography at predefined time points. RESULTS PONV incidence within 24 h did not differ significantly between groups (0% vs 3.2%, P>0.05). Time to anesthesia emergence was comparable between groups (P=0.960). Numerical rating scale scores at PACU discharge were also comparable (P=0.186). Repeated-measures ANOVA showed a significant time effect for ΔQTc (P=0.001), but no significant group effect (P=0.076) or group×time interaction (P=0.171). CONCLUSIONS Oliceridine plus ondansetron did not significantly reduce 24-hour PONV compared with sufentanil plus ondansetron, and this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of limited statistical power. Perioperative ΔQTc changes were minimal and similar between groups, with no clinically significant QTc prolongation.

articles.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Based Molecular Inference and Cerebrospinal Fluid-Derived Cell-Free DNA Profiling in Central Nervous System Tumors.
articles.authors: Song HH, Kim T, Park H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate molecular characterization is increasingly important in the management of central nervous system (CNS) tumors; however, tissue-based molecular testing remains invasive and constrained by sampling limitations. We investigated the feasibility of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) profiling together with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived phenotype inference as complementary approaches for molecular interpretation in CNS tumors.
METHODS: Targeted next-generation sequencing was performed on tumor tissue genomic DNA and matched CSF cfDNA. A multisequence MRI-based deep learning framework was established to estimate tumor phenotype probabilities from T1-weighted, T2-weighted, fluid-attenuated inversion recovery, and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images. Gene-level molecular tendencies were inferred using a phenotype-conditioned probabilistic framework combining imaging-derived phenotype probabilities with class-associated variant frequencies.
RESULTS: Among 91 collected CSF samples, 10 met the sequencing input criterion for cfDNA analysis. Within this limited subset, CSF-derived cfDNA showed concordance with matched tumor tissue for tier I and II variants, while additional source-specific variants were also observed. MRI-derived phenotype probabilities demonstrated modality-dependent discrimination between glial and nonglial tumors, with the highest performance observed for T2-weighted MRI (area under the curve, 0.833). Phenotype-conditioned molecular inference also showed an overall tendency toward concordance with sequencing profiles, supporting the feasibility of deriving complementary molecular information from imaging-based phenotype estimates.
CONCLUSIONS: MRI-derived phenotype information and limited CSF cfDNA profiling may provide complementary molecular information on CNS tumors. The proposed framework is exploratory, does not constitute direct variant prediction, and is not intended to replace tissue-based molecular testing, particularly in settings where conventional molecular profiling remains constrained.
