articles.title: FADS2-STING Signaling in Sertoli Cells Orchestrates Collagen Deposition and Germ Cell Necroptosis in Idiopathic Non-Obstructive Azoospermia.
articles.authors: Lin J, Ke H, Li X et al.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic non-obstructive azoospermia (iNOA) is a severe form of male infertility with poorly defined etiology. While dysregulated lipid metabolism is a hallmark of spermatogenic failure, the molecular drivers linking lipid remodeling to testicular niche deterioration remain elusive. Here, integrated testicular lipidomics and single-cell transcriptomics reveal a metabolic shift from polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)-enriched toward more saturated phospholipids in iNOA testes, accompanied by a selective downregulation of fatty acid desaturase 2 (FADS2) in Sertoli cells. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that FADS2 deficiency acts as a metabolic trigger for stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling, which orchestrates a transcriptional reprogramming in Sertoli cells. This process promotes aberrant collagen metabolic reprogramming and peritubular fibrosis while concurrently sensitizing germ cells to interferon-mediated necroptosis. Importantly, restoring FADS2-dependent metabolites (γ-linolenic acid and docosahexaenoic acid) attenuates STING activation and collagen deposition and partially restores spermatogenesis in vivo. Collectively, these findings define the pathological relevance of Sertoli cell-associated FADS2-PUFA remodeling and STING-associated inflammatory activation in iNOA, supporting PUFA replenishment as a potential strategy to mitigate structural niche pathology and germ-cell vulnerability.

articles.title: Longitudinal methylation analysis for risk stratification of CIN2 lesions by HPV genotype.
articles.authors: Pikkujämsä H, Aro K, Bergqvist L et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is an urgent need for biomarkers that can distinguish regressive from progressive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) lesions to improve risk stratification in cervical cancer screening programs and avoid overtreatment. We aimed to evaluate the longitudinal performance of the S5 methylation classifier in predicting the clinical trajectory of untreated CIN grade 2 (CIN2) across different HPV genotype groups.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study included 122 women (aged 18-30) with histologically confirmed CIN2 enrolled in an active surveillance trial at Helsinki University Hospital, Finland (ISRCTN91953024). Patients were monitored every 6 months for up to 24 months with cytology, HPV genotyping, and colposcopy. S5 methylation levels (pyrosequencing) were compared between women who regressed to normal histology (n = 89) and those who progressed to CIN3+ (n = 22, including one microinvasive cancer) or had persistent CIN2 (n = 11). Analysis was stratified based on baseline HPV genotypes.
RESULTS: The baseline S5 classifier significantly predicted progression/persistence with an odds ratio (OR) of 1.15 (95%CI 1.05-1.25). When excluding HPV16/18, the S5 classifier demonstrated a similar, borderline predictive association (OR 1.19; 95%CI 1.00-1.41), whereas cytology and HPV genotyping did not. Longitudinal analysis showed that S5 methylation levels in progressors remained elevated throughout the 24-month period, significantly predicting progression/persistence up to 18 months prior to histological diagnosis of progression.
CONCLUSIONS: In this active surveillance cohort, the S5 classifier showed potential as a prognostic triage biomarker for identifying progression in untreated CIN2, including cases with non-HPV16/18 types. Our exploratory findings suggest that elevated methylation levels may precede histological progression by up to 18 months. As HPV16/18 prevalence declines, host-viral methylation panels may offer improved risk stratification compared to standard triage, though larger prospective studies in vaccinated populations are needed to confirm these findings and establish clinical utility.

articles.title: Urinary Incontinence, Obesity, Quality of Life, and Loneliness in Older Adults: An Observational Study.
articles.journal: Journal of wound, ostomy, and continence nursing : official publication of The Wound, Ostomy and Continence Nurses Society
articles.authors: Soyanıt Eraslan Ş, Aydın Avcı İ
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to examine the prevalence of urinary incontinence (UI) in older adults; the association between UI and obesity; and, among participants with UI, the associations between obesity and UI-related quality of life and loneliness.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional, descriptive, correlational observational study.
SUBJECTS AND SETTING: This study was conducted with 301 older adults living in a province in the Northern Black Sea.
METHODS: Self-reported UI was measured by an investigator-developed questionnaire. Urinary incontinence-specific quality of life was measured using the Incontinence Quality of Life Scale, and loneliness was measured using the Loneliness in the Elderly Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, simple logistic regression, and independent samples t -tests.
RESULTS: The prevalence of UI was 47.20% (n = 142), and 34.60% (n = 104) of participants were obese. Participants who were obese had significantly greater odds of having UI than those who were not obese (OR = 2.16, 95% confidence interval: 1.33-3.50, P = .002). Among participants with UI, obesity status was not significantly associated with Incontinence Quality of Life Scale or Loneliness in the Elderly Scale scores.
CONCLUSION: Approximately half of the older adults in this study experienced UI. Obesity increased the likelihood of reporting UI. Among those with UI, there were no significant associations between obesity and UI-related quality of life or loneliness.

articles.title: Growth of uncertainty: how fragmented abortion legislation associates with maternal healthcare engagement and outcomes- an ecological cross-sectional analysis of secondary state-level data.
articles.authors: Clunes M, Huaman GG, Gazo A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, abortion policy in the United States has become increasingly fragmented across states. This study examined whether legislative restrictiveness is associated with differences in maternal and perinatal health at the population level.
METHODS: This ecological cross-sectional study assessed state-level associations between abortion-policy restrictiveness and maternal age distribution, intended pregnancy, prenatal care timing and adequacy, gestational age, birth weight, infant mortality subcategories, insurance coverage, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and obstetric service access across the 50 states and the District of Columbia. Policy data from the Guttmacher Institute and the Center for Reproductive Rights were harmonized into a five-point restrictiveness scale. Health indicators were obtained primarily from March of Dimes PeriStats (2020-2025) and supplemented with national datasets. State values were standardized as Z-scores and analyzed using Spearman rank correlations, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons.
RESULTS: Increasing legislative restrictiveness was statistically associated with lower intended pregnancy prevalence, reduced early prenatal care, higher rates of moderate preterm birth, and increased moderate and very low birth weight. More restrictive states also demonstrated younger maternal age distributions. Observed associations ranged from moderate to strong in magnitude.
CONCLUSIONS: Although causal inference is limited by the ecological cross-sectional design, findings suggest that abortion-policy fragmentation is associated with broader patterns of reproductive health disadvantage in the post-Dobbs United States, with potential implications for maternal and perinatal outcomes.

articles.title: Risk factors for gestational hypertension and preeclampsia: a multivariate logistic regression analysis in a less-developed province in south-central China, 2012-2022.
articles.authors: Han T, Gao J, Wu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore risk factors for gestational hypertension and preeclampsia.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the Maternal Near-Miss Surveillance System in Hunan Province, China, 2012-2022. Multivariate logistic regression analysis (method: Enter, α = 0.05) and odds ratios (ORs) were used to identify risk factors for gestational hypertension and preeclampsia.
RESULTS: This study included a total of 780,359 pregnant women, of whom 15,889 were diagnosed with gestational hypertension and 17,782 with preeclampsia. The prevalence of gestational hypertension and preeclampsia was 2.04% (95%CI: 2.00-2.07) and 2.28% (95%CI: 2.25-2.31), respectively. Results of multivariate logistic regression analysis showed risk factors for gestational hypertension: advanced age (≥ 35) (OR = 2.19, 95%CI: 2.09-2.30), nulliparity (OR = 1.61, 95%CI: 1.54-1.67), cesarean section history (OR = 1.15, 95%CI: 1.09-1.20), multi-fetal pregnancy (OR = 2.32, 95%CI: 2.16-2.49), gestational diabetes (OR = 1.91, 95%CI: 1.84-1.99), and kidney disease (OR = 2.00, 95%CI: 1.62-2.47); Risk factors for preeclampsia: advanced age (≥ 35) (OR = 2.42, 95%CI: 2.32-2.53), primary school and below (OR = 1.24, 95%CI: 1.12-1.37), nulliparity (OR = 1.83, 95%CI: 1.76-1.90), cesarean section history (OR = 1.30, 95%CI: 1.25-1.37), multi-fetal pregnancy (OR = 5.81, 95%CI: 5.52-6.12), gestational diabetes (OR = 1.82, 95%CI: 1.75-1.89), and kidney disease (OR = 4.17, 95%CI: 3.56-4.88).
CONCLUSION: We have identified several risk factors for gestational hypertension and preeclampsia, which may be of value for targeted interventions and further research.

articles.title: Association between early pregnancy vitamin A levels and adverse pregnancy outcomes: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Li Y, Zhang Y, Li R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin A plays a critical role during pregnancy, supporting fetal development, maternal immune function, and antioxidant defense. However, both deficiency and excess of vitamin A have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs).
METHODS: This prospective cohort study investigated the association between serum vitamin A concentrations during early pregnancy and the occurrence of APOs, with a particular focus on potential nonlinear relationships. A total of 379 pregnant women were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were employed to evaluate associations between vitamin A levels and both individual adverse pregnancy outcomes and composite maternal outcomes (miscarriage, gestational diabetes mellitus, and postpartum hemorrhage) and composite fetal outcomes (preterm birth, neonatal asphyxia, macrosomia, and low birth weight), adjusting for key covariates. Nonlinear dose-response patterns were examined using restricted cubic spline analysis.
RESULTS: Among the 379 participants, the median maternal age was 29.0 years and the median body mass index was 22.2 kg/m2. Overall, 131 women (34.6%) experienced at least one APO. Specifically, 62 (16.4%) had gestational diabetes mellitus, 34 (9.0%) experienced postpartum hemorrhage, and 33 (8.7%) had macrosomia. In fully adjusted models, higher maternal vitamin A concentrations were associated with higher odds of composite outcomes, with odds ratios of 1.36 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06, 1.77) for maternal outcomes and 1.45 (95% CI: 1.11, 1.90) for fetal outcomes per standard deviation increase. Significant associations persisted for macrosomia and postpartum hemorrhage after full adjustment, whereas the association with gestational diabetes mellitus was attenuated and no longer statistically significant. The main evidence was derived from composite outcomes, with gestational diabetes mellitus and macrosomia accounting for the largest proportions of the maternal and fetal composite outcomes, respectively. However, none of the individual associations remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. Restricted cubic spline analyses indicated a nonlinear association, with a steeper increase in odds above approximately 1.50 µmol/L (0.43 mg/L). Stratified analyses further indicated that this association was more pronounced among women enrolled at ≥ 10 gestational weeks.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that relatively higher maternal vitamin A…

articles.title: Association of salivary matrix metalloproteinase-8 with metabolic syndrome in women at high GDM risk.
articles.authors: Poulsen H, Meurman JH, Kautiainen H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess associations between metabolic syndrome (MetS), insulin resistance, and periodontal diseases with salivary active matrix metalloproteinase-8 (aMMP-8) in metabolically high-risk women.
METHODS: A total of 112 women with a history of high gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) risk were examined 4-6 years postpartum. MetS was defined using National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III criteria, and insulin resistance was estimated using HOMA-IR. Oral health was assessed through clinical and radiographic examination, registering dental plaque, bleeding on probing, attachment loss, and number of teeth. Salivary levels of active and total matrix metalloproteinase-8 (tMMP-8) were determined using immunofluorescence assay and ELISA, respectively. Tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1 (TIMP-1) levels were also measured. Questionnaires provided information on participants' oral health habits and symptoms.
RESULTS: Periodontitis and a high periodontal inflammatory burden index correlated with the tMMP-8/TIMP-1 ratio. The aMMP-8 levels were associated with visible plaque index, HOMA-IR and MetS. The aMMP-8/TIMP-1 ratio correlated with the visible plaque index and it showed a non-significant trend toward higher levels with MetS. The tMMP-8 were associated with HOMA-IR and MetS.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated tMMP-8 concentrations were associated with periodontal diseases among high-risk women, further supporting the potential role of salivary aMMP-8 as a biomarker of insulin resistance and MetS in this population.

articles.title: Prevalence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes of hepatitis E infection in pregnant women in Sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Cakpo GE, Guingané NA, Ouedraogo S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the well-documented epidemiological importance of the hepatitis E virus (HEV) and its adverse impacts during pregnancy are well recognized in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), the data remain fragmented and heterogeneous. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to estimate the prevalence of HEV among pregnant women, to identify key associated risk factors and to assess its impact on maternal and fetal outcomes.
METHODS: A literature review was conducted using the PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science (WoS) databases. Observational studies on HEV among pregnant women in SSA published between 2015 and 2025 were selected according to predefined search strategies. HEV prevalence was defined by the detection of IgG or IgM antibodies in serum or plasma using ELISA, PCR or rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using a random effects model. A narrative synthesis was performed to identify the factors associated with the risk of HEV infection and its consequences during pregnancy. All data were analysed using Stata version 17 software. This review was registered with PROSPERO, CRD420251065899.
RESULTS: A total of 30 studies from SSA were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. The pooled prevalence was 17% (95% CI 13-21) and 4% (95% CI 3-5) for IgG and IgM, respectively. Sub-regional analysis of IgG anti-HEV prevalence showed significant heterogeneity among pregnant women in SSA. Sociodemographic, economic, behavioural, and environmental factors were associated with having a HEV infection. Regarding maternal outcomes, both mild symptomatic cases and severe forms with mortality rates of up to 20% were observed. Neonatal outcomes included jaundice, hypotrophy, and fetal mortality. The reported risk of miscarriage and prematurity varied between studies, ranging from 0% to 8.4%.
CONCLUSIONS: This research showed that HEV infection in pregnant women remains a public health concern in SSA, with significant maternal and neonatal consequences.

articles.title: Hyperglycemia-induced placental inflammation involves differential activation of RAGE-associated PI3K/MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathways.
articles.authors: Vargas-Alcantar D, Martínez-Garfias K, Hernández-Bones K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exposure to elevated glucose levels during intrauterine life is detrimental to both the mother and fetus. As a glucose-sensitive organ, the placenta responds to hyperglycemia by mounting a pro-inflammatory response characterized by increased production of inflammatory mediators that disrupt the immune privilege of the maternal-fetal interface. Although hyperglycemia promotes inflammation in human placental tissue, the molecular mechanisms through which HMGB1 release and advanced glycation end products (AGEs) accumulation converge on RAGE-associated signaling pathways to sustain this response remain poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the molecular mechanisms by which hyperglycemia activates HMGB1/AGEs-dependent signaling networks leading to inflammatory responses in human placental villi.
METHODS: Human term placental villous explants were exposed to normal or high glucose concentrations for 1-9 h or 48 h. For pathway inhibition experiments, explants were treated with selective inhibitors during high-glucose exposure. Inflammatory mediators, extracellular HMGB1, glyoxal-derived AGEs, TLR4 and RAGE expression, and activation of Akt1, ERK1/2, and NF-κB were evaluated.
RESULTS: High-glucose exposure elicited a pro-inflammatory phenotype characterized by increased extracellular HMGB1 release, enhanced glyoxal-derived AGEs formation, and elevated TLR4 expression, supporting the involvement of HMGB1/AGE-RAGE signaling. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia was associated with activation of the PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK1/2 pathways, promoting NF-κB activation, suggesting the participation of both RAGE-dependent and RAGE-independent mechanisms, leading to increased secretion of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. Pharmacological inhibition experiments suggested the existence of putative interconnected positive feedback loops linking AGE accumulation, HMGB1 release, RAGE activation, and downstream inflammatory signaling, supporting the establishment of a self-sustaining metainflammatory network in placental villi.
CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings provide insight into the mechanisms by which sustained maternal hyperglycemia reshapes placental immune signaling and promotes a chronic metainflammatory state that may compromise placental function. Our results support a mechanistic model in which HMGB1/AGE-RAGE/TLR4 signaling contributes to placental dysfunction during gestational hyperglycemia.

articles.title: Paralleled Polymer Degradation and Oxybutynin Release from Short-Chain Polyesters for In-Situ Forming Intravesical Implant Design.
articles.authors: Hartig MU, Appelhaus J, Crombach LF et al.
articles.abstract: In situ forming implants (ISFI) for intravesical drug delivery represent a promising alternative to current treatment options for neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO). Previous formulations demonstrated opportunities for further optimization regarding the temporal alignment between drug release and polymer degradation, which may influence depot persistence during repeated administration. Therefore, different polyester grades with various molecular weights and solvent systems were investigated in order to parallel drug release and polymer degradation. Reducing the molecular weight from 38 to 2 kDa increased degradation threefold (from 8 to 25% within 72 h). Nevertheless, ISFI with PLGA 2 k were characterized by a high initial drug release of 20% after 24 h. By an increase of application frequency from once every nine days to every third day, the initial drug release was reduced to 10% within the first three days paralleling drug release and polymer degradation (10% after 72 h), resulting in a nearly linear relationship between these processes. These findings demonstrate that dose-splitting can effectively modulate release kinetics, supporting improved temporal alignment of drug release and polymer degradation without substantially increasing burst release. In addition, with a low molecular weight polyester grade, depot persistence may be further reduced under repeated administration conditions. Still, an ISFI administered every three days can distinctly improve the quality of life for NDO patients currently administering up to five doses daily.

articles.title: HDFF-Net: A Hybrid Dual-Feature Fusion Network with Bidirectional Gated Fusion for Colposcopic Transformation Zone Classification, Evaluated under a Leakage-Audited Cluster-Level Protocol.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.authors: Shubhaker B, Raghavendra BS
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer screening through colposcopy depends critically on accurate classification of the transformation zone (TZ) according to the 2011 IFCPC nomenclature, as TZ type directly governs treatment eligibility (ablative versus excisional). Inter-rater agreement among trained colposcopists for TZ-type assignment is only κ ≈ 0.42-0.60, well below the κ ≥ 0.80 threshold considered reliable for clinical decision-making. Existing automated methods rely either on handcrafted feature pipelines or deep transfer learning in isolation, and published performance figures on public colposcopy atlases have not been systematically audited for evaluation integrity. This paper reports a leakage-audited, cluster-level evaluation of a hybrid handcrafted-plus-deep fusion design on a public colposcopy atlas and asks whether the fusion adds value over simpler baselines when only a few hundred images are available. We evaluate HDFF-Net (Hybrid Dual-Feature Fusion Network), a dual-stream design that combines a 10,322-dimensional multi-scale handcrafted feature branch (MS-GLCM, MS-LBP, MS-HOG), projected to 512 dimensions and recalibrated by a 1D Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) module, with an EfficientNet branch augmented by CBAM. The two streams are joined by a bidirectional gated fusion (BGF) module that uses feature-wise sigmoid gates; it is not an attention mechanism (no query-key interaction, softmax, attention heads or spatial tokens). Models are trained on a stratified 70/15/15 split made at the level of 194 unique image clusters (seed = 42), obtained by perceptual-hash deduplication (pHash, Hamming distance <= 8) of 366 IARC Cervical Screening Atlas files. Alias files of one cluster are the same physical image, so the primary analysis uses one observation per cluster; all intervals and paired tests are computed at that level and file-level figures are given only as a sensitivity analysis. Ablations compare handcrafted-only, CNN-only, concatenation and gated-fusion variants, and recent CNN and hybrid-feature baselines were retrained on the same locked split. Deduplication reduced 366 files to 194 unique image clusters (120 TZ1/34 TZ2/40 TZ3) after removal of seven label-contradictory clusters. The held-out test partition contains 30 independent clusters (53 files). On these 30 clusters, HDFF-Net (B0) reached accuracy 0.467 (0.283-0.657), balanced accuracy 0.420 (0.204-0.653) and macro-F1 0.407 (0.217-0.585). Ten baselines were compared with it on the same clusters.…

articles.title: The relationship between emotion dysregulation and subjective and objective sleep difficulties from late pregnancy to early postpartum.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.authors: Peak J, Slyepchenko A, Minuzzi L et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The perinatal period is marked by rapid changes in one's life that can increase the risk of sleep difficulties and emotion dysregulation (ED). While the relationship between ED and sleep is well-documented, it remains understudied in the perinatal period despite the resulting adverse maternal-infant outcomes. This study aimed to address gaps in our understanding by (1) examining the relationship between ED and sleep longitudinally from late pregnancy to early postpartum and by (2) using both subjective and objective measures of sleep.
METHODS: Fifty-eight participants were assessed during their third trimester of pregnancy and at 1-3 and 6-12 weeks postpartum. ED was assessed using the Difficulties In Emotion Regulation Scale at visit 1. Participants wore actigraphs for 2-week periods to obtain objective sleep data at each timepoint, including total sleep time, sleep efficiency (SE), wake after sleep onset (WASO), sleep onset latency, and awakenings. Subjective sleep quality was examined using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index.
RESULTS: Subjective sleep quality differed significantly between participants who had high ED compared to those with low ED at all visits. Further, the high ED group experienced worse sleep quality. Significant differences in this direction were also found for SE and WASO during the third trimester of pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: This study provides support for the differential influence of ED on subjective and objective sleep across the third trimester of pregnancy to 1-3 and 6-12 weeks postpartum. With its use of a longitudinal design and subjective and objective sleep measures, this study provides novel insights into the ED-sleep relationship perinatally.
CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: The relationship between emotion dysregulation (ED) and sleep is understudied in the perinatal period, despite the resulting adverse maternal-infant outcomes. To address this gap, this study examined the relationship between ED and sleep longitudinally from late pregnancy to early postpartum using both subjective and objective sleep measures.
STUDY IMPACT: This study provides support for the differential influence of ED on subjective and objective sleep across the third trimester of pregnancy to 1-3 and 6-12 weeks postpartum. The use of a longitudinal design and inclusion of both objective and subjective sleep measures provides novel insights into the ED - sleep relationship perinatally.

articles.title: Expressive priority and somatic testimonial injustice: a framework for women's embodied distress.
articles.authors: Roul SK
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Research on women's mental health increasingly frames female distress as embodied, presenting this as a move beyond mind-body dualism. This paper asks whether the move is complete.
METHODS: Conceptual analysis of the literature on epistemic injustice, somatisation, functional disorders, predictive processing, and gender bias in diagnosis.
RESULTS: A residual assumption, termed here expressive priority, treats bodily distress as the expression of a prior psychological state that holds explanatory priority over the patient's own account. It concerns explanatory practice, not metaphysics, and is compatible with physicalism. Building on Fricker, Carel and Kidd, Dotson, and Pohlhaus, the paper develops somatic testimonial injustice: a sequence in which a bodily account is deflated in credibility, translated into a psychological idiom presented as the patient's own, and redirected so that it counts as evidence about her psychology rather than her body. The mechanism is general, but its burden is gendered, as endometriosis, systemic autoimmune disease, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, and polycystic ovary syndrome illustrate.
CONCLUSIONS: Taking predictive-processing accounts of miscalibrated symptom report, the paper argues for the parity of bodily testimony as evidence, not its primacy, and states three discriminating, falsifiable predictions. Its empirical anchors are illustrative, and the framework awaits testing.

articles.title: Association between birth order and birthweight percentile: population-level and within-mother analyses in a large birth cohort.
articles.authors: Kolp-Asis S, Shtossel O, Yozevitch R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parity is associated with differences in birthweight, but the magnitude and consistency of this association when expressed as birthweight percentiles remain incompletely characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between birth order and birthweight percentile at both the population-level and within mothers across successive pregnancies.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 130,718 singleton live births from 55,057 women delivering at a single tertiary medical center between 2012 and 2024. Birthweight percentiles were calculated using a national sex-specific reference. Linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for mother were used to evaluate the association between birth order and birthweight percentile, adjusting for maternal age, infant sex, and maternal diabetes. Complementary longitudinal within-mother analyses evaluated changes in birthweight percentile across successive pregnancies.
RESULTS: Higher birth order was associated with higher birthweight percentile (β ≈ 0.074 SD per birth order increment, p < 0.001), corresponding to an average increase of approximately 3 percentile points per birth. The largest increase occurred between the first and second births, followed by progressively smaller but persistent increases with advancing birth order. This pattern was consistent across subgroup analyses and complementary within-mother analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher birth order was consistently associated with higher birthweight percentile both across the population and within mothers. The association followed a distinct nonlinear pattern, with the largest increase occurring between the first and second pregnancies and progressively smaller but persistent increases thereafter. These findings provide a more nuanced understanding of parity-associated variation in fetal growth across successive pregnancies.

articles.title: Psychosocial factors associated with fertility-related quality of life among Iranian women with infertility: protocol for a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Tavakoli F, Hasanpoor-Azghady SB, Sharif-Nia H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Infertility is a global public health concern and a multidimensional reproductive health issue with significant psychosocial implications, particularly in sociocultural environments where childbearing holds high social value. While its general impacts are documented, the specific structural pathways through which social vulnerabilities like stigma interact with personal resources (self-efficacy and self-esteem) remain unclear. This study aims to estimate, using a pre-specified path model, the adjusted direct, indirect (through depressive symptoms) and total associations of infertility stigma, self-efficacy and self-esteem with fertility-related quality of life among Iranian women with infertility and to assess the sensitivity of these estimates to unmeasured confounding.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This cross-sectional study will be conducted from November 2026 to March 2027 in two high-referral infertility centres in Tehran province, Iran. A consecutive sample of 220 eligible women will complete the Infertility Stigma Scale, Infertility Self-Efficacy Scale, Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, Beck Depression Inventory-II and the Fertility Quality of Life tool (FertiQoL, Core and Treatment modules, with the total score as the primary outcome). Path analysis (a structural equation model of observed scale scores; using AMOS software), adjusted for measured covariates, will be used. Because the primary model is saturated, fit indices (χ²/df, root mean square error of approximation, standardised root mean square residual, Comparative Fit Index and Tucker-Lewis Index) will be assessed for a restricted model without the direct paths to fertility-related quality of life. Indirect effects will be estimated with 5000 bootstrap resamples and 95% CIs. A pre-specified sensitivity analysis will assess the impact of unmeasured confounding.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Iran University of Medical Sciences (IR.IUMS.REC.1404.370). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences.

articles.title: Diabetes Type and Perinatal Adverse Outcomes Among Women in Pregnancy and Neonates in Japan: A Cohort Study Using a Large-Scale Database.
articles.authors: Okada A, Kawaguchi T, Inoue R et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes across gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes, overt diabetes in pregnancy and normoglycaemia in Japan.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the JMDC claims database, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of mother-neonate pairs from 2015 to 2024. Maternal glycaemic status was classified as normoglycaemia, gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes or overt diabetes in pregnancy using diagnoses, prescriptions, procedures and timing. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia and severe neonatal complications (neonatal death, foetal distress or neonatal intensive care unit admission).
RESULTS: Among 244 402 neonates from 205 594 mothers, gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes and overt diabetes were identified in 20 116 (8.2%), 3287 (1.3%) and 901 (0.4%), respectively. Compared with normoglycaemia, gestational diabetes, preexisting diabetes and overt diabetes were associated with higher risks of maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, with aORs of 1.34 (95% CI: 1.21-1.48), 1.96 (1.64-2.33) and 1.89 (1.35-2.64), respectively. Corresponding aORs for severe neonatal complications were 1.45 (1.38-1.52), 1.95 (1.77-2.15) and 2.55 (2.14-3.03), respectively. Compared directly with preexisting diabetes, overt diabetes was associated with higher odds of severe neonatal complications (aOR: 1.31; 95% CI: 1.07-1.59), with no statistically significant difference detected in maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia (aOR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.67-1.40).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal and neonatal risks varied by hyperglycaemic status. Overt diabetes was associated with a higher risk of severe neonatal complications than preexisting diabetes, with no statistically significant difference detected in maternal pre-eclampsia/eclampsia. Further validation using longitudinal data around pregnancy is warranted.

articles.title: Postoperative Bladder Rehabilitation After Radical Hysterectomy for Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Kuroda K, Ito K
articles.abstract:
AIM: To systematically review the evidence on postoperative bladder management and rehabilitation strategies for women undergoing radical hysterectomy for cervical cancer.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE. Studies evaluating postoperative bladder management or rehabilitation interventions in women undergoing radical hysterectomy for cervical cancer were included. Eligible interventions comprised catheter management, trial-of-void (TOV) strategies, pelvic floor exercises, integrated care, and electrical stimulation. Study characteristics, urinary outcomes, quality of life (QoL), and risk of bias were assessed descriptively.
RESULTS: Eight studies were included. Interventions included intermittent catheterization continuity care, TOV strategies, enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS)-based pelvic floor exercises, integrated nursing care, early pelvic floor muscle exercises, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), and transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS). Intermittent catheterization continuity care was associated with faster bladder function recovery and improved QoL. Pelvic floor exercises and integrated care were associated with improvements in urinary symptoms, pelvic floor muscle strength, or QoL. TENS was associated with a lower urinary retention rate in a retrospective cohort study. In a randomized controlled trial, TEAS improved several secondary bladder-emptying outcomes and QoL, but did not significantly reduce the primary outcome of urinary retention. Heterogeneity in study designs, interventions, and outcome definitions limited comparisons across studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Structured postoperative bladder management and rehabilitation may improve bladder recovery and patient-reported outcomes after radical hysterectomy for cervical cancer. However, the certainty of evidence remains limited. Further well-designed prospective studies and randomized controlled trials using standardized outcome measures are needed to determine optimal rehabilitation strategies.

articles.title: Birthweight and Glucose Tolerance Status Are Associated With Organ Sizes in Older Adults.
articles.authors: Linde V, Pham MHC, Hansen AL et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Low birthweight is a risk factor of Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Organ size is related to organ function and disease, but few studies have examined cardiometabolic organ sizes in relation to birthweight and glucose tolerance. This longitudinal follow-up study investigated whether organ size varied by birthweight and/or glycaemic status in an elderly population.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: 1212 participants aged 53-83 years from the Danish Inter99 20-year follow-up study, with original midwife birthweight records, underwent computed tomography imaging. Linear regression was used to examine associations between birthweight and organ sizes, and differences in organ sizes across normoglycaemic, prediabetes and diabetes groups.
RESULTS: After adjustment for sex, age, birth year, preterm birth and body surface area, a 1 kg lower birthweight was associated with a 2.0% (95% CI: 0.1%, 3.9%) lower kidney volume and a 3.8% (95% CI: 1.2%, 6.5%) lower lung volume, and with a 3.9% (95% CI: 0.3%, 7.5%) larger adrenal gland volume. Further adjustment for subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue attenuated the lung association. Compared with normoglycaemic participants, individuals with prediabetes and/or diabetes showed larger liver, kidney and adrenal gland volumes, whereas pancreas volume was smaller, adjusted for birthweight and body size.
CONCLUSION: Lower birthweight was associated with smaller kidneys, and to some extent lungs, and with larger adrenal glands, whereas diabetes and prediabetes were associated with larger kidney, liver and adrenal glands, and with lower pancreas volumes. Further studies are needed to understand the clinical and/or physiological implications of these findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05166447.

articles.title: KLHDC3-mediated degradation of transcriptional repressor SCAND1 is regulated by Hsp90.
articles.authors: Soltys AL, Kabir F, Woo CM
articles.abstract: The ubiquitin-proteasome system and the stress response pathway are highly integrated in order to maintain proteostasis. C-degron E3 ligase substrate adapters recognize certain proteotoxic substrates, although their integration with the cellular stress response has not been previously investigated. Here, we evaluate the C-degron E3 ligases KLHDC3 and APPBP2 for their substrates and pathway dependencies with chemical inhibitors. KLHDC3 and APPBP2 downregulated SCAN-domain containing transcriptional regulators SCAND1 and ZSCAN18, respectively. A bioactive compound screen in reporter cell lines revealed inhibition of KLHDC3 by a panel of Hsp90 inhibitors. KLHDC3 post-translationally downregulated SCAND1 across multiple cell lines, leading to changes in cell viability in endometrial cancer cell lines. SCAND1 overexpression in MFE-296 cells repressed gene targets that drive proliferation and immune responses. This work reveals a mechanism where constitutive post-translational suppression of a transcription factor is released on Hsp90 inhibition, establishing C-degron E3 ligases and their substrates as mediators of the cellular stress response and expanding the known functions and proteostasis implications of a C-degron E3 ligase.

articles.title: Preventing Maternal Deaths: Lessons Learned From the UK Confidential Enquiries Into Maternal Deaths and Morbidity.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Felker A, Knight M
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: For more than seven decades, the United Kingdom (UK) Confidential Enquiries into Maternal Deaths (CEMD) have reviewed maternal deaths to identify lessons and improve care. This article summarizes key lessons from the enquiries, highlighting recent findings and enduring recommendations.
METHODS: The MBRRACE-UK collaboration, which has delivered the CEMD program since 2012, collects information on all maternal deaths during pregnancy or up to 1 year after pregnancy in the UK and Ireland. Demographic and clinical surveillance data are collected to monitor trends, while medical records, postmortem reports, and relevant local investigations are anonymized and reviewed by multidisciplinary experts to identify key themes and opportunities for improvement.
RESULTS: Recent MBRRACE-UK findings show an increasing trend in UK maternal mortality rates, which is predominantly driven by direct causes of deaths alongside persistent inequalities among women living in deprived areas and from some ethnic minority backgrounds. Confidential enquiries consistently emphasize the importance of individualized care, which considers women's circumstances including medical comorbidities, mental health, and social complexities. Improving outcomes requires joined-up, multidisciplinary care extending beyond maternity services. Care before and after pregnancy is equally important to optimize outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite consistent and recurring messages across confidential enquiries, maternal mortality in the UK is not declining. Sustained action is needed to ensure that lessons from maternal deaths are translated into meaningful and lasting changes in clinical practice, service delivery, and policy to reduce preventable deaths and improve maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome in Adulthood: Diagnostic Recognition, Clinical Spectrum, and Long-Term Follow-Up.
articles.journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
articles.authors: Elüstü Belten Z, Atasoy B, Şahin Kimyon Ö et al.
articles.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome is usually diagnosed during childhood, and data on outcomes in adulthood are limited. This retrospective, single-center study evaluated the diagnostic history, endocrine phenotype, and clinical outcomes of 14 adults with radiologically confirmed pituitary stalk interruption syndrome. The cohort comprised eight men and six women, with a mean age of 28.8±6.4 years and a mean documented follow-up at our center of 5.6±3.2 years. Hypopituitarism was diagnosed during childhood in 12 patients and during adulthood in 2 patients. Thirteen patients had deficiencies of all four anterior pituitary hormone axes, whereas one patient had growth hormone and gonadotropic deficiencies with preserved corticotropic and thyrotropic functions. In six patients diagnosed during childhood, pituitary stalk interruption syndrome was recognized only after later reassessment of pituitary imaging. Eleven patients received growth hormone treatment during childhood, and 13 of 14 patients reached their calculated target height. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia were each present in 10 patients. Four patients had bone mineral density below the expected range for age. One female patient achieved a live birth following in vitro fertilization. In this real-world cohort, the skeletal and metabolic findings observed despite generally favorable growth outcomes support the need for lifelong endocrine follow-up.

articles.title: Barriers to treatment for patients diagnosed with cervical cancer: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Cortez CA, Taffe BD, Ellis C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Previous reviews have described disparities in the treatment of patients diagnosed with gynecologic cancers; however, these reviews are not systematic in nature, and none have focused specifically on individuals diagnosed with cervical cancer, who disproportionately represent marginalized populations in the US. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on treatment-related outcomes and multilevel determinants of care among US patients with cervical cancer.
METHODS: The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023413020). We searched PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL for studies published through May 2026. Eligible studies examined treatment related outcomes among patients diagnosed with cervical cancer in the US. We identified 25 articles that met our inclusion criteria. Treatment-related outcomes were categorized and determinants (i.e., explanatory variables) were mapped on to the socioecological model.
RESULTS: Across 25 studies, 26 treatment-related outcomes were identified. Receipt of surgery, chemotherapy, and brachytherapy were the most frequently assessed outcomes. Key patient-level determinants included race/ethnicity, age, comorbidities, insurance, rurality, and distance to care. Minoritized populations, particularly Black, Hispanic, Native American, Pacific Islander, often experienced worse treatment outcomes. Older age was also a frequent barrier to treatment. Distance to care was inconsistently associated with treatment outcomes. Clinic-level determinants, such as care outside of large-volume facilities and academic medical centers, and contextual determinants, such as residing in a county with lower levels of income and education, were associated with worse treatment outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Cervical cancer treatment in the United States is driven by multilevel determinants at the patient-, clinic-, and community-level. Addressing barriers to treatment requires attention to the broader structural and modifiable factors that hinder treatment for marginalized cervical cancer patients in vulnerable communities. Future studies should more rigorously and thoughtfully measure community-level and individual-level variables.

articles.title: Association of menopausal symptom burden with performance and self-monitoring across cognitive domains.
articles.authors: Naysmith LF, Bălăeţ M, Trender W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perimenopause is a dynamic neuroendocrine transition with increased risk of cognitive, psychological and physical symptoms. How population variability in symptom burden relates to different aspects of cognitive functioning remains unclear.
METHODS: We measured menopausal symptom burden, task-specific cognitive performance, task confidence and metacognitive bias using the online platform "Cognitron" with 1614 participants aged 45-60 from the Great British Intelligence Test. Symptom burden was standardised (mean = 0, SD = 1), allowing coefficients to be interpreted in standard deviation (SD) units.
RESULTS: Exploratory analyses showed early and late perimenopause to be a significant predictor of higher menopausal symptom burden (respectively 0.259 SD, 95% CI 0.116, 0.401, and 0.284 SD, CI 95% 0.115, 0.452, both p < 0.001). Global cognitive performance was significantly lower in individuals with higher symptom burden (-0.092 SD, 95% CI -0.133, -0.050, pFDR < 0.001, ηₚ2 = 0.0117). Higher symptom burden also predicted lower task confidence (-0.225 SD, 95% CI -0.272, -0.178, pFDR < 0.001, ηₚ2 = 0.0527) and negative bias (-0.135 SD, 95% CI -0.181, -0.089, pFDR < 0.001, ηₚ2 = 0.0206). Exploratory analyses showed that symptom burden significantly predicted poorer performance on tasks measuring executive function (Stroop interference), working memory (digit span), spatial reasoning (block design), and verbal analogical reasoning.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight menopausal symptom burden as a significant predictor of cognitive and metacognitive differences and longitudinal research is needed to identify those at greatest risk of cognitive decline.

articles.title: Feasibility of transvaginal ultrasound with endorectal micro-enema for the detection of rectosigmoid anastomotic leakage after cytoreductive surgery for ovarian cancer: preliminary experience from an ambispective single-center study.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.authors: Mascilini F, Ciancia M, Moro F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of transvaginal ultrasound with endorectal micro-enema for post-operative assessment of rectosigmoid anastomosis leakage in patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery for ovarian cancer.
METHODS: This ambispective single-center study included patients with ovarian cancer who underwent primary or interval debulking surgery, or surgery for recurrent disease, with bowel resection and rectosigmoid anastomosis. Transvaginal ultrasound-guided assessment with endorectal saline instillation was performed between postoperative day 5 and 7. Contrast-enhanced CT was used as the reference standard in cases suspicious for anastomotic leakage.
RESULTS: Between January 2024 and December 2025, 67 patients were assessed for participation in the study. The procedure was attempted in 49 patients and successfully completed in 42 (85.7%). Procedural difficulty was rated as easy in 32/42 (76.2%) cases, mildly difficult in 8/42 (19.0%) and moderately difficult in 2/42 (4.8%). Image quality was rated as good or excellent in 34/42 (81.0%) examinations and adequate in 8/42 (19.0%). The pain intensity during the procedure was rated as mild in 35/42 (83.3%) patients and moderate in 7/42 (16.7%), no patient reported severe pain. No procedure-related complications occurred. Ultrasound findings were negative in 40/42 cases, indeterminate in 1, and positive in 1 case of anastomotic leakage, which was confirmed by CT and managed surgically.
CONCLUSION: Transvaginal ultrasound with endorectal micro-enema appeared to be a feasible, and well-tolerated bedside technique for postoperative assessment of rectosigmoid anastomosis after cytoreductive surgery for ovarian cancer, with no procedure-related complications observed in this preliminary experience. These findings support further multicenter studies to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical utility.

articles.title: Development and validation of a Polish version of Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 (ObsQoR-10-Polish).
articles.authors: Maciejewska K, Lonc T, Krzywoń-Somionka J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 is a patient-reported outcome measure designed to evaluate early global postpartum recovery. No Polish version exists, and most prior validations excluded women with high-risk pregnancies.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center cohort study at a tertiary referral center for placenta accreta spectrum, the Polish translation was administered at 24, 48 and 72 h postpartum. The primary aim was a psychometric evaluation at 24 h (structural validity, convergent validity against the EuroQol five-dimension index and visual analogue scale, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, floor and ceiling effects). The secondary aim was to explore univariable associations with obstetric and anesthetic variables.
RESULTS: Of 800 eligible women approached, 441 consented, with data from 410 analyzed. Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha 0.90), test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.85) and convergent validity (r = 0.77 and 0.69) were good, and a modified one-factor model fitted acceptably. At 24 h, 1.5% of women had a maximum score. Scores at 24 h were higher after vaginal compared with cesarean delivery (77.8 vs. 67.0; P < 0.001), higher after spinal compared with general anesthesia for cesarean delivery (68.6 vs. 51.0; P = 0.011), lower with increasing perineal injury severity (53.0 vs. 81.5; P = 0.001) and with placental pathologies (60.7 vs. 72.6; P = 0.003), and lowest in placenta accreta spectrum (42.4; n = 5).
DISCUSSION: The Polish Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 is reliable and demonstrated known-groups validity across the obstetric risk categories represented in this cohort. Associations in high-risk subgroups were unadjusted and require confirmation.

articles.title: (E,E)-farnesol relaxes human umbilical vessels from preeclamptic pregnancies: ex vivo and in silico studies.
articles.authors: Batista PR, Dos Santos Pereira LR, Dias FJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is a serious gestational hypertensive disorder that affects the constrictive mechanisms of the umbilical vessels. Due to limited pharmacotherapy for preeclampsia, natural products (e.g., terpenes) stand out as raw materials for new vasodilators. The objective of this study is to demonstrate the vasorelaxant effect of the sesquiterpenoid (E,E)-farnesol on human umbilical arteries (hUA-PE) and veins (hUV-PE) from preeclamptic pregnancies.
STUDY DESIGN: hUA-PE and hUV-PE rings were mounted in organ bath for isometric recordings (ex vivo). The binding mode of (E,E)-farnesol to vascular targets was determined by molecular docking (in silico).
RESULTS: (E,E)-farnesol (1 μmol/L-1.2 mmol/L) induced concentration-dependent vasodilation in the basal and stimulated tone of hUA-PE and hUV-PE. There was an arteriovenous difference in the potency to relax vessels pre-contracted with KCl (60 mmol/L) (EC50: hUA-PE = 295.50 ± 9.26 μmol/L vs. hUV-PE = 83.83 ± 12.22 μmol/L; p < 0.0001) or 5-HT (10 μmol/L) (EC50: hUA-PE = 451.00 ± 3.63 μmol/L vs. hUV-PE = 172.90 ± 7.43 μmol/L; p < 0.0001). Pre-incubation with (E,E)-farnesol (1.2 mmol/L;±30 min) reduced basal tone and prevented vasoconstriction (by KCl/5-HT) in a time-dependent manner. (E,E)-farnesol interacted with L-type VOCC (-5.1 kcal/mol) and 5-HT1B/1D/2A receptors (≤ - 6.0 kcal/mol). TEA (1 mmol/L; non-specific K+ channel blocker) modified the potency of (E,E)-farnesol to relax 5-HT-induced vasoconstriction in hUA-PE (EC50: 399.42 ± 6.44 μmol/L) and hUV-PE (EC50: 360.42 ± 9.54 μmol/L).
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to demonstrate the potent vasodilatory effect of (E,E)-farnesol in preeclamptic umbilical vessels. Our findings expand the evidence regarding the action of natural products on the fetoplacental vasculature and position (E,E)-farnesol as a promising terpene for restoring vascular homeostasis in preeclampsia.

articles.title: Machine learning in semen analysis for male infertility: A systematic review and future directions.
articles.authors: Varzaneh ZA, Khoshkangini R, Saeedi-Boroujeni A et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate assessment of semen parameters is crucial for diagnosing and managing male infertility. However, conventional manual methods are time-consuming and subject to substantial inter-rater variability. While artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer promising automation solutions, a comprehensive synthesis of their performance and clinical translation remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the performance, clinical applications, and translational potential of AI- and ML-based methods for semen analysis. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched for peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025 evaluating AI/ML methods for semen analysis in male infertility. Data on algorithms, datasets, evaluation metrics, and clinical applications were extracted. Among the 56 included studies, 71% focused on sperm morphology, 13% on motility, 7% on concentration, and 9% addressed multi-parameter sperm assessment. Deep learning (DL), particularly convolutional neural network (CNN)-based models, was used in 71% of the studies. Models for sperm morphology classification frequently achieved accuracies exceeding 90%. Despite these high reported accuracies, the current evidence is largely limited by small, single-center datasets. Current evidence suggests that DL is the most mature AI approach for automated sperm morphology assessment, improving the accuracy, objectivity, and reproducibility of semen analysis. However, broader clinical implementation remains constrained by limited dataset diversity, inconsistent evaluation protocols, insufficient external validation, and poor model generalizability. Future research should prioritize large multicenter datasets, prospective external validation, standardized benchmarking frameworks, and explainable multimodal AI models to facilitate robust clinical translation and implementation in routine reproductive medicine.

articles.title: A sex-specific modification of the SARA questionnaire for obstructive sleep apnea screening: Comparative validation against six other tools in the HypnoLaus cohort.
articles.authors: Solecka S, Tomaskova H, Marques-Vidal P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: and objectivesObstructive sleep apnea is significantly underdiagnosed in women, partly because existing screening tools were developed in male-predominant cohorts and may fail to capture female-specific clinical presentations.
METHODS: We used the HypnoLaus population-based cohort (n = 1540; 718 women, 822 men) to evaluate seven OSA screening tools in this cross-sectional study and assessed whether adding menopausal status to SARA enhances diagnostic accuracy. Moderate-to-severe OSA was defined as AHI ≥ 15 events per hour on polysomnography.
RESULTS: The study included 1540 participants (718 women, 822 men). NoSAS and the updated SARA demonstrated the highest overall discriminative performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs), 0.741 (95% CI, 0.718-0.764) and 0.693 (95% CI, 0.669-0.716), respectively, followed by original SARA (AUC, 0.684), Berlin (0.635), SONA (0.579), STOP-Bang (0.575), and ESS (0.507). Incorporation of menopausal status improved discrimination of SARA in women (AUC 0.675 vs. 0.627; p = 0.001). Although NoSAS showed the highest overall AUC, updated SARA performed more consistently across sex-, age-, and BMI-defined phenotypes. In women ≤55 years, updated SARA showed higher discrimination than NoSAS (AUC 0.616 vs. 0.509; p = 0.014), and in lean women (BMI <25 kg/m2), updated SARA detected cases that NoSAS missed (sensitivity 42.3% vs. 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: Sex-related differences affect OSA screening. Incorporating menopausal status into SARA improved OSA detection in women. At the same time, anthropometry-weighted tools such as NoSAS performed poorly in younger, leaner women, underscoring the limitations of anthropometry-based screening in these phenotypes.

articles.title: Port-site metastasis prevention in gynecologic oncology: widespread practice variation despite limited supporting evidence.
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological cancer : official journal of the International Gynecological Cancer Society
articles.authors: Pan TL, Obermair H, Ramirez PT
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Port-site metastasis remains a rare but clinically significant complication of minimally invasive gynecologic oncology surgery. Despite numerous proposed preventive strategies, high-quality supporting evidence is sparse, and no standardized, evidence-based prevention protocol has been established. We performed an international evaluation of contemporary port-site metastasis prevention practices to define global practice patterns, quantify variability in strategy implementation, and assess clinicians' perceptions of preventive efficacy.
METHODS: An international, anonymous online survey, pilot-tested with surgeons from 5 countries and validated using the content validity index, was distributed from October 2025 to June 2026 through mailing lists and social media. The instrument captured respondent demographics, surgical practice characteristics, perceived risk of port-site metastasis, utilization and indications for preventive strategies, and perceptions of the strength of supporting evidence. Responses were analyzed descriptively, with stratification by geographic region, primary surgical modality, and years of experience.
RESULTS: Among the 190 respondents, Europe accounted for the largest geographic representation (40%, n = 64), followed by North America (18%, n = 28), and Central or South America and Australia or New Zealand each contributing 14% (n = 23). Port-site metastasis emerged as a substantially perceived oncologic concern, with 61% of respondents (97/158) rating it as moderate to high and 60% (93/154) reporting heightened concern over the course of their careers. The most routinely used preventive strategies were specimen retrieval bags (85%, n = 138), avoidance of direct tumor manipulation (74%, n = 122), and separate skin or fascia closure of ≥10 mm ports (70%, n = 116); these were also the strategies most frequently considered evidence-based (80%, 75%, and 37%, respectively). Low-pressure pneumoperitoneum (15%), port-site irrigation (≤14%), and cytotoxic agents (1%) were rarely used and predominantly rated as unsupported by evidence or uncertain. Preventive strategies were preferentially adopted in advanced ovarian cancer (73%, n = 116), particularly in clinical settings considered to confer the highest risk of port-site metastasis, including diffuse carcinomatosis (72%, n = 110), intraoperative tumor spillage (64%, n = 98), and large-volume ascites (56%, n = 85).
CONCLUSIONS: This international survey reveals a gap between…

articles.title: Preconception Care.
articles.authors: Aliberti GM, Kaimal AJ, Hull LE
articles.abstract: Optimizing health and management of medical conditions before conception can improve the likelihood of becoming pregnant and of an uncomplicated pregnancy. This article reviews best practices in preconception medical care for cisgender pregnancy-capable women desiring conception to optimize their fertility, improve their perinatal well-being, and decrease the likelihood of pregnancy complications. Given that almost half of all pregnancies in the United States are unintended or mistimed, internal medicine physicians are well positioned to proactively provide reproductive counseling and care.

articles.title: Primary cauda equina neuroendocrine tumor mimicking myxopapillary ependymoma: illustrative case.
articles.authors: Corliss LE, Benjamin HW, Galgano M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary cauda equina neuroendocrine tumors (CENETs) are rare intradural extramedullary neoplasms that were historically termed cauda equina paragangliomas. They may resemble more common cauda equina lesions, including myxopapillary ependymoma and schwannoma, on preoperative imaging. Recent molecular and immunohistochemical studies support CENET as a distinct entity, creating a need for practical diagnostic frameworks that separate primary tumors from metastatic neuroendocrine disease and nonneuroendocrine mimics.
OBSERVATIONS: A 42-year-old woman presented with progressive nocturnal low back pain, bilateral leg heaviness, lower extremity numbness, and urinary incontinence. MRI demonstrated a 5-cm L1-3 intradural extramedullary mass nearly occupying the spinal canal, with cauda equina compression and prominent surrounding vessels. She underwent urgent L1-3 laminoplasty and microsurgical resection. Intraoperatively, the tumor was extremely vascular, friable, and associated with the filum terminale. Gross-total resection was achieved. Pathology demonstrated a WHO grade 1 primary CENET with neuroendocrine marker expression, CK8/18 positivity, low proliferative index, and no evidence of systemic neuroendocrine malignancy on postoperative staging.
LESSONS: Cauda equina neuroendocrine lesions should be approached as a diagnostic spectrum. Clinical tempo, lesion multiplicity, imaging clues, intraoperative vascularity, and immunohistochemical/molecular workup can help distinguish primary CENET from metastatic neuroendocrine disease and mimics. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26609.

articles.title: Focal Glandular Inflammation of the Endometrium (So-called Focal Necrotizing Endometritis): Clinicopathologic and Immunohistochemical Study of 13 Cases.
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological pathology : official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Pathologists
articles.authors: Siatecka H, Sharma AE, Nucci MR et al.
articles.abstract: Focal necrotizing endometritis (FNE) is a rare phenomenon consisting of localized periglandular and intraglandular inflammation with luminal accumulation, epithelial cell necrosis, and absence of plasma cells. Since its initial morphologic description, FNE has not been further studied. We document clinical correlates, morphology, and immunophenotype of glandular (using PAX2, PTEN, Β-catenin, MSH6, and PMS2) and inflammatory (using CD3, CD20, CD4, CD8, and CD138) populations in 13 cases of FNE identified over a 4-yr period, representing 0.5% of all endometrial biopsies surveyed. Immunohistochemistry for CD3, CD20, CD4, CD8, CD138, PAX2, PTEN, B-catenin, MSH6, and PMS2 was used to characterize cellular components. The mean patient age was 43 (range: 31-61), and body mass index was 32 (range: 23-54). Biopsy was performed for infertility/recurrent pregnancy loss (n=7), abnormal uterine bleeding (n=5), or postmenopausal bleeding (n=1). In all biopsies, the process was confined to <8 glands. The infiltrate was T-cell predominant in 11/13 cases; in 2 cases, there was similar density of CD20- and CD3-positive cells. In all cases, CD8-positive T cells predominated over CD4-positive cells. CD138 was negative in all FNE areas. Affected glands showed normal nuclear PMS2, MSH6, and PAX2, as well as membranous Β-catenin, in all cases. PTEN consistently showed reduced staining, but no definitive loss compared with uninvolved glands. Three patients received doxycycline. Follow-up biopsies were available for 7 patients, with only one showing persistent FNE. Subsequent pregnancy was achieved in 4/7 patients with FNE and infertility. FNE is an uncommon phenomenon characterized by focal gland involvement by a predominant cytotoxic T-cell population, likely in response to cell damage. The lesion tends not to recur and does not appear to be associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes. A nonaberrant profile of PTEN, PAX2, MSH6, PMS2, and Β-catenin argues against FNE representing a response to early endometrioid neoplasia. Pathologists need to be aware of the occurrence of FNE and distinguish it from clinically actionable inflammation, namely chronic endometritis.

articles.title: From measurement to modeling: a systematic factorial framework for comparing structural models of motivation for seeking treatment.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de psiquiatria (Sao Paulo, Brazil : 1999)
articles.authors: Silveira PSP, Tess BH, da Silva SR et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Motivation for seeking treatment is a clinically relevant yet underexplored construct in mental health and behavioral research. This study proposes a systematic methodology to identify, compare, and rank structural models representing the construct of motivation, emphasizing structural plausibility and model comparison.
METHODS: Using the European Obesity Academy Questionnaire: Expectations of Surgical Treatment (EOAQ) as a working example, we analyzed data from 161 treatment-seeking patients with severe obesity, exploring their motivations for undergoing bariatric surgery. Seventy-nine candidate structural models were developed, incorporating one general factor (G) and two or three specific factors. Multigroup confirmatory factor analysis was used to evaluate model fit and test configural invariance across menopausal groups.
RESULTS: Bifactor models with one general factor and three specific dimensions were the most plausible under the proposed comparison (RMSEA 90%CI=0.038-0.102, p-close = 0.1214). The dimensions of personal, social, and healthcare represented intrinsic, extrinsic, and healthcare-related aspects of treatment motivation. The selected bifactor model reached the configural level of measurement invariance across groups and McDonald's omega (ω) coefficients ranged from 0.13 to 0.62.
CONCLUSIONS: This study presents a comprehensive framework for comparing alternative CFA models of motivation for seeking treatment, including unidimensional, first-order, bifactor, and second-order structures. The approach can be flexibly adapted to other instruments and populations, but the empirical structure identified here is preliminary and requiring replication in larger samples.

articles.title: GLP-1-Based Therapies Across the Menopausal Transition: Dermatologic Considerations and Practical Management.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Sanchez-Melendez S, Linkner R
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies have transformed obesity management. Their growing use among perimenopausal and menopausal women introduces new dermatologic considerations, particularly when weight loss occurs alongside menopause-associated changes in skin, adipose tissue, muscle, bone, and hair.
OBJECTIVE: To provide a practical framework for dermatologic management of perimenopausal and menopausal women receiving glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies.
METHODS: PubMed was searched from inception through September 2026 for literature on Glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies, menopause, skin aging, lean mass, alopecia, and aesthetic procedures. Reference lists of relevant reviews and consensus statements were also hand-searched. The senior author, a dermatologist and obesity medicine specialist, provides a practice-based perspective.
RESULTS: Key considerations include weight-loss trajectory, lean mass and bone preservation, nutrition, hair changes, procedural timing, and multidisciplinary comanagement. A staged aesthetic approach prioritizes skin quality during active weight loss, with structural correction as weight stabilizes.
CONCLUSION: Dermatologic care should anticipate the overlapping effects of menopause and substantial weight loss. A longitudinal, tissue-preservation approach may shift care from reactive correction toward proactive management.

articles.title: Effect of onternet-based home treatment with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training on pelvic floor rehabilitation.
articles.authors: Jiang X, Liang Y, Fu L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate the effect of internet-based home treatment with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training on pelvic floor rehabilitation.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Subjects (315 in total) were selected from patients with pelvic floor dysfunction who were diagnosed from October 2022 to June 2023. A home rehabilitation group (n = 178, receiving the Internet-based home treatment with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training) and an in-hospital rehabilitation group (n = 137, treated with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training in hospital) were set up.
RESULTS: After treatment, differences of statistical significance in POP-Aa, POP-Ba, POP-Gh, POP-Ap, POP-Bp, muscle potential, type I muscle fiber, type II muscle fiber, Pelvic Organ Prolapse Distress Inventory-6 (POPDI-6) subscale score, Colorectal-Anal Distress Inventory-8 (CRADI-8) subscale score, and Urogenital Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6) subscale score were observed in the home rehabilitation group compared with those before treatment (p < 0.05). Significant differences were detected in the changes in POP-Ap, type I muscle fiber, and type II muscle fiber between the groups before and after treatment, and a greater decrease in POP-Ap and smaller increases in type I muscle fiber and type II muscle fiber were obtained from the home rehabilitation group after treatment in comparison with those from the in-hospital rehabilitation group (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Although the internet-based home treatment with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training costs a longer time than in-hospital rehabilitation treatment, it can exert better therapeutic effects in terms of improving muscle potential, POP, and urinary symptoms.

articles.title: A meta-analysis on the prevalence of parents' complicated grief and post-traumatic stress disorder following perinatal loss in East and Southeast Asia.
articles.authors: Truong KA, Tran PQQ, Gelmez PS et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Previous reviews have reported high prevalence estimates of complicated grief (CG) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) among parents following perinatal loss. However, evidence has predominantly focused on Western populations, leaving parents in East and Southeast Asia underexamined.Objective: This meta-analysis aims to estimate the prevalence of CG and PTSD among parents experiencing perinatal loss in East and Southeast Asia while identifying potential moderators, including types of loss, parental roles, trimester of loss, maternal age, marital status, and country.Method: This protocol was prepared based on the PRISMA-P 2015 Statement. PubMed, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched using six search strings for peer-reviewed studies and preprints reporting parents' CG at 6 and/or 12 months or PTSD at least 1 month following perinatal loss. Searches will be supplemented manually via Google Scholar and key references. Two authors independently screened records and full texts, with study selection documented using the PRISMA flowchart. The quality of included studies will be assessed using appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Random-effects meta-analyses will be performed to calculate pooled prevalence estimates for CG and PTSD. Subgroup analyses for parental roles, different types of perinatal loss, trimester of loss, maternal age, marital status, and country will also be conducted. Heterogeneity will be assessed by Cochran's Q and I2. Funnel plots, Egger's regression test, and Begg's correlation test will be used to assess publication bias.Results: Results will be reported following the completion of the meta-analysis.Conclusion: The study will provide a comprehensive view of the prevalence of CG and PTSD among parents following perinatal loss in East and Southeast Asia. Implications for researchers and practitioners will be provided. However, pooled prevalence may be inflated owing to publication bias, limited cultural validity, inconsistency in measurements, and the conceptualization of CG in this study.

articles.title: Fetal Lymphatic Dysplasia Targeted RASopathy Gene Panel Sequencing: Molecular Findings and Genotype-Phenotype Correlations.
articles.authors: Yilmaz Celik L, Tug E, Kayhan G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prenatal diagnosis of lymphatic dysplasia (LD) remains difficult, especially in fetuses with normal karyotype and chromosomal microarray (CMA) results. This retrospective and prospective study (2022-2023) aimed to evaluate the contribution of RASopathy-associated gene analysis, as an advanced molecular test, to the etiology of pregnancies undergoing invasive testing for increased NT/NF and/or cystic hygroma when conventional cytogenetic and molecular karyotyping were normal.
METHODS: Twenty fetuses with ultrasound findings including cystic hygroma, increased nuchal translucency (NT ≥3.5 mm), and/or increased nuchal fold (NF ≥6 mm) were enrolled after normal karyotype and CMA analyses. DNA obtained from chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis was analyzed using targeted next-generation sequencing of RASopathy-associated genes. Variants were interpreted according to ACMG/ACGS guidelines.
RESULTS: RASopathy-related variants were identified in 7 of 20 fetuses (35%). Pathogenic variants were detected in the HRAS, PTPN11, and RIT1 genes, while variants of uncertain significance were found in the MAP2K1, RAF1, MAP2K2, and SPRED1 genes. In cases with parental testing, pathogenic variants were confirmed as de novo. No clinically significant variants were identified in the remaining fetuses.
CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that a considerable proportion of fetuses with idiopathic LD harbor RASopathy-related variants. Incorporating targeted RASopathy panels into prenatal evaluation may improve diagnosis, counseling, pregnancy management, and assessment of recurrence risk.

articles.title: Vaginal Progesterone Administration Subtly Influences Biomechanics and Composition of Mouse Cervix in Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Chen M, Weiss SN, Blank JL et al.
articles.abstract: During pregnancy, the cervix provides mechanical support for the developing fetus and then dynamically remodels during late gestation to soften and enable parturition. Dysfunction of the cervix can therefore lead to preterm birth, a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. Progestational agents have been extensively studied for preterm birth prevention, yet data on their direct biomechanical impact on the cervix are limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the biomechanical and compositional effects of systemic and vaginal progesterone administration on cervical tissue integrity in mice during late gestation. Pregnant mice received daily systemic or vaginal progesterone from gestational days 14-17 and were compared to vehicle controls. Cervical tissues were harvested six hours after the final treatment for structural, mechanical, and compositional assessment. Systemic progesterone treatment did not produce changes in cervical structure, mechanical properties, or extracellular matrix composition. In contrast, vaginal progesterone increased cervical tangent modulus at different stages of fatigue life. Vaginal progesterone also reduced cervical cross-sectional area and water content, while increasing collagen concentration relative to wet weight, suggesting that its biomechanical effects may be mediated through modulation of tissue hydration. These findings provide a plausible biomechanical basis for the clinical efficacy of vaginal progesterone in preventing preterm birth by preserving cervical mechanical stability and attenuating premature softening.

articles.title: Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers.
articles.authors: Liu Z, Yang H, Wang M et al.
articles.abstract: Preoperative discrimination of ovarian cancer from benign masses poses significant challenges, particularly in cases where serum biomarkers yield negative or nonspecific results. This multicenter observational diagnostic modeling study analyzed plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from 743 participants across training, internal test, external test, and two exploratory cohorts using low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Four fragmentomic feature classes-fragment size patterns, nucleosome footprint-related features, copy-number variations, and repeat element patterns-were incorporated into a stacked machine-learning model. Model development and cutoff selection were limited to the training cohort, followed by evaluation in the internal-test and external-test cohorts.
