The cfDNA model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.930 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.894-0.966) and 0.932 (95% CI, 0.891-0.972) in the internal-test and external-test cohorts, respectively. Incorporation of cfDNA with cancer antigen 125 (CA125) and human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) increased AUCs to 0.964 (95% CI, 0.938-0.990) and 0.964 (95% CI, 0.938-0.991). At cutoffs derived from the training cohort, the combined model maintained sensitivities of 88.4% and 89.2% while enhancing specificity from 77.9% to 88.4% and from 78.9% to 91.5%, respectively. The cfDNA model also effectively detected cancers with CA125 and/or HE4 levels below conventional thresholds, and post hoc analyses demonstrated complementary discrimination when cfDNA was added to the Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm. These findings advocate for prospective evaluation of integrated cfDNA fragmentomics as an adjunct for preoperative risk stratification of ovarian masses.

articles.title: Single-port robotic surgery versus laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery for the surgical staging of early-stage endometrial cancer: a sequential-period propensity-score analysis.
articles.authors: Kim JH, Kim Y, Jo D et al.
articles.abstract: We compared perioperative outcomes of da Vinci SP robotic surgery and laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery (LESS) for staging early-stage endometrial cancer in a sequential-period cohort. Between 2010 and 2025, 178 women with presumed and final FIGO stage I or II endometrial carcinoma underwent single-port staging with lymph node assessment; LESS was used through 2021 (n = 95), and SP surgery was introduced in 2021 (n = 83). Patients were analyzed by planned approach, including procedures requiring an additional port. The primary outcome was the hemoglobin decline from the preoperative value to the value measured on the day of surgery. The hemoglobin decline was 1.92 ± 1.14 g/dL after LESS and 0.92 ± 0.88 g/dL after SP surgery (p < .001), and estimated blood loss was 205.4 ± 192.4 and 68.5 ± 79.3 mL (p < .001). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, the between-group difference in hemoglobin decline (SP minus LESS) was - 1.06 g/dL (95% CI - 1.42 to - 0.70). This estimate was not materially changed by further adjustment for perioperative fluid volume and sampling time. In a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with pelvic lymphadenectomy, the difference was attenuated to - 0.72 g/dL (95% CI - 1.21 to - 0.22), and operative time was 25.5 min longer with the SP robot. Overall operative time, hospital stay, conversions, and complications did not differ significantly. SP staging was associated with a smaller hemoglobin decline. Because the 2 approaches were used in largely different calendar periods, these findings do not establish an independent effect of the platform.

articles.title: Labor induction with double balloon catheter, oral misoprostol or both: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Bleicher I, Yehuda DB, Basov D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare cesarean delivery rates and induction outcomes among women undergoing labor induction with a cervical ripening double balloon (DB), oral misoprostol (OM), or a combination of both (DOM).
METHODS: This single-center randomized controlled trial included women with singleton term pregnancies, cephalic presentation, Bishop score ≤ 4, and intact membranes. Participants were randomized to DB for 6 h, oral misoprostol, or combined treatment. The primary outcome was cesarean delivery rate. Secondary outcomes included Bishop score after 6 h, time from induction to delivery, failed induction, and maternal and neonatal outcomes. Due to slow recruitment, the study was stopped early, and complete-case analysis was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 216 participants were included in the analysis (DB n = 65, OM n = 75, DOM n = 76). Cesarean delivery rates were 20%, 11%, and 20% in the DB, OM, and DOM groups, respectively (p = 0.2). The combined treatment group demonstrated a significantly shorter induction-to-delivery interval (median 14.7 h vs 20.7 in DB [p = 0.006] and 22.9 h in OM [p < 0.001]); higher 6-h Bishop scores (median 6 vs 5 in DB [p = 0.012] and 4 in OM [p < 0.001]);and lower rates of failed induction (2.6% vs 18% in DB [p = 0.010] and 5.4% in OM [p = 0.4]). Maternal and neonatal outcomes were similar across groups.
CONCLUSION: Despite limited power this study suggests that combined use of cervical ripening balloon and oral misoprostol shortens induction duration and improves early cervical ripening without increasing cesarean delivery rates. This approach may enhance the efficiency of labor induction.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGIRSTRATION: Date of registration: 03-03-2019. Date of initial participant enrollment, July 1st, 2019. Clinical trial identification number #NCT03866772. URL of the registration site: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03866772#study-overview.

articles.title: Neonatal kidney injury: diagnosis, management, and long-term kidney health - the perspective of the European Neonatal Nephrology Working Group.
articles.authors: Hoogenboom LA, Hundscheid T, Snauwaert E et al.
articles.abstract: Advances in perinatal and neonatal care have improved the survival of preterm and intrauterine growth-restricted (IUGR) infants, yet these achievements bring underlit challenges, including kidney development and long-term renal health. Because nephrogenesis occurs largely before birth, preterm birth interrupts this process, resulting in reduced and structurally immature nephrons. These infants, as well as those exposed to adverse intrauterine environments such as malnutrition or preeclampsia, are predisposed to kidney vulnerability that extends into later life, increasing their risk for chronic kidney disease (CKD). Paediatric nephrologists and neonatologists from the Neonatal Nephrology Working Group (WG) of the European Society for Paediatric Nephrology (ESPN) and the Special Interest Group of the European Society for Paediatric Research (ESPR) collaborated to synthesize current evidence on risk factors, mechanisms, and management of kidney injury in neonates.Key findings highlight that neonatal acute kidney injury (AKI) remains difficult to diagnose using adult-derived criteria, as creatinine-based definitions fail to account for postnatal adaptation and fluid dynamics. AKI in neonates commonly arises from multifactorial causes (i.e., perinatal asphyxia, sepsis, patent ductus arteriosus, and/or exposure to nephrotoxic drugs) and often manifests through systemic consequences like fluid overload. Management emphasizes fluid and electrolyte optimization, cautious use of nephrotoxic agents, and individualized nutrition to support growth while minimizing metabolic derangements. Emerging neonatal-specific kidney replacement therapy technologies, including miniaturized and continuous circuits, expand therapeutic options but require further evaluation. Follow-up is warranted; nevertheless, current evidence is unable to provide an evidence-based strategy. This evaluation underscores the urgent need for integrative research, neonatal-specific diagnostic criteria, and evidence-based guidelines tailored to this vulnerable population. By bridging neonatology and nephrology, the newly established WG aims to foster multidisciplinary strategies that improve both short- and long-term kidney outcomes in preterm and critically ill newborns.

articles.title: Bilateral Sacrospinous Fixation Using a Sling-Like Mesh: Real-World Data on Early Safety and Surgical Outcomes from a Large Cohort.
articles.authors: Naumann G, Savic-Mitic Z, Gramm C
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: To describe early safety and feasibility data of Anterior Bilateral Sacrospinous Ligament Fixation (ABSSLF) using Splentis® for apical Pelvic Organ Prolapse (POP).
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of available data from 334 women treated with Splentis between 2016-2023 at a German referral hospital. Proportions of early complications and outcomes are reported with Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence intervals. Anatomical changes (POP-Q stages) and patient-reported outcomes (German Pelvic Floor Questionnaire, gPFQ) were explored with Wilcoxon test.
RESULTS: The median operative time was 19 min (IQR 16-24). Perioperative complications include 0.3% intraoperative bleeding > 200 mL, 43.1% mild and 0.3% moderate gluteal pain (Clavien-Dindo grade I); 1.2% urinary retention (Clavien-Dindo grade II). At median follow-up of 11.3 weeks (IQR 8.9-13.8), 7.2% (95%CI 4.7-10.5%) reported mild and 0.6% (95%CI 0.1-2.1%) moderate gluteal pain (Clavien-Dindo grade I), and 0.9% de novo residual urine > 100 mL (Clavien-Dindo grade I). Early mesh-related complications included three cases requiring partial removal (0.9%, Clavien-Dindo grade IIIa), and one managed conservatively (0.3%, Clavien-Dindo grade I); 98.8% (95% CI 97.0-99.7%) showed apical POP-Q ≤ 1 (median improvement -3.0, 95%CI -3.0 to -2.5; p < 0.0001), with improvements in anterior and posterior compartments. Patient satisfaction was 97.9% (95% CI 95.7-99.1%). Moreover, 115/334 patients (34.4%) completed the gPFQ, and pelvic floor function improved by median 7.4 points (95%CI 6.5-8.3; p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: ABSSLF with Splentis demonstrated favourable perioperative safety and encouraging short-term outcomes, with a low rate of early complications, as a uterus-preserving option for apical POP. Long-term studies are needed to assess effectiveness and late complications.

articles.title: Challenges in perimenopause research and the application of existing criteria for staging reproductive aging in low and middle-income countries: a scoping review.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Jaff NG, Crowther NJ, Islam RM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Perimenopause is an important stage of reproductive aging, yet research in low and middle-income countries (LMICs) is limited and reproductive-stage classification is inconsistent. This narrative review examines methodological and contextual challenges affecting perimenopause research in LMICs, evaluates the application of the Stages of Reproductive Aging Workshop +10 (STRAW +10) framework and proposes practical considerations to strengthen future research.
METHOD: The review was informed by a previously published comprehensive scoping review and supplemented with studies from LMICs published between 2025 and July 2026. Eligible studies applied STRAW, STRAW +10 or comparable reproductive-stage classification methods. Data were synthesized using descriptive and narrative approaches.
RESULTS: Of 288 full-text articles assessed, 90 studies published between 2005 and June 2026 were included. Most were cross-sectional, seven studies (7.8%) were longitudinal and four studies (4.4%) were nationally representative. Considerable heterogeneity in reproductive-stage classification was observed. STRAW +10 was applied in 20.0% of studies, STRAW in 21.0% and World Health Organization (WHO) criteria in 10.0%, while 48.9% relied on menstrual history without explicitly referencing a recognized staging framework.
CONCLUSION: Perimenopause research in LMICs is limited and characterized by substantial heterogeneity in reproductive-stage classification. Wider adoption of standardized frameworks such as STRAW +10, together with greater methodological rigor, is needed to improve the quality, comparability and applicability of future research.

articles.title: Melt-electrowritten gelatin-functionalized PCL scaffolds loaded with human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells for intrauterine adhesions treatment.
articles.authors: Wan Y, Luo X, Ma H et al.
articles.abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a common refractory gynecological disease characterized by endometrial fibrosis and cavity obliteration that often leads to infertility. In this study, we developed a tissue-engineered construct combining 3D printed PCL scaffolds, surface gelatin conjugation and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUCMSCs) for IUA treatment. PCL scaffolds were fabricated by melt electrowriting (MEW) and subjected to sequential surface modification: NaOH hydrolysis (PCL-N), gelatin coating (PCL-NG), and 1-Ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide/N-hydroxysuccinimide (EDC/NHS) crosslinking (PCL-NGE). Physicochemical characterization confirmed the successful surface modification. In vitro cytocompatibility was assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay, live/dead staining, and cytoskeleton staining. The results demonstrated that the PCL-NGE scaffold exhibited superior cytocompatibility toward hUCMSCs, significantly promoting their metabolic activity, adhesion, and spreading. The PCL-NGE-hUCMSCs constructs were then implanted into a rat IUA model, and the histopathological assessment revealed that the PCL-NGE-hUCMSCs group markedly restored endometrial thickness, increased glandular density, and substantially reduced collagen deposition and fibrosis compared to the IUA model group. These findings suggest that gelatin-functionalized PCL scaffolds fabricated using MEW and loaded with hUCMSCs may represent a potential strategy for endometrial regeneration and IUA treatment.

articles.title: Prevalence and ultrasonographic characterization of newly detected findings suggestive of deep and ovarian endometriosis in postmenopausal women undergoing routine gynecological examination.
articles.authors: Barra F, Perrone U, Xholli A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To assess the prevalence and ultrasonographic characteristics of newly detected findings suggestive of ovarian and deep endometriosis (DE) in postmenopausal women undergoing routine gynecological evaluation.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This prospective observational study (NCT07503938) included consecutive postmenopausal participants attending two regional gynecology outpatient clinics for routine examination over 24 months. Transvaginal ultrasound was performed by a single operator according to International Deep Endometriosis Analysis (IDEA) group criteria. Findings suggestive of DE and/or ovarian cysts suggestive of endometriomas were recorded and characterized. Clinical data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with posterior compartment hypoechoic nodules.
RESULTS: Four hundred ninety-two participants were included (mean age 60.2 ± 6.1 years; median time since menopause 8.0 years). Ultrasound findings suggestive of endometriosis were identified in 40 participants (8.1%; 95% CI 5.9%-10.9%), including posterior compartment hypoechoic nodules in 36 (7.3%). Intestinal nodules (n = 21; 4.3%) often showed plaque-like morphology, thickness < 7 mm, regular margins, limited Doppler vascularity, and uncommon submucosal involvement. The prevalence of posterior nodules suggestive of DE decreased with increasing time since menopause (13.9% within ≤5 years vs. 4.3% >10 years; p for trend = 0.001). In multivariable analysis, ≤5 years since menopause was independently associated with posterior nodules (adjusted OR 3.25, 95% CI 1.35-7.83), as were a history of dysmenorrhea (adjusted OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.05-4.60) and chronic pelvic pain (adjusted OR 2.36, 95% CI 1.11-5.00). No independent association was observed with current pelvic pain, dyschezia, previous infertility, or systemic hormone replacement therapy. Six ovarian cysts with ultrasonographic features suggestive of endometriomas were identified (1.2%; 95% CI 0.45%-2.64%), five of which exhibited atypical features, including multilocularity, heterogeneous echoes, papillary excrescences, or wall thickening.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound findings suggestive of DE may be detected after menopause and are associated with earlier postmenopausal timing and a history of reproductive-age pain, but not with specific current pain symptoms or hormonal exposure. Their predominantly plaque-like, poorly vascularized morphology may…

articles.title: Aquatic pelvic floor rehabilitation for persistent stress urinary incontinence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a prospective single-arm study.
articles.journal: Archivio italiano di urologia, andrologia : organo ufficiale [di] Societa italiana di ecografia urologica e nefrologica
articles.authors: Iacovelli V, Carilli M, Vittori M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent stress urinary incontinence (SUI) remains one of the most troublesome functional complications after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Although pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) represents the standard conservative treatment, a proportion of patients continue to experience bothersome symptoms. Aquatic rehabilitation may facilitate pelvic floor activation through reduced gravitational loading, enhanced proprioceptive input, and trunk stabilization; however, its role in post-prostatectomy incontinence has not been investigated. This prospective pilot study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and clinical outcomes associated with hydrokinesitherapy in men with persistent SUI following RARP.  Methods: Men with persistent pure SUI after rArP despite three months of standardized conservative management, including PFMT and biofeedback, were prospectively enrolled between January and May 2023. Participants underwent a five-week hydrokinesitherapy program consisting of ten supervised 40-minute sessions performed twice weekly. outcomes included the 24-hour pad test, International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-short Form (ICIQ-sF), Incontinence Quality of Life questionnaire (I-QoL), International Prostate symptom score (IPSS), IPSS quality-of-life item, and Patient Global Impression of Improvement (PGI-I), assessed at baseline, end of treatment (5 weeks), and 12-week follow-up.
RESULTS: Twenty patients completed the rehabilitation program without treatment-related adverse events or dropouts. significant improvements were observed at the end of treatment in pad weight, IPSS, IPSS-QoL, ICIQ-SF, and I-QoL scores (all p ≤ 0.01). These improvements were maintained or further improved at 12 weeks, particularly for pad weight, QoL, and incontinence-related symptom scores. overall patient satisfaction was high according to PGI-I. Two patients (10%) subsequently underwent male sling surgery because of persistent bothersome sUI.  Conclusions: Hydrokinesitherapy was feasible, safe, and associated with clinically meaningful improvements in urinary continence and health-related QoL in men with persistent SUI after RARP who had not achieved satisfactory recovery following initial conservative rehabilitation. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in adequately powered randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Health Literacy Among Women in Menopause in Western Iran: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Jenabi E, Khazaei S, Abdoli S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a lack of information regarding health literacy in homemaker menopausal women in the western Iran. The aim of this study was to investigate factors associated with health literacy among women in menopause who are homemakers in western Iran.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from February 5, 2025 to August 20, 2025, among 350 women in menopause attending comprehensive health service centers in Hamadan, western Iran. The participants were recruited via systematic random sampling. The data collection instruments consisted of a demographic and midwifery information questionnaire, the Health Literacy for Iranian Adults, the Perceived Stress Scale, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. A p value of < .05 was considered statistically significant. Independent t-tests and one-way ANOVA (analysis of variance) were used to compare mean health literacy across categorical variables. Pearson's correlation coefficient was applied to examine the relationships among social support, perceived stress, and health literacy. In addition, to identify independent predictors of health literacy, a multivariable linear regression model was constructed. All analyses were conducted using Stata version 14.
RESULTS: The health literacy levels show that the majority (267; 76.29%) have inadequate health literacy. The mean health literacy was significantly associated with participants' education (p < .001), occupation (p < .001), husbands' occupation (p < .001), and economic status (p < .001). The significant negative correlation was observed between health literacy and perceived stress (r = -0.86), suggesting that higher health literacy was associated with lower levels of perceived stress. Moreover, health literacy was positively correlated with social support (r = 0.77), indicating that individuals with greater health literacy tended to report higher levels of social support. The multivariable linear regression model identified higher perceived stress (β = -2.05, p < .001) and older age (β = -1.40, p = .03) as significant negative predictors of health literacy, while greater social support (β = 1.46, p < .001) was a significant positive predictor.
CONCLUSION: The findings of the present study revealed that the majority of the women had an inadequate level of health literacy, and this variable had a negative relationship with perceived stress and a positive relationship with social support. The results of this research emphasize…

articles.title: Potential impact of the United States President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief funding cuts on the HIV and cervical cancer burden in Kenya.
articles.authors: Hathaway CL, Klein S, Guha A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The withdrawal of the United States President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) funding has disrupted critical HIV services, including testing, antiretroviral therapy (ART), preexposure prophylaxis, voluntary medical male circumcision, and cervical cancer screening for women with HIV. We modelled the impact of PEPFAR funding scenarios on HIV and cervical cancer outcomes in Kenya.
METHODS: We used a dynamic compartmental model of HIV/human papilloma virus (HPV) for Kenya to evaluate PEPFAR funding scenarios beginning in 2025. Upper and lower bound scenarios simulated a 6-month service halt with partial ART interruption, followed by either full PEPFAR funding withdrawal or continued ART-only support. Both scenarios simulated the Ministry of Health recovery to 2025 funding levels by 2030. Outcomes were compared to scenarios without PEPFAR interruptions: the current status quo or uninterrupted PEPFAR funding meeting UNAIDS/WHO targets.
RESULTS: Over the next 25 years, compared to the status quo, complete PEPFAR withdrawal is projected to cause 191-297 thousand more HIV cases and 132-206 thousand more HIV deaths. If PEPFAR maintains funding for ART, an additional 15-23 thousand HIV deaths and 32-44 thousand HIV cases are expected. Compared to achieving UNAIDS/WHO targets, complete withdrawal could result in an additional 808-915 thousand HIV cases and 667-741 thousand HIV deaths. Cervical cancer cases and deaths are projected to increase by 43-45 thousand and 19-20 thousand, respectively, if funding is completely withdrawn.
CONCLUSION: Any interruptions in PEPFAR support could lead to thousands of HIV and cervical cancer cases and deaths in Kenya. Sustained funding is crucial to continue the progress made against HIV and cervical cancer.

articles.title: Intraoperative Noise Isolation and Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting after Gynecological Laparoscopic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Fu C, Hu X, Tao D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remain common after gynecological laparoscopic surgery despite guideline-based prophylaxis. Auditory information is still processed during clinically adequate general anesthesia, and operating rooms are persistently noisy, but whether attenuating intraoperative sound exposure alters PONV is unknown.
METHODS: In this single-center, patient- and assessor-blinded randomized trial, women aged 18 to 65 yr undergoing elective gynecological laparoscopic surgery were randomized 1:1 to wear passive noise-attenuating earmuffs from induction until the end of surgery or to usual care. All patients received dexamethasone and palonosetron. The primary outcome was PONV incidence within 48 h, defined as any episode of nausea, retching, or vomiting, assessed across three prespecified windows (post-anesthesia care unit, to 24 h, and 24 to 48 h). Secondary outcomes included PONV severity, its components, rescue antiemetic use, pain, and quality of recovery.
RESULTS: Of 364 patients assessed, 192 were randomized. PONV within 48 h occurred in 34 of 96 patients (35.4%) with noise isolation and 50 of 96 (52.1%) with control (adjusted risk difference, -0.179 [95% CI, -0.318 to -0.040]; P = 0.012). Across the three windows the overall adjusted risk difference was -0.134 (95% CI, -0.215 to -0.053; P = 0.001), with no treatment-by-window interaction (P = 0.332); window-specific values were -0.162, -0.172, and -0.068. PONV severity, retching, and three post hoc endpoints (the vomiting-or-retching composite, complete response 72.9% versus 56.2%, and total response 64.6% versus 47.9%) favored noise isolation after false discovery rate correction. Adverse events, quality of recovery, and opioid exposure (post hoc) showed no evidence of a difference.
CONCLUSIONS: Among women receiving dual antiemetic prophylaxis for gynecological laparoscopic surgery, intraoperative noise isolation was associated with a lower incidence and severity of PONV.

articles.title: Anterior Middle Cingulate Cortex Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid Level Is Elevated in Children With Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder With and Without Prenatal Alcohol Exposure.
articles.authors: Alger JR, Gupta I, Farkouh L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior neuroimaging suggests brain differences between children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and prenatal alcohol exposure (ADHD+PAE) and non-exposed children with ADHD due to non-PAE causes (ADHD-PAE). There has been interest in regional brain levels of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and glutamate (Glu) measured in vivo with magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) as possible indicators of local inhibitory, respectively, excitatory activity in ADHD. For the first time, we report here a comparison of GABA and Glu in ADHD+PAE vs. ADHD-PAE.
METHODS: At 3 Tesla, we used J-difference-edited single-voxel MRS to assay GABA and Glu in 27 children with ADHD+PAE, 21 with ADHD-PAE, and 28 typically developing (TD) controls, all aged between 7 and 14 years. MRS was sampled from midline anterior middle cingulate cortex (aMCC), the "cognitive cingulate" considered functionally relevant to ADHD. Spectra were fit with custom software, including a unique technique for isolating the GABA signal from the confounding macromolecular baseline (MMBL).
RESULTS: aMCC GABA was higher in ADHD+PAE and ADHD-PAE than in TD. GABA increased with age in TD, but not in ADHD+PAE or ADHD-PAE. Similar effects were observed for the ratios GABA/Glu and GABA/Glx. For GABA+MMBL (GABA+) these effects were not seen; rather, GABA+ and MMBL increased with age for the ADHD+PAE group only. No significant effects were found for Glu or Glx.
CONCLUSIONS: GABA in the aMCC does not distinguish the two etiologies of ADHD; rather, elevated GABA that follows an abnormal development appears to be common to both. High GABA may reflect increased inhibition of the aMCC impairing its cognitive functions. GABA+ results in ADHD may not track reliably with underlying GABA values. Negative results for Glu and Glx should be reexamined at shorter echo-times.

articles.title: Highly Processed Food Consumption, Maternal Sociodemographic Variables, and Pregnancy Outcomes.
articles.authors: Erbe K, Filatava E, Overton NE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal diet quality during pregnancy is an important modifiable, yet often overlooked, factor in pregnancy outcomes for both the pregnant individual and their baby. Dietary patterns in the United States are often linked to sociodemographic factors and include a significant proportion of highly processed foods (HPF), known contributors to adverse health outcomes. However, these relationships are poorly understood in pregnant populations.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this retrospective observational study were to use Dietary Screener Questionnaire (DSQ) data to (a) explore the consumption of common HPFs during pregnancy, and (b) examine the relationships between HPF consumption and sociodemographic factors and maternal pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: We collected sociodemographic information, pregnancy outcomes, and DSQs capturing dietary intake during the previous 30 days from women who delivered their infants at a large metropolitan hospital in Boston, Massachusetts, between January 2019 and August 2021. We calculated descriptive statistics for sociodemographic, pregnancy outcome, and HPF intake data. We used separate linear regression models to examine associations between total HPF consumption and sociodemographic and pregnancy outcome variables; we further examined significant relationships with multivariable regression.
RESULTS: Ninety-six women participated (most were White), privately insured, and not Hispanic/Latina. Women in this cohort consumed HPFs an average of 1.91 times each day. There was a trend towards lower total HPF consumption among Black/African American and Asian participants compared to White participants. Total HPF consumption was significantly lower among former smokers compared to those without a history of smoking and among participants diagnosed with gestational diabetes compared to those without diabetes. Conversely, participants with chronic hypertension consumed more HPFs than those without a hypertensive disorder. No other significant interactions were noted.
DISCUSSION: Future research is needed to assess the relationships between HPF consumption, sociodemographic factors, and health outcomes across diverse populations of pregnant individuals. Obstetric clinicians, particularly nurses, should consider expanding pregnancy nutrition counseling to include methods such as a DSQ to reduce HPF intake.

articles.title: Safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability, and readability of large language model responses to patient health questions about adenomyosis: A comparative study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Zhang L, Wu F, Ye D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients increasingly use large language model (LLM)-based chatbots to seek health information. Adenomyosis is a common gynecological condition associated with heavy menstrual bleeding, dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, infertility, and pregnancy-related concerns. The quality and safety of chatbot-generated patient information is clinically relevant.
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to compare the safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability, information quality, and readability of LLM responses to patient health questions about adenomyosis.
METHODS: This comparative cross-sectional evaluation was designed and reported according to the CHART checklist for chatbot health advice studies. Standardized chatbot queries were posed from June 13 to June 15, 2026, in Wuhan, China. A 40-item adenomyosis patient question set was submitted to four LLM-based chatbots: ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao. Five trained gynecology experts evaluated the safety, accuracy, empathy, DISCERN score, EQIP (Ensuring Quality Information for Patients) score, Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria, and Global Quality Scale score using prespecified criteria; readability was calculated algorithmically using automated text-processing procedures. Safety was coded as 0 for safe and 1 for potentially unsafe. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Fleiss' kappa for safety and intraclass correlation coefficient (2,1) for the remaining expert-rated metrics. Between-model comparisons used paired nonparametric methods, with Kendall's W and 95% confidence intervals reported as the omnibus effect-size measure for Friedman tests.
RESULTS: A total of 160 model-question responses were evaluated. Inter-rater agreement was substantial to excellent across metrics, with Fleiss' kappa of 0.892 for safety and intraclass correlation coefficient values ranging from 0.768 to 0.886 for the remaining metrics. Most responses were classified as safe; observed safe-response proportions differed descriptively across models, and no pairwise safety comparison remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Accuracy and empathy differed significantly among models (both P < 0.001): ChatGPT achieved the highest median accuracy score. DISCERN, EQIP, and JAMA scores differed significantly among models, whereas Global Quality Scale scores did not. All readability indices differed significantly among models: Doubao had the highest grade-level readability scores and…

articles.title: Internet Access, Health-Related Internet Use, and Pelvic Floor Muscle Exercise Adherence Among Prostate Cancer Patients With Urinary Incontinence After Radical Prostatectomy: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Huang H, He Y, Qu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic floor muscle exercise (PFME) is the primary conservative management for urinary incontinence following radical prostatectomy. While digital health resources are increasing, the specific impact of health-related internet use on PFME adherence remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations between internet access, health-related internet use frequency, and PFME adherence among prostate cancer survivors.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey (N = 251) was conducted between October and December 2025. Data on internet access, health-related internet use, and PFME adherence were analyzed using ordinal logistic regression and restricted cubic splines, with sequential adjustment for sociodemographic and clinical factors.
RESULTS: Health-related internet use was independently associated with PFME frequency (OR = 1.46; 95% CI, 1.03-2.06), whereas mere internet access was not. A significant nonlinear relationship was observed between health-related internet use and exercise frequency (P for nonlinear = .025), while exercise duration demonstrated a linear association. Effects were more pronounced among participants with lower educational attainment or lower baseline physical activity.
CONCLUSIONS: Health-related internet use, rather than simple internet access, is a key independent predictor of PFME adherence. These findings suggest that digital engagement significantly facilitates self-management behaviors during postsurgical recovery.
IMPLICATIONS FOR ONCOLOGY NURSING PRACTICE: Oncology nurses should assess patients' health-related internet use patterns and digital literacy rather than just internet access to identify those requiring additional navigation support. Tailored digital health resources should be integrated into survivorship care, particularly for patients with lower educational backgrounds, to bridge adherence gaps and reduce health disparities.

articles.title: Risk of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome by body mass index: Retrospective cohort study with Korean nationwide population-based cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Kim Y, Chae K, Kim S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a gynecologic endocrine disorder affecting various aspects of women's health. Research examining the association between PCOS, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in Korean populations remains limited. We assessed OSA risk in Korean with PCOS, considering body mass index (BMI).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using health insurance claims data from the National Health Insurance Service. We selected 33 638 people with PCOS and 98 110 controls with available BMI data. This is a subgroup representing our previous retrospective cohort study, which identified the relationship between PCOS and several mental disorders. Hazard ratios (HR) for PCOS were calculated using Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: Obese individuals had a higher prevalence of OSA (0.60% in people with PCOS, 0.20% in controls) compared with the non-obese individuals (0.12% in people with PCOS, 0.13% in controls). PCOS (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.483, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.029-2.137) and BMI (HR: 1.104, 95% CI: 1.069-1.141) were associated with an increased risk of OSA.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that the risk of OSA is higher in people with PCOS. This research holds significance by indicating that obesity at the time of PCOS diagnosis could serve as a potential predictor for OSA. This study supports international PCOS guidelines that recommend screening and managing OSA.

articles.title: Risk-reducing gynecologic surgery in hereditary cancer: Evidence, timing, and counseling.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: da Silva Filho AL, Grandi G, Lopes TL et al.
articles.abstract: Risk-reducing gynecologic surgery is an established preventive option for women with selected hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes. In BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers, observational studies associate risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy with lower tubo-ovarian cancer incidence and mortality. In Lynch syndrome, hysterectomy is associated with reduced endometrial cancer incidence, while ovarian removal requires gene-specific assessment of age, menopausal status, family history, and preferences. Accumulating pathologic and molecular evidence supports a distal tubal origin for many high-grade serous carcinomas, informing complete salpingectomy and meticulous pathology and providing a biologic rationale for investigating salpingectomy with delayed oophorectomy. Prospective preference studies associate this staged strategy with better menopause-related quality of life, but selection bias remains relevant and oncologic non-inferiority is unestablished. This narrative review critically integrates observational findings, risk estimates, guideline recommendations, and expert consensus into a clinical framework for patient selection, procedure choice, timing, counseling, and survivorship. Prevention planning should address fertility, surgical menopause, hormone therapy, residual peritoneal cancer risk, and unequal access to testing and specialist care.

articles.title: Implementation of artificial intelligence-enabled, obstetric point-of-care ultrasounds into routine antenatal care in Lusaka Province of Zambia.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Gazzetta E, Matenga TFL, Chi BH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Access to obstetric ultrasound remains limited in many countries owing to the limited availability of equipment and specialist operators. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled obstetric point-of-care ultrasound (OB POCUS) may expand access to reliable gestational age (GA) dating within routine antenatal care (ANC).
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical utility of implementing AI-enabled OB POCUS for GA assessment across four public-sector facilities in Lusaka Province, Zambia.
METHODS: We integrated routine AI-enabled OB POCUS into ANC using a training-of-trainers model, followed by standardized competency-based training for facility healthcare providers and ongoing mentorship. We abstracted data from facility ANC registers for women scanned between September 2024 and March 2025. Among patients with both last menstrual period (LMP)- and AI-enabled OB POCUS-based dating, we calculated the discrepancy between the two estimates and applied American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) GA-specific thresholds to classify each patient according to whether the discrepancy was large enough to warrant revising the LMP-based estimated due date (EDD) to the AI-enabled OB POCUS-based EDD. We estimated the proportion meeting these re-dating criteria and used logistic regression to assess factors associated with meeting them.
RESULTS: Among 1068 ultrasound recipients, 859 (80.4%) had both a recorded LMP and a documented AI-enabled OB POCUS-based EDD. Of these, the median EDD discrepancy was 11 days (IQR = 5-29 days), and 51% met the ACOG criteria for EDD revision. The proportion meeting re-dating criteria did not differ by GA at presentation and was not affected by facility or demographic characteristics.
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of AI-enabled OB POCUS within public-sector ANC in Zambia was feasible. Half of women scanned met the criteria for revising an LMP-based due date, indicating that such technologies could substantially change pregnancy care where ultrasound is otherwise unavailable.

articles.title: RAD52 is a therapeutic vulnerability for acquired PARP inhibitor resistance in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Ota Y, Elizagaray ML, Gupta V et al.
articles.abstract: Acquired resistance to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) limits their therapeutic benefits in patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSC). Identifying therapeutic vulnerabilities that function across distinct forms of acquired PARPi resistance is an urgent need. In BRCA2-deficient PARPi-naive cells, targeting RAD52 can be synthetic lethal with a PARPi, making RAD52 an attractive therapeutic target. However, this approach has not been tested in HGSC models of acquired PARPi resistance. Here, we assessed the effects of RAD52 loss in 2 distinct Brca2-deficient mouse models of HGSC with acquired PARPi resistance. RAD52 loss suppressed homologous recombination and single-strand annealing DNA repair activity in both models. Genetic depletion and pharmacologic inhibition of RAD52 restored PARPi sensitivity both in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, RAD52 expression was elevated in a newly derived human model of BRCA2-deficient HGSC with acquired PARPi resistance. In this cell line, RAD52 inhibition synergized with a PARPi. Finally, elevated RAD52 expression was associated with poor survival in patients with HGSC. Collectively, these findings establish RAD52 as a clinically relevant therapeutic vulnerability in multiple models of HGSC with acquired PARPi resistance.

articles.title: Maternal asthma symptom frequency in early adulthood and its association with offspring health.
articles.journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology
articles.authors: Hsu NY, Pelecanos A, Waller M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about whether increasing maternal asthma symptom frequency is associated with adverse childhood health outcomes beyond respiratory and allergic diseases.
METHODS: Data were obtained from a prospective cohort of 3033 mothers and 5768 children in the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (ALSWH) and the Mothers and their Children's Health (MatCH) substudy. Maternal self-reported asthma symptom frequency was classified as never, rarely, sometimes, or often (18-23 years). Childhood health outcomes were maternally reported (mean age 7 years). Models accounted for sibling clustering, were adjusted for maternal and child characteristics, and interactions by child sex were assessed.
RESULTS: Graded associations were observed between maternal asthma symptom frequency and multiple offspring outcomes. The largest effects were for childhood asthma (aOR 3.11, 95% CI 2.16-4.48), chest infections (2.50, 1.82-3.44), parent-reported anxiety (2.37, 1.62-3.48), respiratory allergy (2.21, 1.54-3.15), non-food allergy (2.04, 1.33-3.12), and food intolerance (2.03, 1.28-3.20) among children of mothers reporting asthma symptoms often. Graded relationships were also evident for food allergy and eczema. No robust evidence of effect modification by child sex was observed.
CONCLUSION: Asthma symptom frequency in young women may have long-term implications for the health of their future children. These findings underscore the importance of optimizing asthma management before and throughout the reproductive years.

articles.title: Self-reported bleeding patterns during extended etonogestrel implant use beyond 3 years.
articles.journal: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception
articles.ta: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
articles.authors: Soares JTP, Pereira PDC, Rossi-Elias MRB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe self-reported bleeding patterns among etonogestrel implant users beyond 3 years of use and assess perceived changes compared withthe first 3 years.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study at University State of Campinas, Brazil, among women who continued using the same etonogestrel implant beyond 3 years after insertion. Participants completed a structured questionnaire assessing their usual bleeding characteristics during extended use, including bleeding/spotting episodes per month, bleeding/spotting days per month, and bleeding flow. They also reported perceived changes in these characteristics compared with the first 3 years of use.
RESULTS: We included 153 women. The median age was 32 years (IQR 26-37), and the median body mass index (BMI; kg/m2) was 26.6 (IQR 23.8-30.1). The median duration of implant use was 3.9 years (IQR 3.40-5.08). Amenorrhoea was reported by 24.2%, and the median number of bleeding/spotting episodes and days per month was 1 (IQR 0-2) and 4 (IQR 0-7), respectively. Compared with the first 3 years, 62.7% reported unchanged or fewer bleeding episodes, 62.1% reported unchanged or fewer bleeding days, and 58.8% reported unchanged or reduced bleeding flow.
CONCLUSION: Among women who continuied etonogestrel implant use beyond 3 years, approximately one-quarter reported amenorrhoea, and most perceived no increase in bleeding frequency, duration, or flow compared with the first 3 years. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of the retrospective assessment and potential selection bias.

articles.title: Trends in breast, cervical, and colon cancer incidence and mortality rates in Türkiye: national evaluation of three population-based screening-targeted cancers.
articles.journal: European journal of cancer prevention : the official journal of the European Cancer Prevention Organisation (ECP)
articles.authors: Turan G, Turan M, Başpinar Y et al.
articles.abstract: Breast, cervical, and colon cancer are central to cancer control policy in Türkiye, yet their long-term incidence and mortality trends have not been described with formal trend-segmentation methods. We conducted a population-based Joinpoint regression analysis of age-standardized incidence (2009-2020; registry coverage rising from 23.4 to 50.6%) and mortality (2009-2023) rates for breast, cervical, and colon cancer in Türkiye. We estimated annual percentage change per segment and average APC (AAPC), overall and by age group, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs; in brackets). Breast cancer incidence rose [AAPC: 1.51% (0.14, 2.86)]; mortality rose until 2015 and then leveled off [AAPC: 1.13% (-0.16, 2.44)]. Cervical cancer incidence was stable overall [AAPC: 0.79% (-0.62, 2.18)] but rose at ages 30-49 years [AAPC: 1.99% (0.64, 3.40)], while mortality declined [AAPC: -1.44% (-2.37, -0.51)]. Colon cancer incidence rose in women [AAPC: 1.72% (0.20, 3.02)] and men [AAPC: 2.44% (0.52, 4.05)] mainly during 2009-2012. Colon cancer mortality rose until 2015 and then declined; the overall AAPC was significant in men [0.72% (0.25, 1.28)] but not in women [-0.19% (-0.68, 0.36)]. Cervical cancer mortality declined steadily despite rising incidence among younger women, while breast and colon cancer incidence increased and colon cancer carried a disproportionate mortality burden in men. Because registry coverage roughly doubled, the incidence increases may partly reflect wider coverage and case ascertainment rather than a true national increase. These ecological trends cannot be attributed to a single cause and should be read alongside screening-program coverage and performance.

articles.title: Liquid biopsy for brain tumors.
articles.authors: Nooguru S, McFaline-Figueroa JR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Diagnosis and molecular classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors depend largely on neurosurgical sampling, which may be difficult to obtain and is rarely repeated throughout the disease course. This review examines how liquid biopsy may extend molecular assessment of primary and metastatic CNS tumors beyond the initial tissue specimen.
RECENT FINDINGS: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cell-free DNA can identify diagnostically informative alterations in gliomas, CNS lymphoma, and CNS metastases. Serial sampling can reveal evolving tumor clones and resistance-associated alterations absent from archival tissue. Recent advances in error-corrected sequencing, fragment analysis, and methylation classification broaden the molecular information available from blood and CSF. However, diagnostic yield varies with tumor type, anatomical location, sampling compartment, and assay design, and blood-based detection remains challenging in primary brain tumors.
SUMMARY: Liquid biopsy may complement tissue diagnosis, imaging, and conventional CSF studies, particularly when repeat tissue sampling is impractical. Prospective validation is needed to establish standardized workflows, clarify the interpretation of negative results, and determine whether molecular findings improve treatment selection and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal mortality in the Americas, 2000-2023: an ecological study of temporal trends, socioeconomic inequalities, and progress towards 2030 targets.
articles.authors: Sanhueza A, Soliz P, Martinez O et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality rose sharply during 2019-2021, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic, against a backdrop of already fragile progress in maternal survival across the Americas. We assessed whether the subsequent decline restored sufficient and equitable progress towards the 2030 regional benchmark.
METHODS: We conducted an ecological country-year observational analysis using Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG) estimates for 36 countries and territories, together with the regional series for the Americas, from 2000 to 2023. Temporal trends were assessed using continuous log-linear models with zero to four joinpoints. Social inequalities were quantified using the slope index of inequality (SII), relative index of inequality (RII), and health concentration index (CIx). We also estimated the annual rate of reduction required for each country and territory to reach a maternal mortality ratio (MMR) of 30 per 100,000 live births by 2030. As the principal external comparison of the pandemic-period signal, country-year MMRs officially reported to the Pan American Health Organization were compared with the corresponding MMEIG estimates.
FINDINGS: Regional maternal deaths averaged 9408 annually during 2000-2019, peaked at 14,498 in 2021, and declined to 7813 in 2023. The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) decreased from 70.4 in 2000 to 58.5 in 2023, despite rising from 58.9 in 2019 to 106.8 in 2021. Joinpoints occurred in 2014, 2019, and 2021; the 2000-2023 average annual percentage change was -0.9%. Reaching an MMR of 30 by 2030 would require a 9.6% annual regional reduction. In 2023, the SII was -123.6 (95% CI -181.7 to -65.6), the RII was 9.9 (4.4-22.5), and the CIx was -39.6% (-52.4 to -15.3). These measures describe concentration of MMEIG-estimated mortality among countries at the lower end of the GDP distribution and are not interpreted as independent effects of GDP.
INTERPRETATION: The post-2021 decline is consistent with recovery, but it did not restore an adequate or equitable long-term trajectory. The pandemic-period rise was also evident in many independently reported country series, although its magnitude and timing varied and causal attribution cannot be established from this ecological analysis. Reaching the 2030 benchmark requires sustained acceleration, differentiated country support based on mortality and target gaps, stronger maternal-death surveillance and response, and equitable access to high-quality care.
