articles.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses reveal UTF1-associated spermatogenic dysfunction and identify ACTRT2 and AKAP4 as biomarkers in non-obstructive azoospermia.
articles.authors: Yu J, Li M, Zhou Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe male infertility disorder caused by spermatogenic failure, and UTF1 is critical for maintaining undifferentiated spermatogonia and regulating germ cell development. This study aimed to explore the role of UTF1-related spermatogenic dysfunction in NOA and identify potential diagnostic biomarkers.
METHODS: We integrated NOA transcriptomic datasets with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from Utf1 conditional knockout and normal mouse testes. Bioinformatic analyses and machine learning were applied to screen biomarkers, while functional enrichment, immune infiltration, cell-cell communication, and pseudotime trajectory analyses were performed together with histological validation in Utf1-deficient testes.
RESULTS: Spermatogonia, Sertoli cells, and spermatids were identified as key cell populations. ACTRT2 and AKAP4 were confirmed as consistently downregulated NOA biomarkers and were integrated into a well-calibrated nomogram. These two genes were associated with cytoskeletal remodeling and meiotic regulation. NOA was also characterized by altered immune infiltration and cell-cell communication, whereas Utf1 deficiency impaired testicular development and spermatogenesis.
DISCUSSION: Collectively, UTF1 deficiency was closely associated with spermatogenic dysfunction and microenvironmental remodeling in NOA, while ACTRT2 and AKAP4 might serve as potential diagnostic biomarkers of this process. These findings provide new insights into the molecular basis of NOA and may support future disease stratification and targeted intervention strategies.

articles.title: Health Information Literacy Moderates the Associations of Perceived Social Support with Insomnia and Infertility Psychological Distress in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Jiang L, Wu M, Yao J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Psychological distress is common among women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART). Perceived social support, insomnia, and health information literacy may be interrelated with psychological distress during fertility treatment, but their conditional relationships remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the indirect association between perceived social support and infertility psychological distress through insomnia and whether health information literacy moderated the associations among perceived social support, insomnia, and IPD.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to August 2024, enrolling 1007 women undergoing ART at two tertiary hospitals in Wuhan, China. Standardized instruments, including the Perceived Social Support Scale (PSS), the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), the Everyday Health Information Literacy (HIL) questionnaire, and the Infertility Psychological Distress (IPD) Scale, were utilized for data collection. Mediation and moderated mediation analyses were conducted using PROCESS Models 4 and 59 with 5000 bootstrap samples. Seven prespecified sociodemographic and clinical covariates were included in the analyses.
RESULTS: PSS was negatively associated with IPD (B = -0.364, p < 0.001) and ISI (B = -0.094, p < 0.001). A significant indirect association between PSS and IPD through ISI was observed (indirect effect = -0.132, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.175, -0.094]). HIL significantly moderated the associations between PSS and ISI (B = -0.008, p < 0.001), between PSS and IPD (B = -0.029, p < 0.001), and between ISI and IPD (B = -0.071, p = 0.003). At higher levels of HIL, the negative associations of PSS with ISI and IPD were stronger, whereas the positive association between ISI and IPD was weaker.
CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional study, PSS was indirectly associated with IPD through ISI, and HIL modified the associations among PSS, ISI, and IPD. These findings suggest that social support, sleep problems, and HIL may be usefully considered together in psychosocial assessment during ART. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine the temporal and causal relationships among these factors.

articles.title: Pharmacists and Allied Health Professionals in Fertility Care: Rural Patient Perspectives.
articles.authors: Mackay A, Taylor S, Anderson E et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pharmacists and allied health professionals (AHPs) provide fertility care to support patients' wellbeing and chances of conception. However, their endeavors as members of a fertility care team are not always integrated. Rural and remote people experiencing fertility challenges face many barriers to accessing fertility care, including awareness of, and access to AHP services and fertility medications. Therefore, the aim of this study is to explore rural patients' perspectives of pharmacists and AHPs providing fertility care services and their views of a "fertility care team" approach.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Twenty-one persons 18 years or older who were assigned female at birth and had accessed fertility care while living in a rural or remote location in Queensland, Australia participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed thematically following the Braun and Clarke method, with inductively derived themes coded and aligned to the six domains of the Canadian Interprofessional Health Collaborative Competency Framework for Advancing Collaboration.
RESULTS: Six themes were developed, supported by 14 subthemes. Themes included relationship-focused fertility care, communication, role clarification, team functioning, disagreements and differences, and collaborative leadership in the fertility care team. The themes and subthemes outlined potential improvements to both the fertility care interprofessional approach and access to quality pharmacy and AHP fertility care services for those living in rural areas.
CONCLUSION: Findings indicate that although pharmacists and AHPs are involved in fertility care, there is currently little evidence of an AHP interprofessional approach in rural areas, with those experiencing fertility challenges often managing their own overall care. Participants recommended fertility care specific education for rural health professionals to improve their fertility care knowledge and skills. Future research should therefore explore the educational needs of pharmacists and AHPs in rural settings to strengthen accessible, high quality and local fertility care, reducing barriers to treatment and increasing support.

articles.title: Efficient Plasma and Placenta Metabolic Fingerprints for Preeclampsia Diagnosis: A Multicenter Study.
articles.authors: Xu Y, Liu Y, Xu K et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal mortality. There remains a clinical need for accurate and accessible diagnostic approaches to facilitate timely identification of PE. Herein, the nanoparticle-enhanced laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry is applied to obtain plasma (n = 236) and placenta (n = 70) metabolic fingerprints from a multicenter dataset (109 PE patients and 127 non-PE participants, 4 centers). Diagnostic models are constructed with an efficient diagnostic area under the curve (AUC) of 0.941 with external validation. Subsequently, 19 PE-associated metabolites are annotated, demonstrating good diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.871. Moreover, diagnostic scores of severe PE patients are significantly higher than those of PE patients, exhibiting our model's capacity to differentiate disease severity. Related metabolic pathways are revealed to inform potential therapeutic strategies for PE and biological validation on trophoblast cells demonstrates that key biomarkers, including L-alanine, taurine, hypoxanthine, and orotic acid, can significantly enhance migration capabilities (p < 0.01). This work highlights the potential of metabolic analysis for PE detection, paving the way for improved clinical decision-making in obstetrics.

articles.title: Management of Vasomotor Symptoms in Women With Breast Cancer: From Pathophysiology to the Emerging Role of Neurokinin Receptor Antagonism.
articles.authors: Bimpa K, Emmanouil V, Xydias EM et al.
articles.abstract: Vasomotor symptoms (VMS), encompassing hot flashes and night sweats, are among the most frequent and disruptive consequences of estrogen withdrawal in women with breast cancer. In this population, menopause may occur naturally or in association with cancer treatment, while the use of menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is limited by concerns regarding oncological safety. The present narrative review synthesizes current understanding of the neuroendocrine pathophysiology of vasomotor symptoms, centered on the hypertrophy and hyperactivity of hypothalamic neurons co-expressing kisspeptin, neurokinin B (NKB), and dynorphin (KNDy) following estrogen deprivation, and critically appraises the available non-hormonal management options, including selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, oxybutynin, and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Particular emphasis is placed on the neurokinin receptor antagonists, a mechanistically targeted drug class that acts on the thermoregulatory pathways involved in VMS. Fezolinetant is a selective neurokinin-3 receptor antagonist evaluated in the SKYLIGHT program, while elinzanetant is a dual neurokinin-1 and neurokinin-3 receptor antagonist evaluated in the OASIS program, including a pivotal placebo-controlled trial in women experiencing vasomotor symptoms associated with endocrine therapy for breast cancer. Dedicated studies of fezolinetant in women with breast cancer are ongoing. Neurokinin receptor antagonism represents a promising non-hormonal therapeutic strategy for VMS in this population, although agent-specific safety considerations and the need for longer-term oncological safety data require further evaluation.

articles.title: The Effect of Counseling Based on Watson's Human Caring Theory (HCT) on Reproductive Concerns in Women Diagnosed With Cancer: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Altintas RY, Kavlak O, Goktepe B
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite advances in cancer treatments, fertility loss remains a significant psychological burden, and counseling is often inadequate. This study aimed to examine the effect of counseling based on Watson's Human Caring Theory (HCT) on reproductive concerns and patient satisfaction in women diagnosed with cancer.
METHODS: This outcome assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted between October 2023 and September 2024 with 50 women aged 18-45 years diagnosed with cancer, who were randomly allocated to the intervention group (n = 25) or the control group (n = 25). A pre-test, mid-test, and post-test design was applied to the intervention group, while a pre-test and post-test design was applied to the control group. The intervention group received three sessions of counseling based on Watson's Human Caring Theory, whereas the control group received routine care, consisting of a single session of fertility counseling provided at the study center. Data were collected using a descriptive information form, the Reproductive Concerns After Cancer (RCAC) Scale, and the Patient Satisfaction Evaluation Form Based on Watson's Processes of Healing.
RESULTS: At post-test, the intervention group had significantly lower scores than the control group on the total RCAC score (Cohen's d = 0.74) and on the Child Health and Future Concerns and Acceptance Concerns subscales, whereas no significant between group differences were observed for the Fertility and Partner Relationship Concerns and Pregnancy Concern subscales. Participants in the intervention group reported uniformly high patient satisfaction scores; however, interpretation of this outcome is limited by ceiling effects and the restricted discriminative capacity of the measure. These findings were further contextualized through a descriptive summary of participants' open-ended feedback, which highlighted recurring topics of emotional relief, informed decision-making, and practical coping.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-centre trial, counseling based on Watson's Human Caring Theory was associated with lower reproductive concerns in women diagnosed with cancer. Although satisfaction scores in the intervention group were uniformly high, this outcome should be interpreted with caution given the ceiling effect and the limited discriminative capacity of the measure. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger, multicentre trials with longer follow-up.

articles.title: Residual ploidy abnormalities after preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy.
articles.authors: Hatakeyama S, Shirai A, Yamashiro E et al.
articles.abstract: Next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) is widely used for embryo selection, but conventional copy number-based analysis may fail to detect whole-genome ploidy abnormalities such as haploidy and triploidy. This retrospective study evaluated the frequency of residual ploidy abnormalities detected by single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based analysis among embryos reported as euploid or mosaic by NGS-based PGT-A. Between May 2022 and January 2025, 5983 blastocysts underwent NGS-based PGT-A at Sugiyama Clinic. Of these, 1601 embryos reported as euploid or mosaic were subjected to additional SNP-based ploidy analysis. SNP-based results were classified as diploid, haploid, triploid, or uncertain. Among the 1601 embryos analysed, 1550 (96.8%) were classified as diploid, 4 (0.3%) as haploid, 11 (0.7%) as triploid and 36 (2.2%) as uncertain. The overall frequency of whole-genome ploidy abnormalities was 0.9% (15/1601). Among the 11 triploid embryos, 4 were derived from intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) and 7 from conventional in vitro fertilization. All haploid and triploid embryos derived from ICSI showed second polar body extrusion on retrospective time-lapse review. These findings indicate that a small but measurable proportion of embryos reported as euploid or mosaic by NGS-based PGT-A have whole-genome ploidy abnormalities detectable by SNP-based analysis. SNP-based ploidy assessment may provide complementary information in selected clinical workflows.

articles.title: A validated low-abundance uterine microbial signature associated with chronic endometritis.
articles.authors: Ha S, Lv C, Cui J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic endometritis (CE) is a persistent inflammatory endometrial disorder associated with infertility, recurrent implantation failure, and pregnancy loss. While previous microbiome studies have focused on Lactobacillus depletion and common genital tract bacteria, low-abundance microbial lineages remain poorly characterised.
OBJECTIVE: To identify reproducible low-abundance microbial signatures associated with CE and evaluate their robustness through external validation and complementary analyses.
METHODS: Uterine lavage specimens from infertile women with CE (n = 29) and non-CE controls (n = 16) were analysed by 16S rRNA sequencing in a discovery cohort. An independent cohort of 58 participants was used for external validation. CE was diagnosed by hysteroscopy and CD138 immunohistochemistry (≥5 stromal plasma cells/10 high-power fields). Multiple negative controls were included, and contaminants were assessed using decontam. Prespecified analyses included cervicovaginal source tracking, shotgun metagenomics in a subset, cytokine profiling, and post-treatment follow-up.
RESULTS: CE samples exhibited increased richness and modestly higher diversity. Presence/absence-based beta diversity demonstrated clearer separation between CE and controls. CE was associated with enrichment of Patescibacteria, Planctomycetota, Bdellovibrionota, and selected archaeal-lineage signals. After contaminant filtering, major rare-lineage features remained enriched. Patescibacteria and Bdellovibrio-related signals correlated with CD138-positive plasma-cell counts and inflammatory cytokines. A nested discovery model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.84, and the locked marker panel achieved an AUC of 0.81 in external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: CE is associated with a reproducible low-abundance microbial signature in uterine lavage samples. These findings highlight candidate microbial lineages for further investigation but do not establish causality or uterine residency.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Poor Perinatal Mental Health in Women With and Without Gestational Diabetes: Data From a Large Multi-Ethnic Cohort.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Ohene-Agyei P, Gamble GD, Tran T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are common during the perinatal period and women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) may be at greater risk than the general pregnant population.
AIM: We assessed if factors associated with symptoms of anxiety, depression and poor mental health-related quality of life (HRQoL) differed between women with and without GDM.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prospective cohort study of participants from the GEMS Trial. Participants completed questionnaires screening for anxiety, depression or HRQoL at enrolment, 36 weeks' gestation and 6 months postpartum. Potential associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression for each questionnaire at each timepoint.
RESULTS: Of 4061 participants, 433 (10.7%) were diagnosed with GDM. At enrolment, non-European ethnicity, obesity, maternal age and previous perinatal death were associated with symptoms of poor mental health (above threshold for any questionnaire) in the overall cohort. Among women with GDM, Other ethnicity (not European, Māori, Pacific or Asian) was associated with increased risk for poor mental health, while Pacific ethnicity was most often associated with poor mental health in women without GDM. Women with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) had a greater risk for poor mental health at baseline in both groups, but only in women without GDM in late gestation. Older age (≥ 40 years) was associated with poor mental health among women with GDM, and younger age (< 30 years) among women without GDM.
CONCLUSION: Non-European ethnicity, obesity and maternal age are associated with poor mental health, but at different time points and different magnitudes of risk in women with and without GDM.

articles.title: Classical Caesarean Section: Maternal and Foetal Outcomes at a Tertiary Centre in New Zealand.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Shekar P, Ormandy J
articles.abstract: Classical caesarean section (CCS) remains an uncommon but important procedure in obstetrics. We performed a retrospective review of all CCSs at Wellington Regional Hospital between January 2019 and December 2023. 109 CCSs were performed, representing 1.8% of all caesarean sections (n = 5913) and 0.7% of all births (n = 16646). Most (58.7%) were performed before 28 weeks' gestation, with an unformed lower uterine segment being the most common reason for performing a classical incision. Maternal morbidity and foetal mortality were closely linked to underlying conditions prompting delivery. These findings provide contemporary data to support clinical decision-making and patient counselling regarding CCS.

articles.title: Maternal and perinatal factors associated with cord blood thyroid-stimulating hormone levels: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Murugiah V, Jinna MA, Thankamoni RK et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Congenital hypothyroidism (CH) is the most common preventable cause of intellectual disability in children. Umbilical cord blood thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is used for neonatal screening, but maternal and perinatal influences on cord blood TSH remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify maternal and perinatal factors associated with cord blood TSH levels.
METHODS: A descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,088 consecutive live births at a tertiary hospital in South India (January-December 2022). Cord blood samples were analyzed for TSH using an electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. Maternal and neonatal characteristics were recorded, and associations with cord blood TSH were assessed. Neonates with cord blood TSH >20 μIU/mL were recalled for confirmatory serum thyroid function testing.
RESULTS: The median cord blood TSH was 7.22 μIU/mL, with an interquartile range of 5.39-10.28. Elevated cord blood TSH (>20 μIU/mL) was found in 5.9% of neonates. In unadjusted analyses, higher TSH levels were associated with primiparity, gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, vaginal delivery, assisted delivery, and lower Apgar scores (P<0.05). Maternal TSH was positively correlated with cord blood TSH (r=0.193, P=0.002). No associations were observed with neonatal sex, gestational age, birth weight, or maternal anemia. Cord blood TSH showed modest positive correlations with postnatal day-3 serum TSH and free thyroxine.
CONCLUSION: Maternal thyroid status, parity, pregnancy complications, and mode of delivery are significantly associated with cord blood TSH. These factors should be considered when interpreting neonatal screening results for CH.

articles.title: Contemporary age at menarche among Thai girls: a nationwide cross-sectional study and its public health implications.
articles.authors: Rukumnuaykit P, Srilanchakon K, Kwanyou A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Age at menarche has declined globally. However, contemporary population-level data from Southeast Asia remain limited. This study aimed to characterize menarcheal timing among Thai schoolgirls and identify associated factors using survival-based methods.
METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted among 8,161 Thai schoolgirls in grades 3-9. Menarcheal status and age at menarche were assessed using questionnaires and verified by caregivers. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to estimate the cumulative probability of menarche by age, accounting for right-censoring. Determinants of menarcheal timing were examined using Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: At assessment, 52.6% of participants had attained menarche. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that the cumulative probability of menarche rose from 5.56% at 10 years to 85.21% at 13 years, with a median age of 12.0 years (interquartile range, 11.2-12.7 years). Based on survival-derived percentiles, early menarche (approximately <5th percentile) was defined as occurring before 10 years of age. Significant regional differences in menarcheal timing were observed (log-rank test, P<0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, overweight (hazard ratio [HR], 1.67), obesity (HR, 1.64), and high socioeconomic status (HR, 1.28) were independently associated with earlier menarche, whereas underweight status was associated with delayed menarche (HR, 0.45; all P<0.001). After adjustment, only the Southern region remained significantly associated with later menarche compared with Bangkok.
CONCLUSION: Nutritional status and socioeconomic factors are key factors associated with menarcheal timing in Thailand. Survival-based, percentile-defined thresholds provide a useful framework for identifying atypical pubertal timing and may inform population-level public health strategies.

articles.title: Therapeutic Landscape of Folate Receptor-α Targeting: Platforms, Progress, and Clinical Translation.
articles.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
articles.authors: Dey A, Doshi MB, Raul SS et al.
articles.abstract: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) has emerged as a clinically relevant tumor-associated antigen, given its limited distribution in normal epithelial tissues and overexpression in diverse malignancies, including ovarian, endometrial, triple-negative breast cancer, and non-small cell lung cancers. This expression profile has established FRα as a compelling target for immunotherapeutic strategies. Different targeting modalities are under active investigation, ranging from monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to T-cell-redirecting bispecific engagers, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell approaches, biparatopic ADCs and peptide vaccines, each demonstrating promising preclinical and clinical activity. Notably, the ADC mirvetuximab soravtansine has achieved regulatory approval for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, marking a significant milestone in FRα-targeted therapy. Here, we review the biological significance and characteristics of FRα as a promising and now established therapeutic target. This review consolidates current evidence on FRα-targeted immunotherapies from budding therapies to key established ones, highlighting their mechanisms, clinical outcomes across different cancers, and key challenges encountered during development. By synthesizing clinical and translational insights, this review uniquely addresses the gap by bringing together major FRα-targeted strategies within a single framework, positioning clinical trials as the organizing backbone while integrating biological and engineering insights to explain observed outcomes of FRα as both a biomarker and a therapeutic axis in oncology.

articles.title: Molecular Determinants of Treatment Resistance in Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review and Integrative Bioinformatic Analysis of Publicly Available Datasets.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.authors: Bereza K, Kukiełka A, Trojnarska D et al.
articles.abstract: Treatment resistance remains a major challenge in cervical cancer management, particularly among patients undergoing chemoradiotherapy. Despite increasing knowledge of resistance-associated molecular pathways, clinically validated biomarkers capable of predicting treatment outcomes remain limited. This study combined a systematic review of clinical and preclinical studies with an integrative bioinformatic analysis of publicly available transcriptomic datasets. Gene expression profiles from cervical cancer models exposed to chemotherapeutic agents and epigenetic modulators were analyzed to identify treatment-response-associated transcriptional signatures. Candidate genes were subsequently evaluated in clinical datasets comprising normal cervical tissue, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, and invasive cervical cancer. Functional enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction network construction, and survival analyses were performed to assess biological relevance. A total of 38 genes demonstrated concordant expression changes across independent treatment conditions. Clinical evaluation revealed progressive dysregulation of several candidates during cervical neoplastic progression and invasive disease development. Functional analyses indicated enrichment of pathways related to extracellular matrix organization, metabolic regulation, and p53-associated signaling. Network analysis identified lumican (LUM) as a candidate gene occupying a relatively high connectivity within the constructed interaction network. No statistically significant association between LUM expression and overall survival was observed. This integrative approach identified reproducible treatment-response-associated transcriptional signatures that may participate in biological processes relevant to therapeutic adaptation in cervical cancer. LUM emerged as a prioritized candidate for future investigation. However, its biological and clinical significance remains exploratory and requires validation in independent treatment-annotated cohorts and functional studies.

articles.title: Comparison of direct versus hysteroscopy-assisted levonorgestrel intrauterine system placement after high-intensity focused ultrasound ablation for adenomyosis: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
articles.authors: Ding K, Tian C, Zhu Q et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare LNG-IUS stability, clinical outcomes, and safety after direct versus hysteroscopy-assisted placement following high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation for adenomyosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 229 premenopausal patients with adenomyosis who underwent HIFU ablation and attempted LNG-IUS placement (direct, n = 135; hysteroscopy-assisted, n = 94). Post-placement outcomes were evaluated among patients with successful first-attempt placement and included LNG-IUS-related events, treatment continuation, symptom scores, lesion volume, and adverse events. Event-free survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression, with propensity score matching as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: First-attempt placement succeeded in 135 of 135 direct and 91 of 94 hysteroscopy-assisted patients. LNG-IUS-related events were less frequent with hysteroscopy-assisted placement (7.69% vs. 25.93%; p < 0.001), and treatment continuation at last follow-up was higher (92.31% vs. 74.07%; p < 0.001). Event risk remained lower with hysteroscopy-assisted placement before and after adjustment (HR = 0.393, 95% CI 0.173-0.891, p = 0.025; adjusted HR = 0.396, 95% CI 0.158-0.996, p = 0.049). Propensity score matching showed a similar but less precise association (HR = 0.265, 95% CI 0.070-1.002; p = 0.050). Symptom scores and lesion volume decreased in both groups, with no significant between-group difference in adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: Hysteroscopy-assisted LNG-IUS placement after HIFU may be associated with fewer displacement or expulsion events and a higher rate of treatment continuation than direct placement. Symptom improvement and recorded adverse events were similar between groups. It may be considered for selected patients with suspected residual intrauterine necrotic tissue or unfavorable uterine cavity conditions.

articles.title: UHRF1 Supports PARP1 Protein Stability and Ovarian Cancer Progression by Limiting PARP1 Polyubiquitination.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Wu L, Kang J et al.
articles.abstract: Ubiquitin-like with PHD and RING finger domains 1 (UHRF1) is an epigenetic regulator with oncogenic activity, but its role in PARP1 protein homeostasis in ovarian cancer remains unclear. We assessed UHRF1 expression in public datasets and clinical specimens, tested UHRF1 depletion in ovarian cancer cells and mouse models, and examined UHRF1-PARP1 association, protein turnover, ubiquitination, and rescue. UHRF1 was elevated in ovarian tumor samples, and high expression was associated with adverse outcomes in the institutional tissue-microarray cohort. UHRF1 depletion reduced cell growth and migration, increased apoptosis, and reduced endpoint xenograft weight and volume. UHRF1 is associated with PARP1; its depletion reduced PARP1 protein without changing its mRNA, shortened its apparent half-life, and increased total PARP1-associated polyubiquitin. Re-expression of full-length UHRF1, but less effectively the TTD-deletion construct, restored PARP1 association and stability. In separate experiments, RNF4-targeting siRNA attenuated PARP1 loss and ubiquitination associated with UHRF1 depletion. Together, these findings identify UHRF1 as a regulator of PARP1 protein stability in ovarian cancer models and support contributions of the TTD-containing region and RNF4 to this regulation.

articles.title: A Community Engaged Feasibility Study of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling for Cervical Cancer Screening in Sexual and Gender Minority People.
articles.authors: Aleshire M, Tinman JS, Combs R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: We investigated the acceptability and feasibility of at-home self-sampling cervical cancer screening (CCS) for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) in sexual and gender minority (SGM) Kentuckians.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive qualitative study using virtual interviews to investigate socioecological factors influencing CCS and the feasibility and acceptability of at-home hrHPV self-sampling for primary CCS. Criterion and snowball sampling were used. Data were analyzed using a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic approach and team member consensus to identify salient themes.
RESULTS: Nineteen participants completed hrHPV self-sampling and qualitative interviews in 2022-2023. The 6 overarching themes identified were cervical cancer screening perceptions, prior negative healthcare experiences, desirability of hrHPV self-sampling, completing hrHPV self-sampling, concerns about hrHPV self-sampling, and reasons for study participation.
CONCLUSION: At-home hrHPV self-sampling is a promising intervention to increase CCS in SGM people. Individuals should be reassured that self-sampling is an effective method for primary CCS and that they are likely to be able to collect a sample that will yield accurate results. To maximize the possibility of CCS completion by SGM individuals, healthcare providers and healthcare environments must be affirming, culturally competent, and informed partners throughout the CCS process.

articles.title: Gestational age-associated differences in human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells: biological, paracrine, and neuroprotective properties.
articles.authors: Peng X, Zhang Y, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (UCMSCs) have shown considerable therapeutic promise for neonatal brain injury. However, whether gestational age influences UCMSC biological characteristics and therapeutic efficacy remains unclear. This study investigated the potential functional and molecular differences between UCMSCs derived from preterm and full-term infants to inform future autologous and allogeneic cell-based therapies.
METHODS: UCMSCs were isolated from full-term and preterm umbilical cords, with preterm samples further classified into uncomplicated preterm (N-P), gestational diabetes exposure (P-GD), and severe preeclampsia exposure (P-SE) groups. MSC identity, viability, proliferation, apoptosis, trilineage differentiation, and extracellular vesicle (EV) characteristics were evaluated. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to compare N-P and full-term (N-F) UCMSCs, followed by RT-PCR validation of key hub genes. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in a neonatal germinal matrix hemorrhage (GMH) mouse model following intranasal administration of N-F- or N-P-derived UCMSCs, with neurological function and brain injury evaluated by behavioral testing and T2-weighted MRI.
RESULTS: All UCMSCs met standard MSC characterixation criteria. Compared with N-F UCMSCs, N-P UCMSCs showed increased cell viability as assessed by CCK-8, enhanced chondrogenic differentiation potential, and increased secretion of EVs expressing CD9, CD63, and CD81. In contrast, UCMSCs from the P-GD and P-SE groups displayed reduced proliferative and differentiation capacities. Transcriptomic analysis identified 631 differentially expressed genes between N-P and N-F UCMSCs, with significant enrichment of pathways involved in cell proliferation, differentiation, and EV biology. Network analysis identified CTNNB1 and SRC as key hub genes, and RT-qPCR confirmed differential expression of representative hub genes. In the neonatal GMH model, both N-F- and N-P-derived UCMSCs significantly improved behavioral outcomes and reduced brain injury compared with untreated GMH mice. Although N-P-derived UCMSCs showed a trend toward greater therapeutic benefit, no statistically significant difference was observed between the two treatment groups.
CONCLUSION: Healthy preterm UCMSCs display distinct biological and paracrine-related properties while retaining neuroprotective effects comparable to that of full-term UCMSCs. In contrast, adverse intrauterine conditions, including…

articles.title: Early-onset gestational diabetes mellitus and secondary maternal and neonatal complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Mei G, Gan J, Xia Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-onset gestational diabetes mellitus (eGDM) is a distinct phenotype with insulin resistance and adverse metabolic profiles, but its association with secondary maternal and neonatal complications remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate this association compared with late-onset GDM (LGDM).
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched up to April 20, 2026. Observational studies and secondary analyses of randomised controlled trials comparing eGDM with LGDM were included. Outcomes comprised hypertensive disorders, postpartum haemorrhage, stillbirth, congenital malformations, small for gestational age (SGA), macrosomia, respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), shoulder dystocia, and neonatal hypoglycaemia. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Thirty-two studies (113,889 pregnancies) were included. eGDM was associated with higher odds of hypertensive disorders (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.10-1.69) and stillbirth (OR 2.63, 95% CI 1.75-3.95). No significant associations were observed for congenital malformations, SGA, macrosomia, RDS, shoulder dystocia, or neonatal hypoglycaemia. Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes (I² 55.7%-75.0%). GRADE certainty was moderate for stillbirth and SGA, and low for others.
CONCLUSIONS: eGDM is associated with higher odds of gestational hypertension/preeclampsia and stillbirth compared with LGDM, but not with most other secondary complications. The lack of standardized diagnostic criteria across studies warrants cautious interpretation. These findings support early risk-stratified screening in high-risk women and intensified antenatal surveillance, including blood pressure monitoring and fetal assessment.

articles.title: Intimate partner violence and covert contraception use among Ugandan women: a cross-sectional inquiry.
articles.authors: Heck CJ, Wu K, Nakawooya H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is prevalent globally, adversely impacting women's health and autonomy. Covert contraceptive use (CCU), using contraception without a partner's knowledge, may arise in response to IPV and restrictive gender norms. This study examines associations between verbal, physical, and sexual IPV and CCU among Ugandan women, providing insight into the socio-cultural dynamics influencing reproductive health choices.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis using data from the 2011-2013 Rakai Community Cohort Survey, which collected demographic, reproductive, and IPV-related data from women in South-Central Uganda. We included women who reported (1) ever having sex, (2) no current pregnancies, and (3) current use of contraception, including intra-uterine devices, pills, injectables, or implants. Adjusted prevalence ratios (APR) and 95% Confidence Intervals (CI) were estimated using Poisson regression, adjusting for age, education, marital status, HIV status, alcohol use, and other confounders.
RESULTS: Among 2,094 women, 27%, 21%, and 12% respectively survived verbal, physical, and sexual IPV, and 26% practiced CCU. Positive IPV-CCU associations arose for physical IPV (APR = 1.39, CI = 1.17-1.65) and verbal IPV (APR = 1.30, CI = 1.12-1.52), whereas sexual IPV's association was marginally significant (APR = 1.22, CI = 0.99-1.49).
CONCLUSIONS: IPV may influence women's choices about contraception and/or women's use of contraception may precipitate IPV. Integrating efforts to prevent IPV and provide contraception are needed to better serve women.

articles.title: Mapping the network structure of dysmenorrhea-related somatic symptoms and their determinants among adolescents.
articles.authors: Liu H, Qian F, Hu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study investigated factors associated with dysmenorrhea-related somatic symptoms in adolescent girls, stratified by self-reported mental disorder diagnoses.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 1,529 Chinese female students aged 10 to 19 years from middle and secondary schools. A self-reported questionnaire was used to assess the multidimensional manifestations of dysmenorrhea-related somatic symptoms, menstrual characteristics, and psychological and behavioral factors. Network analysis was used to examine interrelationships among somatic symptoms and their correlates in adolescent girls with and without self-reported mental disorder diagnoses.
RESULTS: Of the 1,529 girls, 162 (10.6%) reported a history of at least one mental disorder diagnosis. Among adolescent girls with self-reported mental disorder diagnoses, back/leg pain and dizziness had the highest strength centrality. The presence of dysmenorrhea-related somatic symptoms showed conditional associations with the frequency of dysmenorrhea, anxiety, depression, disappointment, analgesic use, and thermal therapy. Among girls without a mental disorder diagnosis, dizziness and nausea had the highest strength centrality. The severity of dysmenorrhea, hormonal medication use, anxiety, and depressive symptoms were associated with the overall somatic-symptom node. The frequency and severity of dysmenorrhea also showed conditional associations with specific somatic symptoms. For those with mental disorder diagnoses, thermal therapy and analgesic use were associated with most somatic symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported anxiety and depressive symptoms were associated with dysmenorrhea-related somatic symptoms. Thermal therapy and analgesic use were also associated with dysmenorrhea frequency and pain severity among adolescents with self-reported mental disorder diagnoses. Future longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the relationships among psychological distress, coping behaviors, and dysmenorrhea.

articles.title: Do physiotherapy students know enough about the pelvic floor? The impact of university education: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Eroglu HS, Demirtaş A, Demirtaş G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary incontinence (UI) significantly affects quality of life, and physiotherapists play a key role in its conservative management. This study aimed to assess the knowledge levels of physiotherapy and rehabilitation students in Türkiye regarding UI, pelvic floor health, and pelvic organ prolapse, and to identify factors influencing their knowledge.
METHODS: A multi-centred, cross-sectional survey was conducted between November 2022 and November 2023 among undergraduate physiotherapy students from 21 universities. Participants completed validated tools, including the Incontinence Quiz, Pelvic Floor Health Knowledge Quiz, and Prolapse and Incontinence Knowledge Questionnaire. Data were analysed using non-parametric tests, including Spearman correlation to assess relationships between variables.
RESULTS: A total of 437 students participated. Fourth-year students demonstrated significantly higher knowledge scores compared to lower-year students (p < 0.001). Students who had received specific UI education scored significantly better across all questionnaires (p < 0.001). Female students outperformed male students in pelvic floor health and prolapse knowledge assessments (p < 0.001). However, only 3.7% of students reported clinical experience with UI patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Although knowledge levels improved progressively with academic advancement and targeted education, significant gaps remain, particularly in early academic years and clinical exposure. Structured and progressive integration of UI education within physiotherapy curricula is recommended. Future research should explore the impact of educational interventions on both theoretical knowledge and clinical competencies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05702164, registered on 27 January 2023, retrospectively registered. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT05702164 .

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes burden, inequalities, and epidemiological patterns among postmenopausal women, 1990-2021: a global ecological modelling study.
articles.authors: Yao L, Ji Y, Fan W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major global cause of mortality and morbidity globally. Postmenopausal women bear a disproportionately high burden due to the intertwined effects of aging, biological changes, and structural disadvantages. This study aims to assess the global burden, temporal trends, health inequalities, associated risks and divergent epidemiological patterns of T2DM among this population.
METHODS: Data regarding the incidence and mortality rate of T2DM in postmenopausal women were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. Women aged ≥ 55 years were used as an age-based operational proxy for postmenopausal status. Temporal trends were assessed using estimated annual percent changes (EAPC). We applied several machine learning methods, including K-means and hierarchical clustering, ensemble tree-based models (Random Forest and XG Boost) with SHAP analysis to assess the divergent burden and risk profiles and among postmenopausal women globally.
RESULTS: Globally, the incidence rate of T2DM among postmenopausal women increased by 1.40% per year (95% CI 1.35-1.44) since 1990, reaching nearly 600 cases per 100,000 population in 2021. Marked health inequalities persisted, with substantially higher mortality burdens observed in lower-SDI (Sociodemographic index) countries. Three distinct disease patterns were identified: 83 countries, primarily in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, the USA, and Russia, showed a high and rapidly increasing pattern, whereas 33 countries, mainly small island developing states, had the highest incidence rates but relatively stable trends. Three risk profiles were also observed, with Western dietary risks and high LDL cholesterol more prevalent in higher-SDI countries, while high sodium intake and low fruit consumption predominated in Asian and African countries. Trend-based projections suggested continued increases in T2DM incidence rates globally, with persistent inequalities.
CONCLUSIONS: Postmenopausal women face a substantial and growing T2DM burden, marked by pronounced geographic and socioeconomic inequities and heterogeneous risk patterns. These findings underscore the need to move beyond one-size-fits-all strategies toward tailored prevention and healthcare strategies.

articles.title: Mental health outcomes after severe pregnancy complications: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Blackman A, Li A, Shapiro GD et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum mental health issues such as postpartum depression, anxiety and psychosis currently affect up to 17% of women globally. Pregnancy complications including severe maternal morbidity, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and obstetric hemorrhage can be traumatic events that lead to increased risk of postpartum mental illness. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on associations between maternal pregnancy complications including severe maternal morbidity, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and obstetric hemorrhage comorbidly with peripartum mental health outcomes.
METHODS: Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, PsycInfo, and CINAHL (inception-August 2025) for studies comparing mental health outcomes (depression, post-traumatic stress disorder, anxiety, psychosis, suicidality, substance use) in individuals with vs. without pregnancy complications. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted where feasible (I²<80%).
RESULTS: Of 4,188 records initially identified, 79 studies (68.1 million participants) were included in this review. Meta-analyses of up to six studies showed greater odds of postpartum depression following hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (OR = 1.72, 95% confidence interval 1.27-2.32) and obstetric hemorrhage (OR = 1.73, 95% confidence interval 1.27-2.39). Associations between composite severe maternal morbidity and depression were inconsistent. Evidence suggested possible associations between composite severe maternal morbidity and post-traumatic stress disorder, but findings varied across studies. Significant statistical heterogeneity and insufficient studies prevented meta-analyses of studies examining anxiety disorders, substance abuse, suicidality or psychosis, as well as depression and PTSD, in some cases.
CONCLUSION: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and obstetric hemorrhage are associated with increased odds of postpartum depression, while composite severe maternal morbidity shows variable associations with perinatal mental illness. Harmonized outcome definitions and further comprehensive research designs that include the consideration of severe psychiatric outcomes are needed to better understand mental health after severe pregnancy complications.

articles.title: The world health organization's labour care guide's knowledge, usability, acceptability, and practicability among midwives in selected health facilities in Enugu State, Nigeria: a pilot feasibility assessment study.
articles.authors: Chikeme PC, Chinonso UC, Abonyi EO et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Partographs have been used for nearly 50 years to assess labour progress, although their accuracy has been questioned. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended the Labour Care Guide (LCG) as a more robust tool for improving the quality of labour monitoring. This pilot feasibility study aimed to assess the knowledge, usability, acceptability, and practicability of the WHO Labour Care Guide (LCG) among midwives who were early adopters of the guide in selected health facilities in Enugu State, Nigeria.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted between April and July 2024. A total of 43 midwives working in labour wards were purposively selected from three hospitals: Poly General Hospital, Asata; Mother of Christ Specialist Hospital, Holy Ghost; and the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Ituku-Ozalla. Data were collected using a validated, self-developed instrument for demographic characteristics and an adapted questionnaire. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, while Fisher's exact test was used to test the study hypothesis at a 0.05 level of significance using SPSS version 25.
RESULTS: A total of 43 midwives participated in the study. Overall, 67.4% demonstrated good knowledge of the WHO Labour Care Guide; the prevalence of LCG use was 58.1%; usability was rated high by 96.0% of users; acceptability was 69.8% among all midwives and 100% among those who were aware of the LCG; and practicability was rated high by 33.3% of those who were aware of the guide. The usability of the LCG was not significantly associated with the midwives' educational qualifications (p = 0.917), and knowledge of the LCG was not significantly associated with years of professional experience.
CONCLUSIONS: Midwives demonstrated high levels of knowledge and acceptability of the WHO Labour Care Guide (LCG). Although the prevalence of LCG use was moderate, its usability was rated highly. However, practicability was perceived to be low, suggesting that challenges remain in the routine implementation of the LCG in clinical practice. As this was a pilot feasibility study involving early adopters of the WHO LCG, the findings should be interpreted with caution and should not be considered representative of all midwives in Enugu State, Nigeria. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that training, awareness campaigns, and institutional support may help address implementation challenges, facilitate broader adoption of the LCG, and ultimately…

articles.title: Trial of vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC): external validation of the Polish prediction indices of the VBAC.
articles.authors: Paruszewski S, Urban A, Dobrowolska-Redo A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC) is a safe option for both mothers and children. Currently available prediction tools have not been validated in the Polish population. Dobrowolska-Redo proposed a model for predicting VBAC success, and the aim of this study was to evaluate its clinical utility.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis of data collected from 462 pregnant women with a history of one previous cesarean section, all qualified for a VBAC attempt. Deliveries occurred between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2023, at the II Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Medical University of Warsaw. Inclusion criteria were: previous low transverse cesarean section, singleton pregnancy, no indication for elective cesarean delivery, and live birth. Ethical approval was granted by the local committee (reference no. AKBE/300/2024). The data were anonymized before analysis.
RESULTS: Among the cohort of 462 women, 271 (58.7%) had successful VBAC, whereas 191 (41.3%) underwent intrapartum cesarean section. The prediction model for preterm births (pTi) showed no clinical utility. The median Ti score differed significantly between the VBAC group and the cesarean group. Removing two parameters (manual labor and place of residence) improved model performance. Higher BMI increased the likelihood of cesarean delivery, both before pregnancy (23.43 vs. 24.54 kg/m²; p = 0.006) and at delivery (27.99 vs. 29.36 kg/m²; p = 0.007). Prior vaginal birth was a strong predictor of successful VBAC (31.5% vs. 11.2%; p = 0.000), as was a history of fetal macrosomia (15.5% vs. 8.7%; p = 0.047). Gestational diabetes was more common in women who ultimately required cesarean delivery (34.2% vs. 23.7%; p = 0.023). Epidural anesthesia use correlated with a lower cesarean rate (26.6%; p = 0.000).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center cohort, the Polish index model for full-term VBAC (Ti) prediction showed moderate accuracy. A refined version demonstrated improved performance compared with the original. Several predictors of successful VBAC were confirmed, including prior vaginal delivery and history of macrosomia, while high BMI and gestational diabetes increased the risk of intrapartum cesarean section.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.
